title: Cross-Terminal Clipboard Abstraction
description:
# Cross-Terminal Clipboard Abstraction

## Background & Motivation

Clipboard access varies across terminals and platforms:
- OSC 52 (modern terminals)
- pbcopy/pbpaste (macOS)
- xclip/xsel (X11)
- wl-copy/wl-paste (Wayland)

**The solution:**
- Unified Clipboard API
- Auto-detect best method
- Graceful fallback chain

**Relationship to existing beads:**
- Requires bd-10i.4.4 (TerminalCapabilities detection)
- Extends bd-2rs (OSC 52 implementation)

## Technical Design

```rust
pub struct Clipboard {
    backend: ClipboardBackend,
}

pub enum ClipboardBackend {
    Osc52,
    MacOS,  // pbcopy/pbpaste
    X11,    // xclip
    Wayland, // wl-copy
    Unavailable,
}

pub enum ClipboardError {
    NotAvailable,
    WriteError(String),
    ReadError(String),
}

impl Clipboard {
    pub fn detect(caps: &TerminalCapabilities) -> Self {
        // Try OSC 52 first if terminal supports it
        // Fall back to platform-specific tools
    }
    
    pub fn set(&self, text: &str) -> Result<(), ClipboardError> { ... }
    pub fn get(&self) -> Result<String, ClipboardError> { ... }
}
```

## Logging Requirements

```rust
// Backend detected (INFO level)
tracing::info!(backend = ?backend, "Clipboard backend detected");

// Clipboard write (DEBUG level)
tracing::debug!(backend = ?backend, bytes = text.len(), "Clipboard write");

// Fallback triggered (WARN level)
tracing::warn!(
    primary = ?primary_backend,
    fallback = ?fallback_backend,
    reason = reason,
    "Clipboard fallback triggered"
);
```

## E2E Tests

```bash
# Test clipboard roundtrip
./ftui-harness --test-mode clipboard --text "Hello, World!"
# Assert: get() returns same text

# Test with large content
./ftui-harness --test-mode clipboard --size 100KB
# Assert: content preserved

# Test fallback chain
FTUI_CLIPBOARD_BACKEND=none ./ftui-harness --test-mode clipboard --expect-fallback
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] OSC 52 implementation works in modern terminals
- [ ] Platform fallback (macOS, Linux X11, Linux Wayland, Windows)
- [ ] Auto-detection of best method
- [ ] Clear error messages for unsupported environments
- [ ] Works in SSH sessions (OSC 52 preferred)
- [ ] Binary content base64 encoded
- [ ] All tests pass
close_reason: Implemented cross-terminal Clipboard abstraction with backend detection, OSC52/external fallback, env override, logging hooks, and get/set/clear APIs

title: Implement Status Line and Panel widgets
description:
PHASE 5 - STATUS LINE + PANEL WIDGETS

## Background
Status lines and panels are essential for agent harness UIs. Status line shows current mode/status. Panel provides structured chrome around content areas.

## Technical Requirements

### Status Line Widget

pub struct StatusLine<'a> {
    left: Vec<StatusItem<'a>>,
    center: Vec<StatusItem<'a>>,
    right: Vec<StatusItem<'a>>,
    style: Style,
    separator: &'a str,
}

pub enum StatusItem<'a> {
    Text(Text<'a>),
    Spinner(SpinnerState),
    Progress { current: u64, total: u64 },
    KeyHint { key: &'a str, action: &'a str },
    Spacer,
}

impl StatusLine<'_> {
    pub fn left(mut self, item: StatusItem) -> Self;
    pub fn center(mut self, item: StatusItem) -> Self;
    pub fn right(mut self, item: StatusItem) -> Self;
}

// Typical usage
StatusLine::new()
    .left(StatusItem::Text("[INSERT]".into()))
    .center(StatusItem::Text("file.rs".into()))
    .right(StatusItem::KeyHint { key: "^C", action: "Quit" })
    .right(StatusItem::Text("Ln 42, Col 10".into()))

### Panel Widget

pub struct Panel<'a> {
    title: Option<Title<'a>>,
    content: Box<dyn Widget + 'a>,
    footer: Option<Text<'a>>,
    border_style: BorderStyle,
    focus_style: Option<Style>,
    focused: bool,
}

impl Panel<'_> {
    pub fn new(content: impl Widget) -> Self;
    pub fn title(mut self, title: impl Into<Title>) -> Self;
    pub fn footer(mut self, footer: impl Into<Text>) -> Self;
    pub fn focused(mut self, focused: bool) -> Self;
}

### Layout Integration
Panels work with Flex/Grid:

Flex::vertical()
    .add(Panel::new(log_viewer).title("Logs").flex(1.0))
    .add(Panel::new(input).title("Command").height(3))
    .add(StatusLine::new()...)

### Focus Management
- focused property changes border style
- Tab navigation between panels (runtime handles)
- Focus indicator (optional marker)

## Tests Required
- [ ] StatusLine left/center/right positioning
- [ ] StatusLine separator rendering
- [ ] StatusLine truncation behavior
- [ ] Panel border rendering
- [ ] Panel title positioning
- [ ] Panel focus style change
- [ ] Panel with various content types
- [ ] Empty status line

title: Add widget-level span instrumentation
Widget Intrinsic Sizing System (Widget::measure() Trait)
description:
## Goal
Enable widgets to report their intrinsic (preferred/minimum/maximum) dimensions, unlocking content-aware layout like CSS flexbox/Tailwind.

## Background & Motivation
Currently, FrankenTUI widgets receive a `Rect` and render into it, but they cannot communicate their sizing preferences back to the layout system. This is a fundamental limitation that prevents:
- **Shrink-to-fit containers**: A button can't say 'I need 12 chars wide'
- **Content-based sizing**: A paragraph can't report its wrapped height
- **Min/max constraints**: Widgets can't enforce minimum viable sizes
- **Auto-sizing in flex layouts**: Constraint::Min/Max work on ratios, not content

CSS flexbox and Tailwind achieve reflowability by having elements report intrinsic sizes (min-content, max-content, fit-content). We need the same.

## Design Approach
Introduce a `MeasurableWidget` trait (or extend `Widget`) with:
```rust
pub trait MeasurableWidget: Widget {
    /// Compute preferred size given available space
    fn measure(&self, available: Size) -> Size;
    
    /// Minimum size below which widget is unusable
    fn min_size(&self) -> Size { Size::ZERO }
    
    /// Maximum size beyond which more space is wasted
    fn max_size(&self) -> Option<Size> { None }
}
```

## Scope
- Core trait definition and semantics
- Default implementations for existing widgets
- Layout solver integration (Constraint::FitContent)
- Caching/memoization of measure results
- Migration path for custom widgets

## Non-Goals
- GPU-accelerated layout (separate concern)
- CSS-compatible box model (we're terminal-native)

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 37 core widgets implement MeasurableWidget
- Layout solver uses intrinsic sizes for Min/FitContent constraints
- Measure results are cached and invalidated correctly
- No performance regression (lazy evaluation)
- Demo showcase demonstrates content-aware layouts

## Tests / Validation
- Unit tests for measure/min/max outputs across core widgets.
- Property tests: monotonicity with available size; min <= preferred <= max.
- Snapshot tests: content-aware layouts in the demo harness.
- E2E PTY script with JSONL logging of sizes, constraints, chosen intrinsic sizes, and checksums.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Intrinsic sizing is usable end-to-end: widget impls + solver integration + caching + demo.
- [ ] Test suite provides strong guarantees (unit/property/snapshot + deterministic PTY E2E).
- [ ] Performance is budgeted and regressions are caught early (bench + CI gates).
- [ ] Migration guidance enables external widget authors to implement measurement correctly.
close_reason: All sub-tasks completed (bd-2dow.1-8 all closed)

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Architectural Context

### Current State
The existing Widget trait is simple:
```rust
pub trait Widget {
    fn render(&self, area: Rect, frame: &mut Frame);
    fn is_essential(&self) -> bool { false }
}
```

Widgets are 'told' their size by the layout system. They have no voice in the matter.

### The Problem
Consider a responsive dashboard with flexible panels. Currently:
1. Layout solver allocates space based on Constraint ratios
2. Widget receives Rect and renders
3. If content doesn't fit, it truncates or overflows
4. There's no feedback loop to inform better layout decisions

With intrinsic sizing:
1. Layout solver queries widgets for preferred sizes
2. Solver uses these as inputs to constraint resolution
3. Widgets receive well-sized Rects that respect their needs
4. Content naturally fits without truncation

### Why This Matters for Zero-Flicker Reflow
During resize, the layout solver needs to make fast, correct decisions. Without intrinsic sizes, it can only use static ratios. With intrinsic sizes, it can:
- Collapse non-essential widgets when space is tight
- Expand widgets up to their max-content
- Prioritize essential content in constrained layouts

### Relationship to Other Beads
- **bd-1rz0 (Responsive Reflow)**: Intrinsic sizing provides the 'content signal' the reflow engine needs
- **bd-4kq0 (Kernel Optimization)**: Measure caching prevents redundant computation
- **bd-1rz0.5 (Responsive Layout Primitives)**: Breakpoints + intrinsic sizing = full responsive design

### Implementation Strategy
1. Define trait with sensible defaults (min=0, max=unbounded)
2. Implement for simple widgets first (Paragraph, Block, Span)
3. Add layout solver integration (new Constraint::FitContent)
4. Implement for complex widgets (List, Table, Tabs)
5. Add caching layer with invalidation
6. Update demo showcase with examples

# Quality Gates: v1 Stop-Ship Criteria

## Background
Plan Section 0.7 defines four quality gates that are STOP-SHIP if failing. These must be tracked and verified before v1 release.

## Quality Gates

### Gate 1: Inline Mode Stability (CRITICAL)
**Requirement:** Re-rendering UI region while streaming logs cannot corrupt scrollback or cursor placement.

**Verification:**
- [ ] PTY test: continuous log stream + periodic UI refresh does not corrupt scrollback
- [ ] PTY test: cursor returns to correct position after every present()
- [ ] PTY test: resize during active logging re-anchors correctly
- [ ] Manual test: 10-minute stress test with rapid log output
- [ ] Tested on: Linux terminal, tmux, macOS Terminal, WezTerm, Kitty

**Blocking beads:** bd-fbp (overlay redraw), bd-10i.11.2 (PTY tests)

### Gate 2: Diff/Presenter Correctness
**Requirement:** Property tests validate that applying presenter output to a terminal-model yields the expected grid for supported ops.

**Verification:**
- [ ] proptest: BufferDiff.compute() identifies all changes
- [ ] proptest: applying Presenter output to TerminalModel matches source Buffer
- [ ] proptest: style state never "leaks" across runs
- [ ] proptest: OSC 8 links properly opened and closed
- [ ] 1000+ random buffer property test passes

**Blocking beads:** bd-10i.11.1 (terminal-model), bd-10i.4.3 (Presenter)

### Gate 3: Unicode Width Correctness
**Requirement:** Test suite includes emoji/ZWJ/combining marks; no off-by-one wrapping errors.

**Verification:**
- [ ] Width corpus test: ASCII (all printable)
- [ ] Width corpus test: CJK wide characters
- [ ] Width corpus test: Common emoji (🎉, ❤️, 🔥, etc.)
- [ ] Width corpus test: ZWJ sequences (👨‍👩‍👧‍👦, 👩‍💻, etc.)

- [ ] Text wrapping test: no mid-grapheme breaks
- [ ] Truncation test: ellipsis at correct position

**Blocking beads:** bd-16k (Unicode width corpus), bd-2uk (Text type)

### Gate 4: Terminal Cleanup
**Requirement:** PTY tests verify raw mode + cursor visibility + alt screen restoration after normal exit and panic.

title: Text Effects: Vertical and Diagonal Gradients
description:
## Background
Current gradients only support horizontal direction. Vertical, diagonal, and radial gradients complete the gradient system and enable effects like sunset (orange bottom, purple top).

## Implementation

Add new TextEffect variants:
```rust
TextEffect::VerticalGradient {
    gradient: ColorGradient,
    // For multi-line: t = row / total_rows
    // For single-line: uses text height in cells (e.g., ASCII art)
}

TextEffect::DiagonalGradient {
    gradient: ColorGradient,
    angle: f64,  // degrees: 0=right, 90=down, 180=left, 270=up
}

TextEffect::RadialGradient {
    gradient: ColorGradient,
    center: (f64, f64),  // normalized 0-1, (0.5, 0.5) = center
    aspect: f64,         // 1.0 = circular, 2.0 = horizontally stretched
}
```

### Coordinate Mapping:

| Type | t Calculation |
|------|---------------|
| Horizontal | char_idx / total_chars |
| Vertical (multi-line) | row_idx / total_rows |
| Vertical (single-line) | 0.5 (center color) OR uses AsciiArt height |
| Diagonal | (x*cos(θ) + y*sin(θ)) normalized to 0-1 |
| Radial | distance_from_center / max_distance |

### Animation Support:
All gradient variants can be animated by adding time offset:
```rust
// In StyledText, if gradient effect + time > 0:
let animated_t = (t + self.time * speed).rem_euclid(1.0);
```

### Single-Line Vertical Gradient Behavior:
For single-row text, vertical gradient returns gradient.sample(0.5) for all chars (middle of gradient). To get full vertical gradient effect, use multi-line text or AsciiArtText.

## Files
crates/ftui-extras/src/text_effects.rs

## Unit Tests (REQUIRED)
- test_vertical_multiline_top_is_start: Row 0 gets sample(0)
- test_vertical_multiline_bottom_is_end: Last row gets sample(1)
- test_vertical_singleline_is_middle: All chars get sample(0.5)
- test_diagonal_0_is_horizontal: Matches HorizontalGradient
- test_diagonal_90_is_vertical: Top-to-bottom sweep
- test_diagonal_angle_wraps: 450° same as 90°
- test_radial_center_is_start: Center gets sample(0)
- test_radial_corner_is_end: Corners get sample(1)
- test_radial_aspect_stretches: aspect=2 makes ellipse
- test_gradient_animated: Time offset moves gradient

## Visual Tests
- Snapshot vertical on 5-line AsciiArt text
- Snapshot diagonal at 45°
- Snapshot radial with aspect=1 vs aspect=2

## Acceptance Criteria
- Deliver the behavior implied by the title: Text Effects: Vertical and Diagonal Gradients
- Alien Artifact: define invariants + failure modes; if heuristics exist, specify an explainable decision rule (evidence ledger / Bayes factors where applicable)
- Extreme Optimization: baseline -> profile -> opportunity matrix; for each perf change include an isomorphism proof + golden output checksums
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures; add property tests for core invariants where applicable
- E2E: scripts with verbose JSONL logging (env, capabilities, timings, seed, checksums) + deterministic mode

title: Modular Table Theme System (All Tables)
description:
Goal:
- Unify table styling across all tables (widget tables + markdown tables) with a modular, animatable theming system.

Background / Problem:
- Styling is currently split: MarkdownTheme has table fields while widget tables have their own styling path.
- Users want consistent visuals, easy customization, tasteful animation, and clear preset selection guidance.

Design principles:
- Deterministic by default: animation uses explicit phase/time input (no implicit clocks).
- Lightweight: style resolution is O(1) per row/column; avoid hot-path allocations.
- No compatibility shims: adopt the new system directly (project preference).
- Presets should be readable at high density and a11y-friendly.

Deliverables:
- Shared TableTheme struct (border/header/row/alt/selected/hover + spacing/dividers).
- Effect hooks with row/column/section targeting and phase-driven transforms.
- Presets (aurora/graphite/neon/slate/solar/orchard/paper/midnight/terminal_classic) with strong defaults + easy overrides.
- Integrations in widget tables and markdown tables.
- Demo showcase with subtle animated highlight row.
- Preset preview gallery screen to compare presets side-by-side.
- Comprehensive unit tests, snapshots, and E2E scripts with structured logging.
- Public API ergonomics (builder helpers + re-exports) so customization is trivial.

Acceptance:
- All table render paths can be themed via one struct + optional animation phase.
- Presets look great out of the box; customization is ergonomic.

comments.text:
Touchpoints: ftui-widgets Table
- File: crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs
- Styles on Table: base style via Table::style (applied to entire table_area with set_style_area), highlight_style via Table::highlight_style (merged with row.style for selected row), column_spacing affects layout

Touchpoints: ftui-extras Markdown tables
- File: crates/ftui-extras/src/markdown.rs
- Theme fields: MarkdownTheme::table_border/table_header/table_row/table_row_alt
- Rendering: RenderState::flush_table builds widths, applies table_max_width, emits border lines via table_border_line; row lines via table_row_line with base_style + border_style; cell spans styled in apply_table_cell_style
- Constraints: table_max_width (MarkdownRenderer::table_max_width) caps content width; table_cell_spans truncates with ellipsis using Span::split_at_cell (width-sensitive); table layout uses Unicode line-drawing characters

title: Design TableTheme API + presets (spec)
description:
Purpose:
- Specify the TableTheme API and presets so implementation is straightforward and consistent.

API sketch (to be finalized in implementation):
- struct TableTheme { border, header, row, row_alt, row_selected, row_hover, divider, padding, column_gap, row_height, effects: Vec<TableEffectRule>, preset_id }
- enum TableSection { Header, Body, Footer }
- enum TableEffectTarget { Section(TableSection), Row(usize), RowRange{start,end}, Column(usize), ColumnRange{start,end}, AllRows, AllCells }
- enum TableEffect { Pulse{fg_a, fg_b, bg_a, bg_b, speed, phase_offset}, BreathingGlow{fg, bg, intensity, speed, phase_offset, asymmetry}, GradientSweep{gradient, speed, phase_offset} }
- struct TableEffectRule { target, effect, priority, blend_mode, style_mask }
- TableTheme::resolve_style(ctx, phase) -> Style (deterministic, low-cost)

Index semantics (must be explicit in spec):
- Row/column indices are 0-based and refer to body rows/columns (header row is not counted as row 0).
- Header effects should target Section(Header) explicitly.
- AllRows targets body rows only (excludes header); AllCells includes header + body.

Phase semantics:
- Phase input is normalized to [0,1). Resolver should define clamp/wrap semantics (e.g., fract for >1) and document it.

Priority semantics:
- Effects apply in ascending priority, then stable insertion order to keep determinism when priorities tie.

Ergonomics:
- Builder helpers: with_border/with_header/with_effect/preset(...)
- Re-export from ftui prelude or theme module for easy access.
- Accept either ColorToken-based Styles or PackedRgba styles (so themes can be dynamic).

Presets (expanded):
- aurora: luminous header bar + cool zebra + crisp borders.
- graphite: ultra-legible monochrome for data density.
- neon: accent header + subtle color sweep for emphasis.
- slate: subdued neutral for serious dashboards.
- solar: warm, high‑contrast data tables (daylight friendly).
- orchard: muted green accents for financial/ops tables.
- paper: light, minimal, print‑like appearance.
- midnight: dark, restrained palette with low‑glare contrasts.
- terminal_classic: ANSI‑heritage palette; uses 16‑color baseline, but may upgrade to 256/truecolor when available to avoid degraded look on modern terminals.

Constraints:
- Deterministic: resolve_style is pure; phase is passed in explicitly (no internal clocks or RNG).
- Degradation-aware: TableTheme must respect Frame.degradation.apply_styling (no styling when degraded).
- Performance: no allocations or string ops in render hot paths; resolve is O(rules).

Merge / precedence rules (must be explicit in spec):
- Base style from theme (header/row/row_alt) then row_selected / row_hover overlays.
- Explicit Row::style and per-cell Span style must remain honored; define merge order so explicit cell styles are not accidentally overwritten.
- Effects apply last using style_mask to limit which channels (fg/bg/attrs) they may override.

Border mapping (widget tables):
- TableTheme.border + divider should map to Block border styles where Table uses Block.
- Block title styling remains independent; theme should not clobber titles.

Glyph policy:
- TableTheme controls style only; border glyph characters are unchanged unless explicitly extended later.

Acceptance:
- Spec is self-contained and includes fields, effect model, precedence, determinism + perf constraints, index + phase semantics, and border mapping semantics.
close_reason: Spec drafted in docs/specs/table-theme.md

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
TableTheme API spec (draft)

Goals
- Single style source for ftui-widgets Table + markdown tables
- Deterministic and phase-driven; no internal time or randomness
- Low-cost resolve path; no heap allocations on hot render path

Core types
1) struct TableTheme
- preset_id: &'static str (or TablePreset enum)
- border: Style (outer border)
- divider: Style (inner borders between columns/rows)
- header: Style
- row: Style
- row_alt: Style
- row_selected: Style
- row_hover: Style
- padding_x: u16 (cells left/right padding)
- padding_y: u16 (extra row height, or use row_height)
- column_gap: u16 (maps to Table column_spacing)
- row_height: u16 (default 1)
- effects: Vec<TableEffectRule>

2) enum TableSection { Header, Body, Footer }

3) struct TableContext
- section: TableSection
- row: usize
- col: usize
- is_header: bool
- is_selected: bool
- is_hovered: bool
- is_alt_row: bool
- is_divider: bool (optional, for border/divider styling)

4) enum TableEffectTarget
- Section(TableSection)
- Row(usize)
- RowRange { start, end }
- Column(usize)
- ColumnRange { start, end }
- AllRows
- AllCells

5) enum TableEffect
- Pulse { fg_a, fg_b, bg_a, bg_b, speed, phase }
- BreathingGlow { fg, bg, intensity, speed, phase, asymmetry }
- GradientSweep { gradient, speed, phase }

6) struct TableEffectRule
- target: TableEffectTarget
- effect: TableEffect
- style_mask: StyleMask (optional; fg/bg/attrs selection)

Resolve API
- fn resolve_style(&self, ctx: TableContext, phase: f32) -> Style
- Composition order (deterministic):
  - base = if ctx.is_header { header } else if ctx.is_alt_row { row_alt } else { row }
  - base = if ctx.is_selected { row_selected.merge(&base) } else base
  - base = if ctx.is_hovered { row_hover.merge(&base) } else base
  - for rule in effects matching ctx: base = effect_style(rule, phase).merge(&base)
  - return base
- Optional fn resolve_border_style(kind: BorderKind) -> Style
  - BorderKind: OuterTop/OuterMid/OuterBottom/InnerVertical/InnerHorizontal

Determinism constraints
- resolve_style must be pure: output depends only on ctx + phase + theme
- phase is provided by caller (e.g., normalized 0..1 or ticks); no internal clocks
- effects must not mutate state; no RNG
- markdown table rendering should pass a stable phase or 0.0

Performance constraints
- resolve_style should not allocate; prefer precomputed color steps for effects
- effect evaluation should be O(rules) with simple condition checks
- merging uses Style::merge; avoid string allocations or span cloning inside resolve

Presets (initial)
- aurora: bright header bar, cool zebra, crisp borders
- graphite: monochrome, high-contrast, dense data
- neon: accent header, subtle sweep on selected row only

Integration notes
- Table widget: use TableTheme for base row/header/selected/hover; padding_x replaces hardcoded cell spacing; column_gap maps to Table::column_spacing
- Markdown tables: replace MarkdownTheme table_* with TableTheme (border/divider/header/row/row_alt); table_max_width still applies
- Effects are opt-in: markdown uses phase=0.0; Table widget can accept phase from runtime or omit

title: Implement table animation resolver (phase-driven styles)
description:
Purpose:
- Implement deterministic, phase-driven style transforms for table animation.

Implementation detail:
- Provide a resolver that lerps fg/bg colors based on a phase input (0..1).
- Use low-amplitude curves (breathing / pulse) to keep effects tasteful.
- Effects applied at row/column/section level only (avoid per-cell heavy ops).

Phase handling:
- Normalize phase via clamp/wrap semantics from spec (e.g., fract for >1).
- Apply per-effect phase_offset deterministically.

Suggested formula:
- breathing(t) = sin curve with asymmetry (quick inhale, slow exhale).
- alpha = min + (max-min) * breathing(t).
- style = lerp(base, highlight, alpha).

Performance:
- O(1) per row/column resolution; avoid allocations.
- No global time; caller passes phase (deterministic, testable).

Acceptance:
- Resolver produces stable output for identical phase inputs.
- Effect intensity is subtle by default (no visual noise).

E2E Test Scripts with Comprehensive Logging
description:
# E2E Test Scripts with Comprehensive Logging

## Background
Plan Section Testing + Verification requires end-to-end tests that validate the complete pipeline from user input to terminal output. The user specifically requested "comprehensive unit tests and e2e test scripts with great, detailed logging."

## E2E Test Philosophy
E2E tests should:
1. Test the complete system as a user would experience it
2. Run in a PTY to capture real terminal behavior
3. Log every step for post-mortem debugging
4. Be deterministic and reproducible
5. Cover happy paths and error cases

## E2E Test Script Structure

### Directory Layout
```
tests/
  e2e/
    fixtures/          # Test input files
    expected/          # Expected output snapshots
    scripts/           # Test runner scripts
      run_all.sh       # Master test runner
      test_inline.sh   # Inline mode tests
      test_altscreen.sh # Alt-screen tests
      test_cleanup.sh  # Cleanup/panic tests
      test_input.sh    # Input handling tests
    lib/
      common.sh        # Shared utilities
      logging.sh       # Logging functions
      pty.sh           # PTY spawning helpers
```

### Logging Framework (logging.sh)
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Comprehensive logging for E2E tests

LOG_LEVEL=${LOG_LEVEL:-DEBUG}
LOG_FILE=${LOG_FILE:-/tmp/ftui_e2e_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log}

log() {
    local level=$1
    shift
    local timestamp=$(date +"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%3N")
    local caller="${BASH_SOURCE[2]}:${BASH_LINENO[1]}"
    echo "[$timestamp] [$level] [$caller] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
}

log_debug() { [[ "$LOG_LEVEL" == "DEBUG" ]] && log "DEBUG" "$@"; }
log_info()  { log "INFO" "$@"; }
log_warn()  { log "WARN" "$@"; }
log_error() { log "ERROR" "$@"; }

log_test_start() {
    local test_name=$1
    log_info "=========================================="
    log_info "STARTING TEST: $test_name"
    log_info "=========================================="
}

log_test_pass() {
    local test_name=$1
    log_info "✓ PASSED: $test_name"
}

log_test_fail() {
    local test_name=$1
    local reason=$2
    log_error "✗ FAILED: $test_name"
    log_error "  Reason: $reason"
    log_error "  Log file: $LOG_FILE"
}

log_hex_dump() {
    local label=$1
    local data=$2
    log_debug "$label (hex): $(echo -n "$data" | xxd -p | tr -d n)"
}
```

## E2E Test Categories

### 1. Inline Mode Tests (test_inline.sh)
Tests that streaming logs + UI chrome works correctly.

```bash
test_inline_log_scroll() {
    log_test_start "Inline mode: log scrolling"
    
    # Setup
    local pty_output=$(mktemp)
    log_debug "PTY output file: $pty_output"
    
    # Run ftui app that streams 100 log lines with 6-line UI
    log_info "Spawning ftui inline mode app..."
    timeout 10s script -q -c "./target/debug/ftui-harness --mode inline --ui-height 6 --log-count 100" "$pty_output"
    local exit_code=$?
    log_debug "Exit code: $exit_code"
    
    # Verify
    log_info "Verifying output..."
    
    # Check scrollback preservation
    if grep -q "Log line 1" "$pty_output"; then
        log_debug "Early log lines found in scrollback ✓"
    else
        log_test_fail "Inline log scroll" "Early log lines missing from scrollback"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Check UI region intact
    if tail -6 "$pty_output" | grep -q "\[Status\]"; then
        log_debug "UI region present at bottom ✓"
    else
        log_test_fail "Inline log scroll" "UI region not at expected position"
        return 1
    fi
    
    log_test_pass "Inline mode: log scrolling"
    rm "$pty_output"
}
```

### 2. Cleanup Tests (test_cleanup.sh)
Tests that terminal is restored after exit/panic.

```bash
test_panic_cleanup() {
    log_test_start "Panic cleanup: terminal restored"
    
    # Capture terminal state before
    local before_state=$(stty -g)
    log_debug "Terminal state before: $before_state"
    
    # Run app that panics
    log_info "Running app that will panic..."
    ./target/debug/ftui-panic-test 2>/dev/null || true
    
    # Capture terminal state after
    local after_state=$(stty -g)
    log_debug "Terminal state after: $after_state"
    
    # Verify restoration
    if [[ "$before_state" == "$after_state" ]]; then
        log_debug "Terminal state restored ✓"
    else
        log_test_fail "Panic cleanup" "Terminal state not restored"
        log_error "  Before: $before_state"
        log_error "  After:  $after_state"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Check cursor visible (SGR sequence check)
    log_info "Checking cursor visibility..."
    # ... additional checks ...
    
    log_test_pass "Panic cleanup: terminal restored"
}
```

### 3. Input Tests (test_input.sh)
Tests for keyboard, mouse, paste handling.

### 4. ANSI Output Tests
Verify presenter output matches expected sequences.

## Test Output Format

Each test run produces:
1. Console output (PASS/FAIL per test)
2. Detailed log file with timestamps
3. JSON summary for CI
4. PTY captures for failed tests

### JSON Summary Format
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-01-31T23:45:00Z",
  "total": 50,
  "passed": 48,
  "failed": 2,
  "skipped": 0,
  "duration_ms": 12345,
  "tests": [
    {
      "name": "test_inline_log_scroll",
      "status": "passed",
      "duration_ms": 234,
      "log_lines": 45
    },
    {
      "name": "test_panic_cleanup",
      "status": "failed",
      "duration_ms": 567,
      "error": "Terminal state not restored",
      "log_file": "/tmp/ftui_e2e_20260131_234500.log"
    }
  ]
}
```

## E2E Test Inventory

| Test | Description | Priority |
|------|-------------|----------|
| inline_basic | Basic inline mode display | P0 |
| inline_log_scroll | Log scrolling preserves scrollback | P0 |
| inline_resize | Resize re-anchors UI | P0 |
| inline_cursor | Cursor position contract | P0 |
| altscreen_enter_exit | Alt-screen lifecycle | P0 |
| cleanup_normal | Terminal restored on exit | P0 |
| cleanup_panic | Terminal restored on panic | P0 |
| cleanup_io_error | Terminal restored on IO error | P1 |
| input_key_basic | Basic key parsing | P0 |
| input_key_modifiers | Modifier key detection | P1 |
| input_mouse_click | Mouse click handling | P1 |
| input_mouse_scroll | Mouse scroll handling | P1 |
| input_paste | Bracketed paste handling | P1 |
| input_focus | Focus events | P2 |
| ansi_sgr | SGR sequence output | P0 |
| ansi_osc8 | OSC 8 hyperlink output | P1 |
| ansi_sync | Synchronized output | P1 |
| unicode_basic | ASCII width handling | P0 |
| unicode_wide | CJK wide chars | P0 |
| unicode_emoji | Emoji rendering | P0 |
| unicode_zwj | ZWJ sequences | P1 |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] run_all.sh executes all E2E tests
- [ ] Each test has detailed logging
- [ ] Failed tests produce actionable diagnostics
- [ ] JSON summary generated for CI
- [ ] PTY captures preserved on failure
- [ ] Tests run in < 60 seconds total
- [ ] All P0 tests must pass for v1

## Dependencies
- Requires: bd-2kj (Agent Harness exists to test)
- Requires: bd-10i.11.2 (PTY framework)
- Blocks: bd-2gx (Quality Gates)

## CI Integration
- Run on every PR
- Block merge on P0 test failures
- Upload log artifacts on failure

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.

## Extreme Optimization

- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.

title: Fix emoji (VS16) width so borders never misalign (file browser + markdown)
description:
Problem
- In demo showcase, borders get misaligned in the File Browser screen and Markdown screens when emoji icons (esp. VS16 sequences like "⚙️" / "ℹ️" / "✏️") appear. We want to KEEP emojis; fix width/rendering so borders are never corrupted.

Hypothesis
- Some emoji graphemes that include Variation Selector-16 (U+FE0F) are being measured as width=1, so we intern them with width=1 (no continuation cells). Terminals render them as double-width, causing spillover into border cells and cursor/border corruption.

Approach
- Fix shared width calculation for grapheme clusters containing U+FE0F to treat them as width>=2 (when non-zero), matching terminal behavior.
- Add regression tests for widths of common VS16 emoji used in the demo (⚙️, ℹ️, ✏️, 🗑️, etc.).
- Verify via demo-showcase snapshot/e2e or terminal-model tests that right borders remain intact.
close_reason: Closed: root cause was harness serialization; buffer_to_text/buffer_to_ansi now repeat '?' to match grapheme width; snapshots reblessed; width calc for VS16 already correct

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Root cause identified and fixed by CloudyGorge: buffer_to_text()/buffer_to_ansi() in ftui-harness emitted single '?' (width 1) for grapheme pool entries that are width 2. Fix: output '?' repeated to match grapheme display width. Added buffer_to_text_with_pool() variant. All 32 affected snapshots re-blessed. Verified grapheme_width('⚙\u{fe0f}') correctly returns 2 — the underlying width calc was never broken, only the text serialization.

description:
# SIMD/autovec accelerated hot paths (NO unsafe)

## Objective
Improve hot-path performance (cell comparisons, clears, copies, ASCII width checks) **without introducing unsafe code**.

Project constraint: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` across our crates. We must not create an “unsafe-only SIMD crate”.

## Plan Alignment
The plan mentions optional SIMD acceleration. In this repo, that must translate into one of:
- compiler autovectorization via carefully-written scalar loops
- safe portable SIMD (only if available without `unsafe` in our Rust toolchain)
- leveraging well-vetted dependencies that encapsulate unsafe internally (our crate remains `forbid(unsafe_code)`)

## Scope
Target the following operations, in priority order:
1. Cell equality comparisons in diff scan
2. Buffer clear/fill
3. Row/rect copies
4. ASCII-width fast paths

## Strategy
- Write scalar loops that are friendly to autovec:
  - contiguous slices
  - minimal branching
  - row-major iteration
- Use benchmark-driven iteration:
  - measure p50/p95 for 80x24 and larger terminals
  - confirm no regressions in correctness tests

## Explicit Non-Goal
- Adding `unsafe` blocks or `#[target_feature]` functions inside ftui code.

If later we decide explicit unsafe SIMD is required, that needs an explicit policy change (and likely an ADR + safety review).

## Tests Required
- Property tests confirming optimized paths exactly match the reference scalar behavior.
- Benchmarks that show improvements and include regression budgets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Optimizations preserve correctness (property tests pass; byte-for-byte identical results where applicable).
- [ ] Benchmarks demonstrate measurable improvements on at least one key hot path.
- [ ] No unsafe code is introduced in ftui crates.

title: Semantic Event System: High-Level Input Abstraction
description:
## Background

FrankenTUI has excellent low-level input parsing in `ftui-core/src/input_parser.rs` that transforms raw terminal bytes into `Event` types (Key, Mouse, Resize, etc.). However, **every widget must implement its own gesture detection** for common patterns like:

- Double-click detection (file browser, list selection)
- Long-press recognition (context menus)
- Drag operations (text selection, list reordering)
- Chord sequences (Ctrl+K Ctrl+C style shortcuts)
- Swipe gestures (touch terminal support)

This leads to **duplicated, inconsistent, and often missing** gesture handling across widgets.

## Problem Statement

Consider implementing double-click in a List widget:
1. Track last click time and position
2. Define timeout threshold (300ms typical)
3. Handle edge cases (different positions, mouse up/down)
4. This code is repeated in Table, FilePicker, TreeView...

The same applies to drag detection, long-press, and chords.

## Solution: Semantic Event Layer

Add a `GestureRecognizer` in `ftui-runtime` that:
1. Receives raw `Event` from terminal
2. Maintains state (click history, mouse position, key sequences)
3. Emits `SemanticEvent` when gestures are recognized
4. Widgets receive high-level events instead of raw input

## Proposed API

```rust
// New event types in ftui-core
pub enum SemanticEvent {
    // Mouse gestures
    Click { pos: Position, button: MouseButton },
    DoubleClick { pos: Position, button: MouseButton },
    TripleClick { pos: Position, button: MouseButton }, // Line selection
    LongPress { pos: Position, duration: Duration },
    
    // Drag gestures
    DragStart { pos: Position, button: MouseButton },
    DragMove { from: Position, to: Position, delta: (i16, i16) },
    DragEnd { from: Position, to: Position },
    DragCancel,
    
    // Keyboard gestures  
    Chord { sequence: Vec<KeyEvent> }, // e.g., Ctrl+K Ctrl+C
    
    // Touch-like gestures (for touch terminals)
    Swipe { direction: Direction, distance: u16, velocity: f32 },
    Pinch { scale: f32 }, // Future: zoom
}

// Recognizer configuration
pub struct GestureConfig {
    pub double_click_timeout: Duration,  // Default: 300ms
    pub long_press_threshold: Duration,  // Default: 500ms
    pub drag_threshold: u16,             // Default: 3 cells
    pub chord_timeout: Duration,         // Default: 1000ms
    pub enable_swipe: bool,              // Default: false
}

// Stateful recognizer
pub struct GestureRecognizer {
    config: GestureConfig,
    // Internal state
    last_click: Option<(Instant, Position, MouseButton)>,
    drag_state: Option<DragState>,
    chord_buffer: Vec<KeyEvent>,
    chord_start: Option<Instant>,
}

impl GestureRecognizer {
    pub fn process(&mut self, event: Event) -> Vec<SemanticEvent>;
    pub fn reset(&mut self);
    pub fn is_dragging(&self) -> bool;
}
```

## Integration with Runtime

```rust
// In Program::run()
loop {
    let raw_event = terminal.read_event()?;
    
    // Process through gesture recognizer
    let semantic_events = self.gesture_recognizer.process(raw_event.clone());
    
    // Model receives both raw and semantic events
    for semantic in semantic_events {
        let msg = Message::Semantic(semantic);
        self.model.update(msg);
    }
    
    // Raw event still available if needed
    let msg = Message::from(raw_event);
    self.model.update(msg);
}
```

## Benefits

1. **Consistency**: All widgets get the same gesture detection
2. **Correctness**: Edge cases handled once, correctly
3. **Configurability**: Users can tune thresholds
4. **Extensibility**: New gestures added in one place
5. **Testing**: Gesture recognition is unit-testable

## Performance Considerations

- GestureRecognizer maintains minimal state (~100 bytes)
- Processing is O(1) per event
- No allocations on hot path (events returned via SmallVec)
- Configurable to disable unused gesture types

## Files to Create/Modify

- crates/ftui-core/src/semantic_event.rs (NEW)
- crates/ftui-core/src/gesture.rs (NEW)
- crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs (integrate)
- crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs (exports)

## Success Metrics

- Zero duplicated gesture detection in widgets
- All existing widgets migrated to semantic events
- Gesture recognition tests cover edge cases
- No performance regression in event processing

## Success Criteria
- Epic delivers a cohesive user-visible capability: Semantic Event System: High-Level Input Abstraction
- Child tasks are not just implemented; each has unit tests + E2E scripts with verbose JSONL logs and deterministic fixtures

title: Reactive Data Bindings
description:
## Overview
Provide declarative data binding system that automatically updates widgets when underlying data changes.

## Rationale
- Reduces boilerplate in update() handlers
- Prevents missed updates and stale UI
- Familiar pattern from web frameworks (React, Vue)
- Enables cleaner separation of concerns

## Core Components
1. **Observable Trait**: Wrapper that tracks changes to values
2. **Binding Macro**: Declarative syntax for connecting data to widgets
3. **Computed Values**: Derived values that auto-update
4. **Batch Updates**: Coalesce multiple changes into single render
5. **Binding Lifetime**: Automatic cleanup when widgets unmount

## Implementation Strategy
- Create Observable<T> wrapper in ftui-runtime
- Add bind! macro for ergonomic binding creation
- Integrate with Cmd system for change propagation
- Use weak references to prevent memory leaks

## Usage Example
let counter = Observable::new(0);
let label = Label::new().bind(label, counter, |c| format!("Count: {}", c));

// Later:
counter.set(counter.get() + 1);  // Label auto-updates

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests for Observable change detection
- Integration tests for binding propagation
- Memory leak tests for binding cleanup
- Performance tests for batch updates

## Success Criteria
- 50%+ reduction in manual update() code
- No memory leaks from bindings
- Batch updates prevent excessive renders

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.


## E2E Plan
- Provide/extend an E2E script that exercises the feature end-to-end in PTY (where applicable).
- Logging: verbose JSONL with env/capabilities + per-step timings + seed + checksums; include a summary at end.
- On failure: print reproduction command and point to artifacts directory.

title: Demo Showcase: Accessibility Modes
description:
## Background

A jaw-dropping demo still needs to be usable.

This feature provides accessibility modes that apply *uniformly* across the showcase:
- high contrast
- reduced motion
- large text / spacing

Done right, it also stress-tests the theme/token system and the animation system.

## UX / Core Interactions

- A small "A11y" panel with toggles:
  - High contrast
  - Reduced motion
  - Large text
- Immediate application to the whole app.
- Optional: persisted mode in demo state.

Suggested keybindings:
- A: toggle A11y panel
- H: high contrast
- M: reduced motion
- L: large text

## Architecture Notes

- High contrast:
  - implemented as a theme variant or a constraint-enforced palette adjustment
  - enforce WCAG AA (or stronger) in unit tests

- Reduced motion:
  - animation system must expose a global "motion scale" (0..1)
  - when disabled, animations stop deterministically (no half-frames)

- Large text:
  - scale typography tokens and spacing tokens
  - ensure layout remains stable and does not overflow disastrously

## Acceptance Criteria

- Toggles apply immediately and deterministically.
- High contrast mode passes contrast tests.
- Reduced motion mode disables animations in a verifiable way.
- Large text mode remains usable in 80x24.

Additionally (project-wide standards):
- Alien Artifact: define invariants + failure modes; if heuristics exist, specify an explainable decision rule (evidence ledger / Bayes factors where applicable)
- Extreme Optimization: baseline -> profile -> opportunity matrix; for each perf change include an isomorphism proof + golden output checksums
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures; add property tests for core invariants where applicable
- E2E: scripts with verbose JSONL logging (env, capabilities, timings, seed, checksums) + deterministic mode

## Alien Artifact Upgrades (Concrete)

- Contrast constraint solving:
  - treat palette selection as a constrained optimization problem in a perceptual space (OKLCH)
  - prove contrast bounds in tests for all semantic swatches

## Extreme Optimization

- Mode toggles must be O(1) per frame (no rebuilding large structures per frame).
- Add a regression test for mode toggle latency (bd-2o55.2).

title: Complexity Guards + Degradation Strategy
description:
Background

Scope

- Degradation modes: hide labels, collapse clusters, simplify routing, reduce decoration, or ASCII fallback.

Considerations

- Degradation should preserve readability and avoid crashes.

Tests / Validation

title: Half-Block Node Interior Fills with Color
description:
## Goal
Use half-block characters (▀▄█) and background colors to render filled node interiors, giving nodes visual weight and shape distinction even in cell-based (non-Canvas) rendering mode.

## Why
- Currently nodes are just borders + labels with no interior fill. They look hollow and blend together.
- A subtle colored fill makes shapes visually distinct: even two rectangles with different fill colors communicate "these are different types."
- Half-block characters give 1×2 vertical resolution for top/bottom edge rendering — fills look smoother.
- Works on any terminal that supports colors (no Braille/Unicode required).

## Implementation
- For each node, after drawing the border, fill the interior cells with the node's theme background color.
- Use █ (full block) for completely filled cells.
- Use ▀ (upper half) and ▄ (lower half) at the top and bottom edges for smoother shape boundaries.
- For diamond/hexagon shapes: compute which cells are "inside" the shape boundary and fill only those.
- Fill color comes from DiagramPalette (idea #7) or style_refs in the IR.

## Integration with Shape Rendering
- Must work with cell-mode shape rendering (idea #2): fill happens AFTER border drawing, BEFORE label writing.
- Label cells override fill (text on top of colored background).

## Files
- crates/ftui-extras/src/mermaid_render.rs (add fill_node_interior method)

## Tests
- Unit: filled rectangle has correct cells
- Snapshot: nodes with various fill colors at 80×24
- Verify label text remains readable on filled background (contrast check)
notes: Implemented in commit 48c04486. Per-node fill background colors via DiagramPalette::node_fill_for(). Half-block smoothing (▄▀) for Rect/Rounded/Circle shapes in Unicode mode. 4 new tests: node_fill_has_background_color, node_fill_half_block_top_row, node_fill_ascii_mode_no_half_blocks, node_label_preserves_fill_background. All 2282 ftui-extras tests pass, clippy clean.

title: Mouse Playground: Spatial Hit-Test Index + Dirty-Rect Cache
description:
## Goal
Make mouse hit-testing scale to thousands of widgets without hover lag or flicker by adding a spatial index + dirty-rect cache with provable bounds.

## Core Idea
Use a spatial index (choose the simplest that meets bounds):
- Option A: Uniform grid bucketing (fast, simple, O(1) average).
- Option B: Interval tree per axis + z-order list (O(log n) query).
- Option C: BVH (AABB tree) for dynamic layouts.

Maintain a dirty-rect cache so hover/move only recomputes affected regions, not the entire tree.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Hit-test query worst-case <= O(log n) or O(1) average depending on chosen index.
- Updates (layout changes) are incremental and do not rebuild the whole index unless size class changes.
- Guarantees correct topmost target (z-order) with stable tie-breaking.
- No allocations on hot path (steady-state).

## Implementation Notes
- Store each widget hitbox as Rect + z.
- Maintain per-cell lists (grid) or AABB nodes (BVH).
- Cache: last_hover_id + last_hover_rect; on move, if still inside and no dirty overlap, reuse.
- Dirty region produced by layout changes and hover-out events.

## Tests (REQUIRED)
- unit_hit_exact_overlap_topmost: overlapping widgets choose highest z.
- unit_hit_border_inclusive: clicks on edges are consistent with spec.
- unit_update_invalidate_rect: dirty region forces recompute only where needed.
- property_random_layout_vs_naive: spatial index equals naive O(n) hit-test for random layouts.
- perf_micro_hit_test: measure p50/p95 for 10k widgets; log results.

## E2E (REQUIRED)
- PTY mouse-move storm: generate 5k moves/sec, assert no frame drops.
- Log: hit-test time per event + cache hit rate + dirty-rect size.

## Optimization Discipline
- Baseline with and without index (hyperfine).
- Keep isomorphism proof: same selection ordering and tie-breaks.
- Golden trace of hover targets on deterministic scripted input.

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.


## Testing Plan
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures.
- Property tests: invariants (idempotence, monotonicity, determinism) where applicable.
- Fuzz tests: parsers/state machines and any input-facing logic.
- Determinism: fixed seeds/time-freeze; snapshot fixtures must be stable.

title: Implement clipboard integration (OSC 52)
description:
PHASE 7 EXTRAS - CLIPBOARD INTEGRATION

## Background
OSC 52 allows setting the system clipboard from terminal applications. This enables copy/paste functionality without external dependencies.

## Technical Requirements

### OSC 52 Protocol
Sequence: ESC ] 52 ; c ; <base64-data> BEL

c = clipboard selection:
- c = clipboard
- p = primary (X11)
- s = secondary
- 0-7 = cut buffers

### Clipboard API

pub struct Clipboard {
    caps: TerminalCapabilities,
}

impl Clipboard {
    /// Check if OSC 52 is supported
    pub fn is_available(&self) -> bool {
        self.caps.osc52
    }
    
    /// Set clipboard content
    pub fn set(&self, content: &str, writer: &mut impl Write) -> io::Result<()> {
        if !self.is_available() {
            return Err(io::Error::new(
                io::ErrorKind::Unsupported,
                "OSC 52 not available"
            ));
        }
        
        let encoded = base64::encode(content);
        write!(writer, "\x1b]52;c;{}\x07", encoded)?;
        writer.flush()
    }
    
    /// Clear clipboard
    pub fn clear(&self, writer: &mut impl Write) -> io::Result<()> {
        write!(writer, "\x1b]52;c;\x07")?;
        writer.flush()
    }
}

### Terminal Compatibility
OSC 52 support varies:
- ✅ iTerm2, kitty, alacritty, WezTerm, foot
- ⚠️ tmux (needs set-clipboard on)
- ⚠️ screen (needs clipboard support)
- ❌ Many terminal emulators disable by default

### Detection Strategy
1. Check known terminal from TERM/TERM_PROGRAM
2. Check tmux/screen allow-passthrough
3. Attempt set and check for response (risky)
4. Default: assume unsupported

### Size Limits
Most terminals limit OSC 52 payload:
- Common limit: 74994 bytes (base64)
- Split large content or fail gracefully

### Fallback Options
When OSC 52 unavailable:
- Fall back to external clipboard tool (feature: clipboard-fallback)
  - macOS: pbcopy/pbpaste
  - Linux: xclip, xsel, wl-copy
  - Windows: clip.exe
- Or return error for application to handle

## Tests Required
- [ ] OSC 52 sequence generation
- [ ] Base64 encoding correct
- [ ] Size limit handling
- [ ] Clear clipboard works
- [ ] Capability detection
- [ ] Fallback to external tools
- [ ] Error handling when unavailable

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] OSC 52 set clipboard
- [ ] Capability detection
- [ ] Size limit enforcement
- [ ] Clear clipboard
- [ ] Optional external fallback
- [ ] Feature gate: clipboard

## Location: ftui-extras crate (feature = "clipboard")

Keep them taking `&mut Buffer` and have callers pass `&mut frame.buffer`.
This is cleaner than passing Frame unnecessarily.

**For helper functions that DO need Frame features:**
Update to take `&mut Frame` and update all callers.

## Analysis Required

For each helper:
1. Does it need hit_grid? → needs Frame
2. Does it need cursor? → needs Frame
3. Does it need degradation? → needs Frame
4. None of the above? → keep Buffer

## Verification

- `cargo check -p ftui-widgets` must pass
- No function signature mismatches

title: Demo Showcase: Terminal Capability Explorer
description:
## Background

Terminal capability detection is messy:
- TERM lies
- multiplexers change behavior
- color support varies
- sync output may or may not exist

FrankenTUI already does capability detection conservatively. This screen makes those decisions visible and debuggable, and turns them into a compelling demo.

## UX / Core Interactions

- Capability matrix view:
  - detected capability: yes/no/unknown
  - confidence (if modeled)
  - evidence (TERM/COLORTERM/tty, known terminal list, etc.)
  - fallback behavior currently active

- Optional "what if" panel:
  - allow simulating capability profiles (ties into bd-k4lj)
  - show how behavior changes (e.g., sync output on/off)

Suggested keybindings:
- Tab: switch views (matrix / evidence ledger / simulation)
- Enter: expand details for a capability

## Architecture Notes

- Data source: ftui-core terminal capability detection.
- Export: ability to emit the current capability set as JSON (useful for bug reports).
- Keep presentation deterministic; do not rely on unstable environment ordering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Displays all major capabilities FrankenTUI cares about (mouse, focus, color depth, sync output, etc.).
- For each capability, provides:
  - the current decision
  - the fallback behavior
  - a human-readable reason

Additionally (project-wide standards):
- Alien Artifact: define invariants + failure modes; if heuristics exist, specify an explainable decision rule (evidence ledger / Bayes factors where applicable)
- Extreme Optimization: baseline -> profile -> opportunity matrix; for each perf change include an isomorphism proof + golden output checksums
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures; add property tests for core invariants where applicable
- E2E: scripts with verbose JSONL logging (env, capabilities, timings, seed, checksums) + deterministic mode

## Alien Artifact Upgrades (Concrete)

- Evidence ledger view:
  - record evidence contributions and show a compact explanation per capability
- Bayesian framing (optional):
  - represent capability detection as a posterior over states
  - use explicit loss to decide conservative enable/disable

## Extreme Optimization

- Rendering this screen must be cheap (it should not distort the very metrics it displays).

title: Document Windows v1 Limitations and Compatibility
description:
# Document Windows v1 Limitations and Compatibility

## Background
Plan Section ADR-004 and Section 0.6.6 require a "Windows limitations" section that is honest about what works and what doesn't.

## Document Location
`docs/WINDOWS.md` or `docs/compatibility/windows.md`

## Required Content

### 1. Supported Features (v1)
Document what IS expected to work on Windows:
- [ ] Raw mode enter/exit and cleanup on panic
- [ ] Key input handling (basic keys, modifiers)
- [ ] Resize events
- [ ] Basic mouse support (where Crossterm supports it)
- [ ] Color output:
  - 16 colors (always)
  - 256 colors (Windows Terminal, modern ConHost)
  - TrueColor (Windows Terminal)

### 2. Known Limitations (v1)
Be honest about what MAY NOT work or is best-effort:
- [ ] DEC synchronized output (mode 2026): Not widely supported
- [ ] OSC 8 hyperlinks: Windows Terminal only (cmd.exe/ConHost: no)
- [ ] Bracketed paste: Varies by terminal
- [ ] Focus events: May not work in all environments
- [ ] Kitty keyboard protocol: Limited support
- [ ] Scroll-region optimization: Behavior varies
- [ ] Mouse SGR mode: May fall back to legacy encoding

### 3. Terminal Compatibility Matrix (Windows)
| Feature | Windows Terminal | cmd.exe | ConHost | PowerShell |
|---------|------------------|---------|---------|------------|
| TrueColor | ✓ | ✗ | ~ | depends |
| OSC 8 Links | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ~ |
| Mouse | ✓ | ✗ | ~ | ~ |
| Sync Output | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |

### 4. Configuration Recommendations
- Recommend Windows Terminal for best experience
- Document any required ConPTY settings
- Explain TERM/COLORTERM environment handling on Windows

### 5. Troubleshooting Section
Common Windows issues:
- "Colors don't show": Check terminal emulator
- "Mouse not working": Enable in terminal settings
- "Cleanup not working": Known ConHost limitation
- "Unicode display broken": Font/codepage issues

### 6. Future Improvements
List what may improve in future versions:
- Better ConHost support
- WSL integration notes
- Specific terminal emulator enhancements

## Cross-References
- Link to ADR-004 for decision context
- Link to terminal compatibility matrix (bd-1un)
- Link to capability detection implementation

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] WINDOWS.md exists with all sections
- [ ] Honest about limitations (not marketing fluff)
- [ ] Tested on actual Windows systems
- [ ] Includes actionable troubleshooting
- [ ] Linked from main README.md

## Location
`docs/WINDOWS.md`

title: Integration tests use separate lock from unit tests

3. Have integration tests use the shared lock infrastructure

Test isolation failures, potential flaky tests when running full suite

title: Implement snapshot/golden testing framework
description:
TESTING - SNAPSHOT TESTS

## Background
Snapshot testing captures expected Buffer output and compares against future runs. Essential for preventing visual regressions and validating rendering correctness.

## Technical Requirements
- Snapshot capture:
  - Buffer → text representation (with ANSI or stripped)
  - Buffer → binary serialization

- Update workflow:
  - BLESS=1 env var to update snapshots

## Design Rationale
Visual output is hard to assert with unit tests. Snapshots capture 'known good' output and flag any changes for human review. Prevents subtle rendering regressions.

title: Embedded Terminal Widget
description:
## Overview
Provide a widget that renders a fully functional terminal emulator inside the TUI.

## Rationale
- Enables terminal-in-terminal scenarios (IDE-like interfaces)
- Shell output can be embedded in dashboards
- Critical for building terminal multiplexers
- Enables live command execution with output capture

## Core Components
1. **PTY Integration**: Spawn and manage pseudo-terminal
2. **ANSI Parser**: Parse output stream from child process
3. **Terminal State Machine**: Track cursor, scrollback, modes
4. **Input Forwarding**: Pass keystrokes to child process
5. **Resize Handling**: Propagate SIGWINCH to child

## Implementation Strategy
- Build on ftui-pty crate
- Create TerminalEmulator widget in ftui-extras
- Use vte or similar crate for ANSI parsing
- Implement subset of xterm functionality

## Supported Features (MVP)
- 256-color output
- Cursor movement and positioning
- Basic scrollback buffer
- Line wrapping
- Common escape sequences

## Out of Scope (Initial)
- Mouse passthrough
- Sixel/iTerm2 images
- Unicode combining characters

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests for ANSI parser
- Integration tests with real shells (bash, zsh)
- Snapshot tests for terminal output rendering
- Stress tests for rapid output

## Success Criteria
- Can run bash inside the widget
- vim and htop render correctly
- No performance degradation for parent app

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.


## E2E Plan
- Provide/extend an E2E script that exercises the feature end-to-end in PTY (where applicable).
- Logging: verbose JSONL with env/capabilities + per-step timings + seed + checksums; include a summary at end.
- On failure: print reproduction command and point to artifacts directory.

title: Implement Text type with styled spans
description:
# Implement Text type (Segment/Span collection)

## Background
Plan Section 0.4 and Appendix D establish a text pipeline:
- `Segment` is the atomic styled unit (Cow<str> where possible)
- higher-level markup/text APIs produce segments
- widgets/layout paint segments into `Frame`/`Buffer`

Text must support:
- ergonomic construction for app authors
- deterministic style application
- width-correct wrapping/truncation (ZWJ/emoji/combining)
- fast paths for ASCII-heavy workloads (see bd-v6y)

## Proposed model
A `Text` is an owned collection of segments (or spans) plus helpers.

Option A (generic, most faithful to plan):
```rust
pub struct Text<'a> {
    segments: Vec<Segment<'a>>,
}
```

Option B (ergonomic, no lifetimes in app code):
- `Text` stores `Segment<'static>` (Cow<'static, str>)
- constructors accept `&str` and own when needed

We should pick the option that keeps the public API pleasant while preserving the plan's "borrow when you can" benefit for string literals.

## Required behaviors
- Append/push spans/segments
- Apply a base style (inheritance) deterministically
- Split into lines (preserve styles)
- Truncate to width with ellipsis (width-correct)
- Wrap to width (width-correct)

## Width correctness
- ASCII fast path must be correct and allocation-free (bd-v6y)
- Non-ASCII path must use Unicode width + (ideally) grapheme segmentation
- Must not wrap mid-grapheme for common emoji/ZWJ sequences

## Tests
- Line splitting preserves styles across `\n`
- Truncation is width-correct for:
  - ASCII
  - CJK wide chars
  - emoji/ZWJ sequences
- Wrapping is width-correct and stable across widths

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `Text` type exists with an ergonomic builder API.
- [ ] Wrapping/truncation is width-correct.
- [ ] ASCII fast path is integrated (bd-v6y).
- [ ] Unit tests cover ASCII, CJK, emoji/ZWJ cases.

## Location
`ftui-text` crate

title: Pi-style Keybinding UX & Input Semantics
description:
Define and implement a Pi-inspired keybinding model (Ctrl+C clears input, Esc cancels task, Esc Esc toggles tree) that avoids destructive conflicts in interactive UIs built on FrankenTUI.

## Success Criteria
- Epic delivers a cohesive user-visible capability: Pi-style Keybinding UX & Input Semantics
- Child tasks are not just implemented; each has unit tests + E2E scripts with verbose JSONL logs and deterministic fixtures
- Graceful degradation tiers are specified (capabilities, fallbacks, safety) and validated in tests


## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.


## Testing Plan
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures.
- Property tests: invariants (idempotence, monotonicity, determinism) where applicable.
- Fuzz tests: parsers/state machines and any input-facing logic.
- Determinism: fixed seeds/time-freeze; snapshot fixtures must be stable.

All 8 child beads closed: Policy spec (bd-2vne.1), Key sequence interpreter (bd-2vne.2), Harness integration (bd-2vne.3), Tree view overlay (bd-2vne.4), Tests & docs (bd-2vne.5), ActionMapper (bd-2vne.6), Config surface (bd-2vne.7), E2E PTY tests (bd-2vne.8). Keybinding model: Ctrl+C clears/cancels/quits, Esc clears/cancels/closes, Esc Esc toggles tree. 69 unit tests + 8 E2E tests.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Background
- User feedback from X praises Pi’s keybinding model: Ctrl+C clears prompt first; Esc cancels current task; Esc Esc opens a tree view. It avoids the common conflict where Ctrl+C both clears input and interrupts the agent.
- FrankenTUI is a kernel, but the harness and any agent-style app should model best‑in‑class interaction semantics. This epic targets a reference implementation that downstream apps can copy.

Goals
- Define a deterministic, documented keybinding policy that resolves the Ctrl+C vs interrupt ambiguity.
- Support multi-key sequences (Esc Esc) in a way that doesn’t regress normal Esc behavior.
- Ensure the model is testable and works in both inline and alt-screen modes.
- Keep behavior optional and configurable so embedding apps can opt out.

Non‑Goals
- Do not mandate global keybindings for all FrankenTUI apps; provide reference behavior + tooling, not a hard requirement.
- Do not change core terminal handling in ways that break existing examples without an explicit migration.

Risks / Considerations
- Esc is overloaded in terminals; detecting a double-Esc without blocking single-Esc requires a small timing window and careful event buffering.
- Ctrl+C should be treated as “clear input” only when input is non-empty; otherwise it should fall through to “interrupt / quit” behavior (configurable).
- Inline mode + log streaming must not reorder output when toggling views (tree overlay). Ensure the one-writer rule is preserved.

Deliverables
- A written keybinding policy and state machine.
- A sequence/chord interpreter (either in runtime utility or harness-local) with tests.
- A harness view showing the tree toggle and task cancellation semantics.
- Documentation so future selves understand intent and rationale.

description:
# Create comprehensive E2E test suite

## Background
End-to-end tests verify the complete rendering pipeline from widget construction through terminal output. Must test real terminal interactions, not mocked abstractions.

## Technical Requirements

### E2E Test Infrastructure
- `scripts/e2e_test.sh` master script
- Individual test scripts per feature area
- JSON output for CI parsing
- Verbose mode with full trace output
- Exit codes: 0=pass, 1=fail, 2=skip

### Test Categories

#### 1. Rendering Tests (scripts/e2e/render/)
- `hello_world.sh` - Basic text output
- `colors.sh` - Full color palette rendering
- `unicode.sh` - Emoji, CJK, RTL text
- `styles.sh` - Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough
- `hyperlinks.sh` - OSC 8 hyperlink rendering

#### 2. Layout Tests (scripts/e2e/layout/)
- `flex_horizontal.sh` - Row layout constraints
- `flex_vertical.sh` - Column layout constraints
- `grid.sh` - 2D grid positioning
- `nested.sh` - Complex nested layouts
- `resize.sh` - Terminal resize handling

#### 3. Widget Tests (scripts/e2e/widgets/)
- `block.sh` - Borders, titles, padding
- `paragraph.sh` - Text wrapping, alignment
- `table.sh` - Column sizing, selection
- `list.sh` - Selection, scrolling
- `input.sh` - Text entry, cursor

#### 4. Input Tests (scripts/e2e/input/)
- `keyboard.sh` - Key events, modifiers
- `mouse.sh` - Click, scroll, drag
- `paste.sh` - Bracketed paste mode
- `focus.sh` - Focus in/out events

#### 5. Integration Tests (scripts/e2e/integration/)
- `full_app.sh` - Complete application lifecycle
- `inline_mode.sh` - Scrollback-native rendering
- `alt_screen.sh` - Alternate screen buffer
- `raw_mode.sh` - Raw terminal mode transitions

### Test Script Template
```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../common.sh"

TEST_NAME="render/hello_world"
log_start "${TEST_NAME}"

# Run the test binary
output=$(cargo run --example hello_world 2>&1) || fail "Example failed to run"

# Verify output
assert_contains "${output}" "Hello"
assert_no_errors "${output}"

log_pass "${TEST_NAME}"
```

### Logging Requirements
All test scripts must provide detailed logging:

**Start Phase:**
- Timestamp (ISO 8601)
- Test name and category
- Environment info (TERM, COLORTERM, shell)
- Configuration parameters

**Progress Phase:**
- Major checkpoint announcements
- Timing for each phase
- Resource usage snapshots

**Failure Phase:**
- Full context dump
- Expected vs actual comparison
- Stack trace if available
- Terminal state capture
- Reproduction command

**Success Phase:**
- Duration breakdown
- Resource usage summary

title: FrankenTermJS: xterm.js-killer parity + beyond
description:
North Star
- FrankenTermJS replaces xterm.js as the default web terminal engine + renderer.
- Goals: better correctness, determinism, and performance (WebGPU-first), with a smaller/cleaner API and no legacy baggage.

What This Epic Covers
- Remote terminal mode: consume VT/ANSI byte streams (like xterm.js) and render correctly in the browser.
- Local ftui-web mode: continue supporting patch-based rendering from ftui-web/ShowcaseRunner.
- UX parity: scrollback, selection, copy/paste, search, links, resize, IME, accessibility.
- Compliance: implement the VT subset we claim (see docs/spec/frankenterm-vt-support-matrix.md) with conformance fixtures + differential testing.

Guiding Principles
- Rust-first: parsing/state machine/selection/scrollback live in Rust/WASM, JS is a thin host shim.
- Deterministic: identical inputs + time + capability profile => identical output; every nondeterminism is explicit and logged.
- Bounded memory: no unbounded buffers/queues; explicit flow control for remote mode.
- WebGPU-first: GPU-accelerated, but with graceful fallback when WebGPU is missing.

Key Existing Artifacts
- Browser surface API: crates/frankenterm-web/src/wasm.rs (FrankenTermWeb).
- WebGPU renderer: crates/frankenterm-web/src/renderer.rs.
- Terminal engine building blocks: crates/frankenterm-core/* (Parser/Grid/Scrollback/Selection/ReplyEngine).
- Contracts/specs: docs/spec/frankenterm-websocket-protocol.md, docs/spec/frankenterm-vt-support-matrix.md, docs/spec/frankenterm-term-capability-profile.md.

Non-Goals
- Recreating xterm.js addon/plugin system. We will provide first-party feature modules behind stable API methods and explicit capability flags.

## Success Criteria
- Remote terminal mode, UX parity, and conformance tracks are all implemented with passing quality gates.
- Release-readiness artifacts (scorecard, matrix, rollout checklist) are complete and auditable.
- Performance, determinism, and bounded-resource requirements are met in benchmark and stress suites.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
- Every child feature and task in this epic defines and satisfies comprehensive unit tests for implemented behavior and edge cases.
- Every user-critical workflow has deterministic end-to-end scripts in CI, including remote attach, scrollback/navigation/search, selection/clipboard, accessibility/IME, renderer fallback, advanced host APIs, and addon-parity workflows (fit, web-links, image, progress, ligatures, web-font lifecycle).
- All validation pipelines emit structured logs (JSONL) with timestamps, correlation IDs, and failure context sufficient for deterministic replay/debugging.
- Parity and readiness artifacts are complete: xterm.js parity scorecard, browser support matrix, conformance/differential/fuzz gates, security/reliability runbooks, and final go/no-go checklist.
- WebGPU-first performance and bounded-resource requirements are demonstrated with benchmark + stress evidence and enforced regression gates.

title: feature(frankenterm-web): remote VT mode (feed bytes + terminal replies)

title: [EPIC] Widget Trait API Migration: Buffer → Frame
description:
## Background

The Widget trait in ftui-widgets was changed from:
```rust
fn render(&self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer);
```
to:
```rust
fn render(&self, area: Rect, frame: &mut Frame);
```

This change was DIRECTIONALLY CORRECT but POORLY EXECUTED - the trait signature was changed without updating the ~50 widget implementations, leaving the codebase in a broken state.

## Why Frame is Better Than Buffer

Frame provides capabilities that modern TUI widgets need:

1. **buffer: Buffer** - The cell grid (same as before)
2. **pool: &'a mut GraphemePool** - String interning for efficiency
3. **hit_grid: Option<HitGrid>** - Mouse click region registration
4. **cursor_position: Option<(u16, u16)>** - Cursor tracking for inputs
5. **cursor_visible: bool** - Cursor visibility control
6. **degradation: DegradationLevel** - Performance budget adaptation

Without Frame access, widgets CANNOT:
- Register clickable regions for mouse interaction
- Set cursor position (critical for text inputs)
- Adapt rendering based on performance budget
- Use efficient string interning

## Design Decision: Frame is Correct

This is NOT a backwards compatibility issue (we don't care about that per AGENTS.md). 
Frame IS the right abstraction because:

1. **Industry precedent**: Ratatui (dominant Rust TUI framework) uses Frame in Widget trait
2. **Feature requirements**: Hit testing, cursor, degradation are all needed
3. **Future extensibility**: Frame can grow without changing Widget trait again

## The Problem

~50 widget implementations still use `buf: &mut Buffer` instead of `frame: &mut Frame`.
This is a mechanical migration that needs to be done ATOMICALLY and CORRECTLY.

## Success Criteria

- All widgets compile with the new Frame-based signature
- All widgets that need Frame features (hit testing, cursor, degradation) use them
- All widgets that just need buffer access use `frame.buffer`
- All existing tests pass
- No regressions in functionality
close_reason: All widgets migrated to Frame-based API. Verified: 38 Frame implementations, 0 Buffer implementations. Workspace compiles clean.

title: Implement StyleSheet registry for named styles
description:
PHASE 4 - STYLESHEET REGISTRY

## Background
StyleSheet provides named style registration similar to CSS classes. Enables theme-able applications and consistent style reuse without hardcoding colors.

## Technical Requirements
- StyleSheet struct with HashMap<StyleId, Style>
- StyleId: either interned string or u32 index
- Register named styles: stylesheet.define('error', Style::new().fg(RED).bold())
- Lookup by name: stylesheet.get('error')
- Style composition: stylesheet.compose(['base', 'error']) merges in order
- Default styles for common semantic names (error, warning, info, success, muted)

## Design Rationale
Named styles decouple visual appearance from widget logic. Themes can override the stylesheet without changing widget code. Matches patterns from Textual/Rich.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] StyleSheet with define/get/compose API
- [ ] StyleId type (string or integer based on perf analysis)
- [ ] Thread-safe for read access (RwLock or immutable after init)
- [ ] Default semantic style set
- [ ] Style merging for composition
- [ ] Clear error handling for missing styles

## Integration Points
- Widgets reference styles by name
- Theme loading populates stylesheet
- Buffer.set_style() accepts Style or StyleId

## Location: ftui-style crate
close_reason: Implemented StyleSheet registry with thread-safe access, compose API, and 21 tests
