title: Demo Showcase: Virtualized List + Fuzzy Search
description:
## Background

A virtualized list is one of the highest ROI widgets in any UI system. It is also a performance trap:
- large datasets (10k-1M)
- variable row heights
- fast scroll + search-as-you-type

This screen proves FrankenTUI can do large-data interaction with strict performance budgets and deterministic rendering.

## UX / Core Interactions

- List of many items (start with 10k) with stable IDs.
- Keyboard navigation (up/down, page up/down, home/end).
- Search-as-you-type fuzzy search:
  - highlight matches
  - show match score
  - show total results
- Optional: toggle variable-height rows (wrap or multi-line previews).

Suggested keybindings:
- /: focus search input
- Esc: clear search
- J/K or arrows: navigate
- G / Shift+G: top/bottom (optional)

## Architecture Notes

- Rendering must be virtualized: only paint visible rows.
- For variable heights:
  - use bd-2zbk.7 (Fenwick/segment tree) to map scroll offset -> row index
- For allocation control:
  - use bd-2zbk.8 (cache-aware layout + allocation budget)

- Fuzzy search:
  - start with a known algorithm (e.g., fzy-style scoring) with deterministic tie-breaking
  - keep a fast ASCII path; avoid heap churn per keystroke

## Acceptance Criteria

- Scroll remains smooth with 10k items.
- Search remains responsive as the query updates.
- Deterministic ordering:
  - equal scores tie-break by stable ID

Additionally (project-wide standards):
- Alien Artifact: define invariants + failure modes; if heuristics exist, specify an explainable decision rule (evidence ledger / Bayes factors where applicable)
- Extreme Optimization: baseline -> profile -> opportunity matrix; for each perf change include an isomorphism proof + golden output checksums
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures; add property tests for core invariants where applicable
- E2E: scripts with verbose JSONL logging (env, capabilities, timings, seed, checksums) + deterministic mode

## Alien Artifact Upgrades (Concrete)

- Variable height correctness proof:
  - define invariants for prefix sums / tree structure
  - property tests compare Fenwick/segment tree queries against a slow reference

## Extreme Optimization

- Define budgets:
  - scroll step under p95 < 1ms at 80x24
  - search update under p95 < X ms for 10k items
- Profile before optimizing and keep golden outputs for ordering.

title: Constraint-Based Layout Hints via Directives
description:
## Goal
Allow users to annotate Mermaid source with layout hints via %%{...}%% directives that influence the Sugiyama layout. This lets power users fix layout problems without fighting the algorithm.

## Supported Constraints
1. Same-rank: %%{ ftui:rank=same A, B, C }%% — force nodes to the same layer
2. Min-length: %%{ ftui:minlen=3 A-->B }%% — force minimum rank span for an edge
3. Pin position: %%{ ftui:pin A x=100 y=50 }%% — fix a node at specific coordinates
4. Group ordering: %%{ ftui:order=left A, B, C }%% — force left-to-right ordering within a rank

## Why
- Mermaid.js has implicit same-rank support; DOT has full rank constraints. Users expect some layout control.
- The parser already handles %%{...}%% directives (token type Directive in the lexer).
- Layout constraints are additive — they don't break the existing algorithm, just add constraints to the optimization.

## Implementation
1. Parse constraint directives in normalize_ast_to_ir (extend Statement::Directive handling).
2. Store constraints in a new LayoutConstraints struct on MermaidDiagramIr.
3. In diagram_layout.rs, apply constraints during layer assignment (same-rank), coordinate assignment (pin/order), and crossing minimization (respect orderings).
4. Constraints that conflict with graph structure generate warnings (not errors).

## Files
- crates/ftui-extras/src/mermaid.rs (parse constraint directives)
- crates/ftui-extras/src/diagram_layout.rs (apply constraints in layout)

## Tests
- Unit: parse same-rank directive → correct LayoutConstraints
- Unit: same-rank constraint produces equal layer assignment
- Unit: min-length constraint produces correct rank span
- Snapshot: constrained vs unconstrained layout of same graph
close_reason: done

title: Widget State Persistence
description:
## Overview
Enable widgets to save and restore their state across application sessions.

## Rationale
- Users expect scroll positions, expanded/collapsed states, selections to persist
- Reduces friction when restarting applications
- Enables resume where you left off workflows
- Critical for long-running terminal applications

## Core Components
1. **Stateful Trait**: Opt-in trait for widgets with serializable state
2. **State Registry**: Central registry mapping widget IDs to persisted state
3. **Storage Backend**: Pluggable backend (file, memory, custom)
4. **Versioned State**: Schema versioning for backward compatibility
5. **Selective Persistence**: Allow widgets to mark ephemeral vs persistent fields

## Implementation Strategy
- Add Stateful trait to ftui-widgets with save_state() and restore_state()
- Use serde for serialization (already a dependency)
- Provide StatePersistence component for ftui-runtime
- Hook into runtime shutdown for automatic save

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests for each widgets state serialization
- Integration tests for save/restore cycle
- Migration tests for state version upgrades
- Crash-recovery tests (partial writes)

## Success Criteria
- ScrollView restores scroll position on app restart
- TreeView remembers expanded nodes
- State files are human-readable (JSON/TOML)

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.


## E2E Plan
- Provide/extend an E2E script that exercises the feature end-to-end in PTY (where applicable).
- Logging: verbose JSONL with env/capabilities + per-step timings + seed + checksums; include a summary at end.
- On failure: print reproduction command and point to artifacts directory.

title: Diagram Type: Gantt
description:
Background
- Gantt charts are common in project planning and demos.

Scope
- Parse gantt syntax (sections, tasks, dates, dependencies, milestones).
- Respect dateFormat/axisFormat where supported; warn otherwise.
- Layout timeline with adaptive time scale to available width.
- Render bars with labels and progress markers.

Considerations
- Scale must be chosen deterministically based on width.
- Avoid label collision; allow ellipsis.

Tests / Validation
- Unit tests for scale selection and bar placement.
- Snapshot tests for multiple time ranges.
- PTY E2E logs: diagram_type=gantt, size, tier, warnings.

Success Criteria
- Gantt charts render clearly at 80x24 and scale up gracefully.
notes:
Design plan (no code yet; files reserved by others):

Gantt implementation outline
1) AST: extend parse_gantt to handle `dateFormat` and `axisFormat` lines (new Statement variants, e.g., GanttDateFormat { format }, GanttAxisFormat { format }). Unsupported formats -> warning but still store raw string.
2) IR: add optional typed sub-IR to MermaidDiagramIr (docs/spec mentions typed sub-IRs). Proposed `gantt: Option<GanttIr>`, with title, sections, tasks, axis/date formats.
3) Meta parsing: parse GanttTask.meta CSV into structured fields: optional status (done/active/crit/milestone), optional id, optional start date (YYYY-MM-DD), optional duration (Nd / Nw), optional dependency `after <id>`. Any unrecognized token preserved in `raw_tags` with warning.
4) Timeline: compute task start/end deterministically. Anchored tasks with explicit start date use that; `after` tasks start at end of referenced id (warn if missing). If start date missing and no `after`, assign sequentially after prior task within section.
5) Scale selection: derive total day span; choose tick unit (day/week/month) based on available width. Deterministic thresholds (e.g., if days<=width- label_col, unit=day; else if weeks<=width-..., unit=week; else month).

title: Cross-Platform Testing: Windows and macOS Validation
description:
## Background

README.md mentions Windows support is tracked in docs/WINDOWS.md and is still being validated. FrankenTUI should work consistently across platforms.

## Platforms to Test

1. **Linux** (primary) - Already well-tested
2. **macOS** - Terminal.app, iTerm2, Ghostty
3. **Windows** - Windows Terminal, ConEmu, cmd.exe

## Test Matrix

| Platform | Terminal | Expected Support |
|----------|----------|------------------|
| Linux | kitty, alacritty, ghostty | Full |
| Linux | tmux, screen | Degraded (mux passthrough) |
| macOS | Terminal.app | Degraded (limited features) |
| macOS | iTerm2 | Full |
| macOS | Ghostty | Full |
| Windows | Windows Terminal | Full |
| Windows | ConEmu | Full |
| Windows | cmd.exe | Degraded |

## Tests Required

### Terminal Capabilities Detection
```rust
#[test]
#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]
fn windows_terminal_detected() {
    std::env::set_var("WT_SESSION", "1");
    let caps = TerminalCapabilities::detect();
    assert!(caps.true_color);
}

#[test]
#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
fn iterm2_detected() {
    std::env::set_var("TERM_PROGRAM", "iTerm.app");
    let caps = TerminalCapabilities::detect();
    assert!(caps.true_color);
}
```

### Cross-Platform E2E Script

Create `scripts/cross_platform_e2e.sh`:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run on CI with matrix strategy

echo "Platform: $(uname -s)"
echo "Terminal: $TERM"

# Build
cargo build -p ftui-demo-showcase --release

# Run headless tests
cargo test -p ftui-core -- --nocapture
cargo test -p ftui-render -- --nocapture

# Snapshot tests (should be identical across platforms)
cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase --test screen_snapshots
```

## CI Configuration

Add matrix builds to .github/workflows/ci.yml:
```yaml
cross-platform:
  strategy:
    matrix:
      os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
  runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly
    - run: cargo test -p ftui-core
    - run: cargo test -p ftui-render
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Linux tests passing
- [ ] macOS tests passing
- [ ] Windows tests passing
- [ ] CI matrix configured
- [ ] Platform-specific capability detection tested
- [ ] Snapshot tests identical across platforms
- [ ] docs/WINDOWS.md updated with validated status

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.


## Testing Plan
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures.
- Property tests: invariants (idempotence, monotonicity, determinism) where applicable.
- Fuzz tests: parsers/state machines and any input-facing logic.
- Determinism: fixed seeds/time-freeze; snapshot fixtures must be stable.

title: Text Effects: Particle Dissolve / Materialize
description:
## Background
Particle dissolve creates dramatic transitions where text breaks into fragments that drift away, or materializes from scattered particles. Builds on existing SparkleField infrastructure.

## Implementation

Add DissolveMode enum:
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub enum DissolveMode {
    #[default]
    Dissolve,    // Text breaks apart, drifts away
    Materialize, // Particles gather into text
    Explode,     // Fast outward burst from center
    Implode,     // Fast inward gather to center
}
```

Add TextEffect variant:
```rust
TextEffect::ParticleDissolve {
    progress: f64,        // 0.0 = solid text, 1.0 = fully particles
    mode: DissolveMode,   
    speed: f64,           // Particle drift speed
    gravity: f64,         // 0.0 = float, 1.0 = fall downward
    seed: u64,            // Deterministic particle paths
}
```

### Particle Behavior:
```rust
struct Particle {
    origin: (f64, f64),     // Original text position
    offset: (f64, f64),     // Current offset from origin
    char: char,             // Original character
    color: PackedRgba,      // Inherited from text color
}

// Particles inherit color from the text effect chain
// e.g., Rainbow + Dissolve = rainbow-colored particles
```

### Rendering by Mode:

| Mode | progress=0 | progress=0.5 | progress=1 |
|------|------------|--------------|------------|
| Dissolve | Solid text | Half scattered | All particles |
| Materialize | All particles | Half gathered | Solid text |
| Explode | Solid text | Burst outward | Distant particles |
| Implode | Distant particles | Gathering | Solid text |

### Particle Characters:
Default particle chars: `['·', '∙', '•', '*']` - selected based on distance from origin (closer = larger).

### Color Inheritance:
Particles inherit their color from whatever color the text would have at that position. This means gradients, color cycling, etc. all work with dissolve.

## Files
crates/ftui-extras/src/text_effects.rs

## Unit Tests (REQUIRED)
- test_dissolve_progress_0_solid: All original chars visible
- test_dissolve_progress_1_scattered: No chars at original positions
- test_materialize_reverses: progress 0->1 gathers particles
- test_explode_from_center: Particles move away from text center
- test_implode_to_center: Particles converge on center
- test_gravity_affects_y: Particles drift downward with gravity
- test_particle_inherits_color: Gradient text = gradient particles
- test_seed_deterministic: Same seed = same particle paths

## Visual Tests
- Snapshot 'DISSOLVE' at progress 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0
- Snapshot Explode burst pattern
- Snapshot gradient text dissolving (particles should be colorful)

title: Terminal Capability Auto-Upgrade with Safe Probing
DOT/GraphViz Format Import
description:
## Goal
Add a DOT (GraphViz) parser that produces the same MermaidDiagramIr, enabling all existing layout and rendering code to work with DOT input. DOT is the other dominant text-based graph format used by many tools (doxygen, profilers, dependency analyzers, terraform).

## Why
- Broadens utility significantly: any tool that outputs DOT can now be visualized in the terminal.
- The IR is already format-agnostic — a DOT parser just needs to produce IrNodes, IrEdges, IrClusters.
- DOT is simpler to parse than Mermaid (well-defined grammar, no ambiguity).
- Enables workflows like: cargo depgraph | ftui-diagram (visualize Rust crate dependencies).

## DOT Subset to Support (v1)
- graph/digraph declarations
- Node declarations with labels, shapes, colors
- Edge declarations (-> for digraph, -- for graph)
- subgraph/cluster declarations
- Basic attributes: label, shape, color, style, fillcolor
- DOT shape → NodeShape mapping: box→Rect, diamond→Diamond, circle→Circle, ellipse→Rounded, etc.

## DOT Features to Skip (v1)
- HTML labels, record shapes, rank constraints, edge ports, DOT layout hints (pos/neato)
- These can be added later; the basic pipeline is the priority.

## Implementation
- New module: crates/ftui-extras/src/dot_parser.rs (or add to mermaid.rs behind cfg)
- Entry point: parse_dot(input: &str) → Result<MermaidDiagramIr, ...>
- Reuse IrNode, IrEdge, IrCluster, IrLabel types from mermaid.rs
- Auto-detect format: if input starts with "graph" or "digraph", use DOT parser; if "flowchart"/"graph TD"/etc., use Mermaid parser.

## Files
- crates/ftui-extras/src/dot_parser.rs (NEW file — genuinely new parser, not a variation)
- crates/ftui-extras/src/lib.rs (feature-gate and export)
- crates/ftui-extras/src/mermaid_render.rs (auto-detect input format)

## Tests
- Unit: parse simple digraph → correct IR nodes/edges
- Unit: parse subgraph → correct clusters
- Unit: DOT shape attributes → correct NodeShape
- Snapshot: cargo dependency graph (10-20 nodes) rendered from DOT
- E2E: round-trip DOT→IR→render produces deterministic output

title: Semantic Events: Widget Migration Guide and Examples
description:
## Task

Create documentation and examples showing how to use semantic events in widgets.

## Documentation

Create `docs/semantic-events.md`:

1. Overview of semantic vs raw events
2. When to use which
3. Configuration options
4. Migration guide for existing widgets

## Example: List with Double-Click

```rust
enum Msg {
    // Raw events
    Key(KeyEvent),
    Mouse(MouseEvent),
    
    // Semantic events
    ItemClicked(usize),
    ItemDoubleClicked(usize),
    ItemDragged { from: usize, to: usize },
}

impl Message for Msg {
    fn from_semantic(event: SemanticEvent) -> Option<Self> {
        match event {
            SemanticEvent::DoubleClick { pos, .. } => {
                // Convert position to item index
                Some(Msg::ItemDoubleClicked(pos.y as usize))
            }
            SemanticEvent::DragEnd { start, end } => {
                Some(Msg::ItemDragged { 
                    from: start.y as usize, 
                    to: end.y as usize

}
```

title: Demo Showcase: Layout Composer
description:
## Background

Layout is the core promise of a TUI framework. FrankenTUI has dedicated layout solvers (flex + grid), and this screen exists to make that power obvious:
- interactive split panes
- live constraints
- deterministic, stable tie-breaking

The demo should feel like a miniature "layout IDE".

## UX / Core Interactions

- A tree of split panes (horizontal/vertical) with resizable dividers.
- Keyboard and mouse resizing.
- A live "constraint inspector" panel showing:
  - the constraints per node
  - computed sizes
  - which constraints are active/binding

Suggested keybindings:
- Arrow keys: move focus between panes
- Ctrl+Arrow: resize focused split
- M: toggle mouse resizing handles
- Tab: cycle inspector modes (raw constraints / computed sizes / slack)

## Architecture Notes

- Model split layout as a small layout graph:
  - nodes: panes
  - edges: splits with ratios/constraints
- Use ftui-layout as the solver; avoid writing a separate solver.
- Render with widgets + a minimal overlay for resize handles.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Resize interactions are smooth and deterministic.
- Constraint responses are monotone and stable:
  - increasing a pane's min width never increases a different pane below its min
  - tie-breaking is deterministic across runs
- Works in both alt-screen and inline mode.

Additionally (project-wide standards):
- Alien Artifact: define invariants + failure modes; if heuristics exist, specify an explainable decision rule (evidence ledger / Bayes factors where applicable)
- Extreme Optimization: baseline -> profile -> opportunity matrix; for each perf change include an isomorphism proof + golden output checksums
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures; add property tests for core invariants where applicable
- E2E: scripts with verbose JSONL logging (env, capabilities, timings, seed, checksums) + deterministic mode
- Layout invariants: feasibility, stable tie-breaking, monotone constraint response; add metamorphic/property tests

## Alien Artifact Upgrades (Concrete)

- Sensitivity analysis:
  - show how a small change in a constraint affects computed sizes (a "derivative" / slack view)
- Counterexample-driven tests:
  - generate random constraint graphs and assert invariants; when a failure occurs, minimize the counterexample and store as a regression fixture

## Extreme Optimization

- Solver performance budgets:
  - define O(n) / O(n log n) expectations for typical graphs
  - add microbench for interactive resize loops

Choose whether to cancel or wait for an in-flight async validation using a principled, latency-aware decision rule.

## Core Idea (Alien Artifact)
Model validation duration T with an online survival distribution. Use hazard h(t) and expected remaining time to evaluate expected loss:
- Survival: S(t) = P(T > t)
- Hazard: h(t) = f(t) / S(t)
- Expected remaining time: E[T - t | T > t] = (1 / S(t)) * integral_{t}^{inf} S(u) du

Decision rule:
Loss(wait) = L_stale * P(T > deadline) + L_delay * E[T - t | T > t]
Loss(cancel) = L_false_invalid + L_recompute
Choose action with smaller expected loss.

## Implementation Notes
- Track completion times per validator (EMA + variance).
- Approximate with a simple parametric family:
  - Weibull: S(t) = exp(-(t/lambda)^k), h(t) = (k/lambda)*(t/lambda)^(k-1)
  - Log-normal if tails are heavy.
- Expose config for loss weights and deadline budget.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Cancels only when expected loss of waiting exceeds cancel loss.
- Uses rolling window stats to adapt to slow validators.
- Never surfaces stale results after a newer input.

## Tests (REQUIRED)
- unit_cancel_when_long_tail: long-tail durations trigger cancel under tight deadline.
- unit_wait_when_fast: low-latency validator is not cancelled.
- unit_deadline_respected: validation state transitions to timeout cleanly.
- property_random_durations: decision matches expected-loss oracle within tolerance.

## E2E (REQUIRED)
- Simulated validators with controlled latency distributions; log decision + rationale.

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.


## Testing Plan
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures.
- Property tests: invariants (idempotence, monotonicity, determinism) where applicable.
- Fuzz tests: parsers/state machines and any input-facing logic.
- Determinism: fixed seeds/time-freeze; snapshot fixtures must be stable.
close_reason: Implemented async validation deadline controller with survival analysis (Weibull distribution) and expected loss calculation. Features: DeadlineConfig, SurvivalStats, DeadlineController, staleness tracking, 17 unit tests all passing.

title: Label Placement + Collision Avoidance
description:
Background
- Edge and node labels are critical to readability.
- Without explicit placement, labels collide with nodes/edges.

Scope
- Label placement for edges (midpoint, offset, leader lines).
- Reserve label bounding boxes in routing grid to prevent collisions.
- Resolve label-label collisions with deterministic offsets.
- Text layout rules for wrapping and truncation under tight widths.
- Optional label spillover to legend area for compact tiers.

Considerations
- Deterministic tie-breakers and stable offsets.
- Keep labels within bounds; prefer readability over exact positioning.
- Log label collision decisions to JSONL.

Tests / Validation
- Unit tests for collision scenarios.
- Snapshot tests covering dense labels.

Success Criteria
- Labels never overlap nodes/edges in supported cases.
- Small screens still show readable labels.
notes:
Opus: Enhanced label placement engine with:

1. **Multi-line text wrapping** in measure_text() - handles explicit newlines + character-boundary wrapping + vertical truncation with max_lines config.
2. **Edge waypoint collision detection** - computes bounding boxes around edge path segments and adds them to occupied rectangles, preventing labels from overlapping edge paths. Classifies colliders as Node/Edge/Label for diagnostics.
3. **Legend spillover** - when offset search exhausts max_offset and legend_enabled=true, labels spill to a legend area below the bounding box with leader lines connecting to anchors.
4. **Leader lines** - when a label is offset beyond leader_line_threshold, a (anchor, target) point pair is recorded for rendering a connecting line.
5. **Label reservation for routing** - label_reservation_rects() exports placed label bounding boxes for integration with RouteGrid obstacle avoidance.
6. **22 new unit tests** covering: multi-line wrapping, vertical truncation, explicit newlines, edge segment rects, margin-aware overlap, edge midpoint edge cases, dense label no-overlap, mixed node+edge label no-overlap, leader lines, legend spillover, reservation rects, direction consistency, deterministic dense collision, and offset candidate completeness.

Quality gates: fmt clean, clippy clean, 119/123 tests pass (4 pre-existing property test failures from bd-3g7lx, unrelated to label placement).

title: Widget API E2E Test Script
description:
## Purpose

Create a comprehensive E2E test script for Widget API verification with detailed logging.

## Script: scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh

```bash
#\!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-/tmp/widget_api_e2e_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

echo "=== Widget API E2E Test Suite ==="
echo "Log directory: $LOG_DIR"
echo "Started at: $(date -Iseconds)"
echo ""

# Step 1: Workspace Build
echo "[1/7] Building workspace..."
cargo build --workspace 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/01_build.log"
echo "✓ Build complete"

# Step 2: Unit Tests
echo "[2/7] Running unit tests..."
RUST_LOG=debug cargo test --workspace 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/02_test.log"
echo "✓ Tests complete"

# Step 3: Clippy
echo "[3/7] Running clippy..."
cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/03_clippy.log"
echo "✓ Clippy complete"

# Step 4: Feature Combinations
echo "[4/7] Testing feature combinations..."
for feature in canvas forms charts; do
  echo "  - ftui-extras --features $feature"
  cargo check -p ftui-extras --features $feature 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG_DIR/04_features.log"
done
echo "✓ Features complete"

# Step 5: Documentation Build
echo "[5/7] Building documentation..."
cargo doc --workspace --no-deps 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/05_doc.log"
echo "✓ Docs complete"

# Step 6: Widget Signature Verification
echo "[6/7] Verifying Widget signatures..."
echo "Checking for old Buffer signatures..."
if rg 'fn render.*buf: &mut Buffer' crates/ftui-widgets/src/*.rs 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "ERROR: Found old Buffer signature\!"
  exit 1
fi
echo "Checking for new Frame signatures..."
rg 'fn render.*frame: &mut Frame' crates/ftui-widgets/src/*.rs | tee "$LOG_DIR/06_signatures.log"
echo "✓ All signatures use Frame"

# Step 7: Snapshot Tests
echo "[7/7] Running snapshot tests..."
cargo test -p ftui-harness --test widget_snapshots 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/07_snapshots.log"
echo "✓ Snapshots complete"

# Summary
echo ""
echo "=== E2E Test Suite Complete ==="
echo "Ended at: $(date -Iseconds)"
echo "Logs: $LOG_DIR/"
ls -la "$LOG_DIR/"
```

## Detailed Logging

Each step writes to a separate log file:
- `01_build.log` - Full cargo build output
- `02_test.log` - All test results with RUST_LOG=debug
- `03_clippy.log` - Clippy warnings/errors
- `04_features.log` - Feature combination checks
- `05_doc.log` - Documentation build output
- `06_signatures.log` - Widget signature grep results
- `07_snapshots.log` - Snapshot test results

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Script is executable and passes on current codebase
- [ ] All logs are captured with timestamps
- [ ] Exit code 0 only if ALL steps pass
- [ ] Any failure provides clear error message and stops execution

The most important architectural question is not “how do we put Asupersync everywhere,” but “where does it actually improve the system?” The earlier code investigation showed a sharp boundary: FrankenTUI’s render kernel benefits from determinism and simple hot loops, while the runtime shell and `doctor_frankentui` benefit from structured concurrency, cancellation, deadlines, bounded blocking work, and deterministic lab testing.

Codify that adoption boundary so implementation work is fast, coherent, and resistant to scope creep.

- Define target seams, no-go zones, API guardrails, feature-flag strategy, shadow-run strategy, and evidence schema.

title: Gradients: Perceptual Sampling (OkLab) + DeltaE Monotonicity
description:
## Goal
Make gradients look visually uniform by interpolating in a perceptual color space (OkLab) and validating monotonic perceptual distance.

## Core Idea (Alien Artifact)
Convert RGB -> OkLab, interpolate linearly in OkLab, convert back to RGB.
This reduces banding and makes vertical/diagonal gradients feel smoother at low terminal color depth.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Interpolation in OkLab yields smoother perceived steps than linear RGB.
- DeltaE (perceptual distance) across steps is monotonic within tolerance.
- No additional per-character allocation on hot path.

## Implementation Notes
- Precompute conversion matrices and reuse.
- Clamp out-of-gamut values safely.
- Provide fallback to RGB interpolation when OkLab disabled.

## Tests (REQUIRED)
- unit_oklab_roundtrip_identity: convert -> back preserves color within epsilon.
- unit_deltae_monotonic: successive gradient samples have non-decreasing DeltaE.
- unit_out_of_gamut_clamp: no overflow or panic.
- snapshot_compare_rgb_vs_oklab: visual diff snapshots for the same gradient.

## Perf
- Microbench gradient sampling (p50/p95). Must stay within +5 percent vs RGB baseline.

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.


## Testing Plan
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures.
- Property tests: invariants (idempotence, monotonicity, determinism) where applicable.
- Fuzz tests: parsers/state machines and any input-facing logic.
- Determinism: fixed seeds/time-freeze; snapshot fixtures must be stable.


## E2E Plan
- Provide/extend an E2E script that exercises the feature end-to-end in PTY (where applicable).
- Logging: verbose JSONL with env/capabilities + per-step timings + seed + checksums; include a summary at end.
- On failure: print reproduction command and point to artifacts directory.
close_reason: Implemented OkLab perceptual color space with RGB<->OkLab conversion, lerp_color_oklab, delta_e, sample_oklab methods for ColorGradient, and 14 unit tests. All tests pass, clippy clean.

title: Implement interactive widgets (List, Scrollbar, Input)
description:
PHASE 5 - INTERACTIVE WIDGETS

## Background
Interactive widgets handle user input and state changes. List provides selectable items, Scrollbar visualizes scroll position, Input accepts text entry.

## Technical Requirements

### List Widget
- Items with optional styling per item
- Single/multi selection modes
- Keyboard navigation (up/down/pageup/pagedown/home/end)
- Highlight style for selected item
- Scroll into view on selection change
- Item filtering/search support

### Scrollbar Widget
- Vertical and horizontal orientation
- Track, thumb, and arrow styles
- Thumb size proportional to content ratio
- Click/drag support (if mouse enabled)
- Auto-hide when content fits

### Input Widget
- Single-line text input
- Cursor positioning with blinking
- Text selection (shift+arrow)
- Clipboard operations (copy/paste)
- Placeholder text when empty
- Password mode (masked input)
- Input validation hooks

## Design Rationale
These widgets encapsulate common interaction patterns. State management follows Elm architecture - widgets emit events, parent handles state updates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] List with selection modes
- [ ] List keyboard navigation
- [ ] Scrollbar sizing algorithm
- [ ] Scrollbar orientation support
- [ ] Input cursor management
- [ ] Input text selection
- [ ] All widgets implement StatefulWidget trait
- [ ] Event emission for state changes

## StatefulWidget Trait
pub trait StatefulWidget {
    type State;
    fn render(&self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer, state: &mut Self::State);
}

title: Implement syntax highlighting for code blocks
description:
PHASE 7 - EXTRAS: SYNTAX HIGHLIGHTING

## Background
Syntax highlighting is essential for code-centric TUI applications. Feature-gated as optional extra.

## Technical Requirements

### Highlighting Engine
- Use syntect or tree-sitter for parsing
- Support common languages: Rust, Python, TypeScript, JSON, YAML, TOML, Markdown
- Theme integration (VS Code themes, base16, etc.)
- Line number gutter option
- Diff highlighting (additions, deletions)

### API Design

pub struct SyntaxHighlighter {
    syntax_set: SyntaxSet,
    theme_set: ThemeSet,

}

impl SyntaxHighlighter {
    pub fn new() -> Self;

    /// Set theme
    pub fn set_theme(&mut self, name: &str);
    
    /// Get available themes
    pub fn themes(&self) -> &[String];
}

### Performance Considerations
- Lazy syntax loading
- Incremental re-highlighting for edits
- Cache parsed syntax per file extension
- Background highlighting for large files

title: task(e2e): E2E test suite for Recipe F Policy-as-Data
description:
## E2E Integration Test: Recipe F Policy-as-Data Controllers (EV=recipe)

### Scope
Full integration test loading policy artifact, shadow-running against baked-in policy, logging divergences, and verifying fallback on verification failure.

### Test Scenario
1. Create a policy artifact bundle containing:
   - Diff strategy policy (thresholds, weights)
   - Resize coalescing policy (delay, max-batch)
   - Degradation policy (level thresholds, hysteresis)
2. Sign the policy artifact with test key.
3. Load policy artifact into FrankenTUI runtime.
4. Shadow-run: execute both loaded policy and baked-in deterministic policy in parallel.
5. Log every decision where loaded policy diverges from baked-in.
6. Progressive delivery test:
   a. Shadow mode (100% baked-in, 0% loaded) - just log divergences.
   b. Canary mode (90% baked-in, 10% loaded) - verify canary decisions.
   c. Ramp mode (50/50) - verify no regression.
   d. Default mode (100% loaded) - full switch.
7. Inject verification failure: corrupt policy artifact signature.
8. Verify immediate fallback to baked-in deterministic policy.
9. Verify fallback is seamless (no dropped frames, no visual glitch).

### JSONL Structured Logging Specification
Each policy decision emits:
```json
{
  "event": "recipe_f_policy",
  "ts_ns": u64,
  "frame_id": u64,
  "policy_source": "loaded|baked_in|shadow",
  "delivery_stage": "shadow|canary|ramp|default",
  "decision_point": "diff_strategy|resize_coalesce|degradation",
  "loaded_action": "string",
  "baked_in_action": "string",
  "divergence": bool,
  "divergence_reason": "string|null",
  "policy_version": "string",
  "signature_valid": bool,
  "fallback_triggered": bool,
  "frame_time_ms": f64
}
```

### Success Criteria
- Shadow mode logs all divergences without affecting rendering.
- Progressive delivery stages execute in correct order.
- Signature verification failure triggers immediate fallback (within 1 frame).
- fallback_triggered == true when signature_valid == false.
- No dropped frames during fallback transition.
- Loaded policy produces same or better frame times than baked-in.
- No panics, no unsafe code (#\![forbid(unsafe_code)]).
- JSONL log is schema-compliant and parseable.
- Policy artifact is a self-contained data file (no executable code).
close_reason: done

title: Diagram Minimap for Large Graph Navigation
description:
## Goal
For diagrams with 20+ nodes, render a small minimap (8-12 cells tall) in a corner showing the entire diagram at tiny scale using Braille dots. A rectangular viewport indicator shows which portion is currently visible.

## Why
- Large diagrams are the primary case where terminal rendering struggles — 80×24 shows maybe 8-10 nodes at readable size.
- Without a minimap, users lose spatial orientation when panned/zoomed into a large graph.
- Minimaps are a well-understood UX pattern from code editors, games, and CAD tools.
- The Canvas/Braille system is perfect: at 2×4 dots per cell, a 20×8 minimap covers 40×32 "pixels" — enough to show topology of a 50-node graph.

## Implementation
1. Compute minimap scale: full diagram bounds / minimap area dimensions.
2. Render nodes as filled Braille dots (small filled rectangles at minimap scale).
3. Render edges as Braille lines between node centers.
4. Overlay viewport rectangle (highlighted border) showing currently visible region.
5. Position minimap in configurable corner (default: bottom-right).
6. Toggle with 'm' key.
7. Click on minimap to jump viewport to that position (if mouse support available).

## Design Decisions
- Minimap always uses Braille mode (even if main diagram uses cell mode) for maximum information density.
- Node labels are NOT shown in minimap — just dots for topology.
- Selected node (from navigation feature) highlighted in minimap with accent color.
- Minimap has a subtle border/background to distinguish from main diagram.

## Dependencies
- Canvas rendering infrastructure (bd-ukp1f)
- Viewport/zoom math (already partially in MermaidShowcase)

## Files to Modify
- crates/ftui-extras/src/mermaid_render.rs (add render_minimap method)
- crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/mermaid_showcase.rs (minimap toggle + positioning)

## Tests
- Unit: minimap scale calculation for various diagram sizes
- Snapshot: 20-node diagram with minimap visible at 120×40
- Unit: viewport indicator position matches actual viewport

## Background

The demo-showcase already demonstrates Ctrl+T theme cycling via `ftui-extras::theme`; the harness should too so the first-run experience is visually impressive and consistent across both demos.

## Scope

- Add `Ctrl+T` hotkey to cycle the active theme (`ftui_extras::theme::cycle_theme`).
- Apply theme tokens consistently across harness chrome:
  - Frame background fill (e.g., `bg::DEEP`)
  - Panels/blocks use alpha surfaces (`alpha::SURFACE` / `alpha::OVERLAY`) to demonstrate compositing
  - Foregrounds use semantic tokens (`fg::PRIMARY`, `fg::MUTED`)
  - Status line includes current theme name + key hints

## Acceptance Criteria

Checklist:

- [ ] `Ctrl+T` cycles through built-in themes and updates the UI immediately.
- [ ] Harness chrome (background/panels/status line) uses theme tokens rather than hard-coded colors.
- [ ] Alpha blending is exercised: at least one panel uses a semi-transparent background over a different base background.
- [ ] Snapshot/E2E evidence: at least one deterministic artifact proves theme cycling works.

## Testing Plan

- Unit tests:
  - Theme cycling wraps correctly (`N` themes, `N+1` returns to first).
  - Style invariants (fg/bg present for status line style).
- Snapshot tests (if harness has them): add/extend snapshots for at least 2 themes.
- If no snapshot infra exists for harness: add a minimal deterministic PTY E2E check that asserts:
  - theme name changes in status line after `Ctrl+T`

Extend an existing harness E2E script or add a small PTY-driven test run that:
- launches `ftui-harness` in a PTY at fixed size
- sends `Ctrl+T` twice
- captures frames or stdout artifacts
- logs verbose JSONL: env/capabilities, timings, seed, and the observed theme names

## Alien Artifact Upgrades

- Color rigor: treat palette selection as a constraint satisfaction problem in perceptual space (OKLCH) and enforce WCAG AA in tests.
- Graceful degradation: if alpha is unsupported (future), fall back deterministically to opaque surfaces without breaking layout.

## Extreme Optimization

title: Create adversarial tests for escape injection
description:
TESTING - ADVERSARIAL SECURITY TESTS

## Background
FrankenTUI must be secure against untrusted content. Escape sequences in user-provided text could corrupt the terminal or execute malicious sequences. This implements ADR-006 (Sanitize-by-Default).

## Threat Model

### Attack Vectors
1. **Log injection**: Untrusted output contains escape sequences
2. **Title injection**: OSC sequences to change window title
3. **Clipboard injection**: OSC 52 to set clipboard
4. **Cursor corruption**: CSI sequences to move cursor
5. **Mode hijacking**: Enabling raw mode, mouse, etc.

### Example Malicious Inputs
- "\x1b[2J" - Clear screen
- "\x1b[H" - Home cursor
- "\x1b]0;pwned\x07" - Set window title
- "\x1b]52;c;SGVsbG8=\x07" - Set clipboard
- "\x1b[?1049h" - Enter alt screen
- "\x1b[?1000h" - Enable mouse
- "\x1b[31mred\x1b[0m" - Color injection

## Technical Requirements

### Sanitizer Implementation
pub fn sanitize_for_display(input: &str) -> Cow<str> {
    // Fast path: no control characters
    if !input.bytes().any(|b| b < 0x20 || b == 0x7F || b == 0x1B) {
        return Cow::Borrowed(input);
    }
    
    // Slow path: filter control sequences
    let mut output = String::with_capacity(input.len());
    let mut chars = input.chars().peekable();
    
    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
        match c {
            '\x1b' => skip_escape_sequence(&mut chars),
            c if c.is_control() && c != '\n' && c != '\t' => {
                // Replace with visual representation
                output.push_str(&format!("^{}", (c as u8 + 64) as char));
            }
            _ => output.push(c),
        }
    }
    
    Cow::Owned(output)
}

### Test Categories

#### 1. Escape Sequence Filtering
- [ ] ESC [ ... (CSI) filtered
- [ ] ESC ] ... (OSC) filtered
- [ ] ESC P ... (DCS) filtered
- [ ] ESC _ ... (APC) filtered
- [ ] ESC ^ ... (PM) filtered

#### 2. Control Character Handling
- [ ] NUL (0x00) filtered
- [ ] BEL (0x07) filtered
- [ ] BS (0x08) filtered
- [ ] Tab (0x09) preserved
- [ ] LF (0x0A) preserved
- [ ] CR (0x0D) handled
- [ ] DEL (0x7F) filtered

#### 3. Incomplete Sequence Handling
- [ ] Truncated ESC at end
- [ ] Truncated CSI at end
- [ ] Truncated OSC at end
- [ ] Invalid sequence bytes

#### 4. Raw Passthrough (Explicit Opt-In)
- [ ] raw_text() API exists
- [ ] Loud documentation warning
- [ ] Works for ANSI colors when intended

## PTY Tests

### Test Script
for payload in "${MALICIOUS_PAYLOADS[@]}"; do
    # Run payload through ftui log viewer
    echo "$payload" | ftui-test-harness
    
    # Verify terminal state unchanged
    verify_terminal_state
    
    # Verify no escape sequences in output
    verify_no_escapes
done

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All ESC/CSI/OSC/DCS/APC filtered by default
- [ ] Control characters filtered except tab/newline
- [ ] Fast path for clean input (no allocation)
- [ ] Raw passthrough API documented with warnings
- [ ] PTY tests verify terminal state preserved
- [ ] Fuzz testing for parser robustness

title: Modal/Dialog System with Proper Stacking
description:
## Background

FrankenTUI needs modals for:
- Confirmations ('Delete file?')
- Prompts ('Enter filename:')
- Complex dialogs (settings, wizards)
- Help overlay (already exists, but ad-hoc)
- Command palette (planned in bd-39y4)

Current approach: Each feature implements its own overlay logic.

## Solution: Modal Layer System

```rust
/// Modal size presets
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub enum ModalSize {
    Small,      // 40x10
    Medium,     // 60x20
    Large,      // 80%x80%
    FullScreen,
    Custom { width: Constraint, height: Constraint },
}

/// A modal dialog
pub struct Modal {
    pub id: ModalId,
    pub content: Box<dyn Widget>,
    pub size: ModalSize,
    pub title: Option<String>,
    pub dismissable: bool,  // Escape closes
    pub backdrop: BackdropStyle,
    pub animation: Option<ModalAnimation>,
    pub on_dismiss: Option<Box<dyn FnOnce() + Send>>,
}

/// Backdrop behind modal
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum BackdropStyle {
    None,
    Dim { opacity: f32 },  // 0.0-1.0
    Blur,  // If terminal supports
    Custom(Style),
}

/// Modal animation
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub enum ModalAnimation {
    FadeIn { duration: Duration },
    SlideUp { duration: Duration },
    Scale { duration: Duration },
}

/// Manages modal stack
pub struct ModalLayer {
    stack: Vec<Modal>,
    focus_manager: FocusManager,  // Uses #2
}

impl ModalLayer {
    pub fn push(&mut self, modal: Modal) -> ModalId;
    pub fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<Modal>;
    pub fn close(&mut self, id: ModalId);
    pub fn is_open(&self, id: ModalId) -> bool;
    pub fn has_modals(&self) -> bool;
    pub fn render(&self, frame: &mut Frame); // Renders all modals
}

// Convenience builders
pub fn confirm(title: &str, message: &str) -> ConfirmDialogBuilder;
pub fn prompt(title: &str, placeholder: &str) -> PromptDialogBuilder;
pub fn alert(title: &str, message: &str) -> AlertDialogBuilder;

    .with_cancel("Cancel")
    .with_confirm("Delete")
    .danger()  // Red confirm button
    .show(&mut modal_layer);
```

title: Command Palette spec + UX flow
description:
## Purpose
Define the UX and behavioral spec for the command palette so implementation and tests are unambiguous.

## UX / Behavior Spec
- Open/close: `Ctrl+P` (primary), `/` optional if not used by search elsewhere; `Esc` closes.
- Navigation: Up/Down, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End; `Enter` executes; `Tab` toggles preview focus (if present).
- Query input: live filtering; backspace deletes; empty query shows top actions.
- Empty state: show “No results” + hints for query syntax.
- Selection: always visible highlight + optional right-side preview.
- Action metadata: title, optional description, category, and tags.

## Scoring Rules (must be deterministic)
- Prefer contiguous matches over scattered
- Prefer start‑of‑word matches
- Prefer shorter candidates given equal match quality
- Stable tie‑breakers (original index) to avoid reordering flicker

- Color is not the only indicator; selection should invert or add marker.

title: Text Effects: Composable Effect Chains
description:
## Background
Current TextEffect enum is mutually exclusive - you can only have ONE effect. Users want combinations like 'rainbow AND pulsing'. This enables effect composition.

## Implementation

Change StyledText:
```rust
pub struct StyledText {
    text: String,
    effects: Vec<TextEffect>,  // Multiple effects, applied in order
    easing: Easing,            // Global easing for time-based effects
    // ... other fields
}
```

### Effect Categories and Combination Rules

Effects are categorized by what they modify:

| Category | Effects | Combination Rule |
|----------|---------|------------------|
| ColorModifier | Gradient, ColorCycle, ColorWave, Glow | BLEND: multiply/modulate colors |
| AlphaModifier | FadeIn, FadeOut, Pulse | MULTIPLY: alpha values multiply |
| PositionModifier | Wave, Bounce, Shake, Cascade | ADD: offsets sum together |
| CharModifier | Typewriter, Scramble, Glitch, Reveal | PRIORITY: first visible char wins |
| StyleModifier | bold/italic toggles | OR: flags combine |

### Blending Examples:
- Rainbow + Pulse: Rainbow provides hue, Pulse modulates brightness
- FadeIn + Pulse: Overall alpha = fade_alpha * pulse_alpha  
- Wave + Shake: Total offset = wave_offset + shake_offset
- Typewriter + Scramble: Revealed chars can be scrambled

### Builder API:
```rust
StyledText::new("Hello")
    .effect(TextEffect::RainbowGradient { speed: 0.1 })
    .effect(TextEffect::Pulse { speed: 2.0, min_alpha: 0.3 })
    .effect(TextEffect::Wave { amplitude: 2.0, wavelength: 10.0, speed: 1.0 })
    .easing(Easing::EaseInOut)

// Convenience for multiple effects at once
.effects([effect1, effect2, effect3])

// Clear all effects
.clear_effects()
```

### Performance Guard:
Maximum 8 effects per StyledText to prevent performance issues.

## Files
crates/ftui-extras/src/text_effects.rs

## Unit Tests (REQUIRED)
- test_single_effect_backwards_compat: .effect(e) still works
- test_multiple_color_effects_blend: Rainbow + Pulse modulates
- test_multiple_alpha_effects_multiply: FadeIn * Pulse
- test_multiple_position_effects_add: Wave + Shake offsets sum
- test_char_effects_priority: First visible char wins
- test_effect_order_deterministic: Same effects = same output
- test_clear_effects: Returns to plain rendering
- test_empty_effects_vec: Renders as plain text
- test_max_effects_enforced: >8 effects errors or truncates

## Integration Tests
- Rainbow + Wave: Verify both color and position effects visible
- Pulse + Glow: Verify compound brightness looks correct

## Acceptance Criteria
- Deliver the behavior implied by the title: Text Effects: Composable Effect Chains
- Alien Artifact: define invariants + failure modes; if heuristics exist, specify an explainable decision rule (evidence ledger / Bayes factors where applicable)
- Extreme Optimization: baseline -> profile -> opportunity matrix; for each perf change include an isomorphism proof + golden output checksums
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures; add property tests for core invariants where applicable
- E2E: scripts with verbose JSONL logging (env, capabilities, timings, seed, checksums) + deterministic mode

title: task(e2e): E2E test suite for IVM Incremental Views
description:
## E2E Integration Test: Incremental View Maintenance (EV=5.6)

### Scope
Full integration test applying theme change + layout change via IVM delta propagation, verifying incremental result matches full recompute, and logging delta sizes.

### Test Scenario
1. Initialize FrankenTUI with IVM-backed style resolution and computed layout.
2. Render initial frame (full materialization of all views).
3. Apply theme change: switch from dark to light theme.
4. Process IVM deltas (signed tuples through DAG of delta operators).
5. Simultaneously do full recompute of style resolution.
6. Verify incremental result == full recompute (byte-identical rendered frame).
7. Apply layout change: resize from 80x24 to 120x40.
8. Repeat delta vs full recompute comparison.
9. Test cascading changes: theme + layout + content edit simultaneously.

### JSONL Structured Logging Specification
Each incremental update emits:
```json
{
  "event": "ivm_update",
  "ts_ns": u64,
  "frame_id": u64,
  "change_type": "theme|layout|content|combined",
  "delta_count": u32,
  "delta_size_bytes": u32,
  "full_recompute_size_bytes": u32,
  "delta_ratio": f64,
  "dag_depth": u32,
  "operators_executed": u32,
  "incremental_time_ns": u64,
  "full_recompute_time_ns": u64,
  "speedup_factor": f64,
  "result_hash": "hex_string",
  "recompute_hash": "hex_string",
  "match": bool
}
```

### Success Criteria
- match == true for all change types (incremental always matches full recompute).
- delta_ratio < 0.5 for single-property theme changes (deltas smaller than full).
- speedup_factor > 1.0 for incremental vs full recompute on large layouts.
- DAG processes topologically without cycles.
- No panics, no unsafe code (#![forbid(unsafe_code)]).
- JSONL log is schema-compliant and parseable.

title: Text Effects: Wave/Position Animation System
description:
## Background
Most terminal UIs render static text. Adding per-character positional offsets creates dynamic, living text that's a major differentiator for FrankenTUI.

## Implementation

Add Direction enum for cascade/wave direction:
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub enum Direction {
    #[default]
    Down,       // Characters fall from above
    Up,         // Characters rise from below
    Left,       // Characters slide from right
    Right,      // Characters slide from left
}
```

Add CharacterOffset (internal, not exposed):
```rust
struct CharacterOffset { 
    dx: i16,  // Horizontal offset in cells
    dy: i16,  // Vertical offset in rows
}
```

Add TextEffect variants:
```rust
TextEffect::Wave {
    amplitude: f64,   // Max offset in cells (typically 1-3)
    wavelength: f64,  // Characters per wave cycle (typically 5-15)
    speed: f64,       // Waves per second
    direction: Direction,  // Wave travel direction
}

TextEffect::Bounce {
    height: f64,      // Max bounce height in cells
    speed: f64,       // Bounces per second
    stagger: f64,     // Delay between adjacent chars (0-1)
    damping: f64,     // How quickly bounce settles (0.8-0.99)
}

TextEffect::Shake {
    intensity: f64,   // Max offset (typically 0.5-2)
    speed: f64,       // Shakes per second
    seed: u64,        // For deterministic randomness
}

TextEffect::Cascade {
    speed: f64,       // Characters per second
    direction: Direction,
    stagger: f64,     // Delay between chars (0-1 of total duration)
}
```

### Offset Calculation:
```rust
impl StyledText {
    fn char_offset(&self, idx: usize, total: usize, time: f64) -> CharacterOffset {
        // Sum offsets from all position-modifying effects
        let mut offset = CharacterOffset { dx: 0, dy: 0 };
        for effect in &self.effects {
            match effect {
                TextEffect::Wave { amplitude, wavelength, speed, direction } => {
                    let phase = (idx as f64 / wavelength + time * speed) * TAU;
                    let wave = (phase.sin() * amplitude) as i16;
                    match direction {
                        Direction::Up | Direction::Down => offset.dy += wave,
                        Direction::Left | Direction::Right => offset.dx += wave,
                    }
                }
                // ... other effects
            }
        }
        offset
    }
}
```

### Terminal Bounds Handling:
- Use saturating arithmetic for all position calculations
- If y + dy < 0, clamp to 0 (don't wrap)
- If x + dx >= width, clamp to width-1

## Files
crates/ftui-extras/src/text_effects.rs

## Unit Tests (REQUIRED)
- test_wave_offset_sinusoidal: Offset follows sine curve
- test_wave_amplitude_respected: Max offset equals amplitude
- test_wave_wavelength_period: Characters wavelength apart have same offset
- test_wave_direction_up_down: Vertical wave affects dy only
- test_wave_direction_left_right: Horizontal wave affects dx only
- test_bounce_starts_high: Initial position offset by height
- test_bounce_settles: Offset approaches 0 over time with damping
- test_bounce_stagger: Adjacent chars offset in time
- test_shake_bounded: Offset never exceeds intensity
- test_shake_deterministic: Same seed + time = same offset
- test_cascade_reveals_in_order: Characters appear in direction order
- test_offset_bounds_saturate: No overflow at terminal edges
- test_negative_offset_clamped: dy=-5 at row 0 doesn't wrap

## Visual Tests  
- Snapshot Wave at t=0, t=0.25, t=0.5, t=0.75 (shows motion)
- Snapshot Bounce settling sequence
- Snapshot Cascade reveal progression

## Performance
Offset calculation: <50ns per character

## Acceptance Criteria
- Deliver the behavior implied by the title: Text Effects: Wave/Position Animation System
- Alien Artifact: define invariants + failure modes; if heuristics exist, specify an explainable decision rule (evidence ledger / Bayes factors where applicable)
- Extreme Optimization: baseline -> profile -> opportunity matrix; for each perf change include an isomorphism proof + golden output checksums
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures; add property tests for core invariants where applicable
- E2E: scripts with verbose JSONL logging (env, capabilities, timings, seed, checksums) + deterministic mode
close_reason: Implemented Wave, Bounce, Shake, Cascade position effects with Direction enum and CharacterOffset struct. Added char_offset() method, updated render_at() to apply offsets, and added 20 unit tests. All 68 tests pass.

title: Rich Renderables Collection (rich_rust port)
description:
# Rich Renderables Collection (adapted into ftui-widgets)

## Purpose
This epic tracks a set of composable renderables/layout helpers inspired by `rich_rust`.

Unlike a widget zoo, these are meant to be small building blocks that make it easier to implement the **agent harness essential widgets** in Phase 5.

## Reference Source
- `legacy_reference_library_code/rich_rust/`

## Plan Alignment
Plan Phase 5 requires:
- `Renderable` trait
- Panel
- Text wrapping
- Table (basic)
- Viewport/TextInput (harness essentials)

This epic’s renderables are optional but useful for building those features with less bespoke code.

## Scope
Renderables in this epic are expected to:
- render into `Frame`/`Buffer` deterministically
- have clear layout contracts
- be testable via snapshot tests (frame grids)

## Non-Goals
- porting every rich renderable
- shipping “pretty” renderables that aren’t needed for the harness before Gate 1–2

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Each renderable has deterministic snapshot tests and is integrated into the widget layer.
- [ ] Dependencies are explicit (renderables depend on core primitives, not vice versa).
- [ ] Renderables do not introduce new side-channel output (one-writer rule preserved).

title: Rich Renderables Test Suite
description:
Comprehensive test suite for all rich_rust renderables. Ensures correct rendering, measurement, and styling across all components.

## Testing Philosophy
Renderables require three types of verification:
1. **Measurement correctness** - min/max width calculations
2. **Rendering correctness** - Output matches expected segments
3. **Style propagation** - Styles cascade properly through nesting

## Test Requirements by Renderable

### Align (bd-3bp.1)
Unit tests:
- `test_align_left_no_change` - Left alignment is identity
- `test_align_center_even_width` - Symmetric padding for even widths
- `test_align_center_odd_width` - Extra space goes right
- `test_align_right_full_pad` - All padding on left
- `test_align_justify_word_spacing` - Even word spacing
- `test_align_vertical_middle` - Correct top/bottom padding
- `test_align_custom_fill_char` - Non-space fill characters

Snapshot tests:
- `snapshot_align_all_modes` - Visual grid of all alignment modes

### Columns (bd-3bp.2)
Unit tests:
- `test_columns_equal_width` - Each column gets 1/N of space
- `test_columns_ratio_distribution` - Proportional width allocation
- `test_columns_fixed_width` - Fixed columns don't flex
- `test_columns_auto_width` - Auto columns shrink to content
- `test_columns_gutter_applied` - Correct spacing between columns
- `test_columns_overflow_truncate` - Content truncated when too wide
- `test_columns_height_alignment` - Shorter columns padded to match tallest

Property tests:
- `prop_total_width_matches` - Sum of column widths + gutters = total
- `prop_no_overlap` - Column content areas don't overlap

### Emoji (bd-3bp.3)

- `test_emoji_lookup_valid` - Known emoji names resolve
- `test_emoji_lookup_invalid` - Unknown names return None
- `test_emoji_width_standard` - Most emoji are 2 cells

- `test_emoji_zwj_family` - Family emoji width correct
- `test_emoji_skin_tone` - Skin tone modifiers work
- `test_emoji_shortcode_replace` - :thumbsup: -> 👍

Corpus tests:

### Group (bd-3bp.4)

- `test_group_single_item` - Single item renders unchanged
- `test_group_multiple_items` - Items stacked vertically

- `test_group_measurement_max` - Width is max of all children

### JSON (bd-3bp.5)

Snapshot tests:

### Layout (bd-3bp.6)
Unit tests:
- `test_layout_single_cell` - One item fills grid
- `test_layout_multiple_rows` - Items wrap to next row
- `test_layout_column_span` - Item spans multiple columns
- `test_layout_row_span` - Item spans multiple rows
- `test_layout_gap_applied` - Row and column gaps
- `test_layout_auto_sizing` - Auto columns fit content

Property tests:

### Padding (bd-3bp.7)

# Implement Columns renderable (column layout)

## Objective
Implement a column layout container that places children side-by-side with configurable spacing and width allocation.

## Reference (for ideas)
- `legacy_reference_library_code/rich_rust/src/renderables/columns.rs`

## Scope
- Place N children in horizontal columns.
- Support:
  - fixed spacing between columns
  - proportional or constraint-based width allocation (delegate to ftui Flex where possible)
- Deterministic rendering order.

## Integration Notes
- Prefer to use `bd-yzu` (Flex) for width allocation rather than implementing a second constraint solver.

## Tests Required
- Unit tests for width allocation and rect computation.
- Snapshot tests for 2/3/4-column layouts under narrow and wide terminals.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Columns container positions children side-by-side with correct spacing.
- [ ] Width allocation is deterministic and uses ftui layout primitives.
- [ ] Unit + snapshot tests cover representative cases.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria

### Functional Requirements
- [ ] Equal width distribution across columns
- [ ] Ratio-based width distribution
- [ ] Fixed width columns
- [ ] Auto-fit columns to content
- [ ] Range-constrained columns (min/max)
- [ ] Gutter spacing between columns
- [ ] Per-column padding
- [ ] Expand mode fills available width
- [ ] Fit mode uses minimum necessary width

### Layout Requirements
- [ ] Column widths sum to available width (with gutters)
- [ ] Content truncated when column too narrow
- [ ] Vertical alignment within row
- [ ] Shorter columns padded to match tallest
- [ ] No content overlap between columns

### Measurement Requirements
- [ ] Minimum = sum of column minimums + gutters
- [ ] Maximum = sum of column maximums + gutters
- [ ] Constraint solving for ratio columns

### Logging Requirements
- [ ] tracing::debug! for width distribution decisions
- [ ] tracing::trace! for column measurement
- [ ] tracing::warn! for constraint violations

### Test Coverage
- [ ] Unit tests for each width mode
- [ ] Property test: no column overlap
- [ ] Property test: total width correct
- [ ] Snapshot tests for visual verification
- [ ] Edge case: zero-width column
- [ ] Edge case: single column

title: Implement Padding renderable (spacing container)
description:
# Implement Padding renderable (spacing container)

## Objective
Implement a padding container that wraps a child renderable and applies `Sides` padding around it.

This is a basic building block for Panel, layouts, and widget composition.

## Reference (for ideas)
- `legacy_reference_library_code/rich_rust/src/renderables/padding.rs`

## Scope
- A padding wrapper that:
  - computes an inner rect (frame minus padding)
  - renders the child into the inner rect
  - reports measurement bounds that include padding

## Design Notes
- Padding must never produce negative dimensions; clamp at 0.
- If padding consumes all space, child render is a no-op.

## Tests Required
- Unit tests for inner-rect calculation across edge cases:
  - zero padding
  - padding larger than frame
  - asymmetric padding
- Snapshot tests showing padding effect with a simple child.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Padding correctly computes inner rect and clamps at 0.
- [ ] Child rendering is clipped to inner rect.
- [ ] Measurement bounds include padding consistently.
- [ ] Unit tests and at least one snapshot test exist.

# Implement Panel widget/renderable (bordered box + title)

## Objective
Implement a Panel component that draws a border around content with optional title/subtitle and configurable padding.

  - rounded, square, double, heavy, ascii
- Title placement (at least top-left/top-center/top-right)
- Subtitle support (optional, but plan-friendly)
- Title truncation for narrow panels (must be Unicode-width correct)
- Padding between border and content
- Style customization for border and title
- Safe/ASCII-only mode for maximum compatibility

## Integration Notes
- Must render via `Buffer` operations (no direct terminal output).
- Should reuse:
  - `BorderChars` presets (`bd-1ho.4`)
  - padding helpers (`bd-3bp.7`)
  - drawing ops (`bd-3ky.2`)

- [ ] Panel renders borders correctly with all presets and custom borders.
- [ ] Titles are positioned correctly and truncated safely under narrow widths.
- [ ] Padding is applied correctly and never draws out of bounds.

comments.text:
Implemented in crates/doctor_frankentui/src/posterior_core.rs (library-only, deterministic-stack pattern; reuses BayesianPosterior + MigrationDecision from semantic_contract for downstream expected-loss interop).

Design: log-odds (logit) accumulation. posterior_logit = prior_logit + Σ_channel(weight·log_BF) − missing_penalty, over 5 evidence channels (semantic/visual/performance/accessibility/determinism). Closed-form, exactly additive in the log domain, so every verdict decomposes into per-signal contributions.

- PosteriorRecord per claim_id: prior/posterior logit, posterior_prob + credible interval (logit-Normal via delta-method variance), moment-matched Beta posterior (BayesianPosterior alpha/beta/mean/var) for the downstream expected-loss/loss-matrix compiler, MigrationDecision.

- CounterfactualFlip: smallest single-channel log-BF change that crosses the accept/reject boundary (Δlogit + which channel + required log_BF), verified by a test that applies the counterfactual and confirms the flip.

AC#1 (log-domain stable + deterministic): stable_sigmoid (branch on sign, no overflow at ±1e9), fixed-order channel aggregation, deterministic ledger sort; report_id/sha stable across repeated runs (tested).
AC#2 (every record includes posterior + Bayes factors + additive contributions with artifact linkage): all in PosteriorRecord + ChannelContribution.
AC#3 (sparse/missing → graceful degradation, not hard failure): each missing required channel applies a conservative logit penalty (bias toward reject) + variance inflation (wider CI); when present-channels < min_present_for_accept an otherwise-accepting verdict degrades to ConservativeFallback; non-finite log-BFs are neutralized to 0.

title: task(opentui-import alien): Implement hierarchical conjugate Bayesian evidence fusion with dependence-aware corrections
description:
Background:
OpenTUI→FrankenTUI migration evidence streams are heterogeneous, sparse in long tails, and often correlated (e.g., widget-coverage signal correlates with runtime-event signal). Naive score fusion overstates certainty and creates brittle decisions.

Goal:
Build an alien-artifact-grade evidence-fusion core that is closed-form, deterministic, and auditable under correlated weak signals.

Work packages:
1) Conjugate online kernels:
- Beta-Binomial for Bernoulli outcomes (pass/fail checks, parity flags).
- Gamma-Poisson for rate processes (event/error intensity).
- Dirichlet-Multinomial for categorical strategy outcomes.
2) Hierarchical shrinkage:
- Partial pooling across project family, component class, and widget archetype.
- Empirical-Bayes prior initialization from corpus strata to reduce variance in sparse regimes.
3) Dependence-aware fusion:
- Correlation/copula-inspired correction term to deflate double-counted evidence.
- Posterior covariance proxy exported with each fused decision.
4) Robustification:
- Huberized likelihood fallback for outlier-heavy telemetry.
- Prior-stress hooks (epsilon-contamination / prior-perturbation probes) to quantify model-risk sensitivity.
5) Diagnostics + audit artifacts:
- Posterior predictive checks and simulation-based calibration (SBC) harness entry-points.
- Deterministic evidence hash + ledger rows for replay and explainability cards.

Deliverables:
- Runtime fusion module integrated with existing evidence ledger contracts.
- JSONL artifact schema additions: posterior_state_id, shrinkage_profile_id, dependence_factor, robust_mode, sensitivity_band.
- Operator-facing diagnostics for mismatch and overconfidence detection.

Acceptance criteria:
1) All posterior updates are replay-stable and numerically stable in log-domain at extreme values.
2) Correlated channels never increase confidence without explicit dependence adjustment trace.
3) Sensitivity bands are emitted for each high-impact decision; high sensitivity auto-raises conservative action policy.
4) Predictive-check failures trigger explicit degraded-confidence flags consumed by downstream policy gates.

close_reason: Implemented tiered optimization round escalator (tier_escalator.rs): operationalizes Round1(low-hanging)/Round2(algorithmic)/Round3(exotic) multi-round strategy over the opportunity matrix. title: Fix flaky subscription_manager_partial_update test
description:
The test subscription_manager_partial_update is failing due to a race condition. When reconcile() removes subscription 2, the subscription might have already sent a message before checking the stop signal. The test expects zero messages from subscription 2 after reconcile, but due to the race window between checking stop signal and sending, a message can slip through.

Fix: Make the test more robust by either:
1. Accepting that 0-1 messages from the stopped subscription is valid behavior
2. Adding a longer drain period after reconcile
3. Clearing the channel after reconcile before the timing window starts
close_reason: Fixed race condition by draining in-flight messages immediately after reconcile, before the timing window starts. Test now passes consistently (verified 5 runs).

title: Audit all Widget implementations and categorize by migration complexity
description:
## Purpose

Before migrating, we need a complete inventory of all Widget/StatefulWidget implementations
and categorize them by how they use the buffer parameter.

## Categories

### Category A: Simple buffer-only widgets
These just write to the buffer and don't need any Frame features.
Migration: Change `buf: &mut Buffer` to `frame: &mut Frame`, then use `frame.buffer` internally.

### Category B: Widgets needing hit testing
These need mouse interaction (buttons, links, list items).
Migration: Use `frame.hit_grid` to register clickable regions.

### Category C: Widgets needing cursor control
These are input widgets that need to position the cursor.
Migration: Use `frame.cursor_position` and `frame.cursor_visible`.

### Category D: Widgets that could benefit from degradation
Complex widgets that could simplify rendering under time pressure.
Migration: Check `frame.degradation` and adapt rendering.

## Deliverable

A comment on this bead with:
1. List of all widgets by file
2. Category assignment for each
3. Estimated complexity (trivial/medium/complex)
4. Any special considerations

## Files to check

- crates/ftui-widgets/src/*.rs (all widget files)
- Look for `impl Widget for` and `impl StatefulWidget for`

title: Performance Benchmark Validation Suite
description:
## Background

FrankenTUI has strict performance requirements as documented in AGENTS.md:
- 16-byte Cell for SIMD comparisons
- Row-major buffer layout for cache prefetching
- Sub-millisecond execution for typical operations
- 64KB buffered output (one write per frame)

This bead creates a comprehensive benchmark suite to validate these requirements.

## Benchmarks to Create

### Cell Operations (crates/ftui-render/benches/cell_bench.rs)
```rust
#[bench] fn cell_comparison_simd_aligned() { /* 4 cells per cache line */ }
#[bench] fn cell_default_construction() { /* <10ns */ }
#[bench] fn cell_clone_16_bytes() { /* verify no heap allocation */ }
```

### Buffer Operations (crates/ftui-render/benches/buffer_bench.rs)
```rust
#[bench] fn buffer_create_80x24() { /* <100μs */ }
#[bench] fn buffer_create_200x50() { /* <500μs */ }
#[bench] fn buffer_fill_80x24() { /* <1ms */ }
#[bench] fn buffer_row_major_scan() { /* verify cache efficiency */ }
```

### Diff Computation (crates/ftui-render/benches/diff_bench.rs)
```rust
#[bench] fn diff_identical_buffers() { /* O(1) fast path */ }
#[bench] fn diff_single_cell_change() { /* <10μs */ }
#[bench] fn diff_full_screen_change_80x24() { /* <1ms */ }
#[bench] fn diff_full_screen_change_200x50() { /* <5ms */ }
```

### Presenter (crates/ftui-render/benches/presenter_bench.rs)
```rust
#[bench] fn presenter_emit_no_change() { /* <1μs */ }
#[bench] fn presenter_emit_single_cell() { /* <10μs */ }
#[bench] fn presenter_emit_full_screen() { /* <5ms */ }
#[bench] fn presenter_state_tracking() { /* verify no redundant SGR */ }
```

### Widget Rendering (crates/ftui-widgets/benches/widget_bench.rs)
```rust
#[bench] fn paragraph_render_100_chars() { /* <100μs */ }
#[bench] fn list_render_100_items() { /* <1ms */ }
#[bench] fn table_render_10x10() { /* <500μs */ }
```

## Performance Budget Enforcement

Create `scripts/bench_budget.sh`:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

BUDGETS=(
    'cell_comparison:100ns'
    'buffer_create_80x24:100μs'
    'diff_full_screen:1ms'
    'presenter_emit_full:5ms'
)

cargo bench --bench '*' -- --save-baseline current 2>/dev/null

for budget in "${BUDGETS[@]}"; do
    name=${budget%%:*}
    limit=${budget##*:}
    actual=$(cargo bench --bench '*' -- $name --noplot 2>/dev/null | grep 'time:' | awk '{print $3}')
    echo "[$name] Budget: $limit, Actual: $actual"
done
```

## CI Integration

Add to .github/workflows/ci.yml:
```yaml
benchmark:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly
    - run: cargo bench --bench '*' -- --noplot
    - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: benchmark-results
        path: target/criterion
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Cell benchmarks created and passing
- [ ] Buffer benchmarks created and passing
- [ ] Diff benchmarks created and passing
- [ ] Presenter benchmarks created and passing
- [ ] Widget benchmarks created and passing
- [ ] bench_budget.sh script working
- [ ] CI job configured (warn-only, not blocking)
- [ ] All benchmarks have documented budgets
- [ ] No benchmark exceeds 2x budget (panic threshold)

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.
- Drift/Regimes: if runtime metrics vary (resize storms, frame pacing), incorporate change-point detection and regime-specific policies.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
