title: epic(G01): Library consumers can run a program under the ftui facade's default features
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md promises, under "Getting Started (Library Consumers)" (README.md:73-76): "If you want to embed FrankenTUI in your own Rust app (not just run the demo), start here: docs/getting-started.md". The "Why Use FrankenTUI?" table (README.md:64-66) promises "Composable crates ... Add only what you need", and the "Crates.io (Published So Far)" section (README.md:303-316) tells consumers to add `ftui = "0.5"`. The "Minimal API Example" (README.md:137-190) ends with `App::new(TickApp { ticks: 0 }).screen_mode(ScreenMode::Inline { ui_height: 1 }).run()`.

None of that works for a consumer today. With the published facade's default features, `App::run()` is a stub that returns `Err(io::ErrorKind::Unsupported, "enable `crossterm-compat` feature to use AppBuilder::run()")`. Nothing in README.md or docs/getting-started.md mentions any feature flag. The native `ftui-tty` backend, which `ftui-core`'s own manifest calls the preferred backend (it labels crossterm "legacy"), is not reachable through the `ftui` facade at all. The demo showcase works only because `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml` sets `default = ["caps-probe", "native-backend", "crossterm-compat", "clipboard", "image", "logging", "screen-mermaid"]`, i.e. it enables both backends itself. Feature-flag defaults were optimized for the demo, not the consumer (reality-check root cause 4 of 6).

This block is the first of the five "critical" gaps (G01-G07) from the 2026-09-01 reality check against commit `ab07291f`. It closes vision rows V5 ("Composable crates, add only what you need": PARTIAL, "facade defaults cannot open a terminal") and V32 ("Elm architecture Model/Cmd/Subscriptions": WORKING but `run()` unusable under defaults), and onboarding gap letters A.1 (README example does not compile), A.2 (`App::run()` returns Unsupported under defaults) and A.3 (native backend unreachable through the facade). It also serves the original plan document's section 0.8.1 "canonical entrypoint". User-visible consequence today: a developer who reads the README, adds `ftui` to Cargo.toml and pastes the example gets a compile error (missing `Widget` import), fixes it, and then gets an `Unsupported` error at runtime with no pointer to the fix except the error string.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml` features: `default = ["runtime", "extras"]`, `runtime = ["dep:ftui-runtime"]`, `extras = ["dep:ftui-extras"]`, `crossterm = ["runtime", "ftui-core/crossterm", "ftui-runtime/crossterm-compat"]`. There is no `native-backend` feature in the facade and nothing enables `ftui-runtime/native-backend`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml`: `default = []`; `crossterm-compat = ["ftui-core/crossterm"]` (line 32); `native-backend = ["dep:ftui-tty"]` (line 35); the `ftui-core` dependency already enables `caps-probe` (line 63).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `pub struct App` at :6904 (`App::new<M: Model>(model) -> AppBuilder<M>`, plus `App::fullscreen`, `App::inline`); `pub struct AppBuilder<M: Model>` at :6956. Four `run` variants: `run()` gated `#[cfg(feature = "crossterm-compat")]` at :7090 (calls `Program::with_config`, exits with `128 + signal` on `SignalTerminationError`); `run_native()` gated `#[cfg(all(feature = "native-backend", unix))]` at :7107 (calls `Program::with_native_backend`); a stub `run()` gated `#[cfg(not(feature = "crossterm-compat"))]` at :7124 that consumes the model and returns `Err(Unsupported, "enable `crossterm-compat` feature to use AppBuilder::run()")`; a stub `run_native()` gated `#[cfg(any(not(feature = "native-backend"), not(unix)))]` at :7140.
- `Program::new` (:4806) and `Program::with_config` (:4814) live in an `impl<M: Model> Program<M, CrosstermEventSource, Stdout>` block gated `#[cfg(feature = "crossterm-compat")]` (:4803). `Program::with_native_backend` (:5140, `#[cfg(unix)]`) lives in `#[cfg(feature = "native-backend")] impl<M: Model> Program<M, ftui_tty::TtyBackend, Stdout>` (:5126-5127). `Program::run(&mut self)` is at :5207.
- The facade prelude (`crates/ftui/src/lib.rs:75-93`) re-exports `App, Cmd, Model, ScreenMode, ...` but not the `Widget` / `StatefulWidget` traits (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/lib.rs:423` and `:549`). `Paragraph` implements `Widget` at `crates/ftui-widgets/src/paragraph.rs:291` and has no inherent `render`, so the README example's `Paragraph::new(text).render(area, frame)` does not compile without `use ftui_widgets::Widget`.
- `crates/ftui/examples/` and `crates/ftui/tests/` do not exist.
- `docs/getting-started.md:18` and `:167-168` claim only `ftui-core`, `ftui-layout`, `ftui-i18n` are on crates.io; in fact all 17 library crates are published at 0.6.0. README.md:314 says `ftui = "0.5"`. The getting-started example (`docs/getting-started.md:192-263`) calls `.run()?` and would hit the stub under defaults.
- `ftui-tty` is Unix-only inside (`crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs:5` "Unix-first; Windows deferred"); the Windows CI clippy job fails with 19 `dead_code` errors because unix-only items are not cfg-gated (owned by G04.3, bead `g04-03-impl`).

## Target state

`ftui = "0.6"` with default features opens a terminal on Linux, macOS and Windows. `App::new(m).screen_mode(..).run()` selects the native backend on unix and crossterm elsewhere, and fails only with an `Unsupported` error naming the feature to enable when neither backend was compiled. Explicit `run_native()` / `run_crossterm()` remain for callers who care. `Program::open(model, config)` gives non-builder users the same dispatch. `use ftui::prelude::*` brings `Widget` and `StatefulWidget` into scope so `.render(area, frame)` works. `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs` is the README example verbatim and runs under the PTY driver in CI on a fresh consumer crate.

## Implementation plan (block level; each step is a child bead)

1. `g01-impl`: one `AppBuilder::run()` that dispatches by cfg; `run_crossterm()`; `Program::open`; `ftui_runtime::DEFAULT_BACKEND` const.
2. `g01-impl-facade`: facade features `default = ["runtime", "extras", "backend"]`, `backend = ["native-backend", "crossterm"]`, `native-backend = ["runtime", "ftui-runtime/native-backend"]`; prelude gains `Widget`, `StatefulWidget`; `examples/minimal_inline.rs`; README example block made identical to it. Blocked by `g04-03-impl` (ftui-tty must compile clean on Windows before it is a default dependency).
3. `g01-tests`: `crates/ftui/tests/default_backend.rs` and runtime unit tests.
4. `g01-e2e`: `scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh` with JSONL logging, in CI.
5. `g01-docs`: README Installation / Quick Start / Minimal API Example text and getting-started feature notes; claims-ledger rows.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `AppBuilder::run`, `run_crossterm`, `run_native`, `Program::open`, `DEFAULT_BACKEND`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs`: re-export `DEFAULT_BACKEND`.
- `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`, `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`: features, prelude, `Program::open` re-export.
- `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs` (new), `crates/ftui/tests/default_backend.rs` (new).
- `scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh` (new), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (new `consumer-smoke` job).
- `README.md`, `docs/getting-started.md`, `docs/claims-ledger.md` (rows for `ftui = "0.6"`, default backends).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `crates/ftui/tests/default_backend.rs` passes: under default features `cfg!(any(feature = "native-backend", feature = "crossterm"))` is true and `ftui::runtime::DEFAULT_BACKEND` is `"native"` on unix / `"crossterm"` on windows; under `--no-default-features --features runtime` it is `"none"` and `App::new(..).run()` returns `ErrorKind::Unsupported` whose message contains both `native-backend` and `crossterm-compat`.
- [ ] `scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh` exits 0 on Linux and macOS in CI job `consumer-smoke` and its JSONL shows `exit_code: 0`, `screen_contains_ticks: true`, `sync_pairs_balanced: true`, `cursor_hide_show_balanced: true`.
- [ ] The same script with `--no-default-features --features runtime` asserts the `Unsupported` message names `native-backend` and `crossterm-compat`.
- [ ] Windows: `cargo build -p ftui --examples` green in the Windows check job once `g04-03-impl` lands, and `crates/ftui/tests/default_backend.rs` reports `"crossterm"` there.
- [ ] README doc-tests (G02) compile the example unchanged.

## Tests and logging

Unit: `crates/ftui/tests/default_backend.rs`, runtime tests `app_run_dispatch_reports_backend`, `program_open_matches_builder_backend`. E2E: `scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh` using `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` (`pty_run`, `PTY_TIMEOUT=2`, `PTY_SEND=q`, `PTY_SEND_DELAY_MS=2000`, `PTY_COLS=100`, `PTY_ROWS=30`), JSONL fields `run_id, scenario, features, backend, exit_code, bytes, count_1049h, count_1049l, count_2026h, count_2026l, count_25l, count_25h, count_decstbm, count_decstbm_reset, screen_contains_ticks, duration_ms`, validated by `tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py --strict`.

## Dependencies and ordering

- `g01-impl-facade` is blocked by `g04-03-impl` (Windows leg). `g01-impl` can start immediately.
- Unblocks: `g02-impl` (README doc-tests must run under defaults), `g26-impl` (agent shell example), `g13-impl` (constructors), `g31-impl` (Windows validation), `g06-docs-readme`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Making `native-backend` a default pulls `ftui-tty` (and its `libc`/`nix`-style deps) into every consumer build; the slim path `--no-default-features --features runtime` stays available and is documented. Rejected alternative: keep defaults empty and improve only the error message. Rejected because the README's front-page example must work as pasted; a better error is not a working example.
- Dispatch order native-before-crossterm on unix matches `ftui-core`'s stated preference (crossterm is "legacy"). If a consumer wants crossterm on unix they call `run_crossterm()`.
- No compatibility shims: the two stub `run`/`run_native` functions are replaced, not wrapped. No deletion of files. No script-based edits.
- Risk: `Program::open` must return one concrete type per cfg; use a cfg-selected `pub type DefaultProgram<M>` alias (see `g01-impl`). Risk: doubling the facade's default dependency count could slow docs.rs builds; acceptable.

## Definition of done

All five child beads closed with evidence (test names, CI run id of a green `consumer-smoke` job on main, JSONL artifact path). `docs/claims-ledger.md` rows `ftui = "0.6"`, "default backends", "Minimal API Example compiles and runs" marked proven. Main green for the affected jobs.

title: feature(G01): Make AppBuilder::run() dispatch to the compiled backend and add Program::open
description:
## Context and why this matters README.md:137-190 ("Minimal API Example") ends with `App::new(TickApp { ticks: 0 }).screen_mode(ScreenMode::Inline { ui_height: 1 }).run()`. README.md:64 promises "Composable crates ... Add only what you need". Today `AppBuilder::run()` is compiled as a stub whenever the `crossterm-compat` feature is off, which is the case for every consumer of the published `ftui` facade under default features, and the native backend (the preferred one per `ftui-core`'s manifest, where crossterm is labelled "legacy") is only reachable through a differently named method `run_native()` that also disappears on non-unix. This bead makes the runtime side of the promise true: one `run()` that uses whatever backend was compiled and one `Program::open` constructor with the same rule. It closes onboarding gaps A.2 and A.3 and serves vision rows V5 and V32 from the 2026-09-01 reality check (commit `ab07291f`). Without it, `g01-impl-facade` (which flips the facade defaults) would still leave consumers calling a method that picks the wrong backend or none. ## Current state (evidence) - `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs:7090` `#[cfg(feature = "crossterm-compat")] pub fn run(self) -> io::Result<()>`: `Program::with_config(self.model, self.config)?`, then `program.run()`, then on `signal_termination_from_error(err) == Some(signal)` it drops the program and `std::process::exit(128 + signal)`. - `:7107` `#[cfg(all(feature = "native-backend", unix))] pub fn run_native(self)`: identical shape over `Program::with_native_backend`. - `:7124` `#[cfg(not(feature = "crossterm-compat"))] pub fn run(self)`: `let _ = (self.model, self.config); Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Unsupported, "enable `crossterm-compat` feature to use AppBuilder::run()"))`. - `:7140` `#[cfg(any(not(feature = "native-backend"), not(unix)))] pub fn run_native(self)`: stub; on non-unix it points the caller at `crossterm-compat`. - `:4803` `#[cfg(feature = "crossterm-compat")] impl Program` holds `new` (:4806) and `with_config` (:4814). - `:5126-5127` `#[cfg(feature = "native-backend")] impl Program` holds `with_native_backend` (:5140, `#[cfg(unix)]`). - `:4695` `pub struct Program, W: Write + Send = Stdout>`; `:5207 pub fn run(&mut self) -> io::Result<()>`. - `crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml`: `default = []`, `crossterm-compat = ["ftui-core/crossterm"]`, `native-backend = ["dep:ftui-tty"]`. - No constant or function reports which backend was compiled; a consumer cannot ask. ## Target state - Exactly one `AppBuilder::run(self) -> io::Result<()>` exists for all cfg combinations. Dispatch: `#[cfg(all(feature = "native-backend", unix))]` -> native; else `#[cfg(feature = "crossterm-compat")]` -> crossterm; else `Err(io::ErrorKind::Unsupported, "no terminal backend compiled: enable `native-backend` (unix) or `crossterm-compat`")`. - `AppBuilder::run_crossterm(self)` exists under `#[cfg(feature = "crossterm-compat")]`; `run_native(self)` keeps its current gate; the non-compiled variants of both return the same `Unsupported` error text (with the platform hint on non-unix that `:7140` has today). - `Program::open(model, config) -> io::Result>` exists with the same dispatch, where `pub type DefaultProgram = Program` under `all(feature = "native-backend", unix)`, `Program` under `crossterm-compat` otherwise, and the function is absent (compile error with a doc note) when neither is compiled. `new`, `with_config`, `with_native_backend` stay. - `pub const DEFAULT_BACKEND: &str` in `ftui-runtime` equals `"native"`, `"crossterm"` or `"none"` by the same cfg rule and is re-exported from `crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs`. - The signal-exit behaviour (`std::process::exit(128 + signal)` after dropping the program) is preserved in a single private helper `fn finish_run

(program: P, result: io::Result<()>) -> io::Result<()>` used by all three builder methods so the three paths cannot drift. ## Implementation plan 1. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`, near `:7088`: add `pub const DEFAULT_BACKEND: &str = { cfg-if chain }` implemented with three `#[cfg]`-gated `const` items feeding one public name (no `cfg_if` crate; three gated `const DEFAULT_BACKEND: &str = "native";` etc. with mutually exclusive predicates). Predicates: native = `all(feature = "native-backend", unix)`; crossterm = `all(feature = "crossterm-compat", not(all(feature = "native-backend", unix)))`; none = `not(any(all(feature = "native-backend", unix), feature = "crossterm-compat"))`. 2. Add `pub type DefaultProgram` with the same three predicates (for "none", do not define the alias; document in the module docs that `Program::open` requires a backend feature). 3. Replace the two `run` bodies (:7090 and :7124) with one `pub fn run(self) -> io::Result<()> where M::Message: Send + 'static` whose body is three cfg-gated blocks that each `return`; the native block calls `self.run_native()`, the crossterm block calls `self.run_crossterm()`, the none block consumes `(self.model, self.config)` and returns the `Unsupported` error. Keep `#[must_use]`-free signature as today. 4. Add `#[cfg(feature = "crossterm-compat")] pub fn run_crossterm(self)` containing the current crossterm body (`Program::with_config` + `finish_run`). Keep `run_native` (:7107) and its non-compiled stub (:7140); change both stubs' error text to the new sentence while keeping the non-unix hint. 5. Add `Program::open`: in a new `impl DefaultProgram` block gated on `any(native, crossterm)` predicates; body dispatches to `Self::with_native_backend(model, config)` or `Self::with_config(model, config)`. Rustdoc: "Opens the default backend for this build; see `DEFAULT_BACKEND`." 6. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs`: `pub use program::{DEFAULT_BACKEND, DefaultProgram};` next to the existing `App`/`AppBuilder` re-exports. 7. Update rustdoc on `App` and `AppBuilder` to state the dispatch rule and the slim-build error. 8. Run `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` for the four feature combinations: none, `crossterm-compat`, `native-backend`, both (the `features` CI job matrix must include these; add if missing). Run `ubs crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs` before committing. What NOT to do: no wrapper that keeps the old `Err("enable crossterm-compat ...")` text for "compatibility" (AGENTS.md forbids compatibility shims); no new file variants (`program_v2.rs`); no script-driven edits; do not delete any file; do not touch feature defaults here (that is `g01-impl-facade`). ## Files to change - `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `DEFAULT_BACKEND`, `DefaultProgram`, `AppBuilder::{run, run_crossterm, run_native}`, `finish_run`, `Program::open`, rustdoc. - `crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs`: re-exports. - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `features` job (line 119): ensure the four backend combinations for `ftui-runtime` are checked (only if not already covered; verify by reading the job). ## Success criteria - [ ] `cargo check -p ftui-runtime` succeeds with `--no-default-features`, `--features crossterm-compat`, `--features native-backend`, and `--features crossterm-compat,native-backend`; clippy `-D warnings` and fmt clean for each. - [ ] Unit test `app_run_dispatch_reports_backend` (program.rs tests module): asserts `DEFAULT_BACKEND` equals the value implied by `cfg!(..)` predicates and that under the "none" configuration `App::new(model).run()` returns `ErrorKind::Unsupported` with a message containing `native-backend` and `crossterm-compat` (test compiled only under the none cfg). - [ ] Unit test `program_open_matches_builder_backend`: `std::any::type_name::>()` contains `TtyBackend` on unix+native and `CrosstermEventSource` otherwise. - [ ] Unit test `run_variants_share_signal_exit_path`: `finish_run` maps a `SignalTerminationError` result through the same helper (test the helper's non-exiting branch: an `Ok(())` and a non-signal error pass through unchanged). - [ ] `rg -n 'enable `crossterm-compat` feature to use AppBuilder::run' crates` returns nothing. ## Tests and logging Unit tests above live in `program.rs`'s `mod tests`. Add `tracing::info!(target: "ftui.runtime.backend", backend = DEFAULT_BACKEND, "selected default backend")` at the top of `AppBuilder::run` and `Program::open` so the PTY E2E (`g01-e2e`) and the consumer can see which backend ran when `FTUI_LOG`/tracing is enabled. No JSONL here; the E2E bead logs. ## Dependencies and ordering Blocked by: nothing. Unblocks: `g01-impl-facade`, `g01-tests`, `g01-e2e`, `g13-impl` (which later makes `Program` present through `BackendPresenter` and will build on `Program::open`), `g26-impl`, `g31-impl`. ## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected - Alternative: a runtime `Backend` enum argument to `run(Backend::Auto)`. Rejected: the choice is a compile-time fact; an enum invites a runtime "Unsupported" for a backend that was not compiled, which is the bug we are removing. - Alternative: make `Program::open` return `Box`. Rejected: `Program` is not object-safe over `E`/`W`, and the type alias is zero-cost and honest. - Risk: `type_name` assertions are brittle across rustc versions; assert on `contains("TtyBackend")`, not the full path. - Rollback: revert the single commit; no data or format changes. ## Definition of done Reachable from the production path (every `App::run()` caller). Close reason names the four cfg check runs, the three unit tests, and the commit hash. Claims-ledger row "App::run() works under default features" moves to proven only after `g01-impl-facade` and `g01-e2e`; this bead updates the row's proof column with the test names.
close_reason: Landed in 8e602592/cd9b15ba: one AppBuilder::run() dispatching native (unix+native-backend) / crossterm / none via run_default_backend, run_crossterm(), finish_run helper, Program::open, DefaultProgram<M>, DEFAULT_BACKEND, NO_BACKEND_MESSAGE. Proof: cargo check -p ftui-runtime with --no-default-features, --features crossterm-compat, --features native-backend, both; tests program::tests::default_backend_constant_matches_cfg and run_without_backend_reports_missing_features (none cfg); clippy -D warnings and fmt clean.

title: feature(G01): Enable backends by default in the ftui facade, prelude Widget traits, minimal_inline example
description:
## Context and why this matters

The `ftui` facade is what the README tells consumers to depend on: README.md:295-300 ("Use as a Workspace Dependency", `ftui = { path = "../frankentui/crates/ftui" }`) and README.md:303-316 ("Crates.io (Published So Far)", `ftui = "0.5"`). Its prelude is advertised in `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs:14` ("A lightweight prelude for day-to-day use"). Today the facade's default features cannot open a terminal, the native backend cannot be enabled through it at all, and its prelude omits the two traits (`Widget`, `StatefulWidget`) that every `view()` body needs to call `.render(area, frame)`, which is exactly why the README's front-page example fails to compile (onboarding gap A.1). This bead flips the facade to consumer-correct defaults, completes the prelude, and creates the single source-of-truth example file that G02's doc-tests and G06's byte-identity check both rely on. It closes A.1-A.3 and serves V5/V32 of the 2026-09-01 reality check (commit `ab07291f`).

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml` (whole manifest verified 2026-09-01): `[features] default = ["runtime", "extras"]; runtime = ["dep:ftui-runtime"]; extras = ["dep:ftui-extras"]; crossterm = ["runtime", "ftui-core/crossterm", "ftui-runtime/crossterm-compat"]`. Dependencies: `ftui-core`, `ftui-render`, `ftui-style`, `ftui-text`, `ftui-layout`, `ftui-widgets` (required), `ftui-runtime` and `ftui-extras` (optional), all `version = "0.6.0"`. `readme = "../../README.md"`.
- `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs:75-93` prelude: `TerminalSession` (only with `crossterm` and not wasm32), `Buffer, Cx, CxController, CxError, Error, Event, Frame, KeyCode, KeyEvent, LabClock, Modifiers, Result, Style, TablePresetId, TableTheme, Theme`; with `runtime`: `App, Cmd, Model, PredictiveConfig, ScreenMode, TerminalWriter, TickDecision, TickStrategy, TickStrategyKind`; module aliases `core, layout, pane, render, style, text, widgets`, and `runtime`. No `Widget`, no `StatefulWidget`, no `Rect`, no `Paragraph`.
- `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs:59-64` re-exports from `ftui_runtime`: `App, Cmd, EffectQueueConfig, InlineAutoRemeasureConfig, Locale, LocaleContext, LocaleOverride, Model, PredictiveConfig, Program, ProgramConfig, ResizeBehavior, RuntimeDiffConfig, ScreenMode, TaskSpec, TerminalWriter, TickDecision, TickStrategy, TickStrategyKind, UiAnchor, current_locale, detect_system_locale, set_locale`.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/lib.rs:423 pub trait Widget`, `:549 pub trait StatefulWidget`. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/paragraph.rs:291 impl Widget for Paragraph<'_>`; no inherent `render`.
- `crates/ftui/examples/` and `crates/ftui/tests/` do not exist. `ls` on both returns "No such file or directory".
- README.md:139-190 example imports `ftui_core::event::Event`, `ftui_core::geometry::Rect`, `ftui_render::frame::Frame`, `ftui_runtime::{App, Cmd, Model, ScreenMode}`, `ftui_widgets::paragraph::Paragraph` (the internal crates, not the facade) and never imports `Widget`.
- `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs:5`: "Unix-first; Windows deferred"; Windows clippy currently fails with 19 dead-code errors (G04.3, bead `g04-03-impl`). Making `ftui-tty` a default dependency before that lands would turn the Windows `check` job red for the facade.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml` default features enable `native-backend` and `crossterm-compat` directly on `ftui-runtime`, which is why the demo works.

## Target state

- `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`: `default = ["runtime", "extras", "backend"]`; `backend = ["native-backend", "crossterm"]`; `native-backend = ["runtime", "ftui-runtime/native-backend"]`; `crossterm` unchanged. A consumer who wants the slim build uses `default-features = false, features = ["runtime"]` and gets the `Unsupported` error from `g01-impl` naming the features.
- Prelude additionally exports `Widget`, `StatefulWidget` (from `ftui_widgets`), `Rect` (from `ftui_core::geometry`), and, under `runtime`, `Program`, `ProgramConfig`, `DEFAULT_BACKEND`, `DefaultProgram`. Root re-exports gain `DEFAULT_BACKEND` and `DefaultProgram`.
- `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs` exists and is byte-identical to the README "Minimal API Example" block (README.md:139-190 after this bead), which is rewritten to use the facade: `use ftui::prelude::*; use ftui::widgets::paragraph::Paragraph;` and otherwise the same `TickApp` program (ticks counter, `q` quits, `ScreenMode::Inline { ui_height: 1 }`).
- `cargo run -p ftui --example minimal_inline` opens an inline UI showing `Ticks: 0  (press 'q' to quit)` and exits 0 on `q`.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`: add the three feature lines above. Do not add `ftui-tty` as a direct dependency; it comes through `ftui-runtime/native-backend`.
2. `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`: extend `pub use ftui_runtime::{ ... }` with `DEFAULT_BACKEND, DefaultProgram` (from `g01-impl`); in `pub mod prelude` add `pub use ftui_widgets::{StatefulWidget, Widget};`, `pub use ftui_core::geometry::Rect;`, and under `#[cfg(feature = "runtime")]` add `Program, ProgramConfig, DEFAULT_BACKEND, DefaultProgram`. Extend the existing test `prelude_re_exports_core_types` (lib.rs:223) to name `Widget` and `StatefulWidget` (e.g. `fn _assert<W: Widget>() {}` with `Paragraph`).
3. Create `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs` with the corrected example. Structure: `use ftui::prelude::*; use ftui::widgets::paragraph::Paragraph;` then `struct TickApp { ticks: u64 }`, `enum Msg { Tick, Quit }`, `impl From<Event> for Msg` (`Event::Key(k) if k.is_char('q') => Msg::Quit`, else `Msg::Tick`), `impl Model for TickApp` (`type Message = Msg; update; view` with `let area = Rect::new(0, 0, frame.width(), 1); Paragraph::new(text).render(area, frame);`), `fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> { App::new(TickApp { ticks: 0 }).screen_mode(ScreenMode::Inline { ui_height: 1 }).run() }`. 5. `docs/getting-started.md` "Add The Dependency" (lines 165-188): switch to `ftui = "0.6"` and add a two-line note on `backend` default and the slim path (full doc rewrite is `g01-docs` / `g06-docs-getting-started`; here only the lines that would otherwise contradict the new defaults).

What NOT to do: do not create `examples/minimal_inline_v2.rs` or keep an old copy; do not add `ftui-tty` to the facade's `[dependencies]`; do not gate the prelude traits behind a feature; do not delete anything.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`: features.
- `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`: prelude and root re-exports, test extension.
- `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs`: new.

- `docs/getting-started.md:165-188`: dependency snippet.

- [ ] `cargo run -p ftui --example minimal_inline` under `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` prints a line containing `Ticks:` and exits 0 on `q` (asserted by `g01-e2e`).
- [ ] `crates/ftui/tests/default_backend.rs` (from `g01-tests`) reports `DEFAULT_BACKEND == "native"` on Linux/macOS under defaults.

- [ ] `cargo doc -p ftui --no-deps` clean (prelude additions have docs).

## Tests and logging

Unit: prelude test extension in `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`; `default_backend.rs` (in `g01-tests`). E2E: `g01-e2e`. Logging: none beyond the `ftui.runtime.backend` tracing event from `g01-impl`.

title: task(G01): Unit tests for default-backend dispatch, BACKEND const, prelude, and Unsupported message
description:
## Context

G01 makes `App::run()` work under the `ftui` facade's default features and adds `Program::open`, `DEFAULT_BACKEND` and prelude traits. This bead is the companion unit/integration test bead for `g01-impl` and `g01-impl-facade`. The reality check (2026-09-01, commit `ab07291f`) found that `AppBuilder::run()` under `#[cfg(not(feature = "crossterm-compat"))]` (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs:7124`) returned `Err(Unsupported)` for every facade consumer and that no test anywhere asserted which backend a build could open. These tests make that regression impossible to reintroduce silently and give `g01-e2e` a stable contract to assert against.

## What to test

1. Backend selection is a compile-time fact reported by `ftui_runtime::DEFAULT_BACKEND` and re-exported by the facade.
2. Under the facade's defaults at least one backend is compiled and `run()` is not the stub.
3. Under the slim build (`--no-default-features --features runtime`) `run()` returns `ErrorKind::Unsupported` whose message names both `native-backend` and `crossterm-compat`.
4. `Program::open` is the same type as the builder's backend.
5. The prelude exports `Widget`, `StatefulWidget`, `Rect`, `App`, `Model`, `Cmd`, `ScreenMode`, `Program`, `ProgramConfig` so that the README example compiles with `use ftui::prelude::*`.
6. The README example file `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs` builds (`cargo build -p ftui --examples`).

## Test types (unit, property, bench, E2E) with names and assertions

Integration test file `crates/ftui/tests/default_backend.rs` (new; `crates/ftui/tests/` does not exist today):
- `default_features_compile_a_backend`: `assert!(cfg!(any(feature = "native-backend", feature = "crossterm")))` compiled only under `#[cfg(any(feature = "native-backend", feature = "crossterm"))]`; and `assert_ne!(ftui::DEFAULT_BACKEND, "none")`.
- `default_backend_matches_platform`: on `cfg!(all(unix, feature = "native-backend"))` expect `"native"`; on `cfg!(all(not(all(unix, feature = "native-backend")), feature = "crossterm"))` expect `"crossterm"`.
- `slim_build_reports_none_and_unsupported` under `#[cfg(not(any(feature = "native-backend", feature = "crossterm")))]`: `assert_eq!(ftui::DEFAULT_BACKEND, "none")`; build a trivial `Model` (`struct Noop; impl Model for Noop { type Message = (); fn update(..) -> Cmd<()> { Cmd::none() } fn view(..) {} }`), call `App::new(Noop).run()`, assert `err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Unsupported`, `err.to_string().contains("native-backend")`, `err.to_string().contains("crossterm-compat")`. This test never opens a terminal because the stub returns before construction.
- `prelude_exposes_render_traits`: `use ftui::prelude::*; fn needs_widget<W: Widget>(_: &W) {} needs_widget(&ftui::widgets::paragraph::Paragraph::new("x"));` plus a `StatefulWidget` bound check with `ftui::widgets::log_viewer::LogViewer` (which the getting-started example already uses as a `StatefulWidget`), and `let _ = Rect::new(0, 0, 1, 1);`.
- `program_open_type_matches_default_backend` under `#[cfg(feature = "runtime")]` and `any(native, crossterm)`: `let name = std::any::type_name::<ftui::DefaultProgram<Noop>>(); if ftui::DEFAULT_BACKEND == "native" { assert!(name.contains("TtyBackend")) } else { assert!(name.contains("CrosstermEventSource")) }`.

Runtime unit tests in `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` `mod tests` (added by `g01-impl`, verified here):
- `app_run_dispatch_reports_backend`, `program_open_matches_builder_backend`, `run_variants_share_signal_exit_path` (see `g01-impl`).

Build checks (run via rch, recorded in the close reason):
- `cargo test -p ftui --test default_backend` under defaults; `cargo test -p ftui --test default_backend --no-default-features --features runtime`; `cargo build -p ftui --examples`.

No property tests or benches: the block claims no speed.

## Logging (structured JSONL fields, tracing targets)

Integration tests print one line per assertion group via `eprintln!("{{\"test\":\"default_backend\",\"backend\":\"{}\",\"features\":\"{}\"}}", ftui::DEFAULT_BACKEND, feature_list)` where `feature_list` is built from `cfg!` checks, so a failing CI job shows the resolved backend without re-running. Tracing target `ftui.runtime.backend` (from `g01-impl`) is not asserted here.

## Files

- `crates/ftui/tests/default_backend.rs`: new.
- `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`: no `[dev-dependencies]` needed unless `LogViewer` requires a feature (verify; it is in `ftui-widgets`, a required dependency).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `features` job (:119): add `cargo test -p ftui --test default_backend --no-default-features --features runtime` so the slim-build assertion runs in CI.

## Success criteria

- [ ] All five integration tests green under defaults on Linux and macOS; `slim_build_reports_none_and_unsupported` green under the slim feature set; Windows leg green after `g04-03-impl`.
- [ ] `cargo build -p ftui --examples` green in the `docs` job (add the step next to `cargo build --examples -p ftui-harness` at ci.yml:117).
- [ ] The three runtime unit tests from `g01-impl` green.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `g01-impl-facade` (features, prelude, example must exist). Unblocks: `g01-e2e` (the E2E asserts the same backend string), `g42-impl`.

## Definition of done

Tests exist on main, are wired into the `features` and `docs` CI jobs, and the close reason lists the test names and the CI run id. No claims-ledger rows are owned here; `g01-docs` references these test names as proofs.
close_reason: tests landed and green locally (see closing note on bd-g00-root-epic-ewths.1.1); Windows execution pending CI

title: task(G01): consumer_smoke_e2e.sh builds a fresh consumer crate against the facade and runs it in a PTY
description:
## Context and why this matters

The reality check's Section 1 evidence table shows the demo showcase working under a PTY (kitty identity, 26/26 sync pairs, clean teardown) while a library consumer following README.md:139-190 and README.md:303-316 could not run anything. Unit tests inside the workspace cannot catch that class of failure because the workspace's own feature unification hides consumer defaults. This bead adds the only test that reproduces what a consumer sees: a fresh crate outside the workspace, depending on the `ftui` facade by path with default features, containing the README example verbatim, built and run under a real PTY, with escape-sequence tallies logged as JSONL. It is the E2E proof for G01 (vision rows V5, V32; onboarding gaps A.1-A.3) and the row "V5 composable crates, A onboarding" of the final verification plan expects `scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh` green on Linux, macOS and Windows.

## Current state (evidence)

- No `scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh` exists (`ls scripts | rg consumer` is empty).
- `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` is a real Python-`pty` driver: `pty_run <output_file> -- <cmd...>` (line 142) reads `PTY_TIMEOUT` (default 5 s), `PTY_SEND`, `PTY_SEND_FILE`, `PTY_SEND_DELAY_MS`, `PTY_COLS` (80), `PTY_ROWS` (24), `PTY_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS`, `PTY_TERMINATE_GRACE_MS`, `PTY_READ_POLL_MS`, `PTY_READ_CHUNK`, `PTY_RETRIES`, `PTY_MIN_BYTES`; requires `E2E_PYTHON`. `pty_canonicalize_file` (line 60) and `pty_record_metadata` (line 72) exist.
- `tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py` validates JSONL against `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json` with `--registry tests/e2e/lib/e2e_hash_registry.json --strict` (usage as in `.github/workflows/ci.yml:412-425`, job `e2e-widget-api`).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` jobs today: `check` (:23), `docs` (:86), `features` (:119), `coverage`, `benchmarks`, `docs-build` (:339), `e2e-widget-api` (:376), `demo-showcase` (:438), `e2e-pty` (:528), `golden-trace-gates`, `doctor-frankentui-verification`, `fuzz`, `frankenterm-conformance-gates`, `msrv`, `wasm`, `pane-perf-artifacts`, `perf-rollout-gates`. None builds an out-of-workspace consumer.
- On the development machine `rch` (remote compilation helper, AGENTS.md "RCH") refuses cargo invocations for paths outside `/data/projects`, and `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is `/data/tmp/cargo-target`. The temporary crate therefore must live under `/data/projects/` locally (e.g. `/data/projects/tmp-consumer-<pid>`); in CI `$RUNNER_TEMP` is fine.
- The audit's identity driver (to become `scripts/pty_identity_matrix.py` in `g05-e2e`) counted these regexes over raw PTY bytes: `\x1b\[\?1049[hl]`, `\x1b\[\?2026[hl]`, `\x1b\[>\d*u` / `\x1b\[<u`, `\x1b\[\?100[0236][hl]`, `\x1b\[\?2004[hl]`, `\x1b\[\?1004[hl]`, `\x1b\[\?25[lh]`, `\x1b\[\d+;\d+r`, `\x1b\[r`. The same tallies are reused here.

## Target state

`scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh [--features <list>] [--no-default-features] [--out-dir DIR]` creates a temporary consumer crate, builds it against `crates/ftui` by path, runs it under the PTY driver for 2 s, sends `q`, and writes `consumer_smoke.jsonl` with one `run` record and one `summary` record. Default mode asserts success and balanced sequences; `--no-default-features --features runtime` mode asserts the `Unsupported` error text. A CI job `consumer-smoke` runs both modes on `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest` (Windows added by `g31-impl` when the headless variant exists) and uploads the JSONL and raw PTY capture.

## Implementation plan

1. Create `scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh` (bash, `set -euo pipefail`, sources `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh`, `tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh`, `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh`). Arguments parsed with a small `case` loop; `RUN_ID="consumer_smoke_$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)_$$"`.
2. Choose the crate directory: `CONSUMER_ROOT="${CONSUMER_SMOKE_ROOT:-}"`; if empty and `/data/projects` is writable use `/data/projects/tmp-consumer-$$`, else `${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/tmp-consumer-$$`. Never delete the directory from the script (AGENTS.md rule 1: no deletion without permission); print its path in the summary record and in the job log so the operator can remove it. Reuse an existing directory when `--reuse DIR` is passed.
3. Write `Cargo.toml` for the consumer: `[package] name = "ftui_consumer_smoke" edition = "2024"`; `[dependencies] ftui = { path = "<abs repo>/crates/ftui" }` plus `default-features = false, features = [...]` when requested; `[workspace]` empty table so it is not adopted by the frankentui workspace; `[toolchain]` is inherited by copying `rust-toolchain.toml` from the repo root into the consumer dir (nightly pin).
4. Extract the README example: `python3 - <<'PY'` reads README.md, finds the fence that follows the heading `## Minimal API Example`, writes its body to `src/main.rs`, and also byte-compares it with `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs`; mismatch is a failure with both paths printed (this duplicates `g06-impl-checker` deliberately so the smoke fails fast even if the docs job is skipped).
5. Build: `cargo build --manifest-path "$CONSUMER_ROOT/Cargo.toml" --locked 2>&1 | tee "$OUT/build.log"`; record `build_seconds` and `build_exit`.
6. Run under PTY: `PTY_TIMEOUT=6 PTY_SEND=q PTY_SEND_DELAY_MS=2000 PTY_COLS=100 PTY_ROWS=30 pty_run "$OUT/run.raw" -- "$CONSUMER_ROOT/target/debug/ftui_consumer_smoke"`; then `pty_canonicalize_file "$OUT/run.raw" "$OUT/run.canonical.txt"`.
7. Tally with an inline python block: counts for `1049h`, `1049l`, `2026h`, `2026l`, `?25l`, `?25h`, DECSTBM set (`\x1b\[\d+;\d+r`), DECSTBM reset (`\x1b\[r`), kitty push/pop (`\x1b\[>\d*u`, `\x1b\[<u`), mouse modes, `2004`, `1004`; `screen_contains_ticks = "Ticks:" in canonical`; `exit_code` from the PTY driver.
8. Assertions (default mode): `build_exit == 0`, `exit_code == 0`, `screen_contains_ticks`, `count_2026h == count_2026l`, `count_25l >= 1 and count_25h >= 1`, `count_1049h == 0` (inline mode must never enter the alt screen), `count_decstbm_set == count_decstbm_reset` (either both 0 or both >= 1; the value depends on the identity policy, see G05). Assertions (slim mode): `build_exit == 0`, `exit_code != 0`, stderr contains `native-backend` and `crossterm-compat`.
9. Write JSONL records `{"schema":"consumer_smoke.v1","kind":"run",...}` and `{"kind":"summary",...}` to `"$OUT/consumer_smoke.jsonl"` through `tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh` helpers; register the schema fields in `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json` if the strict validator requires it (read the schema first; it currently has no top-level `required`).
10. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: new job `consumer-smoke` (matrix `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest`; `timeout-minutes: 30`; nightly toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml`; python 3.11; steps: run default mode, run slim mode, validate JSONL with `validate_jsonl.py --strict`, upload `consumer-smoke-<os>` artifact with the out dir). Do not use `continue-on-error`.
11. Document the script in README "E2E Scripts" (README.md:431 area) via `g01-docs`.

What NOT to do: no `rm -rf` of the consumer directory; no editing of repo sources from the script; no hard-coded `/tmp` when `CONSUMER_SMOKE_ROOT` or `RUNNER_TEMP` is available; no mocks (the CI `check` job's no-mock policy at ci.yml:57-66 greps `crates` and `tests`; keep the words mock/fake/stub out of the script and the JSONL keys).

## Files to change

- `scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh`: new.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: job `consumer-smoke`.
- `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json`: `consumer_smoke.v1` fields if strict validation needs them.
- `README.md` "E2E Scripts" list: one line (via `g01-docs`).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `./scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh` exit 0 locally (Linux, under rch constraints) and in the `consumer-smoke` job on `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest`.
- [ ] JSONL `summary` record has `exit_code: 0`, `screen_contains_ticks: true`, `count_2026h == count_2026l`, `count_1049h == 0`, `count_25l >= 1`, `count_25h >= 1`.
- [ ] `./scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh --no-default-features --features runtime` exit 0 with `summary.mode = "slim"`, `program_exit_code != 0`, `stderr_names_features: true`.
- [ ] A deliberate revert of `g01-impl-facade`'s `default` line makes the default-mode run fail with `program_exit_code != 0` and `stderr` containing `no terminal backend compiled` (verified once during rollout; the log is attached to the close reason).
- [ ] `validate_jsonl.py --strict` passes on the artifact.

## Tests and logging

E2E script above; PTY driver `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh`. JSONL fields per record: `schema, kind, run_id, scenario ("consumer_smoke_default" | "consumer_smoke_slim"), os, features, backend_expected, consumer_root, build_exit, build_seconds, program_exit_code, duration_ms, bytes, count_1049h, count_1049l, count_2026h, count_2026l, count_25l, count_25h, count_decstbm_set, count_decstbm_reset, count_kitty_push, count_kitty_pop, count_mouse_on, count_mouse_off, count_2004h, count_2004l, count_1004h, count_1004l, screen_contains_ticks, stderr_names_features, raw_path, canonical_path, ok`. Raw and canonical captures are uploaded as artifacts so a failure can be replayed without rerunning CI.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g01-impl-facade` (defaults, example file, README block identity). Not blocked by G04 job-topology work, but the job should be placed in the workflow section that `g04-12-impl` creates for E2E jobs if that lands first. Unblocks: `g31-impl` (adds the Windows leg), `g42-impl`, `g41-impl` (release checklist item "consumer smoke green").

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative: test the example only as a workspace example (`cargo run -p ftui --example`). Rejected: workspace feature unification masks the consumer's default-feature view; the bug this block fixes was invisible that way.
- Risk: building `ftui` with `native-backend` and `extras` in a fresh target dir takes minutes on CI; mitigate with `actions/cache` keyed on `Cargo.lock` and the consumer manifest hash; local runs reuse `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/cargo-target` when set.
- Risk: DECSTBM expectations depend on the identity the CI runner presents (`TERM=xterm-256color`, no `TERM_PROGRAM`); until G05 lands the count is expected 0/0 there, so the assertion is "balanced", not "present". `g05-e2e` owns per-identity expectations.
- Rollback: remove the job; the script has no side effects on the repo.

## Definition of done

Job green on main for both OSes (run id in the close reason), artifact contains JSONL and captures, the deliberate-failure verification log is attached, README lists the script, and the claims-ledger rows "ftui = 0.6 works with default features" and "Minimal API Example runs" cite `consumer_smoke_e2e.sh` as proof.
close_reason: scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh landed and passed locally (exit 0, Ticks rendered, inline, terminal restored); CI wiring tracked in G04

title: docs(G01): Document default backends and the slim path in README Installation/Quick Start and getting-started
description:
## Context and why this matters

The README's consumer-facing sections currently describe a workflow that fails: README.md:303-316 says `ftui = "0.5"` (crates.io has 0.6.0 for all 17 library crates), README.md:320-333 "Quick Start" only builds the workspace and runs the demo, README.md:137-190 "Minimal API Example" does not mention that a backend feature is needed (because after G01 none is), and `docs/getting-started.md:18` and `:167-168` claim that only `ftui-core`, `ftui-layout` and `ftui-i18n` are published. The plan's "no truth mechanism between README and code" root cause (Section 2.3 item 1) means these lines were never checked. This bead writes the consumer text for the state G01 creates (default backends, slim path, `Program::open`, prelude) and registers each statement in the claims ledger so `g06-impl-checker` keeps it true. It closes onboarding gap A.4 (crates.io sentence) and the doc half of A.2/A.3; the broad README rewrite is `g06-docs-readme` and must not duplicate these sections.

## Current state (evidence)

- README.md:277-316 "Installation": tarball, git clone, workspace path dependency, "Crates.io (Published So Far)" with `ftui = "0.5"` and the sentence "Only the demo/WASM showcase targets remain workspace-local."
- README.md:320-333 "Quick Start": install nightly, clone, `cargo build`, run the showcase. No consumer step.
- README.md:349-360 "Feature Flags" table lists `ftui-core` `tracing`/`tracing-json`, `ftui-render` `tracing`, `ftui-runtime` `tracing`/`telemetry`. It does not list `ftui` facade features, `native-backend`, `crossterm-compat`, `caps-probe`, `state-persistence`, or the new `backend`.
- README.md:1200-1204 Troubleshooting "output flickers": "Inline mode uses synchronized output where supported. If you're in a very old terminal or multiplexer, expect reduced capability." (G05 rewrites this; leave it alone here.)
- README.md:431-440 "E2E Scripts" lists scripts; `consumer_smoke_e2e.sh` (from `g01-e2e`) is absent.
- `docs/getting-started.md:15-19` "Stability Notes" with the false crates.io sentence; `:165-188` "Add The Dependency" with path-only instructions; `:192-263` inline example calling `.run()?`; the "Run it" section follows.
- `docs/claims-ledger.md` does not exist yet (`g06-impl-ledger` creates it; if this bead lands first, it creates the file with the header row and its own rows, and `g06-impl-ledger` extends it).

## Target state

README "Installation" says `ftui = "0.6"`, states that default features compile a terminal backend (`native-backend` on unix, `crossterm` everywhere), shows the slim dependency line `ftui = { version = "0.6", default-features = false, features = ["runtime"] }` with the sentence "with no backend feature, `App::run()` returns `io::ErrorKind::Unsupported` naming the features to enable". "Quick Start" gains a consumer path: create a crate, add the dependency, paste the Minimal API Example, `cargo run`. "Feature Flags" lists the facade features (`runtime`, `extras`, `backend`, `native-backend`, `crossterm`) and the runtime backend features with one line each. "E2E Scripts" lists `scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh`. `docs/getting-started.md` states that all 17 library crates are on crates.io at 0.6.x, documents the default backend and slim path, and its example is marked as verified by doc-test (`g02-docs`). # epic(G41): Release and version hygiene — checklist plus idempotent release — PARTIAL -> WORKING

## Context and why this matters

README.md "Installation" (README.md:305-315) says "All 17 library crates are published on crates.io"
and then shows `ftui = "0.5"` while the workspace is at `0.6.0` (`Cargo.toml:27-28`) and all 17 crates
are `0.6.0` on crates.io (Section 1, row "crates.io"); `docs/getting-started.md:18` and `:167` say "only
`ftui-core`, `ftui-layout`, and `ftui-i18n` are published" — contradicting README; `ftui-demo-showcase`
`0.1.1` lingers on crates.io (G33); `release.yml`'s publish loop is not idempotent (Section 5.1;
`g04-11-impl`). Vision rows V66 (crates.io: WORKING, docs contradict) and V70; Section 2.2.A item 4;
Section 7.3 G41: "Release checklist file `docs/release-checklist.md`: README version string, crates.io
versions, claims ledger green, compat matrix green, consumer smoke green, CHANGELOG entry; `release.yml`
idempotent (G04.11)." The consequence: a consumer copying the README gets an old version; a release can
half-publish; and nobody can tell what "ready to release" means, so the next release repeats the
2026-08-24 v0.6.0 experience (CHANGELOG.md:12 lists it; `release.yml` failed on the re-run).

## Current state (evidence)

- `release.yml`: `verify` job checks tag vs `Cargo.toml` first `^version` (:36-54); `publish-crates`
  loop (:77-129) with the `already uploaded` text check (`g04-11-impl` fixes); no preflight of docs,
  changelog or CI status.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (70 KB): version timeline table (:12-19) through v0.6.0 (2026-08-24), sections `## [vX.Y.Z]
  -- date (GitHub Release)` with `Compare:` links (:23-30); "v0.4.0 is a tag only — there is no GitHub
  Release at that tag" (:9).
- No `docs/release-checklist.md`; `docs/` has `frankenterm-js-release-readiness.md` and
  `pane-release-gate-policy.md` (sub-system gates); `scripts/` has
  `doctor_frankentui_release_candidate_e2e.sh`, `frankenterm_js_release_rehearsal_e2e.sh`,
  `pane_release_gate.py`, `pane_release_evidence.py` — none is a whole-project release preflight.
- Gates that a release should require but that do not exist yet: claims ledger (`g06-impl`,
  `scripts/check_readme_claims.py`), compat matrix (`g05-impl`, `emulator_compat_matrix.yml` currently
  simulates profiles without real identities), consumer smoke (`g01-impl`,
  `scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh`), green streak (`g04-e2e`, `scripts/ci/green_streak.sh`).

## Target state

A release is a mechanical, checklisted act: `scripts/release_preflight.sh vX.Y.Z` verifies version
strings (workspace, README, getting-started), CHANGELOG entry, green `ci.yml` on the tag's commit, the
claims ledger/compat/consumer gates (each "required" once its bead has landed, "pending <slug>" before),
and `cargo publish --dry-run` order; `release.yml` runs it as a `preflight` job before publishing;
`docs/release-checklist.md` is the human-readable version of the same list with the commands; README
and getting-started state the current version and the full crate list.

`g41-docs` (`docs/release-checklist.md` and pointers). `g04-11-impl` first.

      `pending` rows for the rest with bead slugs.
- [ ] `release.yml` dry-run dispatch runs preflight then the idempotent loop, all `skipped`.
- [ ] README.md:313 shows `ftui = "0.6"`; `docs/getting-started.md` lists all 17 crates.
- [ ] `docs/release-checklist.md` exists and matches the script's checks one-to-one.

## Dependencies and ordering

`g41-impl` blocked by `g04-11-impl`; `g41-docs` blocked by `g41-impl`. Uses when present: `g06-impl`,
`g05-impl`, `g01-impl`, `g04-e2e`. Related owner decision: `g33-decision` (`ftui-simd` and the stale
`ftui-demo-showcase 0.1.1`). Unblocks: `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: a checklist document without a script. Documents drift; the script is the checklist and the
  document explains it.
- Rejected: bumping README to `0.6.0` by hand only. The preflight compares README to the workspace
  version so it cannot drift again.
- Risk: `cargo publish --dry-run` cannot fully validate a workspace whose new versions are unpublished
  (path deps); the script reports that limitation explicitly rather than failing.

Children closed; preflight wired into `release.yml`; docs truthful; evidence in close reasons.

# task(G41): `scripts/release_preflight.sh` + `release.yml` preflight job + version strings in README/getting-started

## Context and why this matters

README.md:313 shows `ftui = "0.5"` although the workspace and crates.io are at 0.6.0 (`Cargo.toml:28`;
Section 1 crates.io row), `docs/getting-started.md:18,167` claims only three crates are published, and
the last v0.6.0 release re-run failed in `release.yml` on `ftui-simd@0.6.0 already exists`
(`g04-11-impl`). Vision rows V66, V70; Section 2.2.A item 4; Section 7.3 G41. This bead makes "ready to
release" a command whose output is the evidence, and wires it before publishing. Parent: `g41-epic`.

## Current state (evidence)

- `release.yml:27-54` `verify` (tag == first `^version` in root `Cargo.toml`); `:59-131` `publish-crates`
  (needs `verify`; skipped for pre-release tags `:64-65`; token-gated `:74`).
- Version sources: `Cargo.toml:27-28 [workspace.package] version = "0.6.0"`; `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml:3
  version = "0.6.0"` and its 17-crate dependency list at `:22-30`; README.md:305-315 (crate list of 17 +
  `ftui = "0.5"`); `docs/getting-started.md:18` "As of today, only `ftui-core`, `ftui-layout`, and
  `ftui-i18n` are published on crates.io", `:167` "Right now only a subset of crates are published".
- `CHANGELOG.md:12-19` version table; `:23` `## [v0.6.0] -- 2026-08-24 (GitHub Release)`.
- crates.io API: `https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/<name>` returns `crate.max_version`;
  `https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/<name>/<version>` returns 200 when published (needs a User-Agent).
- Gates from other blocks (may not exist yet): `scripts/check_readme_claims.py` (`g06-impl`),
  `scripts/pty_identity_matrix.py`/`docs/compat-matrix.md` (`g05-impl`), `scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh`
  (`g01-impl`), `scripts/ci/green_streak.sh` (`g04-e2e`), `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh` (exists;
  run by CI only after `g25-impl`).

## Target state

`scripts/release_preflight.sh vX.Y.Z [--strict]` prints one line per check
(`check | status(pass|fail|pending:<slug>) | detail`) and JSONL to `--out`, exits 1 on any `fail` (and
on `pending` when `--strict`); `release.yml` has a `preflight` job between `verify` and `publish-crates`
and a `dry_run` path (from `g04-11-impl`); README and getting-started state the real version and
crate list, and the preflight keeps them honest.

## Implementation plan

1. `scripts/release_preflight.sh`: checks, in order —
   `workspace_version` (root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package] version` == tag minus `v`);
   `facade_version` (`crates/ftui/Cargo.toml` and every `crates/*/Cargo.toml` with `publish != false`
   equal the workspace version; list mismatches);
   `readme_version` (README.md `ftui = "<major.minor>"` line equals the tag's major.minor);
   `readme_crate_list` (the 17 names in README.md:305-311 equal the set of publishable crates from
   `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 | jq` minus `publish = false` ones);
   `getting_started` (no sentence claiming a subset is published: `rg -n "only .* are published"
   docs/getting-started.md` empty);
   `changelog_entry` (`## [vX.Y.Z]` heading exists in CHANGELOG.md and the timeline table has the row);
   `git_tag_on_main` (tag commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`);
   `ci_green_on_commit` (`gh run list --commit <sha> --workflow ci.yml --json conclusion` has a
   `success`; fall back to `scripts/ci/green_streak.sh` when present);
   `claims_ledger` (`python3 scripts/check_readme_claims.py` if present, else `pending:g06-impl`);
   `compat_matrix` (`docs/compat-matrix.md` generated within 30 days and its JSONL has no `fail`, if
   present, else `pending:g05-impl`);
   `consumer_smoke` (`scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh` exit 0 if present, else `pending:g01-impl`);
   `perf_gate` (`scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh --json` exit 0 if `tests/baseline.json` rows exist for
   the plan's budgets, else `pending:g25-impl`);
   `cratesio_state` (for each crate: the version is not yet published — else `note: already
   published, loop will skip`; and `max_version` <= tag);
   `publish_dry_run` (`cargo publish -p <crate> --dry-run` in the `release.yml` order; report the
   path-dependency limitation as `note`, not `fail`, when the error is "no matching package named
   ... found" for an unpublished sibling).
2. `release.yml`: new job `preflight` (`needs: verify`, ubuntu, `./.github/actions/rust-pin`, `gh`
   available by default) running `scripts/release_preflight.sh v${{ needs.verify.outputs.version }}
   --out preflight.jsonl`, uploading `preflight.jsonl`; `publish-crates` gets `needs: [verify,
   preflight]`. In `dry_run` mode the preflight runs without `--strict`.
3. README.md:313 -> `ftui = "0.6"`; `docs/getting-started.md:18,167` -> "All 17 library crates are
   published on crates.io at the workspace version; see README Installation." (`g06-impl` owns the
   broader rewrite; these two lines are needed now for the preflight to pass and are ledger rows).
4. `ubs` on the script and YAML; `shellcheck` if available.

## Files to change

- `scripts/release_preflight.sh`: new.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: `preflight` job; `needs` edge.
- `README.md:313`, `docs/getting-started.md:18,167`: version/crate-list truth.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `scripts/release_preflight.sh v0.6.0` on `main`: `workspace_version`, `facade_version`,
      `readme_version`, `readme_crate_list`, `getting_started`, `changelog_entry`, `git_tag_on_main`,
      `cratesio_state` = pass; `ci_green_on_commit` = pass once `g04-e2e` lands (else fail — expected
      today, recorded); the rest `pending:<slug>` until their beads land (output pasted).
- [ ] `release.yml` dispatch `tag=v0.6.0 dry_run=true`: `preflight` job green (non-strict), artifact
      `preflight.jsonl` present, publish loop all `skipped`/`dry-run-ok` (run id).
- [ ] Negative (scratch branch): README reverted to `ftui = "0.5"` -> preflight `readme_version fail`
      (output pasted).
- [ ] `g41-docs` checklist rows map one-to-one to the script's check names.

## Tests and logging

Shell test `scripts/release_preflight_test.sh`: stubs `gh`, `curl`, `cargo` on `PATH`; fixtures for
(a) all-pass, (b) README version drift, (c) missing changelog heading, (d) crate list mismatch, (e)
`pending` handling with/without `--strict`; asserts statuses and exit codes; validates the JSONL
(`check`, `status`, `detail`, `elapsed_s`). Logging: table on stdout, JSONL file, `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`
in CI.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-11-impl` (idempotent loop; the preflight's `cratesio_state` complements it). Uses when
present: `g06-impl`, `g05-impl`, `g01-impl`, `g04-e2e`, `g25-impl`. Unblocks: `g41-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: hard-failing on `pending` checks by default. Releases must remain possible while the bridge
  plan is in progress; `--strict` is for the final state (`g42-impl` flips `release.yml` to `--strict`).
- Risk: `cargo metadata` includes non-published members (`doctor_frankentui`, `ftui-demo-showcase`,
  `ftui-showcase-wasm` have `publish = false`? verify each; the script reads the `publish` field).

## Definition of done

Script + tests committed; `release.yml` preflight job green in dry-run dispatch; README/getting-started
lines fixed; outputs and run id in the close reason.
notes: Refinement 1 supersedes the old non-strict/pending-green acceptance: mandatory release preflight checks fail closed from first use; diagnostic pending output is never publish authorization. Candidate packaging and real post-publication registry verification are separate phases, so preflight must not depend on publishing first. Existing 0.6.0 cannot be replaced. New G43 tasks .10.3/.10.4 own dependency-origin proof; skipped existing packages only prove idempotency, not shipment of new source.

title: docs(G41): docs/release-checklist.md mirroring the preflight, linked from README, AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG
description:
# docs(G41): `docs/release-checklist.md` mirroring the preflight, linked from README, AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG

## Context and why this matters

There is no release checklist in the repository (`ls docs | grep -i release` on 2026-09-01 shows only
`frankenterm-js-release-readiness.md` and `pane-release-gate-policy.md`, both sub-system gates). The
v0.6.0 release (CHANGELOG.md:12, 2026-08-24) left README at `ftui = "0.5"` (README.md:313),
getting-started claiming three published crates (`docs/getting-started.md:18,167`), and a failing
`release.yml` re-run. Section 7.3 G41 names the checklist's rows: README version string, crates.io
versions, claims ledger green, compat matrix green, consumer smoke green, CHANGELOG entry, idempotent
`release.yml`. `g41-impl` implements the same rows as `scripts/release_preflight.sh`; this bead writes
the human-readable checklist so a release engineer (or agent) knows the order, the commands, and what
each `pending:<slug>` means. Parent: `g41-epic`.

## Current state (evidence)

- `release.yml` triggers on `v*` tags and `workflow_dispatch` with `tag` (and after `g04-11-impl`,
  `dry_run`); `verify` -> `preflight` (after `g41-impl`) -> `publish-crates`.
- CHANGELOG.md format: timeline table rows `| [vX.Y.Z](link) | Release|Tag | date | summary |`, sections
  `## [vX.Y.Z] -- YYYY-MM-DD (GitHub Release)` with `Compare:` links (CHANGELOG.md:12-30).
- AGENTS.md has no release section; README.md has "Installation" (:305-315) and no release/contributor
  process.
- Owner decisions affecting releases: `g33-decision` (`ftui-simd` publish or yank; `ftui-demo-showcase`
  0.1.1 yank or README-only 0.6.0).

## Target state

`docs/release-checklist.md` with: preconditions (green streak, owner decisions resolved), the exact
command sequence (`scripts/release_preflight.sh vX.Y.Z --strict`, version bump procedure, CHANGELOG
entry format, tag + push, `release.yml` dry-run dispatch, real run, post-release verification via
crates.io API and docs.rs build status), a table mapping each preflight check name to what it proves and
the bead that introduced it, a "when a check is `pending`" section, and a rollback/yank procedure
(`cargo yank` needs owner permission; never delete tags). Linked from README "Installation" (one line),
AGENTS.md (one line under "Landing the Plane" or a new "Releasing" heading), and CHANGELOG.md's header.

## Implementation plan

1. Write `docs/release-checklist.md` (target 80-120 lines) with the sections above; the check table
   must list exactly the `check` names printed by `scripts/release_preflight.sh` (`workspace_version`,
   `facade_version`, `readme_version`, `readme_crate_list`, `getting_started`, `changelog_entry`,
   `git_tag_on_main`, `ci_green_on_commit`, `claims_ledger`, `compat_matrix`, `consumer_smoke`,
   `perf_gate`, `cratesio_state`, `publish_dry_run`).
2. Version bump procedure: edit `Cargo.toml [workspace.package] version` and every internal dependency
   version in `crates/*/Cargo.toml` (they are pinned, e.g. `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml:22-30`
   `version = "0.6.0"`) — by hand or with parallel subagents, never a script (AGENTS.md "No Script-Based
   Changes"); README `ftui = "X.Y"`; run the preflight; commit `chore(release): vX.Y.Z`.
3. CHANGELOG entry: follow the existing format; the preflight's `changelog_entry` check enforces the
   heading.
4. Post-release: `curl https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/ftui | jq .crate.max_version`, docs.rs build
   status for `ftui`, `git push origin main:master` (AGENTS.md:37-39 rule), close the release bead with
   `ci-run:<release run id>`.
5. Add the three links (README, AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG header).
6. Add a "Checks vs checklist" one-liner to `scripts/release_preflight_test.sh` (`g41-impl`): every
   check name printed by the script appears in `docs/release-checklist.md` (grep), so the two cannot
   drift.

## Files to change

- `docs/release-checklist.md`: new.
- `README.md` (Installation, one line), `AGENTS.md` (one line), `CHANGELOG.md` (header line).
- `scripts/release_preflight_test.sh`: drift check.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Every preflight check name appears in the checklist (grep count == 14).
- [ ] Links present in the three files (`rg -n "release-checklist.md" README.md AGENTS.md CHANGELOG.md`
      = 3 hits).
- [ ] A dry-run dispatch of `release.yml` executed while following the checklist step by step; any
      step that did not match reality fixed in the same PR (note in the close reason).

## Tests and logging

Docs bead: the grep drift check in `release_preflight_test.sh`; the dry-run walk-through's run id.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g41-impl` (the checklist documents the script's checks). Related: `g33-decision`,
`g06-impl` (ledger rows for README version and crate list). Unblocks: `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: putting the checklist only in AGENTS.md. Releases are rare and long; a dedicated doc keeps
  AGENTS.md short; AGENTS.md links it.
- Risk: the `pending` rows tempt people to release with gates missing; the doc states that `--strict` is
  required once `g42-impl` closes.

## Definition of done

Checklist written, linked, drift-checked; dry-run walk-through evidence in the close reason.

title: G43: Isolated registry consumer and immutable release identity
description:
The actual ftui 0.6.0 archive was published August 24 and defaults to runtime+extras, while README/getting-started describe September source with backend and prelude fixes. Existing consumer_smoke_e2e.sh only tests source/path dependencies and its --scratch mode assumes SCRATCH/target despite inherited CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Extend existing smoke/release tooling with separately named source, packaged-candidate and registry modes. In registry mode use a fresh standalone workspace and explicit toolchain/config; record Cargo.lock package source/checksum/features and reject hidden patch/path/git substitution. Test minimal and streaming facade consumers without workspace feature unification. Bind docs to the actual accepted version; prepare a new version rather than treating skip-already-published as shipping changed 0.6.0. Do not publish as part of this task.

Verification contract (companion task):
Build the current README/getting-started examples from the actual registry in a clean consumer, record failures as failures, then prove the corrected release once it exists. Exercise nondefault CARGO_TARGET_DIR, parent Cargo config with path patch, custom CARGO_HOME, offline/cache state, missing toolchain and feature-disabled Unsupported diagnostics. Assert package source/checksum and no hidden workspace features. PTY acceptance must render, process input/stream logs, quit with exit 0 and restore actual termios and terminal modes. Unit-test identity validation; real registry E2E cannot be replaced by mocked downloads. Candidate-package acceptance and post-publication acceptance are distinct.

Context: September 4 reality check at 21a4e48b. Source and shipped 0.6.0 are different evidence domains. Preserve all current functionality and in-progress ownership; no file deletion, yanking, publishing, or compatibility shims are authorized by this task. Use existing files where coherent, manual edits, Cargo only. Acceptance must identify exact commit, feature set, target, toolchain, command, exit status and artifact hashes; skipped/missing evidence remains unproven. Run the relevant unit/property and real integration/E2E checks, archive diagnostic logs with seeds and bounded redacted payloads, and run workspace check, Clippy -D warnings, fmt --check and rustdoc -D warnings for substantive Rust changes. Do not close on compilation alone.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Implement the complete scoped contract without losing existing functionality.
- [ ] Unit/property and error-boundary checks specified below pass.
- [ ] Companion real integration/E2E proof is linked with exact provenance and useful redacted logs.
- [ ] Apply the ambition-regeneration boundary and evidence requirements in the notes; preserve both successes and failures.
notes:
