title: epic(G07): Quarantine dead modules behind experimental, gate reachability in CI, exercise unused widgets
description:
## Context and why this matters

The README presents an "alien artifact" intelligence layer (W-TinyLFU width cache, S3-FIFO caches, PAC-Bayes Count-Min sketch, e-processes with GRAPA, flat combining, rough-path signatures, SOS barrier certificates, lenses, IVM DAG, SLO safe mode, accessibility tree, height prediction, e-graph layout optimizer, time-travel debugging, ...) as features of the framework. The reality check of 2026-09-01 (commit `ab07291f`) found that roughly half of that layer is code that compiles and has unit tests but is unreachable from any production path: it is never called from `Program`, `Frame`, `TerminalWriter`, any widget's `render`, or the demo showcase. Two files are not even compiled. The root cause (Section 2.3 of the reality check) is that hundreds of beads were closed on "module + unit tests exist" with no "reachable from production" definition of done, so parallel unused implementations accreted (three width caches, two e-process controllers, two degradation ladders, two evidence ledgers, two CUSUM allocation monitors).

This epic closes Section 2.2.B (intelligence layer dead/off/mis-described) and vision rows V12-V25, V45, V46, V55, V58-V60 by doing three things: (1) quarantine every dead internal module behind an `experimental` cargo feature so the README can be truthful immediately; (2) add a CI reachability gate so new orphans cannot appear; (3) exercise the legitimate-but-unused public widgets and harness types in the showcase so they are proven rather than hidden. The wiring of modules that SHOULD be live is delegated to sibling blocks: width cache G08, a11y G09, VirtualizedList G10, conformal G11, BOCPD G12, controllers G13, keybinding G14, gesture/hover G18, hint ranker G19, evidence G20, SAT and caps ledger G28.

User-visible consequence today: a consumer reading the README believes `TimeTravel`, `field_lens!`, `slo.yaml` safe mode, IVM, the SOS barrier, etc. are usable framework features; none of them does anything in a running program, and two of the README's headline algorithms (PAC-Bayes CMS, timeline aggregator) are not compiled at all.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs` declares 64 `pub mod` lines (counted with `rg -c '^\s*pub mod '` on 2026-09-01; the plan document says 63). About 30 of them (~25K lines) have no production reference. `rg -n 'timeline_aggregator|countmin_sketch' crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs` returns nothing: `timeline_aggregator.rs` (990 lines, mtime 2026-02-06) and `countmin_sketch.rs` (1,022 lines, mtime 2026-03-03) are orphan files that are never compiled.
- No crate in the workspace has an `experimental` feature (`rg -n experimental crates/*/Cargo.toml` is empty). `ftui-runtime` features today: `default = []`, `render-thread`, `stdio-capture`, `tracing`, `state-persistence`, `policy-config`, `crossterm-compat`, `native-backend`, `hamt`, `event-trace`, `telemetry`, `asupersync-executor`.
- Modules referenced only by their own file plus `lib.rs` (verified with rg over `crates/*/tests`, `benches`, `ftui-harness`, `ftui-demo-showcase`, `doctor_frankentui`): `rough_path`, `flat_combine`, `lens`, `alpha_investing`, `validation_pipeline`, `conformal_stages`, `resize_sla`, `reversible`, `schedule_trace`, `wasm_runner`, `diff_evidence`.
- Modules referenced only by test/bench files (list in `g07-impl`): `ivm`, `cost_model`, `sos_barrier`, `flake_detector`, `slo`, `policy_config`, `policy_registry`, `evidence_bridges`, `degradation_cascade`, `conformal_frame_guard`, `conformal_alert`, `eprocess_throttle`, `allocation_budget`.
- Other crates: `crates/ftui-render/src/lib.rs:45 pub mod roaring_bitmap` (callers: only `tests/e2e_roaring_dirty_tracking.rs`, `tests/proptest_roaring_bitmap_invariants.rs`, `tests/roaring_dirty_e2e.rs`, `benches/roaring_bench.rs`); `crates/ftui-text/src/lib.rs:86 pub mod tier_budget` (only `tests/proptest_layout_shaping_invariants.rs`, `tests/snapshot_justified_matrix.rs`); `crates/ftui-layout/src/lib.rs:46 pub mod egraph` (`solve_layout` at `egraph.rs:768` and `solve_layout_default` at `:801` have no callers); `crates/ftui-layout/src/cache.rs:441 S3FifoLayoutCache` (used only by the `lib.rs:67` re-export and `tests/layout_cache_ratio.rs`, while `CoherenceCache` at `cache.rs:618` is live via `crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs:380`); `crates/ftui-widgets/src/command_palette/scorer.rs:973 pub struct ConformalRanker` (re-exported at `command_palette/mod.rs:39`, used only by the test at `scorer.rs:2049`).
- Public widgets and harness types with no production or demo consumer: `DecisionCard` (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/decision_card.rs:56`), `DriftVisualization` (`drift_visualization.rs:197`), `CachedWidget<W, K>` (`cached.rs:56`), `ErrorBoundary<W>` (`error_boundary.rs:144`); `TimeTravel` (`crates/ftui-harness/src/time_travel.rs:287`, `new(capacity)` `:308`, `record(&Buffer, FrameMetadata)` `:325`, `get` `:411`, `rewind` `:429`) and `TimeTravelInspector` (`time_travel_inspector.rs:16`, `seek(index, &TimeTravel)` `:32`). `rg DecisionCard|DriftVisualization|CachedWidget|ErrorBoundary crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src` is empty. The `snapshot_player` screen keeps its own `frames: Vec<Buffer>` (`snapshot_player.rs:414`) and `current_frame` (`:418`); `TimeTravel` appears there only as the tab label (`:1770`) and a doc comment (`:16`).
- No `scripts/check_module_reachability.py` and no `docs/module-reachability-allowlist.txt` exist.
- CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `check` job (`:23-85`) runs fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, a no-mock `rg` policy step, build, `cargo test --workspace --lib`, and all-features tests on nightly; the `features` job (`:119-157`) checks extras features, `ftui-widgets --features debug-overlay`, `ftui-runtime --no-default-features --features native-backend`, and `--workspace --no-default-features`.

## Target state

Every declared module in every crate is either reachable from a production path with a test proving it, or is compiled only under `--features experimental` and listed in a README "Experimental modules" section with one line per module and the feature flag. `timeline_aggregator` and `countmin_sketch` are declared (under the feature) and compile. `scripts/check_module_reachability.py` runs in the CI `check` job with an allowlist that may only shrink. `DecisionCard`, `DriftVisualization`, `CachedWidget`, `ErrorBoundary<W>` each have a `widget_gallery` entry and an insta snapshot; the `snapshot_player` scrubber is backed by `TimeTravel` + `TimeTravelInspector`. Deletions (of loser width caches, merged duplicates, and the seven "never referenced" modules) happen only after explicit written owner permission recorded in `g07-decision`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `scripts/check_module_reachability.py` exits 0 on `main` in the `check` job, and exits 1 when a scratch `pub mod orphan;` is added to any crate's `lib.rs` without a non-test reference (verified once during rollout, documented in the close reason).
- [ ] `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --features experimental` both green; the `features` job includes the experimental combination.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` green with and without the feature.
- [ ] README "Experimental modules" section exists; each listed module's `tests/*.rs` and `benches/*.rs` are gated with `#![cfg(feature = "experimental")]` (or the bench target has `required-features = ["experimental"]` in `Cargo.toml`).
- [ ] Snapshots `widget_gallery_decision_card_80x24.snap`, `widget_gallery_drift_visualization_80x24.snap`, `widget_gallery_cached_widget_80x24.snap`, `widget_gallery_error_boundary_80x24.snap` exist and pass; `snapshot_player_scrub_frame_5_80x24.snap` shows the scrubbed frame from `TimeTravel::get(5)`.
- [ ] Deletion list in `g07-decision` answered by the owner in writing before any `git rm`.

## Implementation plan (block level; each step is a child bead)

1. `g07-impl`: add `experimental = []` to `ftui-runtime`, `ftui-widgets`, `ftui-layout`, `ftui-render`, `ftui-text`, `ftui-core`, `ftui-harness`; gate the `pub mod` lines and their test/bench files; declare `timeline_aggregator` and `countmin_sketch` under the feature and fix whatever no longer compiles.
2. `g07-impl-gate`: write `scripts/check_module_reachability.py`, seed `docs/module-reachability-allowlist.txt` from today's set, wire into the `check` job and add the experimental combination to `features`.
3. `g07-impl-gallery`: widget gallery entries + snapshots for the four widgets; `snapshot_player` scrubber over `TimeTravel`/`TimeTravelInspector`.
4. `g07-tests`: unit tests for the gate script (fixture crates), feature-matrix compile tests, snapshot tests.
5. `g07-decision`: owner permission for the deletion list.
6. `g07-docs`: README "Experimental modules" section, AGENTS.md note on the reachability gate.

## Dependencies and ordering

- No dependency for quarantine and the gate; G13 (`g13-impl`) must land before the merged duplicate pairs (`eprocess_throttle`, `degradation_cascade`, `diff_evidence`, `allocation_budget`) are deleted; they are quarantined here first.
- This epic unblocks `g06-impl` (claims ledger needs to know what is experimental), `g13-impl` (quarantine mechanics), `g21-impl` (orphans compile under the feature).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Quarantine before delete (reality-check convention 7.0): the feature flag makes the README truthful today without asking permission for every file; deletion stays a separate owner decision because AGENTS.md rule 1 forbids deleting any file without explicit written permission.
- Alternative rejected: deleting orphans outright (forbidden) or leaving them compiled but documented as "internal" (still misleading and still costs compile time for every consumer).
- Risk: gating `pub mod` lines can break `pub use` re-exports in `lib.rs` and downstream `doctor_frankentui`/`ftui-harness` imports; each gated module needs its re-exports gated with the same `#[cfg]`. The gate script catches regressions.
- Risk: the two orphan files have been un-compiled since Feb/Mar 2026 and will need API fixes (e.g. `CountMinSketch` name clash with `ftui_text::width_cache::CountMinSketch` at `width_cache.rs:807`, which is a second CMS implementation).
- Rollback: the feature is additive; removing `#[cfg(feature = "experimental")]` restores today's state.

## Definition of done

All child beads closed; the reachability gate is green on `main`; the README section exists; the deletion decision is recorded (permission granted or refused) and any permitted deletions are done in the owning `g13-impl`/`g08-impl` beads with the permission text quoted in the commit message. Close reason names the CI run id of the first green `check` job with the gate.

title: task(G07): Add experimental feature, gate 26 dead modules, declare the two orphan files
description:
## Context and why this matters

The README lists lenses, IVM, SLO safe mode, SOS barriers, rough paths, flat combining, alpha investing, flake detection, multi-stage conformal monitors, and a PAC-Bayes Count-Min sketch as framework features. In the code these modules are compiled into every consumer's build yet nothing in `Program`, `Frame`, `TerminalWriter`, any widget, or the showcase calls them; two of them are not compiled at all. This bead puts every such internal module behind one `experimental` cargo feature (per crate) so that (a) the README can say "experimental" truthfully (G06/G07 docs), (b) consumers stop paying compile time for dead code, and (c) the reachability gate (`g07-impl-gate`) has a clean baseline. It closes the "quarantine" half of Section 2.2.B and vision rows V14, V16-V19, V22-V25, V58, V59.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs` `pub mod` lines (verified 2026-09-01): `allocation_budget` :28, `alpha_investing` :29, `conformal_alert` :34, `conformal_frame_guard` :35, `conformal_stages` :37, `cost_model` :38, `degradation_cascade` :41, `diff_evidence` :43, `eprocess_throttle` :45, `evidence_bridges` :48, `flake_detector` :51, `flat_combine` :52, `ivm` :55, `lens` :56, `policy_config` :61, `policy_registry` :62, `resize_sla` :70, `reversible` :72, `rough_path` :73, `slo` :76, `sos_barrier` :77, `validation_pipeline` :89, `wasm_runner` :91, `schedule_trace` :94. Existing `#[cfg(feature = ...)]` gates are only on `event_trace` :46, `render_thread` :66, `stdio_capture` :79, `telemetry` :95.
- Not declared anywhere in `lib.rs`: `crates/ftui-runtime/src/timeline_aggregator.rs` (990 lines; `TimelineAggregator` :300 with `new` :330, `observe` :351, `stats` :425, `estimate` :434, `current_evidence` :439, `calibrate` :499; header says bd-11ck.7) and `crates/ftui-runtime/src/countmin_sketch.rs` (1,022 lines; `SketchConfig` :68, `ErrorEvidence` :101 with `pac_bayes_kl_term` :119, `CountMinSketch` :168 with `new` :195, `with_dimensions` :225, `increment` :247, `add` :252).
- Test/bench files that import the quarantine modules (each must be gated or they fail to compile without the feature): `ivm` -> `benches/ivm_bench.rs`, `tests/e2e_ivm_incremental_views.rs`, `tests/proptest_ivm_invariants.rs`; `cost_model` -> `tests/proptest_cost_model_invariants.rs`; `sos_barrier` -> `tests/e2e_sos_barrier.rs`, `tests/e2e_recipe_b_tail_safe.rs`, `tests/sos_barrier_integration.rs`; `flake_detector` -> `tests/proptest_statistical_invariants.rs`; `slo` -> `tests/slo_yaml_validation.rs`; `policy_config`/`policy_registry` -> `tests/policy_e2e.rs`, `tests/policy_controller_tests.rs`, `tests/e2e_recipe_f_policy_as_data.rs`; `evidence_bridges` -> `tests/e2e_unified_evidence.rs`; `degradation_cascade` -> `tests/policy_controller_tests.rs`, `tests/e2e_recipe_b_tail_safe.rs`, `tests/e2e_recipe_f_policy_as_data.rs`, `tests/recipe_b_tail_safe_controller.rs`; `conformal_frame_guard` -> the same three minus `e2e_recipe_f`; `conformal_alert` -> `tests/proptest_voi_conformal_invariants.rs`; `eprocess_throttle` -> `tests/e2e_unified_evidence.rs`, `tests/proptest_statistical_invariants.rs`, `tests/policy_controller_tests.rs`, `tests/e2e_recipe_b_tail_safe.rs`, `tests/voi_eprocess_unit_tests.rs`; `allocation_budget` -> `tests/proptest_allocation_budget_invariants.rs`. In-crate cross references: `src/evidence_bridges.rs` uses `eprocess_throttle`; `src/policy_config.rs` uses `degradation_cascade`.
- Other crates: `crates/ftui-render/src/lib.rs:45 pub mod roaring_bitmap` with `tests/e2e_roaring_dirty_tracking.rs`, `tests/proptest_roaring_bitmap_invariants.rs`, `tests/roaring_dirty_e2e.rs`, `benches/roaring_bench.rs`; `crates/ftui-text/src/lib.rs:86 pub mod tier_budget` with `tests/proptest_layout_shaping_invariants.rs`, `tests/snapshot_justified_matrix.rs`; `crates/ftui-layout/src/lib.rs:46 pub mod egraph`; `crates/ftui-layout/src/cache.rs:441 S3FifoLayoutCache` re-exported at `lib.rs:66-67` and used by `tests/layout_cache_ratio.rs`; `crates/ftui-widgets/src/command_palette/scorer.rs:973 ConformalRanker` re-exported at `command_palette/mod.rs:39`.
- `crates/ftui-text/src/width_cache.rs` (`pub mod width_cache` at `lib.rs:63`, re-exports `:167-169`) is handled by G08, not here: the winner moves into ftui-core and the losers are quarantined or deleted there.

## Target state

`experimental = []` exists in the `[features]` table of `ftui-runtime`, `ftui-widgets`, `ftui-layout`, `ftui-render`, `ftui-text`, `ftui-core`, `ftui-harness` (ftui-core and ftui-harness get the flag even if nothing is gated there yet, so the gate script and the `features` job have a uniform matrix). Every module in the quarantine list, its `lib.rs` re-exports, and every test/bench file that imports it compile only with the feature. `timeline_aggregator` and `countmin_sketch` are declared under the feature and compile. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` is green with and without `--features experimental`.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml`: add `experimental = []` under `[features]` with a doc comment: "Compiles research modules that are not reachable from Program/Frame/TerminalWriter. Not part of the supported API. See README 'Experimental modules'." Add `required-features = ["experimental"]` to a `[[bench]] name = "ivm_bench"` entry (create the entry; criterion benches need `harness = false`, copy the pattern from the existing bench entries in the same file).
2. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs`: prefix each of the 24 `pub mod` lines listed above with `#[cfg(feature = "experimental")]`, and add `#[cfg(feature = "experimental")] pub mod timeline_aggregator;` and `#[cfg(feature = "experimental")] pub mod countmin_sketch;`. Gate every `pub use` that re-exports items from those modules with the same attribute (search `lib.rs` for each module name; `degradation_cascade` and `policy_config` are re-exported in the lines after :100). Keep the order alphabetical as the file is today.
3. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/evidence_bridges.rs` and `src/policy_config.rs`: both are themselves quarantined, so their internal references need no change; verify with `cargo check -p ftui-runtime` (no feature) that nothing outside the quarantine set imports them (the `policy-config` cargo feature enables `dep:toml` for `policy_config.rs`; make `policy-config` imply `experimental` in Cargo.toml: `policy-config = ["experimental", "dep:serde", "dep:serde_json", "dep:toml"]`, so the existing feature keeps working).
4. Gate test files: add `#![cfg(feature = "experimental")]` as the first line of each test file listed in "Current state" (this is a hand edit per file; AGENTS.md forbids script-based edits; use parallel subagents if desired, one file each). Benches use `required-features` instead of an inner attribute.
5. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/timeline_aggregator.rs` and `countmin_sketch.rs`: compile them under the feature and fix what broke since 2026-02/03 (expect: import paths for `bocpd`, `conformal_alert`, `evidence_sink`; `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` inner attributes at the top of each file must move to `lib.rs` or be removed since inner attributes in non-root modules are rejected for `forbid` at crate level; clippy pedantic/nursery lints). Do NOT rename `CountMinSketch` in ftui-text; the two types live in different crates.
6. `crates/ftui-render/Cargo.toml` + `src/lib.rs`: `experimental = []`; gate `pub mod roaring_bitmap` and its three test files; `roaring_bench` gets `required-features`.
7. `crates/ftui-text/Cargo.toml` + `src/lib.rs`: `experimental = []`; gate `pub mod tier_budget` (:86) and its two test files. Leave `width_cache` alone (G08).
8. `crates/ftui-layout/Cargo.toml` + `src/lib.rs`: `experimental = []`; gate `pub mod egraph` (:46) and the `S3FifoLayoutCache` re-export in the `pub use cache::{...}` list at `:66-67` (split the `pub use` so `CoherenceCache`, `CoherenceId`, `LayoutCache`, `LayoutCacheKey`, `LayoutCacheStats` stay ungated); gate `tests/layout_cache_ratio.rs`; in `cache.rs` wrap `S3FifoLayoutCache` and its impl/tests in `#[cfg(feature = "experimental")]`.
9. `crates/ftui-widgets/Cargo.toml` + `src/command_palette/mod.rs` + `scorer.rs`: `experimental = []`; gate the `ConformalRanker` struct, impls, its re-export at `mod.rs:39`, and the test at `scorer.rs:2049`. `height_predictor` (`lib.rs:164`) and `fenwick` (`lib.rs:158`) are NOT gated: G10 wires them.
10. `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml` and `crates/ftui-harness/Cargo.toml`: `experimental = []` (empty for now; G08 may use ftui-core's).
11. Do not gate `sos_barrier_coeffs.rs` separately: it is a private `mod` inside `sos_barrier.rs`'s neighborhood; G21 owns its header. Do not touch `degradation_cascade`, `eprocess_throttle`, `diff_evidence`, `allocation_budget` beyond gating: G13 merges them.
12. Run `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, the same with `--features experimental` (per crate: `-p ftui-runtime --features experimental`, etc.; the workspace-level flag requires the feature to exist in every member, which is why step 10 adds it to core and harness; ftui-web, ftui-tty, ftui-backend, ftui-a11y, ftui-i18n, ftui-style, ftui-pty, ftui-extras, doctor_frankentui, showcase get `experimental = []` too if `cargo check --workspace --features experimental` complains), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` both ways, `cargo fmt --check`, then `ubs` on every touched file.

What NOT to do: no deletions (owner permission required, see `g07-decision`); no compatibility shims such as re-exporting a stub type when the feature is off; no new `*_v2` files; no script-driven edits.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml`: `experimental` feature; `policy-config` implies it; `[[bench]]` entry for `ivm_bench` with `required-features`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs`: 24 gated `pub mod` lines + 2 new declarations + gated re-exports.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/timeline_aggregator.rs`, `countmin_sketch.rs`: compile fixes only.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/tests/{e2e_ivm_incremental_views,proptest_ivm_invariants,proptest_cost_model_invariants,e2e_sos_barrier,e2e_recipe_b_tail_safe,sos_barrier_integration,proptest_statistical_invariants,slo_yaml_validation,policy_e2e,policy_controller_tests,e2e_recipe_f_policy_as_data,e2e_unified_evidence,recipe_b_tail_safe_controller,proptest_voi_conformal_invariants,voi_eprocess_unit_tests,proptest_allocation_budget_invariants}.rs`: `#![cfg(feature = "experimental")]`.
- `crates/ftui-render/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs}`, `tests/{e2e_roaring_dirty_tracking,proptest_roaring_bitmap_invariants,roaring_dirty_e2e}.rs`.
- `crates/ftui-text/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs}`, `tests/{proptest_layout_shaping_invariants,snapshot_justified_matrix}.rs`.
- `crates/ftui-layout/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs,src/cache.rs}`, `tests/layout_cache_ratio.rs`.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/{Cargo.toml,src/command_palette/mod.rs,src/command_palette/scorer.rs}`.
- `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml`, `crates/ftui-harness/Cargo.toml`: empty `experimental` feature.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` green (no feature): proves every gated test/bench file is gated.
- [ ] `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --features experimental` green: proves the two orphans compile.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` green both ways.
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-runtime --features experimental --test e2e_sos_barrier` and `--test proptest_ivm_invariants` still pass (the quarantined tests are not deleted, they are gated).
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-runtime --lib` passes without the feature (no production test depended on a quarantined module).
- [ ] `rg -n 'pub mod (rough_path|flat_combine|lens|ivm|cost_model|sos_barrier|alpha_investing|flake_detector|slo|policy_config|policy_registry|evidence_bridges|validation_pipeline|degradation_cascade|conformal_frame_guard|conformal_alert|conformal_stages|eprocess_throttle|allocation_budget|resize_sla|reversible|schedule_trace|wasm_runner|diff_evidence|timeline_aggregator|countmin_sketch)' crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs -B1` shows a `#[cfg(feature = "experimental")]` line above every match.

## Tests and logging

- Unit: `crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs` test `experimental_modules_are_gated` (under `#[cfg(all(test, not(feature = "experimental")))]`) asserts via `cfg!` that the feature is off; and `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "experimental"))]` test `timeline_aggregator_and_cms_compile` constructs `timeline_aggregator::TimelineAggregator::new(AggregatorConfig::default())` and `countmin_sketch::CountMinSketch::with_dimensions(64, 4)`, adds 100 items, and asserts `estimate` >= true count (CMS never under-estimates).
- Feature-matrix compile checks are CI steps, not tests (see `g07-impl-gate`).
- Logging: none at runtime; the CI step prints `cargo check` output. `ubs` output for each touched file is pasted into the close reason if non-empty.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: nothing.
- Unblocks: `g07-impl-gate` (allowlist baseline), `g07-docs`, `g13-impl`, `g13-impl-ladder`, `g13-impl-ledger`, `g13-impl-alloc`, `g21-impl`, `g06-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- One feature name across crates (`experimental`) rather than per-module features: per-module features would multiply the CI matrix and give the README 30 flags to explain.
- `policy-config` implying `experimental`: the existing feature loads TOML into `policy_config.rs`, which is itself unreachable from `Program` (Section 2.2.C: safe mode never enters `Program`). Making it imply `experimental` keeps `cargo check --features policy-config` green without un-quarantining the module.
- Inner `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in the two orphan files: the crate already forbids unsafe at the root; a duplicate inner attribute in a module is allowed for `forbid` only at crate root, so expect to remove those lines.
- Risk: `doctor_frankentui` (192K lines) may import one of the quarantined runtime modules; only 7 of its 128 files import any `ftui_*` crate, so check with `rg 'ftui_runtime::(rough_path|...)' crates/doctor_frankentui/src` before gating and add `ftui-runtime = { features = ["experimental"] }` in its Cargo.toml only if a real import exists (then note it in the close reason for G22).
- Rollback: remove the `#[cfg]` lines.

## Definition of done

Feature exists in all seven crates; all listed modules and their tests/benches gated; the two orphans compile under the feature; check/clippy/fmt green both ways; `ubs` clean; close reason names the commit hash and the two `cargo check` command lines that were run.

title: task(G07): Add scripts/check_module_reachability.py, shrink-only allowlist, and CI reachability gate
description:
## Context and why this matters

The reality check's second root cause (Section 2.3) is that "reachable from production" was never part of the definition of done, so 30 of 64 `ftui-runtime` modules, three width caches, two e-process controllers, and two orphan files accumulated without anyone noticing. Quarantining (`g07-impl`) fixes today's set; nothing stops the next swarm from adding another unreachable module and closing the bead. This bead adds the mechanism: a CI gate that fails when a `pub mod` declared in any crate's `lib.rs` (outside the `experimental` feature) has no reference from a non-test file outside its own file or directory. It serves Section 2.2.B, vision rows V70 (mandatory gates) and the process gap in Section 6 ("design gap: duplicated controllers"), and it is the tool `g13-impl` uses to prove the duplicate pairs are gone.

## Current state (evidence)

- `ls scripts/check_module_reachability.py` and `ls docs/module-reachability-allowlist.txt`: both missing (verified 2026-09-01).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `check` job (`:23-85`): steps are "Check formatting" (`cargo fmt --all -- --check`), "Run clippy" (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`), "Enforce no-mock policy (bd-2nu8.18)" (an `rg` invocation with glob exclusions at `:63-71`), "Build workspace", "Run tests" (`--lib`), "Run tests (all features)" on nightly. The `features` job (`:119-157`) has no experimental combination.
- `rg` is available in CI only after G04.6 installs it (`tests/e2e/scripts/test_inline.sh:57` fails today because `rg` is missing on runners); the gate script must therefore be pure Python (`re` + `os.walk`), not shell out to `rg`.
- Module declarations to scan: `crates/*/src/lib.rs` `pub mod X;` lines (ftui-runtime has 64; ftui-core `:23-150` includes inline modules such as `pub mod text_width {` at `:150` and `pub mod shutdown_signal {` at `:79`, which are not files and must be recognized).
- Reachability definition from the reality check (7.0): reachable from `Program`, `Frame`, `TerminalWriter`, a widget's `render`, or the showcase; for public widgets and harness types, "exercised by a showcase screen or a harness binary/example" counts.

## Target state

`scripts/check_module_reachability.py` walks every workspace crate, parses `src/lib.rs` for `pub mod` declarations (file modules and inline modules), skips those under `#[cfg(feature = "experimental")]`, and for each remaining module requires at least one reference (`<module>::`, `use crate::<module>`, `use ftui_<crate>::<module>`, `ftui_<crate>::<module>::`, or the crate's `pub use <module>::{...}` names being referenced from another crate) from a `.rs` file that is (a) not under `tests/`, `benches/`, `examples/`, `fuzz/`, (b) not inside a `#[cfg(test)]` block (approximation: lines after `#[cfg(test)]` in the same file are ignored), and (c) not the module's own file or directory. `docs/module-reachability-allowlist.txt` lists modules that are known-unreachable-but-not-yet-quarantined with a bead id per line; the script fails if a module is unreachable and not allowlisted, and also fails if an allowlisted module has become reachable (so the list only shrinks). It runs in the `check` job after clippy; the `features` job gains `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --features experimental`.

## Implementation plan

1. Write `scripts/check_module_reachability.py` (Python 3.11+, stdlib only, `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, executable bit):
   - `discover_crates()`: read root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace] members` (parse with `tomllib`), return `(crate_name, crate_dir)` for each member whose `src/lib.rs` exists (skip `fuzz`, binaries without lib.rs such as `ftui-demo-showcase` if it is bin-only; if it has `lib.rs` include it).
   - `declared_modules(lib_rs)`: regex `^\s*(#\[cfg\((?P<cfg>[^\]]*)\)\]\s*)?pub mod (?P<name>[a-z0-9_]+)\s*[;{]` over the file with a one-line lookbehind for a preceding `#[cfg(...)]` line (the attribute is on its own line in this repo, e.g. `lib.rs:46-47`). Return `(name, cfg_text, is_inline)`; mark `experimental` when `cfg_text` contains `feature = "experimental"`.
   - `references(crate_name, module, crate_dir, workspace)`: scan all `crates/*/src/**/*.rs` (excluding the module's own file `src/<module>.rs` and dir `src/<module>/`), plus `crates/*/src/main.rs` and `crates/*/examples/*.rs` for the showcase/harness exception, plus `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/**`. Strip `#[cfg(test)]`-guarded regions (track a `mod tests` / `#[cfg(test)]` marker and ignore to end of file, which matches this repo's convention of trailing test modules). Count a hit for patterns: `\b{module}::`, `use crate::{module}\b`, `use ftui_{crate_snake}::{module}\b`, `use ftui_{crate_snake}::\{[^}]*\b{module}\b`, `use super::{module}\b` from sibling modules of the same crate. Return list of `(path, line_no, text)`.
   - Output: one line per module `OK <crate>::<module> (first ref path:line)`, `EXPERIMENTAL <crate>::<module>`, `ALLOWLISTED <crate>::<module>`, `UNREACHABLE <crate>::<module>`, `STALE_ALLOWLIST <crate>::<module> (now reachable: path:line)`; summary counts; `--json <path>` writes the same as JSON (`{"schema":"module-reachability-v1","crates":[...],"unreachable":[...],"stale_allowlist":[...]}`); exit 1 on any UNREACHABLE or STALE_ALLOWLIST; `--allowlist` path option (default `docs/module-reachability-allowlist.txt`); `--crate <name>` filter for local runs.
   - Public-API exception (reality check 7.0 "Public-API rule"): for `ftui-widgets` and `ftui-harness`, a module counts as reachable if referenced from `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/**` or `crates/ftui-harness/src/main.rs` or `crates/ftui-harness/examples/*.rs`; otherwise widgets modules such as `decision_card` are UNREACHABLE until `g07-impl-gallery` lands (they go on the initial allowlist with `g07-impl-gallery` as the bead id).
2. Seed `docs/module-reachability-allowlist.txt`: run the script once after `g07-impl` and paste the UNREACHABLE set with the format `<crate>::<module>  # <bead slug that will wire or quarantine it>`; expected entries include `ftui-widgets::height_predictor # g10-impl`, `ftui-widgets::fenwick # g10-impl`, `ftui-widgets::decision_card # g07-impl-gallery`, `ftui-widgets::drift_visualization # g07-impl-gallery`, `ftui-widgets::cached # g07-impl-gallery`, `ftui-widgets::error_boundary # g07-impl-gallery`, `ftui-harness::time_travel # g07-impl-gallery`, `ftui-text::width_cache # g08-impl`, `ftui-core::gesture # g18-impl`, `ftui-core::hover_stabilizer # g18-impl`, `ftui-runtime::conformal_predictor` is reachable (program.rs:4882) so it must NOT appear. The header comment states: "This list may only shrink. Add a line only with a bead id and only for a module that is being wired by that bead."
3. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `check` job: add step "Module reachability gate" after "Run clippy": `python3 scripts/check_module_reachability.py --json target/module-reachability.json` and upload the JSON as an artifact (`actions/upload-artifact@v4`, name `module-reachability-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.rust }}`), only on `ubuntu-latest` (add `if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'` to avoid three identical runs). `features` job: add step "Check experimental feature" `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --features experimental` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features experimental -- -D warnings`.
4. Add a `scripts/README.md` line? No: there is no such file; document the script in AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks" (owned by `g07-docs`).
5. Run the script locally on the post-`g07-impl` tree; fix false positives in the reference regex before committing the allowlist (the allowlist must not hide regex bugs: every allowlisted module must be confirmed unreachable by a manual `rg`).

What NOT to do: do not make the script modify any source file; do not use `rg`/`ast-grep` from the script (runner tooling is not guaranteed until G04.6); do not allowlist a module without a bead id.

## Files to change

- `scripts/check_module_reachability.py`: new (genuinely new functionality: no existing script scans module reachability).
- `docs/module-reachability-allowlist.txt`: new, seeded once.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `check` job step + artifact; `features` job two steps.
- `scripts/tests/test_check_module_reachability.py`: new pytest-style file (see `g07-tests`).

## Success criteria

- [ ] Script exits 0 on `main` after `g07-impl`; CI `check (ubuntu-latest, nightly)` shows the step green and uploads `module-reachability.json`.
- [ ] Negative test verified once: a scratch branch adds `pub mod orphan_probe;` with an empty `src/orphan_probe.rs` in ftui-render, the step fails with `UNREACHABLE ftui-render::orphan_probe`; the branch is discarded (no file left behind; document the run URL in the close reason).
- [ ] Stale-allowlist detection verified: temporarily allowlisting `ftui-runtime::program` fails with `STALE_ALLOWLIST`.
- [ ] `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --features experimental` step green in `features`.

## Tests and logging

- Unit (Python, `scripts/tests/test_check_module_reachability.py`, run with `python3 -m pytest scripts/tests` in the `check` job before the gate step; pytest is in the runner's Python via `pip install pytest` in the same step): fixture workspaces built in `tmp_path` with a fake `Cargo.toml` and two crates; tests `declares_file_and_inline_modules`, `experimental_cfg_is_skipped`, `reference_in_cfg_test_block_does_not_count`, `reference_from_own_dir_does_not_count`, `showcase_reference_counts_for_widgets`, `allowlist_only_shrinks`, `json_output_schema`.
- Logging: the script prints one line per module and a summary `unreachable=<n> stale=<n> experimental=<n> ok=<n>`; JSON artifact carries `git_commit` (from `git rev-parse HEAD`) and `generated_at`.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: `g07-impl` (the allowlist baseline must be taken after quarantine, otherwise it would contain 40 entries that the quarantine removes anyway).
- Unblocks: `g13-impl` (uses the gate to prove duplicates are gone), `g07-docs`, `g42-impl` (via the epic).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Regex-based scanning rather than `cargo`-level analysis (`cargo udeps`/`-Wunused`): unused `pub` items do not warn in Rust, and a `pub mod` is "used" by being public. Text scanning with an explicit reachability definition is the only cheap gate; it is deliberately conservative (any reference from any non-test production file counts).
- False negatives: a module referenced only from another unreachable module passes. Accepted; the gate is a ratchet, not a proof. `g13-impl` still reads the JSON manually for the four duplicate pairs.
- Alternative rejected: making the gate part of `check_readme_claims.py` (G06) — different cadence and different owners.
- Rollback: remove the CI step; the script is inert otherwise.

## Definition of done

Script and allowlist committed; CI `check` step green on `main` with the JSON artifact; negative and stale-allowlist checks verified once and documented; Python tests green; `ubs scripts/check_module_reachability.py` clean.
notes: Refinement 2 supersedes the blanket no-in-tree-caller failure rule: a public library API can be valid without an in-tree production caller. Classify runtime-integrated, opt-in/public-example, experimental, test-only and orphan separately; prove advertised production behavior through the actual runtime path. A reference in a comment or synthetic caller is not integration. Fail only on a claim/compilation/reachability-contract mismatch; preserve legitimate external-facing APIs.

title: feature(G07): Gallery entries for DecisionCard, DriftVisualization, CachedWidget, ErrorBoundary; TimeTravel
description:
## Context and why this matters

Widgets and harness types are library surface: a widget does not need an in-tree consumer to be legitimate, it needs to be exercised so that its snapshot proves it renders and the README can list it truthfully (reality check 7.0 "Public-API rule"). Four production widgets (`DecisionCard`, `DriftVisualization`, `CachedWidget`, `ErrorBoundary<W>`) and the harness `TimeTravel`/`TimeTravelInspector` pair are implemented and unit-tested but appear in no showcase screen, so the README's "Time-travel debugging" row is DEAD (V45) and the "Plus" widget names are unverified (Section 2.2.C). This bead gives each widget a `widget_gallery` entry with an insta snapshot and backs the `snapshot_player` screen's frame store and scrubber with `TimeTravel` + `TimeTravelInspector`, so the README API names corrected by G06 (`TimeTravel::new(capacity)`, `record(&Buffer, FrameMetadata)`, `get(idx)`, `rewind(steps)`; `seek` on `TimeTravelInspector`) are demonstrated by running code.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/decision_card.rs:56 pub struct DecisionCard<'a>` (24 KB), `drift_visualization.rs:197 pub struct DriftVisualization<'a>` (34 KB), `cached.rs:56 pub struct CachedWidget<W, K = NoCacheKey>` with `CachedWidgetState` at `:69` (18 KB), `error_boundary.rs:144 pub struct ErrorBoundary<W>` (32 KB). `rg -n 'DecisionCard|DriftVisualization|CachedWidget|ErrorBoundary' crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src` returns nothing.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/widget_gallery.rs`: `SECTION_COUNT: usize = 8` (`:26` and `:65`), `SECTION_NAMES` (`:29`, `:68`), section renderers `render_display_widgets` :442, `render_borders` :468, `render_text_styles` :533, `render_paragraph_wraps` :610, `render_lists_and_table` :646, `render_code_and_quote` :702, `render_colors` :740, `render_badges` :845, `render_status_widgets` :895, `render_spinners` :918, `render_toast_demo` :948, `render_inputs` :967, `render_text_inputs` :1018; the `VirtualizedList` usage at `:1920`; test `gallery_renders_all_sections` at `:2084`. Existing snapshots for the gallery are the a11y-mode ones (`a11y_*_widget_gallery_{80x24,120x40}.snap`).
- `crates/ftui-harness/src/time_travel.rs`: `TimeTravel` :287, `new(capacity)` :308, `record(&mut self, buf: &Buffer, metadata: FrameMetadata)` :325, `get(index) -> Option<Buffer>` :411, `rewind(steps) -> Option<Buffer>` :429; `FrameMetadata::new(frame_number, render_time)` :248. `crates/ftui-harness/src/time_travel_inspector.rs`: `TimeTravelInspector` :16, `new` :22, `index` :27, `seek(index, &TimeTravel)` :32, `step_back` :41, `step_forward(&TimeTravel)` :48, `render(&TimeTravel) -> Option<Buffer>` :55.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/snapshot_player.rs` (83 KB): `SnapshotPlayerConfig` :72 with `max_frames: 100` :86, `FrameInfo` :123, `SnapshotPlayer` :412 with `frames: Vec<Buffer>` :414 and `pub current_frame: usize` :418, `timeline_scrubbing: bool` :455 (mouse-drag scrub); tab label `"TimeTravel"` :1770; doc comment :16 "Memory budget: Bounded by TimeTravel capacity (default 100 frames)". The showcase already depends on `ftui-harness` (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml:73`). Tests: `tests/snapshot_player_e2e.rs`, `tests/snapshot_player_ux_a11y.rs`.

## Target state

`widget_gallery` has a ninth section "Diagnostics" (`SECTION_COUNT = 9`) rendering, in a 2x2 grid: a `DecisionCard` fed with a fixed decision (title "Diff strategy", posterior 0.82, three evidence rows), a `DriftVisualization` fed with a deterministic 32-sample series with a drift at index 20, a `CachedWidget` wrapping a `Paragraph` whose cache key is the section's tick counter and whose hit/miss counter is printed in the block title, and an `ErrorBoundary<Paragraph>` whose inner widget is forced to fail on odd ticks so the fallback branch is visible. Each has an insta snapshot at 80x24. `snapshot_player` stores frames in `TimeTravel` and drives the scrubber through `TimeTravelInspector::seek`.

## Implementation plan

1. `widget_gallery.rs`: bump `SECTION_COUNT` to 9 in both places (`:26`, `:65`; they are duplicated today, keep them consistent or collapse to one `const` if the second is a leftover); append `"Diagnostics"` to `SECTION_NAMES`; add `fn render_diagnostics(&self, frame: &mut Frame, area: Rect)` dispatched from `render_section_content` (`:417`); split `area` with `Flex` into four cells; construct the four widgets from fields added to `WidgetGallery` (`diag_tick: u64`, `cached_state: CachedWidgetState`, `drift_samples: [f32; 32]` filled in `new` from a fixed formula, no RNG). Read `DecisionCard`, `DriftVisualization`, `CachedWidget`, `ErrorBoundary` constructors from their source files (they are the source of truth; do not guess names) and use the builder methods that exist.
2. Update `gallery_renders_all_sections` (`:2084`) to iterate 9 sections.
3. `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/screen_snapshots.rs`: add snapshot cases `widget_gallery_decision_card_80x24`, `widget_gallery_drift_visualization_80x24`, `widget_gallery_cached_widget_80x24`, `widget_gallery_error_boundary_80x24` (select section 9 via the screen's existing section navigation before rendering; if the four-in-one grid makes per-widget snapshots redundant, take one `widget_gallery_diagnostics_80x24` plus `..._120x40` and name the four widgets in the snapshot header comment). Bless with `BLESS=1 cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase --test screen_snapshots`.
4. `snapshot_player.rs`: replace `frames: Vec<Buffer>` with `time_travel: ftui_harness::time_travel::TimeTravel` (capacity from `config.max_frames`) and `inspector: ftui_harness::time_travel_inspector::TimeTravelInspector`; `record` calls `time_travel.record(&buf, FrameMetadata::new(frame_number, render_time))`; `current_frame` becomes `inspector.index()`; scrub/seek paths call `inspector.seek(idx, &self.time_travel)`, step keys call `step_back`/`step_forward`; the rendered frame comes from `inspector.render(&self.time_travel)`. Keep `FrameInfo` for the side panel. Keep the mouse-drag scrubber (`timeline_scrubbing`) but route it through `seek`.
5. Update `tests/snapshot_player_e2e.rs` and `snapshot_player_ux_a11y.rs` expectations if frame-count semantics change (capacity eviction is now `TimeTravel`'s ring behavior; assert the eviction explicitly: record 105 frames with capacity 100, `get(0)` is `None`... read `time_travel.rs:325-430` to confirm the exact eviction semantics before writing the assertion).
6. Add snapshot `snapshot_player_scrub_frame_5_80x24` (record 10 frames, `seek(5)`, render).
7. Gates: `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt`, `ubs` on touched files.

What NOT to do: do not add these widgets to a new screen (the gallery exists for this); do not keep a parallel `Vec<Buffer>` next to `TimeTravel`; no README edits here (G06 owns API-name rows; `g07-docs` owns the experimental section).

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/widget_gallery.rs`: ninth section, four widget instances, test update.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/snapshot_player.rs`: frame store on `TimeTravel`, scrubber on `TimeTravelInspector`.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/screen_snapshots.rs`: five new snapshot cases; `tests/snapshots/*.snap` blessed files.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/snapshot_player_e2e.rs`, `snapshot_player_ux_a11y.rs`: assertion updates.

## Success criteria

title: task(G07): Tests for the experimental feature matrix, reachability gate, and gallery/TimeTravel snapshots
description:

title: question(G07): Owner permission to delete orphan modules, loser width caches, and merged duplicates
description:
## Context and why this matters

AGENTS.md rule 1: "YOU ARE NEVER ALLOWED TO DELETE A FILE WITHOUT EXPRESS PERMISSION. ... YOU MUST ALWAYS ASK AND RECEIVE CLEAR, WRITTEN PERMISSION BEFORE EVER DELETING A FILE OR FOLDER OF ANY KIND." Nothing may be deleted until the owner has answered here; the answer text is copied verbatim into the commit message of the deleting commit (AGENTS.md "Document the confirmation": record the exact user text that authorized it, the command run, and the time).

title: epic(G08): Put one benchmark-selected width cache on the production grapheme_width path
description:
## Context and why this matters

README "### Width Calculation" (README.md:1370-1383) promises: "Grapheme width calculation uses a **W-TinyLFU admission cache** for expensive `unicode-width` lookups: Doorkeeper (Bloom filter) → Count-Min Sketch → LRU cache ... High hit-rate even under adversarial access patterns", and the "S3-FIFO Cache" row (V20) claims an S3-FIFO cache for "caps + width". In the code, three complete width caches exist in `crates/ftui-text/src/width_cache.rs` (2,608 lines) and none is on the production path: every width the renderer or wrapper computes goes through `ftui_core::text_width::grapheme_width`, which has an ASCII fast path and then calls `unicode_display_width` uncached. The claim is DEAD (Section 2.2.B row 1; vision rows V20, V21), and the three parallel implementations are the canonical example of the "accreted parallel implementations" root cause in Section 2.3.

Why it matters to users: non-ASCII-heavy screens (CJK logs, emoji-rich chat, ZWJ sequences) pay the full Unicode table lookup for every grapheme on every wrap and every grapheme-pool intern; a cache keyed by grapheme hash removes that cost at steady state. Why it matters to the project: this is the first block that establishes the pattern "pick one implementation by benchmark, put it where both consumers can reach it, delete or quarantine the rest".

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-text/src/width_cache.rs`: `CacheStats` :46, `WidthCache` (LRU) :97 with `new` :108, thread-local `THREAD_CACHE` :268-271 and `cached_width` :275 / `clear_thread_cache` :281 under cargo feature `thread_local_cache` (declared in `crates/ftui-text/Cargo.toml`, not enabled by any crate), `CountMinSketch` :807 (`new(width, depth, reset_interval)` :834), `Doorkeeper` :926, `fingerprint_hash` :979, `tinylfu_admit` :996, `TinyLfuWidthCache` :1034 (`new(total_capacity)` :1054), `S3FifoWidthCache` :1233 (`new(capacity)` :1249) built over `ftui_core::s3_fifo::S3Fifo`. Re-exported from `crates/ftui-text/src/lib.rs:167-169`. `rg` for the three type names outside the file finds only doc comments (`shaping.rs:478`) and `lib.rs` docs; no constructor call in any production file.

Also `char_width` :360 and `display_width` :381 (ASCII fast path at `:385`). No cache anywhere in this module.
- `crates/ftui-render/Cargo.toml` `[dependencies]` lists `ftui-core` as the only workspace crate ("ftui-render is the core kernel and should not depend on ftui-style"; `ftui-text` is a commented-out TODO), so a cache in ftui-text cannot serve the grapheme pool; it must live in ftui-core.

- Section 2.2.C also notes the README's "GraphemeId packs display width into bits [31:25]" is wrong (real layout: width 4 bits [30:27]); that row is G06 DOC, not this block.

## Target state

One cache implementation, selected by the `cache_bench.rs` data on a mixed CJK/emoji/ZWJ corpus, lives in `ftui-core` as the submodule `text_width::cache` (file `crates/ftui-core/src/text_width/cache.rs`; the inline `text_width` module gains a `pub mod cache;` line), is thread-local, keyed by the grapheme's 64-bit hash, capped at 4,096 entries, consulted by `grapheme_width` only after the ASCII fast path, and disabled by `FTUI_WIDTH_CACHE=0`. `ftui-text` wrap and `ftui-render` grapheme pool both benefit without code changes because both already call `ftui_core::text_width::grapheme_width`. `text_width::cache_stats()` exposes hits/misses/size for telemetry. The losers are quarantined behind `experimental` or deleted with permission (`g07-decision`). The README names the policy that is actually used with the measured hit rate.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Bench `text_width_non_ascii` in `tests/baseline.json` (criterion name from `crates/ftui-text/benches/cache_bench.rs`, bench group `wrap/non_ascii_corpus`) shows the cached path at least 30% fewer ns per non-ASCII grapheme than the uncached path at steady state; the baseline row's p99 is set from the measured artifact.
- [ ] Proptest `proptest_width_cache_transparency` in `crates/ftui-core/src/text_width/cache.rs` tests: for arbitrary grapheme clusters, cached width == uncached width, including under CJK mode toggles.
- [ ] `text_width::cache_stats()` hit-rate is logged once per showcase run in `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh` JSONL (event `width_cache_stats`).
- [ ] `scripts/check_module_reachability.py` shows `ftui-core::text_width::cache` reachable and `ftui-text::width_cache` either experimental or gone.
- [ ] README "Width Calculation" states the real policy (G06 ledger row updated by `g08-docs`).

## Implementation plan (child beads)

1. `g08-impl`: run the bench, choose the winner, move it into `ftui-core::text_width::cache`, wire `grapheme_width`, add `FTUI_WIDTH_CACHE=0`, quarantine/delete losers per permission.
2. `g08-tests`: proptest transparency, corpus bench + baseline row, hit-rate stats in the showcase E2E JSONL, concurrency test (thread-local isolation).
3. `g08-docs`: README "Width Calculation" rewrite and claims-ledger row.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: nothing (day-one parallel track per Section 7.5).
- Related: `g07-decision` (deleting losers), `g25-impl` (perf gate runs the baseline row in CI; the row can be added before the gate exists), `g06-impl` (ledger).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Why ftui-core and not ftui-text: the render crate's dependency rule (core only) is a deliberate architecture decision (comment in `ftui-render/Cargo.toml`); the pool interns graphemes and needs widths at intern time.
- Why thread-local: `WidthCache` docs say it is not thread-safe (`width_cache.rs:94`); the render thread feature (`render-thread`) means two threads may compute widths; a thread-local avoids a mutex on the hot path and matches the existing `THREAD_CACHE` pattern at `:268`.
- Why decide by data: the module docs claim S3-FIFO wins; the README claims W-TinyLFU; measuring on a realistic corpus settles it and the bench artifact becomes the README's proof.
- Risk: a cache that is slower than the uncached path for ASCII-only workloads. Mitigated by consulting the cache only after the ASCII fast path, and by the `frame_allocations_ascii_scene` / `frame_render` baseline rows (G25) not regressing.
- Risk: hash collisions returning a wrong width. Keyed by full 64-bit hash of the grapheme bytes plus a length check; the proptest covers collisions statistically; store the grapheme length alongside the width and compare on hit.
- Rollback: `FTUI_WIDTH_CACHE=0` at runtime; reverting the `grapheme_width` change at code level.

## Definition of done

Winner wired in ftui-core and reachable from both wrap and pool paths; baseline row present with a measured number; proptest and stats tests green; README updated; losers quarantined or deleted with recorded permission; close reason cites the bench artifact path and the numbers.

title: task(G08): Bench-select width cache, move into ftui-core text_width::cache, wire grapheme_width, env switch
description:
## Context and why this matters

The README says grapheme width uses a W-TinyLFU admission cache (README.md:1370-1383); the code computes every non-ASCII width uncached in `ftui_core::text_width::grapheme_width` (`crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs:333`) while three finished caches sit unused in `crates/ftui-text/src/width_cache.rs`. This bead makes one of them real: it selects the policy by benchmark, moves it into ftui-core where both the text wrapper and the render grapheme pool can reach it, wires it into `grapheme_width` behind the ASCII fast path, and adds an environment kill-switch. Serves V20, V21 and Section 2.2.B.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs`: `pub mod s3_fifo;` :43; `pub mod text_width {` :150 (inline module; imports `unicode_display_width::width as unicode_display_width` :183); helpers `use_cjk_width()` :219, `ascii_display_width` :284, `ascii_width` :299; `grapheme_width` :333-355 (ASCII fast path :334, zero-width check, `width_cjk()` under `use_cjk_width()`, VS16 stripping, `unicode_display_width` :352/:354); `char_width` :360; `display_width` :381. Tests at `:709-725` (`grapheme_width_ascii_char`, `grapheme_width_cjk_ideograph`, `grapheme_width_combining_sequence`, `grapheme_width_zwj_cluster`).
- `crates/ftui-core/src/s3_fifo.rs`: `S3Fifo<K, V>` :41 (`new(capacity)` :108, `get(&K) -> Option<&V>` :133, `insert(K, V) -> Option<V>` :150, `remove` :185, `len` :209, `capacity` :219, `stats() -> S3FifoStats` :224, `clear` :236, `contains_key` :248).
- `crates/ftui-text/src/width_cache.rs`: `WidthCache` :97 (LRU; `new` :108; `with_default_capacity`; `get_or_compute`), `TinyLfuWidthCache` :1034 (`new(total_capacity)` :1054; uses `CountMinSketch` :807 + `Doorkeeper` :926 + `tinylfu_admit` :996), `S3FifoWidthCache` :1233 (`new(capacity)` :1249, `Default` :1349), `CacheStats` :46; thread-local `cached_width` :275 under feature `thread_local_cache`. Re-exports at `crates/ftui-text/src/lib.rs:167-169` (`CacheStats, CountMinSketch, DEFAULT_CACHE_CAPACITY, Doorkeeper, S3FifoWidthCache, TinyLfuWidthCache, WidthCache`).
- `crates/ftui-text/benches/cache_bench.rs`: workloads `zipfian_workload` :17, `scan_workload` :34, `mixed_workload` :39; benches `bench_lru` :55, `bench_tinylfu` :79, `bench_s3fifo` :103, `bench_hit_rates` :128.

## Target state

`crates/ftui-core/src/text_width/cache.rs` exists (submodule of the inline `text_width` module via `pub mod cache;` inside the `pub mod text_width {` block, which requires the `#[path]`-free layout `src/text_width/cache.rs`; Rust resolves `pub mod cache;` inside an inline module `text_width` declared in `lib.rs` to `src/text_width/cache.rs`). It exposes `pub fn cached_grapheme_width(grapheme: &str, compute: impl FnOnce(&str) -> usize) -> usize`, `pub fn cache_stats() -> WidthCacheStats { hits, misses, len, capacity, enabled }`, `pub fn clear()`, and `pub const DEFAULT_CAPACITY: usize = 4096`. The store is `thread_local! { static WIDTH_CACHE: RefCell<Option<Store>> }` where `Store` is the winning policy (expected `S3Fifo<u64, (u8 /*len*/, u8 /*width*/)>` but decided by data). `grapheme_width` (`lib.rs:333`) becomes: ASCII fast path unchanged; then `cache::cached_grapheme_width(grapheme, compute_uncached)` where `compute_uncached` is today's body from the zero-width check onward. Disabled when `FTUI_WIDTH_CACHE=0` (read once per thread on first use, cached in the thread-local). The key is the 64-bit hash of the grapheme bytes (use `ahash`, already a dependency of ftui-render/ftui-a11y; add it to ftui-core if absent, or use `std::hash::DefaultHasher` to avoid a new dependency; decide by the bench) and the value stores the byte length so a collision with a different-length grapheme is treated as a miss. CJK mode participates in the key (fold `use_cjk_width()` into the hash seed) so toggling the env at runtime cannot serve stale widths.

## Implementation plan

1. Bench first (no code change yet): extend `crates/ftui-text/benches/cache_bench.rs` with `non_ascii_corpus_workload(size)` built from a fixed table of CJK ideographs, Hangul syllables, emoji with VS16, ZWJ family sequences, flag pairs, combining marks, Devanagari conjuncts, and Thai clusters (a `const CORPUS: &[&str]` of ~200 graphemes, sampled by a Zipf(1.0) index with a fixed LCG seed), and a group `wrap/non_ascii_corpus` with variants `uncached`, `lru`, `tinylfu`, `s3fifo` measuring ns per grapheme at steady state (warm 10k lookups, then measure 100k). Run `rch exec -- cargo bench -p ftui-text --bench cache_bench -- wrap/non_ascii_corpus` and save the criterion output to `docs/perf/width_cache_selection_2026-09.md` (table: policy, ns/grapheme p50, hit rate; the file is new and is the evidence for the README). Pick the policy with the lowest steady-state ns/grapheme; on a tie within 5% pick the smaller code (S3-FIFO over TinyLFU).
2. Create `crates/ftui-core/src/text_width/cache.rs` with the winner's logic ported (not copied wholesale: only the store, hit/miss counters, and the get-or-compute path; drop `CacheStats` features that the API above does not expose). If the winner is S3-FIFO, build on `crate::s3_fifo::S3Fifo` (no new implementation). If TinyLFU wins, port `CountMinSketch`, `Doorkeeper`, `tinylfu_admit` into the same file as private items.
3. `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs`: inside `pub mod text_width {` add `pub mod cache;` and `pub use cache::{cache_stats, WidthCacheStats};`; refactor `grapheme_width` (:333) into `grapheme_width` (fast path + cache call) and `fn grapheme_width_uncached(grapheme: &str) -> usize` (today's body from `:337` to `:354`). `char_width` (:360) and `display_width` (:381) are unchanged (display_width iterates graphemes through `grapheme_width` when non-ASCII; confirm at `:385-395` and keep it that way so the cache is hit).
4. Env switch: `fn cache_enabled() -> bool` reads `FTUI_WIDTH_CACHE` once per thread (`"0"` disables; anything else or unset enables); document next to `FTUI_TEXT_CJK_WIDTH` in the module docs.
5. `crates/ftui-text/src/width_cache.rs`: after the winner is in core, gate the whole module with `#[cfg(feature = "experimental")]` (`lib.rs:63` and re-exports `:167-169`), and gate `benches/cache_bench.rs` sections that use the losers with `required-features = ["experimental"]` in `Cargo.toml` (keep the `uncached` vs `core-cache` comparison ungated by moving that part into `crates/ftui-core/benches/width_cache_bench.rs`, a new bench file in ftui-core, since the winner now lives there). Delete the loser types only after `g07-decision` grants permission (quote the permission in the commit). The `thread_local_cache` feature of ftui-text becomes dead: remove the feature line from `crates/ftui-text/Cargo.toml` (it is a Cargo.toml line, not a file deletion) and the `cached_width`/`clear_thread_cache` functions with it.
6. Stats hook for E2E: `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` `complete_lifecycle` (around `:5490`, where G03 touches the same function; coordinate by adding a single call) writes an evidence line `{"event":"width_cache_stats","hits":..,"misses":..,"len":..,"capacity":..,"enabled":..}` through the `EvidenceSink` (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/evidence_sink.rs:200 write_jsonl`) when a sink is configured. This is the render thread's stats if `render-thread` is on; document that.
7. Gates: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` (both feature states), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test -p ftui-core -p ftui-text -p ftui-render`, `ubs` on touched files.

What NOT to do: no `WidthCacheV2`; no wrapper "shim" in ftui-text that forwards to core (consumers call `ftui_core::text_width::grapheme_width` already; `ftui_text::grapheme_width` at `wrap.rs:451` stays as is); no global mutex; no deletion without the quoted permission.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-core/src/text_width/cache.rs`: new (winner store, stats, env switch, tests).
- `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs`: `pub mod cache;` + re-export inside `text_width`; `grapheme_width` split.
- `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml`: `ahash` dependency only if the bench shows it matters; `[[bench]] width_cache_bench`.
- `crates/ftui-core/benches/width_cache_bench.rs`: new, `uncached` vs `cached` on the corpus (criterion name `text_width/non_ascii_corpus/cached`).
- `crates/ftui-text/benches/cache_bench.rs`: corpus workload + policy comparison (gated experimental after selection).
- `crates/ftui-text/src/lib.rs`, `src/width_cache.rs`, `Cargo.toml`: gate/remove per steps 5.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `width_cache_stats` evidence line.
- `docs/perf/width_cache_selection_2026-09.md`: new bench record.
- `tests/baseline.json`: row `text_width_non_ascii` (in `g08-tests`).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `docs/perf/width_cache_selection_2026-09.md` records the four policies' ns/grapheme and hit rates; the chosen policy is the fastest by that table.
- [ ] `cargo bench -p ftui-core --bench width_cache_bench` shows `cached` at least 30% faster than `uncached` per non-ASCII grapheme at steady state.
- [ ] `FTUI_WIDTH_CACHE=0 cargo test -p ftui-core text_width` passes (all width tests are cache-independent) and `cache_stats().enabled == false` in a test that sets the env before first use (test runs in its own thread to control thread-local init).
- [ ] `grapheme_width` for ASCII input never touches the cache (test: stats unchanged after 1,000 ASCII lookups).
- [ ] Reachability gate: `ftui-core::text_width` reachable (already), `ftui-text::width_cache` EXPERIMENTAL or removed.

## Tests and logging

- Unit (`text_width/cache.rs`): `hit_after_miss`, `collision_with_different_length_is_miss` (construct two strings whose hashes are forced equal by using a test-only hasher seam), `cjk_mode_is_part_of_key`, `capacity_bounded_at_4096` (insert 10k distinct, `len() <= 4096`), `disabled_by_env_returns_uncached_and_counts_nothing`, `stats_reset_on_clear`.
- Property: `proptest_width_cache_transparency` (in `g08-tests`).
- Bench: `text_width/non_ascii_corpus/{uncached,cached}` in ftui-core; policy comparison in ftui-text (experimental).
- E2E: `width_cache_stats` line in the showcase E2E JSONL (`g08-tests` adds the assertion in `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh`).

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: nothing.
- Deletion step blocked by: `g07-decision`.
- Unblocks: `g08-tests`, `g08-docs`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Keying by hash and storing length: storing the full grapheme string in the cache would allocate on every miss; hash + length is collision-safe enough for widths 0-2 where a wrong answer is a one-cell misrender, and the proptest guards it.

- Alternative rejected: caching inside `GraphemePool` only (render side) leaves wrap uncached; caching in ftui-text only leaves the pool uncached.

title: task(G08): Width cache transparency proptest, corpus bench and baseline row, hit-rate stats in E2E JSONL
description:
## Context

Companion test bead for `g08-impl`. The block claims correctness (cached width == uncached width, always) and speed (at least 30% fewer ns per non-ASCII grapheme), and it introduces runtime telemetry (hit rate). Each claim needs its own proof: a property test for transparency, a criterion bench with a baseline row for speed, and an E2E assertion that the hit-rate statistics reach the showcase JSONL.

## What to test

1. Transparency: for any grapheme cluster (including ZWJ sequences, VS15/VS16, combining marks, CJK, control characters, zero-width joiners), `grapheme_width` with the cache equals `grapheme_width_uncached`, under both CJK modes, and `display_width` of any string equals the sum over its graphemes (existing invariant) with the cache on.
2. Isolation: two threads have independent caches (stats on thread B unchanged by thread A's lookups); `FTUI_WIDTH_CACHE=0` disables per thread.
3. Speed: steady-state ns/grapheme on the non-ASCII corpus, cached vs uncached, recorded in `tests/baseline.json`.
4. Telemetry: `width_cache_stats` event appears in the showcase E2E JSONL with sane values.

## Test types (unit, property, bench, E2E) with names and assertions

Property (`crates/ftui-core/src/text_width/cache.rs`, `#[cfg(test)] mod proptests` using `proptest`, which ftui-core already uses for its terminal-model property tests):
- `proptest_width_cache_transparency`: strategy builds strings from a weighted union of `any::<char>()` filtered to assigned scalars, a curated table of emoji/ZWJ/flag/skin-tone sequences, CJK ranges, combining ranges (U+0300..U+036F), and Thai/Devanagari clusters; for each generated string iterate `unicode_segmentation::graphemes(true)` and assert `grapheme_width(g) == grapheme_width_uncached(g)`; 2,048 cases; run twice in one test with `FTUI_TEXT_CJK_WIDTH` toggled via the module's `set_cjk_width_override_for_tests` seam if one exists (else run the CJK variant in a separate `#[test]` that sets the env before the first lookup on a fresh thread).
- `proptest_display_width_matches_grapheme_sum_with_cache`: `display_width(s) == s.graphemes(true).map(grapheme_width).sum()` for the same strategy.
- `proptest_cache_never_exceeds_capacity`: after N random lookups, `cache_stats().len <= DEFAULT_CAPACITY`.

Unit (`cache.rs`): `hit_after_miss`, `collision_with_different_length_is_miss`, `cjk_mode_is_part_of_key`, `capacity_bounded_at_4096`, `disabled_by_env_returns_uncached_and_counts_nothing`, `stats_reset_on_clear`, `ascii_never_touches_cache` (1,000 ASCII lookups, `hits + misses == 0`), `thread_local_isolation` (spawn a thread, do 100 non-ASCII lookups, join; main thread's `cache_stats().misses == 0`).

Bench (`crates/ftui-core/benches/width_cache_bench.rs`, criterion, `harness = false`): group `text_width/non_ascii_corpus` with `uncached` and `cached` variants over the 200-grapheme corpus sampled Zipf(1.0) with a fixed LCG seed, warm 10k then measure; `throughput = Elements(n)`. Baseline row in `tests/baseline.json`:
```
"text_width_non_ascii": {
  "description": "Cached non-ASCII grapheme width lookup at steady state (per grapheme)",
  "criterion_name": "text_width/non_ascii_corpus/cached",
  "bench_file": "width_cache_bench",
  "crate": "ftui-core",
  "slo_metric": "text_width_non_ascii_p99_ns",
  "p50_ns": <measured>, "p95_ns": <measured>, "p99_ns": <measured>, "p999_ns": <measured>,
  "threshold_pct": 10
}
```
plus a second row `text_width_non_ascii_uncached` with the uncached criterion name so the 30% claim is checkable from the two rows (`p50(cached) <= 0.7 * p50(uncached)`); `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh` reads `criterion_name`, `bench_file`, `p99_ns`, `threshold_pct`, `slo_metric` (`:290-302`), so both rows follow that format. If `slo.yaml` validation (`slo_metric_declared()` at `perf_regression_gate.sh:120`) requires the metric to be declared, add it to the same file that declares `render_frame_p99_us`.

E2E (`scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh`): in the existing evidence step that runs the demo with `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL` (the explain step at `:2364` sets `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL="$EXPLAIN_REPORT"`), add an assertion `jsonl_assert "width_cache_stats_present" ...` that the evidence file contains exactly one `"event":"width_cache_stats"` line with `hits >= 0`, `misses >= 1` (the showcase renders non-ASCII box drawing and emoji on the dashboard), `enabled == true`, `len <= 4096`; log the parsed values into the E2E JSONL via `jsonl_assert` detail text. Use `tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py` to validate the run's JSONL; extend `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json` only if the assert event needs new fields (it does not: `jsonl_assert` already exists).

## Logging (structured JSONL fields, tracing targets)

- Evidence line: `{"schema_version":"<sink version>","event":"width_cache_stats","hits":u64,"misses":u64,"len":usize,"capacity":usize,"enabled":bool,"thread":"main|render"}` written once at lifecycle completion.
- E2E JSONL: `jsonl_assert` rows with names `width_cache_stats_present`, `width_cache_hit_rate` (detail `hit_rate=<f64>`); run-level `run_id`, `scenario`, `exit_code` are already produced by `tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh`.
- Bench: criterion HTML/JSON under `target/criterion/text_width/`; the perf gate's report table row for `text_width_non_ascii`.
- Tracing: `ftui.text.width_cache` at `trace` on miss (feature `tracing` only).

description:
## Context and why this matters

Admission: New item admitted only if CMS frequency ≥ eviction candidate frequency → High hit-rate even under adversarial access patterns. Width Embedding: GraphemeId packs display width into bits [31:25], avoiding pool lookup for width queries". After `g08-impl`, the production path uses whichever policy won the benchmark, lives in `ftui_core::text_width::cache`, and has a measured hit rate; the README must say exactly that, and the claims ledger (G06) must have a row whose proof is the bench artifact and the proptest name. The "bits [31:25]" sentence is wrong today (real layout per Section 2.2.C: width 4 bits [30:27], generation 11 bits, slot 16 bits) and is a G06 DOC row; this bead fixes it in the same section since the section is being rewritten anyway (coordinate with `g06-impl` so the ledger row points here).

title: G08: Preserve exact grapheme identity on width-cache hits
description:
crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs::text_width uses deterministic ahash -> S3Fifo<u64,u8> and returns cached width without checking original cluster bytes. The comment acknowledges hash collision can misreport width. No natural collision was found in this audit; the defect is a correctness contract that relies on collision probability. Store or otherwise verify exact cluster identity before reusing width while retaining bounded cache cost, cache-off fallback, thread-local behavior and valid Unicode semantics. Coordinate existing cache transparency/benchmark task .12.2. Do not misdiagnose arbitrary whole-string u8 saturation without respecting grapheme API input contracts.

Verification contract (companion task):
Inject a constant/colliding hasher in tests or equivalent controlled collision seam, insert distinct valid graphemes of different widths, and prove cached == uncached on every hit/eviction/order. Include combining marks, emoji ZWJ, wide/ambiguous-width policies, repeated misses, capacity pressure and multithread independence. Existing corpus/property tests run with cache on/off. Measure hit memory/latency and steady/cold/adversarial streams with identical policies; correctness cannot be traded for a preferred benchmark number.

Context: September 4 reality check at 21a4e48b. Source and shipped 0.6.0 are different evidence domains. Preserve all current functionality and in-progress ownership; no file deletion, yanking, publishing, or compatibility shims are authorized by this task. Use existing files where coherent, manual edits, Cargo only. Acceptance must identify exact commit, feature set, target, toolchain, command, exit status and artifact hashes; skipped/missing evidence remains unproven. Run the relevant unit/property and real integration/E2E checks, archive diagnostic logs with seeds and bounded redacted payloads, and run workspace check, Clippy -D warnings, fmt --check and rustdoc -D warnings for substantive Rust changes. Do not close on compilation alone.

notes:

Execution TODO: (1) reproduce forced collisions through the production cache lookup; (2) retain and compare exact grapheme bytes on hits with bounded key storage and unchanged policy; (3) cover collision order, eviction, Unicode corpus and thread-local behavior; (4) exercise real wrapping/rendering cache on/off and measure cold/steady/adversarial costs; (5) run required workspace checks; (6) re-execute in a fresh verification pass at the committed revision before closure. Three seeded public Unicode properties pass cache-on and cache-off (512 cases/property, seed 450512). Current same-binary criterion run on hz4, western width + Unicode VS16: repeated 488 clusters uncached 57.012-57.271 us, exact-cache steady 16.062-16.237 us, cold 23.844-23.964 us; 5000-distinct-cluster scan uncached 685.87-708.62 us, cached 2.9223-2.9342 ms. title: epic(G09): Build the accessibility tree every frame, diff it, announce live regions, show it in the panel
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:2290-2300 "## Accessibility" promises: "The `ftui-a11y` crate provides an accessibility tree that mirrors the widget render tree: Semantic nodes for every interactive widget ... Role/state/label properties following WAI-ARIA semantics ... Focus graph ... Live regions for announcing dynamic content changes to screen readers ... The `accessibility_panel` demo screen visualizes the a11y tree in real time as you navigate the UI." Vision row V46 ("Accessibility tree, live regions") is DEAD: the crate exists (2,019 lines: `lib.rs` 123, `node.rs` 273, `preferences.rs` 815, `tree.rs` 808) and nine widgets implement the `Accessible` trait, but no production code ever calls `accessibility_nodes()`, nothing constructs `A11yTreeBuilder` outside tests, `Frame` has no accessibility hook, and the `accessibility_panel` screen renders theme toggles (high contrast, large text, reduced motion), not a tree. A screen-reader user gets nothing from FrankenTUI today, and the README claim is false.

This epic makes the tree real end to end: `Frame` collects nodes during `view()`, the nine widgets push their existing node declarations, `Block` scopes children, the runtime builds and diffs the tree per frame when enabled, live-region changes become `a11y_announcement` evidence lines, the model can read the tree through a default-no-op hook, and the showcase panel renders the real tree. Closes Section 2.2.B row "ftui-a11y tree" and V46; feeds G20 (evidence names) and G04.9 (a11y E2E cases).

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-a11y/Cargo.toml` `[dependencies]`: `ftui-core`, `ahash` only (no cycle risk for ftui-render, which depends on ftui-core only).
- `crates/ftui-a11y/src/lib.rs:117 pub trait Accessible { fn accessibility_nodes(&self, area: Rect) -> Vec<A11yNodeInfo>; }`.
- `crates/ftui-a11y/src/tree.rs`: `A11yTreeBuilder` :25 (`new` :40, `with_capacity`, `add_node(A11yNodeInfo)` :60, `set_root(u64)`, `set_focused(Option<u64>)`, `build() -> A11yTree` :78); `A11yTree` :94 (flat `AHashMap<u64, A11yNodeInfo>`; parent/child ids live inside `A11yNodeInfo`); `A11yTree::diff(&self, previous) -> A11yTreeDiff` :290; `A11yTreeDiff { added, removed, changed: Vec<(u64, Vec<A11yChange>)>, focus_changed: Option<(Option<u64>, Option<u64>)> }` :341; `ScreenReaderPolicy` :440, `ScreenReaderMirror` :461, `ScreenReaderAnnouncements` :478, `ScreenReaderAnnouncement` :487, `AnnouncementReason` :500, `A11yChange` :513. `node.rs`: `A11yRole` :19 (23 variants per `docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md`), `A11yState` :124, `LiveRegion` :160, `A11yNodeInfo` :184 (`new(id, role, bounds)` :210, builder methods).
- Widgets implementing `ftui_a11y::Accessible`: `block.rs:440`, `tabs.rs:518`, `progress.rs:209`, `input.rs:1155`, `list.rs:973`, `table.rs:332`, `spinner.rs:187`, `scrollbar.rs:540`, `paragraph.rs:582`. `crates/ftui-widgets/Cargo.toml:27` depends on ftui-a11y. Callers of `accessibility_nodes(` outside tests: none (only `crates/ftui-a11y/tests/a11y_tests.rs`, `paragraph.rs:1128-1176` tests, `crates/ftui-web/tests/frankenterm_js_a11y_e2e.rs:174`).
- `crates/ftui-render/src/frame.rs:425 pub struct Frame<'a>` fields: `buffer`, `pool`, `links`, `hit_grid`, `hit_owner_stack` (private), `widget_budget`, `widget_signals`, `cursor_position`, `cursor_visible`, `degradation`, `arena`. Constructors `new` :477, `with_links` :516, `with_hit_grid` :540; `with_hit_owner` :731 is the existing scoped-container pattern to mirror. `crates/ftui-render/Cargo.toml` does not depend on ftui-a11y.
