title: epic(G10): Connect VirtualizedList to the Fenwick index, height predictor, VOI remeasure, and search screens
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:859-884 promises two things for virtualized lists: "Variable-height virtualized lists use a **Fenwick tree** (Binary Indexed Tree) for fast prefix sums ... O(log n) height lookup and scroll positioning without scanning all rows" and "Virtualized lists predict unseen row heights to avoid scroll jumps, using a **Normal-Normal** conjugate update plus conformal bounds ... Variance is tracked online with Welford's algorithm, and `q` is the empirical quantile of |residuals|". The widget table at README.md:2165 says `VirtualizedList | Large lists | Fenwick tree scroll, Bayesian height prediction`, and the demo table at :111 credits `virtualized_search` and `log_search` with "Fenwick-backed virtualization". Vision row V11 (VOI sampling) is PARTIAL and Section 2.2.B rows for `height_predictor.rs` (DEAD, 1,079 lines) and `fenwick.rs` (opt-in mode nobody opts into) are the gap: the Fenwick index exists but the default is `Fixed(1)` and no caller opts in; the predictor has zero consumers; VOI-driven remeasurement does not exist; and the two demo screens that the README credits do not use `VirtualizedList` at all.

Why users care: long lists with variable row heights (log viewers with wrapped lines, search results with multi-line previews) jump when a row's real height differs from the assumed height; the predictor plus Fenwick index is the mechanism that keeps `scroll_to(i)` stable as rows get measured. Why the project cares: this block, like G08, replaces "exists and is tested" with "on by default, measured, and demonstrated".

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/virtualized.rs` (3,536 lines): `Virtualized<T>` :54 with `item_height: ItemHeight` :64; `pub enum ItemHeight { Fixed(u16), Variable(HeightCache), VariableFenwick(VariableHeightsFenwick) }` :88-95; `HeightCache` :99; `new(capacity)` :116 defaults `ItemHeight::Fixed(1)` :122 (and `external` :130 at :139); `with_item_height` :147, `with_fixed_height` :154, `with_variable_heights_fenwick(default_height, capacity)` :164; `visible_range` :222 matches on `item_height` at :228; `scroll_to(idx)` :329; `VariableHeightsFenwick` :626 (`new` :644, `from_heights` :661, `get` :690, `set` :699, `offset_of_item` :711, `find_item_at_offset` :730, `visible_count` :766, `total_height` :803, `resize` :810, `rebuild` :831) over `crate::fenwick::FenwickTree` (:604 import); `RenderItem` trait :845 with `fn height(&self) -> u16` :858; `VirtualizedListState` :865; `VirtualizedList<'a, T>` :1206 with fields `items, style, highlight_style, show_scrollbar, fixed_height: u16, hit_id`; `new(items)` :1224, `fixed_height` :1258, `hit_id` :1265; `impl<T: RenderItem> StatefulWidget for VirtualizedList` :1271.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/fenwick.rs` (851 lines): `FenwickTree` :37 (`new` :46, `from_values` :56, `update` :92, `set` :101, `get` :121, `prefix` :133, `range` :148, `total` :158, `batch_update` :170, `rebuild` :182, `find_prefix` :208, `resize` :235).
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/height_predictor.rs` (1,079 lines): `PredictorConfig` :48 (`Default` :63), `WelfordStats` :84, `HeightPrediction` :124, `HeightPredictor` :137 (`new(config)` :149, `register_category() -> usize` :166, `predict(category) -> HeightPrediction` :178, `observe(category, actual_height: u16) -> bool` :204 (returns whether the observation violated the interval), `posterior_mean` :282, `posterior_variance` :290, `total_measurements` :305, `total_violations` :310, `violation_rate` :315, `category_count` :323, `category_observations` :328).
- `rg -n 'HeightPredictor|with_variable_heights_fenwick|VariableFenwick' crates --glob '*.rs'` outside the two files: nothing.
- Consumers: `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/widget_gallery.rs:1920` `VirtualizedList::new(&self.virtualized_items).fixed_height(1).hit_id(VIRTUALIZED_SCROLLBAR_HIT_ID)` (fixed height); `virtualized_search.rs:613-621` `pub struct VirtualizedSearch { items: Vec<String>, filtered: Vec<FuzzyMatch>, selected, scroll_offset, viewport_height: Cell<usize>, search_input: TextInput, .. }` with items built at `:651` (doc header `:6` claims "`VirtualizedList` with large datasets (10k+ items)"); `log_search.rs:43` imports `ftui_widgets::log_viewer::{LogViewer, LogViewerState, LogWrapMode, SearchConfig, SearchMode}` and holds `viewer: LogViewer` :627 built at `:654` with `MAX_LOG_LINES`.
- VOI: `crates/ftui-runtime/src/voi_sampling.rs` (`VoiConfig` :152 with `alpha` :155, `sample_cost` :176, `min/max_interval_ms` :179/:183, `min/max_interval_events` :186/:190; `VoiSampler` :350 with `new` :372, `posterior_params` :450, `posterior_mean` :456, `expected_variance_after` :468, `last_decision` :474; `VoiDecision::to_jsonl` :244, `VoiObservation::to_jsonl` :284) is used only by inline-auto remeasure (`program.rs` `InlineAutoRemeasureConfig` :4022, state :4054); `voi_sample` evidence is never written (Section 2.2.C, G20).
- `crates/ftui-render/src/frame.rs:321 pub struct WidgetSignal { widget_id, essential, priority, staleness_ms, focus_boost, interaction_boost, area_cells, cost_estimate_us, recent_cost_us, estimate_source }` is a struct, not an enum; `Frame.widget_signals: Vec<WidgetSignal>`; `program.rs:6582 self.widget_signals = frame.take_widget_signals()`.
- Benches: `crates/ftui-widgets/benches/widget_bench.rs` has `virtualized/log_ring_push` :182, `virtualized/log_ring_push_full` :200, `bench_virtualized_scroll` :219; no `virtualized_bench.rs`.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/scripts/test_virtualized_search.sh` cases `vsearch_screen_load, vsearch_focus_search, vsearch_query, vsearch_navigation, vsearch_jump_bottom` (`:191`); `tests/e2e/scripts/test_log_search.sh`; showcase tests `virtualized_search_e2e.rs`, `virtualized_search_ux_a11y.rs`, `log_search_e2e.rs`; snapshots `log_search_*_{80x24,120x40}.snap` (14 files). Section 5.1 lists `vsearch_*` among macOS PTY failures.

## Target state

`Virtualized::with_variable_heights(default_height)` returns the Fenwick mode and is the documented way to get variable heights (the `Variable(HeightCache)` linear-scan mode stays available but is not the default for variable heights); `Virtualized` owns an optional `HeightPredictor` with per-category registration; `measure(idx, height)` feeds `observe` and updates the Fenwick tree; unmeasured rows use `predict().mean` rounded; a `RemeasurePolicy` (Beta-VOI, same formula as `voi_sampling.rs`) decides when to re-measure a visible row and emits a remeasure request through `Frame` that the runtime turns into `voi_sample` evidence (G20's writer); `virtualized_search` and `log_search` render through `VirtualizedList` with variable heights; the README claims for Fenwick, prediction, and VOI are backed by a proptest, a bench with a scroll-jump metric, re-blessed snapshots, and E2E evidence lines.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Proptest `scroll_to_index_is_stable_under_late_measurements` (`virtualized.rs`): after measuring rows out of order, `scroll_to(i)` lands within the predictor's conformal interval of the true offset, and the scroll-jump metric (sum of absolute offset corrections) is lower with the predictor than with a mean-height baseline on a synthetic long-tail corpus.
- [ ] Bench `crates/ftui-widgets/benches/virtualized_bench.rs` group `virtualized/scroll_jump` reports the metric for `fixed`, `mean_baseline`, `predictor` variants; the predictor variant's metric is the lowest; recorded in `docs/perf/virtualized_scroll_jump_2026-09.md`.
- [ ] `virtualized_search` and `log_search` snapshots re-blessed with `VirtualizedList`; `tests/e2e/scripts/test_virtualized_search.sh` and `test_log_search.sh` green on ubuntu and macOS (G04.9 cluster `vsearch_*`).
- [ ] Evidence `voi_sample` lines in the showcase E2E JSONL with fields `alpha, beta, voi, sample_cost, decision` (G20 names).
- [ ] Reachability gate: `ftui-widgets::height_predictor` and `fenwick` reachable (allowlist lines removed).

## Implementation plan (child beads)

1. `g10-impl`: Fenwick default for variable heights + predictor integration in `Virtualized`/`VirtualizedList`.
2. `g10-impl-voi`: `RemeasurePolicy`, remeasure requests through `Frame`, runtime translation to `voi_sample` (blocked by `g20-impl`).
3. `g10-impl-screens`: rewrite `virtualized_search` and `log_search` on `VirtualizedList`.
4. `g10-tests`: proptest, bench + metric, unit tests, snapshots.
5. `g10-e2e`: PTY cases + evidence assertions.
6. `g10-docs`: README rows and ledger.

## Dependencies and ordering

- `g10-impl-voi` blocked by `g20-impl` (evidence writer owns `voi_sample`).
- Unblocks: G04.9 `vsearch_*` root-cause cluster (`g04-09-impl`), `g06-impl` ledger rows for V11 and the widget-table row.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- `WidgetSignal` is a struct, so the plan's `WidgetSignal::Remeasure { index, voi, cost }` variant cannot exist; `g10-impl-voi` adds a sibling `Frame.remeasure_requests: Vec<RemeasureRequest>` with `push_remeasure_request`, keeping `WidgetSignal` untouched. Documented deviation from the plan text.
- Why not make Fenwick the default for ALL lists: fixed-height lists are the common case and `Fixed(1)` costs nothing; the default changes only for the variable-height constructor.
- Predictor categories: callers supply a category id per item kind (`RenderItem::category(&self) -> usize` default 0); the showcase's log viewer uses severity as the category so multi-line stack traces get their own prior.
- `LogViewer` is a real widget with search/highlight features that `VirtualizedList` lacks; `g10-impl-screens` must either compose `VirtualizedList` inside `LogViewer` or move the search decoration into the item renderer; the bead chooses composition so `LogViewer`'s search API survives.
- Risk: re-blessing 14 `log_search` snapshots hides regressions; the bead requires reviewing each diff for content parity (same lines visible at the same scroll positions).
- Rollback: `with_fixed_height` and `Variable(HeightCache)` remain.

## Definition of done

All child beads closed; proptest, bench record, snapshots, and E2E evidence committed; README rows truthful; close reason lists the metric numbers and the CI run id.

title: task(G10): Fenwick default for variable heights, HeightPredictor integration, variable-height VirtualizedList
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:859-884 says variable-height virtualized lists use a Fenwick tree and Bayesian height prediction; the code has both (`fenwick.rs`, `height_predictor.rs`) but `Virtualized<T>` defaults to `ItemHeight::Fixed(1)`, the Fenwick mode is opt-in with no caller, and `HeightPredictor` has no consumer at all. This bead connects them inside the widget: variable heights use the Fenwick index by default, unmeasured rows are predicted, measurements train the predictor. It is the primary implementation bead of G10 (V11 partial, Section 2.2.B rows for `height_predictor` and `fenwick`).

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/virtualized.rs`: `ItemHeight` :88-95; `Virtualized::new` :116 sets `Fixed(1)` :122; `external(len, cache_capacity)` :130 sets `Fixed(1)` :139; `with_item_height` :147; `with_fixed_height` :154; `with_variable_heights_fenwick(default_height, capacity)` :164; `visible_range(viewport_height)` :222 dispatches on `item_height` :228; `scroll_to` :329; `item_height()/item_height_mut()` :442/:450; `VariableHeights` (the `HeightCache` implementation) `new` :539, `get` :550, `set` :562, `clear` :594; `VariableHeightsFenwick` :626 (`new` :644, `from_heights` :661, `len` :672, `default_height` :684, `get` :690, `set` :699, `offset_of_item` :711, `find_item_at_offset` :730, `visible_count` :766, `total_height` :803, `resize` :810, `clear` :825, `rebuild` :831); `RenderItem` :845 with `height()` :858 defaulting (read the default body); `VirtualizedListState` :865; `VirtualizedList` :1206 (`fixed_height: u16` field; `new` :1224; `fixed_height` :1258; `hit_id` :1265); `StatefulWidget::render` :1271 (clears area with `clear_text_area`, reserves scrollbar space, iterates visible items with `fixed_height`).
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/height_predictor.rs`: `PredictorConfig` :48 (fields per `:48-62`; `Default` :63), `HeightPrediction` :124 (mean/lower/upper per `:124-136`), `HeightPredictor::new` :149, `register_category` :166, `predict(category)` :178, `observe(category, actual_height) -> bool` :204, `posterior_mean` :282, `posterior_variance` :290, `total_measurements` :305, `violation_rate` :315.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/fenwick.rs`: `FenwickTree::find_prefix(target) -> Option<usize>` :208 (the O(log n) scroll-to-offset primitive), `set` :101, `prefix` :133, `resize` :235.
- README claim for the widget table row: `VirtualizedList | Large lists | Fenwick tree scroll, Bayesian height prediction` (README.md:2165).

## Target state

- `Virtualized<T>`: new builder `with_variable_heights(default_height: u16)` (returns `VariableFenwick` sized to `len()`/capacity) and `with_height_predictor(PredictorConfig)`; new field `predictor: Option<HeightPredictor>`; new field `categories: Vec<usize>` is NOT stored (category comes from the item via `RenderItem::category(&self) -> usize`, default 0, at measurement time); new method `measure(&mut self, idx: usize, height: u16)` that sets the Fenwick entry and calls `predictor.observe(category, height)`; new method `predicted_height(&self, category) -> u16` returning `predict(category).mean.round().clamp(1, u16::MAX)` when a predictor exists, else `default_height`; `VariableHeightsFenwick` learns an "unmeasured" marker (a parallel `measured: BitVec`-style `Vec<u64>` bitset) so `get(idx)` returns the predicted height for unmeasured rows and the stored height otherwise; `scroll_to(idx)` uses `offset_of_item` (already O(log n)).
- `VirtualizedList<'a, T>`: `fixed_height: u16` becomes `height_mode: ListHeightMode { Fixed(u16), Variable }`; `variable_heights()` builder; in `render`, when `Variable`, each rendered row's actual height (from `RenderItem::height` or the number of wrapped lines produced) is fed back through `state.measure(idx, h)` (the `VirtualizedListState` :865 owns a `Virtualized<()>`-like index or exposes the `Virtualized` it wraps; read `:865-1160` to see what state holds and put `measure` where the Fenwick index lives).
- Predictor stats accessible: `Virtualized::predictor_stats() -> Option<PredictorStats { measurements, violations, violation_rate, categories }>` for the E2E/evidence path.

## Implementation plan

1. `virtualized.rs`: add `with_variable_heights(default_height)` next to `with_variable_heights_fenwick` (:164); keep `with_variable_heights_fenwick` as the explicit-capacity form (no shim: it stays because callers may want capacity control); update the doc comment on `ItemHeight::Variable(HeightCache)` to say it is the legacy linear-scan mode.
2. Add `predictor: Option<HeightPredictor>` to `Virtualized<T>` (:54-70), initialized `None` in `new` (:116) and `external` (:130); builder `with_height_predictor(config: PredictorConfig)`; `measure(idx, height)` and `predicted_height(category)`; wire `predicted_height` into `VariableHeightsFenwick::get` via a closure parameter or by storing the prediction inside the Fenwick wrapper on `set_default_height_for_unmeasured` (choose the simpler: `VariableHeightsFenwick` gets `unmeasured_height_for(&self, idx, fallback: impl Fn() -> u16)`; keep `fenwick.rs` unchanged).
3. `VariableHeightsFenwick`: add the measured bitset (`measured: Vec<u64>` with bit ops; no new dependency), `is_measured(idx)`, and make `set` mark the bit; `rebuild`/`from_heights` mark all; `clear`/`resize` maintain it.
4. `RenderItem` (:845): add `fn category(&self) -> usize { 0 }` (default method, backward compatible).
5. `VirtualizedList`: replace `fixed_height: u16` with `height_mode: ListHeightMode` (`Fixed(u16)` default 1, `Variable`); `fixed_height(h)` keeps its name and sets `Fixed(h)`; new `variable_heights()`; `render` (:1271): for `Variable`, compute each visible item's height via `RenderItem::height` (or the lines actually drawn), call `state.measure(idx, h)`, and use `find_item_at_offset`/`offset_of_item` for the scrollbar thumb and scroll math instead of multiplying by `fixed_height`.
6. `VirtualizedListState` (:865): ensure it owns the `Virtualized` index with `VariableFenwick` when the widget is `Variable` (state is created by the caller; add `VirtualizedListState::variable(default_height)` and `with_predictor(config)` constructors; `new()` :893 stays fixed).
7. `widget_gallery.rs:1920`: unchanged (fixed height is right there); `g10-impl-screens` converts the two search screens.
8. Gates: `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt`, `cargo test -p ftui-widgets` (existing virtualized tests must pass; update tests that assert the `Variable(HeightCache)` default path if any), `ubs`.

What NOT to do: no changes to `fenwick.rs` semantics; no removal of `Variable(HeightCache)`; no VOI logic here (`g10-impl-voi`); no `VirtualizedListV2`.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/virtualized.rs`: builders, predictor field, `measure`, `predicted_height`, measured bitset, `RenderItem::category`, `ListHeightMode`, `VirtualizedList::render`, state constructors.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/height_predictor.rs`: `PredictorStats` struct + `stats()` accessor (small addition; `Default` for `PredictorConfig` already exists).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `with_variable_heights(3)` on a 10,000-item list: `scroll_to(9_999)` then `visible_range(24)` computes in O(log n) (test asserts `offset_of_item(9_999) == 3 * 9_999` before any measurement and that `find_item_at_offset` round-trips for 100 random offsets).
- [ ] `measure(5, 7)` changes `offset_of_item(6)` by +4 and trains the predictor (`predictor_stats().measurements == 1`).
- [ ] Unmeasured rows use the predicted mean after 20 observations of height 4 in category 0: `predicted_height(0) == 4`.
- [ ] `VirtualizedList::variable_heights()` renders a 3-line item followed by a 1-line item at the correct rows (unit test with a `RenderItem` whose `height()` returns 3 for even ids).
- [ ] Existing `cargo test -p ftui-widgets virtualized` tests pass.

## Tests and logging

- Unit (`virtualized.rs`): `variable_heights_defaults_to_fenwick`, `offset_of_item_is_prefix_sum`, `find_item_at_offset_round_trips`, `measure_updates_fenwick_and_predictor`, `unmeasured_rows_use_predicted_mean`, `variable_list_renders_multi_line_items_at_correct_rows`, `category_default_is_zero`, `measured_bitset_tracks_set_and_rebuild`.
- Property/bench: in `g10-tests`.
- Logging: none in the widget (tracing `widget_render` span already exists at `:1275-1284` with `items`; add `height_mode` field to that span).

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: nothing (day-one track per Section 7.5).
- Unblocks: `g10-impl-voi`, `g10-impl-screens`, `g10-tests`, `g10-docs`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Why keep `fixed_height` as the default for `VirtualizedList::new`: fixed 1-line rows are the dominant use (gallery, simple lists) and need no Fenwick allocation.
- Why a bitset rather than `Option<u16>` per row: `VariableHeightsFenwick` stores `u32` sums in the tree; a parallel bitset is 1 bit/row and keeps `get` O(1).
- Predictor rounding: heights are integers; `predict().mean` rounds to nearest, clamped to at least 1 so a row never has zero height.
- Risk: `RenderItem::height` may be unknown until wrapping at the actual width; the render path measures after drawing, so the first frame uses predictions and the second frame is exact for visible rows. This is the designed behavior ("late measurements") that the proptest exercises.

## Definition of done

Builders, predictor integration, and variable-height rendering implemented; eight unit tests green; gates and `ubs` clean; close reason lists test names.

title: task(G10): RemeasurePolicy (Beta-VOI), Frame remeasure requests, voi_sample evidence for list and inline_auto
description:
## Context and why this matters

README vision row V11 "VOI sampling for expensive ops" is PARTIAL: value-of-information sampling exists in `crates/ftui-runtime/src/voi_sampling.rs` but is used only for inline-auto height remeasure, and the README's promised `voi_sample` evidence event is never written (Section 2.2.C row "Evidence events"). The reality check's G10 plan adds a second, widget-driven use: a virtualized list with variable heights should re-measure a visible row only when the expected reduction in scroll-position uncertainty is worth the measurement cost, and that decision should be visible in the evidence stream. This bead adds `RemeasurePolicy` to the widget, a remeasure-request channel through `Frame`, and the runtime translation into `voi_sample` evidence (whose canonical name and writer belong to G20, cluster D).

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/voi_sampling.rs`: `VoiConfig` :152 (`alpha` :155, `sample_cost` :176, `min_interval_ms` :179, `max_interval_ms` :183, `min_interval_events` :186, `max_interval_events` :190, `max_log_entries` :196), `VoiDecision` :222 (`cost` :229, `to_jsonl` :244), `VoiObservation` :269 (`alpha` :275, `beta` :276, `to_jsonl` :284), `VoiLogEntry` :302, `VoiSummary` :320, `VoiSamplerSnapshot` :335 (`alpha` :337, `beta` :338), `VoiSampler` :350 (`new` :372, `new_at` :377, `config` :444, `posterior_params` :450, `posterior_mean` :456, `posterior_variance` :462, `expected_variance_after` :468, `last_decision` :474). Section 2.2.B: `VoiConfig` defaults are alpha 1 / beta 1 / max 250 ms / min 0 / cost 0.01 (README's 1/9/1000/100/0.08 are `InlineAutoRemeasureConfig` values at `program.rs:4022-4052`).
- The VOI code lives in ftui-runtime; ftui-widgets cannot depend on ftui-runtime (runtime depends on widgets). The Beta-VOI formula is small (posterior variance of a Beta(alpha, beta) minus expected posterior variance after one more Bernoulli sample, compared with `sample_cost`); the widget needs its own minimal implementation of the decision rule, and the runtime keeps `VoiSampler` for inline-auto. To avoid a third copy, move the pure formula into `ftui-core` as `ftui_core::voi::{beta_voi(alpha, beta) -> f64, BetaPosterior}` and have `voi_sampling.rs` call it (a refactor of a few lines; no behavior change; tests in `voi_sampling.rs` stay).
- `crates/ftui-render/src/frame.rs:321 pub struct WidgetSignal { .. }` is a struct; `Frame.widget_signals: Vec<WidgetSignal>`; `program.rs:6582 self.widget_signals = frame.take_widget_signals()`; `Program::last_widget_signals` :5230. So a `WidgetSignal::Remeasure` variant is impossible; a sibling collection is needed.
- Evidence: `EvidenceSink::write_jsonl` (`evidence_sink.rs:200`); `Program.evidence_sink: Option<EvidenceSink>`; showcase enables the sink via `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL` (`main.rs:219-229`). `voi_decision`/`voi_observe` have `to_jsonl` but `Program` never writes them (Section 2.2.C, `program.rs:6301` per the reality check).
- `telemetry_schema.rs:47 TARGET_VOI = "ftui.voi"` exists.

## Target state

- `ftui-core`: `pub mod voi` with `BetaPosterior { alpha: f64, beta: f64 }` (`mean`, `variance`, `expected_variance_after_sample`, `voi()`), `pub fn beta_voi(alpha, beta) -> f64`; `voi_sampling.rs` uses it.
- `ftui-widgets` `virtualized.rs`: `RemeasurePolicy { posterior: BetaPosterior, sample_cost: f64, min_interval_frames: u32, last_sample_frame: u64 }` with `should_remeasure(&mut self, frame_idx, violation_observed: bool) -> Option<RemeasureDecision { voi, cost }>`; the Bernoulli event is "the last measurement violated the predictor's interval" (`HeightPredictor::observe` returns exactly that bool at `:204`), so `alpha` counts violations and `beta` counts confirmations; when VOI > cost and the interval has elapsed, the widget re-measures the topmost visible row (forces its `measured` bit off so the next render measures it) and pushes a `RemeasureRequest` to the frame.
- `ftui-render` `frame.rs`: `pub struct RemeasureRequest { pub widget_id: u64, pub index: usize, pub voi: f64, pub cost: f64, pub alpha: f64, pub beta: f64 }`, `Frame.remeasure_requests: Vec<RemeasureRequest>` (private) with `push_remeasure_request` and `take_remeasure_requests`.
- `ftui-runtime` `program.rs`: after `take_widget_signals` (:6582), `for req in frame.take_remeasure_requests()` write one `voi_sample` evidence line `{"event":"voi_sample","source":"virtualized_list","widget_id":..,"index":..,"alpha":..,"beta":..,"voi":..,"sample_cost":..,"decision":"sample"}` through the sink and `tracing::debug!(target: TARGET_VOI, ...)`; also emit `voi_sample` with `"source":"inline_auto"` from the existing inline-auto decision path (the same event name, G20's canonical fields `alpha, beta, voi, sample_cost, decision`), replacing the never-written `voi_decision` line.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-core/src/voi.rs` (new; genuinely new shared math) + `pub mod voi;` in `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs`; port the formula from `voi_sampling.rs:450-472` (`posterior_variance`, `expected_variance_after`) verbatim, with unit tests `beta_voi_decreases_as_evidence_accumulates`, `beta_voi_is_nonnegative`.
2. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/voi_sampling.rs`: replace the private formula bodies with calls to `ftui_core::voi`; run its existing tests.
3. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/virtualized.rs`: `RemeasurePolicy` (+ `Default` matching README's documented defaults for this use: alpha 1, beta 9, cost 0.08, min interval 6 frames; document that these are the list defaults, distinct from inline-auto) and `Virtualized::with_remeasure_policy(policy)`; in `VirtualizedList::render` (Variable mode) call `state.remeasure_tick(frame_idx_from_state_or_counter)` and push the request via `frame.push_remeasure_request` when it returns `Some`; the widget id is the `hit_id` value if set else `stable_id_for`-style hash of the area (reuse G09's helper if merged, else a local hash).
4. `crates/ftui-render/src/frame.rs`: `RemeasureRequest`, the vec, `push_remeasure_request`, `take_remeasure_requests`; initialize in the three constructors.
5. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: translate requests into `voi_sample` lines (format registered with `g20-impl`); rewrite the inline-auto decision emission to the same event with `source: "inline_auto"`; use `telemetry_schema::TARGET_VOI` for tracing.
6. Gates and `ubs`.

What NOT to do: no `ftui-widgets -> ftui-runtime` dependency; no enum-ification of `WidgetSignal`; no second VOI formula copy (the core module is the only implementation); no event name other than the one G20 registers (`voi_sample`).

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-core/src/voi.rs` (new), `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/voi_sampling.rs`: delegate formula.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/virtualized.rs`: `RemeasurePolicy`, wiring in render.
- `crates/ftui-render/src/frame.rs`: `RemeasureRequest` channel.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `voi_sample` emission (both sources).

## Success criteria

- [ ] Unit `remeasure_policy_samples_when_voi_exceeds_cost`: alpha=1, beta=1, cost=0.01 -> `Some`; alpha=1, beta=200, cost=0.08 -> `None`.
- [ ] Unit `remeasure_policy_respects_min_interval`: two consecutive frames -> second is `None`.
- [ ] Headless runtime test `virtualized_list_remeasure_request_emits_voi_sample_evidence`: a model rendering a variable-height `VirtualizedList` with a policy that always samples produces a `"event":"voi_sample"` line with `"source":"virtualized_list"` and the five canonical fields.
- [ ] Headless test `inline_auto_remeasure_emits_voi_sample_evidence` with `"source":"inline_auto"`.
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-runtime voi_sampling` unchanged and green after the formula moves.

## Tests and logging

- Unit: as above plus `beta_voi_*` in core.
- Property (in `g10-tests`): `proptest_voi_monotone_in_beta` (for fixed alpha, VOI is non-increasing in beta).
- Logging: evidence `voi_sample` with `source, widget_id, index, alpha, beta, voi, sample_cost, decision`; tracing `ftui.voi` debug per decision.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: `g10-impl` (variable heights and the predictor's violation bool), `g20-impl` (canonical `voi_sample` fields and the evidence writer; if G20 defines a typed writer API, use it instead of `format!`).
- Unblocks: `g10-tests`, `g10-e2e`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Bernoulli event choice: "interval violation" is the quantity the predictor already reports and is the natural signal of model misfit; sampling more when violations are frequent is exactly what VOI should do.
- Alternative rejected: re-measure every visible row every frame (that is what fixed-height lists effectively do and what `Variable(HeightCache)` does with a linear scan); the whole point of the predictor is to avoid it.
- Risk: a policy that never samples on a list whose content changes silently (rows edited in place); `Virtualized::invalidate(idx)` (clears the measured bit) is the caller's tool and is documented.

## Definition of done

Shared formula in core; policy and request channel implemented; runtime writes `voi_sample` for both sources; five tests green; gates and `ubs` clean; close reason includes one sample evidence line of each source.

title: task(G10): virtualized_search and log_search (via LogViewer) render through VirtualizedList, variable heights
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:111 credits the `virtualized_search` and `log_search` showcase screens with "Fenwick-backed virtualization", and `virtualized_search.rs:6` says the screen demonstrates "`VirtualizedList` with large datasets (10k+ items)". Neither screen uses `VirtualizedList`: `virtualized_search` keeps its own `Vec<String>` plus filter indices and hand-rolled scroll math, and `log_search` is built on `LogViewer`. The only `VirtualizedList` consumer is the widget gallery with fixed heights. After `g10-impl`, the two screens must actually run on `VirtualizedList` with variable heights so the README row is true, the predictor and Fenwick index are exercised by the reference app, and the `vsearch_*` PTY cases (a failing cluster in Section 5.1) have a real subject. Serves V11, Section 2.2.B, and G04.9.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/virtualized_search.rs` (73 KB): `pub struct VirtualizedSearch` :613 with `items: Vec<String>` :615, `filtered: Vec<FuzzyMatch>` (indices into items + scores), `selected: usize`, `scroll_offset: usize`, `viewport_height: Cell<usize>`, `search_input: TextInput`; items built at `:651` from `0..TOTAL_ITEMS`; header doc `:6`.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/log_search.rs` (84 KB): `:43 use ftui_widgets::log_viewer::{LogViewer, LogViewerState, LogWrapMode, SearchConfig, SearchMode};` `viewer: LogViewer` :627, `viewer_state: LogViewerState` :628, `LogViewer::new(MAX_LOG_LINES)` :654; wrap modes and search highlighting are `LogViewer` features.
- `widget_gallery.rs:1920`: `VirtualizedList::new(&self.virtualized_items).fixed_height(1).hit_id(VIRTUALIZED_SCROLLBAR_HIT_ID)`.
- Snapshots: `log_search_{after_ticks,case_sensitive,context_lines,filter_mode,highlighted_matches,initial,match_navigation}_120x40.snap`, `log_search_{bar_open,filter_bar_open,high_contrast_highlight,initial,no_results,paused}_80x24.snap` (13 files); `virtualized_search_*` snapshots exist in `tests/snapshots` (list them with `ls crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/snapshots | rg virtualized_search` before starting).
- Tests: `tests/virtualized_search_e2e.rs`, `tests/virtualized_search_ux_a11y.rs`, `tests/log_search_e2e.rs`; PTY `tests/e2e/scripts/test_virtualized_search.sh` (cases `vsearch_screen_load, vsearch_focus_search, vsearch_query, vsearch_navigation, vsearch_jump_bottom` at `:191-231`), `tests/e2e/scripts/test_log_search.sh`.
- `VirtualizedList<'a, T: RenderItem>` renders from a slice `&'a [T]`; filtering must therefore produce a slice of items or the list must support an index set. `Virtualized<T>` has `VirtualizedStorage::External` (`external(len, cache_capacity)` :130, `set_external_len` :520) which is designed for "the caller owns the items" cases.

## Target state

- `virtualized_search`: the screen owns `items: Vec<SearchItem>` (unchanged data) and a `VirtualizedListState` in variable-height mode with a predictor (category = item kind: 0 plain, 1 multi-line preview); the visible list is `VirtualizedList::new(&self.filtered_items)` where `filtered_items: Vec<SearchRow>` is rebuilt on query change (each `SearchRow` references the item index and match spans; `RenderItem` impl renders the highlighted name plus a 1-2 line preview whose height depends on the item, so heights vary); navigation keys and mouse use the state's `scroll_to`/`select` APIs instead of the hand-rolled offset math; the 10k-item claim stays.
- `log_search`: `LogViewer` keeps its search/filter/highlight API but renders its visible window through `VirtualizedList` in variable-height mode (wrapped lines have variable height, which is exactly the Fenwick case). Concretely: `crates/ftui-widgets/src/log_viewer.rs` gains an internal `VirtualizedListState` and delegates viewport/scroll computation to it (so ALL `LogViewer` users get Fenwick, not only the demo), and the demo screen is unchanged except for re-blessed snapshots. If `LogViewer`'s internals make that a large change, the fallback is the demo-only rewrite; the bead records which path was taken and why.
- Snapshots for both screens re-blessed with content parity reviewed line by line.

## Implementation plan

1. Read `virtualized_search.rs:600-900` (state, update, view) and `log_viewer.rs` (viewport code) to locate the hand-rolled scroll math.
2. `virtualized_search.rs`: add `list_state: VirtualizedListState` (variable, predictor with two categories), `filtered_rows: Vec<SearchRow>`; implement `RenderItem for SearchRow` (`height()` = 1 + preview lines; `category()` = 0/1; render with match highlighting using the existing `FuzzyMatch` spans); replace `scroll_offset`/`viewport_height` bookkeeping with `list_state` calls; keep `selected` as the list's selection; keep `search_input` and the keymap; `hit_id` for the scrollbar so mouse works as in the gallery.
3. `log_viewer.rs`: introduce `VirtualizedListState` for the visible window (variable heights = wrapped line counts per `LogWrapMode`); `LogViewerState` scroll fields map onto it; search/highlight decoration remains in the line renderer. Keep the public API of `LogViewer` unchanged.
4. `log_search.rs`: no logic change expected; re-bless the 13 snapshots and review diffs (same visible lines at the same positions; only the scrollbar thumb may move if the height model changed).
5. Re-bless `virtualized_search_*` snapshots; review.
6. Update `tests/virtualized_search_e2e.rs` / `log_search_e2e.rs` expectations if scroll semantics changed (e.g. `jump_bottom` now lands on the exact last row via `scroll_to_end`).
7. Gates, `cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase -p ftui-widgets`, `ubs`.

What NOT to do: no second list widget; no keeping the old scroll math beside the new state ("temporary" dual paths are shims); no snapshot blessing without diff review (list the reviewed files in the close reason).

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/virtualized_search.rs`: `VirtualizedList` + state + `RenderItem`.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/log_viewer.rs`: Fenwick-backed viewport via `VirtualizedListState` (preferred path).
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/log_search.rs`: only if the fallback path is taken.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/snapshots/{virtualized_search_*,log_search_*}.snap`: re-blessed.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/{virtualized_search_e2e,log_search_e2e}.rs`: expectation updates.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `rg -n 'VirtualizedList' crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/virtualized_search.rs crates/ftui-widgets/src/log_viewer.rs` hits both (or `log_search.rs` on the fallback path).
- [ ] `virtualized_search` unit test `filter_then_scroll_to_end_selects_last_match` (10k items, query "7", `scroll_to_end`, selected == last filtered index) passes.
- [ ] `log_viewer` unit test `wrapped_lines_have_variable_heights_in_fenwick_index` (three lines of 10/100/250 chars at width 40 -> heights 1/3/7; `offset_of_item(2) == 4`).
- [ ] All showcase snapshot tests green after re-bless; diff review recorded.
- [ ] `tests/e2e/scripts/test_virtualized_search.sh` and `test_log_search.sh` pass locally under `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` on Linux (macOS handled by G04.9's runner work; the JSONL from a local run is attached to the close reason).

## Tests and logging

- Unit: the two tests above plus `search_rows_report_category_by_preview_lines`.
- Snapshot: re-blessed sets.
- E2E: `g10-e2e` extends the PTY scripts with evidence assertions.
- Logging: showcase tracing `ftui.demo.vsearch` debug with `query_len, filtered, selected, scroll_offset` on each update (helps diagnose `vsearch_*` PTY failures).

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: `g10-impl`.
- Unblocks: `g10-e2e`, `g04-09-impl` (vsearch cluster), `g10-docs`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- `LogViewer` path chosen over demo-only rewrite because README's widget table (`LogViewer` is a production widget) and the plan's intent ("the two search demos use `VirtualizedList`") are both served, and every consumer of `LogViewer` benefits.
- Risk: `log_search` snapshots at 120x40 include highlighted match positions; if the wrap height model changes where lines break, the diffs will be visible and must be judged for correctness, not just accepted.
- Risk: `VirtualizedList` needs `&[T]`; rebuilding `filtered_rows` on every keystroke for 10k items is fine (the fuzzy filter already does O(n) work per keystroke).

## Definition of done

Both screens run on `VirtualizedList` with variable heights; snapshots re-blessed with reviewed diffs; unit and E2E scripts green locally; gates and `ubs` clean; close reason lists the path taken for `log_search` and the reviewed snapshot files.

title: task(G10): Scroll-stability proptest, Fenwick mutation proptest, scroll-jump bench metric, VOI policy tests
description:
## Context

Companion test bead for `g10-impl` (Fenwick default + predictor), `g10-impl-voi` (remeasure policy + `voi_sample`), and `g10-impl-screens` (search screens on `VirtualizedList`). The README claims are algorithmic ("O(log n) scroll positioning", "predict unseen row heights to avoid scroll jumps") so the proofs are a property test on scroll stability under late measurements, a benchmark that measures a scroll-jump metric across strategies, and unit tests on the policy; the screen rewrite is proven by snapshots and the PTY scripts (`g10-e2e`).

## What to test

1. Scroll stability: measuring rows out of order after `scroll_to(i)` keeps the landed offset within the predictor's conformal interval of the true offset, and the total correction is smaller with the predictor than with a mean-height baseline.
2. Fenwick correctness under mutation: prefix sums and `find_prefix` agree with a naive scan after random `set`/`resize`/`rebuild`.
3. Predictor behavior: violation rate near alpha on a stationary corpus; categories are independent.
4. VOI policy: monotonicity in beta; interval gating; request emission.
5. Speed: scroll-jump metric and `scroll_to` latency on 100k rows, recorded.

## Test types (unit, property, bench, E2E) with names and assertions

Property (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/virtualized.rs` `mod proptests`, `proptest`):
- `scroll_to_index_is_stable_under_late_measurements`: strategy generates `n in 500..5000` rows with a long-tail height distribution (80% height 1, 15% height 2-4, 5% height 5-30, seeded), a permutation for measurement order, and a target `i`; build `Virtualized::with_variable_heights(1).with_height_predictor(default)`; measure the first 10% of rows in permutation order (training); `scroll_to(i)`; record `offset_before`; then measure the remaining rows in permutation order, after each batch of 50 re-derive the list's offset for `i` (`offset_of_item(i)`) and accumulate `|delta|` into `jump_predictor`; assert final `offset_of_item(i)` within `predict(cat).upper - lower` cells of the true prefix sum (compute from the generated heights) and that `jump_predictor <= jump_mean_baseline` where the baseline run uses a fixed `default_height = round(mean height)` and no predictor. 256 cases; `ProptestConfig { cases: 256, .. }`.
- `fenwick_prefix_matches_naive_after_random_mutations` (`fenwick.rs`): random `set`/`update`/`resize`/`rebuild` ops; `prefix(k)` equals naive sum; `find_prefix(t)` equals naive search. 512 cases.
- `proptest_voi_monotone_in_beta` (`ftui-core/src/voi.rs`): for `alpha in 1..50`, `beta1 < beta2` -> `beta_voi(alpha, beta1) >= beta_voi(alpha, beta2)`.

Unit (`virtualized.rs`): the eight from `g10-impl` (`variable_heights_defaults_to_fenwick`, `offset_of_item_is_prefix_sum`, `find_item_at_offset_round_trips`, `measure_updates_fenwick_and_predictor`, `unmeasured_rows_use_predicted_mean`, `variable_list_renders_multi_line_items_at_correct_rows`, `category_default_is_zero`, `measured_bitset_tracks_set_and_rebuild`) plus `remeasure_policy_samples_when_voi_exceeds_cost`, `remeasure_policy_respects_min_interval`, `invalidate_clears_measured_bit`.
Unit (`height_predictor.rs`): `violation_rate_near_alpha_on_stationary_data` (alpha 0.1, 2,000 Normal samples -> rate in [0.05, 0.15]), `categories_are_independent` (train cat 0 at 3, cat 1 at 9; `predict(0).mean` near 3, `predict(1).mean` near 9).
Headless (`program.rs`): `virtualized_list_remeasure_request_emits_voi_sample_evidence`, `inline_auto_remeasure_emits_voi_sample_evidence`, `voi_sample_line_is_valid_json_with_registered_fields`.
Unit (showcase/widgets): `filter_then_scroll_to_end_selects_last_match`, `wrapped_lines_have_variable_heights_in_fenwick_index`, `search_rows_report_category_by_preview_lines`.

Bench (`crates/ftui-widgets/benches/virtualized_bench.rs`, new criterion bench with `harness = false`; the existing `widget_bench.rs` keeps its `virtualized/log_ring_push*` groups and `bench_virtualized_scroll` :219; the new file exists because the scroll-jump metric needs a custom measurement loop that does not fit `widget_bench.rs`'s render-timing groups):
- Group `virtualized/scroll_to` at 10k and 100k rows: `fixed`, `variable_linear` (`Variable(HeightCache)`), `variable_fenwick`; assert in the README (via `g10-docs`) only what the numbers show.
- Group `virtualized/scroll_jump` (custom `iter_custom`): same corpus generator as the proptest, 100k rows; variants `fixed_1`, `mean_baseline`, `predictor`; the metric (sum of |offset corrections| while measuring all rows after a `scroll_to(n/2)`) is reported through `criterion::black_box` timing AND written as JSON to `target/criterion/virtualized_scroll_jump.json` (`{variant, rows, jump_cells, measurements}`) by the bench itself; `docs/perf/virtualized_scroll_jump_2026-09.md` copies the table.
- Baseline row `tests/baseline.json` `virtualized_scroll_to_100k` with criterion name `virtualized/scroll_to/variable_fenwick/100000`, `bench_file: "virtualized_bench"`, `crate: "ftui-widgets"`, `slo_metric: "virtualized_scroll_to_p99_ns"`, p99 from the artifact, `threshold_pct: 10`.

Snapshot: `virtualized_search_*` and `log_search_*` re-blessed (`g10-impl-screens`), plus `widget_gallery` unchanged.

E2E: `g10-e2e`.

## Logging (structured JSONL fields, tracing targets)

- Proptest failures print the seed, `n`, `i`, `jump_predictor`, `jump_mean_baseline`, and the interval bounds via the assertion message.
- Bench JSON `virtualized_scroll_jump.json` fields: `variant, rows, jump_cells, measurements, generated_at, git_commit`.
- Evidence `voi_sample` fields `source, widget_id, index, alpha, beta, voi, sample_cost, decision`; tracing `ftui.voi`.
- Showcase tracing `ftui.demo.vsearch`.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/{virtualized,fenwick,height_predictor}.rs` test modules; `crates/ftui-widgets/benches/virtualized_bench.rs` (new) + `Cargo.toml` `[[bench]]`; `crates/ftui-core/src/voi.rs` tests; `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` tests; showcase test modules; `tests/baseline.json`; `docs/perf/virtualized_scroll_jump_2026-09.md`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] All named tests pass (`rch exec -- cargo test -p ftui-widgets -p ftui-core -p ftui-runtime -p ftui-demo-showcase`).
- [ ] `scroll_to_index_is_stable_under_late_measurements` passes 256 cases; the assertion `jump_predictor <= jump_mean_baseline` holds in every case (if it fails on some seeds, the predictor config is tuned in `g10-impl`, not the test loosened, unless the reason is documented).
- [ ] Bench artifact and `docs/perf/virtualized_scroll_jump_2026-09.md` committed; `predictor` has the lowest `jump_cells`.
- [ ] Baseline row committed with measured numbers.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: `g10-impl`, `g10-impl-voi` (VOI tests), `g10-impl-screens` (screen tests).
- Related: `g25-impl` for running the baseline row in CI.

## Definition of done

Tests, proptests, bench, baseline row, and perf record exist and pass; close reason lists test names, proptest case counts, and the metric table.
notes: Refinement 2 supersedes the universal jump_predictor <= mean_baseline criterion: a statistical predictor cannot dominate every arbitrary sequence. Prove exact viewport-anchor/index invariants independently of prediction quality; compare predictive jump/error cost on held-out declared corpora with uncertainty and include adverse sequences. Do not tune against failing property seeds until the claim passes or require predictor to win by construction. Preserve bounded worst-case correction/fallback and report losing/inconclusive cases.

title: task(G10): PTY cases for variable heights and Fenwick scroll positions; voi_sample assertions in showcase E2E
description:
## Context and why this matters

The G10 wiring is only "WORKING" per the reality check's definition when it is proven under a real PTY with structured logs. Two PTY scripts already target the affected screens (`tests/e2e/scripts/test_virtualized_search.sh` with five `vsearch_*` cases, `tests/e2e/scripts/test_log_search.sh`) and the `vsearch_*` cluster is among the PTY failures on macOS in Section 5.1. This bead makes those scripts assert the new behavior (variable heights, Fenwick scroll positioning) and adds evidence assertions for `voi_sample` in the showcase E2E run, so both the README claims and the G04.9 root-cause work have a named, logged proof.

## Current state (evidence)

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_virtualized_search.sh`: `RUN_ID="vsearch_$(e2e_log_stamp)"` :29; cases listed at `:191` (`vsearch_screen_load vsearch_focus_search vsearch_query vsearch_navigation vsearch_jump_bottom`); each case writes `$E2E_LOG_DIR/<case>.log` and `.pty` (`:203-231`).
- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_log_search.sh` exists; `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh` runs the suite (166 cases per Section 5.1).
- `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh` (108 KB) has an evidence step at `:2364` that runs the demo with `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL="$EXPLAIN_REPORT"`, `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS=3200`, `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN=40`, and a `stty` resize storm; `jsonl_assert`/`jsonl_step_*` helpers from `tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh` (63 KB); JSONL validated with `tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py`.
- `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` (17 KB) is the Python-`pty` driver (real PTY, key injection, capture, canonicalization).
- After `g10-impl-voi`: `voi_sample` lines with `source: virtualized_list|inline_auto`.

## Target state

- `test_virtualized_search.sh` gains cases `vsearch_variable_heights` (query that matches items with multi-line previews; assert the canonicalized screen shows a preview line under a result, i.e. rows of different heights) and `vsearch_scroll_position_after_jump` (`End` then `Home` then `PageDown` x3; assert the selected row marker is on the row the Fenwick offset math predicts: the script knows the corpus, so it computes the expected row index and asserts the highlighted text matches the item at that index), and every case logs `frames` (count of `2026h` brackets), `bytes`, `exit_code`, and `duration_ms`.
- `test_log_search.sh` gains `logsearch_wrapped_lines_variable_height` (enable wrap mode via the screen's key, assert a long line occupies more than one row and the following line starts below it).
- `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh` evidence step gains assertions `voi_sample_present_virtualized_list` (at least one `voi_sample` line with `"source":"virtualized_list"` when the run visits the `virtualized_search` screen; add a second evidence run with `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN=<virtualized_search index resolved from screens/mod.rs>` if screen 40 is not it) and `voi_sample_fields` (each line has `alpha, beta, voi, sample_cost, decision`), plus `voi_sample_present_inline_auto` in the inline-mode run if one exists.
- All three scripts pass on ubuntu via `run_all.sh`; macOS via G04.9.

## Implementation plan

1. Read `test_virtualized_search.sh:1-120` for the helper names (`e2e_pty_*`, `canonicalize`), then add the two cases following the `vsearch_query` pattern (`:203-260`): key sequences with 200 ms gaps, capture, canonicalize, assert with `grep -c`/python (no `rg` dependence until G04.6).
2. Compute expected rows inside the script from the corpus rule (the showcase builds items from `0..TOTAL_ITEMS` at `virtualized_search.rs:651`; the preview rule is defined in `g10-impl-screens`; the script mirrors it in a small python snippet to avoid drift, or the screen exposes `FTUI_DEMO_VSEARCH_DUMP=1` to print `selected_index` and `offset` to stderr for the script to read; prefer the dump because it is exact).
3. `test_log_search.sh`: add the wrap case; the wrap toggle key is in `log_search.rs`'s keymap (read it).
4. `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh`: after the existing evidence assertions in the `:2364` step, add the `voi_sample` assertions with python one-liners over the evidence file; log the counts in `jsonl_assert` details.
5. Add the new case names to `run_all.sh`'s enumeration if it lists cases explicitly.
6. Run locally: `tests/e2e/scripts/test_virtualized_search.sh`, `test_log_search.sh`, `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh`; validate JSONL; attach paths.

What NOT to do: no timing-based assertions (frame counts are logged, not asserted); no screen-index constants (resolve from `screens/mod.rs` slugs); no editing of the showcase to special-case the tests beyond the optional dump env var.

## Files to change

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_virtualized_search.sh`: two cases + logging fields.
- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_log_search.sh`: one case.
- `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh`: evidence assertions.
- `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh`: case list if explicit.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/virtualized_search.rs`: optional `FTUI_DEMO_VSEARCH_DUMP` stderr line (one `eprintln!` guarded by the env var; keep it out of the PTY stdout).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `tests/e2e/scripts/test_virtualized_search.sh` reports 7/7 cases PASS locally with JSONL validated.
- [ ] `test_log_search.sh` PASS including `logsearch_wrapped_lines_variable_height`.
- [ ] `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh` shows `voi_sample_present_virtualized_list pass` and `voi_sample_fields pass`; the evidence file has at least one `virtualized_list` line and one `inline_auto` line when the inline run exists.
- [ ] CI `e2e-pty` job (ubuntu) green for these scripts after G04.6 tooling (run id in the close reason); macOS tracked by `g04-09-impl`.

## Tests and logging

- E2E JSONL per case: `run_id`, `scenario` (`vsearch`, `logsearch`, `demo_showcase`), `case_step_start`/`case_step_end` with `duration_ms`, `assert` rows with `detail` (`selected_index=..`, `expected_index=..`, `voi_lines=..`), escape tallies `sync_pairs=<n> altscreen_enter=<n> cursor_hide=<n>` in the case detail, `exit_code`, PTY raw capture paths.
- Showcase evidence lines quoted in the close reason.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: `g10-impl-screens` (screens on `VirtualizedList`), `g10-impl-voi` (evidence lines).
- Related: `g04-06-impl` (runner tooling), `g04-09-impl` (macOS failures), `g20-impl` (schema validation of `voi_sample`).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- The dump env var is a test seam in production code; it is a single guarded `eprintln!` and documented in the screen header; acceptable because it makes the assertion exact instead of heuristic.
- Alternative rejected: asserting scroll positions by pixel-like row counting from the canonicalized screen only; row heights vary by design so text matching plus the dump is more robust.

## Definition of done

Scripts extended and green locally with validated JSONL; CI ubuntu run green; close reason lists case names, the evidence lines, and the run id.

title: docs(G10): README Fenwick/height-prediction/VOI sections and widget/demo table rows match the code
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:859-884 (Fenwick tree; Bayesian height prediction + conformal bounds), README.md:2165 (widget table row `VirtualizedList | Large lists | Fenwick tree scroll, Bayesian height prediction`), README.md:111 (demo table: `virtualized_search`, `log_search` "Fenwick-backed virtualization"), and the VOI defaults row in Section 2.2.C (README quotes 1 / 9 / 1000 / 100 / 0.08, which are `InlineAutoRemeasureConfig` values, while `VoiConfig` defaults are 1 / 1 / 250 / 0 / 0.01) must match the code after G10. The claims ledger (G06) needs rows for V11 and the two table rows, each pointing at the proptest, the bench record, the snapshots, and the E2E cases.

## Current state (evidence)

- README.md:859-870: Fenwick pseudo-code and "O(log n) height lookup and scroll positioning without scanning all rows".
- README.md:871-884: Normal-Normal prior/posterior, conformal interval, Welford variance, "q is the empirical quantile of |residuals|".
- README.md:2165 and :111 as quoted above.
- After G10: `Virtualized::with_variable_heights`, `with_height_predictor(PredictorConfig)`, `measure`, `RemeasurePolicy` (list defaults alpha 1, beta 9, cost 0.08, min interval 6 frames), `RenderItem::category`, `VirtualizedList::variable_heights`, `voi_sample` evidence with `source`.

## Target state

The README sections state how to opt in (`VirtualizedList::new(&items).variable_heights()` with `VirtualizedListState::variable(default_height).with_predictor(PredictorConfig::default())`), what the predictor does (per-category Normal-Normal with Welford variance; conformal interval from residual quantiles; `observe` reports interval violations), how remeasurement is scheduled (Beta-VOI on violation events, list defaults, `voi_sample` evidence with `source: "virtualized_list"`), and what the measured scroll-jump improvement was (from `docs/perf/virtualized_scroll_jump_2026-09.md`, with the date). The VOI defaults paragraph names both configs (`VoiConfig` for the runtime sampler, `InlineAutoRemeasureConfig` for inline auto-remeasure, `RemeasurePolicy` for lists) with their real numbers. The demo table row is true. `docs/spec/telemetry-events.md` lists `voi_sample` (coordinate with `g20-impl`, which owns the event registry; this bead supplies the list-source fields).

1. README :859-884: keep the math, add an "In code" paragraph with the builder calls and file paths (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/virtualized.rs`, `height_predictor.rs`, `fenwick.rs`), and the measured metric line "On a 100k-row long-tail corpus the predictor reduced total scroll correction from X to Y cells (docs/perf/virtualized_scroll_jump_2026-09.md)".

title: epic(G11): Conformal frame-time gating on by default with warm-up; stages stay experimental
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:994-1004 "### Mondrian Conformal Frame-Time Risk Gating" promises: "Frame-time risk gating uses **bucketed (Mondrian) conformal prediction** keyed by screen mode, diff strategy, and size: Residuals r_t = y_t - ŷ_t; Upper bound ŷ_t^+ = ŷ_t + q_{1-α}(|r|); Risk if ŷ_t^+ > budget. Buckets fall back from (mode, diff, size) → (mode, diff) → (mode) → global default", and README.md:1388-1410 "## Degradation Cascade" draws "Conformal Frame Guard → Budget Controller (PID) → Degradation Level Selection". Vision row V13 is OPT-IN: the predictor is real and wired into `render_frame`, but `ProgramConfig::default()` sets `conformal_config: None`, so no consumer and not even the showcase runs it; only `ftui-harness/src/main.rs` (env `FTUI_HARNESS_CONFORMAL`) and unit tests enable it. Vision row V14 (multi-stage conformal monitors, README.md:2630-2645) is DEAD: `conformal_stages.rs` is unreferenced. A user who reads the README believes frames are risk-gated before they blow the budget; in practice only the reactive PID/e-process controller runs.

This epic flips the predictor on by default with a warm-up so it cannot degrade on cold buckets, keeps headless/simulator constructors off (determinism), gives the showcase the same default, records the `fallback_level` distribution in the showcase E2E evidence, proves the cost is one quantile lookup per frame against the `frame_render` baseline row, and leaves `conformal_stages` experimental until per-stage timings justify wiring it. Closes V13, V37 (PID cascade as documented), and the OPT-IN row in Section 2.2.B.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `pub conformal_config: Option<ConformalConfig>` :2940; default `conformal_config: None` :3008; builders `with_conformal_config(ConformalConfig)` :3143 and `without_conformal()` :3151; predictor constructed with `config.conformal_config.clone().map(ConformalPredictor::new)` at :4882 (crossterm ctor), :5025 (event-source ctor), :11317 (headless test ctor `headless_program_with_resolved_config` :11276); field `conformal_predictor: Option<ConformalPredictor>` :4745; predict path in `render_frame` :6196-6243 (`if let Some(predictor) = self.conformal_predictor.as_ref()` :6197, `predictor.predict(key, baseline_us, budget_us)` :6213, tracing with `fallback_level` :6220/:6234, `conformal_prediction = Some(prediction)` :6243); observe path :6400-6408 (`self.conformal_predictor.as_mut()` with `conformal_prediction.as_ref()`, diff strategy from `self.writer.last_diff_strategy()`); `budget_decision` JSONL :4150 carries `bucket_key, n_b, alpha, q_b, y_hat, upper_us, risk, fallback_level, window_size, reset_count` (fallback_level derived at :4144); default-config test asserts `config.conformal_config.is_none()` :7483; a test builds `with_conformal_config(ConformalConfig { alpha: 0.2, .. })` :9714-9719.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/conformal_predictor.rs`: `ConformalConfig` :21 with `min_samples: usize` :28 (default 20 at :43; `alpha` field present); `BucketKey` :52 (`from_context` :60), `ModeBucket` :76, `DiffBucket` :102; `ConformalPrediction` :142 (`to_jsonl` :170), `ConformalUpdate` :190; `ConformalPredictor` :215 (`new` :223, `config` :232, `bucket_samples(key)` :237, `reset_all` :245, `reset_bucket` :251, `observe(key, y_hat_us, observed_us)` :259, `predict(key, y_hat_us, budget_us)` :280; fallback chain exact -> mode_diff -> mode_only when `len() >= min_samples` :330-343).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/conformal_stages.rs`: `pub struct StagedConformalPredictor { config: StagedConfig, states: [StageState; 3] }` :265; `rg StagedConformalPredictor` outside the file: nothing.
- `crates/ftui-harness/src/main.rs:1923-1929`: `FTUI_HARNESS_CONFORMAL` env toggles `with_conformal_config(ConformalConfig::default())` / `without_conformal()`.
- Load governor default `enabled: true` at `program.rs:2344`; `render_budget_from_program_config` :3329-3336 attaches the `BudgetController` when enabled. So the PID/e-process half of the README cascade is on; the conformal guard half is off.
- `tests/baseline.json` row `frame_render`: criterion `pipeline/truecolor/diff_and_present/full/80x24@5%`, `bench_file: presenter_bench`, `crate: ftui-render`, `p99_ns: 2000000`, `threshold_pct: 10`, `_updated: 2026-07-20`. That bench is in ftui-render and does not include the runtime predictor; the runtime cost needs its own row (see `g11-tests`).
- The showcase builds `ProgramConfig` at `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/main.rs:65-71, :110-115, :166-170` with `..ProgramConfig::default()` and never touches `conformal_config`.

## Target state

`ProgramConfig::default()` has `conformal_config: Some(ConformalConfig::default_with_warmup(30))` where `default_with_warmup(n)` sets `min_samples = n` (no gating until 30 observations per bucket, up from 20); headless and simulator constructors force `None`; `with_conformal(Option<ConformalConfig>)` is the single builder (replacing the pair `with_conformal_config`/`without_conformal` per the no-shim rule: callers are updated); the showcase runs with the default; `budget_decision` lines in the showcase E2E JSONL show a `fallback_level` distribution; the per-frame cost is measured and within the baseline threshold; `conformal_stages` stays experimental with a follow-up trigger.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Unit test `conformal_default_on_with_warmup` (`program.rs`): with a headless program explicitly configured with the default (since headless forces `None`, the test passes `ProgramConfig::default().conformal_config.clone()` back through `with_conformal`), the first 30 frames never produce `fallback_level >= 1`; a synthetic series of frames at 3x budget after warm-up triggers `fallback_level >= 1`; frames back under budget recover to 0 within the predictor's window.
- [ ] `budget_decision` lines present in the showcase E2E JSONL with `fallback_level` distribution logged by `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh` (`jsonl_assert` detail `fallback_levels=0:N,1:M,...`).
- [ ] New bench row `runtime_render_frame_headless_80x24` (criterion in `crates/ftui-runtime/benches`) with and without the predictor; the delta is under 5% of p50 and the row's p99 is committed to `tests/baseline.json`.
- [ ] `conformal_stages` listed in README "Experimental modules" with the follow-up condition ("wired when per-stage timings in `budget_decision` show one stage dominating").

## Implementation plan (child beads)

1. `g11-impl`: defaults, warm-up constructor, builder consolidation, headless/simulator exemption, showcase unchanged (inherits default), per-stage timing fields in `budget_decision` as the trigger data for stages.
2. `g11-tests`: warm-up/degrade/recover test, bench row, E2E assertion.
3. `g11-docs`: README "Degradation Cascade" and "Mondrian" sections, experimental note for stages, ledger rows.

## Dependencies and ordering

- `g11-impl` blocked by `g25-impl` (baseline row conventions and the perf gate that enforces it) and `g20-impl` (evidence event fields for `budget_decision` are owned by G20's registry; the added `stage_*_us` fields must be registered there).
- Unblocks: `g06-impl` ledger rows V13/V14/V37; `g13-impl-ladder` (the merged ladder must keep honoring `fallback_level`).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Warm-up of 30 per bucket, not 20: buckets are keyed by (mode, diff, size) and a fresh app sees several sizes early; 30 keeps false degradations away during the first second at 60 fps while the fallback chain still provides coverage from coarser buckets (`conformal_predictor.rs:330-343`).
- Headless off by default: the simulator and headless tests must be deterministic and independent of wall-clock frame times; a predictor there would make snapshot tests timing-dependent. Tests that want it pass the config explicitly.
- Alternative rejected: enabling only in the showcase. The README claim is about the framework's default behavior, and consumers never enable optional intelligence (Section 2.3 item 4).
- Risk: a consumer on a slow CI runner sees degradation on the first slow frames after warm-up; that is the designed behavior and `with_conformal(None)` is the documented opt-out; `FTUI_CONFORMAL=0` env override is added for operators.
- `conformal_stages` stays out: wiring three monitors without evidence that stages diverge would be speculative; the trigger data (per-stage timings) is added now so the decision can be made from logs.

## Definition of done

Child beads closed; default on with warm-up; tests, bench row, E2E assertion, and docs in place; close reason lists the test names, the bench numbers, and the E2E JSONL fallback distribution observed.

title: task(G11): Conformal on by default with 30-sample warm-up, with_conformal builder, headless_default, env off
description:
## Context and why this matters

The README (README.md:994-1004 Mondrian gating; :1388-1410 Degradation Cascade) describes conformal frame-time risk gating as how FrankenTUI decides to shed fidelity before a frame overruns. The code is wired (`program.rs:6196-6243` predict, `:6400-6408` observe) but off: `ProgramConfig::default()` sets `conformal_config: None` (`program.rs:3008`). This bead flips the default with a warm-up, keeps deterministic constructors off, consolidates the builder API, adds an operator env override, and records per-stage timings in `budget_decision` so the multi-stage question (V14) can later be decided from evidence. Serves V13, V37, Section 2.2.B "off by default" list.

## Current state (evidence)

- `program.rs`: field :2940; default :3008; `with_conformal_config` :3143; `without_conformal` :3151; predictor created at :4882, :5025, :11317; predict block :6196-6243 uses `key` from `BucketKey::from_context` (`conformal_predictor.rs:60`), `baseline_us` = `self.last_frame_time_us` (field :4747 area), `budget_us` from the render budget; observe block :6400-6408 uses `self.writer.last_diff_strategy().unwrap_or(DiffStrategy::Full)`; `budget_decision` JSONL :4150 (fields listed in the epic; `fallback_level` computed at :4144 via `Self::opt_u8(conformal.map(|c| c.fallback_level))`); tests :7483 (`is_none()` on default) and :9714 (alpha 0.2 round trip).
- `conformal_predictor.rs`: `ConformalConfig` :21, `min_samples` :28 default 20 :43, `alpha`; `ConformalPredictor::predict` :280 falls through buckets when `len() < min_samples` :330-343; `ConformalPrediction` :142 has `fallback_level` (u8) and `to_jsonl` :170.
- `render_frame` :6113 already measures `render_elapsed` and `present_elapsed` (used at :6398 `frame_time = render_elapsed.saturating_add(present_elapsed)`) and `total_us`/`present_us` for `FrameTiming` (:6391-6396); a layout/view timing is not separated from render today (view and layout happen inside `model.view`).
- `crates/ftui-harness/src/main.rs:1923-1929` env `FTUI_HARNESS_CONFORMAL`; `crates/ftui-runtime/src/simulator.rs` wraps the headless constructor (verify how `ProgramSimulator` builds its config; it must end with `None`).
- No `FTUI_CONFORMAL` env override exists (`rg -n 'FTUI_CONFORMAL' crates` empty except the harness variable).

## Target state

`ConformalConfig::default_with_warmup(min_samples: usize) -> Self`; `ProgramConfig::default().conformal_config == Some(ConformalConfig::default_with_warmup(30))`; `ProgramConfig::with_conformal(self, Option<ConformalConfig>) -> Self` is the only builder (the two old builders are removed and their callers updated: harness `main.rs:1925-1927`, tests at `:9714`); `headless_program_with_resolved_config` (:11276) and `ProgramSimulator` force `conformal_config = None` unless the caller passes `ProgramConfig::with_conformal(Some(..))` explicitly through a new `keep_conformal_in_headless: bool` flag (default false) — or, simpler and chosen here: headless constructors respect the config as given but `ProgramConfig::headless_default()` returns the default with `None`, and all headless/simulator code paths use it; env `FTUI_CONFORMAL=0` forces `None` at construction for interactive constructors (read once in `Program::with_config`/`with_native_backend`/`with_event_source`); `budget_decision` gains `stage_view_us`, `stage_diff_us`, `stage_present_us` (view = time inside `model.view`; diff = `TerminalWriter` diff time if exposed, else 0 with a note; present = `present_elapsed`).

## Implementation plan

1. `conformal_predictor.rs`: add `pub fn default_with_warmup(min_samples: usize) -> Self { Self { min_samples, ..Self::default() } }` with docs explaining warm-up = no gating for a bucket until it has `min_samples` observations and the fallback chain covers it meanwhile.
2. `program.rs` defaults block (:3006-3013): `conformal_config: Some(ConformalConfig::default_with_warmup(30))`; add `pub fn headless_default() -> Self { Self { conformal_config: None, ..Self::default() } }` on `ProgramConfig`; replace `with_conformal_config`/`without_conformal` (:3143-:3155) with `pub fn with_conformal(mut self, config: Option<ConformalConfig>) -> Self`; update the test at :7483 to assert `is_some()` and `min_samples == 30`, and :9714 to use `with_conformal(Some(..))`.
3. Headless/simulator: `headless_program_with_resolved_config` (:11276) and every test helper that builds `ProgramConfig::default()` for headless runs switch to `ProgramConfig::headless_default()` (search `ProgramConfig::default()` inside `#[cfg(test)]` in `program.rs` and `simulator.rs`; hand-edit each; parallel subagents allowed, no scripts). The simulator's public constructor documents that conformal is off.
4. Env override: in the interactive constructors (`with_config` region :4840-4940, `with_event_source` :4983-5073, `with_native_backend` :5140), before `config.conformal_config.clone().map(ConformalPredictor::new)`, apply `if std::env::var("FTUI_CONFORMAL").as_deref() == Ok("0") { config.conformal_config = None; }` through one private `fn apply_conformal_env(config: &mut ProgramConfig)`; document in the `ProgramConfig` docs alongside other `FTUI_*` variables.
5. Per-stage timings: in `render_frame`, wrap `model.view(&mut frame)` with an `Instant` pair to get `view_us`; obtain diff time from `TerminalWriter` (add `last_diff_elapsed() -> Option<Duration>` to `terminal_writer.rs` next to `last_diff_strategy()`; it records the duration around the diff computation in the present path); add the three fields to the `budget_decision` struct and JSONL at :4150 (`"stage_view_us":{:.3},"stage_diff_us":{:.3},"stage_present_us":{:.3}`); register with `g20-impl`.
6. Harness `main.rs:1923-1929`: use `with_conformal(Some(ConformalConfig::default()))` / `with_conformal(None)`.
7. Showcase: no change needed (inherits the default); verify `main.rs:65-170` does not set `conformal_config`.
8. Gates: `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt`, `cargo test -p ftui-runtime --lib`, `cargo test -p ftui-harness`, `ubs`.

What NOT to do: no keeping `with_conformal_config` as a deprecated alias (no shims); no enabling in headless by default; no wiring of `conformal_stages` (experimental via `g07-impl`).

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/conformal_predictor.rs`: `default_with_warmup`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: default, `headless_default`, `with_conformal`, env override, stage timings, tests updated.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`: `last_diff_elapsed`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `ProgramConfig::headless_default().conformal_config.is_none()`; `ProgramSimulator` runs have no `bucket_key` in `budget_decision` lines (test `simulator_has_no_conformal_predictor`).
- [ ] `FTUI_CONFORMAL=0` yields `conformal_predictor.is_none()` in an interactive-constructor test that uses the event-source constructor with a headless event source and a `Vec<u8>` writer (pattern at `program.rs:10855-10871` where `TerminalWriter::new` is used in tests).
- [ ] `budget_decision` line contains `stage_view_us`, `stage_diff_us`, `stage_present_us` (test extends `:10247`-style JSONL assertions).
- [ ] `rg -n 'with_conformal_config|without_conformal' crates` is empty.

## Tests and logging

- Unit: the four tests above plus `conformal_default_on_with_warmup` (in `g11-tests`).
- Logging: `budget_decision` gains the three stage fields; tracing at :6220/:6234 unchanged (target should use `telemetry_schema` constants per G20).

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: `g25-impl` (baseline row conventions/perf gate), `g20-impl` (event field registry). If G20/G25 land later, this bead may merge first with the fields documented in its close reason for G20 to register; the dependency exists so `g42-impl` verification sees a consistent registry.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- `headless_default()` versus a flag: a distinct constructor is explicit at every headless call site and greps cleanly; a hidden flag inside `ProgramConfig::default()` would surprise consumers.

title: task(G11): Warm-up/degrade/recover headless test, coverage proptest, render_frame bench row, E2E histogram
description:
## Context

Companion test bead for `g11-impl`. The block claims behavior (no gating during warm-up; degradation on sustained overrun; recovery), cost (one quantile lookup per frame), and observability (`fallback_level` in the showcase evidence). Proofs: a headless test that drives synthetic frame times through the real `render_frame` path, a runtime bench row with the predictor on and off, and an E2E assertion over the showcase JSONL.

## What to test

1. Warm-up: 30 frames at any duration produce `fallback_level == 0` and `risk == false` in every `budget_decision` line.
2. Degrade: after warm-up, a run of frames at 3x budget yields `fallback_level >= 1` (and the degradation level rises through `BudgetController` per `budget.rs:530-596`).
3. Recover: frames back under budget return `fallback_level` to 0 within the predictor window and the degradation level returns toward `Full`.
4. Headless/simulator: no predictor.
5. Cost: p50 delta of a headless 80x24 frame with predictor on vs off is under 5%.
6. Evidence: `fallback_level` distribution in the showcase run.

## Test types (unit, property, bench, E2E) with names and assertions

Unit / headless (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` tests; use `headless_program_with_resolved_config` :11276 with `ProgramConfig::headless_default().with_conformal(Some(ConformalConfig::default_with_warmup(30)))`; inject frame times through the existing test seam that sets `last_frame_time_us`/records frame time — if none exists, add `#[cfg(test)] fn inject_frame_time_for_tests(&mut self, us: f64)` that calls `self.budget.record_frame_time` and the conformal `observe` with the same values the production path would use):
- `conformal_default_on_with_warmup`: 30 frames at 3x budget -> all lines `fallback_level == 0`; next 10 frames at 3x -> at least one line `fallback_level >= 1` and `risk == true`; next 40 frames at 0.3x budget -> last line `fallback_level == 0`.
- `default_config_enables_conformal_with_warmup_30`.
- `simulator_has_no_conformal_predictor`.
- `env_ftui_conformal_zero_disables_predictor`.
- `budget_decision_has_stage_timing_fields` (parse with `serde_json`; assert the three keys are numbers >= 0).

Unit (`conformal_predictor.rs`): `default_with_warmup_sets_min_samples`, `predict_uses_fallback_bucket_until_warmup` (exact bucket has 29 samples, mode bucket has 40 -> prediction comes from the mode bucket; assert via `fallback_level == 2` or whatever the level numbering at `:330-343` yields; read the code for the exact mapping).

Property (`conformal_predictor.rs`, `proptest`): `proptest_coverage_at_least_one_minus_alpha_on_stationary_residuals` (Normal residuals, alpha 0.1, 2,000 observations after warm-up -> empirical coverage of `upper_us` over observed in [0.85, 0.97]).

Bench (`crates/ftui-runtime/benches/render_frame_bench.rs`, new criterion bench, `harness = false`; ftui-runtime benches today are `ivm_bench`, `pane_terminal_bench`, `telemetry_bench`, `tick_strategy_bench`): group `runtime/render_frame_headless_80x24` with variants `conformal_off` (`headless_default()`) and `conformal_on` (default with warm-up, pre-warmed by 40 frames before measurement) rendering a fixed dashboard-like model (Block + Table + Paragraph) each iteration; baseline row `tests/baseline.json`:
```
"runtime_render_frame_headless_80x24": {
  "description": "Headless render_frame (view + diff + budget + conformal) at 80x24",
  "criterion_name": "runtime/render_frame_headless_80x24/conformal_on",
  "bench_file": "render_frame_bench", "crate": "ftui-runtime",
  "slo_metric": "runtime_render_frame_p99_us",
  "p50_ns": <measured>, "p95_ns": <measured>, "p99_ns": <measured>, "p999_ns": <measured>,
  "threshold_pct": 10
}
```
and a note in `docs/perf/conformal_default_2026-09.md` with both variants' p50 and the delta (must be < 5%).

E2E (`scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh`, the evidence step at `:2364`): after the run, python one-liner over the evidence file computes the histogram of `fallback_level` across `budget_decision` lines and asserts at least 60 lines exist (3.2 s at 60 Hz minus warm-up) and that every line parses; `jsonl_assert "conformal_fallback_distribution" pass "fallback_levels=0:N,1:M,2:K"`; a second assertion `conformal_warmup_no_risk_first_30` checks the first 30 `budget_decision` lines have `risk == false`.

## Logging (structured JSONL fields, tracing targets)

- Evidence `budget_decision` fields already present: `frame_idx, decision, degradation_before, degradation_after, frame_time_us, budget_us, pid_*, e_value, in_warmup, bucket_key, n_b, alpha, q_b, y_hat, upper_us, risk, fallback_level`; new: `stage_view_us, stage_diff_us, stage_present_us`.
- Headless tests print the evidence file on failure.
- Bench artifact under `target/criterion/runtime/`; perf record `docs/perf/conformal_default_2026-09.md`.
- E2E JSONL `assert` rows named above with the histogram in `detail`.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` tests; `crates/ftui-runtime/src/conformal_predictor.rs` tests + proptest (add `proptest` dev-dep if missing); `crates/ftui-runtime/benches/render_frame_bench.rs` (new) + `Cargo.toml` `[[bench]]`; `tests/baseline.json`; `docs/perf/conformal_default_2026-09.md`; `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] All named tests pass (`rch exec -- cargo test -p ftui-runtime`).
- [ ] Bench delta `conformal_on` vs `conformal_off` p50 < 5%; row committed; perf record committed.
- [ ] Showcase E2E run shows the two new assertions passing; the histogram is in the close reason.
