## Context and why this matters

Three README sections describe conformal gating: "### Mondrian Conformal Frame-Time Risk Gating" (README.md:994-1004), "## Degradation Cascade" (README.md:1388-1410, which also lists the wrong level names "Full → SimpleBorders → NoColors → TextOnly"; the real `DegradationLevel` at `crates/ftui-render/src/budget.rs:800-816` is `Full, SimpleBorders, NoStyling, EssentialOnly, Skeleton, SkipFrame`, a G06 DOC row), and "## Multi-Stage Conformal Monitoring" (README.md:2630-2645). After `g11-impl` the first two are true by default with stated preconditions and the third is experimental. This bead makes the text match, adds the opt-out and env override, and records the ledger rows (V13, V14, V37).

## Current state (evidence)

- README.md:994-1004: formula and bucket fallback chain (accurate to `conformal_predictor.rs:330-343`); no mention of defaults, warm-up, or how to disable.
- README.md:1388-1410: cascade diagram with "Conformal Frame Guard" (the real component is `ConformalPredictor` in `program.rs`; `conformal_frame_guard.rs` is a quarantined module) and wrong level names.
- README.md:2630-2645: multi-stage monitors described as existing ("Individual render pipeline stages have independent conformal monitors").
- After `g11-impl`: default `Some(ConformalConfig::default_with_warmup(30))`, `ProgramConfig::with_conformal(Option<..>)`, `ProgramConfig::headless_default()`, `FTUI_CONFORMAL=0`, `budget_decision` stage fields.

## Target state

- Mondrian section: adds "Defaults: on since 0.7 with a 30-observation warm-up per bucket; disable with `ProgramConfig::default().with_conformal(None)` or `FTUI_CONFORMAL=0`; headless/simulator constructors are off for determinism; every decision is a `budget_decision` evidence line with `bucket_key, n_b, q_b, upper_us, risk, fallback_level`".
- Degradation Cascade section: diagram names `ConformalPredictor` (predictive) and `BudgetController` (PID + e-process, reactive) as the two gates, level list corrected to the six real levels, note that `conformal_frame_guard`/`degradation_cascade` modules are experimental/merged (G13).
- Multi-Stage section: badge "**Status: experimental**", one sentence that the per-stage timings are now recorded in `budget_decision` (`stage_view_us`, `stage_diff_us`, `stage_present_us`) and that stage monitors will be wired when the recorded data shows a dominating stage; link to "Experimental modules".
- Ledger rows: V13 CODE (proof: `conformal_default_on_with_warmup`, baseline `runtime_render_frame_headless_80x24`, E2E `conformal_fallback_distribution`); V14 experimental (proof: the badge and `g07-impl` gating); V37 DOC (level names).

## Implementation plan

1. Edit README.md:994-1004 (append the defaults paragraph and a `rust,no_run` snippet: `let cfg = ProgramConfig::default().with_conformal(None);`).
2. Edit README.md:1388-1410 (diagram labels, level names, module note).
3. Edit README.md:2630-2645 (badge + trigger sentence).
4. Ledger rows in `docs/claims-ledger.md` if present; otherwise in the close reason and a comment on `g06-impl`.
5. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` rustdoc for `ProgramConfig` lists `FTUI_CONFORMAL` with the other env variables.

## Files to change

- `README.md`: three sections.
- `docs/claims-ledger.md` (if present).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: rustdoc only.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `rg -n 'with_conformal\(None\)|FTUI_CONFORMAL' README.md` hits.
- [ ] `rg -n 'NoColors|TextOnly' README.md` is empty after the edit.
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui --doc` green (G02) for the added snippet.
- [ ] Ledger rows recorded.

## Tests and logging

- Doc-only; the `rg` checks above and rustdoc.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: `g11-impl`; numbers from `g11-tests`.
- Unblocks: `g06-impl` ledger rows.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- The Degradation Cascade section overlaps G06 (level names) and G13 (module merge); this bead fixes the names and the module note so the section is consistent once; G06's ledger row points here.

## Definition of done

Sections updated; ledger rows recorded; close reason lists README line ranges touched.

Commit 5eb8c6e4. Degradation Cascade / Multi-Stage sections not audited here.

title: epic(G12): BOCPD default resize regime detector with heuristic fallback, proven by a differential replay
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:885-913 "### BOCPD: Online Change-Point Detection" states: "Resize coalescing uses **Bayesian Online Change-Point Detection** to detect regime transitions: Steady: x_t ~ Exponential(λ_steady) where μ_steady ≈ 200ms; Burst: ... μ_burst ≈ 20ms ... Hazard function H(r) = 1/λ_hazard where λ_hazard = 50 ... K=100 run-length truncation ... p_burst > 0.7 → Burst regime, p_burst < 0.3 → Steady regime". README.md:1831 and :1578-1597 repeat that BOCPD is how resize regimes are detected. Vision row V10 is OPT-IN: `CoalescerConfig::default().enable_bocpd = false` (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/resize_coalescer.rs:202`), so every consumer and the showcase (unless `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL` is set) run a 10/5 events-per-second heuristic. The README also states coalescing delays of 200/20 ms while the code uses 16/40 ms (V36; the 200/20 are BOCPD observation means, not delays). Open bead bd-1za0z lists resize-coalescer telemetry defects that were partly fixed on 2026-08-22 and partly left as product decisions.

This epic makes BOCPD the default regime detector with the heuristic as a defined fallback, closes the telemetry defects enumerated in bd-1za0z (so that bead can be closed with a reference), tags every decision with the detector that made it, proves parity-or-better with a differential replay of recorded resize storms, and corrects the README numbers. Serves V10, V36, V51 and Section 2.2.B "off by default".

## Current state (evidence)

- `resize_coalescer.rs` (156 KB, mtime 2026-08-22): `CoalescerConfig` `Default` :192-205 (`steady_delay_ms: 16`, `burst_delay_ms: 40`, `hard_deadline_ms: 100`, `burst_enter_rate: 10.0`, `burst_exit_rate: 5.0`, `cooldown_frames: 3`, `rate_window_size: 8`, `enable_logging: false`, `enable_bocpd: false` :202, `bocpd_config: None`); two `with_bocpd`-style setters set `enable_bocpd = true` at :219 and :227; config JSONL :244 (no `enable_bocpd` field); `CoalesceAction` :258-275 (`None`, `ShowPlaceholder` :264, `ApplyResize { width, height, coalesce_time, forced_by_deadline }` :273); `Regime` :278; `TransitionReasonCode` :300-318 (`HeuristicEnterBurstRate`, `HeuristicExitBurstCooldown`, `BocpdPosteriorBurst`, ...); `DecisionEvidence` docs :367-380 and `decision_evidence` JSONL :473-480 (fields `log_bayes_factor, regime_contribution, timing_contribution, rate_contribution, explanation`); `RegimeTransitionLog::to_jsonl` :605-624 (`from_regime, to_regime, reason_code, confidence, event_rate, p_burst, cooldown_remaining`); `ResizeCoalescer::new` :725-757 builds `BocpdDetector` only if `enable_bocpd` :725-732 and initializes `regime: Regime::Steady` :742; `handle_resize` returns `ShowPlaceholder` at :943; `tick_at` :955-975 runs the heuristic cooldown exit only when `self.bocpd.is_none()` :961 (comment cites bd-1za0z); apply path :1300-1318 sets `forced_by_deadline: forced`; `current_delay_ms` :1322-1330 uses `bocpd.recommended_delay(steady, burst)`; BOCPD-to-regime mapping :1346-1392. Tests `isolated_resize_after_quiet_gap_is_not_forced` :2118 and `resize_arriving_while_pending_past_deadline_stays_forced` :2142 exist.
- `bocpd.rs`: `BocpdConfig` :198 with defaults :250-258 (`mu_steady_ms: 200.0`, `mu_burst_ms: 20.0`, `hazard_lambda: 50.0`, `max_run_length: 100`, `steady_threshold: 0.3`, `burst_threshold: 0.7`, `burst_prior: 0.2`, `min_observation_ms: 1.0`, `max_observation_ms: 10000.0`) matching the README; `BocpdDetector` :469 (`new` :500, `p_burst` :567, `regime` :582, `observe_event(now)` :697, `observation_count` :684, `recommended_delay` :909).
- `program.rs`: `ProgramConfig.resize_coalescer: CoalescerConfig` :2948 default :3012, `resize_behavior: ResizeBehavior::Throttled` :3013; `with_resize_coalescer` :3185; coalescer built :4886/:5029 with evidence sink :4889/:5032; `handle_resize` call at :5728-5730 matches only `ApplyResize` (so `ShowPlaceholder` is produced but never consumed); `tick` :6702-6724; test at :7486 asserts `!config.resize_coalescer.enable_bocpd`.
- Showcase: `main.rs:219-229` enables `with_logging(true).with_bocpd()` only when `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL` is set; `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh:2364` runs a `stty` resize storm with the sink on.
- bd-1za0z (open, P3, created 2026-07-08, updated 2026-08-22) comment trail: forced_by_deadline quiet-gap and heuristic-cooldown-in-BOCPD-mode FIXED (third pass, tests above); "Immediate-mode stats().regime pins Burst" verified stale (constructor initializes Steady); `ShowPlaceholder` "remains produced-but-unconsumed ... product decision, left as-is"; remaining open: ShowPlaceholder consumer, batch-evidence stamping semantics, capacity-vs-usage sensor (guardrails, item 1), queue_depth wiring (item 3, owned by G20).
- Differential tooling: `tests/e2e/lib/resize_storm_differential.py` compares labelled JSONL traces (`--trace LABEL=PATH` repeated, `--baseline`, `--known` TSV, `--report` JSON, `--mode warn|strict`); `crates/ftui-harness/src/resize_storm.rs` has `StormPattern` :53 (`Burst{count}`, `Sweep{..}`, `Oscillate{..}`, ...), `StormConfig` :132, `ResizeStorm` :325, `RecordedStorm` :821, `get_storm_seed` :914, `analyze_storm_output` :940.

## Target state

BOCPD is the default detector (`enable_bocpd: true`) with `heuristic_fallback: true` used whenever the posterior is undefined (no observations yet, or an inter-arrival outside `[min_observation_ms, max_observation_ms]`); the four bd-1za0z coalescer items are closed in code with regression tests; `decision_evidence` and `regime_transition` lines carry `detector: "bocpd"|"heuristic"`; the differential replay shows BOCPD renders no more frames during a drag than the heuristic and applies the final size within 40 ms of the last event, archived under `docs/perf/`; README states the real delays (16/40 ms) and the BOCPD observation means (200/20 ms); bd-1za0z is closed with a reference to `g12-impl-telemetry` (items 1-2 as enumerated by the plan) and `g20-impl` (item 3).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `tests/e2e/lib/resize_storm_differential.py` run over traces produced from `resize_storm.rs` patterns: `frames_during_drag(bocpd) <= frames_during_drag(heuristic)` for every pattern and `final_apply_latency_ms(bocpd) <= 40` for Burst/Sweep/Oscillate; report archived as `docs/perf/resize_differential_2026-09.md` (+ JSON).
- [ ] Unit tests for each bd-1za0z item (`g12-impl-telemetry`): quiet-gap resize not forced; no contradictory `regime_transition` pairs in BOCPD mode; Immediate mode reports `Steady`; `ShowPlaceholder` consumed or removed.
- [ ] `decision_evidence` lines carry `detector`; test `config_default_enables_bocpd_with_heuristic_fallback` replaces the assertion at `program.rs:7486`.
- [ ] README BOCPD sections state defaults and delays.

## Implementation plan (child beads)

1. `g12-impl-telemetry` (bug): close the bd-1za0z coalescer items with regression tests; record the product decisions.
2. `g12-impl`: flip the default, add `heuristic_fallback`, tag evidence with `detector`.
3. `g12-tests`: unit + property tests for the fallback and the tags.
4. `g12-e2e`: differential harness + PTY storm assertions + archived report.
5. `g12-docs`: README numbers and ledger rows.

## Dependencies and ordering

- `g12-impl` blocked by `g12-impl-telemetry` (the telemetry must be trustworthy before the differential is run).
- No external block dependencies; day-one track per Section 7.5.
- Unblocks: `g06-impl` ledger rows V10/V36; bd-1za0z closure.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Heuristic as fallback rather than removal: BOCPD needs at least one inter-arrival observation; the heuristic gives a sane answer on the very first resize and when observations are clamped.
- "Flip back if it loses": the differential is the gate; if BOCPD renders more frames or lands the final size later, the default stays off and the README says so (recorded in `docs/perf`).
- The 200/20 vs 16/40 confusion is a doc bug, not a code bug; both numbers are real and the README must name them correctly.
- Risk: consumers with custom `BocpdConfig` and `enable_bocpd: false` explicitly are unaffected (explicit config wins).

## Definition of done

Child beads closed; default on; bd-1za0z closed with references; differential report archived; README truthful; close reason cites the report path and the differential numbers.

title: bug(G12): Close bd-1za0z coalescer items: quiet-gap forced flag, cooldown exit, Immediate regime, placeholder
description:
## Context and why this matters

Before BOCPD can be made the default detector (`g12-impl`) and proven by a differential replay (`g12-e2e`), the resize coalescer's telemetry must be trustworthy: open bead bd-1za0z ("Guardrails + resize-coalescer telemetry/design gaps", P3, created 2026-07-08) lists four resize-coalescer defects: (a) `forced_by_deadline` inflation for isolated resizes after a quiet gap, (b) the heuristic cooldown exit running in BOCPD mode and emitting contradictory `regime_transition` pairs, (c) Immediate-mode `stats().regime` pinned to Burst, (d) `ShowPlaceholder` produced but never consumed. The reality-check plan (G12) says this bead "closes bd-1za0z items (1)-(2)" in the plan's numbering (the coalescer telemetry defects); bd-1za0z item (3) (queue depth hardcoded 0) is owned by G20 (`g20-impl`), and its guardrail capacity-vs-usage sensor question is routed to `g13-impl-alloc`, which consumes the same `memory_bytes` series. After this bead lands, bd-1za0z is to be closed with a reference to this bead and to `g20-impl`/`g13-impl-alloc` for the routed items.

This is a `bug` bead: it verifies what the bead's own comment trail says was already fixed on 2026-08-22, pins those fixes with tests, fixes what remains, and records the product decisions so the close reason of bd-1za0z is explicit.

## Current state (evidence)

- (a) `forced_by_deadline`: `resize_coalescer.rs:1300-1318` apply path sets `forced_by_deadline: forced`; tests `isolated_resize_after_quiet_gap_is_not_forced` :2118 and `resize_arriving_while_pending_past_deadline_stays_forced` :2142 exist (bd-1za0z third pass, 2026-08-22). Status: fixed in tree; needs no code change, only inclusion in this bead's verification list.
- (b) heuristic cooldown exit: `tick_at` :955-975 gates the rate-based exit with `if self.regime == Regime::Burst && self.bocpd.is_none()` :961 with a comment citing bd-1za0z. Status: fixed; no dedicated test asserts "no `HeuristicExitBurstCooldown` transition ever appears in BOCPD mode"; add one.
- (c) Immediate-mode regime: `ResizeCoalescer::new` :742 initializes `regime: Regime::Steady`; bd-1za0z comment says the pinning "no longer reproduces". Status: stale; add a regression test that `ResizeBehavior::Immediate` (see `program.rs:563` `ResizeBehavior::Throttled` and the enum near it) leaves `stats().regime == Steady` after events.
- (d) `ShowPlaceholder`: produced at `resize_coalescer.rs:943` (end of `handle_resize` when coalescing), consumed nowhere: `program.rs:5728-5730` matches only `CoalesceAction::ApplyResize`; tests reference the variant at :2055, :3825 (`CoalesceAction::None | CoalesceAction::ShowPlaceholder =>`), :4457-4460. bd-1za0z: "whether throttled resizes should render a placeholder frame is a product decision, left as-is rather than deleted".
- Also in bd-1za0z (2): "batch evidence export stamps historical rows with CURRENT last_applied vs decision-time size" with a note that the current shape has a defensible reading and changing it risks golden evidence fixtures.
- `regime_transition` JSONL :605-624 has `reason_code` (so a contradictory pair is detectable as `HeuristicExitBurstCooldown` following `BocpdPosteriorBurst` without an intervening event).

## Target state

- (a) and (b): verified and pinned: the two existing tests are listed in this bead's close reason; a new test `bocpd_mode_never_emits_heuristic_cooldown_exit` drives 200 events at burst rate then 100 ticks with no events under `enable_bocpd: true` and asserts no `regime_transition` with `reason_code == "heuristic_exit_burst_cooldown"` was logged and that consecutive transitions alternate `from_regime`/`to_regime` (no `Burst -> Burst`).
- (c): `immediate_mode_regime_stays_steady` (regression).
- (d): decision: REMOVE the `ShowPlaceholder` variant. Rationale for the default: the runtime has never rendered a placeholder, the README does not promise one, and a never-consumed variant is exactly the kind of dead surface G07 targets; `handle_resize` returns `CoalesceAction::None` while coalescing. The owner can override in this bead's comments before implementation ("consume" = render the last frame with `DegradationLevel::Skeleton` at the pending size); if overridden, implement the consumer in `program.rs:5728` and keep the variant.
- Batch-evidence stamping: keep the current shape (decision-time `applied_w/h` are already on the rows); document the semantics in the `to_jsonl` doc comment so the "defect" is closed as by-design.
- bd-1za0z closure text drafted in this bead's close reason: "items (1) capacity-vs-usage -> g13-impl-alloc; (2) resize telemetry -> this bead (quiet-gap fixed 2026-08-22 + pinned; cooldown-exit fixed 2026-08-22 + pinned; Immediate pinning stale + regression test; ShowPlaceholder removed/consumed per decision; batch stamping documented by-design); (3) queue depth -> g20-impl".

## Implementation plan

1. Read `resize_coalescer.rs:900-1000` and `:1290-1400` to confirm the current control flow around `ShowPlaceholder` and the apply path.
2. Add the two tests (b) and (c) in the `#[cfg(test)]` module of `resize_coalescer.rs` using the `_at` time-injection variants (`tick_at` :955; `handle_resize_at` if present, else add it mirroring `tick_at`; time injection is required for deterministic rate computation).
3. Remove `CoalesceAction::ShowPlaceholder` (:264) and its production site (:943 returns `None`); update tests :2055, :3825, :4457-4460; update the `program.rs` match at :5728 if it names the variant (it does not today). If the owner chose "consume", implement instead: `program.rs` Throttled branch sets `self.pending_resize_placeholder = Some((w, h))` and `render_frame` draws the last buffer with `frame.degradation = DegradationLevel::Skeleton` until `ApplyResize` arrives.
4. Doc comment on the batch export function (`export`/`to_jsonl` for logs; find with `rg -n 'fn export|last_applied' resize_coalescer.rs`) stating the stamping semantics.
5. Gates: `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt`, `cargo test -p ftui-runtime resize_coalescer`, `ubs`.
6. Close-reason text for bd-1za0z prepared (the orchestrator/owner closes bd-1za0z; `br close bd-1za0z --reason "..."` referencing this bead's id).

What NOT to do: no change to delays/thresholds (that is `g12-impl`); no new evidence fields (`detector` is `g12-impl`); no deletion of files.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/resize_coalescer.rs`: two tests, `ShowPlaceholder` removal (or consumer), doc comment.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: only on the "consume" path.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `isolated_resize_after_quiet_gap_is_not_forced`, `resize_arriving_while_pending_past_deadline_stays_forced`, `bocpd_mode_never_emits_heuristic_cooldown_exit`, `immediate_mode_regime_stays_steady` all pass.
- [ ] `rg -n ShowPlaceholder crates` is empty (removal path) or `program.rs` consumes it with a test `throttled_resize_renders_skeleton_placeholder_until_apply` (consume path).
- [ ] bd-1za0z closed by the owner with the reference text; this bead's close reason contains the same text.

## Tests and logging

- Unit: the four tests above; the transition test asserts on the coalescer's in-memory transition log (`regime_transition_count` :832 and the log entries) rather than parsing JSONL.
- Logging: no new fields; `regime_transition` and `decision_evidence` unchanged in shape.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: nothing.
- Unblocks: `g12-impl` (which flips the default and adds `detector`), closure of bd-1za0z.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Removing an enum variant is an API change for consumers matching on `CoalesceAction`; the project does not keep backward compatibility (AGENTS.md), and the variant never carried behavior.
- Alternative rejected: leaving `ShowPlaceholder` "for future use"; that is the pattern that produced 30 dead modules.

## Definition of done

Tests green; variant removed or consumed; doc comment added; bd-1za0z closure text recorded; gates and `ubs` clean.
close_reason: bd-1za0z coalescer items resolved and pinned (commit HEAD): (a) quiet-gap forced flag was already fixed 2026-08-22, pinned by isolated_resize_after_quiet_gap_is_not_forced and resize_arriving_while_pending_past_deadline_stays_forced; (b) heuristic cooldown exit gated to heuristic mode, pinned by bocpd_mode_never_emits_heuristic_cooldown_exit (200 burst events + 100 quiet ticks under BOCPD: no heuristic_exit_burst_cooldown, transitions chain); (c) Immediate-mode regime pinning DID still reproduce: the frame loop never ticks the coalescer in ResizeBehavior::Immediate and record_external_apply zeroed the cooldown, so one burst pinned regime=Burst; record_external_apply now exits Burst on the event path when the rate is below burst_exit_rate (new reason code heuristic_exit_burst_rate), pinned by immediate_mode_regime_is_not_pinned_to_burst; (d) ShowPlaceholder REMOVED (default decision, no owner override in comments): never consumed, handle_resize returns None while coalescing, harness chaos log derives coalesce from has_pending(); batch export stamping documented by-design on decision_logs_jsonl. 115 resize_coalescer tests green via rch. bd-1za0z closure text: items (1) capacity-vs-usage -> g13-impl-alloc (bd-g00-root-epic-ewths.17.x); (2) resize telemetry -> this bead; (3) queue depth -> g20-impl (bd-g00-root-epic-ewths.26.1, closed).

title: task(G12): Flip enable_bocpd default, add heuristic_fallback, tag evidence lines with detector
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:885-913 presents BOCPD as how resize coalescing detects regimes; the code defaults to a 10/5 events-per-second heuristic (`CoalescerConfig::default().enable_bocpd = false`, `resize_coalescer.rs:202`) and builds a `BocpdDetector` only when a caller opts in (`:725-732`). Only the showcase with `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL` set (`main.rs:225`) and the harness ever do. This bead makes BOCPD the default, defines the heuristic as the fallback for undefined posteriors, and tags every decision and transition with the detector that made it so the differential (`g12-e2e`) and the evidence consumers can tell them apart. Serves V10, V51.

## Current state (evidence)

- `resize_coalescer.rs`: `CoalescerConfig` fields incl. `cooldown_frames` :167, `enable_bocpd` :185/:202, `bocpd_config` :187; setters that enable BOCPD at :219 and :227; config JSONL :244-252 (fields `steady_delay_ms, burst_delay_ms, hard_deadline_ms, burst_enter_rate, burst_exit_rate, cooldown_frames, rate_window_size, logging_enabled`; no `enable_bocpd`); `TransitionReasonCode` :300-318; `DecisionEvidence` :367-430 with `regime_contrib = if regime == Regime::Burst { 1.0 } else { -0.5 }` :426; `decision_evidence` JSONL :473-480; `RegimeTransitionLog::to_jsonl` :605-624; `ResizeCoalescer` fields incl. `bocpd: Option<BocpdDetector>` :692, `cooldown_remaining` :653, `regime_transitions` :684; `new` :725-757; `tick_at` :955; `current_delay_ms` :1322-1330 (BOCPD `recommended_delay` else regime delay); posterior-to-regime mapping :1346-1392 (`BocpdRegime::Burst => Regime::Burst` :1346; reason codes `BocpdPosteriorBurst` :1355; cooldown arming :1388).
- `bocpd.rs`: `BocpdDetector::observe_event(now) -> BocpdRegime` :697; `p_burst` :567; `observation_count` :684; `min_observation_ms`/`max_observation_ms` in config (:250-258); `BocpdRegime` :310 (variants incl. a transitional state per README "otherwise → Transitional").
- `program.rs`: default `resize_coalescer: CoalescerConfig::default()` :3012; test :7486 `assert!(!config.resize_coalescer.enable_bocpd)`; harness `main.rs:1920` sets `config.resize_coalescer.bocpd_config = None` in one env branch (read `:1900-1922` for the flag name).
- Showcase `main.rs:225`: `.with_logging(true).with_bocpd()` when the evidence env is set.

## Target state

`CoalescerConfig::default()` has `enable_bocpd: true`, `heuristic_fallback: true` (new field), `bocpd_config: None` (meaning `BocpdConfig::default()`); `ResizeCoalescer::new` always builds the detector when enabled; a private `fn active_detector(&self, observation_ms: Option<f64>) -> Detector { Bocpd | Heuristic }` returns `Heuristic` when `bocpd.is_none()`, or when `heuristic_fallback && (bocpd.observation_count() == 0 || observation is outside [min_observation_ms, max_observation_ms] || !p_burst.is_finite())`; the regime update path uses the heuristic rate rule in that case and records transitions with the existing heuristic reason codes; `decision_evidence` JSONL gains `"detector":"bocpd"|"heuristic"` and `"p_burst":<f64|null>`; `regime_transition` gains `"detector"`; config JSONL gains `enable_bocpd` and `heuristic_fallback`; `ResizeStats` (`stats()` :6450 consumer) gains `detector_decisions: { bocpd: u64, heuristic: u64 }`; the showcase's `.with_bocpd()` call becomes redundant and is removed (the evidence sink toggle stays); harness env branch keeps working.

## Implementation plan

1. `CoalescerConfig`: add `pub heuristic_fallback: bool` after `enable_bocpd` with docs; `Default` sets `enable_bocpd: true`, `heuristic_fallback: true`; rename/keep the setters at :219/:227 (`with_bocpd()` stays as the explicit form; add `without_bocpd()`), no deprecated aliases.
2. `ResizeCoalescer`: add `detector_decisions: (u64, u64)` counters; implement `active_detector`; in the event path where BOCPD is consulted (:1346-1392) branch on it; in `tick_at` :961 keep `bocpd.is_none()` semantics but also treat "fallback active" as heuristic mode for the cooldown exit (so the fallback is a complete heuristic, not half of one); `current_delay_ms` :1322 uses the heuristic delay when the fallback is active.
3. Evidence: `DecisionEvidence` gets `detector: &'static str` and `p_burst: Option<f64>`; `to_jsonl` :473 appends the two fields; `RegimeTransitionLog::to_jsonl` :605 appends `detector`; config JSONL :244 appends `enable_bocpd`, `heuristic_fallback`. Register the new fields with `g20-impl` (evidence registry) and update `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json` only if it validates evidence events.
4. `program.rs:7486` test: assert `enable_bocpd && heuristic_fallback`; add `stats()` exposure of the counters into the `budget_decision`/resize stats path at :6450 if a field exists for resize stats (`resize_coalescing_active` is already in `budget_decision` :4150; add `resize_detector` string there).
5. Showcase `main.rs:225`: drop `.with_bocpd()`; harness `main.rs:1900-1929`: keep the env override semantics (an env that disables BOCPD must call `without_bocpd()`).
6. Gates: `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt`, `cargo test -p ftui-runtime`, `cargo test -p ftui-harness`, `cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase` (golden evidence fixtures: if any snapshot/golden compares `decision_evidence` lines, re-bless and review), `ubs`.

What NOT to do: no change to `BocpdConfig` defaults (they match the README); no change to delays 16/40; no silent downgrade to heuristic without the `detector` tag showing it.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/resize_coalescer.rs`: config field/default, fallback logic, counters, evidence fields.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: test :7486, `resize_detector` in `budget_decision`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `config_default_enables_bocpd_with_heuristic_fallback` (both flags true; `bocpd_config.is_none()`).
- [ ] `first_event_uses_heuristic_then_bocpd`: with defaults, the first `decision_evidence` line has `detector == "heuristic"`, the third has `"bocpd"`.
- [ ] `clamped_observation_falls_back_to_heuristic`: an inter-arrival of 20 s (> `max_observation_ms`) yields a heuristic-tagged decision.
- [ ] `explicit_disable_keeps_heuristic_only`: `without_bocpd()` yields only heuristic-tagged lines and no `BocpdDetector` (`bocpd.is_none()`).
- [ ] `rg -n '"detector"' crates/ftui-runtime/src/resize_coalescer.rs` shows both JSONL sites.

## Tests and logging

- Unit: the four tests above plus `stats_counts_detector_decisions`.
- Logging: `decision_evidence` (+`detector`, `p_burst`), `regime_transition` (+`detector`), `config` (+`enable_bocpd`, `heuristic_fallback`), `budget_decision` (+`resize_detector`); tracing target `ftui.decision.resize` (`telemetry_schema::TARGET_RESIZE` :44) debug per detector switch.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Unblocks: `g12-tests`, `g12-e2e`, `g12-docs`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative rejected: BOCPD-only with no fallback; the first resize of a session has no inter-arrival and must still coalesce sensibly.
- Alternative rejected: making the fallback silent; the differential and evidence consumers need to attribute decisions.
- Risk: golden evidence fixtures in the showcase or harness that string-compare `decision_evidence` lines will change shape; re-bless with review (bd-1za0z noted this risk for a different field).
- Rollback: `without_bocpd()` or `CoalescerConfig { enable_bocpd: false, .. }`.

## Definition of done

title: task(G12): Fallback-rule and detector-tag unit tests, regime-consistency proptests, README constant guard
description:
## Context

Companion test bead for `g12-impl` (BOCPD default + heuristic fallback + detector tags) and the regression tests pinned by `g12-impl-telemetry`. The README claims specific BOCPD behavior (thresholds 0.7/0.3, hazard 50, K=100, means 200/20 ms) and this block claims the default flip does not regress coalescing. Proofs: unit tests on the fallback rule and tags, property tests on regime consistency, and the differential replay (`g12-e2e`).

## What to test

1. Default configuration and fallback rule (first event, clamped observations, non-finite posterior, explicit disable).
2. Tagging: every `decision_evidence` and `regime_transition` line carries `detector`; the value matches the code path that produced it.
3. Regime consistency: transitions alternate; no heuristic-cooldown reason codes while BOCPD is active; `p_burst` is `null` exactly when the heuristic decided.
4. README constants: `BocpdConfig::default()` equals the README numbers (guard against drift).
5. Existing coalescer invariants still hold with BOCPD on (hard deadline 100 ms; steady 16 ms; burst 40 ms).

## Test types (unit, property, bench, E2E) with names and assertions

Unit (`resize_coalescer.rs` tests, time-injected via `tick_at`/`handle_resize_at`):
- `config_default_enables_bocpd_with_heuristic_fallback`, `first_event_uses_heuristic_then_bocpd`, `clamped_observation_falls_back_to_heuristic`, `explicit_disable_keeps_heuristic_only`, `stats_counts_detector_decisions` (from `g12-impl`).
- `bocpd_mode_never_emits_heuristic_cooldown_exit`, `immediate_mode_regime_stays_steady`, `isolated_resize_after_quiet_gap_is_not_forced`, `resize_arriving_while_pending_past_deadline_stays_forced` (pinned by `g12-impl-telemetry`).
- `hard_deadline_still_forces_apply_with_bocpd_on`: 30 events at 5 ms spacing (burst) -> an `ApplyResize` with `forced_by_deadline == true` no later than 100 ms after the first pending event.
- `steady_regime_delay_is_16ms_and_burst_is_40ms`: `current_delay_ms` under each regime (via `recommended_delay` when BOCPD decides with `p_burst` > 0.7 / < 0.3).
- `decision_evidence_json_has_detector_and_p_burst` (parse with `serde_json`).
Unit (`bocpd.rs`): `default_config_matches_readme_constants` (200.0, 20.0, 50.0, 100, 0.3, 0.7, 0.2).

Property (`resize_coalescer.rs`, `proptest`, 256 cases): `proptest_transitions_alternate_and_tags_match_path`: random event schedules (inter-arrivals from a mixture of Exp(20 ms) and Exp(200 ms), 50-500 events, plus random ticks) -> for the transition log: consecutive transitions have `from != to` and `to(prev) == from(next)`; every heuristic-tagged decision has `p_burst == None`; every bocpd-tagged decision has `p_burst` in [0, 1]; no `HeuristicExitBurstCooldown` while the detector is bocpd. `proptest_final_size_always_applied`: after the last event plus 200 ms of ticks, `last_applied == last event size`.

Bench: none (the coalescer runs once per resize event; no speed claim).

E2E: `g12-e2e` (differential + PTY storm).

## Logging (structured JSONL fields, tracing targets)

- `decision_evidence`: existing fields + `detector`, `p_burst`; `regime_transition`: + `detector`; `config`: + `enable_bocpd`, `heuristic_fallback`; `budget_decision`: + `resize_detector`.
- Proptest failures print the event schedule seed and the transition log.
- Tracing target `ftui.decision.resize`.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/resize_coalescer.rs` (tests + proptests; `proptest` dev-dep exists for ftui-runtime: `tests/proptest_*` files use it), `crates/ftui-runtime/src/bocpd.rs` (constant test).

## Success criteria

- [ ] All named unit tests pass; both proptests pass 256 cases (`rch exec -- cargo test -p ftui-runtime resize_coalescer bocpd`).
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: `g12-impl`.
- Related: `g12-impl-telemetry` (pinned tests), `g12-e2e`.

## Definition of done

Tests and proptests exist and pass; close reason lists names and case counts.

title: task(G12): Detector differential replay over resize_storm patterns, docs/perf report, PTY storm assertions
description:
## Context and why this matters

Flipping BOCPD on is only justified if it is not worse than the heuristic on real resize storms: the reality check (G12 success criterion 1) requires a differential run over recorded traces showing BOCPD "renders no more frames during drag than heuristic and applies the final size within 40 ms of the last event", archived under `docs/perf/`. The tooling half exists: `tests/e2e/lib/resize_storm_differential.py` compares labelled JSONL traces, and `crates/ftui-harness/src/resize_storm.rs` generates storm patterns with seeds. What is missing is a replay that runs both detectors over identical event schedules and writes comparable traces, plus a PTY leg that shows `detector: "bocpd"` in a real showcase run. Serves V10, V36, and the "flip back if it loses" rule of the plan.

## Current state (evidence)

- `tests/e2e/lib/resize_storm_differential.py` (16 KB): "Cross-browser differential checker for remote resize-storm JSONL traces"; args `--trace BROWSER=PATH` (repeat, min 2), `--baseline` (default first), `--known` TSV of known divergences, `--report` JSON (required), `--mode warn|strict`, `--max-printed-unknown`; labels are opaque strings, so `bocpd=` and `heuristic=` work.
- `crates/ftui-harness/src/resize_storm.rs` (63 KB): `StormPattern` :53 (`Burst { count }`, `Sweep { start_width, start_height, end_width, end_height, steps }`, `Oscillate { size_a, .. }`, further variants), `StormConfig` :132, `ResizeEvent` :288, `ResizeStorm` :325, `StormLogger` :565, `StormResult` :755, `RecordedStorm` :821, `get_storm_seed()` :914, `compute_output_checksum` :929, `analyze_storm_output(output, run_id) -> FlickerAnalysis` :940. `crates/ftui-render/benches/resize_storm_bench.rs` exists.
- `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh:2364`: PTY run of the showcase with `stty rows/cols` changes at 0.6 s intervals, `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL`, `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS=3200`, `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN=40`.
- `ResizeCoalescer` time-injected API: `tick_at(now)` :955 (and `handle_resize_at` per `g12-impl-telemetry`).
- `docs/perf/` holds `baseline_profiles.md` and pane perf notes; no resize differential.

## Target state

- Rust replay: `crates/ftui-harness/tests/resize_storm_detector_differential.rs` (integration test, ignored by default with `#[ignore]` and run by the script with `--ignored`, so it does not slow the unit suite): for each `StormPattern` fixture (Burst 50, Burst 200, Sweep 80x24 -> 200x60 in 40 steps, Oscillate 10 cycles, plus any drag-like pattern the module offers) and for each detector config (`CoalescerConfig::default()` = bocpd, `CoalescerConfig::default().without_bocpd()` = heuristic), drive a `ResizeCoalescer` with the pattern's timestamps (virtual clock from `get_storm_seed`-seeded jitter), tick every 16 ms, count `ApplyResize` actions during the storm ("frames during drag" = applies before the last event), record the time from the last event to the final `ApplyResize` ("final_apply_latency_ms"), and write one JSONL trace per (pattern, detector) under `target/resize_differential/<pattern>.<detector>.jsonl` with events `resize_event`, `apply`, `regime_transition`, `summary`.
- Script `scripts/resize_storm_differential_e2e.sh`: runs the ignored test, invokes the python differ per pattern with `--trace heuristic=... --trace bocpd=... --baseline heuristic --report target/resize_differential/<pattern>.report.json --mode warn`, aggregates the summaries into `docs/perf/resize_differential_<date>.md` (table: pattern, frames_during_drag heuristic/bocpd, final_apply_latency_ms heuristic/bocpd, transitions, verdict) and `.json`, and exits 1 if any pattern has `frames_bocpd > frames_heuristic` or `latency_bocpd > 40`. JSONL run log via `tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh`.
- PTY leg: `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh` evidence step gains `jsonl_assert "resize_detector_bocpd_present"` (at least one `decision_evidence` line with `"detector":"bocpd"`), `"resize_final_size_applied"` (last `regime_transition`/apply reflects 120x35 from the storm's last `stty`), and logs the counts of `decision_evidence` per detector.
- Report archived: `docs/perf/resize_differential_2026-09.md` committed with the run's git commit and seed.

## Implementation plan

1. Read `resize_storm.rs:53-330` to enumerate patterns and the event timestamp API; read `resize_coalescer.rs:955-1000` for `tick_at` and the apply path.
2. Write the ignored integration test with a small `Trace` writer (`serde_json` is a dev-dependency of ftui-harness? check; else `format!` JSON as the runtime does).
3. Write the script; use python for aggregation (stdlib only); produce the markdown table.
4. Extend the showcase E2E assertions.
5. Run locally: `scripts/resize_storm_differential_e2e.sh` -> commit `docs/perf/resize_differential_2026-09.{md,json}`; if BOCPD loses on any pattern, do NOT flip the default in `g12-impl` (revert to `enable_bocpd: false`) and record why in the report and in `g12-docs`.
6. CI: add the script to the `e2e-pty` job (after G04.6 tooling) or to the `perf-rollout-gates` job (`ci.yml:2480`), uploading `target/resize_differential` as an artifact.

What NOT to do: no wall-clock timing in the replay (virtual clock only); no editing of the python differ's semantics beyond accepting the labels (if it requires browser-specific keys, add a `--generic` flag rather than a copy of the script).

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-harness/tests/resize_storm_detector_differential.rs`: new (genuinely new: no replay of the coalescer exists).
- `scripts/resize_storm_differential_e2e.sh`: new.
- `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh`: assertions.
- `docs/perf/resize_differential_2026-09.{md,json}`: archived report.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: job step + artifact.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Report shows `frames_bocpd <= frames_heuristic` for every pattern and `latency_bocpd <= 40` for Burst/Sweep/Oscillate; the table is in the close reason.
- [ ] Python differ reports no unknown divergences in `warn` mode beyond the expected `apply` timing differences (recorded as known in a `--known` TSV committed under `tests/e2e/lib/resize_storm_known_divergences.tsv`).
- [ ] Showcase E2E assertions pass locally with `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL`; the count of `bocpd` vs `heuristic` decisions is logged.
- [ ] CI step green (run id in the close reason).

## Tests and logging

- Replay traces: per line `{"event":"resize_event","t_ms":..,"w":..,"h":..}`, `{"event":"apply","t_ms":..,"w":..,"h":..,"forced":bool,"coalesce_ms":..,"detector":".."}`, `{"event":"regime_transition",...}`, `{"event":"summary","pattern":"..","detector":"..","events":n,"applies_during_storm":n,"final_apply_latency_ms":x,"transitions":n,"seed":s,"git_commit":".."}`.
- Script JSONL: `run_id`, `scenario` (`resize_differential`), `step_start/step_end` per pattern with `duration_ms`, `assert` rows `frames_not_worse_<pattern>`, `latency_within_40ms_<pattern>` with details.
- PTY leg: escape tallies and the detector counts in `jsonl_assert` details.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: `g12-impl` (default + tags).
- Related: `g04-06-impl` (CI tooling), `g25-impl` (perf artifacts convention), `g12-docs` (quotes the numbers).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Virtual-clock replay instead of PTY-only: PTY storms via `stty` have 600 ms gaps and cannot exercise burst regimes; the replay covers the regimes and the PTY leg proves the integration.
- Alternative rejected: rewriting the python differ for this purpose; it already does labelled trace comparison with known-divergence lists.
- Risk: patterns in `resize_storm.rs` may lack timestamps; if so the replay assigns them from the pattern semantics (Burst: 5 ms spacing; Sweep: 30 ms; Oscillate: 50 ms) and says so in the report.

## Definition of done

Replay test, script, showcase assertions, and archived report exist; verdict recorded; CI step green; close reason has the table and run id.
notes: Refinement 2: BOCPD frame-count dominance on every trace is not a universal algorithm guarantee. Preserve hard event-order/resize/final-size/latency contracts and report a paired cost-latency frontier on fixed corpora, including patterns where heuristic wins. Known-divergence files may describe expected scheduling differences only, never hide dropped events/wrong final state or unbounded latency.

title: epic(G13): One controller each (e-process, ladder, diff ledger, allocation), shared teardown, presenter seam
description:
## Context and why this matters

The reality check's Section 2.3 names the root cause of the dead intelligence layer: with no "reachable from production" definition of done, the codebase accreted parallel, unused implementations of the same idea. Section 6 lists them as the design gap: two e-process controllers (`ftui-render/src/budget.rs` `EProcessState`, wired; `ftui-runtime/src/eprocess_throttle.rs` with GRAPA adaptive betting, dead), two degradation ladders (`BudgetController`, wired; `degradation_cascade.rs`, dead), two diff-evidence ledgers (`terminal_writer.rs` `diff_decision`, wired; `diff_evidence.rs`, dead), two allocation monitors (`ftui-render/src/alloc_budget.rs` `AllocLeakDetector`, referenced only by a doc comment; `ftui-runtime/src/allocation_budget.rs`, dead) with allocation leak detection therefore not wired at all, two terminal-session teardown stacks (`ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs` crossterm with its own panic hook; `ftui-tty` `RawModeGuard` with its own hook), and a half-built backend seam (`ftui-backend` `BackendPresenter` implemented by ftui-web and by a `TtyPresenter` in ftui-tty that `Program` never uses; presentation still goes through `W: Write`). README rows V12 (e-process/GRAPA), V15 (CUSUM allocation), V37 (PID degradation), V58 (degradation cascade module), V4 (RAII cleanup) depend on these.

This epic merges each pair into the wired implementation (porting what is worth keeping: GRAPA lambda adaptation, essential-widget filtering, diff regime transitions, leak detection), extracts one teardown sequence shared by both session stacks, and makes `Program` present through `BackendPresenter`. Deletions of the losing halves happen only with owner permission (`g13-decision`). It is XL and is the block that most directly fixes the design gap, so it is P1.

title: task(G13): PTY teardown byte-identity native vs crossterm (quit, SIGTERM, panic); cleanup_* on both backends
description:
## Context and why this matters

The README's RAII guarantee ("terminal restored on any exit path, even crashes") is backend-agnostic; after `g13-impl-teardown` both backends emit the same teardown plan and after `g13-impl-presenter` both present through the same presenter. The proof must be observed on a real PTY: the same program, run once with the native backend and once with crossterm, must produce byte-identical teardown sequences (kitty pop once, focus off, paste off, mouse off, cursor show, alt-screen leave, in that order) and the four failing `cleanup_*` PTY cases must pass. Serves V4 and G04.9.

## Current state (evidence)

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh`: cases `cleanup_normal, cleanup_cursor_visible, cleanup_sigterm, cleanup_mouse_disabled, cleanup_bracketed_paste_disabled, cleanup_altscreen_exit, cleanup_altscreen_mouse_focus` (:15-21); per-case logs under `$E2E_LOG_DIR/cleanup_*.log`; Section 5.1 reports 4 `cleanup_*` failures on ubuntu (after tooling).
- `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` (17 KB) Python-`pty` driver; `tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh`; `validate_jsonl.py`.
- Showcase enables both backends (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml` default features `native-backend`, `crossterm-compat`); backend selection at runtime: read `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/main.rs:186-218` (`run_program`) to see whether an env/flag selects the backend; if it always prefers native, add `FTUI_DEMO_BACKEND=native|crossterm` (documented in the README Configuration section by G35).
- Teardown sequences today: core `best_effort_cleanup_to` :1256-1288 and explicit `cleanup` :1101-1192; tty `write_cleanup_sequence_policy_with_mouse` :1660-1682 (see `g13-impl-teardown`).
- Kitty identity for PTY runs: `TERM=xterm-kitty` + `KITTY_WINDOW_ID` (Section 2.2.D) enables sync brackets, kitty keyboard, and alt-screen features so the full teardown plan is exercised.

## Target state

`tests/e2e/scripts/test_teardown_identity.sh` (new case file in the suite, listed in `run_all.sh`): builds the showcase, runs it under `pty.sh` at 80x24 with the kitty identity, alt-screen mode, mouse and paste enabled, for 1.5 s then `q`, once per backend (`FTUI_DEMO_BACKEND=native`, `=crossterm`); extracts the teardown suffix from each raw capture (bytes after the last sync-end `ESC [ ? 2026 l` that precedes program exit, or after the last frame's cursor-position sequence; the extraction rule is implemented in a small python helper `tests/e2e/lib/teardown_suffix.py` that also tokenizes escape sequences); asserts the two suffixes are byte-identical and equal the expected token list `[DECSC, DECSTBM-reset, DECRC, SGR0, kitty-pop, focus-off, paste-off, mouse-off, cursor-show, alt-leave]` (with kitty-pop exactly once); a second scenario sends `SIGTERM` instead of `q` and asserts the same suffix (signal path); a third scenario runs a panic-inducing showcase entry if one exists (`FTUI_DEMO_PANIC_AFTER_MS`, add if absent as a test seam guarded by an env check) and asserts the suffix after the panic message. All seven `cleanup_*` cases pass under both backends (parameterize `test_cleanup.sh` by `FTUI_DEMO_BACKEND` and run it twice from `run_all.sh`).

## Implementation plan

1. Read `main.rs:186-218`; add backend selection if missing (`native` default on unix; `crossterm` when requested; error if the feature is off).
2. Write `tests/e2e/lib/teardown_suffix.py` (stdlib; tokenizes CSI/OSC/DCS/ESC sequences; prints JSON with `tokens` and `hex` keys); unit-test it in `scripts/tests/` (pytest, from `g07-tests` infrastructure).
3. Write `test_teardown_identity.sh` following `test_cleanup.sh`'s structure; three scenarios x two backends; JSONL asserts `teardown_bytes_identical`, `teardown_token_order`, `kitty_pop_once`, `exit_code`, escape tallies.
4. Parameterize `test_cleanup.sh` by backend; update `run_all.sh`.
5. Run locally; attach `$E2E_LOG_DIR` listing and the two hex suffixes to the close reason.
6. CI: part of `e2e-pty` (ubuntu/macos) after G04.6.

What NOT to do: no fixed sleeps over 2 s; no assertion on frame content; no backend selection through a compile-time feature toggle (both are compiled; runtime selection only).

## Files to change

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_teardown_identity.sh`: new case.
- `tests/e2e/lib/teardown_suffix.py`: new helper; `scripts/tests/test_teardown_suffix.py`: tests.
- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh`, `run_all.sh`: backend parameterization.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/main.rs`: `FTUI_DEMO_BACKEND` (and optional panic seam).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `test_teardown_identity.sh` passes locally: 3 scenarios x 2 backends, `teardown_bytes_identical pass` for each scenario pair.
- [ ] `test_cleanup.sh` 7/7 under both backends locally.
- [ ] JSONL validated by `validate_jsonl.py`; CI `e2e-pty` ubuntu green (run id in the close reason); macOS tracked by `g04-09-impl`.

## Tests and logging

- E2E JSONL: `run_id`, `scenario` (`teardown_identity`), `identity` (`kitty`), `backend`, `case_step_*` with `duration_ms`, `assert` rows with `detail` (`native_hex=...`, `crossterm_hex=...`, `tokens=[...]`), escape tallies (`2026h/l`, `1049h/l`, `?25l/h`, `?1000/1002/1006`, `?2004`, `CSI<u` count), `exit_code`, PTY raw capture paths.

title: task(G13): Port GRAPA lambda adaptation into budget.rs EProcessState; eprocess_lambda telemetry
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:952-973 ("### E-Process: Anytime-Valid Testing") says "W_t = W_{t-1} × (1 + λ_t × (X_t - μ₀)) where λ_t is the betting fraction from GRAPA" and README.md:1609-1625 says "GRAPA tunes the betting fraction". The wired e-process (`ftui-render/src/budget.rs` `EProcessState`, used by `BudgetController` in every `Program` via the load governor) has a FIXED lambda (0.5); the GRAPA adaptation exists only in the dead `ftui-runtime/src/eprocess_throttle.rs`. This bead ports the adaptation into the wired controller so V12 becomes true on the production path, exposes lambda in telemetry, and leaves the throttle module quarantined for `g13-decision`.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-render/src/budget.rs`: `EProcessConfig` :212-236 (`lambda: f64` :215 "Sensitivity parameter λ", default 0.5 :236; `alpha` 0.05 "Degrade when E_t > 1/α"; `beta` 0.5 "Upgrade allowed when E_t < β"; EMA decay for σ estimation); `EProcessState::update(frame_time_ms, target_ms, config) -> f64` :274 computing a standardized residual and `log_factor = lambda * residual - lambda * lambda / 2.0` :298-299 (Gaussian likelihood-ratio e-value with warm-up of 10 frames per the doc at :212); `BudgetController::update` :530 gates degrade on `e_value > 1/alpha` (:562-563) and upgrade on `e_value < beta` (:578-579); `e_value()` :668; `eprocess_sigma_ms()` :674; `telemetry()` :697 (`BudgetTelemetry` with `pid_gate_threshold`, `evidence_threshold`, ...).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/eprocess_throttle.rs`: Bernoulli form (`x_t` in {0,1}, `mu_0`, `lambda_max = 1/mu_0 - 1e-6` :290): `multiplier = 1 + lambda (x_t - mu_0)` :337; GRAPA: `grad = (x_t - mu_0) / (1 + lambda (x_t - mu_0))` :341-342, `lambda = (lambda + grapa_eta * grad).clamp(1e-6, lambda_max)` :345; config `initial_lambda` 0.5, `grapa_eta` 0.1 (:126-127); tracing target `ftui.eprocess` :382.
- `program.rs` `budget_decision` JSONL :4150 has `e_value`, `pid_*`, `in_warmup`; no lambda field.
- `telemetry_schema.rs:53 TARGET_EPROCESS = "ftui.eprocess"` exists and is unused by budget.rs (ftui-render has no tracing dependency on the runtime's schema; ftui-render's `tracing` feature is separate).

## Target state

`EProcessConfig` gains `adaptive_lambda: bool` (default true), `grapa_eta: f64` (default 0.1), `lambda_min: f64` (0.05), `lambda_max: f64` (2.0); `EProcessState` gains `lambda: f64` (initialized from `config.lambda`) and after each residual `r_t` applies the GRAPA step for the Gaussian form: the per-step log-wealth is `λ r − λ²/2`, whose gradient in λ is `r − λ`, so `λ_{t+1} = clamp(λ_t + η (r_t − λ_t), λ_min, λ_max)` (this is the GRAPA update specialized to the Gaussian e-value; document the derivation in the doc comment and cite `eprocess_throttle.rs:340-345` for the Bernoulli form it generalizes); the log-factor uses the CURRENT λ before the update (predictable betting: λ_t must be measurable at time t-1 for anytime validity; state that invariant in the doc and test it); `BudgetTelemetry` and `budget_decision` gain `eprocess_lambda`; `BudgetController::eprocess_lambda()` accessor.

2. `BudgetController` (:420-560): `eprocess_lambda()` accessor; `telemetry()` :697 adds `eprocess_lambda`.
3. `program.rs` :4150 `budget_decision`: add `"eprocess_lambda":{:.6}` sourced from `self.budget` controller telemetry (find where `e_value` is read for the line, around :4140-4160, and add the sibling); register with `g20-impl`.
4. Tracing: in `budget.rs` under `#[cfg(feature = "tracing")]`, `tracing::trace!(target: "ftui.eprocess", lambda, e_value, residual)` per update (ftui-render cannot import the runtime's `telemetry_schema`; the literal is in ftui-render only, which G20's "no literals" rule must allowlist or G20 moves the constants into ftui-core; note it for `g20-impl`).
5. Quarantine: `eprocess_throttle.rs` and `evidence_bridges.rs` are already behind `experimental` (`g07-impl`); no change here; do not delete (owner permission via `g13-decision`, executed by `g13-impl`).
6. Gates and `ubs`; run `cargo test -p ftui-render budget` and `cargo test -p ftui-runtime --lib` (budget_decision JSONL tests around `program.rs:10205-10257` need the new field).

What NOT to do: no port of the Bernoulli throttle API (`observe(matched: bool)`) into budget.rs (different quantity); no second e-process struct; no deletion.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-render/src/budget.rs`: config fields, state lambda, GRAPA update, telemetry, tests.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `budget_decision` field, JSONL tests.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `budget_controller_grapa_adapts_lambda`: two controllers (adaptive on/off) fed 30 frames at target then a step to 1.8x target: the adaptive one crosses `e_value > 1/alpha` (20) in fewer frames than the fixed one (assert strictly fewer, and print both counts); fed 10,000 frames at target with N(0, 1σ) noise (seeded), neither crosses.
- [ ] `lambda_is_predictable`: the log-factor at step t uses λ_{t-1} (assert by reconstructing from telemetry: `e_value_t == e_value_{t-1} * exp(λ_{t-1} r_t − λ_{t-1}²/2)` within 1e-9).
- [ ] `lambda_stays_within_bounds` over adversarial residual sequences (±1e6).
- [ ] `budget_decision` line contains `eprocess_lambda` (existing JSONL test extended).

## Tests and logging

- Unit: the four tests above in `budget.rs` and `program.rs`.
- Property (`budget.rs`, `proptest`): `proptest_e_value_is_supermartingale_under_null` (mean of `e_value` over 200 independent null runs of 500 frames stays below 3 with adaptation on; Ville's inequality sanity).
- Logging: `budget_decision.eprocess_lambda`; tracing `ftui.eprocess` trace.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: `g07-impl` (the throttle is quarantined there; this bead must not race the gating of `evidence_bridges.rs`).
- Unblocks: `g13-impl`, `g13-tests`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Gaussian-form GRAPA rather than transplanting the Bernoulli throttle: the wired controller models standardized frame-time residuals; the betting fraction that maximizes expected log-wealth for a Gaussian shift is the shift itself, which the update tracks.
- Bounds 0.05..2.0: λ below 0.05 makes the test blind; above 2.0 the Gaussian approximation and the σ̂ EMA make the e-value explode on single outliers (the doc at `budget.rs:185-210` already warns thresholds are empirically tuned).
- Risk: adaptation makes degradation trigger earlier on real load; the `frame_render`/`runtime_render_frame_headless_80x24` baselines and the showcase E2E `fallback`/degradation histograms (G11) will show it; the config flag allows disabling.

## Definition of done

GRAPA in `EProcessState`; telemetry field; tests and proptest green; gates and `ubs` clean; close reason lists the crossing-frame counts from the adapt test.
notes: Refinement 2: a selected seeded null sequence with no threshold crossing is only a fixture, not anytime-valid error control. Adopt a precise null/alternative and valid denominator/assumptions before claiming GRAPA bounds; preserve predictability and numerical domain tests. Repeated calibration/power experiments need truth labels, confidence intervals and held-out data. G45 claim and quantile tasks govern mathematical validity; do not duplicate controllers or overfit strict 'fewer frames' to one seed.

title: task(G13): Merge diff_evidence into TerminalWriter: DiffRegime classification and diff_regime_transition event

title: task(G13): Wire AllocLeakDetector into FrameGuardrails::check_frame with leak fields in guardrail_snapshot
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:1004-1012 ("### CUSUM Control Charts": "Allocation budget tracking uses **CUSUM** for fast change detection") and the e-process applications list ("Allocation budget alerts", README.md:968-972) promise allocation leak detection; vision row V15 is DEAD. Two implementations exist and neither runs: `ftui-render/src/alloc_budget.rs` `AllocLeakDetector` (1,413 lines; CUSUM + e-value; referenced only by a doc comment in `frame_guardrails.rs:6` and an integration test) and `ftui-runtime/src/allocation_budget.rs` `AllocationBudget` (45 KB; dead). Meanwhile `FrameGuardrails::check_frame(memory_bytes, queue_depth)` already receives a per-frame memory series from `Program`. This bead wires `AllocLeakDetector` into `FrameGuardrails` so the series it already sees is monitored, surfaces alerts in `guardrail_snapshot`, and records the bd-1za0z item (1) sensor-semantics decision (capacity vs usage) in the code where the number is produced. Serves V15, the README CUSUM claim, and Section 6.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-render/src/frame_guardrails.rs` (1,401 lines): module doc :3-12 says it "complements the time-based RenderBudget and allocation-tracking AllocLeakDetector"; `MemoryBudget::new` :190; `QueueGuardrails::new` :398; `GuardrailsConfig` :577; `FrameGuardrails` :630 (`new(config)` :642; `check_frame(&mut self, memory_bytes: usize, queue_depth: u32) -> GuardrailVerdict` :655 with `queue.check(queue_depth)` :670; snapshot construction :737); `GuardrailSnapshot` :760 (`queue_depth` :776; `to_jsonl` :791-810 emits `queue_depth`, `queue_peak`, `queue_drops`, memory counters incl. `mem_emergency_violations` per bd-1za0z F5).
- `crates/ftui-render/src/alloc_budget.rs`: `LeakDetectorConfig` :54, `EvidenceEntry` :95 (`to_jsonl` :116), `LeakAlert` :137, `AllocLeakDetector` :181 (`new` :204, `observe(value: f64) -> LeakAlert` :221, `e_value` :314, `cusum_upper` :320, `cusum_lower` :326, `mean` :332, `sigma` :338, `frames` :344, `ledger` :350, `threshold` :356, `reset` :361); `crates/ftui-render/tests/allocation_budget_integration.rs` uses it (:21, :168, :209, :251).

`GuardrailsConfig` gains `leak: Option<LeakDetectorConfig>` (default `Some(LeakDetectorConfig::default())`); `FrameGuardrails` owns `leak: Option<AllocLeakDetector>`; `check_frame` calls `leak.observe(memory_bytes as f64)` and includes the `LeakAlert` in `GuardrailVerdict` (`leak_alert: Option<LeakAlert>`) with a new `GuardrailKind::AllocationLeak`; `GuardrailSnapshot` gains `leak_e_value`, `leak_cusum_upper`, `leak_mean_bytes`, `leak_alert: bool` and `to_jsonl` emits them; `FrameGuardrails::reset_leak_detector()` is called by `Program` after a capacity trim (so the intentional drop is not a change point) and after an emergency shed; the sensor semantics are documented at the `memory_bytes` computation in `program.rs`: "retained capacity; a monotone increase in retained capacity across frames is the leak signal; usage-level accounting is not available without an allocator hook (feature `alloc-count`, G25)"; `guardrail_snapshot` is emitted when the leak alert fires (alerts are already rate-limited by the degradation logic). `allocation_budget.rs` (runtime) stays quarantined for `g13-decision`.

## Implementation plan

## Tests and logging

- Property (`alloc_budget.rs`, already has proptest? check `tests/proptest_*` in ftui-render; add `proptest_no_alert_on_stationary_series` with 512 cases if absent).
