## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: `g07-impl` (runtime `allocation_budget` quarantined).
- Unblocks: `g13-impl`, `g13-tests`; closes bd-1za0z item (1) as "documented sensor semantics + leak detection on retained capacity" (the close reason of bd-1za0z references this bead, see `g12-impl-telemetry`).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Capacity as the signal: bd-1za0z observed that the degradation actuator cannot move a capacity sensor; the soft trim fixed that. For leak detection, retained capacity growing monotonically IS the symptom a user would report ("memory keeps growing"); usage accounting would need an allocator hook, deferred to G25's `alloc-count` bench feature.
- Alternative rejected: running the detector inside `Program` next to guardrails; `FrameGuardrails` already owns the per-frame memory policy and its snapshot is the evidence surface.

## Definition of done

Detector wired with resets and evidence; tests green; gates and `ubs` clean; close reason lists test names and one snapshot line with `leak_alert`.

title: task(G13): Extract ftui_core::session_teardown (plan, kitty latch, chained hook) shared by both session stacks
description:
## Context and why this matters

README vision row V4 "RAII cleanup even on panic" is WORKING but implemented twice: `ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs` (crossterm session) and `ftui-tty/src/lib.rs` (native backend) each have their own teardown byte sequence, their own panic hook, and their own kitty-keyboard pop latch. The two sequences differ in what they emit and in what order (core emits DECSC/DECSTBM-reset/DECRC/SGR0/SYNC_END before the feature disables; tty emits `write_terminal_state_resets` then the feature disables with `alt_screen = true` unconditionally in the panic path), tty installs its panic hook only under `panic = "abort"`, and the PTY `cleanup_*` E2E cases fail (Section 5.1). Two stacks means two places for the next teardown bug. This bead extracts one `ftui_core::session_teardown` module (ordered steps, pop-once latch, chained hook installation) used by both, so the byte order is identical on both backends and `g13-e2e` can assert byte identity. Serves V4, Section 6 design gap "two terminal-session stacks", and G04.9's `cleanup_*` cluster.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs` (98 KB): module docs :43-54 list the restore table and order ("2. Disable kitty keyboard (if enabled) ... 6. Show cursor (always)"); `cleanup(&mut self)` :1101-1192 (sets `EXPLICIT_TEARDOWN_STARTED` :1106, takes `terminal_output_lock()` :1109, drops `signal_guard` :1112, headless early-return :1114-1122, then: kitty disable :1141-1150 (comment bd-kdn7n about the tty context's kitty entry), `DisableBracketedPaste` :1160, `cursor::Show` :1174, `LeaveAlternateScreen` :1177, `disable_raw_mode`, flush, `session_lock.take()`); `Drop` :1207-1209; `install_panic_hook` :1222-1236 (`OnceLock`, chains `previous`, guards on `!panic_cleanup_suppressed() && TERMINAL_SESSION_ACTIVE`); `best_effort_cleanup_for_exit` :1243; `best_effort_cleanup` :1247-1251; `best_effort_cleanup_to(stdout, caps)` :1256-1288 (DECSC `\x1b7`, `RESET_SCROLL_REGION`, DECRC `\x1b8`, `RESET_STYLE`, `SYNC_END`, `emit_stack_pops = !BEST_EFFORT_KITTY_POP_EMITTED.swap(true)` :1274, kitty disable if `caps.kitty_keyboard && !caps.in_any_mux()`, `DisableFocusChange` if focus, `DisableBracketedPaste`, `mouse_disable_sequence_for_caps`, `cursor::Show`, `LeaveAlternateScreen`, `disable_raw_mode`, flush); `SignalGuard` :1292 (SIGINT/TERM/HUP/QUIT/WINCH).
- `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs`: `store_raw_mode_snapshot` :235; `best_effort_termination_cleanup` :284-302 (`write_terminal_state_resets(&mut stdout)`, `emit_sync_end = false`, `cleanup_features_for_capabilities(caps)`, `mouse_disable_sequence_for_capabilities(caps)`, `write_cleanup_sequence_policy_with_mouse(&features, true, false, mouse_disable, &mut stdout)`, flush, `restore_raw_mode_snapshot()`); `install_abort_panic_hook` :305-317 (returns early unless `cfg!(panic = "abort")`; `OnceLock`; chains previous); `install_termination_signal_hook` :320; `RawModeGuard` :365-395 (`enter` :374 opens `/dev/tty`, `enter_on` :380 `tcgetattr`/`cfmakeraw`/`tcsetattr` + `store_raw_mode_snapshot`), `Drop` :398 (`tcsetattr` restore); `TtyBackend::open` :1460, `Drop` :1538; `write_cleanup_sequence` :1621, `write_cleanup_sequence_with_sync_end` :1632, `write_cleanup_sequence_policy_with_mouse` :1660-1682 (order: `SYNC_END` if `emit_sync_end`, `KITTY_KEYBOARD_DISABLE` if kitty, `FOCUS_DISABLE`, `BRACKETED_PASTE_DISABLE`, mouse disable, `CURSOR_SHOW`, `ALT_SCREEN_LEAVE` if alt).
- ftui-tty depends on ftui-core (`TerminalCapabilities`), so a shared module in core is reachable from both.
- PTY E2E: `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh` cases `cleanup_normal, cleanup_cursor_visible, cleanup_sigterm, cleanup_mouse_disabled, cleanup_bracketed_paste_disabled, cleanup_altscreen_exit, cleanup_altscreen_mouse_focus`.

## Target state

`crates/ftui-core/src/session_teardown.rs` (new; `pub mod session_teardown;` in `lib.rs`) with:
- `pub struct TeardownPlan { pub emit_sync_end: bool, pub reset_scroll_region: bool, pub reset_style: bool, pub kitty_keyboard: bool, pub focus_events: bool, pub bracketed_paste: bool, pub mouse: Option<&'static [u8]>, pub show_cursor: bool, pub leave_alt_screen: bool }` and `impl TeardownPlan { pub fn from_capabilities(caps: &TerminalCapabilities, features: TeardownFeatures, alt_screen: bool, owns_sync_block: bool) -> Self; pub fn write(&self, w: &mut impl Write) -> io::Result<()> }` writing the canonical order: DECSC, DECSTBM reset, DECRC (only when `reset_scroll_region`), SGR0 (when `reset_style`), `SYNC_END` (when `emit_sync_end`), kitty pop (through the latch), focus off, paste off, mouse off, `CURSOR_SHOW`, `ALT_SCREEN_LEAVE`. Raw-mode restore is NOT part of the plan (backend-specific: crossterm `disable_raw_mode` vs termios snapshot) and is documented as "always last, after `write` and flush".
- `pub struct KittyPopLatch` (process-wide `AtomicBool`): `pub fn try_claim() -> bool` (first caller true) and `pub fn reset_for_tests()`; both `BEST_EFFORT_KITTY_POP_EMITTED` (core) and tty's implicit behavior use it; explicit `cleanup()` of a live session that enabled kitty pops unconditionally (it owns the entry), best-effort paths go through the latch.
- `pub fn install_chained_panic_hook(name: &'static str, f: fn())`: `OnceLock` per name, chains the previous hook, runs `f` then `previous(info)`; core's `install_panic_hook` and tty's `install_abort_panic_hook` both call it with their `best_effort_*` functions; tty's `cfg!(panic = "abort")` early return is removed (the hook must run under unwind too; the guard on "a session is active" is what prevents spraying escapes, and tty gets an equivalent `TTY_SESSION_ACTIVE` atomic set in `TtyBackend::open` and cleared in `Drop`).
- The escape constants (`SYNC_END`, `RESET_SCROLL_REGION`, `RESET_STYLE`, kitty/focus/paste/mouse/cursor/alt sequences) live in one place in core (`session_teardown::seq`), and both crates use them (tty currently has its own `KITTY_KEYBOARD_DISABLE`, `FOCUS_DISABLE`, `BRACKETED_PASTE_DISABLE`, `CURSOR_SHOW`, `ALT_SCREEN_LEAVE`, `SYNC_END` constants; move them).

## Implementation plan

1. Create `session_teardown.rs` with the types above and unit tests (`write_emits_canonical_order`, `latch_claims_once`, `chained_hook_runs_previous`).
2. `terminal_session.rs`: `cleanup` :1101 and `best_effort_cleanup_to` :1256 build a `TeardownPlan` and call `write`, then perform the crossterm-specific raw-mode disable and flush; delete the now-duplicated inline sequence code in those two functions (in-file code removal, not file deletion); `install_panic_hook` :1222 delegates to `install_chained_panic_hook("ftui-core", best_effort_cleanup)`; `BEST_EFFORT_KITTY_POP_EMITTED` becomes `KittyPopLatch`.
3. `ftui-tty/src/lib.rs`: `write_cleanup_sequence_policy_with_mouse` :1660 becomes a thin call to `TeardownPlan::write` (keep the public `write_cleanup_sequence`/`_with_sync_end` names since PTY tests use them); `best_effort_termination_cleanup` :284 builds the plan with `reset_scroll_region: true, reset_style: true, emit_sync_end: false`; `install_abort_panic_hook` :305 becomes `install_chained_panic_hook("ftui-tty", best_effort_termination_cleanup)` without the abort-only guard; `TtyBackend::open`/`Drop` set/clear `TTY_SESSION_ACTIVE`; `RawModeGuard::drop` :398 unchanged (raw-mode restore stays last because `TtyBackend::Drop` :1538 orders presenter teardown before the guard drop; verify and document the field order in `TtyBackend`, since Rust drops fields in declaration order).
4. Mux policy: the plan's `from_capabilities` applies the same rule both crates apply today (`kitty && !in_any_mux`, focus likewise) so behavior in tmux/screen is unchanged.
5. Gates; `cargo test -p ftui-core -p ftui-tty`; `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh` locally; `ubs`.

What NOT to do: no change to the crossterm raw-mode API usage; no removal of `TerminalSession` (Windows path); no third sequence for the web backend (ftui-web has no terminal); no `#[deprecated]` wrappers.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-core/src/session_teardown.rs`: new module.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs`: `pub mod session_teardown;`.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs`: use the plan and latch; hook delegation.
- `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs`: use the plan/constants; hook delegation; session-active atomic.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `write_emits_canonical_order` asserts the exact byte string for a full-feature plan (kitty, focus, paste, SGR mouse, alt) equals the concatenation of the constants in the documented order.
- [ ] `core_cleanup_and_tty_cleanup_produce_identical_bytes`: with the same capabilities/features/alt flags, `TerminalSession`'s best-effort writer path (`best_effort_cleanup_to` into a `Vec<u8>`) and tty's `write_cleanup_sequence_with_sync_end` into a `Vec<u8>` are byte-identical.
- [ ] `latch_claims_once` and `hook_runs_under_unwind` (a test thread panics with a session-active flag set; the hook's side effect is observed; run with `panic = "unwind"` which is the test profile).
- [ ] `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh` all 7 cases pass locally on Linux with the native backend and with crossterm (the showcase enables both features; select per `g13-e2e`).

## Tests and logging

- Unit: the four above plus tty's existing cleanup tests (`:1700-1800` region: `event_source_*`, cleanup sequence tests) updated to the constants' new home.
- E2E: `g13-e2e` (byte identity under PTY, JSONL).
- Logging: tracing `ftui.core.session` (feature `tracing`) `info!` at teardown start/end with `backend = "crossterm"|"tty"`, `plan = ?TeardownPlan`.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: `g03-impl` (it edits `complete_lifecycle`/signal clearing in `program.rs`, and the core `SignalGuard` region; land it first to avoid conflicting edits in the same functions).
- Unblocks: `g13-impl-presenter`, `g13-e2e`, `g13-impl`, `g13-tests`; G04.9 `cleanup_*`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- One plan type instead of two functions: the byte order is the contract; a struct makes it testable without a terminal and greppable.
- Removing tty's abort-only hook guard: under `panic = "unwind"` (the default for tests and `cargo run` dev builds), a panic in a native-backend program today never runs tty's cleanup; core's hook covers only crossterm sessions. The session-active guard replaces the abort-only guard.
- Risk: DECSC/DECRC + DECSTBM reset in the tty path is new bytes for the native backend's panic path; the PTY tests assert the scroll region is reset (`test_inline.sh` checks DECSTBM) so this is a fix, not a regression; if a terminal misbehaves on DECRC after alt-screen leave, the plan's order keeps DECRC before the feature disables, as core does today.

## Definition of done

Shared module in core; both crates use it; identical-bytes test green; `test_cleanup.sh` green locally; gates and `ubs` clean; close reason lists the tests and the E2E log path.

title: task(G13): Program generic over BackendPresenter; TerminalPresenter wraps TerminalWriter; remove TtyPresenter
description:
## Context and why this matters

`ftui-backend` (Section 5.3) is "half a seam": events reach `Program` through `BackendEventSource`, but presentation writes straight to `W: Write` via `TerminalWriter`, and `BackendPresenter` is implemented by ftui-web (`lib.rs:379`) and by a `TtyPresenter` in ftui-tty (`lib.rs:1322-1357`) that `Program` never constructs. The README architecture ("TerminalSession (crossterm) → ... → TerminalWriter") and AGENTS.md diagram describe a single output layer; the reality is that the web backend and the terminal backends take different code paths into the runtime. This bead completes the seam: the terminal presenter wraps `TerminalWriter` (so inline mode, the one-writer rule, `write_log` sanitization, and `diff_decision` evidence are preserved), `Program` becomes generic over `P: BackendPresenter` instead of `W: Write`, and both terminal constructors (native and crossterm) build the same presenter. Serves Section 6 design gap, V8 (web parity), and prepares G31 (Windows over crossterm) and G23.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-backend/src/lib.rs`: `BackendPresenter` :84-110 (`type Error`, `capabilities(&self) -> &TerminalCapabilities`, `write_log(&mut self, text) -> Result`, `present_ui(&mut self, buf: &Buffer, diff: Option<&BufferDiff>, full_repaint_hint: bool) -> Result`, `gc(&mut self) {}`); `Backend` :117+ (`type Presenter: BackendPresenter<Error = Self::Error>`).
- `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs`: `TtyPresenter<W: Write + Send = io::Stdout> { capabilities, inner: Option<Presenter<W>> }` :1322-1326; `new(caps)` headless :1330, `live(caps)` :1339, `with_writer(writer, caps)` :1349; `impl<W: Write + Send> BackendPresenter for TtyPresenter<W>` :1357 (`type Error = io::Error`); `TtyBackend` :1407 implements `Backend` :1595 with `Presenter = TtyPresenter`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `writer: TerminalWriter<W>` :4699; `impl<M: Model, E: BackendEventSource<Error = io::Error>, W: Write + Send> Program<M, E, W>` :4972; `with_event_source(model, backend: E, features, writer: TerminalWriter<W>, config)` :4983; crossterm ctor builds `TerminalWriter::with_diff_config(...)` :4840; `with_native_backend` :5140-5197 builds `TerminalWriter::with_diff_config(io::stdout(), config.screen_mode, config.ui_anchor, capabilities, config.diff_config.clone())` :5187 and passes it to `with_event_source` :5195; test constructors use `TerminalWriter::new(...)` with `Vec<u8>` at :10855-10939; `Program` calls on the writer include `last_diff_strategy()` (:6404), present/inline/log paths, `set_evidence_sink`, resize handling (:5728-5760), `write_log` (Section 2.1), `last_diff_elapsed` (G11).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs` (252 KB): `TerminalWriter<W>` with `with_diff_config`, `new`, `tile_diff_config` :345, evidence emission :1653-1701, `write_log` sanitization (:2157 per Section 2.2), inline strategies.
- `crates/ftui-web/src/lib.rs:379`: `WebPresenter` with `outputs.logs` and patch production.
- Dependency direction: ftui-runtime depends on ftui-tty (feature `native-backend`); ftui-tty cannot name runtime types. `TerminalWriter` is a runtime type.

## Target state

- `BackendPresenter` (ftui-backend) is extended with what `Program` actually needs beyond `present_ui`/`write_log`: `fn resize(&mut self, cols: u16, rows: u16)`, `fn screen_mode(&self) -> ScreenMode`, `fn set_screen_mode(&mut self, mode: ScreenMode)`, `fn set_evidence_writer(&mut self, w: Option<Arc<dyn Fn(&str) + Send + Sync>>)` (evidence types live in ftui-runtime, so the sink is passed as a line-writer callback to keep ftui-backend free of runtime types), `fn last_diff_strategy(&self) -> Option<DiffStrategy>`, `fn last_diff_elapsed(&self) -> Option<Duration>`, `fn begin_shutdown(&mut self) -> Result` (presenter-owned state; session teardown remains in the backend's `Drop`), `fn flush(&mut self) -> Result`. Each has a default returning a neutral value so `WebPresenter` compiles with minimal changes and overrides what it supports.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_presenter.rs` (new): `TerminalPresenter<W: Write + Send> { writer: TerminalWriter<W> }` implementing every trait method by delegation; `with_writer(writer, caps, screen_mode, ui_anchor, diff_config)` and `live(..)` over `io::stdout()`. It lives in ftui-runtime because `TerminalWriter` does and the dependency direction is runtime -> tty.
- `Program<M, E, P: BackendPresenter<Error = io::Error>>`; field `presenter: P`; `with_event_source(model, events: E, features, presenter: P, config)`; `with_native_backend` and the crossterm constructor both build `TerminalPresenter::with_writer(io::stdout(), ..)` (ANSI output does not depend on crossterm); headless/test constructors and `ProgramSimulator` use `TerminalPresenter::with_writer(Vec<u8>, ..)`.
- `ftui-tty`: `TtyPresenter` (:1322-1405) is removed as redundant (a struct removal inside `lib.rs`, not a file deletion); `TtyBackend` stops declaring a `Presenter` associated type: the `Backend` trait's `Presenter` type is dropped (the runtime composes `Events` + `Presenter` itself, which is what it does today), and ftui-web's `Backend` impl (if any) is adjusted.
- `Program` no longer has a `W: Write` parameter; `ftui::App`/`Program::open` (G01) build the presenter.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-backend/src/lib.rs`: extend `BackendPresenter` with the methods above (defaults); drop the `Presenter` associated type from `Backend` (or keep it but stop requiring it in `Program`; choose drop, and update `ftui-web`'s `Backend` impl if it implements `Backend`).
2. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_presenter.rs` (genuinely new: no runtime type implements `BackendPresenter` today) + `pub mod terminal_presenter;` and `pub use terminal_presenter::TerminalPresenter;` in `lib.rs`.
3. `program.rs`: replace `W: Write + Send` with `P: BackendPresenter<Error = io::Error>` in the struct (:4699 field type), the impl block (:4972), `with_event_source` (:4983), the crossterm ctor (:4840 region), `with_native_backend` (:5187-5195), headless/test constructors (:10855-10939, :11276-11364), and every `self.writer.` call site (`rg -n 'self\.writer\.' program.rs`; each becomes a trait call; where the trait lacks a method the writer had, add it to the trait with a default rather than downcasting).
4. `simulator.rs`, `ftui-harness`, `ftui-demo-showcase`, `doctor_frankentui` (7 files import ftui): update constructor calls (`rg -n 'TerminalWriter::' crates/ftui-harness crates/ftui-demo-showcase crates/doctor_frankentui`).
5. `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs`: remove `TtyPresenter` (:1322-1405) and the `Presenter` associated type in `impl Backend for TtyBackend` :1595; keep everything else.
6. `crates/ftui-web`: implement the new methods where meaningful (`resize`, `screen_mode`); confirm `pane_web_e2e.rs`/`pane_cross_host_parity.rs` still pass.
7. Gates: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` (all feature combos in the `features` job), clippy, fmt, `cargo test -p ftui-runtime -p ftui-tty -p ftui-web -p ftui-harness -p ftui-demo-showcase`, `ubs`.

What NOT to do: no `impl BackendPresenter for TerminalWriter<W>` (the writer is the core; the presenter is the seam type that owns evidence/callback plumbing); no keeping `W: Write` alongside `P` "for compatibility"; no deletion of `ftui-tty/src/lib.rs`.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-backend/src/lib.rs`: trait extension; `Backend` adjustment.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_presenter.rs`: new; `crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs`: module + re-export.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: generic parameter, constructors, call sites, tests.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/simulator.rs`: constructor.
- `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs`: remove `TtyPresenter`; `Backend` impl.
- `crates/ftui-web/src/lib.rs`: new trait methods.
- `crates/ftui-harness`, `crates/ftui-demo-showcase`, `crates/doctor_frankentui`: constructor call sites.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `rg -n 'W: Write' crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` returns no `Program` generic (only unrelated helpers).
- [ ] `rg -n 'impl.*BackendPresenter for' crates` shows exactly `TerminalPresenter` (ftui-runtime) and `WebPresenter` (ftui-web).
- [ ] `program_presents_through_backend_presenter`: a headless `Program` with a counting presenter implemented in the test module (`CountingPresenter`, per the no-mock naming rule in `.github/workflows/ci.yml:63-71`) records `present_ui` calls == frames and receives `write_log` text.
- [ ] `native_and_crossterm_constructors_build_terminal_presenter` (both paths call `TerminalPresenter::with_writer`; assert via a type-level check in tests).
- [ ] ftui-web tests unchanged and green; showcase runs under both backends (PTY in `g13-e2e`).

## Tests and logging

- Unit: the two above plus existing writer tests (unchanged) and `terminal_presenter.rs` delegation tests (`resize_forwards_to_writer`, `evidence_callback_receives_diff_decision`).
- Logging: none new; the presenter forwards the writer's tracing.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: `g01-impl` (constructor consolidation: `Program::open`/`run` dispatch; doing the generic change once), `g13-impl-teardown` (ftui-tty edits in the same file).
- Unblocks: `g13-impl`, `g13-tests`, `g13-e2e`; G31 and G23 benefit.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Why the presenter lives in ftui-runtime: `TerminalWriter` is a runtime type (one-writer rule, inline strategies, evidence), and the dependency direction is runtime -> tty, so the ANSI presenter cannot live in ftui-tty without moving `TerminalWriter` down (a much larger move; rejected for now, noted as a possible follow-up if ftui-tty ever needs to present without the runtime).
- The trait gains several methods with defaults; that is the honest shape of what `Program` needs, and defaults keep ftui-web small.
- Risk: the generic change touches ~all constructors and doctor_frankentui; do it after G01 so constructors are already consolidated.

## Definition of done

`Program` generic over `BackendPresenter`; `TerminalPresenter` in ftui-runtime; `TtyPresenter` removed; web unchanged; tests green across crates; gates and `ubs` clean; close reason lists the call sites changed (count) and test names.
notes: Refinement 2: counting presenter instrumentation proves call dispatch only. Do not rename a fake to evade policy or equate its calls with terminal restoration. Real native/Crossterm PTY state and output evidence is mandatory; preserve library seam behavior and all backends.

title: G13: Integrate unified controllers and teardown with retained experimental sources
description:
## Context and why this matters

This is the integrating bead of G13 ("Duplicate controllers and half-finished seams", XL, P1). The four merges (`g13-impl-eprocess`, `-ladder`, `-ledger`, `-alloc`), the shared teardown (`g13-impl-teardown`) and the presenter seam (`g13-impl-presenter`) each land independently and leave the losing halves quarantined behind `experimental` (`g07-impl`). This bead finishes the block: it executes the deletions the owner permitted in `g13-decision` (quoting the permission), removes the now-orphaned references (`evidence_bridges.rs`, `policy_config.rs`'s `CascadeConfig` field, test files that only exercised the deleted modules), runs the reachability gate to prove no duplicate remains, reconciles the README sections that named the deleted modules, and verifies the block's success criteria end to end. Other clusters depend on `g13-impl` as the block's primary bead (`g42-impl`).

## Current state (evidence)

- Before this bead: the four dead modules are gated (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs` `#[cfg(feature = "experimental")]` on `allocation_budget` :28, `degradation_cascade` :41, `diff_evidence` :43, `eprocess_throttle` :45, `evidence_bridges` :48 per `g07-impl`); their useful parts are ported; `scripts/check_module_reachability.py` reports them EXPERIMENTAL.
- Test files tied to them (from `rg` 2026-09-01): `crates/ftui-runtime/tests/{proptest_allocation_budget_invariants,voi_eprocess_unit_tests,recipe_b_tail_safe_controller}.rs` (dedicated); `policy_controller_tests.rs`, `e2e_recipe_b_tail_safe.rs`, `e2e_recipe_f_policy_as_data.rs`, `e2e_unified_evidence.rs`, `proptest_statistical_invariants.rs` (mixed; the flake_detector part of the last stays).
- `src/policy_config.rs` references `degradation_cascade` (a `CascadeConfig` field); `src/evidence_bridges.rs` references `eprocess_throttle`.
- README sections naming the modules: "## Degradation Cascade" :1388 (module note added by `g11-docs`), "### E-Process" :952-973, "### CUSUM Control Charts" :1004-1012, "Experimental modules" table rows (`g07-docs`).
- `g13-decision` holds the per-file verdicts.

## Target state

For every file with a DELETE verdict: `git rm` in one commit per pair with the permission text, the command lines, and the timestamp in the commit message (AGENTS.md "Document the confirmation"); dependent test files deleted (dedicated) or edited (mixed) in the same commit; `policy_config.rs` loses its `CascadeConfig` field; `lib.rs` loses the `pub mod` lines; README "Experimental modules" rows removed and the three README sections say "one controller" language; `scripts/check_module_reachability.py --json` shows no `eprocess_throttle`, `degradation_cascade`, `diff_evidence`, `allocation_budget` entries and no allowlist lines; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --features experimental` green; all block success criteria verified: `budget_controller_grapa_adapts_lambda`, `guardrails_detect_allocation_drift`, `teardown_sequence_identical_native_vs_crossterm` (PTY), presenter seam complete. For KEEP EXPERIMENTAL verdicts: README rows say "superseded by <X>"; nothing deleted.

## Implementation plan

1. Confirm all six sibling beads are closed and `g13-decision` has verdicts; run the gate and paste its JSON summary into this bead.
2. Per DELETE pair (order: ledger, ladder, alloc, eprocess): `git rm crates/ftui-runtime/src/<module>.rs` (+ dedicated tests; + `evidence_bridges.rs` with the throttle if permitted); hand-edit mixed test files to drop the sections (no scripts); remove the `pub mod` lines; drop the `CascadeConfig` field in `policy_config.rs` (and its TOML key; update `tests/slo_yaml_validation.rs`/`policy_e2e.rs` fixtures if they carry the key); `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --features experimental`; commit with the quoted permission.
3. README: remove the rows; adjust :952-973 (applications list: "Budget degradation decisions (BudgetController with GRAPA)", "Allocation leak alerts (FrameGuardrails)"), :1004-1012 (CUSUM: "in `FrameGuardrails` via `AllocLeakDetector`"), :1388 note; AGENTS.md architecture diagram: "Output Layer: BackendPresenter (TerminalPresenter over TerminalWriter; WebPresenter)" if G06 has not already rewritten it.
4. Run the block's tests and the PTY identity test (`g13-e2e`) once more on the final tree; record run ids.
5. Gates, `ubs`, `br` updates.

What NOT to do: no deletion without the verdict; no "temporary" re-exports of deleted names; no README claims beyond what the sibling beads proved.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs`, `src/policy_config.rs`, the deleted module files and their tests (per verdict).
- `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`: reconciled sections.
- `docs/module-reachability-allowlist.txt`: no entries for these modules (assert).

## Success criteria

title: epic(G21): Truthful SOS barrier provenance; compile orphan aggregator/CMS; exercise in action_timeline
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:2435-2457 "## SOS Barrier Certificates" states: "Frame-budget admissibility is checked using a **sum-of-squares (SOS) polynomial barrier certificate**, precomputed offline via semidefinite programming ... B(x₁, x₂) = Σ cᵢⱼ x₁ⁱ x₂ʲ (polynomial, degree ≤ 6) ... The polynomial coefficients are solved by `scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py` using SOS/SDP relaxation. The Rust evaluator (`sos_barrier.rs`) is 257 lines and runs in constant time per frame". The reality check (Section 1, Section 2.2.B, V19) found: `scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py` does not exist and never existed in git history (`git log --all -- scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py` is empty); `crates/ftui-runtime/src/sos_barrier_coeffs.rs` says "Auto-generated by scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py / Generated: 2026-03-05T23:36:24Z / Polynomial degree: 4" over 15 hand-typed round constants (0.0, -0.5, -0.1, 1.0, -0.3, 0.1, -0.15, 0.05, 0.02) introduced in commit b48eab99 (2026-03-05, "add SOS barrier certificates, CEGIS synthesis, e-graph optimizer, ..."); the evaluator (`sos_barrier.rs`, 257 lines: `evaluate` :50, `safety_margin` :103, `is_admissible` :109) is not used for frame admissibility anywhere in `Program`. Separately, two runtime source files are orphaned: `timeline_aggregator.rs` (990 lines, "Sketch-Based Aggregation + Change-Point Alerts", bd-11ck.7) and `countmin_sketch.rs` (1,022 lines, "Count-Min Sketch with PAC-Bayes error budgeting for action timeline aggregation") are not declared in `lib.rs`; README's PAC-Bayes claim (V21) points at them.

The provenance claim is the most serious kind of README error in the audit: it asserts a reproducible scientific artifact that was never produced. This epic makes the header truthful, puts the owner's choice (write the real solver, or declare the constants hand-chosen and experimental) in a decision bead, gates the barrier as experimental (G07), compiles the two orphans under the feature, and wires the aggregator into the `action_timeline` showcase screen (under the feature) so the PAC-Bayes CMS has one exercised consumer. Serves V19, V21, Section 2.2.B, and the README truth goal.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/sos_barrier_coeffs.rs` (45 lines): header :1-12; `BARRIER_DEGREE: usize = 4` :15; `BARRIER_N_TERMS: usize = 15` :18; `BARRIER_COEFFS: [f64; 15]` :24-40 with the values above (monomial order i=0..=4, j=0..=4-i); `BARRIER_VERIFICATION_POINTS: usize = 8` :44 ("Verification results from offline SDP solver"). README says degree ≤ 6; file says 4.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/sos_barrier.rs` (257 lines): `BarrierResult` :28, `evaluate(budget_remaining, change_rate) -> BarrierResult` :50, `safety_margin` :103, `is_admissible` :109. Referenced by `tests/e2e_sos_barrier.rs` (emits `sos_barrier_eval` events :68), `tests/sos_barrier_integration.rs`, `tests/e2e_recipe_b_tail_safe.rs`; not by `program.rs`. `sos_barrier_coeffs` is not in the `lib.rs` `pub mod` list (:28-97); it is declared privately (verify the exact `mod` line with `rg -n sos_barrier_coeffs crates/ftui-runtime/src`).
- `timeline_aggregator.rs`: `AggregatorConfig` :61, `AggregationEvidence` :98, `AggregatorStats` :123, `TimelineAggregator` :300 (`new` :330, `observe<T: Hash>(..)` :351, `stats` :425, `estimate` :434, `current_evidence` :439, `reset` :486, `calibrate` :499); depends on BOCPD and conformal alerting per its header :3-30. `countmin_sketch.rs`: `SketchConfig` :68 (PAC-Bayes calibration default true :77), `ErrorEvidence` :101 (`pac_bayes_kl_term` :119, `error_bound` :124, `summary` :129), `SketchStats` :143, `CountMinSketch` :168 (`new` :195, `with_dimensions` :225, `increment` :247, `add` :252). A second `CountMinSketch` exists in `crates/ftui-text/src/width_cache.rs:807` (TinyLFU admission); different crate, no clash.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/action_timeline.rs` (1,707 lines): `TimelineEvent` :146, `ActionTimeline` :157 with `tick_count` :168, `tick(&mut self, tick_count)` :873 generating bursts every `EVENT_BURST_EVERY`; counts events per kind/component/severity with plain counters; snapshots `action_timeline_{after_ticks,clear_filters,details_collapsed,end_key,filter_component,filter_kind,filter_severity,follow_off}_120x40.snap`; PTY `tests/e2e/scripts/test_action_timeline.sh`.
- `g07-impl` gates `sos_barrier`, `timeline_aggregator`, `countmin_sketch` under `experimental` and fixes their compilation.

## Target state

Header of `sos_barrier_coeffs.rs` is truthful (either "Generated by scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py (cvxpy + SCS) from sos_barrier_spec.toml; regenerate with ..." and the file is byte-identical to the script's output in CI, or "Hand-chosen coefficients, 2026-03-05 (commit b48eab99). No solver was run. Experimental: not used for frame admissibility."); the README section says the same; the barrier module is experimental; the two orphans compile under the feature with tests; `action_timeline` renders an "Aggregate" pane backed by `TimelineAggregator` when built with the showcase `experimental` feature, with a snapshot under that feature.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `sos_barrier_coeffs.rs` header matches the owner's route; `scripts/check_readme_claims.py` (G06) has a ledger row for the README sentence whose proof is either the script + CI byte-identity step or the truthful header line.
- [ ] Script route only: `python3 scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py --spec crates/ftui-runtime/sos_barrier_spec.toml --out /tmp/coeffs.rs && diff /tmp/coeffs.rs crates/ftui-runtime/src/sos_barrier_coeffs.rs` exits 0 in a CI step.
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-runtime --features experimental timeline_aggregator countmin_sketch` green.
- [ ] Snapshot `action_timeline_aggregate_pane_120x40.snap` (feature-gated test) shows sketch estimates and a change-point alert after a burst.
- [ ] Reachability gate: `timeline_aggregator` and `countmin_sketch` EXPERIMENTAL (not allowlisted, not orphaned).

## Implementation plan (child beads)

1. `g21-decision`: script route vs hand-chosen constants (owner).
2. `g21-impl`: truthful header; gating confirmation; aggregator pane in `action_timeline` under the feature; (script route) the solver script + spec + CI step.
3. `g21-tests`: coefficient/evaluator consistency tests; aggregator and CMS tests; snapshot.
4. `g21-docs`: README SOS section and ledger rows; experimental table rows.

## Dependencies and ordering

- `g21-impl` blocked by `g07-impl` (feature flag and orphan compilation) and `g21-decision`.
- Unblocks: `g06-impl` ledger rows V19/V21.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Default recommendation (from the reality check): hand-chosen + experimental, because nothing consumes the barrier for admissibility and G11/G13 make `ConformalPredictor` + `BudgetController` the admissibility mechanism; writing an SDP solver for an unused certificate is effort without a consumer.
- If the owner wants the script route, the spec must pin the safe/unsafe regions and the degree (4, matching the file; README's "≤ 6" is corrected either way), and CI needs `cvxpy`/`scs` installed in the `docs` or `check` job (a Python dependency the repo does not have today).
- The aggregator pane is additive (only under the feature) so the default showcase snapshots do not change.

## Definition of done

Child beads closed; header truthful; orphans compiled and tested; aggregator exercised under the feature; README section matches; close reason names the route chosen and the test/snapshot names.

title: question(G21): SOS coefficients: hand-chosen + experimental (Route A) or solver script with CI diff (Route B)
description:
## Context and why this matters

`crates/ftui-runtime/src/sos_barrier_coeffs.rs:1-12` claims the constants were "Auto-generated by scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py" on 2026-03-05; the script never existed in git history and the constants are round hand-typed numbers (commit b48eab99). README.md:2435-2457 repeats the claim ("solved by `scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py` using SOS/SDP relaxation"). The reality check (G21) says the fix is an owner decision between two routes, and defaults to the cheaper one. This `question` bead (priority 1) records the owner's choice so `g21-impl` can proceed. It is not a deletion question; nothing is deleted on either route.

## Current state (evidence)

- `sos_barrier_coeffs.rs`: `BARRIER_DEGREE = 4` :15, `BARRIER_N_TERMS = 15` :18, `BARRIER_COEFFS` :24-40 = [0.0, 0.0, -0.5, 0.0, -0.1, 1.0, 0.0, -0.3, 0.0, 0.1, 0.0, -0.15, 0.05, 0.0, 0.02] (monomials x1^i x2^j, i=0..=4, j=0..=4-i), `BARRIER_VERIFICATION_POINTS = 8` :44.
- `sos_barrier.rs`: `evaluate` :50 (B > 0 safe per the file header :10-12; note the README says "B(x) ≤ 0 ⟹ admissible", the opposite sign convention: README.md:2447-2449 vs `sos_barrier_coeffs.rs:10-12`; whichever route is chosen, the docs must agree with `is_admissible` :109).
- No consumer for admissibility in `program.rs`; tests `tests/e2e_sos_barrier.rs`, `tests/sos_barrier_integration.rs`, `tests/e2e_recipe_b_tail_safe.rs` exercise the evaluator.
- G11 (`ConformalPredictor`, default on) and G13 (`BudgetController` with GRAPA) are the admissibility mechanisms that actually run.

## Question for the owner

Choose one:

**Route A (recommended, S): hand-chosen + experimental.** The header is rewritten to state the truth ("Hand-chosen coefficients, 2026-03-05, commit b48eab99; no solver was run; experimental; not used for frame admissibility"); the README section says the same and links "Experimental modules"; the constants stay so the existing tests keep passing; the barrier is not wired.

**Route B (M): real solver.** `scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py` is written (cvxpy + SCS; spec in `crates/ftui-runtime/sos_barrier_spec.toml` pinning degree 4, the safe set {x1 in [0.3, 1], x2 in [0, 0.6]}, the unsafe set {x1 in [0, 0.15]} u {x2 in [0.85, 1]}, and a decrease condition along a documented vector field), regenerates `sos_barrier_coeffs.rs` byte-identically (deterministic solver settings and rounding to 6 decimals), a CI step diffs the regenerated file, and the `BARRIER_VERIFICATION_POINTS` become real solver residuals. The current hand-typed constants are replaced by solver output (values will change; tests that assert specific margins must be updated to assert properties instead). Still experimental unless the owner also wants it wired as a third admissibility gate (not recommended: two gates already exist).

Please answer "Route A" or "Route B" in this bead's comments, and for Route B confirm that adding Python dependencies (`cvxpy`, `scs`) to a CI job is acceptable.

## Target state

The answer recorded; `g21-impl` scoped accordingly (its plan has both routes).

## Success criteria

- [ ] Owner answer in the bead comments.
- [ ] `g21-impl` close reason quotes the answer.

## Tests and logging

- None (decision).

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: nothing.
- Blocks: `g21-impl` (route selection), `g21-docs` (wording).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Route A costs nothing and removes a false provenance claim immediately; Route B produces a real artifact for a module with no consumer.
- A third option, deleting the barrier module, belongs on `g07-decision`'s list if the owner prefers it; it is not proposed there today because the README dedicates a section to it.

## Definition of done

Answer recorded; bead closed with the answer as the close reason.
close_reason: Decision: Route A. The coefficients are hand-chosen (no solver ever existed in the repo or its history); the header now says so and the module stays experimental until G07 gates it. Route B (solver script + CI diff) rejected: no SDP solver dependency is justified for a module with no production caller.

title: task(G21): Truthful sos_barrier_coeffs header per route; TimelineAggregator pane in action_timeline
description:
## Context and why this matters

Two truthfulness fixes and one wiring: (1) `sos_barrier_coeffs.rs` carries a false "Auto-generated by scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py" provenance header (the script never existed; constants hand-typed in commit b48eab99); (2) `timeline_aggregator.rs` and `countmin_sketch.rs` are not compiled at all (no `pub mod` in `lib.rs`), so the README's PAC-Bayes CMS claim (V21) points at dead files; (3) the `action_timeline` showcase screen counts events with plain counters and could exercise the aggregator (sketch estimates + BOCPD change-point alerts) under the experimental feature. This bead implements the route chosen in `g21-decision` (default Route A), confirms the gating from `g07-impl`, and adds the aggregator pane. Serves V19, V21, Section 2.2.B.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/sos_barrier_coeffs.rs` (45 lines): header :1-12 ("Auto-generated by scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py", "Generated: 2026-03-05T23:36:24Z", "Polynomial degree: 4", properties "B(x) > 0 in safe region, B(x) <= 0 at/beyond unsafe boundary"); constants :15-44. `git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short -- crates/ftui-runtime/src/sos_barrier_coeffs.rs | tail -1` = `b48eab99 2026-03-05 feat(doctor,runtime,render,widgets): add SOS barrier certificates, CEGIS synthesis, e-graph optimizer, quotient filter, drift visualization, and bounded thread join`. `ls scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py`: missing; `git log --all --oneline -- scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py`: empty.
- `sos_barrier.rs`: `evaluate` :50, `safety_margin` :103, `is_admissible` :109; consumers are three test files only.
- After `g07-impl`: `lib.rs` has `#[cfg(feature = "experimental")] pub mod sos_barrier;`, `... pub mod timeline_aggregator;`, `... pub mod countmin_sketch;` and both orphans compile.
- `timeline_aggregator.rs` API: `AggregatorConfig` :61, `TimelineAggregator::new(config)` :330, `observe<T: Hash>(&mut self, category: &T, ...)` :351 (read the full signature: it takes a timestamp or count), `stats()` :425 -> `AggregatorStats` :123, `estimate(&category)` :434, `current_evidence()` :439 -> `AggregationEvidence` :98, `calibrate(&category, true_count)` :499. `countmin_sketch.rs`: `CountMinSketch::with_dimensions(width, depth)` :225, `increment` :247, `add` :252, `ErrorEvidence::error_bound` :124.
- `action_timeline.rs`: `TimelineEvent` :146, `ActionTimeline` :157 (`tick_count` :168; event generation in `tick` :873 every `EVENT_BURST_EVERY` ticks; counters per kind/component/severity used by the filter bar); layout code renders a list plus a details panel; snapshots at 120x40 listed in the epic.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml` features: `debug-render`, `caps-probe`, `native-backend`, `crossterm-compat`, `clipboard`, `image`, `logging`, `screen-mermaid`, `test-support`; no `experimental`.

## Target state

Route A (default): `sos_barrier_coeffs.rs:1-12` replaced by:
```
// Hand-chosen barrier coefficients (2026-03-05, commit b48eab99).
// No solver was run to produce these values; they were typed by hand as a
// plausible degree-4 polynomial for the (budget_remaining, change_rate) state.
// Status: experimental. Not used for frame admissibility (see ConformalPredictor
// and BudgetController). The `BARRIER_VERIFICATION_POINTS` below are hand-checked
// evaluations of this polynomial, not SDP residuals.
```
plus the unchanged constants; README wording via `g21-docs`. Route B: the script, spec, regenerated file, and CI diff step (details in the plan). Both routes: the showcase gains `experimental = ["ftui-runtime/experimental"]`; `action_timeline` gets an additive "Aggregate" pane (visible only with the feature) showing, per event kind, the CMS estimate vs exact count, the PAC-Bayes error bound, and the BOCPD change-point alert state from `TimelineAggregator`, fed from the same `tick` that generates events.

## Implementation plan

1. Route A: rewrite the header comment (lines 1-12) as above; keep constants; add a doc comment on `BARRIER_VERIFICATION_POINTS` :44 saying "hand-checked". Route B: write `scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py` (argparse `--spec`, `--out`, `--seed`; cvxpy SOS program: B in Σ[x] with degree 4, B - ε ∈ Σ on the safe set via Putinar multipliers, -B ∈ Σ on the unsafe set, and the decrease condition on the boundary; SCS with fixed `max_iters`, `eps`; print the file with the same layout as today, rounding to 6 decimals), `crates/ftui-runtime/sos_barrier_spec.toml`, regenerate, update tests in `sos_barrier.rs`/`tests/sos_barrier_integration.rs` that assert specific values to assert properties (`B > 0` on sampled safe points, `B <= 0` on sampled unsafe points), and add a CI step in the `docs` job (`pip install cvxpy scs` then regenerate + `diff`).
2. Confirm gating: `rg -n -B1 'pub mod (sos_barrier|timeline_aggregator|countmin_sketch)' crates/ftui-runtime/src/lib.rs` shows the `#[cfg(feature = "experimental")]` lines; `sos_barrier_coeffs` is declared inside `sos_barrier.rs` (or gated alongside it).
3. Showcase `Cargo.toml`: `experimental = ["ftui-runtime/experimental"]`.
4. `action_timeline.rs`: under `#[cfg(feature = "experimental")]` add field `aggregator: TimelineAggregator` (config: sketch width 256, depth 4, PAC-Bayes on, BOCPD hazard from `AggregatorConfig::default()`), feed `observe(&event.kind, ..)` in `tick` :873 for each generated event, and render the pane in the details column when `self.show_aggregate` (toggle key `a`, listed in the screen's key help); without the feature the screen is unchanged (no stub pane, no placeholder text: the field and pane simply do not exist).
5. Tests: `g21-tests`.
6. Gates: `cargo check -p ftui-demo-showcase` with and without `--features experimental`; clippy both ways; fmt; `ubs`.

What NOT to do: no wiring of the barrier into `Program`; no "regenerated" claim without the script; no `action_timeline_v2`; no placeholder pane when the feature is off.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/sos_barrier_coeffs.rs`: header (Route A) or regenerated content (Route B).
- Route B only: `scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py` (new), `crates/ftui-runtime/sos_barrier_spec.toml` (new), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` step, tests in `sos_barrier.rs` and `tests/sos_barrier_integration.rs`.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml`: `experimental` feature.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/action_timeline.rs`: aggregator field + pane (feature-gated).
