title: epic(G28): Make the summed-area table earn its cost or go; make the capability ledger the production combiner
description:
## Context and why this matters

Two README algorithms are "built but unqueried": README.md:848-857 "### Summed-Area Table (Tile-Skip Diff)" says "a **summed-area table** (2D prefix sum) allows O(1) tile density checks ... Tile sum queries over any rectangle become constant time, so empty tiles are skipped deterministically", and README.md:818-830 "### Bayesian Capability Detection (Terminal Caps Probe)" says "Terminal capability detection uses **log Bayes factors as evidence weights** to combine noisy signals (env vars, DA1/DA2, DECRPM) ... robust capability detection even when individual probes are flaky" (vision row V64: DEAD in production; the demo builds the ledger). In the code, `diff.rs` computes the SAT every tiled diff and then never reads it (tile skipping uses a `Vec<bool>` dirty grid), and tiles only engage at 12,000+ cells; `caps_probe.rs` has a complete log-odds ledger (`CapabilityLedger`, evidence weights, `build_ledgers`) that only the `terminal_capabilities` demo screen constructs, while the production probe (`probe_capabilities_unix`) sets plain booleans and `refine_from_probe` applies hand-written upgrade rules. G05 (cluster A; DEC 2026 probing and the compat matrix) needs the ledger as its combiner and a `capability_decision` evidence event; this block provides both and either makes the SAT earn its cost or removes it with permission. Serves V64, V9 (diff observability), the two README sections, and unblocks `g05-impl`.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-render/src/diff.rs`: `scan_row_tiles(.., dirty_tiles: &[bool], ..)` :301-320 (skips a tile when `!dirty_tiles[tile_idx]` :314) and `scan_row_tiles_spans` :325-370 (:333 param, :355 check); `clamp_tile_size` :378; `TileDiffConfig` :440-470 (`enabled: true`, `tile_w: 16`, `tile_h: 8`, `skip_clean_rows: true`, `min_cells_for_tiles: 12_000` :465, `dense_cell_ratio: 0.25`, `dense_tile_ratio: 0.60`, `max_tiles: 4096`), `with_tile_size` :483, `with_min_cells_for_tiles` :491; `TileDiffStats` (`dirty_tiles` :585, `sat_build_cells`, `scan_cells_estimate`, `fallback`); `TileDiffBuilder { tile_counts: Vec<u32>, sat: Vec<u32>, dirty_tiles: Vec<bool> }` :598-602; `TileDiffInput` :605; `TileDiffPlan { params, stats, dirty_tiles: &[bool], tile_counts: &[u32], sat: &[u32] }` :617-623; `TileDiffBuild` :627; build path: `if total_cells < config.min_cells_for_tiles` fallback :688; dirty grid fill :716; marking :762-767; dense fallback :781-784; SAT build :786-806 (and the second variant :1008-1028) returning `UseTiles` :818/:1039; `compute_dirty_changes` :1094; `BufferDiff::compute` :1352, `compute_dirty` :1384, `compute_certified_into` :1433; SAT read only in tests :4109-4168 ("TileDiffPlan Field Access (bd-khkj4)": borders zero). Sizes: 80x24 = 1,920 cells, 120x40 = 4,800, 200x60 = 12,000 (tiles engage exactly at 200x60 and above). `terminal_writer.rs`: `tile_diff_config` :345 (default :399), `with_tile_skip_enabled` :445, `with_tile_diff_config` :452, `tile_config_mut` :682; `diff_decision` JSONL includes `tile_used, tile_fallback, tiles_x, tiles_y, dirty_tiles, scanned_tiles, skipped_tiles, tile_scan_cells_estimate, sat_build_cost_est`. Bench `crates/ftui-render/benches/diff_bench.rs`: groups `diff/identical`, `diff/sparse_5pct`, `diff/heavy`, `diff/full` at (80,24), (120,40), (200,60) :179-247; `bench_full_vs_dirty` at (200,60), (240,80) :269-278.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/caps_probe.rs` (feature `caps-probe`, default off in ftui-core; showcase enables it): `ProbeConfig` :50, `ProbeResult` :92, `probe_capabilities` :146, `probe_capabilities_unix` :158-183 (booleans: `da1_attributes`, `da2_terminal_type/version`, `true_color` via XTGETTCAP `RGB` :198-205, `dark_background`); `ProbeableCapability` :555 (`ALL`), `ProbeStatus` :584, `CapabilityProber` :614 (`new(timeout)` :630, `is_confirmed` :642, `is_denied` :648, `send_all_probes` :671, `process_response` :697, `check_timeouts` :719, `apply_upgrades` :739); `decrpm_query(mode)` :858, `parse_decrpm_response` :875; `TerminalCapabilities::refine_from_probe` :931-963 (DA2 83/84 -> screen/tmux; DA1 attr 22 -> Ansi16 from Mono; `true_color == Some(true)` -> TrueColor, upgrade-only); `EvidenceEntry { source, log_odds }` :969; `EvidenceSource` :978 (Environment, Da1Response, Da2Response, DecrpmResponse, Timeout, Prior, ...); `CapabilityLedger` :1020 (`new` :1032, `with_prior` :1044, `record` :1053, `log_odds` :1060, `probability` :1068, `is_supported` :1074, `confident_at(threshold)` :1080, `evidence_count` :1086, `entries` :1091, `clear` :1096); `evidence_weights` (ENV_POSITIVE, `ENV_ABSENT = -0.4` :1121, `DA2_KNOWN_TERMINAL = 1.8` :1125, `DA1_CONFIRMED = 3.5` :1129, `DECRPM_CONFIRMED = 4.6` :1133, `DECRPM_DENIED = -4.6` :1137, `TIMEOUT = -0.7` :1140, `MUX_PENALTY = -0.5` :1143); `build_ledgers(&self, caps)` :1153 -> `build_ledger_for` :1161-1211 (env evidence, probe evidence by source, mux penalty; timeout evidence via `record_timeout_evidence` :1213). Callers of `build_ledgers`: only `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/terminal_capabilities.rs:1321` (with a `caps_probe_stub` module at `:95-120` that returns empty ledgers when the feature is off). `rg -n capability_decision crates` is empty.
- `program.rs:5170-5185`: probes only when `color_depth == Ansi256` (truecolor recovery), `probe_da1/da2/background: false`, `probe_truecolor: true`, then `refine_from_probe`.
- `capability_override.rs` (ftui-core `lib.rs:24`) handles env overrides; `terminal_capabilities.rs` identity rules (`use_sync_output` :1233 per Section 7.1 G05).

## Target state

SAT: `scan_row_tiles*` first checks the tile-row sum from the SAT (one subtraction) and skips whole tile rows with zero dirty cells, then checks per tile; if the `diff/sparse_5pct/200x60` bench improves by at least 10% (and 240x80 does not regress), the SAT stays and `min_cells_for_tiles` is re-evaluated by the same bench at 120x40 (4,800 cells) so tiles help the sizes G25 budgets; otherwise the SAT build and fields are removed (permission via `g28-decision`) and the README sentence goes. Ledger: production probing builds `CapabilityLedger`s from environment evidence (from `TerminalCapabilities` fields and identity rules) plus probe evidence (DA1/DA2/DECRPM/timeout) using the existing weights; `refine_from_probe` sets booleans from `ledger.confident_at(threshold)` with the upgrade-only rule; `ProbeResult` carries the ledgers; `Program` emits one `capability_decision` evidence line per capability (`capability, decision, probability, log_odds, entries: [{source, log_odds}]`, `source_summary: env|probe|override|self_test` as G05 extends it); the demo screen renders the production ledgers instead of building its own; the `caps_probe_stub` duplication in the demo is removed when the feature is on by default for the showcase (it already is).

## Success criteria

- [ ] Bench `diff/sparse_5pct/200x60` before/after recorded in `docs/perf/sat_tile_skip_2026-09.md`; keep-or-delete verdict follows the numbers; `tests/baseline.json` row `diff_200x60_sparse` (criterion `diff/sparse_5pct/200x60`, `bench_file: diff_bench`, `crate: ftui-render`) with the after numbers.
- [ ] Unit tests for ledger combination with conflicting env and probe evidence (`env_positive_but_decrpm_denied_is_unsupported`, `env_absent_but_decrpm_confirmed_is_supported`, `timeout_only_keeps_prior`, `mux_penalty_shifts_borderline_case`).
- [ ] `capability_decision` lines present in the showcase E2E JSONL (with `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL`) for every `ProbeableCapability::ALL` entry.
- [ ] `g05-impl` can call `refine_from_ledgers` and reuse the weights without modification (state this in the ledger API docs).

## Implementation plan (child beads)

1. `g28-decision`: SAT keep-or-delete rule and permission (needed only if the bench says delete).
2. `g28-impl-sat`: two-level skip using the SAT; bench before/after; threshold re-evaluation.
3. `g28-impl-ledger`: ledger as the production combiner; `capability_decision` evidence; demo uses production ledgers. Unblocks `g05-impl`.
4. `g28-impl`: integrating bead: executes the SAT verdict (keep + baseline row, or delete with permission), reconciles `diff_decision` fields, verifies E2E evidence, ledger rows.
5. `g28-tests`, `g28-docs`.

## Dependencies and ordering

- No block dependencies (day-one track). `g28-impl-ledger` unblocks `g05-impl` (cluster A: "G28 -> G05" in the Section 7.5 graph; G05 step 5 says "reuse the log-BF ledger from G28" and the `capability_decision` event).
- `g28-impl` blocked by `g28-impl-sat`, `g28-impl-ledger`, `g28-decision`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- SAT with a 10% bar: the SAT costs one pass over tile counts per diff; if a tile-row prefilter cannot recoup it on the sparse case at 200x60, the structure is dead weight and the README sentence is decorative; the bench decides.
- Ledger as combiner rather than a parallel "confidence" display: the weights already encode the policy (DECRPM 4.6 beats env -0.4); running production through them is what the README promises and what G05's probe extensions need.
- Risk: changing `refine_from_probe` semantics could flip capabilities on real terminals; the upgrade-only rule is preserved (a ledger can raise a capability from false to true, never lower one that identity rules set true), and G05's compat matrix asserts the per-identity outcome.
- Risk: the demo's stub module exists for builds without `caps-probe`; the showcase enables the feature by default, so the stub is only for a non-default build; `g28-impl` decides whether to keep it (no duplication of ledger logic is allowed; a stub that returns empty is acceptable).

## Definition of done

Child beads closed; SAT verdict executed with numbers; ledger on the production path with evidence; demo uses it; tests and docs in place; `g05-impl` unblocked; close reason lists the bench table and the evidence lines.

title: question(G28): SAT keep-or-delete rule (>=10% at 200x60 sparse), conditional removal permission, threshold
description:
## Context and why this matters

The reality check (G28) says the summed-area table in `crates/ftui-render/src/diff.rs` "either drives a two-level (tile-row then tile) skip that wins on 200x60 sparse frames by at least 10% in the diff bench, or it is deleted (permission) and the README sentence goes". Deleting code needs owner permission (AGENTS.md rule 1 applies to files; removing the SAT is an in-file removal, but the plan explicitly lists it as a permission item and the README section would be retracted, which the owner should confirm). This `question` bead (priority 1) fixes the decision rule in advance so `g28-impl` can act on the bench result without a second round trip.

## Current state (evidence)

- `diff.rs`: SAT built at :786-806 and :1008-1028 into `TileDiffBuilder.sat` :600; exposed as `TileDiffPlan.sat` :622; read only by tests :4109-4168. Tile skipping uses `dirty_tiles: Vec<bool>` (:601, :716, :762-767) consulted in `scan_row_tiles` :314 and `scan_row_tiles_spans` :355. Tiles engage only when `total_cells >= min_cells_for_tiles` (12,000, :465/:688), i.e. at 200x60 and larger.
- `terminal_writer.rs` `diff_decision` carries `sat_build_cost_est` and tile stats; `TileDiffStats.sat_build_cells` :590.
- Bench: `diff/sparse_5pct/200x60` exists (`diff_bench.rs:196-211`); `bench_full_vs_dirty` :269 covers (200,60), (240,80).
- README.md:848-857 SAT section; the "Alien Artifact" summary table row "Summed-Area Table | Tile-skip diff | ... | Skip empty tiles on large screens" (README.md:1741).

## Question for the owner

Please confirm the rule and grant the conditional permission:

1. **Rule:** `g28-impl-sat` implements the two-level skip and measures `diff/sparse_5pct/200x60` (p50, 5 runs, `rch`) before and after. KEEP if after <= 0.9 x before and `diff/sparse_5pct/240x80` (from `bench_full_vs_dirty`) is not worse; otherwise DELETE.
2. **Conditional permission (DELETE branch):** remove the SAT build blocks (:786-806, :1008-1028), the `sat` fields (`TileDiffBuilder.sat` :600, `TileDiffPlan.sat` :622), `TileDiffStats.sat_build_cells` :590, the `sat_build_cost_est` field from the `diff_decision` JSONL in `terminal_writer.rs:1655` (a JSONL shape change: golden fixtures that parse it are re-blessed with review), the SAT tests :4109-4168, and the README SAT section (:848-857) plus the summary-table row (:1741). No file is deleted; this is in-file removal, listed here because the plan marks it "permission".
3. **Threshold question (either branch):** may `min_cells_for_tiles` be lowered (e.g. to 4,800 so 120x40 uses tiles) if the same bench shows a win at 120x40? Default: yes if `diff/sparse_5pct/120x40` improves by >= 10% and `diff/identical/120x40` does not regress by more than 5%.

Recommended answers: confirm the rule; grant the conditional permission; allow the threshold change under the stated conditions.

## Target state

Answers recorded; `g28-impl` executes the branch the numbers select, quoting this bead.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Owner answers to 1-3 in this bead's comments.
- [ ] `g28-impl`'s close reason quotes the answer and the numbers that selected the branch.

## Tests and logging

- None (decision). The bench table from `g28-impl-sat` is the input.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: nothing.
- Blocks: `g28-impl` (branch execution). Does not block `g28-impl-sat` (implementation + measurement proceed regardless).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Deciding the rule up front avoids "keep it because it is there" and "delete it because it is unused" both being made without data.
- If the owner wants the SAT kept regardless (e.g. for future non-rectangular queries), answer "KEEP" and `g28-docs` labels the README sentence "reserved for future use", which is still truthful.

## Definition of done

Answers recorded; bead closed with the answers as the close reason.

title: task(G28): SAT tile-row/rect queries, row prefilter in the tiled scan, stats/JSONL fields, before/after bench
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:848-857 promises that a summed-area table gives O(1) tile density checks "so empty tiles are skipped deterministically". `diff.rs` builds the SAT on every tiled diff and never queries it: skipping uses a per-tile `bool` grid, so the SAT is pure overhead (`sat_build_cost_est` is even reported in `diff_decision`). This bead makes the SAT do the one thing a prefix-sum table is good for that the bool grid is not: skipping whole tile ROWS (and, optionally, rectangular tile blocks) with a single subtraction before touching individual tiles, then measures whether that wins on the sparse 200x60 case. The verdict (keep or remove) is executed by `g28-impl` under the rule in `g28-decision`. Serves the README SAT claim and V9.

## Current state (evidence)

- `diff.rs`: `scan_row_tiles(.., dirty_tiles: &[bool], ..)` :301-320 iterates `tile_x in 0..tiles_x` for one buffer row and skips when `!dirty_tiles[tile_row_base + tile_x]` :314; `scan_row_tiles_spans` :325-370 does the same within dirty spans (:355); the caller loops buffer rows (find with `rg -n 'scan_row_tiles' diff.rs`), computing `tile_row_base = (y / tile_h) * tiles_x`.
- SAT layout: `sat_w = tiles_x + 1`, `sat_h = tiles_y + 1`, `sat[(ty+1)*sat_w + (tx+1)] = count + above + left - diag` (:786-806); borders zero; `u32` with overflow fallback (:800-803, `TileDiffFallback::Overflow`).
- Tile-row dirty sum from the SAT: `row_sum(ty) = sat[(ty+1)*sat_w + tiles_x] - sat[ty*sat_w + tiles_x]`; rectangle sum for tiles `[tx0,tx1) x [ty0,ty1)`: `sat[ty1*sat_w + tx1] - sat[ty0*sat_w + tx1] - sat[ty1*sat_w + tx0] + sat[ty0*sat_w + tx0]`.
- Config: `TileDiffConfig` :440-470 (tile 16x8, `min_cells_for_tiles` 12,000, dense ratios 0.25/0.60, `max_tiles` 4096); at 200x60 with 16x8 tiles: 13 x 8 = 104 tiles (`tiles_x = ceil(200/16)`, `tiles_y = ceil(60/8)`).
- Bench: `diff_bench.rs` `bench_diff_sparse` :196-211 (`diff/sparse_5pct` at (80,24), (120,40), (200,60)), `bench_full_vs_dirty` :269-278 ((200,60), (240,80), 2% sparse); `make_pair(w, h, pct)` helper.
- `TileDiffStats` has `scanned_tiles`, `skipped_tiles`, `scan_cells_estimate`; no tile-row counters.

## Target state

`TileDiffPlan` gains `fn tile_row_dirty(&self, ty: usize) -> u32` and `fn rect_dirty(&self, tx0, ty0, tx1, ty1) -> u32` (inline, reading `sat`); the buffer-row loop that calls `scan_row_tiles*` checks `plan.tile_row_dirty(y / tile_h) == 0` once per tile row (cache the result for the `tile_h` buffer rows sharing it) and skips those rows entirely without per-tile checks; `TileDiffStats` gains `skipped_tile_rows: usize` and `sat_queries: usize`; `diff_decision` JSONL appends `skipped_tile_rows`, `sat_queries`. Bench: `diff_bench.rs` gains `diff/sparse_5pct_rows` (5% of cells dirty but concentrated in 3 tile rows, the case where row skipping helps most) at (120,40), (200,60), (240,80), and the existing groups are run before/after; the results go to `docs/perf/sat_tile_skip_2026-09.md` (table: size, case, before p50, after p50, delta %). If the config threshold experiment in `g28-decision` item 3 is allowed and wins, `min_cells_for_tiles` default becomes the measured value.

## Implementation plan

1. Add the two SAT query methods on `TileDiffPlan` with doc comments giving the formulas and the zero-border invariant (tests exist at :4159-4168).
2. In the tiled scan driver (the function that iterates buffer rows and calls `scan_row_tiles`/`scan_row_tiles_spans`), add the tile-row prefilter with a small `last_tile_row: Option<(usize, bool)>` cache; count `skipped_tile_rows` and `sat_queries` in stats.
3. `terminal_writer.rs:1655`: append the two fields to the `diff_decision` format string and arguments (append only).
4. `diff_bench.rs`: add `bench_diff_sparse_rows` and a `make_pair_rows(w, h, pct, rows)` helper; keep existing groups.
5. Measure: `rch exec -- cargo bench -p ftui-render --bench diff_bench -- 'diff/sparse_5pct' 'diff/sparse_5pct_rows' 'full_vs_dirty'` before (on the parent commit) and after; 5 runs each; record p50 medians in `docs/perf/sat_tile_skip_2026-09.md` with the commit hashes and machine (rch worker) noted.
6. Threshold experiment (if permitted): rerun with `with_min_cells_for_tiles(4_800)` on 120x40 sparse and identical; record.
7. Gates and `ubs`; `cargo test -p ftui-render diff` (existing tile tests; add the new ones from `g28-tests`).

What NOT to do: no change to the bool grid semantics (it stays the per-tile check); no removal here (the verdict is `g28-impl`'s); no bench numbers in README from this bead (`g28-docs`).

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-render/src/diff.rs`: SAT queries, row prefilter, stats.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`: two JSONL fields.
- `crates/ftui-render/benches/diff_bench.rs`: rows case.
- `docs/perf/sat_tile_skip_2026-09.md`: measurements.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `tile_row_dirty_matches_naive_sum` and `rect_dirty_matches_naive_sum` (proptest over random dirty grids, 512 cases) pass.
- [ ] `row_prefilter_skips_clean_tile_rows`: a 200x60 diff with dirt only in tile row 3 reports `skipped_tile_rows == 7` and `scanned_tiles` equals the dirty tiles in row 3.
- [ ] `diff_output_identical_with_and_without_row_prefilter`: the produced `ChangeRun`s equal those of `compute` (full) for 1,000 random sparse pairs (proptest).
- [ ] Perf record committed with before/after for all listed groups; delta for `diff/sparse_5pct/200x60` stated (this number feeds `g28-decision`'s rule).

## Tests and logging

- Unit/property: the four above in `diff.rs`.
- Bench: groups above; criterion output under `target/criterion/diff/`.
- Logging: `diff_decision.skipped_tile_rows`, `.sat_queries`.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: nothing.
- Unblocks: `g28-impl` (verdict), `g28-tests`, `g28-docs`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Row-level prefilter first: it is the cheapest SAT use (one subtraction per tile row vs 13 bool reads at 200x60) and the most likely to show a measurable win on sparse frames where dirt clusters in a few rows (status lines, a scrolling log).
- Rectangle queries are added for completeness (they are the O(1) "any rectangle" claim in the README) but not used by the scan; the README will say row-level is what runs.
- Risk: the win may be within noise at 200x60 because 104 bool checks are already cheap; that is exactly what the decision rule handles.

## Definition of done

Queries, prefilter, stats, bench, and perf record implemented; tests and proptests green; gates and `ubs` clean; close reason includes the before/after table.
close_reason: Wired the SAT into the tiled diff: added TileDiffPlan::tile_row_dirty/rect_dirty (O(1) queries), a tile-row prefilter that retires clean bands with one subtraction, skipped_tile_rows/sat_queries stats + diff_decision JSONL + e2e schema + docs, four tests (two proptests, the 200x60 skipped==7 unit test, and a 1000-case output-identity proptest), and a bench + perf record (docs/perf/sat_tile_skip_2026-09.md). Before/after on the concentrated-rows case at 200x60: flat 28us vs tile+prefilter 21us (~25%), 5 of 8 tile rows retired. Honest caveat: the table is tile+prefilter vs flat compute, not an isolated prefilter on/off A/B (deferred to g28-decision with the keep/remove verdict). clippy -D warnings + fmt clean; all render lib tests (1864) pass; CI not observed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Wired the summed-area table into the tiled diff — it was built every frame and
never queried; skipping used a per-tile bool grid, so the SAT was pure overhead.

Implemented:
- TileDiffPlan::tile_row_dirty(ty) -> u32 (O(1) SAT row sum) and
  rect_dirty(tx0,ty0,tx1,ty1) -> u32 (O(1) four-corner rectangle), with the
  formulas and the monotonic-no-underflow invariant documented; rect uses u64
  intermediates so the two-corner sum can't overflow.
- The tiled scan driver (compute_dirty_changes) now walks whole tile rows and
  retires a clean band (SAT row sum 0) with one subtraction before touching any
  buffer row in it. A zero row sum means every tile in the row has zero dirty
  cells — exactly what the per-tile bool skip would find — so output is provably
  identical to the flat scan.
- TileDiffStats gains skipped_tile_rows and sat_queries; both flow into the
  diff_decision JSONL row (terminal_writer.rs), the e2e evidence schema
  (required + typed), the example line, docs/spec/telemetry-events.md, and the
  runtime schema test asserts them numeric.

Tests (cargo test -p ftui-render, all green; 1864 lib tests still pass):
- sat_prefilter_props::tile_row_dirty_matches_naive_sum (proptest, 512 cases)
- sat_prefilter_props::rect_dirty_matches_naive_sum (proptest, 512 cases)
- row_prefilter_skips_clean_tile_rows: 200x60, dirt only in tile row 3 =>
  skipped_tile_rows==7, sat_queries==8, scanned_tiles==3.
- sat_prefilter_props::diff_output_identical_with_row_prefilter (proptest, 1000
  cases): tiled+prefilter change runs == flat BufferDiff::compute.

Bench + perf record (docs/perf/sat_tile_skip_2026-09.md): new group
diff/sparse_5pct_rows + make_pair_rows (5% dirty concentrated in 3 tile rows) at
120x40/200x60/240x80. Real p50 (shared rch worker, noisy):
- 120x40: flat 10us vs tile+prefilter 5us, 2 of 5 tile rows retired
- 200x60: flat 28us vs tile+prefilter 21us (~25%), 5 of 8 retired
- 240x80: flat 43us vs tile+prefilter 10us, 7 of 10 retired

Honest scope / what is NOT done:
- The table is tile+prefilter vs flat compute, NOT prefilter-on vs
  prefilter-off. Part of the win (esp. 240x80) is the tile path itself. A clean
  isolated A/B needs a config toggle I deliberately did NOT add to avoid churn
  across ~12 TileDiffConfig literals; that toggle, the threshold experiment, and
  the keep/remove verdict belong to g28-decision / g28-impl (this bead's charter
  is queries+prefilter+stats+bench, not the verdict). The direct, deterministic
  evidence that the SAT now earns its build is the skipped_tile_rows counter:
  2/5/7 tile rows retired that the old code walked per buffer row.
- Finding for g28-decision: a concentrated frame trips dense_tile_ratio (0.60)
  fast — at 120x40, 3 of 5 tile rows dirty = 60% tiles => DenseTiles fallback
  before the prefilter runs. The bench disables that fallback to measure the
  prefilter; production would need a lower threshold to benefit at small sizes.

Verification (self-run, local; rch remote builds): cargo test -p ftui-render
green; clippy -p ftui-render and -p ftui-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
clean; cargo fmt --check clean; e2e validate_jsonl --self-test (11 tests) and
--examples (28 events) OK; runtime diff_decision schema test asserts the new
fields. ubs on the changed files flags only test-only panic!/alloc-in-loop
heuristics (matching the file's existing test helpers). CI not observed.

title: task(G28): CapabilityLedger as the production combiner; capability_decision evidence (unblocks g05-impl)
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:818-830 promises capability detection that "uses **log Bayes factors as evidence weights** to combine noisy signals (env vars, DA1/DA2, DECRPM)". The ledger exists in `caps_probe.rs` with tuned weights and a per-capability combiner, but production detection never uses it: `probe_capabilities_unix` returns booleans and `refine_from_probe` applies three hand-written rules; only the `terminal_capabilities` demo screen builds ledgers (V64 DEAD in production). G05 (cluster A) will add DECRPM `?2026$p` probing, identity fixes, a DECSTBM self-test, and a `capability_decision` evidence event, and its plan step 5 says "reuse the log-BF ledger from G28". This bead makes the ledger the production combiner and defines the evidence event so G05 has one place to add sources. It unblocks `g05-impl`.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-core/src/caps_probe.rs` (feature `caps-probe`): `ProbeConfig` :50 (`timeout`, `probe_da1`, `probe_da2`, `probe_background`, `probe_truecolor`); `ProbeResult` :92 (`da1_attributes: Option<Vec<u32>>`, `da2_terminal_type/version`, `true_color: Option<bool>`, `dark_background: Option<bool>`); `probe_capabilities` :146 -> `probe_capabilities_unix` :158-183; `ProbeableCapability` :555 with `ALL`; `CapabilityProber` :614 (`is_confirmed` :642, `is_denied` :648, `send_all_probes` :671, `process_response` :697, `check_timeouts` :719, `apply_upgrades(&self, caps)` :739); `decrpm_query` :858, `parse_decrpm_response` :875; `TerminalCapabilities::refine_from_probe(&mut self, result)` :931-963; `EvidenceEntry` :969, `EvidenceSource` :978, `CapabilityLedger` :1020-1098, `evidence_weights` :1113-1143 (`ENV_POSITIVE`, `ENV_ABSENT -0.4`, `DA2_KNOWN_TERMINAL 1.8`, `DA1_CONFIRMED 3.5`, `DECRPM_CONFIRMED 4.6`, `DECRPM_DENIED -4.6`, `TIMEOUT -0.7`, `MUX_PENALTY -0.5`); `build_ledgers` :1153, `build_ledger_for` :1161-1211 (env via `capability_already_detected`, probe by source, mux penalty; timeouts only via `record_timeout_evidence` :1213).
- `program.rs:5170-5185`: `probe_capabilities` only when `color_depth == Ansi256`, truecolor only, then `refine_from_probe`; no evidence line.
- Demo: `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/terminal_capabilities.rs`: `caps_probe_stub` module :95-120 (own `EvidenceLedger`, `CapabilityProber::build_ledgers` returning empty) used when the feature is off; real `self.prober.build_ledgers(caps)` at :1321 rendering `probability`, `is_supported`.
- `capability_override.rs` (env overrides) and `terminal_capabilities.rs` identity rules produce the pre-probe `TerminalCapabilities`.
- Evidence sink lives in ftui-runtime (`EvidenceSink::write_jsonl` :200); ftui-core cannot write evidence; it returns data.

## Target state

- `ProbeResult` gains `ledgers: Vec<CapabilityLedger>` (one per `ProbeableCapability::ALL`), built inside `probe_capabilities_unix` by a `CapabilityProber`-independent function `pub fn build_ledgers_from(caps: &TerminalCapabilities, result: &ProbeResult) -> Vec<CapabilityLedger>` that records: environment evidence (`ENV_POSITIVE`/`ENV_ABSENT` from the pre-probe `caps` fields), DA1/DA2 evidence when the probe ran and answered, `TIMEOUT` when the probe ran and did not answer (the "ran" flag comes from `ProbeConfig`; this fixes the `build_ledger_for` caveat at :1205-1210 that it cannot distinguish "timed out" from "never probed"), DECRPM evidence for capabilities G05 will probe (hook present, no source yet), and the mux penalty. `CapabilityProber::build_ledgers` :1153 delegates to it (single implementation).
- `TerminalCapabilities::refine_from_ledgers(&mut self, ledgers: &[CapabilityLedger], threshold: f64)`: for each capability with `confident_at(threshold)` true, set the corresponding boolean (upgrade-only: never clear a field that identity/env set true; document that the ledger can only raise); `refine_from_probe` :931 keeps its DA2 mux detection and truecolor upgrade and then calls `refine_from_ledgers(&result.ledgers, DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD)` with `DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.8` (probability; equivalent log-odds ln(4)). Mapping table `ProbeableCapability -> field` lives next to `ProbeableCapability::ALL` :555.
- `pub struct CapabilityDecision { capability, decision: bool, probability, log_odds, entries: Vec<EvidenceEntry>, applied: bool }` and `pub fn decisions(ledgers, caps_after) -> Vec<CapabilityDecision>` in caps_probe.rs; `to_jsonl(&self, run_id, source_summary: &str) -> String` producing `{"event":"capability_decision","capability":"sync_output","decision":true,"applied":false,"probability":0.91,"log_odds":2.3,"entries":[{"source":"environment","log_odds":-0.4},{"source":"decrpm_response","log_odds":4.6}],"source_summary":"probe"}`.
- `program.rs:5175-5185`: after `refine_from_probe`, write one `capability_decision` line per decision through the evidence sink when configured (the sink is created earlier in the constructor? verify; if the sink is built after :5185, buffer the lines and write them once the sink exists); `source_summary` is `"probe"` here; G05 adds `"env"|"override"|"self_test"` sources and the DECRPM entries.
- Demo: `terminal_capabilities.rs` renders `ProbeResult.ledgers` obtained from the program's probe (expose `Program::capability_decisions()` or pass through the showcase model) instead of constructing its own prober; the `caps_probe_stub` module shrinks to what a feature-off build needs (types only, no ledger logic).

## Implementation plan

1. `caps_probe.rs`: `build_ledgers_from`, `ProbeResult.ledgers`, `CapabilityDecision` + `decisions` + `to_jsonl` (JSON escaping helper: ftui-core has none? reuse `capability_override`'s or add a 10-line `json_escape` in caps_probe.rs), `refine_from_ledgers`, capability-to-field mapping, `DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD`; make `build_ledgers` :1153 delegate; keep `record_timeout_evidence` :1213 for the prober path.
2. `probe_capabilities_unix` :158: after the probes, `result.ledgers = build_ledgers_from(caps_before, &result)` (needs `caps_before`: change the signature to `probe_capabilities(config, caps: &TerminalCapabilities)`; update the one production caller at `program.rs:5177` and any tests).
3. `refine_from_probe` :931: append the `refine_from_ledgers` call.
4. `program.rs:5170-5190`: emit `capability_decision` lines; add `Program::capability_decisions(&self) -> &[CapabilityDecision]` (stored once at startup) for the demo/harness.
5. Demo screen: replace `self.prober.build_ledgers(caps)` (:1321) with the stored decisions; remove the ledger logic from `caps_probe_stub` (keep type shims minimal; if the showcase always builds with `caps-probe`, delete the stub module contents down to a `compile_error!`-free empty module and note it for `g07-decision`-style cleanup — no file deletion is involved).
6. Register `capability_decision` with `g20-impl`; `docs/spec/telemetry-events.md` row.
7. Gates: `cargo check -p ftui-core --features caps-probe`, `cargo test -p ftui-core --features caps-probe`, showcase tests, `ubs`.

What NOT to do: no change to the weights' values (they are tuned and documented at :1113-1143; G05 may retune with matrix data); no lowering of any capability by the ledger; no second ledger type in the demo.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-core/src/caps_probe.rs`: builder, decisions, refine, mapping, JSON.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: probe call signature, evidence emission, accessor.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/terminal_capabilities.rs`: render production decisions; stub reduction.
- `docs/spec/telemetry-events.md`: event row (with G20).

## Success criteria

- [ ] Ledger tests: `env_positive_but_decrpm_denied_is_unsupported` (-0.4? no: +ENV_POSITIVE then -4.6 -> `is_supported() == false`), `env_absent_but_decrpm_confirmed_is_supported` (-0.4 + 4.6 -> true, `confident_at(0.8)` true), `timeout_only_keeps_prior` (prior 0, ENV_ABSENT, TIMEOUT -> false; `evidence_count == 2`), `mux_penalty_shifts_borderline_case` (a ledger at log-odds 0.6 with mux -> below threshold), `refine_from_ledgers_is_upgrade_only` (field true before, ledger says false -> still true).
- [ ] `build_ledgers_from_records_timeout_only_when_probe_ran`.
- [ ] `capability_decision_jsonl_shape` (parse; keys as specified).
- [ ] Showcase E2E JSONL contains `capability_decision` lines for all `ALL` capabilities (asserted in `g28-tests`).
- [ ] `g05-impl` reviewer confirms the API is sufficient (comment on `g05-impl` linking this bead's commit).

## Tests and logging

- Unit: the seven tests above in `caps_probe.rs` and `program.rs`.
- Logging: `capability_decision` evidence; tracing `ftui.core.caps` debug per decision (feature `tracing`).

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: nothing.
- Unblocks: `g05-impl` (cluster A), `g28-impl`, `g28-tests`, `g28-docs`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Threshold 0.8: with `DECRPM_CONFIRMED = 4.6` a single confirmed probe reaches P = 0.985 even against `ENV_ABSENT`; `DA2_KNOWN_TERMINAL = 1.8` alone reaches 0.80 only with `ENV_POSITIVE` (whose value must be read from :1113-1120 before asserting numbers in tests).
- The probe signature change (passing `caps`) is the cleanest way to give the ledger its environment evidence; the alternative (a second call to `TerminalCapabilities::with_overrides()` inside the probe) would double-read the environment.

## Definition of done

Ledger on the production path with upgrade-only refinement; evidence event emitted; demo renders production decisions; tests green; gates and `ubs` clean; `g05-impl` notified; close reason lists test names and one evidence line.
close_reason: CapabilityLedger is now the production combiner: caps_probe::ledger_for builds the per-capability ledger (environment +3.0/-0.4, XTGETTCAP/DECRPM +/-4.6, timeout -0.7, mux -0.5, operator +/-9.2) and TerminalCapabilities::refine_from_probe applies an upgrade only when the posterior clears DECISION_THRESHOLD (0.8), upgrade-only. decisions_from_probe exports the same rows; Program hands them to TerminalWriter::with_capability_decisions, which writes capability_decision rows (truecolor, sync_output, scroll_region) plus one inline_strategy row as soon as an evidence sink is attached. Tests (ftui-core --features caps-probe, 110 passed): refine_from_probe_decides_through_the_ledger_threshold, decisions_from_probe_records_decrpm_confirmation, decisions_from_probe_marks_timeouts_as_weak_negative_evidence, operator_override_dominates_the_ledger, capability_decision_jsonl_is_valid_and_stable; ftui-runtime terminal_writer::tests::evidence_sink_exports_capability_decisions_and_inline_strategy. README capability section rewritten. Commits 378c69ba + follow-up. Not done here: refine_from_ledgers name/API as written in the bead (the combiner is ledger_for + threshold inside refine_from_probe), DA1/DA2 rows in the startup path (only XTGETTCAP + DECRPM are sent).

title: G28: Select SAT default from ablation and verify capability evidence
description:
## Context and why this matters

Integrating bead for G28 ("Built-but-unqueried structures", P1 because it unblocks G05). `g28-impl-sat` measures whether a SAT-driven row skip wins; `g28-decision` fixes the keep/delete rule and grants conditional permission; `g28-impl-ledger` puts the capability ledger on the production path. This bead executes the SAT verdict (keep with a baseline row, or remove under the granted permission), reconciles the `diff_decision` evidence shape, verifies the `capability_decision` evidence flows end to end in the showcase, and records the ledger rows so `g42-impl` and cluster A can depend on one bead named `g28-impl`.

## Current state (evidence)

- After the sibling beads: `TileDiffPlan::tile_row_dirty/rect_dirty`, the row prefilter, `skipped_tile_rows`/`sat_queries` stats and JSONL fields, `docs/perf/sat_tile_skip_2026-09.md` (before/after table); `ProbeResult.ledgers`, `refine_from_ledgers`, `CapabilityDecision::to_jsonl`, `capability_decision` emission at `program.rs:5175-5190`, demo rendering production decisions.
- `tests/baseline.json` format: `{description, criterion_name, bench_file, crate, slo_metric, p50_ns, p95_ns, p99_ns, p999_ns, threshold_pct}`; `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh:290-302` reads those keys.
- README.md:848-857 SAT section, :1741 summary row; :818-830 capability section.

## Target state

KEEP branch (after <= 0.9 x before at 200x60 sparse and no 240x80 regression): `tests/baseline.json` row `diff_200x60_sparse` (`criterion_name: "diff/sparse_5pct/200x60"`, `bench_file: "diff_bench"`, `crate: "ftui-render"`, `slo_metric: "diff_sparse_200x60_p99_ns"`, numbers from the after run, `threshold_pct: 10`) and, if the threshold experiment won, `TileDiffConfig::min_cells_for_tiles` default updated with a doc comment citing the perf record; README SAT sentence says "row-level tile skipping via the SAT" (in `g28-docs`). DELETE branch (permission from `g28-decision` item 2): remove the SAT build blocks, fields, stats, JSONL fields (`sat_build_cost_est`, `sat_queries`), tests, and the README section/row; keep the row prefilter only if it can be expressed over `tile_counts` (a per-tile-row sum array is cheaper than a SAT: if the row skip won but the SAT is not needed for it, replace `sat` with `tile_row_counts: Vec<u32>` and keep the win). Either branch: `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh` asserts `capability_decision` lines (`g28-tests`), `docs/spec/telemetry-events.md` rows for `capability_decision` and the `diff_decision` field changes, ledger rows for V64 and the SAT claim, and the reachability gate green.

## Implementation plan

1. Read `docs/perf/sat_tile_skip_2026-09.md`; apply the `g28-decision` rule; quote the answer and numbers in the commit message.
2. KEEP: add the baseline row; threshold default change if permitted and won; done. DELETE: in-file removals listed above in `diff.rs`, `terminal_writer.rs` (JSONL fields removed at the end of the format string; golden fixtures re-blessed with review), `diff_bench.rs` untouched (the groups still measure the diff), README edits handed to `g28-docs`.
3. Run `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh` locally with `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL`; confirm `capability_decision` lines (one per `ProbeableCapability::ALL` entry) and the `diff_decision` shape; attach.
4. `docs/spec/telemetry-events.md` rows (coordinate with `g20-impl`).
5. Ledger rows: SAT (CODE keep with `diff_200x60_sparse` proof, or DOC retracted), capability ledger (CODE; proofs: ledger tests, `capability_decision` E2E assertion).
6. Gates, `ubs`; comment on `g05-impl` that the ledger API is final.

What NOT to do: no removal without the numbers and the quoted permission; no keeping both the SAT and a `tile_row_counts` array.

## Files to change

- `tests/baseline.json` (KEEP) or `crates/ftui-render/src/diff.rs` + `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs` (DELETE).
- `docs/spec/telemetry-events.md`; `docs/claims-ledger.md` (if present).

## Success criteria

- [ ] Branch executed per the numbers; commit message quotes `g28-decision` and the table row.
- [ ] `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh` (local) reports `diff_200x60_sparse` PASS (KEEP branch).
- [ ] Showcase E2E run shows `capability_decision_all_capabilities pass`.
- [ ] Reachability gate green; `cargo test -p ftui-render -p ftui-core --features caps-probe -p ftui-runtime --lib` green.

title: task(G28): SAT exactness/prefilter-transparency proptests, ledger combination tests, capability_decision E2E
description:
## Context

Companion test bead for `g28-impl-sat`, `g28-impl-ledger`, and `g28-impl`. 2. Prefilter transparency (identical `ChangeRun`s with and without the prefilter; stats counters).

4. Ledger combination rules and upgrade-only refinement; timeout recording; JSON shape.
5. E2E: evidence lines in the showcase run; the demo screen renders production decisions (snapshot).

title: epic(G02): Every rust fence in README, getting-started and agent-harness is a compiled doc-test
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:73-76 tells library consumers to "start here: docs/getting-started.md", README.md:137 offers a "Minimal API Example", and the rest of the README contains 31 ```rust fences illustrating the runtime, harness, widgets, focus, modal, persistence, macro, simulator and intelligence-layer APIs. None of those fences is ever compiled. The 2026-09-01 reality check (commit `ab07291f`) found that the front-page example does not compile (missing `Widget` import, onboarding gap A.1), that at least nine fences are fragments that cannot compile in isolation, and that many others describe APIs that do not exist (Section 2.2.C, e.g. `frame.render_widget`, `Layout::horizontal`, `focus_manager.register("input1", ..)`, `modal_stack.push(ConfirmDialog::new(..))`, `Cmd::perform`, `frame.checksum()`, `PersistenceConfig::new().with_backend(FileBackend::new(..))`, `field_lens!`). The plan's root cause 1 ("no truth mechanism between README and code") applies directly: a prior truth pass in April 2026 (bead bd-1zmo3) regressed within weeks because nothing failed when the docs drifted.

This block turns every `rust` fence in README.md, docs/getting-started.md and docs/tutorials/agent-harness.md into a rustdoc doc-test so drift fails CI. It closes A.1, A.4-A.6 (getting-started accuracy, harness example, `view_string`/`StringModel` visibility), every Section 2.2.C row that has a code block, and vision rows V41-V45 (widget composition helpers, hyperlinks, focus, modal, time-travel APIs whose README shapes are wrong).

## Current state (evidence)

- README.md ```rust fences (31) start at lines 139, 369, 603, 620, 636, 660, 1812, 1895, 1945, 1973, 1984, 2001, 2018, 2047, 2076, 2190, 2201, 2213, 2228, 2249, 2257, 2270, 2278, 2354, 2511, 2539, 2580, 2651, 2674, 2711, 2725 (`rg -n '^```rust' README.md`, 2026-09-01). `docs/getting-started.md` has 1 (line 192, the inline `LogViewer` harness example). `docs/tutorials/agent-harness.md` has 9. Total 41.
- Plan-identified fragments that cannot compile alone: evidence sink (README "Evidence Logs (JSONL Diagnostics)", :363-389), rollout scorecard (:632-655), effect queue (:656-673), focus, modal, lens, persistence, macro, simulator (Widget System / runtime sections between :2143 and :2725). `ShadowRun`, `RolloutScorecard`, `RolloutEvidenceBundle` snippets (:616-655) are exact per the harness audit (Section 5.3) and only need a wrapper.
- `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs` has no `#[cfg(doctest)]` items (`grep -n 'cfg(doctest)\|include_str' crates/ftui/src/lib.rs` is empty).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `docs` job (:86-117) already runs `cargo test --doc --workspace` (:111) and `cargo build --examples -p ftui-harness` (:117), on floating `nightly` (pinning is G04.10, `g04-10-impl`). Because the README is not included anywhere as documentation, that step never sees it.
- `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md` exists (llvm-cov instructions) and is where the deliberate-failure verification will be recorded.
- `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml` has `readme = "../../README.md"`; crates.io renders the README, so rustdoc hidden lines (`# `) would be visible there as plain comment lines.

## Target state

Every `rust` fence in the three files is a doc-test compiled by `cargo test -p ftui --doc`. Complete programs that open a terminal are ```rust,no_run (compiled, not executed). Fragments are either rewritten as complete `no_run` programs or marked ```rust,ignore with a visible line "(fragment: not compiled)" directly above the fence. Fences describing APIs that `g06-decision` marks DOC are rewritten to the real API; fences for modules quarantined by G07 (`lens`, `slo`, `ivm`) move to the README "Experimental modules" section as ```rust,ignore. `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs` is byte-identical to the README block. CI fails when any fence stops compiling; this was proven once by a deliberately broken snippet and the procedure is written down.

## Implementation plan (block level)

1. `g02-impl`: `#[cfg(doctest)]` include items in `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs` for the three files; dev-dependencies needed by the fences (`ftui-harness` for the ShadowRun/RolloutScorecard blocks, if no dependency cycle); the fence-by-fence audit with a classification table kept in the bead's close notes and in `docs/claims-ledger.md`.
2. `g02-tests`: `cargo test -p ftui --doc` in the `docs` job explicitly (in addition to `--workspace`), the deliberate-failure verification, and the write-up in `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md`.
3. `g02-docs`: `docs/getting-started.md` example becomes a complete, doc-tested `no_run` program with working "Run it" instructions under default features.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`: `#[cfg(doctest)]` items.
- `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`: `[dev-dependencies]` for doc-test-only crates.
- `README.md`: fence info-strings and bodies (41 fences audited; ~31 in README).
- `docs/getting-started.md`, `docs/tutorials/agent-harness.md`: fences.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `docs` job; `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md`.
- `docs/claims-ledger.md`: one row per fence (kind: example; proof: doc-test name).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui --doc` compiles README.md, docs/getting-started.md and docs/tutorials/agent-harness.md (the doc-test names appear in the output as `README.md - ReadmeDoctests (line N)` etc.), zero failures, zero `ignored` except fences explicitly marked with the "(fragment: not compiled)" line.
- [ ] CI `docs` job runs it; a deliberately broken snippet in a PR fails that job (verified once during rollout, screenshot/log in `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md` "Doc-test gate" section with the run id).
- [ ] `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs` is byte-identical to the README block (checked by `scripts/check_readme_claims.py --example-identity`, `g06-impl-checker`).
- [ ] Count of ```rust,ignore fences is recorded in the claims ledger and may only shrink (the checker enforces a ceiling equal to the count at close time).

## Tests and logging

Doc-tests are the tests; the CI job log is the log. `g02-tests` adds a one-line summary step that greps the rustdoc output for `test result:` lines per file and prints `doc_tests_readme=<n> ignored=<m>` so the trend is visible in the job summary (`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`).

## Dependencies and ordering

- `g02-impl` is blocked by `g01-impl-facade` (the example must run under default features; the prelude must export `Widget`) and by `g06-decision` (which mismatched fences are CODE vs DOC decides whether a fence is rewritten to the real API now or waits for the CODE bead).
- Unblocks: `g06-docs-readme` (rewrite happens on doc-tested fences), `g06-impl-checker` (example identity check), `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative: a custom script that extracts fences and compiles them with `rustc`. Rejected: rustdoc already does this, with the crate's dev-dependencies in scope, on the `docs` job that exists.
- Risk: README on crates.io shows rustdoc `# ` hidden lines. Mitigation: prefer complete examples; use hidden lines only for `# fn main() {}` wrappers around type-level snippets, and prefer `no_run` complete programs where the README benefits from a full example.
- Risk: fences that need `ftui-harness` or `ftui-extras` types require dev-dependencies of the facade; check for cycles (`crates/ftui-harness/Cargo.toml` must not depend on `ftui`; if it does, those fences are marked `ignore` with the fragment line and a follow-up bead is filed).
- Risk: doc-tests slow the `docs` job; 41 small programs is minutes at most.
- No deletion: fences are rewritten or marked, never removed without owner permission; when a fence describes a feature that does not exist and G06 says DOC, the fence is replaced by the real API, not dropped.

## Definition of done

`cargo test -p ftui --doc` green on main in the `docs` job (run id in the close reason), the deliberate-failure verification recorded, ledger rows for every fence present, and the README example file identity check green.

title: task(G02): cfg(doctest) includes for README and docs plus audit of all 41 rust fences
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:137-190 "Minimal API Example" is the first code a consumer sees, and it does not compile: `Paragraph::new(text).render(area, frame)` needs the `Widget` trait in scope (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/paragraph.rs:291 impl Widget for Paragraph<'_>`; no inherent `render`). Thirty more README fences and ten in the two docs files are equally unverified. The reality check's root cause 1 is that nothing fails when README code drifts from the crate. This bead installs the mechanism (rustdoc doc-tests over the markdown files) and does the one-time audit that makes all 41 fences compile or be visibly marked as fragments. It closes A.1, the code-block half of every Section 2.2.C row, and V41-V45. `g02-tests` proves the gate bites; `g06-docs-readme` later rewrites prose on top of compiled fences.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`: no `#[cfg(doctest)]` items; the crate's own rustdoc examples (e.g. `capability_override.rs:36-50` in ftui-core) are compiled, but README.md is not attached to any crate's documentation.
- README.md fence lines (31): 139, 369, 603, 620, 636, 660, 1812, 1895, 1945, 1973, 1984, 2001, 2018, 2047, 2076, 2190, 2201, 2213, 2228, 2249, 2257, 2270, 2278, 2354, 2511, 2539, 2580, 2651, 2674, 2711, 2725. `docs/getting-started.md`: 192. `docs/tutorials/agent-harness.md`: 9 fences (enumerate with `rg -n '^```rust' docs/tutorials/agent-harness.md`).
- Known-wrong API shapes inside fences (Section 2.2.C): `frame.render_widget(w, area)`, `frame.render_stateful_widget(..)`, `frame.area()` (real: `widget.render(area, frame)`, `frame.width()`/`height()`; CODE in `g17-09-impl`); `Layout::horizontal([Constraint::Percentage(30), ..]).split(frame.area())` (real: `Flex::horizontal().constraints(..).split(area)`, `Percentage(f32)`; CODE in `g17-09-impl`); `focus_manager.register("input1", FocusNode::new()); set_next(..)` (real: `FocusId = u64`, `graph.insert(FocusNode::new(id, bounds))`, `connect(from, NavDirection, to)`, `focus_next/prev`; DOC); `modal_stack.push(ConfirmDialog::new("Delete file?"))` (real: `push(Box<dyn StackModal>)`, `Dialog::confirm(title, msg)`; DOC); `frame.link_registry().register(url)`, `cell.link_id = id` (real: `Frame::register_link/with_links/set_links`, `Cell::with_link(u32)`, `cell.link_id()`; DOC); `TimeTravel::new(); record(frame); seek(i); current()` (real: `new(capacity)`, `record(&Buffer, FrameMetadata)`, `get(idx)`, `rewind(steps)`, `seek` on `TimeTravelInspector`; DOC + quarantine G07); `Stylesheet::new(); sheet.register(..); sheet.get(..).unwrap_or_default()` (real: `StyleSheet::define/get -> Option<Style>/get_or_default/compose`; DOC now, consumer CODE in `g17-08-impl`); `TableTheme::modern().with_stripe_period(2)...` (CODE in `g17-07-impl`; until then the fence uses a real preset such as `TableTheme::aurora()`); `Cmd::perform(future, mapper)` (real: `Cmd::task/task_with_spec/task_named`; DOC); `Cmd::SetClipboard/GetClipboard` (CODE `g15-impl`); `tick_every`, `file_watcher` (CODE `g16-impl`; until then the fence uses `Every::new(Duration, || Msg::Tick)`); `frame.checksum()`, `MacroPlayer::next() -> (event, delay)`, `simulator.send_event` (real: `ftui_harness::golden::compute_buffer_checksum`, `MacroPlayer::step/replay_all/replay_with_timing`, `sim.inject_events`; DOC); `PersistenceConfig::new().with_auto_save(true).with_backend(FileBackend::new(..))`, `MemoryBackend` (real: `PersistenceConfig::with_registry(Arc<StateRegistry>).auto_load(bool).auto_save(bool)`, `FileStorage` under feature `state-persistence`, `MemoryStorage`; DOC); `field_lens!` (no macro exists; DOC + quarantine G07); `slo.yaml` schema (DOC + quarantine G07).
- The ShadowRun / RolloutScorecard / RolloutEvidenceBundle fences (README.md:616-655) are exact against `ftui-harness` (Section 5.3) and need only a wrapper.
- `include_str!` resolves relative to the source file. From `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs` the repository root is `../../../` (src -> ftui -> crates -> root), so the correct path is `"../../../README.md"`, not `"../../README.md"` (that is the `Cargo.toml` `readme` path, which is relative to the package root).
- `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml` has no `[dev-dependencies]`.

## Target state

`cargo test -p ftui --doc` compiles all 41 fences. Each fence has exactly one of: (a) ```rust (compiled and executed; only for pure-computation snippets), (b) ```rust,no_run (complete programs that open a terminal or spawn tasks), (c) ```rust,ignore preceded by the line `*(fragment: not compiled)*`. Every fence body uses real, current API names or, for CODE rows, the real API that exists today with a one-line comment naming the bead that will add the convenience (`// convenience form lands with g17-09-impl`). The README Minimal API Example is byte-identical to `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs`.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`: add
   ```rust

   #[doc = include_str!("../../../README.md")]
   pub struct ReadmeDoctests;
   #[cfg(doctest)]
   #[doc = include_str!("../../../docs/getting-started.md")]
   pub struct GettingStartedDoctests;
   #[cfg(doctest)]

   ```

2. `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`: add `[dev-dependencies] ftui-harness = { path = "../ftui-harness", version = "0.6.0" }` only after confirming `crates/ftui-harness/Cargo.toml` does not depend on `ftui` (avoid a cycle). If it does, fences needing harness types are marked `ignore` with the fragment line and a follow-up bead is filed against G06.
3. Audit each fence in order of line number. For each, record in a table (kept in the close notes and copied into `docs/claims-ledger.md` as rows of kind `example`): file, line, section heading, classification (compiled / no_run / ignore), APIs touched, and the G06 decision (CODE bead slug or DOC). Rules: `Widget`/`StatefulWidget` imports come from `ftui::prelude::*`; use `ftui::` paths, never `ftui_core::` internal paths in consumer-facing fences (harness fences may use `ftui_harness::`); fences that need a running terminal are `no_run`; type-level snippets get `# fn main() {}` wrappers only when a complete program would triple the fence length.
4. Minimal example (README.md:139): body already replaced by `g01-impl-facade`; set the fence to ```rust,no_run and re-verify byte identity with `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs` (the example file has no fence, so identity is of the inner bytes).
5. Evidence-sink fence (README.md:369) and effect-queue fence (:660): rewrite as complete `no_run` programs using `ProgramConfig::default()` and the real builder methods (read `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` `ProgramConfig` for the exact names before writing).
6. ShadowRun/RolloutScorecard/RolloutEvidenceBundle fences (:603-655): wrap in `# fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {` ... `# Ok(()) }` and mark `no_run`.
7. Focus, modal, hyperlink, time-travel, stylesheet, table-theme, `Cmd`, persistence, macro, simulator, checksum fences: rewrite to the real API (names listed in "Current state"); where `g06-decision` marks CODE, use the existing idiom and add the one-line comment naming the owning bead. Do not invent APIs.

README.md` returns only lines inside fences marked `ignore` or lines whose comment names the CODE bead.

Prefer enabling `ftui-runtime/state-persistence` in a `doc-examples` dev feature only if it is cheap; otherwise mark and record.
