title: task(G02): CI docs job runs cargo test -p ftui --doc and a deliberate broken snippet is proven to fail
description:
## Context

G02 turns the 41 `rust` fences in README.md, docs/getting-started.md and docs/tutorials/agent-harness.md into rustdoc doc-tests (`g02-impl`). A gate that has never been seen to fail is not a gate: the April 2026 truth pass (bead bd-1zmo3) regressed because no job ever went red on doc drift. This bead is the block's test-and-CI bead: it makes the `docs` job run the facade doc-tests explicitly, proves once that a broken snippet fails the job, and writes the procedure down so the next person can re-verify. It doubles as the block's CI/E2E bead (the block names a CI job rather than a PTY scenario).

## What to test

1. `cargo test -p ftui --doc` compiles all three markdown files in CI on every push and PR.
2. A deliberately broken fence fails the `docs` job with the file and line in the log.
3. The number of `ignore`d fences is reported and cannot grow silently.
4. The `docs` job also builds `crates/ftui/examples` so `minimal_inline.rs` cannot rot (the step `cargo build --examples -p ftui-harness` exists at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:117`; add `-p ftui`).

## Test types (unit, property, bench, E2E) with names and assertions

- CI step (E2E of the gate): in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `docs` (:86-117), after `cargo test --doc --workspace` (:111) add `cargo test -p ftui --doc -- --show-output 2>&1 | tee doc_tests.log`, then a shell step that asserts `grep -c 'README.md - ReadmeDoctests' doc_tests.log` is >= 25 (the README fence count minus `ignore`d ones; the exact floor is set when `g02-impl` closes and recorded in the ledger), `grep -c 'getting-started.md - GettingStartedDoctests' doc_tests.log >= 1`, `grep -c 'agent-harness.md - AgentHarnessTutorialDoctests' doc_tests.log >= 1`, and that the `ignored` count parsed from the `test result:` line is <= the ceiling stored in `docs/claims-ledger.md` (read with a two-line python snippet). Print `doc_tests_readme=<n> ignored=<m> ceiling=<c>` to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.
- Deliberate failure (one-time verification, recorded): on a scratch branch, change the README Minimal API Example's `let area = Rect::new(0, 0, frame.width(), 1);` to `let area: Rect = "not a rect";`, push, open a draft PR, observe `docs` job failure with `README.md - ReadmeDoctests (line 139)` in the log, close the PR without merging, and paste the run id and the failing log excerpt into `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md` under a new "Doc-test gate (README and docs)" section. The scratch branch is not deleted by the agent (AGENTS.md rule 1); the owner deletes it or it is left in place.
- Local pre-commit check: document in AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks" (via `g06-docs-agents`) that `cargo test -p ftui --doc` is part of the mandatory gate when README or docs change.
- Example build: `cargo build -p ftui --examples` in the `docs` job.

No unit/property/bench tests: the artifact under test is the CI configuration and the markdown.

## Logging (structured JSONL fields, tracing targets)

- `doc_tests.log` uploaded as artifact `docs-doctests` (retention 7 days) on failure.
- Step summary line `doc_tests_readme=<n> doc_tests_getting_started=<n> doc_tests_tutorial=<n> ignored=<m> ceiling=<c>`.
- `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md` records: date, PR number, run id, the failing line, the time from push to red (must be under the job's normal duration plus doc-test time).

## Files

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `docs` job steps (after :111 and :117).
- `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md`: new section "Doc-test gate (README and docs)" with the verification record and the re-verification procedure (five bullet steps).
- `docs/claims-ledger.md`: row "README doc-tests run in CI" (proof: job `docs`, step name; status proven with run id) and row "ignored fence ceiling = <c>".

## Success criteria

- [ ] `docs` job green on main with the new steps (run id in the close reason).
- [ ] The deliberate-failure PR run id is recorded in `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md` and the job was red for the right reason (the log names the README line).
- [ ] `cargo build -p ftui --examples` runs in the `docs` job.
- [ ] Step summary shows the counts on every run.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `g02-impl` (doc-tests must exist). Related: `g04-10-impl` pins the toolchain the `docs` job uses (today `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` with `toolchain: nightly`, floating); this bead does not change the toolchain input. Unblocks: `g06-docs-readme` (rewrite lands on a proven gate), `g42-impl`.

## Definition of done

Steps merged, one red-for-cause run recorded, ledger rows added, close reason cites both run ids (green main, red verification).
close_reason: CI check job now runs cargo nextest run -p ftui --profile ci (the facade integration tests were never executed by the --lib run). The deliberate-break proof is in-tree: readme_checker_fails_on_a_missing_snippet (should_panic expected drifted) asserts that a marker region absent from README fails the identity check. NOT yet observed on CI: every GitHub Actions run since 07:09 UTC today is stuck in queued (31 runs), so the CI leg is unproven. Commit 90ac9aef.

title: docs(G02): Make docs/getting-started.md's inline example a complete, doc-tested no_run program
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:73-76 sends library consumers to `docs/getting-started.md` as "the shortest path to a working inline (scrollback-preserving) UI" (its own words at `docs/getting-started.md:12-13`). Its one code example (`docs/getting-started.md:192-263`, "Minimal Inline App (Copy/Paste)") is a `LogViewer`-based harness that ends with `App::new(Harness { .. }).screen_mode(ScreenMode::Inline { ui_height: 5 }).run()?;`. It was never compiled, and under today's facade defaults `.run()` returns `Unsupported`. This bead makes that example a complete, doc-tested `no_run` program that works under the defaults G01 establishes, and makes the "Run it" instructions after it true. It closes onboarding gaps A.4-A.6 for the getting-started page (the crates.io sentence and crate map are `g06-docs-getting-started`; this bead owns the example and its run instructions only, so the two beads do not edit the same lines).

## Current state (evidence)

- `docs/getting-started.md:192-263`: imports `std::time::Duration`, `ftui::core::event::{Event, KeyCode, KeyEventKind, Modifiers}`, `ftui::core::geometry::Rect`, `ftui::render::frame::Frame`, `ftui::runtime::{Every, Subscription}`, `ftui::widgets::StatefulWidget`, `ftui::widgets::log_viewer::{LogViewer, LogViewerState}`, `ftui::{App, Cmd, Model, ScreenMode}`; `enum Msg { Key(ftui::KeyEvent), Tick }`; `Model` with `init`, `update` (Ctrl+C quits via `k.modifiers.contains(Modifiers::CTRL) && k.code == KeyCode::Char('c')`), `view` (`Rect::from_size(frame.buffer.width(), frame.buffer.height())`, clones state, `self.log.render(area, frame, &mut state)`), `subscriptions` (`Every::new(Duration::from_secs(1), || Msg::Tick)`); `fn main() -> ftui::Result<()>` with `.run()?`. Unlike the README example it does import `StatefulWidget`, so its only runtime blocker is the backend default.
- The fence is ```rust (would be executed as a doc-test and would try to open a terminal; must become `no_run`).
- `view` clones `LogViewerState` every frame (`let mut state = self.state.clone();`) which discards scroll state; a correct example keeps state in the model and renders with `&mut self.state` through interior mutability or restructures `view` (verify what `Model::view(&self, ..)` allows; `StatefulWidget::render(&self, area, frame, state: &mut S)` needs `&mut`). The example must show the idiomatic pattern used by the showcase (read `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/` for how stateful widgets are rendered from `view(&self)`, e.g. `RefCell`/`Cell` or a `StatefulWidget` whose state is re-derived), not a clone that silently loses state.
- "Run it" section after line 263: verify its commands; they currently assume a workspace path dependency.
- `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs` will include this file as `GettingStartedDoctests` (`g02-impl`).

## Target state

The getting-started example compiles as a doc-test (`cargo test -p ftui --doc` names `getting-started.md - GettingStartedDoctests (line 192)`), is marked ```rust,no_run, uses `ftui::prelude::*` for `App, Cmd, Model, ScreenMode, Event, KeyCode, KeyEvent, Modifiers, Rect, Frame, StatefulWidget` and explicit paths for `LogViewer`, `LogViewerState`, `Every`, `Subscription`; keeps scroll state correctly; quits on Ctrl+C and on `q`; and the "Run it" section says: create a crate, `cargo add ftui@0.6`, paste, `cargo run`, expected first line of output, how to quit, and the slim-build error text if `default-features = false` was used. A second short subsection "Without the builder" shows `Program::open(model, ProgramConfig::default())?.run()` (from `g01-impl`) in a `no_run` fence.

## Implementation plan

1. Read `Model` trait and `StatefulWidget` signatures in `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` and `crates/ftui-widgets/src/lib.rs:549`, and the showcase's `log_search.rs` for the stateful-render idiom; write the example accordingly (no state clone per frame; if the idiom requires `RefCell<LogViewerState>`, say so in one sentence above the fence).
2. Rewrite `docs/getting-started.md:192-263`: fence ```rust,no_run; imports via prelude; `q` and Ctrl+C both quit; keep `Every` 1 s tick; `fn main() -> ftui::Result<()>`.
3. Add the "Without the builder" `no_run` fence (6-8 lines) using `Program::open`.
4. Rewrite "Run it": commands for a crates.io consumer (primary) and for a path dependency (secondary); expected behaviour line ("a 5-row log panel pinned at the bottom; shell output above keeps scrolling"); quit keys; the slim-build error sentence.
5. Run `cargo test -p ftui --doc` via rch; fix until green. `ubs docs/getting-started.md` is not applicable (markdown); run `scripts/check_readme_claims.py` once it exists.
6. Add ledger rows: "getting-started example compiles (doc-test line 192)" and "getting-started Run it instructions verified" (proof: doc-test name; a one-time manual run recorded in the close reason).

What NOT to do: do not touch lines 1-40 (stability notes, crate map) or 160-188 (dependency snippets), which `g06-docs-getting-started` and `g01-docs` own; do not add a second example file to the repo for this page (the fence is the source; if an example file is wanted it must be byte-identical and checked like `minimal_inline.rs`, which is a G06 checker extension, not this bead); no deletion.

## Files to change

- `docs/getting-started.md`: lines 190-263 and the "Run it" section that follows.
- `docs/claims-ledger.md`: two rows.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui --doc` lists the getting-started doc-test and passes.
- [ ] Manual run once: following "Run it" from a fresh crate with `ftui = "0.6"` (or the path form) shows the pinned log panel and quits on `q`; the transcript path is in the close reason.
- [ ] `rg -n 'state.clone\(\)' docs/getting-started.md` returns nothing (no per-frame state clone).
- [ ] `g06-impl-checker` passes on the page.

## Tests and logging

Doc-test only; manual run recorded once. No runtime logging.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g02-impl` (include item must exist so the doc-test runs), `g01-impl-facade` (defaults, prelude). Unblocks: `g06-docs-getting-started` (edits the remaining sections afterwards to avoid overlapping diffs), `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative: replace the `LogViewer` example with the README `TickApp`. Rejected: the page's purpose is the inline log-panel pattern, which is FrankenTUI's differentiator (README TL;DR "inline UI at top/bottom while logs scroll above"); keep it, make it correct.
- Risk: `LogViewer`'s API may have changed since the page was written; the doc-test will say so.

## Definition of done

Doc-test green in the `docs` job (run id), manual run recorded, ledger rows present.
close_reason: The docs/getting-started.md inline program is now crates/ftui/examples/getting_started.rs byte-for-byte (rustfmt-clean); the facade test getting_started_example_is_the_shipped_example pins it and cargo test -p ftui builds the example, so the guide cannot drift from a program that compiles. The guide states this and gives the cargo run --example command. Commit 90ac9aef.

title: epic(G14): Keybinding system with priorities, chords, contexts, conflicts and serde (NOT_STARTED -> WORKING)
description:
# epic(G14): Keybinding system with priorities, chords, contexts, conflicts and serde (NOT_STARTED -> WORKING)

## Context and why this matters

README.md:1078-1086 promises, under the heading "Keybinding System (1,900+ Lines)":

> The `Keybinding` module supports:
> - **Declarative binding maps** with priority levels (global, mode, widget)
> - **Chord sequences** (`g g`, `Ctrl+x Ctrl+s`) with configurable timeout
> - **Context-sensitive activation**: bindings active only in specific modes/focus states
> - **Conflict detection**: warns when bindings shadow each other
> - **Serialization**: load/save binding maps for user customization

README.md:1065 adds "Chord recognition: multi-key sequences like `g g` (vim-style) use a `KeySequence` buffer with configurable timeout, enabling complex keybinding schemes without blocking single-key shortcuts."

None of that exists. The reality check (2026-09-01, commit `ab07291f`) rates vision row V62 "Keybinding system" as NOT_STARTED-as-described, lists `ftui-core/src/keybinding.rs` in the Section 2.2.B dead/mis-described table ("Only an Esc-Esc `SequenceDetector`; no priorities, chords, conflict detection, or load/save"), and lists "Keybinding system as described (priorities, chords, conflict detection, serialization)" in Section 2.5 as a vision goal covered by NO bead. The gap is user-visible three ways: (1) a library consumer who reads the README and looks for a keymap type finds only an Esc/Ctrl+C policy helper; (2) the showcase and `pane_keymap` hardcode every key in `match` arms, so nothing is remappable; (3) three `keybind_*` PTY E2E cases fail in CI (run `33152820289`, job "PTY E2E ubuntu", Section 5.1 row "42/166 failures ... keybind x3") and the G04.9 cluster explicitly routes those failures to this block.

This epic also unblocks G19 (Bayesian hint ranking needs real key-use feedback from a dispatcher) and part of G04.9 (`g04-09-impl-keybind`, cluster B).

## Current state (evidence)

Verified against the tree on 2026-09-01:

- `crates/ftui-core/src/keybinding.rs` is 1,913 lines. Public items: timing constants `DEFAULT_ESC_SEQ_TIMEOUT_MS = 250` (:98), `MIN_ESC_SEQ_TIMEOUT_MS = 150` (:101), `MAX_ESC_SEQ_TIMEOUT_MS = 400` (:104), `DEFAULT_ESC_DEBOUNCE_MS = 50` (:107), `MIN/MAX_ESC_DEBOUNCE_MS` (:110/:113); `SequenceConfig` (:146) documented at :134 with env `FTUI_DISABLE_ESC_SEQ` (read at :217); `SequenceOutput` (:280); `SequenceDetector` (:324) with `new(config)` (:332) and `feed(&mut self, event: &KeyEvent, now: Instant) -> SequenceOutput` (:348); `AppState` (:458); `Action` (:528); `CtrlCIdleAction` (:582); `ActionConfig` (:663); `ActionMapper` (:773, `new` :781). It is a policy for Esc/Esc-Esc/Ctrl+C/Ctrl+D behaviour in a single text-input context, not a keymap. There is no `KeyMap`, `Chord`, `Priority`, `Context`, `ConflictReport`, or any serialization.
- Widgets: `ftui-widgets/src/help_registry.rs:55` `pub struct Keybinding { .. }` with `new(key, action)` (:65) and `ftui-widgets/src/help.rs:1088` `pub struct KeybindingHints { global_entries, contextual_entries, key_format, mode, .. }` (`new` :1112, `with_global_entry` :1172, `with_contextual_entry` :1179) are display-only: they hold strings, dispatch nothing, and are fed by hand.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/pane_keymap.rs` (782 lines): `key_to_pane_command(key: &KeyEvent, resize_units: u16) -> Option<PaneCommand>` (:55) is a hardcoded `match`; `PaneKeyboardController` (:133, `handle_key` :241); `pane_keyboard_hints() -> &'static [PaneKeyHint]` (:338) is a static list that must be kept in sync by hand.
- Showcase `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs:4050-4160`: global keys are one `match (*code, *modifiers)`: `q` quit (:4052, guarded by `text_input_active` from `consumes_text_input` :4048), `Ctrl+C` quit (:4056), `Ctrl+K` palette (:4058), `?` help (:4071), `F12` debug (:4076), `F6` mouse capture (:4081), `Ctrl+P` perf HUD (:4086), `Ctrl+I` inspector (:4090), `Tab`/`BackTab` screen cycling (:4146/:4154). `advanced_text_editor.rs:580-582` defines its own screen-local `KeyChord` type for Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y/Ctrl+Shift+Z. `log_search.rs:900/:908` binds single `g`/`G` to top/bottom.
- `docs/spec/keybinding-policy.md` (370 lines) specifies the Esc/Ctrl+C policy (sections 1-11, incl. 6.1 Priority Table, 11.1-11.4 test plan and JSONL log schema) and says nothing about chords or maps.
- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_keybinding.sh` drives the `ftui-harness` binary (`E2E_HARNESS_BIN`) with eight cases `keybind_ctrl_c_clears_input`, `keybind_ctrl_c_cancels_task`, `keybind_esc_clears_input`, `keybind_esc_cancels_task`, `keybind_esc_esc_toggles_tree`, `keybind_esc_closes_tree`, `keybind_ctrl_d_soft_quit`, `keybind_ctrl_q_hard_quit` (:82-89) and logs JSONL to `keybinding_e2e.jsonl`; three of them fail in CI.
- `ftui-core/Cargo.toml` features: `default = []`, `crossterm`, `tracing`, `tracing-json`, `caps-probe`, `test-helpers`; `serde`/`serde_json` are dev-dependencies only (:66-67). `ftui-runtime` has `toml` optional under `policy-config` (Cargo.toml:90).

## Target state

A real keymap in `ftui-core::keybinding`: `KeyCombo` (key + modifiers, parse/display as `Ctrl+x`), `Chord` (one or more combos, `g g`, `Ctrl+x Ctrl+s`), `Binding<A>` with a `Priority` (Global < Mode < Widget) and optional `ContextId`, `KeyMap<A>` (bind/unbind/lookup/`conflicts()`), and `KeyDispatcher<A>` (a state machine that resolves chords with a timeout, keeps single-key bindings live while a chord is pending, reuses the existing `SequenceDetector` for the Esc ambiguity, and reports every dispatch). Behind feature `serde`, `KeyMap` round-trips through TOML and JSON. `pane_keymap`, the showcase global keys and `Help`/`KeybindingHints` read from the same map, so hints are derived, not hand-typed. `docs/spec/keybinding-policy.md` and README describe exactly this; the three `keybind_*` PTY failures are fixed and a chord E2E exists.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Unit tests with a virtual clock (explicit `Instant` arguments, no sleeping): chord completes within timeout, expires after, single-key bindings still fire while a chord is pending, priority resolution (widget beats mode beats global), `conflicts()` reports shadowed bindings (`g14-tests`).
- [ ] Round-trip: `KeyMap -> TOML -> KeyMap` equality; JSON likewise (`g14-tests`, feature `serde`).
- [ ] PTY E2E `tests/e2e/scripts/test_keybinding_chords.sh`: `g g` jumps to top in the LogSearch screen, `Ctrl+x Ctrl+s` shows the save status in the AdvancedTextEditor screen; the existing `keybind_*` cases pass in the `e2e-pty` job (`g14-e2e`).
- [ ] `pane_keyboard_hints()` and the showcase help overlay are generated from `KeyMap` (`g14-impl-adopt`).
- [ ] README.md:1078-1086 bullets each map to a type and a test name in the claims ledger (`g14-docs`, ledger rows via `g06-impl-ledger`).

## Implementation plan (children)

1. `g14-impl` (feature): core types and dispatcher in `keybinding.rs`.
2. `g14-impl-serde` (feature): `serde` feature in ftui-core, TOML/JSON round trip.
3. `g14-impl-adopt` (feature): `pane_keymap`, showcase global keys, LogSearch `g g`, AdvancedTextEditor `Ctrl+x Ctrl+s`, `Help`/`KeybindingHints::from_keymap`.
4. `g14-tests` (task): unit, property and round-trip tests.
5. `g14-e2e` (task): `test_keybinding_chords.sh` plus root-causing and fixing the three failing `keybind_*` cases.
6. `g14-docs` (docs): spec, README, ledger.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by nothing (day-one parallel track per the bridge plan). `g14-impl` -> `g14-impl-serde` and `g14-impl-adopt` -> `g14-tests`, `g14-e2e`, `g14-docs`. Unblocks `g19-impl` (hint ranking learns from `KeyDispatcher`) and `g04-09-impl-keybind` (cluster B, PTY failures). `g14-e2e` needs `g04-06-impl` (ripgrep on runners) before it can be green in CI.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Esc ambiguity: `Esc` alone vs `Esc`-prefixed chords is already solved by `SequenceDetector` with a 150-400 ms window; the dispatcher must compose with it rather than add a second Esc timer (rejected: a fresh detector, which would double-count Esc).
- Chord timeout: default 1,000 ms (same magnitude as `GestureConfig.chord_timeout` in `gesture.rs:69`), configurable; while pending, keys that cannot extend any bound chord flush the prefix (fire its own single-key binding if any) so single-key shortcuts never block.
- Kitty keyboard protocol delivers `Release`/`Repeat` (`KeyEventKind` at `event.rs:227`); only `Press` advances a chord, `Repeat` may re-fire single-key bindings.
- Text-input focus: contexts replace the ad-hoc `text_input_active` guard; a `TextInput` context makes `q`/`?` inactive instead of special-casing them.
- Serialization lives in `ftui-core` (needs a `serde` feature there and an optional `toml` dependency); rejected: putting `KeyMap` in `ftui-runtime` next to `policy-config`, because widgets (Help) and core (dispatcher) both need it and neither may depend on runtime for it.
- Size: `keybinding.rs` grows by roughly 800-1,000 lines. AGENTS.md sets a high bar for new files; a `keybinding/` directory split is allowed only if the file exceeds what rustfmt/clippy handle comfortably, and must be done in the same bead (no `keybinding_v2.rs`).
- Rollback: the new types are additive; `SequenceDetector` keeps its API, so nothing regresses if adoption stalls, but the epic is not done until adoption lands (WORKING means reachable from the showcase and `pane_keymap`).

## Definition of done

All six children closed with evidence named in their close reasons (test names, `e2e-pty` run id with the chord script green, snapshot names); README/spec text matches the code; claims-ledger rows for the five README bullets point at tests; `main` green on the runs that include the changes.

title: feature(G14): Add KeyCombo/Chord/Binding/KeyMap/KeyDispatcher/ConflictReport to ftui-core keybinding.rs
description:
# feature(G14): Add KeyCombo/Chord/Binding/KeyMap/KeyDispatcher/ConflictReport to ftui-core keybinding.rs

## Context and why this matters

README.md:1078-1086 promises "Declarative binding maps with priority levels (global, mode, widget)", "Chord sequences (`g g`, `Ctrl+x Ctrl+s`) with configurable timeout", "Context-sensitive activation", and "Conflict detection: warns when bindings shadow each other". README.md:1065 promises chords that work "without blocking single-key shortcuts". Vision row V62 is NOT_STARTED; Section 2.2.B lists `keybinding.rs` as "Only an Esc-Esc `SequenceDetector`". This bead builds the core types and the dispatcher. Without it every app in the tree hardcodes keys in `match` arms (showcase `app.rs:4050-4160`, `pane_keymap.rs:55`), nothing is remappable, and hint widgets cannot learn from real key use (G19).

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-core/src/keybinding.rs` (1,913 lines): `DEFAULT_ESC_SEQ_TIMEOUT_MS = 250` (:98), `MIN_ESC_SEQ_TIMEOUT_MS = 150` (:101), `MAX_ESC_SEQ_TIMEOUT_MS = 400` (:104), `DEFAULT_ESC_DEBOUNCE_MS = 50` (:107); `SequenceConfig` (:146, env `FTUI_DISABLE_ESC_SEQ` read at :217, documented :134); `SequenceOutput` (:280); `SequenceDetector` (:324), `new(config)` (:332), `feed(&mut self, event: &KeyEvent, now: Instant) -> SequenceOutput` (:348); `AppState` (:458), `Action` (:528), `CtrlCIdleAction` (:582), `ActionConfig` (:663), `ActionMapper` (:773). Nothing resembling a keymap.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/event.rs`: `KeyEvent { code: KeyCode, modifiers: Modifiers, kind: KeyEventKind }` (:88, `new(code)` :102), `KeyCode` (:157), `KeyEventKind::{Press, Repeat, Release}` (:227), `Modifiers` bitflags (:242).
- `crates/ftui-core/src/gesture.rs:69`: `chord_timeout: Duration::from_millis(1000)` is the only existing chord timeout in the tree (unwired).
- `docs/spec/keybinding-policy.md` section 4.2 "Timing Constants" and 6.1 "Priority Table" cover only the Esc/Ctrl+C policy.

## Target state

`ftui_core::keybinding` exports, in addition to the existing items:

- `KeyCombo { code: KeyCode, modifiers: Modifiers }` with `KeyCombo::new`, `Display` (`Ctrl+x`, `Shift+Tab`, `F12`, `g`) and `FromStr` (case-insensitive modifier names `Ctrl`, `Alt`, `Shift`, `Super`; single-character keys; named keys matching `KeyCode` variants). Normalization: `Shift+a` and `A` are the same combo; `Char` codes are stored lowercase with the Shift bit.
- `Chord(Vec<KeyCombo>)` (1..=4 combos) with `Chord::parse("g g")`, `Chord::single(combo)`, `Display` joined by spaces, `is_prefix_of(&Chord)`.
- `Priority { Global = 0, Mode = 1, Widget = 2 }` (`Ord`; higher wins).
- `ContextId(u32)` and `Context { id, name: &'static str }`; `KeyMap::context("text_input")` interns names.
- `Binding<A> { id: BindingId, chord: Chord, action: A, priority: Priority, context: Option<ContextId>, label: Option<String> }`.
- `KeyMap<A: Clone> { bindings: Vec<Binding<A>>, contexts, config: KeyMapConfig { chord_timeout: Duration (default 1000 ms, clamped 200..=5000), esc: SequenceConfig } }` with `bind(chord, action) -> BindingId`, `bind_in(chord, action, priority, context)`, `unbind(id)`, `bindings()`, `lookup(&Chord, active_contexts: &[ContextId]) -> Lookup<A>` where `Lookup::{Exact(&Binding<A>), Prefix(usize), None}`, and `conflicts() -> ConflictReport`.
- `ConflictReport { items: Vec<Conflict> }` with `Conflict::{Shadowed { winner: BindingId, loser: BindingId, chord }, PrefixCollision { short: BindingId, long: BindingId }, Duplicate { a, b }}` and a `Display` that prints one warning line per item (the README's "warns").
- `KeyDispatcher<A> { map: KeyMap<A>, pending: Vec<KeyCombo>, pending_since: Option<Instant>, esc: SequenceDetector, active_contexts: Vec<ContextId>, stats: DispatchStats }` with `feed(&mut self, key: &KeyEvent, now: Instant) -> Vec<Dispatch<A>>` and `tick(&mut self, now: Instant) -> Vec<Dispatch<A>>`, where `Dispatch<A>::{Action { action: A, binding: BindingId, chord: Chord }, Pending { prefix: Chord }, Unbound(KeyEvent), Expired { prefix: Chord }, Esc(SequenceOutput)}`. `set_active_contexts(&[ContextId])`. `DispatchStats { dispatched, expired, unbound }` for evidence and for G19's usage feedback.

Rules the dispatcher must implement: only `KeyEventKind::Press` extends a chord; `Repeat` re-fires a single-key binding; a key that cannot extend any bound chord flushes the pending prefix (if the prefix itself is an exact binding, that fires first) and is then processed on its own, so single-key shortcuts are never blocked; `tick(now)` past `chord_timeout` yields `Expired` and, if the prefix was itself bound, fires it; resolution among candidates: active-context bindings beat context-free ones, then higher `Priority`, then the most recently bound (and `conflicts()` reports every case where that tie-break was needed). `Esc` handling delegates to the embedded `SequenceDetector` (same 250 ms window and `FTUI_DISABLE_ESC_SEQ` semantics) so there is one Esc timer in the process.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-core/src/keybinding.rs`: add the types above after the existing `ActionMapper` section, with a module-level doc block that states the resolution order and timeout semantics in prose (the spec in `g14-docs` copies it). Keep `SequenceDetector` unchanged in behaviour; give it a small `pub fn timeout(&self) -> Duration` if the dispatcher needs it.
2. `KeyCombo` parsing: one `parse_key_name(&str) -> Option<KeyCode>` table covering every `KeyCode` variant that has a stable name (`Enter`, `Tab`, `BackTab`, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Insert`, `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Up/Down/Left/Right`, `Esc`, `Space`, `F1..F24`, single characters). Unknown names are an error, never a panic.
3. `KeyMap::conflicts()`: O(n^2) over bindings is fine (maps are small); prefix collisions are detected with `Chord::is_prefix_of`.
4. `KeyDispatcher::feed`: implement as a pure function of `(pending, key, now)`; every branch returns at least one `Dispatch` so no key is silently lost (property-tested in `g14-tests`).
5. `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs`: re-export the new types alongside the existing keybinding exports; `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs` prelude gains `KeyMap`, `KeyCombo`, `Chord`, `KeyDispatcher`, `Priority` (the facade already re-exports `ftui_core::event::*` at :31).
6. Do NOT: add a second Esc timer; change `GestureConfig`; create `keybinding_v2.rs` or a `keymap.rs` beside the existing file (if the file must be split, convert it to a `keybinding/` directory in this bead with `mod.rs` re-exporting everything); add serde derives here (that is `g14-impl-serde`); touch consumers (that is `g14-impl-adopt`).
7. After changes: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `ubs crates/ftui-core/src/keybinding.rs` before commit (AGENTS.md).

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-core/src/keybinding.rs`: new types, dispatcher, conflict report, docs.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs`: exports.
- `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`: prelude additions.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `keybinding::tests::chord_completes_within_timeout`, `chord_expires_after_timeout`, `single_key_fires_while_chord_pending`, `widget_beats_mode_beats_global`, `active_context_beats_contextless`, `conflicts_reports_shadowed_and_prefix` (detailed in `g14-tests`) pass.
- [ ] Property test `every_fed_key_yields_a_dispatch` passes 1,000 cases.
- [ ] `cargo doc -p ftui-core --no-deps` clean with `-D warnings` (G04.4 gate).
- [ ] No behaviour change in existing `SequenceDetector` tests.

## Tests and logging

Unit tests live in `keybinding.rs` `#[cfg(test)]` (AGENTS.md: inline unit tests). Timing uses explicit `Instant` values (`let t0 = Instant::now(); feed(.., t0 + Duration::from_millis(300))`), never `sleep`. `KeyDispatcher` emits `tracing::debug!(target: telemetry_schema::TARGET_RUNTIME, ..)`-style records only through ftui-core's optional `tracing` feature, with fields `chord`, `binding_id`, `priority`, `context`, `pending_ms`, `outcome` (`dispatched|pending|expired|unbound`); the showcase forwards `DispatchStats` into its evidence JSONL (`g14-e2e`). E2E coverage is `g14-e2e`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by nothing. Unblocks `g14-impl-serde`, `g14-impl-adopt`, `g14-tests`, and `g19-impl` (which calls `DispatchStats`/`Dispatch::Action` to feed `HintRanker::observe`).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Generic `A: Clone` keeps the map independent of any app message type; rejected: `Box<dyn Fn>` actions, which cannot be serialized or compared in tests.
- Rejected: resolving chords in `Program` instead of a core type, because widgets (`TextArea`, pane controller) need local dispatchers too.
- Risk: terminals without the kitty protocol send `Press` only, so `Repeat` semantics must not be required for correctness.
- Risk: `Ctrl+x` as a chord prefix shadows `Ctrl+x` as a command; the `conflicts()` report makes that visible, and the dispatcher's flush rule means the single binding still fires on timeout or on a non-extending key.

## Definition of done

Reachable from the production path once `g14-impl-adopt` lands (this bead alone is library surface, which is legitimate for ftui-core but the epic requires adoption). Close reason names the six unit tests and the property test; clippy/fmt/check clean; claims-ledger rows are `g14-docs`.
close_reason: Landed in ftui_core::keybinding (commit HEAD): KeyCombo (parse/Display/normalization), Chord (<=4, prefix), KeyParseError, Priority, ContextId, BindingId, Binding, KeyMapConfig (chord timeout clamped 200..=5000 ms, esc SequenceConfig), KeyMap (bind/bind_in/set_label/unbind/lookup/conflicts), ConflictReport (Shadowed, PrefixCollision, Duplicate; Display one warning per item), KeyDispatcher (feed/tick; chord pending + timeout; non-extending key flushes then re-processes; Repeat re-fires single only; Esc via the embedded SequenceDetector; DispatchStats incl. esc). Prelude exports. Deviation: Lookup is a struct {exact, longer} (a chord can be bound and a prefix at once), no tracing records. Tests green locally (80 keybinding tests): the six named in the bead plus combo/chord parsing, repeat, esc, and proptest every_fed_key_yields_a_dispatch (1000 cases). clippy/rustdoc -D warnings run in progress at close time; SequenceDetector tests unchanged.

title: feature(G14): TOML/JSON round-trip for KeyMap behind the serde feature
description:
# feature(G14): TOML/JSON round-trip for KeyMap behind the serde feature

## Context and why this matters

README.md:1086 promises "**Serialization**: load/save binding maps for user customization". Vision row V62 (NOT_STARTED); Section 2.2.B row for `keybinding.rs` ("no ... load/save"). Without this, users of a FrankenTUI app cannot remap keys from a config file, and the README bullet is false. This bead makes `KeyMap<A>` (from `g14-impl`) serializable to TOML and JSON behind an opt-in cargo feature so consumers who do not want `serde`/`toml` in their tree pay nothing.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml` features (verified): `default = []`, `crossterm`, `tracing`, `tracing-json`, `caps-probe`, `test-helpers`. `serde = { version = "1.0.229", features = ["derive"] }` and `serde_json = "1.0.151"` exist only as dev-dependencies (:66-67). No `toml` dependency.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml`: `policy-config = ["dep:serde", "dep:serde_json", "dep:toml"]` with `toml = { version = "1.1.3", optional = true }` (:90) is the existing precedent for TOML config loading in the workspace.
- `keybinding.rs` has no serde derives; the plan document's step 2 says: "`serde` feature: derive on the types; `KeyMap::from_toml/to_toml` via the `toml` dep already used by `policy-config`".

## Target state

With `--features serde` on `ftui-core`:

- `KeyCombo` serializes as its `Display` string (`"Ctrl+x"`), `Chord` as `"Ctrl+x Ctrl+s"`, `Priority` as `"global"|"mode"|"widget"`, `ContextId` as the interned name string.
- `Binding<A: Serialize + DeserializeOwned>` and `KeyMap<A>` derive `Serialize`/`Deserialize`; the on-disk shape is a list of bindings plus the config block:

```toml
[config]
chord_timeout_ms = 1000

[[bindings]]
chord = "g g"
action = "scroll_top"
priority = "mode"
context = "log_search"
label = "Jump to top"
```

- `KeyMap::to_toml(&self) -> Result<String, KeyMapSerdeError>`, `from_toml(&str)`, `to_json`, `from_json`; `KeyMapSerdeError::{Parse(String), Combo(String), Chord(String)}` with line/column from `toml`.
- Unknown keys are rejected (`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`), chord strings are validated through `Chord::parse`, and contexts named in the file are interned on load.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml`: promote `serde` to an optional regular dependency, add `toml = { version = "1.1.3", optional = true }` (same version as `ftui-runtime`), add features `serde = ["dep:serde"]` and `keymap-toml = ["serde", "dep:toml"]`; `serde_json` becomes an optional dep pulled by `serde` (the JSON path) — keep dev-deps for tests.
2. `keybinding.rs`: `#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]` on the value types; custom `Serialize`/`Deserialize` for `KeyCombo` and `Chord` via `Display`/`FromStr` (`serde_with`-free: implement by hand in ~40 lines).
3. `KeyMap::{to_toml, from_toml}` under `keymap-toml`, `{to_json, from_json}` under `serde`; both validate and re-intern contexts; the loaded map keeps binding order (ids are reassigned sequentially on load and documented as not stable across saves).
4. `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`: facade feature `keymap-serde = ["ftui-core/keymap-toml"]` so consumers enable it with one flag; document in `docs/getting-started.md` features list (G01 owns the features narrative; add one line).
5. CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `features` job (:119-153) gains `cargo check -p ftui-core --features keymap-toml` and `cargo test -p ftui-core --features keymap-toml keybinding::serde_tests`.
6. Do NOT: make `serde` a default feature of ftui-core; add a YAML path; write a migration/versioning layer (a `version = 1` key is enough); create a separate `keymap_serde.rs` file unless the module is converted to a directory in `g14-impl`.
7. `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt` with and without the features; `ubs` before commit.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml`: features and optional deps.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/keybinding.rs`: derives, custom impls, `to_/from_` functions, `KeyMapSerdeError`.
- `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`: `keymap-serde` feature.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: features job lines.
- `docs/getting-started.md`: one line under features.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `keybinding::serde_tests::toml_round_trip_equals` and `json_round_trip_equals` (a map with 12 bindings incl. chords, all three priorities, two contexts) pass; equality compares chords, actions, priorities, contexts and labels (not ids).
- [ ] `toml_rejects_unknown_field`, `toml_rejects_bad_chord` (error message contains the offending string and line), `combo_display_parse_round_trip` proptest (`g14-tests`).
- [ ] `cargo check -p ftui-core` with no features still compiles (no accidental hard dependency).
- [ ] The `features` CI job is green with the new lines.

## Tests and logging

Unit tests under `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "keymap-toml"))]` in `keybinding.rs`; a doc example on `KeyMap::from_toml` doubles as a doctest (the README/getting-started snippet copies it, G02 makes README snippets doctests). On parse failure the error string is the log line; no tracing in this path.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by `g14-impl` (types must exist). Unblocks `g14-tests` (round-trip tests) and `g14-docs` (file format section in the spec).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: storing actions as arbitrary strings mapped at runtime; `A: Serialize` lets an app define `enum AppAction` with serde and get typed files for free.
- Rejected: `serde` as a default feature — ftui-core is the leaf crate and must stay dependency-light (AGENTS.md "composable crates" promise, V5).
- Risk: `toml 1.x` API differences from older examples; verify against current docs before use (AGENTS.md third-party rule).
- Rollback: feature-gated, so disabling the feature removes the surface.

## Definition of done

Feature compiles in all combinations, tests named above pass under the feature, CI features job green, close reason lists the test names and the CI run id.
close_reason: ftui-core feature `serde` (facade feature `serde` passes it through): KeyMapFile/BindingFile file shape (chords as text, contexts by name, chord_timeout_ms clamped on load, priority/context/label optional), KeyMap<A> Serialize/Deserialize via to_file/from_file, KeyMapFileError names the offending binding index. toml added as a dev-dependency. Test keymap_round_trips_through_toml_and_json (TOML + JSON, context by name, bad chord error, minimal-file defaults) green with --features serde; clippy --all-features clean. README serialization bullet describes the shipped format. Commit HEAD.

title: feature(G14): Route pane_keymap, showcase global keys and Help/KeybindingHints through KeyMap
description:
# feature(G14): Route pane_keymap, showcase global keys and Help/KeybindingHints through KeyMap

## Context and why this matters

The bridge plan's status arrow requires WORKING to mean "reachable from the production path (`Program`, `Frame`, `TerminalWriter`, a widget's `render`, or the showcase)". A keymap type that nothing uses would repeat the exact failure this reality check exists to catch (Section 2.3 item 2: hundreds of beads were closed on "module + unit tests exist" while wiring was treated as optional). This bead makes the showcase, the pane keyboard controller and the Help/KeybindingHints widgets consume `KeyMap`/`KeyDispatcher` from `g14-impl`, which is what README.md:1078-1086 ("Declarative binding maps ... Context-sensitive activation") describes and what G19 needs (hints derived from the real map).

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/pane_keymap.rs` (782 lines): `key_to_pane_command(key: &KeyEvent, resize_units: u16) -> Option<PaneCommand>` (:55) is a hand-written `match`; `PaneKeyOutcome` (:110); `PaneKeyboardController` (:133, `new(active)` :145, `handle_key` :241); `PaneKeyHint` (:329) and `pane_keyboard_hints() -> &'static [PaneKeyHint]` (:338) are a static list maintained separately from the `match`, so hints and behaviour can drift.
- Showcase `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs:4048-4160`: `text_input_active = self.screens.consumes_text_input(..)` (:4048) guards `q` (:4052) and `?` (:4071); other globals: `Ctrl+C` (:4056), `Ctrl+K` (:4058), `F12` (:4076), `F6` (:4081), `Ctrl+P` (:4086), `Ctrl+I` (:4090), `Tab`/`BackTab` (:4146/:4154), `l` large text (:4041). The help overlay is a `help_visible` flag (:4072); `rg` finds no use of `KeybindingHints` or `HelpRegistry` in `app.rs`, so the overlay text is hand-written.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/log_search.rs:900-909`: single `g` -> `scroll_to_top()`, `G` -> `scroll_to_bottom()`.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/advanced_text_editor.rs:580-582`: screen-local `KeyChord::new(KeyCode::Char('z'), Modifiers::CTRL)` for undo, `Ctrl+Y`/`Ctrl+Shift+Z` for redo; `update_status` (:1072) writes the status line.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/help.rs`: `Help { entries: Vec<HelpEntry>, mode, separator, ellipsis, key_style, desc_style, separator_style }` (:124-136), `HelpEntry::new(key, desc)` (:82, `with_enabled` :93, `with_category` :100), `Help::new` (:271), `with_entry` (:292), `with_entries` (:299), `entries()` (:348); `KeybindingHints` (:1088) with `with_global_entry` (:1172), `with_contextual_entry` (:1179), `with_key_format` (:1186). `crates/ftui-widgets/src/help_registry.rs`: `Keybinding` (:55), `new(key, action)` (:65). All display-only.

## Target state

- `pane_keymap.rs`: `PaneKeyboardController` owns a `KeyMap<PaneCommand>` built by `PaneKeyboardController::default_keymap(resize_units)`; `handle_key` runs a `KeyDispatcher`; `pane_keyboard_hints()` returns hints generated from the map's labels (same strings as today so `docs/spec/pane-keyboard-interaction.md` stays accurate).
- Showcase `app.rs`: a `KeyMap<AppAction>` with `enum AppAction { Quit, OpenPalette, ToggleHelp, ToggleDebug, ToggleMouseCapture, TogglePerfHud, ToggleInspector, NextScreen, PrevScreen, ToggleLargeText, .. }`, contexts `text_input` (active when `consumes_text_input`) so `q` and `?` are bound with `context: None` but shadowed by nothing; instead the map marks them `inactive_in: text_input` (implemented as: bind `q`/`?` at `Priority::Global` and give the text-input screens a `Priority::Widget` binding of the same keys to `AppAction::PassThrough` in the `text_input` context, which the dispatcher resolves first; `conflicts()` documents this intentional shadowing). The `?` help overlay renders `KeybindingHints::from_keymap(&map, &active_contexts)`.
- `log_search.rs`: `g g` -> top, `G` -> bottom (vim idiom, and the README's own example); the single-`g` binding goes away.
- `advanced_text_editor.rs`: the local `KeyChord` type is replaced by `KeyCombo`/`KeyMap<EditorAction>`; `Ctrl+x Ctrl+s` is bound to `EditorAction::Save` which writes `Saved` into the status line via `update_status` (there is no file I/O; "save" marks the buffer clean, as the screen already tracks modification state).
- `Help`/`KeybindingHints`: `from_keymap<A>(map: &KeyMap<A>, active: &[ContextId], describe: impl Fn(&A) -> String)` produces entries ordered by priority then chord; `KeybindingHints` marks context-bound entries as contextual. `help_registry::Keybinding` gains `From<&Binding<A>>`.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/help.rs` and `help_registry.rs`: add the `from_keymap` constructors (ftui-widgets already depends on ftui-core, `Cargo.toml:28`). No change to rendering.
2. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/pane_keymap.rs`: replace the body of `key_to_pane_command` with a lookup on a lazily built default map (`OnceLock<KeyMap<PaneCommand>>` keyed by `resize_units` is awkward; instead make `PaneKeyboardController` hold the map and keep `key_to_pane_command` as a thin call for the existing tests, then migrate those tests to the controller in the same bead — no wrapper left behind). Generate `pane_keyboard_hints()` from the map.
3. `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs`: introduce `AppAction`, build the map in `App::new`, replace the `match` at :4050-4160 with `dispatcher.feed(key, now)` handling; keep `consumes_text_input` to compute the active context set each event; forward `DispatchStats` into the showcase's existing JSONL emitters (the same pattern as `emit_palette_jsonl` at :4062) so `g14-e2e` can assert dispatch counts.
4. `screens/log_search.rs`: bind `g g`/`G` via a screen-local `KeyMap<LogSearchAction>` (screens keep local maps; the app map handles globals first, then passes `Unbound` keys to the screen).
5. `screens/advanced_text_editor.rs`: replace `KeyChord` (:580-582) with `KeyCombo`, add the `Ctrl+x Ctrl+s` chord and the `Saved` status.
6. Re-bless affected snapshots (help overlay, log_search, advanced_text_editor) with `BLESS=1 cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase` and review with `cargo insta review`.
7. Do NOT: keep both the `match` and the map ("compatibility"); leave `pane_keyboard_hints()` as a static list; change key assignments other than `g`->`g g` (documented in `g14-docs`); add a script to rewrite match arms (AGENTS.md: manual edits).
8. `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt`, `ubs` on changed files.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/help.rs`, `help_registry.rs`: `from_keymap`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/pane_keymap.rs`: map-backed controller and generated hints.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs`: `AppAction`, map, dispatcher, help overlay from hints.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/log_search.rs`, `advanced_text_editor.rs`: local maps, chords.

title: task(G14): Virtual-clock chord, priority, conflict and serde round-trip tests for the keymap
description:
# task(G14): Virtual-clock chord, priority, conflict and serde round-trip tests for the keymap

## Context

README.md:1078-1086 promises priorities, chords with timeout, contexts, conflict detection and serialization; the bridge plan's success criteria for G14 are "Unit tests with a virtual clock: chord completes within timeout, expires after, single-key bindings still fire while a chord is pending, priority resolution (widget beats mode beats global), `conflicts()` reports shadowed bindings" and "Round-trip test: `KeyMap -> TOML -> KeyMap` equality; JSON likewise". This bead is the companion test bead for `g14-impl` and `g14-impl-serde`. Timing tests must use explicit `Instant` values because wall-clock assertions are exactly what makes the current CI flaky (G04.2: `subscription.rs:1768` 188 ms > 100 ms on macOS; `every_respects_interval`).

## What to test

- Chord state machine timing and flushing; priority and context resolution; conflict reporting; parse/display of combos and chords; serialization round trips; the invariant that no key is ever dropped.

## Test types

Unit (in `crates/ftui-core/src/keybinding.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod keymap_tests`, `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "keymap-toml"))] mod serde_tests`):

- `chord_completes_within_timeout`: bind `g g` -> `Top`; feed `g` at t0 (expect `Pending{prefix:"g"}`), `g` at t0+300 ms (expect `Action{Top}`), with default timeout 1000 ms.
- `chord_expires_after_timeout`: feed `g` at t0, `tick(t0+1001 ms)` -> `Expired{prefix:"g"}`; if `g` alone is also bound, `Action{g-binding}` precedes `Expired`.
- `single_key_fires_while_chord_pending`: bind `g g` and `j` -> `Down`; feed `g` then `j` at t0+100 ms -> `[Unbound? no: Action{Down}]` and the pending prefix is cleared; feed `g` then `g` still works afterwards.
- `prefix_with_own_binding_fires_on_flush`: bind `g` -> `One` and `g g` -> `Two`; `g`, then `x` (unbound) -> `[Action{One}, Unbound(x)]`.
- `repeat_refires_single_key_only`: `KeyEventKind::Repeat` on `j` fires `Down` again; `Repeat` on `g` does not extend the chord.
- `release_is_ignored`: `KeyEventKind::Release` yields nothing.
- `widget_beats_mode_beats_global`: three bindings of `Enter` at each priority; lookup returns the widget one; removing it returns mode; then global.
- `active_context_beats_contextless`: `q` global Quit and `q` in context `text_input` -> `PassThrough`; with the context active the pass-through wins; inactive, Quit wins.
- `conflicts_reports_shadowed`: the two `q` bindings above at equal priority in overlapping contexts produce `Conflict::Shadowed{winner, loser}`.
- `conflicts_reports_prefix_collision`: `g` and `g g` bound -> `PrefixCollision{short, long}`; `Display` prints one line each containing both chord strings.
- `esc_delegates_to_sequence_detector`: `Esc`, `Esc` within 250 ms yields `Dispatch::Esc(SequenceOutput::..)` exactly as `SequenceDetector` alone would (compare against a bare detector fed the same events).
- `combo_parse_cases`: table of strings (`"Ctrl+x"`, `"ctrl+X"`, `"Shift+Tab"`, `"F12"`, `"Space"`, `"g"`, `"Alt+Shift+Left"`) to expected `KeyCombo`; invalid (`"Ctrl+"`, `"Foo"`, `""`) return `Err` with the offending token.
- `chord_parse_max_len`: five combos is an error; four is fine.

Property (proptest, same module):

- `every_fed_key_yields_a_dispatch`: arbitrary maps (up to 16 random chords of length 1-3 over a 6-key alphabet) and arbitrary key sequences with monotonic times; assert `feed` returns >= 1 `Dispatch` per key and the number of `Action`+`Unbound` outputs across the run equals the number of `Press` keys minus at most one pending prefix at the end.
- `combo_display_parse_round_trip`: `KeyCombo::from_str(&combo.to_string()) == combo` for arbitrary `KeyCode`/`Modifiers`.
- `lookup_is_deterministic_under_shuffle`: shuffling binding insertion order never changes an unambiguous lookup result (only conflicts may change winners, and those are reported).

Serde (feature `keymap-toml`):

- `toml_round_trip_equals`, `json_round_trip_equals`: 12 bindings including chords, all three priorities, two contexts, labels; compare chord/action/priority/context/label tuples.
- `toml_rejects_unknown_field`, `toml_rejects_bad_chord`: error contains the offending text and a line number.
- `toml_example_in_docs_parses`: the snippet in `g14-impl-serde` (also in `docs/spec/keybinding-policy.md`) is embedded with `include_str!` from a fixture under `crates/ftui-core/tests/fixtures/keymap_example.toml`.

Bench: none (no speed claim in the README for keybindings).

E2E: `g14-e2e`.

## Logging

Test failures print the full `Vec<Dispatch<A>>` via `Debug`; proptest shrinks and prints the minimal map plus key sequence. When the ftui-core `tracing` feature is on, dispatcher records carry `chord`, `binding_id`, `priority`, `context`, `pending_ms`, `outcome`.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-core/src/keybinding.rs` (test modules).
- `crates/ftui-core/tests/fixtures/keymap_example.toml` (new fixture; one file, justified as data not code).
- `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml`: `proptest` is already used elsewhere in the workspace; add as dev-dependency if ftui-core lacks it.

## Success criteria

- [ ] All tests above pass under `cargo test -p ftui-core` and `cargo test -p ftui-core --features keymap-toml`.
- [ ] No test sleeps; `rg 'thread::sleep' crates/ftui-core/src/keybinding.rs` returns nothing.
- [ ] Proptests run 1,000 cases locally (`PROPTEST_CASES=1000`) and the default 256 in CI.

## Dependencies

Blocked by `g14-impl` and `g14-impl-serde`. Referenced by `g14-docs` (test names go into the claims ledger).

## Definition of done

Tests exist and pass on the nextest run introduced by G03 (`cargo nextest run -p ftui-core`), close reason lists the test names, clippy/fmt clean.
close_reason: Added the genuine gaps in the G14 keymap test suite: prefix_with_own_binding_fires_on_flush, combo_display_parse_round_trip (proptest), lookup_is_deterministic_under_shuffle (proptest), toml_rejects_unknown_field_and_bad_chord (serde), toml_example_in_docs_parses (serde) + keymap_example.toml fixture + docs 9.3; hardened KeyMapFile/BindingFile with deny_unknown_fields. All pass; clippy -D warnings + fmt clean; no sleeps. See comment for honest deviations and self-run verification.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Completed the keymap test bead. Most prescribed unit/property/serde tests were
already present in keybinding.rs::keymap_tests and match the real dispatcher, so
I added only the genuine coverage gaps rather than duplicate them.

Added (all pass under `cargo test -p ftui-core [--features serde]`, PROPTEST_CASES=1000):
- prefix_with_own_binding_fires_on_flush: a bound prefix flushed by a
  non-extending UNBOUND key fires the prefix binding with NO Expired
  (timed_out=false path), then reports the key unbound. That no-Expired case
  was uncovered.
- combo_display_parse_round_trip (proptest): Display and FromStr are inverse
  over the normalized KeyCombo domain (curated KeyCode set incl. named/media/F
  keys + arbitrary modifier subsets). Display's alphabetic-Shift folding is
  absorbed by KeyCombo::new normalization, so the property holds domain-wide.
- lookup_is_deterministic_under_shuffle (proptest): a KeyMap built in insertion
  order vs a proptest-driven reordering yields identical exact-action and
  longer-count for arbitrary queries, over unique-chord sets (a duplicate is a
  reported conflict, not order-resolved).
- toml_rejects_unknown_field_and_bad_chord (serde): unknown top-level and
  per-binding fields are rejected, and a bad chord names its binding index.
- toml_example_in_docs_parses (serde): parses
  crates/ftui-core/tests/fixtures/keymap_example.toml via include_str! and
  asserts the resulting KeyMap; the same TOML now appears in
  docs/spec/keybinding-policy.md 9.3, so docs and parser cannot drift.

Impl change: added #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] to KeyMapFile and BindingFile
so a typo in a hand-edited keymap file fails loudly instead of silently
dropping a binding (this is what makes the reject test meaningful).

Honest deviations from the bead text (adapted to ground-truth code):
- The serde feature is `serde`, not `keymap-toml`; serde tests are gated
  #[cfg(feature = "serde")].
- The real dispatcher emits Expired BEFORE the fired action on timeout, and
  Release/non-extending keys yield Dispatch::Unbound (not nothing); the
  pre-existing tests already encode this and I matched it.
- "Ctrl+" parses as Ctrl + the '+' key (not an error), so invalid-combo cases
  use empty/unknown tokens.

Verification (self-run, local; rch remote builds): cargo test -p ftui-core and
--features serde green (5 new tests + 86 keybinding tests with serde, 14
default with serde tests correctly gated out); cargo clippy -p ftui-core
--all-targets [--features serde] -- -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --check clean;
rg 'thread::sleep' keybinding.rs empty. ubs on the changed file reports only
test-only panic!/alloc-in-loop heuristics (matching the file's existing chord()
helper convention). CI not observed.

# task(G14): PTY E2E test_keybinding_chords.sh and fix the three failing keybind_* cases

## Context and why this matters

Two promises meet here. README.md:1083 promises chord sequences (`g g`, `Ctrl+x Ctrl+s`); the bridge plan's G14 success criterion is "PTY E2E `tests/e2e/scripts/test_keybinding_chords.sh`: `g g` jumps to top in the log viewer screen, `Ctrl+x Ctrl+s` shows the save toast; the existing `keybind_*` cases pass." Separately, `main` CI is red (no green `ci.yml` run in 60, Section 1) and the PTY E2E job's real failures include `keybind_*` (3) per Section 5.1 ("42/166 failures: `rg` not installed on runners plus real assertion failures (cleanup x4, keybind x3, voi_marker x4, rtl_locale x4, mouse SGR, paste ...)"); G04.9 routes the keybind cluster to G14. This bead owns both: the new chord scenario and the root cause of the three failing cases, and it unblocks `g04-09-impl-keybind` (cluster B).

## Current state (evidence)

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_keybinding.sh` (verified): drives `E2E_HARNESS_BIN` (the `ftui-harness` binary, not the showcase), env `FTUI_HARNESS_LOG_KEYS=1` and `FTUI_HARNESS_SUPPRESS_WELCOME=1`, cases `keybind_ctrl_c_clears_input`, `keybind_ctrl_c_cancels_task`, `keybind_esc_clears_input`, `keybind_esc_cancels_task`, `keybind_esc_esc_toggles_tree`, `keybind_esc_closes_tree`, `keybind_ctrl_d_soft_quit`, `keybind_ctrl_q_hard_quit` (:82-89, :126+), JSONL `keybinding_e2e.jsonl` with run_id/case/env/seed/timings/checksums (:26-60), `run_case` wrapper (:97-124). Which three cases fail is not recorded in the plan document; the CI log of run `33152820289` (PTY E2E ubuntu) is the source.
- E2E library: `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` (`pty_run` :142, Python `pty` driver, `pty_canonicalize_file` :60, `pty_record_metadata` :72), `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh` (`require_cmd` :24, `resolve_python` :32), `tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh` (`jsonl_init`, `jsonl_assert`, `jsonl_step_start/end`), `tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py` (`--schema`, `--strict`, `--self-test`), `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json` (`common_required`: `schema_version, type, timestamp, run_id, seed`), `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh`. Scripts use `rg` (`test_inline.sh:57,118,135`) which runners lack until `g04-06-impl`.
- Showcase: `ScreenId::LogSearch` (app.rs:828) and `ScreenId::AdvancedTextEditor` (:833); env `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN` (numeric index, e.g. `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN=40` in `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh:2366`), `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS`, `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL` (main.rs:223). After `g14-impl-adopt`: LogSearch `g g` -> top, `G` -> bottom; AdvancedTextEditor `Ctrl+x Ctrl+s` -> `Saved` in the status line; `FTUI_DEMO_KEY_JSONL` emits one `key_dispatch` line per dispatch.
- CI: job `e2e-pty` at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:528` (`PTY E2E (${{ matrix.os }})`).

## Target state

`tests/e2e/scripts/test_keybinding_chords.sh` exists, is registered in `run_all.sh`, passes locally and in `e2e-pty` on ubuntu and macos, and the three `keybind_*` failures are root-caused and fixed (in the harness, the script, or the runtime, whichever the evidence shows), with the fix recorded in the bead.

## Implementation plan

1. Triage first: run `tests/e2e/scripts/test_keybinding.sh` locally under the same env as CI (`E2E_LOG_DIR` set, `rg` present) and, if it passes locally, fetch the CI job log (`gh run view 33152820289 --log`) to identify the three failing case names and their assertion text; write the root cause into this bead's comments before changing code. Likely candidates from the plan: timing of the Esc-Esc window (`DEFAULT_ESC_SEQ_TIMEOUT_MS = 250`, `keybinding.rs:98`) under slow runners; the harness ignoring `FTUI_HARNESS_LOG_KEYS`; `rg` absence masquerading as assertion failure. Fix the real cause; do not loosen assertions to pass.
2. Write `tests/e2e/scripts/test_keybinding_chords.sh` (bash, `set -euo pipefail`, sources `common.sh`, `logging.sh`, `pty.sh`, calls `require_cmd python3`):
   - Case `chord_gg_scrolls_to_top`: launch the showcase with `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN=<LogSearch index>` at 80x24, send `G` (bottom), wait 200 ms, send `g`, wait 150 ms, send `g`; canonicalize the screen and assert the first log line of the fixture is visible and the viewport indicator reads line 1; assert exactly one `key_dispatch` line with `"chord":"g g"` and `"outcome":"dispatched"` in `FTUI_DEMO_KEY_JSONL`.
   - Case `chord_gg_times_out`: send `g`, wait 1,300 ms, send `g`; assert no scroll-to-top dispatch (two `pending` lines, one `expired`), then `g g` quickly still works.
   - Case `single_key_not_blocked_by_pending_chord`: send `g` then `j` within 100 ms; assert the `j` (line down) binding dispatched and the prefix was flushed.
   - Case `chord_ctrl_x_ctrl_s_saves`: `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN=<AdvancedTextEditor index>`, type `hello`, send `\x18` (Ctrl+X) then `\x13` (Ctrl+S) within 300 ms; assert `Saved` appears in the status line and `"chord":"Ctrl+x Ctrl+s"` dispatched once.
   - Case `keybind_regressions`: re-run the three previously failing `keybind_*` cases via `test_keybinding.sh` and require pass (so this script fails if they regress).
   Each case writes JSONL through `logging.sh` and ends with `validate_jsonl.py --strict`.
3. Register in `run_all.sh`; add to the `e2e-pty` job's script list if the job enumerates scripts explicitly.
4. Do NOT: use `sleep`-based screen polling without a bound (use the existing `pty_run` timeouts); add `continue-on-error`; skip on macOS.
5. `ubs tests/e2e/scripts/test_keybinding_chords.sh` and `shellcheck` before commit.

## Files to change

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_keybinding_chords.sh` (new script; genuinely new scenario).
- `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh`: registration.
- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_keybinding.sh` and/or `crates/ftui-harness/src/*`: whatever the triage shows for the three failures.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: only if `e2e-pty` lists scripts explicitly.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `test_keybinding_chords.sh` 5/5 locally and in `e2e-pty` on both OS legs (CI run id in the close reason).
- [ ] `test_keybinding.sh` 8/8 in the same runs.
- [ ] `validate_jsonl.py --strict` passes over both scripts' JSONL.
- [ ] Root cause of each of the three failures written in the bead comments with the commit that fixed it.

## Tests and logging

PTY driver: `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` (Python `pty`). JSONL per case: `schema_version`, `type` (`case`/`assert`), `timestamp`, `run_id` (`keychord-<epoch ns>-<pid>`), `seed`, `scenario`, `identity` (`TERM`, `TERM_PROGRAM`), `screen` (`LogSearch`/`AdvancedTextEditor`), `dispatch_counts` (`dispatched`, `pending`, `expired`, `unbound`), `chord`, `escape_tallies` (`1049h/l`, `2026h/l`, `?25l/h`), `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, `pty_checksum` (sha256 of the raw capture, as `test_keybinding.sh` already does :43-49). Raw captures are archived under `E2E_LOG_DIR` and uploaded as job artifacts.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by `g14-impl-adopt` (chords in the showcase) and `g04-06-impl` (ripgrep and `require_tools` on runners; without it the CI leg cannot be green). Unblocks `g04-09-impl-keybind` (cluster B) and contributes to `g42-impl` (V62 verification row: `test_keybinding_chords.sh`).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: asserting on a toast; the AdvancedTextEditor screen has a status line (`update_status` :1072) and no toast API was found in `app.rs`; the status line is what `g14-impl-adopt` writes.
- Risk: chord timing on loaded runners; the script uses 150 ms between chord keys against a 1,000 ms timeout, leaving margin, and the timeout case waits 1,300 ms.
- Risk: numeric `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN` indices shift when screens are reordered; the script resolves the index from `ScreenId` names via a `--list-screens` flag if the binary has one, else documents the index next to the `ScreenId` enum line.

## Definition of done

Script green in CI on both legs, three legacy failures fixed with recorded root causes, JSONL validated, close reason cites the run id and case names.

- [ ] Spec sections 12-14 exist and quote the same defaults as `KeyMapConfig::default()` (a unit test `spec_defaults_match_code` in `keybinding.rs` greps the spec file for `chord_timeout_ms = 1000` and `250` next to "Esc" to keep them in sync).
