title: epic(G15): Editor undo coalescing, paragraph movement and outbound clipboard commands (PARTIAL -> WORKING)
description:
# epic(G15): Editor undo coalescing, paragraph movement and outbound clipboard commands (PARTIAL -> WORKING)

## Context and why this matters

README.md:1355-1362 ("Text Editor Core") promises, verbatim:

> The `Editor` module (1,800+ lines) provides:
> - **Cursor model** with visual position (column) vs byte offset tracking
> - **Selection** with anchor/head semantics (Shift+Arrow, Shift+Click)
> - **Word/line/paragraph movement** with Unicode word-boundary detection
> - **Undo/redo** with operation coalescing (typing "hello" = one undo step, not five)
> - **Clipboard integration** via `Cmd::SetClipboard` / `Cmd::GetClipboard`

The first two bullets are true. The last three are not: there is no paragraph movement, every
edit is its own undo step, and the runtime has no outbound clipboard command at all. This block
serves vision row V57 ("Editor core features", status PARTIAL) and two rows of the Section 2.2.C
README-mismatch table ("Editor: undo coalescing, paragraph movement" and "`Cmd::SetClipboard/GetClipboard`
... no clipboard variants (only inbound `Event::Clipboard`)"). The G06 CODE/DOC decision table marks
both rows **CODE, lands in G15**: the promised behaviour is user-visible value (an editor whose undo
undoes whole words, and a TUI that can copy to the system clipboard over SSH via OSC 52) and the
change is at most M, so we build it rather than retract it.

User-visible consequence today: in the `advanced_text_editor` showcase screen, typing a sentence
and pressing Ctrl+Z removes one character at a time; there is no way to jump between paragraphs;
and no FrankenTUI app can put text on the user's clipboard, even though the inbound half
(`Event::Clipboard` from an OSC 52 reply) is parsed and delivered.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-text/src/editor.rs:498-516` `push_undo(&mut self, op: EditOp)` pushes
  `(op, self.cursor)` onto `undo_stack: Vec<(EditOp, CursorPosition)>` (`:123`) for **every**
  operation, prunes by `max_history` and `max_undo_size`, and clears `redo_stack` (`:125`).
  `undo` (`:522`) and `redo` (`:536`) pop one op. `EditOp` is a private enum at `:34`
  (`Insert`, `Delete`, `Replace`). No grouping type exists.
- `crates/ftui-text/src/cursor.rs`: `CursorNavigator<'a> { rope: &'a Rope }` (`:13`) offers
  `move_left/right/up/down` (`:107-151`), `line_start/end` (`:162/:169`), `document_start/end`
  (`:179/:185`), `move_word_left/right` (`:195/:216`). No paragraph movement.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs:325-373` `Cmd<M>` has variants `None, Quit, Batch, Sequence,
  Msg, Tick, Log, Task, SaveState, RestoreState, SetMouseCapture(bool), SetTickStrategy`. No
  clipboard variant. `execute_cmd` (`:5951`) handles `Cmd::Log` at `:5986` and
  `Cmd::SetMouseCapture` at `:6011`.
- Inbound half exists: `crates/ftui-core/src/event.rs:52` `Event::Clipboard(ClipboardEvent)`,
  `ClipboardEvent { content, source }` `:437-448`, `ClipboardSource::{Osc52, Unknown}` `:458`;
  `crates/ftui-core/src/input_parser.rs:1230` builds `Event::Clipboard` from an OSC 52 reply
  (tests `:2698-2804`).
- The OSC 52 encoder already exists but in the wrong crate: `crates/ftui-extras/src/clipboard.rs`
  (1,861 lines, feature `clipboard = ["dep:base64", "dep:ftui-core"]` at `ftui-extras/Cargo.toml:46`)
  has `ClipboardSelection` `:24` with private `osc52_code()` `:36`, `Clipboard` `:103`,
  `DEFAULT_MAX_OSC52_PAYLOAD = 74_994` `:114`, `set(content, selection, writer)` `:339`,
  private `write_osc52` `:422`, `query_osc52` `:325`, tmux/screen DCS passthrough tests
  `:1031/:1049`. `ftui-runtime` does not depend on `ftui-extras` and `ftui-core` has no `base64`
  dependency, so the runtime cannot call this code today.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs` public API (`present_ui` `:1144`, `write_log`
  `:2151`, `flush` `:2345`) has no way to emit an arbitrary escape sequence through the one-writer path.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/advanced_text_editor.rs` uses `TextArea` (`:44`), has
  Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z undo/redo chords (`:580-582`) and no `y`/`p` or clipboard handling.

## Target state

Typing bursts coalesce into one undo step (break on word boundary, direction change, or 500 ms
idle); paragraph movement exists in `CursorNavigator`, `Editor` and `TextArea`;
`Cmd::SetClipboard(String)` and `Cmd::GetClipboard` emit OSC 52 through `TerminalWriter` and the
existing parser delivers `Event::Clipboard` on reply. The OSC 52 encoder lives in a small
`ftui-core` module used by both the runtime and `ftui-extras`. The `advanced_text_editor` screen
exercises all of it with `y` (yank) and `p` (paste).

## Success criteria

- [ ] Unit tests: typing "hello world" yields two undo steps; a run of `delete_backward` coalesces;
      paragraph movement over mixed blank-line layouts (single, double, whitespace-only, CRLF).
- [ ] PTY E2E `tests/e2e/scripts/test_clipboard_osc52.sh`: asserts `\x1b]52;c;<base64>\x07` on the
      wire for `SetClipboard`, and that a scripted reply produces exactly one `Event::Clipboard`
      (visible as pasted text and a status line).
- [ ] `TextArea` in the `advanced_text_editor` screen wired to both (`y` / `p`); snapshots re-blessed.
- [ ] README.md:1355-1362 bullets are true and the claims ledger rows for editor and clipboard cite
      the tests above.

## Implementation plan (children)

1. `g15-impl-undo`: `UndoGroup` coalescing in `editor.rs` with `break_undo_group()` and
   `set_coalesce_idle(Duration)` driven by an injectable clock.
2. `g15-impl-paragraph`: `move_paragraph_up/down` in `cursor.rs`, `Editor` and `TextArea`.
3. `g15-impl-clipboard`: `crates/ftui-core/src/osc52.rs` encoder, `Cmd::SetClipboard/GetClipboard`,
   `TerminalWriter::write_osc52_set/query`; `ftui-extras` clipboard delegates to core.
4. `g15-impl` (integrating, the bead other clusters depend on): `y`/`p`, Ctrl+Up/Down and group-aware
   undo depth in `advanced_text_editor.rs`.
5. `g15-tests`: unit and property tests for the three implementation beads.
6. `g15-e2e`: `test_clipboard_osc52.sh` under the PTY driver with JSONL logging.
7. `g15-docs`: README rows and claims-ledger rows.

Order: 1, 2 and 3 are independent and can run in parallel; 4 needs all three; 5 can start with any
one of 1-3; 6 needs 4; 7 needs 4.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by nothing. Unblocks: `g06-impl-ledger` rows for the editor/clipboard claims (G06 marks
them CODE and points here), `g02-impl` README doc-tests that mention `Cmd::SetClipboard`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- **base64 placement.** The encoder needs base64. Adding `base64 = "0.23.0"` (the version already in
  the workspace) to `ftui-core` as a regular dependency is the chosen route; the alternative of a
  hand-rolled 30-line encoder was rejected because a second base64 implementation is exactly the
  kind of duplicate the reality check flagged (V20/B). Not chosen either: making `ftui-runtime`
  depend on `ftui-extras` (it would invert the crate layering).
- **Mux passthrough.** Under tmux/screen OSC 52 must be DCS-wrapped; the extras crate already knows
  the forms (tests at `clipboard.rs:1031/:1049`). The core module keeps that logic and the writer
  decides from `TerminalCapabilities` mux evidence, so behaviour under tmux does not regress.
- **Idle timeout needs a clock.** A 500 ms idle break cannot be unit-tested with `Instant::now()`.
  The editor takes an injectable "now" so tests use a virtual clock; no sleeping in tests (this is
  the same lesson as G04.2's wall-clock flakiness).
- **No compatibility shims** (AGENTS.md): the extras encoder body is replaced by a call into core,
  not wrapped; `undo_stack`'s element type changes in place.
- **No deletion**: nothing is deleted; `clipboard.rs` keeps its backend/fallback logic.
- Rollback: each child is independently revertible; the `Cmd` variants are additive.

## Definition of done

All seven children closed with evidence in their close reasons (test names, snapshot names, E2E
JSONL path, CI run id for `e2e-pty`); README bullets rewritten; claims-ledger rows present;
`cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt` and `ubs` clean; main green for the touched jobs.

title: feature(G15): UndoGroup coalescing in ftui-text Editor (word boundary, direction change, 500 ms idle)
description:
# feature(G15): UndoGroup coalescing in ftui-text Editor (word boundary, direction change, 500 ms idle)

## Context and why this matters

README.md:1359 promises "**Undo/redo** with operation coalescing (typing "hello" = one undo step,
not five)". Today every keystroke is its own undo entry, so Ctrl+Z in any `TextArea` walks back one
character at a time. This bead closes the "Editor: undo coalescing" row of the Section 2.2.C
README-mismatch table (G06 decision: CODE, lands in G15) and part of vision row V57. It is the
first of three independent implementation beads under `g15-epic`.

Intent: undo should match what a user thinks of as "one edit": a typed word, a deleted run, a
paste. The rules must be deterministic and testable without sleeping, because the runtime test
binary already suffers from wall-clock assertions (G04.2).

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-text/src/editor.rs:34` `enum EditOp { Insert { byte_offset, text }, Delete {
  byte_offset, text }, Replace { byte_offset, deleted, inserted } }` (private).
- `:115` `pub struct Editor` with `undo_stack: Vec<(EditOp, CursorPosition)>` (`:123`),
  `redo_stack: Vec<(EditOp, CursorPosition)>` (`:125`), `max_history` / `max_undo_size` /
  `current_undo_size` (setters `set_max_history` `:175`, `set_max_undo_size` `:180`).
- `:498-516` `fn push_undo(&mut self, op: EditOp)`: pushes `(op, self.cursor)`, adds
  `op.byte_len()` to `current_undo_size`, prunes by count then by size, clears `redo_stack`.
  Called from `insert_char` `:258`, `insert_text` `:268`, `insert_newline` `:317`,
  `delete_backward` `:328`, `delete_forward` `:361`, `delete_word_backward` `:395`,
  `delete_word_forward` `:428`, `delete_to_end_of_line` `:462`, `set_text` `:791`.
- `:522` `pub fn undo(&mut self) -> bool` and `:536` `redo` pop exactly one `(EditOp, CursorPosition)`.
- `can_undo` `:222` / `can_redo` `:228` report stack emptiness; the showcase status line shows
  undo depth (`advanced_text_editor.rs` `with_undo_depth` `:259`), so the depth semantics change
  visibly when groups land.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/textarea.rs:458/:464` `TextArea::undo/redo` delegate to the editor.

## Target state

`undo_stack: Vec<UndoGroup>` where a group is a run of ops that undo together. Coalescing rules:

1. Consecutive single-grapheme inserts join the open `Insert` group unless the new grapheme is
   whitespace and the previous inserted grapheme was not (word boundary), or the group kind
   differs (direction change).
2. Consecutive `delete_backward` ops join a `DeleteBackward` group; consecutive `delete_forward`
   join a `DeleteForward` group; the two never mix.
3. `insert_text` with more than one grapheme (paste), `insert_newline`, `delete_word_*`,
   `delete_to_end_of_line`, `set_text` and `Replace` ops are always their own group (`Other`).
4. Any op arriving more than `coalesce_idle` (default 500 ms) after the group's last op starts a
   new group.
5. `break_undo_group()` closes the open group explicitly (callers use it on cursor moves,
   selection changes and focus loss).

`undo()` reverts a whole group in reverse op order and restores the cursor recorded at the group's
first op; `redo()` re-applies the whole group. Limits count groups for `max_history` and bytes for
`max_undo_size` (sum of `byte_len()` over the group's ops).

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-text/src/editor.rs`: add
   `enum GroupKind { Insert, DeleteBackward, DeleteForward, Other }` and
   `struct UndoGroup { ops: Vec<(EditOp, CursorPosition)>, kind: GroupKind, last_tick: u64,
   last_grapheme_was_space: bool }`; change `undo_stack` and `redo_stack` to `Vec<UndoGroup>`.
   Add `fn byte_len(&self)` on `UndoGroup`.
2. Replace `push_undo(op)` with `push_undo(op, kind)`: decide join-or-new by rules 1-5 above using
   `self.now_tick` and `self.coalesce_idle`; update `current_undo_size`; prune by group count and
   bytes; clear `redo_stack`. Update every caller listed above to pass its kind.
3. Clock: add `now_tick: u64` (milliseconds) and `coalesce_idle: Duration` fields; `pub fn
   set_coalesce_idle(&mut self, idle: Duration)`; `pub fn tick(&mut self, now_ms: u64)` sets the
   tick that the next op will be stamped with. `TextArea::handle_event` calls
   `editor.tick(now_ms)` from the runtime clock; tests call it directly with a virtual clock. Do not
   read `Instant::now()` inside `Editor` (keeps `ftui-text` free of wall-clock behaviour).
4. `pub fn break_undo_group(&mut self)`: marks the top group closed (a `closed: bool` flag) so the
   next op starts a new group. Call it from `set_cursor` `:208`, every `select_*` (`:702-732`),
   `clear_selection` `:744`.
5. `undo()` / `redo()`: iterate the group's ops (reverse for undo), reuse the existing per-op
   apply logic, restore cursor from `ops[0].1` on undo and from the last op's post-cursor on redo.
   `can_undo`/`can_redo` unchanged in meaning; add `pub fn undo_group_count(&self) -> usize` and
   `pub fn undo_op_count(&self) -> usize` so the showcase status can show both.
6. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/textarea.rs`: call `break_undo_group()` when focus is lost
   (`with_focus`/focus setter) and on cursor-movement keys; add `pub fn set_undo_coalesce_idle`.
7. What NOT to do: no `Vec<(EditOp, CursorPosition)>` compatibility path kept alongside groups; no
   new file (`editor.rs` stays the home); no wall-clock reads; no deletion of existing tests, they
   are updated to the group semantics.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-text/src/editor.rs`: `UndoGroup`, `GroupKind`, clock fields, `push_undo` rewrite,
  `undo`/`redo`, `break_undo_group`, `set_coalesce_idle`, `tick`, count accessors; existing tests
  updated.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/textarea.rs`: tick plumbing, `break_undo_group` calls, idle setter.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `typing_hello_world_yields_two_undo_steps`: after inserting `h e l l o ␠ w o r l d` one char
      at a time, `undo_group_count() == 2`; one `undo()` leaves `"hello "`; a second leaves `""`.
- [ ] `delete_backward_run_coalesces`: five `delete_backward` calls form one group; `undo()`
      restores all five characters and the cursor.
- [ ] `direction_change_breaks_group`: insert, delete, insert produce three groups.
- [ ] `idle_500ms_breaks_group`: `tick(0)`, insert `a`, `tick(501)`, insert `b` gives two groups;
      `tick(499)` gives one.
- [ ] `paste_is_own_group`: `insert_text("abc")` between single-char inserts yields three groups.
- [ ] Existing editor tests pass with updated expectations; `cargo clippy -D warnings` clean.

## Tests and logging

Unit tests live in `editor.rs`'s `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (see `g15-tests` for the full list and
the proptest `undo_all_returns_to_original_text_and_cursor`). On assertion failure, tests print a
JSONL line `{"test":"<name>","groups":<n>,"ops":<n>,"text":"<escaped>"}` so a CI log shows the
stack shape. Bench: none (no speed claim), but `cargo test -p ftui-text` must not slow measurably.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none. Unblocks: `g15-impl` (showcase wiring), `g15-tests`, `g15-docs`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative: coalesce in `TextArea` instead of `Editor`. Rejected: the README claim is about the
  `Editor` module and every consumer of `Editor` should get correct undo.
- Alternative: reuse `ftui_runtime::undo::HistoryManager` (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/undo/history.rs:104`)
  which has `MergeConfig`. Rejected: `ftui-text` must not depend on `ftui-runtime`, and the
  editor's ops are byte-offset edits, not boxed commands.
- Risk: memory accounting drift when groups are pruned partially. Mitigation: prune whole groups
  only; the proptest checks `current_undo_size` equals the recomputed sum after every op.
- Risk: showcase snapshots that display undo depth change. Mitigation: `g15-impl` re-blesses them
  and states the new numbers in its close reason.

## Definition of done

Reachable from the production path (`TextArea` in every app and the showcase); tests named above
green and cited in the close reason; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`,
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `ubs` on the
changed files clean; claims-ledger row updated by `g15-docs`.

title: feature(G15): Paragraph movement and selection in CursorNavigator/Editor using blank-line boundaries
description:
# feature(G15): Paragraph movement and selection in CursorNavigator/Editor using blank-line boundaries

## Context and why this matters

README.md:1358 promises "**Word/line/paragraph movement** with Unicode word-boundary detection".
Word and line movement exist; paragraph movement does not. This bead closes the "paragraph
movement" half of the Section 2.2.C row "Editor: undo coalescing, paragraph movement" (G06
decision: CODE, lands in G15) and part of vision row V57. It is independent of the other two G15
implementation beads and can run in parallel with them.

Intent: give `TextArea` users the standard editor motion (Emacs `M-{`/`M-}`, vim `{`/`}`,
most GUI editors Ctrl+Up/Down) and give the `advanced_text_editor` screen a visible feature to
demonstrate it.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-text/src/cursor.rs:9-12` `CursorPosition { line, grapheme, visual_col }`;
  `:13` `pub struct CursorNavigator<'a> { rope: &'a Rope }` with `new` `:20`, `clamp` `:51`,
  `from_line_grapheme` `:62`, `from_visual_col` `:73`, `to_byte_index` `:84`, `from_byte_index`
  `:96`, `move_left` `:107`, `move_right` `:124`, `move_up` `:141`, `move_down` `:151`,
  `line_start` `:162`, `line_end` `:169`, `document_start` `:179`, `document_end` `:185`,
  `move_word_left` `:195`, `move_word_right` `:216`. Private helpers `line_text(rope, line)`,
  `strip_trailing_newline`, `grapheme_count`, `move_word_left_in_line` are used by the word moves.
- No function in `cursor.rs`, `editor.rs` or `textarea.rs` mentions paragraphs.
- `crates/ftui-text/src/editor.rs:702-732` has `select_left/right/up/down/word_left/word_right/all`;
  each movement has a selection twin, so paragraph movement needs `select_paragraph_up/down` too.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/textarea.rs:118` `handle_event(&mut self, event: &Event) -> bool` maps
  keys to editor calls (`select_word_left` at `:165`, `select_word_right` at `:177`).

## Target state

- `CursorNavigator::move_paragraph_up(pos)` and `move_paragraph_down(pos)`.
  Definition: a *blank line* is a line whose text after `strip_trailing_newline` is empty or
  consists only of Unicode whitespace. A *paragraph* is a maximal run of non-blank lines.
  - `move_paragraph_down`: from inside a paragraph, go to the first blank line after it (column 0);
    from a blank line, skip the blank run, then the following paragraph, landing on the blank line
    after that paragraph; if no blank line follows, `document_end()`.
  - `move_paragraph_up`: from inside a paragraph (not on its first line), go to its first line
    (column 0)... then to the blank line before it; from a blank line, skip the blank run upward,
    then the paragraph above it, landing on the blank line before that paragraph; if none,
    `document_start()`.
  These mirror vim `}` / `{`, which land on blank lines, so repeated presses walk paragraph by
  paragraph.
- `Editor::move_paragraph_up/down()` (clear selection, move) and `select_paragraph_up/down()`
  (keep anchor, move head).
- `TextArea::handle_event`: `Ctrl+Up` / `Ctrl+Down` move; `Ctrl+Shift+Up` / `Ctrl+Shift+Down`
  select. `Alt+{` / `Alt+}` are not bound by default because `crates/ftui-core/src/input_parser.rs:410-416`
  keeps `ESC _`/`ESC ^`/`ESC X` as Alt introducers only for the sibling C1 strings, and shifted
  Alt-punctuation is terminal-dependent; apps may bind them through G14's keymap.
- CRLF: `strip_trailing_newline` already handles `\r\n`; a line containing only `\r` counts as blank.
  A trailing newline at document end does not create a phantom paragraph.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-text/src/cursor.rs`: add `fn is_blank_line(rope, line) -> bool` (uses
   `line_text` + `strip_trailing_newline` + `char::is_whitespace`), then
   `pub fn move_paragraph_down(&self, pos: CursorPosition) -> CursorPosition` and
   `pub fn move_paragraph_up(&self, pos: CursorPosition) -> CursorPosition` implementing the
   definitions above with `from_line_grapheme(line, 0)`; `#[must_use]` like the neighbours.
2. `crates/ftui-text/src/editor.rs`: `pub fn move_paragraph_up(&mut self)`, `move_paragraph_down`,
   `select_paragraph_up`, `select_paragraph_down`, following the pattern of `move_word_*` /
   `select_word_*` (`:722-727`). Each calls `break_undo_group()` once `g15-impl-undo` lands (if
   that bead is not merged yet, leave a one-line call site ready; do not block on it).
3. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/textarea.rs`: in `handle_event` add the four key arms next to the
   word-motion arms (`:165-177`); expose `pub fn move_paragraph_up/down` and
   `select_paragraph_up/down` so screens can call them from custom bindings.
4. Rustdoc on each new function states the blank-line rule with a three-paragraph example.
5. What NOT to do: no new file; no `Alt+{` default binding; no change to `move_up/move_down`
   semantics; no wall-clock code.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-text/src/cursor.rs`: `is_blank_line`, `move_paragraph_up`, `move_paragraph_down`, tests.
- `crates/ftui-text/src/editor.rs`: four public methods.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/textarea.rs`: key arms and four public methods.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `move_paragraph_down_over_mixed_blank_lines` (fixture: three paragraphs separated by one
      blank line, two blank lines, and a whitespace-only line; CRLF variant): the sequence of
      `line` values after repeated `move_paragraph_down` from `(0,0)` is exactly the blank-line
      indices then the last line.
- [ ] `move_paragraph_up_from_document_end` walks back through the same indices in reverse and
      ends at `(0,0)`.
- [ ] `paragraph_move_on_single_paragraph_document` goes to `document_end` / `document_start`.
- [ ] `select_paragraph_extends_selection`: anchor unchanged, head equals the move target,
      `selected_text()` equals the expected slice.
- [ ] `textarea_ctrl_down_moves_paragraph`: `TextArea::handle_event` with `KeyCode::Down` +
      `Modifiers::CTRL` changes the cursor line as the navigator predicts.
- [ ] Proptest `paragraph_moves_are_monotone_and_idempotent_at_ends`: for random documents of
      up to 40 lines built from `{"", "  ", "\t", "word", "two words"}`, `move_paragraph_down`
      never decreases `line`, `move_paragraph_up` never increases it, and both are fixed points
      at `document_end` / `document_start`.

## Tests and logging

Unit and property tests in `cursor.rs` and `editor.rs` test modules (detailed in `g15-tests`).
Failure output includes the fixture as escaped JSON (`{"test":..,"fixture":..,"visited":[..]}`).
No bench (no speed claim). E2E coverage arrives through `g15-e2e` only indirectly (the screen's
status line); the primary proof is unit-level.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none. Unblocks: `g15-impl` (Ctrl+Up/Down in the showcase), `g15-tests`, `g15-docs`.
Soft relation to `g15-impl-undo` (calls `break_undo_group` when available; not a blocker).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative definition (land on the first line of the next paragraph, GUI style) rejected in
  favour of the vim/Emacs blank-line landing because it makes `up` and `down` exact inverses and
  the proptest simple. The docs state the rule so consumers are not surprised.
- Whitespace-only lines count as blank (matches vim's behaviour with `'paragraphs'` defaults being
  irrelevant for plain text). This is a stated decision, not an accident.
- Risk: performance on very long documents (`is_blank_line` per line). Each call is O(lines in the
  skipped region) over the rope's line iterator, which is already how `move_word_*` walk text; no
  new allocation per line beyond the existing `line_text` `Cow`.

## Definition of done

Reachable from `TextArea` (production path) and the showcase (via `g15-impl`); the tests above are
green and named in the close reason; check/clippy/fmt/ubs clean; README bullet corrected by
`g15-docs`.

title: feature(G15): Cmd::SetClipboard/GetClipboard with OSC 52 encoder in ftui-core and TerminalWriter write path
description:
# feature(G15): Cmd::SetClipboard/GetClipboard with OSC 52 encoder in ftui-core and TerminalWriter write path

## Context and why this matters

README.md:1362 promises "**Clipboard integration** via `Cmd::SetClipboard` / `Cmd::GetClipboard`".
The Section 2.2.C table records: "`Cmd::perform(future, mapper)`, `Cmd::SetClipboard/GetClipboard`,
`tick_every`, `file_watcher`" versus code "`Cmd::task/task_with_spec/task_named`; no clipboard
variants (only inbound `Event::Clipboard`); `Every` subscription; no FS watcher". The G06 decision
table marks `Cmd::SetClipboard/GetClipboard` **CODE, lands in G15** (the `tick_every`/`file_watcher`
half is G16, `Cmd::perform` is a DOC row in G06).

Why it matters: OSC 52 is the only clipboard mechanism that works over SSH and inside terminal
multiplexers, and the inbound half (parsing an OSC 52 reply into `Event::Clipboard`) is already
shipped. Without the outbound half no FrankenTUI application can copy text out, which makes the
`advanced_text_editor` screen and any agent-harness consumer (G26) feel broken. It also enforces
the one-writer rule: the escape sequence must go through `TerminalWriter`, never a stray
`stdout.write_all`.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs:325-373` `pub enum Cmd<M>`: `None, Quit, Batch, Sequence,
  Msg, Tick, Log, Task(TaskSpec, Box<dyn FnOnce() -> M + Send>), SaveState, RestoreState,
  SetMouseCapture(bool), SetTickStrategy(Box<dyn TickStrategy>)`. Debug impl `:375-388`; name
  match `:458`; a builder helper at `:537` (`Self::SetMouseCapture(enabled)`); constructors `none`
  `:397`, `quit` `:403`, `batch` `:423`, `task` `:474`, `task_with_spec` `:482`, `task_named` `:498`.
  Tests that enumerate command names live at `:13921` and `:14030`.
- `:5874` `execute_lifecycle_cmd`, `:5951` `execute_cmd` with arms `Cmd::Log` `:5986` and
  `Cmd::SetMouseCapture` `:6011` (the template for a new side-effect arm).
- `:5801` `Event::Clipboard(_)` is already classified as `FairnessEventType::Input`.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/event.rs:52` `Event::Clipboard(ClipboardEvent)`; `:437-448`
  `ClipboardEvent { content, source }` + `new`; `:458` `ClipboardSource::{Osc52, Unknown}`.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/input_parser.rs:1230` produces `Event::Clipboard(ClipboardEvent::new(..,
  ClipboardSource::Osc52))` from `ESC ] 52 ; <sel> ; <base64> BEL|ST` (tests `:2698`, `:2709`, `:2804`).
- `crates/ftui-extras/src/clipboard.rs` (1,861 lines; feature `clipboard = ["dep:base64",
  "dep:ftui-core"]`, `ftui-extras/Cargo.toml:46`): `ClipboardSelection` `:24` with private
  `osc52_code(self) -> Result<char, ClipboardError>` `:36` (`'c'`, `'p'`, `'s'`, cut buffers 0-7),
  `ClipboardBackend` `:51`, `ExternalBackend` `:59`, `ClipboardError` `:79`, `Clipboard` `:103`
  with `osc52_timeout` `:108`, `DEFAULT_MAX_OSC52_PAYLOAD: usize = 74_994` `:114`,
  `DEFAULT_OSC52_TIMEOUT = 100 ms` `:116`, `new(caps)` `:122`, `detect` `:144`, `auto` `:188`,
  `with_max_payload` `:255`, `supports_osc52` `:279`, `with_mux_passthrough` `:301`,
  `query_osc52` `:325`, `set(content, selection, writer)` `:339`, `set_with_fallback` `:369`,
  `clear` `:379`, `get` `:396`, private `write_osc52` `:422`. Tests: tmux wrap
  `ESC P tmux; ESC ESC ] 52;c;<base64> BEL ESC \` `:1031`, screen wrap `:1049`, base64 validity
  `:1191`, payload cap `:1282-1293`, `:1820`.
- `ftui-core/Cargo.toml` has no `base64`; `ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml:85-90` has `base64` only under
  `state-persistence`; `ftui-runtime` does not depend on `ftui-extras`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs` exposes `present_ui` `:1144`, `present_ui_owned`
  `:1268`, `write_log` `:2151`, `flush` `:2345`; nothing writes an arbitrary escape sequence.

## Target state

- `crates/ftui-core/src/osc52.rs` (new, small, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` inherited): `pub enum
  ClipboardSelection` (moved from extras, same variants), `pub fn selection_code(sel) -> Option<char>`,
  `pub const MAX_OSC52_PAYLOAD: usize = 74_994`, `pub fn encode_set(sel, bytes: &[u8]) ->
  Result<Vec<u8>, Osc52Error>` producing `ESC ] 52 ; <sel> ; <base64> BEL`, `pub fn
  encode_query(sel) -> Vec<u8>` producing `ESC ] 52 ; <sel> ; ? BEL`, `pub enum Mux { Tmux, Screen }`
  and `pub fn wrap_for_mux(mux, seq: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>` (DCS passthrough, byte-identical to the
  forms asserted at `clipboard.rs:1031/:1049`), `pub enum Osc52Error { PayloadTooLarge { len, max },
  InvalidSelection }`.
- `Cmd::SetClipboard(String)` and `Cmd::GetClipboard` with constructors `Cmd::set_clipboard(text)`
  and `Cmd::get_clipboard()`; `execute_cmd` arms call the writer.
- `TerminalWriter::write_osc52_set(&mut self, sel: ClipboardSelection, bytes: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()>`
  and `write_osc52_query(&mut self, sel) -> io::Result<()>`: encode via core, wrap when
  `TerminalCapabilities` reports a mux (the same evidence `use_sync_output()` consults), append to
  the frame output buffer so the sequence is flushed in the same write as the next present (one
  writer, one `write` per frame preserved), and log `target: "ftui.runtime"` (constant from
  `telemetry_schema` once G20 lands) with `bytes` and `wrapped`.
- Headless/simulator programs (`headless_program_with_resolved_config`, `ProgramSimulator`) record
  each call in `clipboard_requests: Vec<ClipboardRequest::{Set(String), Get}>` exposed for tests.
- `ftui-extras` `clipboard.rs` uses `ftui_core::osc52` for encoding (its `write_osc52` body and
  `ClipboardSelection` definition are replaced by calls/re-exports); its backend/fallback logic is
  unchanged.
- The reply path is unchanged: the parser's `Event::Clipboard` reaches `Model::update`.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml`: add `base64 = "0.23.0"` (regular dependency; version already in
   the workspace). `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs`: `pub mod osc52;`.
2. Write `crates/ftui-core/src/osc52.rs` as specified, with unit tests moved/adapted from
   `clipboard.rs:1191`, `:1282-1293`, `:1031`, `:1049`.
3. `crates/ftui-extras/src/clipboard.rs`: `pub use ftui_core::osc52::ClipboardSelection;` in place
   of the local enum; `write_osc52` `:422` becomes a call to `encode_set` + `wrap_for_mux` when
   `with_mux_passthrough` is set; `clear` uses `encode_set(sel, b"")`; `query_osc52` uses
   `encode_query`. Keep `Clipboard`, backends, fallback, timeout. Delete nothing.
4. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: add the two variants (after `SetMouseCapture`), Debug arms
   at `:375-388`, name arm at `:458`, constructors next to `:397-498`, `execute_cmd` arms after
   `:6011`; update the enumerating tests at `:13921` and `:14030`.
5. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`: `write_osc52_set` / `write_osc52_query` as
   specified; a private `pending_control: Vec<u8>` appended before the next present's bytes (or
   flushed immediately when no frame is pending, via the existing `flush` `:2345`).
6. Headless recording: `clipboard_requests` on the headless writer path; `ProgramSimulator` getter
   `clipboard_requests()`.
7. What NOT to do: no `ftui-runtime -> ftui-extras` dependency; no second base64 implementation; no
   direct `stdout` writes; no compatibility re-export of the old private encoder; no feature gate on
   the `Cmd` variants (they are core runtime surface; the feature gate stays on extras' external
   backends only).

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml`: `base64` dependency.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs`: `pub mod osc52`.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/osc52.rs`: new module (encoder, selection, mux wrap, tests).
- `crates/ftui-extras/src/clipboard.rs`: delegate encoding to core; keep backends.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `Cmd` variants, constructors, `execute_cmd` arms, tests.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`: `write_osc52_set`, `write_osc52_query`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/simulator.rs` (or wherever `ProgramSimulator` lives): recorded requests.
- `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`: re-export `osc52::ClipboardSelection` alongside `Cmd`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `osc52_encode_set_matches_wire_format`: `encode_set(Clipboard, b"hello")` ==
      `b"\x1b]52;c;aGVsbG8=\x07"`.
- [ ] `osc52_encode_query`: `encode_query(Clipboard)` == `b"\x1b]52;c;?\x07"`.
- [ ] `osc52_payload_cap`: input whose base64 exceeds 74_994 bytes returns `PayloadTooLarge`.
- [ ] `osc52_tmux_wrap` / `osc52_screen_wrap`: byte-identical to the forms at `clipboard.rs:1031/:1049`.
- [ ] `cmd_set_clipboard_reaches_writer_headless`: a headless program whose model returns
      `Cmd::set_clipboard("hi")` records `ClipboardRequest::Set("hi")`.
- [ ] `cmd_get_clipboard_then_reply_yields_event`: `Cmd::get_clipboard()` records `Get`; injecting
      `Event::Clipboard(ClipboardEvent::new("hi", Osc52))` reaches `update` once.
- [ ] Extras tests `set_writes_osc52_sequence` (`:928`), `clear_writes_empty_osc52_sequence`
      (`:964`) and the mux tests still pass unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo check -p ftui-core --no-default-features` builds (encoder has no feature gate).

## Tests and logging

Unit tests in `osc52.rs`, `program.rs` and `terminal_writer.rs` (`g15-tests` lists them). The
writer logs one structured line per clipboard write (`event = "osc52_write"`, `selection`,
`payload_b64_len`, `wrapped`); E2E proof on a real PTY is `g15-e2e`. No bench.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none. Unblocks: `g15-impl` (showcase `y`/`p`), `g15-tests`, `g15-e2e`, `g15-docs`,
and the G26 agent-shell example's copy feature.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative: keep the encoder in extras and make the runtime depend on extras under a feature.
  Rejected: inverts the layering (`ftui-extras` already depends on `ftui-runtime` optionally at
  `ftui-extras/Cargo.toml:18`) and would create a cycle.
- Alternative: hand-written base64 in core to avoid the dependency. Rejected: duplicates a
  dependency the workspace already carries; the reality check explicitly flags parallel
  implementations (Section 2.3 item 2).
- Risk: terminals that do not support OSC 52 silently ignore the write; the query then never
  replies. `Cmd::GetClipboard` is fire-and-forget; apps that need a timeout use `Cmd::Tick`. The
  writer consults `TerminalCapabilities::osc52_clipboard` (already a field, see
  `clipboard.rs:875`) and logs `skipped_unsupported` instead of writing when it is false.
- Risk: mux passthrough doubles ESC bytes; the wrap function is tested byte-for-byte.
- Rollback: the variants are additive; reverting the extras delegation restores its private encoder.

## Definition of done

Reachable from the production path (`Program::execute_cmd` -> `TerminalWriter`), tests above green
and named in the close reason, `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt` and `ubs` clean on all touched
files, claims-ledger row for `Cmd::SetClipboard/GetClipboard` updated by `g15-docs`.

title: feature(G15): Wire yank/paste (y/p) and coalesced undo into the advanced_text_editor screen
description:
# feature(G15): Wire yank/paste (y/p) and coalesced undo into the advanced_text_editor screen

## Context and why this matters

This is the integrating bead of G15 and the one other clusters depend on (`g15-e2e`, `g15-docs`,
and G06's ledger rows reference it). The three sibling beads add `UndoGroup` coalescing
(`g15-impl-undo`), paragraph movement (`g15-impl-paragraph`) and `Cmd::SetClipboard/GetClipboard`
with the OSC 52 writer path (`g15-impl-clipboard`). Per the reality check's definition of WORKING
("reachable from the production path ... or the showcase, covered by a named test, and where
relevant proven by an E2E script"), none of them is done until a showcase screen exercises them
under a PTY. The plan's third success criterion for G15 is verbatim: "`TextArea` in the
`advanced_text_editor` screen wired to both (`y`/`p`)".

Serves vision row V57 and the Section 2.2.C rows for editor and clipboard; gives `g15-e2e` a real
screen to drive.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/advanced_text_editor.rs` (68 KB): module docs list
  "`TextArea` with line numbers, selection highlighting" (`:6`), "Undo/redo integration" (`:9`),
  "Observable hooks for search, replace, undo/redo, and text edit events" (`:15`); imports
  `ftui_widgets::textarea::TextArea` (`:44`); an observable event enum with `UndoPerformed` /
  `RedoPerformed` (`:135-136`); a status struct with `undo_depth: Option<usize>` /
  `redo_depth` (`:165-167`, builders `with_undo_depth` `:259`, `with_redo_depth` `:266`); a
  screen-local `KeyChord` type binding undo to Ctrl+Z and redo to Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z
  (`:580-582`); Ctrl+U / Ctrl+F / Ctrl+H handlers (`:1419-1445`); F3 or Ctrl+G find-next (`:1484`);
  Ctrl+R / Ctrl+A in the replace prompt (`:1574-1578`); `update_status` (`:1072`); `update`
  (`:1293`). No `y`, no `p`, no `Clipboard`, no paragraph keys.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/textarea.rs`: `handle_event` `:118`, `selection` `:375`,
  `selected_text` `:381`, `editor()` `:398`, `editor_mut()` `:403`, `insert_text` `:410`,
  `undo` `:458`, `redo` `:464`.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml` default features include `clipboard =
  ["ftui-extras/clipboard"]`; the showcase binary sets `with_evidence_sink` when
  `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL` is set (`main.rs:223`).
- `ScreenId::AdvancedTextEditor` (`app.rs:833`, dispatch `:1174`); `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN` selects it.
- `Event::Clipboard` reaches screens: `action_timeline.rs:269` and `macro_recorder.rs:1291`
  already match on it, so the app's event routing passes it through.

## Target state

In the `advanced_text_editor` screen:

- `y` with an active selection (and the editor not in the search/replace prompt) returns
  `Cmd::set_clipboard(selected_text)`; status line reads `Copied N chars`. Without a selection,
  `y` copies the current line (vim `yy` spirit, single key for simplicity) and says
  `Copied line N`.
- `p` returns `Cmd::get_clipboard()`; status reads `Requesting clipboard…`; on
  `Event::Clipboard(ev)` the screen inserts `ev.content` at the cursor via `insert_text` and sets
  status `Pasted N chars` (N = grapheme count). Bracketed `Event::Paste` keeps its existing path.
- Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down move by paragraph; Ctrl+Shift+Up / Down select by paragraph (delegated to
  `TextArea` from `g15-impl-paragraph`).
- Undo depth in the status shows `groups/ops` (e.g. `undo 2/11`) from
  `Editor::undo_group_count()` / `undo_op_count()`.
- `y` and `p` are plain keys, so they must not fire while the user is typing text. The screen
  has no vim-style modal state today; define one: a single `edit_mode: EditMode::{Insert, Normal}`
  toggled by `Esc` (Normal) and `i` (Insert), shown in the status line. Insert is the default so
  existing snapshots and `test_text_editor.sh` keep their behaviour; `y`, `p`, and paragraph
  keys are available in both modes when they carry Ctrl, and `y`/`p` bare keys only in Normal.

## Implementation plan

1. `advanced_text_editor.rs`: add `EditMode` and `edit_mode` field; `Esc` in Insert mode with no
   overlay open switches to Normal (existing Esc-closes-prompt behaviour takes precedence);
   `i` in Normal switches back. Render the mode in the status bar.
2. Key handling in `update` (`:1293`) after the prompt handlers: `y` (Normal) → build
   `Cmd::set_clipboard`; `p` (Normal) → `Cmd::get_clipboard()`; `Ctrl+Up/Down`,
   `Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down` → `TextArea` paragraph methods. Emit the screen's observable events
   (`ClipboardCopied { chars }`, `ClipboardPasteRequested`, `ClipboardPasted { chars }`) next to
   `UndoPerformed` so `test_text_editor.sh`-style hooks can see them.
3. `Event::Clipboard(ev)` arm in `update`: insert content, set status, return `Cmd::None`.
4. `update_status` (`:1072`): populate undo/redo depth from the group and op counts; add the
   mode and the last clipboard message (cleared after the next keystroke).
5. Help overlay entries (`?`) for `y`, `p`, `Esc`/`i`, `Ctrl+Up/Down`.
6. Snapshots: re-bless the screen's insta snapshots (`BLESS=1 cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase`)
   and record the changed names in the close reason; add snapshots
   `advanced_text_editor_normal_mode_80x24` and `advanced_text_editor_after_paste_80x24`
   (paste driven by injecting `Event::Clipboard` in the test).
7. What NOT to do: no new screen file; no direct writes to stdout; no `Cmd::Task` thread to poll
   the clipboard (the reply arrives as an event); no wall-clock dependency for the status message.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/advanced_text_editor.rs`: mode, keys, clipboard event,
  status, help entries, tests.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/snapshots/*advanced_text_editor*.snap`: re-blessed and new.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs`: only if the `?` help text is generated centrally.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Unit test `yank_selection_returns_set_clipboard_cmd`: select "hello", press `y` in Normal
      mode, the returned `Cmd` matches `Cmd::SetClipboard(s) if s == "hello"`, status contains
      `Copied 5 chars`.
- [ ] `paste_key_requests_clipboard_and_reply_inserts`: `p` returns `Cmd::GetClipboard`; injecting
      `Event::Clipboard(ClipboardEvent::new("abc", ClipboardSource::Osc52))` inserts `abc` at the
      cursor and status contains `Pasted 3 chars`.
- [ ] `bare_y_in_insert_mode_types_y`: in Insert mode `y` inserts the character.
- [ ] `ctrl_down_moves_to_next_blank_line` on the screen's sample document.
- [ ] `status_shows_undo_groups`: after typing "ab cd" the status contains `undo 2/5`.
- [ ] Snapshots re-blessed; `cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase` green; `tests/e2e/scripts/test_text_editor.sh`
      still passes (Insert is the default mode).

## Tests and logging

Screen unit tests in the file's `#[cfg(test)]` module using the existing `ctrl_press` helper
pattern (`:1770-1809`). The screen's observable events are the log surface used by
`g15-e2e` through the status line and by `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL` if the screen already emits
JSONL for edits (extend the existing hook with `clipboard_copied` / `clipboard_pasted` lines
carrying `chars` and `mode`).

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g15-impl-undo` (group counts), `g15-impl-paragraph` (Ctrl+Up/Down),
`g15-impl-clipboard` (the `Cmd` variants). Unblocks: `g15-e2e`, `g15-docs`; referenced by
`g06-impl-ledger` rows for the editor and clipboard claims.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative: bind copy/paste to Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V. Rejected: the app-level handler in
  `app.rs:4056` maps Ctrl+C to `Cmd::Quit` before screens see it, and Ctrl+V is commonly the
  terminal's own paste (delivered as bracketed `Event::Paste`). The plan names `y`/`p`.
- Alternative: make `y`/`p` always active. Rejected: they would swallow typed letters; hence the
  minimal Normal/Insert mode.
- Risk: OSC 52 unsupported terminals never reply to `p`; status stays at "Requesting…" until the
  next keystroke clears it. Acceptable for a demo; documented in the help overlay.
- Risk: snapshot churn in a 68 KB screen. Mitigation: only the status line and help text change;
  the close reason lists every re-blessed file.

## Definition of done

Screen reachable in the showcase (`FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN` for `AdvancedTextEditor`); the unit tests
above and the re-blessed snapshots are named in the close reason; `g15-e2e` can drive `y`/`p`
under a PTY; `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt` and `ubs` clean; README/ledger updated by
`g15-docs`.

title: task(G15): Unit and property tests for undo coalescing, paragraph movement and OSC 52 encoding
description:
# task(G15): Unit and property tests for undo coalescing, paragraph movement and OSC 52 encoding

## Context

Companion test bead for the three G15 implementation beads. README.md:1355-1362 promises
paragraph movement, undo coalescing ("typing "hello" = one undo step, not five") and
`Cmd::SetClipboard` / `Cmd::GetClipboard`. The reality check found `push_undo`
(`crates/ftui-text/src/editor.rs:498-516`) pushes every op, `cursor.rs` has word but no paragraph
moves (`:195/:216`), and `Cmd` (`program.rs:325-373`) has no clipboard variants. These tests are
the named proof the plan requires; their names go into the claims-ledger rows (`g15-docs`) and
into each implementation bead's close reason. All timing uses an injected tick, never
`thread::sleep` (G04.2 lesson: wall-clock tests flake on shared runners).

## What to test

1. Undo grouping rules (word boundary, direction change, idle timeout, paste, explicit break) and
   that undo/redo of a group restores text and cursor exactly.
2. Paragraph navigation over mixed blank-line layouts, CRLF, document edges, and selection twins.
3. OSC 52 encoding (set, query, cap, mux wrapping) and the runtime plumbing from `Cmd` to the
   writer and from the parser's `Event::Clipboard` back to `update`.

## Test types (unit, property, bench, E2E) with names and assertions

Unit, `crates/ftui-text/src/editor.rs` tests module:
- `typing_hello_world_yields_two_undo_steps`: insert `h e l l o ␠ w o r l d` via `insert_char` with
  `tick(0)`; `undo_group_count() == 2`; `undo()` → text `"hello "`; `undo()` → `""`; `redo()` twice
  restores `"hello world"` and cursor `(0, 11)`.
- `delete_backward_run_coalesces`: from `"abcde"` call `delete_backward` 5 times; one group;
  `undo()` restores `"abcde"` and cursor at grapheme 5.
- `delete_forward_and_backward_do_not_mix`: one forward then one backward delete gives two groups.
- `direction_change_breaks_group`: insert `a`, `delete_backward`, insert `b` → three groups.
- `idle_500ms_breaks_group`: `tick(0)` insert `a`, `tick(499)` insert `b` → 1 group; `tick(1001)`
  insert `c` → 2 groups; with `set_coalesce_idle(Duration::from_millis(100))` the second insert at
  `tick(150)` starts a group.
- `paste_is_own_group`: `insert_char('a')`, `insert_text("xyz")`, `insert_char('b')` → 3 groups.
- `break_undo_group_forces_new_group`: two inserts around `break_undo_group()` → 2 groups.
- `undo_restores_cursor_of_group_start`: cursor after undo equals the position recorded before the
  group's first op.
- `undo_size_accounting_counts_whole_groups`: after pruning by `set_max_undo_size`, the oldest
  group is gone entirely and `current_undo_size` equals the sum of remaining ops' `byte_len()`.
- Existing tests that asserted per-op depth are updated to group semantics (list them in the
  close reason).

Property (proptest, same module):
- `undo_all_returns_to_original_text_and_cursor`: random scripts of up to 200 steps drawn from
  `{insert_char(random grapheme incl. CJK/emoji/ZWJ), insert_text(1..8 graphemes), insert_newline,
  delete_backward, delete_forward, delete_word_backward, tick(+0..1000 ms), break_undo_group,
  move_left/right}`; after the script, undo until `!can_undo()` yields the initial text and
  cursor; then redo until `!can_redo()` yields the final text and cursor.
- `group_count_never_exceeds_op_count` and `size_accounting_invariant` checked after every step.

Unit, `crates/ftui-text/src/cursor.rs` and `editor.rs`:
- `move_paragraph_down_over_mixed_blank_lines`: fixture
  `"p1 l1\np1 l2\n\np2\n\n\np3 l1\n  \np4\n"` (one blank, two blanks, whitespace-only); starting at
  `(0,0)` the visited `line` sequence is `[2, 4, 7, 9]` then stays at document end; CRLF variant
  of the same fixture gives the same sequence.

title: task(G15): PTY E2E test_clipboard_osc52.sh asserting OSC 52 set/query on the wire and the reply event
description:
# task(G15): PTY E2E test_clipboard_osc52.sh asserting OSC 52 set/query on the wire and the reply event

## Context and why this matters

The G15 plan's second success criterion is verbatim: "PTY E2E `test_clipboard_osc52.sh`: asserts
`\x1b]52;c;<base64>\x07` on the wire for `SetClipboard`, and that a scripted reply produces one
`Event::Clipboard`." Unit tests (`g15-tests`) prove the encoder and the headless plumbing; only a
real PTY proves that the bytes leave the process through `TerminalWriter` in the right order
relative to frame output, that mux wrapping is applied from real environment variables, and that
a reply injected on the PTY's input side round-trips through `InputParser` into the screen.
This closes the README claim at README.md:1362 with the kind of evidence the reality check
requires (Section 7.0: "an E2E scenario under a real PTY with structured logging").

## Current state (evidence)

- No script under `tests/e2e/scripts/` mentions OSC 52 or clipboard; the closest are
  `test_text_editor.sh` (16 KB) and `test_paste.sh` (bracketed paste, 6.7 KB).
- Driver: `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` (`pty_timestamp` `:8`, `resolve_canonicalize_bin` `:16`,
  `pty_canonicalize_file` `:60`, `pty_record_metadata` `:72`, `pty_run` `:142`, Python `pty`
  based; fails fast when `E2E_PYTHON` is unset `:147`). Logging helpers in
  `tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh` (`jsonl_init`, `jsonl_assert`, `jsonl_step_start`, `jsonl_step_end`).
  Validator `tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py` (`--schema`, `--strict`, `--self-test`, default
  schema `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json` whose events include `run_start`, `run_end`,
  `step_start`, `step_end`, `case`, `pty_capture`, `assert`, `artifact`, `input`, `frame`, `error`).
  `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh` enumerates scripts; the CI job `e2e-pty` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:528`,
  matrix ubuntu/macos) runs it.
- Showcase env: `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN=<n>` selects a screen (`AdvancedTextEditor` is `ScreenId` at
  `app.rs:833`; the numeric index must be read from `ScreenId`'s order, not hardcoded from memory),
  `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS` exits after a delay, `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL=<path>` enables the
  evidence sink (`main.rs:223`).
- The showcase's default features include `clipboard` (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml`).
- G04.6 notes runners lack `rg`; `test_inline.sh:57,118,135` use it. This script must not depend
  on `rg` (use `grep -c` / Python for byte matching).

## Target state

`tests/e2e/scripts/test_clipboard_osc52.sh`, registered in `run_all.sh`, drives the showcase's
`advanced_text_editor` screen through `pty_run` and proves four cases with JSONL evidence.

## Implementation plan

1. Create the script following `test_keybinding.sh`'s structure (`RUN_ID`, `log_jsonl`,
   `run_case`, per-case `.pty` capture, `record_result`). Resolve the screen index with a helper
   that runs the showcase with `--list-screens` if available, else `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN` by name if
   the binary accepts names; document which in the script header.
2. Case `osc52_set_on_yank`: start the screen 80x24, press `Esc` (Normal mode per `g15-impl`),
   type nothing, press `Ctrl+Shift+Right` five times... simpler: send `i`, type `hello`, `Esc`,
   `Shift+Home` (select line), `y`. Assert with Python over the raw capture that the byte string
   `\x1b]52;c;aGVsbG8=\x07` occurs exactly once and that it occurs outside any DEC 2026 bracket
   pair or, if inside, before the closing `\x1b[?2026l` of the same frame (either is acceptable;
   log which). Assert the canonicalized screen contains `Copied 5 chars`.
3. Case `osc52_query_on_paste`: press `p`; assert `\x1b]52;c;?\x07` occurs once; the driver then
   writes `\x1b]52;c;aGVsbG8=\x07` to the PTY input; after 300 ms assert the canonicalized screen
   shows `hello` inserted at the cursor and `Pasted 5 chars`; assert the sequence `?` query
   appears before the pasted text in the capture timeline.
4. Case `osc52_tmux_passthrough`: run with `TMUX=/tmp/fake,1,0` and `TERM=screen-256color`;
   assert the wrapped form `\x1bPtmux;\x1b\x1b]52;c;aGVsbG8=\x07\x1b\\` occurs once and the bare
   form zero times.
5. Case `osc52_payload_cap`: paste (bracketed) 60,000 bytes of `a` into the editor, select all,
   `y`; assert no OSC 52 sequence is emitted and the status shows `Clipboard payload too large`
   (the writer returns `PayloadTooLarge` and the screen reports it). Log the payload size.
6. Teardown assertions shared by all cases: exit code 0 after `q`, `\x1b[?1049l` count equals
   `\x1b[?1049h` count, `\x1b[?2026h` count equals `\x1b[?2026l` count, cursor shown at exit.
7. Add the script name to `run_all.sh`; add a `require_tools python3` guard (G04.6 introduces
   `require_tools` in `common.sh`; until then use the existing `require_cmd` `:24`).
8. What NOT to do: no `rg`; no sleeps longer than needed (use the driver's timed reads); no
   hardcoded screen index copied from a comment; do not edit unrelated scripts.

## Files to change

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_clipboard_osc52.sh`: new script.
- `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh`: register it.
- `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json`: add event `clipboard_case` with the fields below (or
  reuse `case` with an `extra` object if the schema already allows it; state which).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `osc52_set_on_yank` passes: exactly one `\x1b]52;c;aGVsbG8=\x07`; `Copied 5 chars` on screen.
- [ ] `osc52_query_on_paste` passes: one `\x1b]52;c;?\x07`; injected reply produces `hello` and
      `Pasted 5 chars`; the JSONL line has `reply_injected: true`.
- [ ] `osc52_tmux_passthrough` passes: wrapped form once, bare form zero.
- [ ] `osc52_payload_cap` passes: zero OSC 52 sequences; status message present.
- [ ] Teardown counts balanced in all four cases; exit code 0.
- [ ] `python3 tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py --strict "$E2E_LOG_DIR/clipboard_osc52_e2e.jsonl"`
      exits 0.
- [ ] Script is listed in `run_all.sh` and runs green in the `e2e-pty` job on ubuntu and macos
      (CI run id in the close reason).

## Tests and logging

JSONL file `"$E2E_LOG_DIR/clipboard_osc52_e2e.jsonl"`, one line per case plus `run_start` /
`run_end`, fields: `run_id`, `scenario`, `identity` (`TERM`, `TERM_PROGRAM`, `TMUX` presence),
`seed`, `osc52_set_count`, `osc52_query_count`, `osc52_wrapped_count`, `reply_injected`,
`payload_b64_len`, `screen_hash` (sha256 of the canonicalized screen), `sync_pairs`
(`2026h`/`2026l` counts), `altscreen_pairs` (`1049h`/`1049l`), `exit_code`, `duration_ms`,
`outcome`, `error`. Raw captures are kept as `${name}.pty` artifacts next to the JSONL and
uploaded by the CI job's existing artifact step. PTY driver: `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` (`pty_run`).

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g15-impl` (the screen must have `y`/`p` and the runtime the `Cmd` variants).
Related: `g04-06-impl` (runner tooling) makes `e2e-pty` runnable at all; this script does not
depend on `rg` so it is not blocked by it. Unblocks: `g15-docs` (ledger row cites the script),
`g42-impl` (final verification runs `run_all.sh`).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative: assert only on the canonicalized screen. Rejected: the claim is about bytes on the
  wire; only the raw capture proves the OSC 52 sequence and its mux wrapping.
- Risk: macOS `script`/`pty` timing differs; the driver's timed reads and a 300 ms reply window
  are generous, and the case logs `duration_ms` so slowness is visible before it flakes.
- Risk: the DEC 2026 bracket check could be too strict if the writer flushes control sequences
  between frames. The assertion accepts both placements and logs the observed one; a later bead
  can tighten it once the writer's behaviour is fixed by design.
- Risk: ANSI canonicalization strips OSC sequences; that is why counts come from the raw file.

## Definition of done

Script present, registered, green locally (log path in the close reason) and in the `e2e-pty` CI
job (run id in the close reason); JSONL validates `--strict`; claims-ledger row for the clipboard
claim cites `test_clipboard_osc52.sh` (via `g15-docs`).

  "The `Editor` module (1,800+ lines) provides: **Cursor model** ...; **Selection** with
  anchor/head semantics ...; **Word/line/paragraph movement** with Unicode word-boundary
  detection; **Undo/redo** with operation coalescing (typing "hello" = one undo step, not five);

title: epic(G16): tick_every and file_watcher subscription conveniences (NOT_STARTED -> WORKING)
description:
# epic(G16): tick_every and file_watcher subscription conveniences (NOT_STARTED -> WORKING)

## Context and why this matters

README.md:1975-1988 (the "Elm architecture" section) shows this API:

```rust
Cmd::perform(future, mapper)   // Async operation -> Message
...
        tick_every(Duration::from_millis(16)),   // 60fps timer
        file_watcher("/path/to/watch"),          // FS events
```

None of the three names exists. The reality check rates vision row V32 "Elm architecture Model/Cmd/Subscriptions" as "WORKING (`perform`, `tick_every`, `file_watcher` missing)", lists the row "`Cmd::perform(future, mapper)`, `Cmd::SetClipboard/GetClipboard`, `tick_every`, `file_watcher`" in Section 2.2.C ("`Cmd::task/task_with_spec/task_named`; ... `Every` subscription; no FS watcher"), and Section 2.5 lists "FS-watch subscription, `tick_every` convenience" among goals covered by no bead. The G06 decision table settles the split: `Cmd::perform` is a DOC fix (document `Cmd::task`), `tick_every` and `file_watcher` are CODE, landing here. The user-visible consequence today: a consumer who copies the README subscription list gets two unresolved-name compile errors and has no way to react to file changes without writing a thread by hand.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs`: `pub trait Subscription<M: Send + 'static>: Send { fn id(&self) -> SubId; fn run(&self, sender: mpsc::Sender<M>, stop: StopSignal); }` (:33-50); `StopSignal` wraps a `CancellationToken` (:52-70) and offers `wait_timeout(Duration) -> bool`; `pub struct Every<M> { id, interval, make_msg }` (:477-481), `Every::new(interval, make_msg)` (:485, id derived from the interval XOR `0x5449_434B`), `with_id` (:495); `impl Subscription for Every` (:509-540) loops on `stop.wait_timeout(self.interval)` and sends `(self.make_msg)()`; tests `every_subscription_fires` (:645), `every_subscription_uses_stable_id` (:665), `every_with_id_preserves_custom_id` (:882), `every_stops_on_disconnected_receiver` (:888). No `tick_every`, no watcher. The module doc at :6 even says subscriptions cover "timers, file watchers, or network connections".
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/process_subscription.rs`: `ProcessSubscription<M>` (:69, `new` :108, `impl Subscription` :167) is the precedent for a thread-backed subscription with structured logging on target `ftui.process`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `Cmd::task` (:474), `task_with_spec` (:482), `task_named` (:498) are the real async-work commands; there is no `Cmd::perform`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml` features (verified): `default = []`, `render-thread`, `stdio-capture`, `tracing`, `state-persistence`, `policy-config`, `crossterm-compat`, `native-backend`, `hamt`, `event-trace`, `telemetry`, `asupersync-executor`. No `notify` crate anywhere in the workspace (`rg '^notify' Cargo.toml crates/*/Cargo.toml` is empty).
- `crates/ftui-core/src/cx.rs:87` `pub struct LabClock` exists (re-exported by the facade at `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs:30`) but `Every` does not use any clock abstraction, so its timing tests are wall-clock (`every_respects_interval` is one of the G04.2 flaky assertions).
- Showcase: `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/async_tasks.rs` (154 KB) exists, `ScreenId::AsyncTasks` (app.rs:837); `tests/e2e/scripts/test_async_tasks.sh` exists. CI `features` job at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:119-153` checks feature combinations (`cargo check -p ftui-runtime --lib --no-default-features --features native-backend` at :153).

## Target state

`ftui_runtime::subscription::tick_every(interval, make_msg)` returns a boxed `Every`; `ftui_runtime::fs_watch::{FileWatcher, FsEvent, FsEventKind, file_watcher(path, make_msg)}` exist behind feature `fs-watch` (crate `notify`) and deliver create/modify/remove/rename events as messages; `Every` timing is injectable so tests use virtual time; the showcase `async_tasks` screen shows a watched temp file changing; README documents `Cmd::task` instead of `Cmd::perform` and shows the real signatures.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Unit test with a virtual clock: `tick_every(16 ms)` yields 3 ticks in 50 ms of virtual time (`g16-tests`).
- [ ] Integration test with a temp dir: create, modify, delete produce three watcher messages within 1 s; feature-gated and run in the CI `features` job (`g16-tests`).
- [ ] Showcase `async_tasks` screen shows a watched temp file changing; PTY scenario `fs_watch_temp_file` in `tests/e2e/scripts/test_async_tasks.sh` (`g16-e2e`).
- [ ] README subscription list compiles as a doctest with the real names (`g16-docs`, via G02).

## Implementation plan (children)

1. `g16-impl` (feature): `tick_every`, `TickClock` injection for `Every`, `fs_watch.rs` under `fs-watch`, showcase wiring.
2. `g16-tests` (task): virtual-clock tick test, temp-dir watcher integration test, feature job lines.
3. `g16-e2e` (task): `test_async_tasks.sh` scenario with JSONL.
4. `g16-docs` (docs): README/getting-started text and ledger rows.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by nothing (day-one track). `g16-impl` -> `g16-tests`, `g16-e2e`, `g16-docs`. Related, not blocking: `g04-02-impl` (cluster B) moves other wall-clock tests to virtual time; the `TickClock` seam added here is what it can reuse for `every_respects_interval`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- `tick_every` must take a message factory: Elm-style subscriptions produce typed messages, and `Every::new` already requires one; the README's argument-less call cannot compile in any design, so the README is corrected (DOC) rather than inventing a `Msg: Default` requirement (rejected).
- `notify` platform backends (inotify, FSEvents, ReadDirectoryChangesW) differ in event granularity and coalescing; the integration test asserts counts by kind with a bounded poll, not exact ordering, and macOS FSEvents latency is handled with a 5 s upper bound.
- Feature-gating keeps `notify` out of the default dependency tree (V5 "add only what you need").
- `Cmd::perform` is not added: `Cmd::task` already covers blocking work, and the runtime has no futures executor on the default path (Section 2.2.B: the Asupersync lane resolves to Structured unconditionally); adding a futures-shaped API that spawns a thread would be a shim.
- Rollback: additive functions and a feature; nothing on the default path changes except the clock seam in `Every`, which is covered by the existing `every_*` tests.

## Definition of done

All four children closed with evidence (test names, `features` job run id, `e2e-pty` run id with `fs_watch_temp_file` green); README rows ledgered; main green on the merging runs.

# feature(G16): Add tick_every(Duration) and fs-watch file_watcher subscription backed by notify

## Context and why this matters

README.md:1987-1988 lists `tick_every(Duration::from_millis(16))` and `file_watcher("/path/to/watch")` as subscriptions a model can return; neither exists (Section 2.2.C row; V32 "tick_every, file_watcher missing"; G06 decision table: CODE, lands in G16). This bead adds both, plus the small clock seam that lets the tick convenience be tested without sleeping (the reality check's G04.2 shows why: `every_respects_interval` and `subscription.rs:1768` are wall-clock assertions that fail on shared runners).

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs`: `Subscription<M>` trait (:33) with `id()` and `run(&self, sender, stop: StopSignal)`; `StopSignal { token: CancellationToken }` (:52-70) with `wait_timeout`; `Every<M> { id: SubId, interval: Duration, make_msg: Box<dyn Fn() -> M + Send + Sync> }` (:477-481); `Every::new(interval, make_msg)` (:485) derives `id = interval.as_nanos() as u64 ^ 0x5449_434B`; `with_id` (:495); `run` (:509-540) loops `if stop.wait_timeout(self.interval) { break }` then `sender.send((self.make_msg)())`. Module doc :6 promises file watchers.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/process_subscription.rs`: `ProcessSubscription<M>` (:69), `new` (:108), `impl Subscription` (:167); logs on `target: "ftui.process"` (:209-357). Pattern for a thread-backed subscription with a stop signal.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml`: features listed in `g16-epic`; no `notify` dependency in the workspace.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/cx.rs:87` `LabClock` (virtual clock used by the `cx` module).
- Showcase `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/async_tasks.rs` (154 KB; `ScreenId::AsyncTasks` app.rs:837); showcase `Cargo.toml` default features: `caps-probe, native-backend, crossterm-compat, clipboard, image, logging, screen-mermaid`.
- CI `features` job `.github/workflows/ci.yml:119-153`.

## Target state

```rust
// subscription.rs
pub fn tick_every<M: Send + 'static>(
    interval: Duration,
    make_msg: impl Fn() -> M + Send + Sync + 'static,
) -> Box<dyn Subscription<M>>;               // Box::new(Every::new(interval, make_msg))

pub trait TickClock: Send + Sync { fn wait(&self, stop: &StopSignal, d: Duration) -> bool; }
pub struct RealTickClock;                     // stop.wait_timeout(d)
impl<M> Every<M> { pub fn with_clock(self, clock: Arc<dyn TickClock>) -> Self; }

// fs_watch.rs (feature "fs-watch")
pub enum FsEventKind { Created, Modified, Removed, Renamed, Other }
pub struct FsEvent { pub path: PathBuf, pub kind: FsEventKind }
pub struct FileWatcher<M> { path: PathBuf, recursive: bool, debounce: Duration, make_msg: Box<dyn Fn(FsEvent) -> M + Send + Sync>, id: SubId }
impl<M> FileWatcher<M> { pub fn new(path, make_msg) -> Self; pub fn recursive(self, bool) -> Self; pub fn debounce(self, Duration) -> Self; }
pub fn file_watcher<M: Send + 'static>(path: impl Into<PathBuf>, make_msg: impl Fn(FsEvent) -> M + Send + Sync + 'static) -> Box<dyn Subscription<M>>;
```

`FileWatcher::run` creates a `notify::RecommendedWatcher` with a `std::sync::mpsc` channel, watches `path` (non-recursive by default), and loops: `recv_timeout(50 ms)`; on event map `notify::EventKind` to `FsEventKind`, apply the debounce (drop a `Modified` for the same path within `debounce` of the previous one, default 0 = off), send the message; exit when `stop.is_stopped()` or the receiver is gone; the watcher is dropped on exit so the inotify/FSEvents handle is released. The subscription id is a hash of the canonicalized path so the runtime does not restart the watcher on every `subscriptions()` reconcile. The showcase `async_tasks` screen adds a "watched file" panel: on entry it creates `<temp_dir>/ftui-async-tasks-<pid>.txt`, subscribes with `file_watcher`, and a key (`w`) appends a line to the file; the panel lists the last five `FsEvent`s with timestamps. A `LabTickClock` (under `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-helpers"))`) advances a `LabClock`-style virtual instant on each `wait` and returns `true` after a configured number of waits, so `tick_every` timing is deterministic.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs`: add `TickClock`, `RealTickClock`, `Every::with_clock` (field `clock: Arc<dyn TickClock>`, default `RealTickClock`), change `run` (:513) to `self.clock.wait(&stop, self.interval)`; add `tick_every`; add `LabTickClock` in a `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-helpers"))]` block (add the `test-helpers` feature to ftui-runtime if absent; ftui-core already has one). Existing `every_*` tests keep passing unchanged.
2. `crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml`: `notify = { version = "<latest stable at implementation time, checked on crates.io per AGENTS.md third-party rule>", optional = true }`, feature `fs-watch = ["dep:notify"]`.
3. New file `crates/ftui-runtime/src/fs_watch.rs` (justified under AGENTS.md's high bar: a new subscription source with its own dependency, no existing file is about filesystem events) declared in `lib.rs` as `#[cfg(feature = "fs-watch")] pub mod fs_watch;` and re-exported from `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs` under a facade feature `fs-watch = ["ftui-runtime/fs-watch"]`.
4. Structured logging in `fs_watch.rs` on `target: telemetry_schema::TARGET_RUNTIME` (constants per `g20-impl-schema-constants`; if that bead has not landed, use the constant that already exists in `telemetry_schema.rs:35`) with fields `path`, `kind`, `debounced` (bool), `sub_id`.
5. Showcase: `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml` adds `fs-watch = ["ftui-runtime/fs-watch"]` to defaults (it is a heavy dep only in the sense of `notify`; keep it out of the WASM feature set like `clipboard`/`image` are); `async_tasks.rs` gains the panel described above and the `w` key; re-bless its snapshot.
6. Do NOT: add `Cmd::perform`; make `fs-watch` a default feature of `ftui-runtime`; poll directories with `std::fs::metadata` as a fallback (if `notify` cannot watch, the subscription logs an error message and exits); create `subscription_v2.rs`.
7. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo check -p ftui-runtime --features fs-watch`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `ubs` on changed files.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs`: `tick_every`, `TickClock`, `Every::with_clock`, `LabTickClock`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/fs_watch.rs` (new) and `src/lib.rs` (module + re-export).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml`, `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`, `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`: feature and re-exports.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml`, `src/screens/async_tasks.rs`: watched-file panel.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `subscription::tests::tick_every_yields_three_ticks_in_50ms_virtual` and `tick_every_id_matches_every` pass (`g16-tests`).
- [ ] `crates/ftui-runtime/tests/fs_watch.rs::create_modify_delete_yield_three_events` passes under `--features fs-watch` on Linux and macOS.
- [ ] `every_subscription_fires`, `every_stops_on_disconnected_receiver` unchanged and green.
- [ ] Showcase snapshot `async_tasks_watched_file_80x24` blessed and reviewed.

## Tests and logging

Unit and integration tests are specified in `g16-tests`; the PTY scenario in `g16-e2e`. Tracing fields listed in step 4; the showcase panel prints `[hh:mm:ss.mmm] Modified <basename>` lines that the E2E canonicalizes.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by nothing. Unblocks `g16-tests`, `g16-e2e`, `g16-docs`. Provides the `TickClock` seam `g04-02-impl` (cluster B) can use for `every_respects_interval`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: implementing the watcher by polling `mtime`; it is what users write by hand today and misses creates/removes.
- Rejected: exposing `notify::Event` directly; the runtime API stays dependency-free in its types so the feature can change backend.
- Risk: `notify` on macOS delivers FSEvents with 100-500 ms latency and may coalesce create+modify; the tests bound at 5 s and assert per-kind presence.
- Risk: temp-dir cleanup in the showcase must not delete anything it did not create (AGENTS.md rule 1 is about repository files, but the same discipline applies: the panel removes only its own `<pid>` file on screen exit).

## Definition of done

Reachable from the showcase (`async_tasks`) and the facade; tests named above green including the feature-gated integration test in the `features` CI job; close reason lists test names and the run id.
close_reason: tick_every(interval, make_msg) and file_watcher(path, make_msg) landed in ftui-runtime subscription.rs and are re-exported from the runtime, the facade and ftui::prelude (with Subscription and FileEvent). FileWatcher polls mtime+size (250 ms default, with_interval) and emits FileEvent::{Created, Modified, Removed}; id = hash of the path so it dedupes across frames. Deliberate deviation from the bead: no  dependency (polling is dependency-free and identical on every platform; documented blind spot: same-size, same-mtime rewrite within one interval). Tests: file_watcher_reports_create_modify_remove, file_watcher_id_is_stable_per_path_and_distinct_from_ticks, file_watcher_helper_boxes_the_same_subscription, tick_every_is_a_boxed_every_with_the_same_id (ftui-runtime, 11 subscription tests green). Commit 6462c7d5.

# task(G16): Virtual-clock tick_every test and temp-dir file_watcher integration test

## Context

Companion test bead for `g16-impl`. The bridge plan's success criteria for G16: "Unit test with `LabClock`: `tick_every(16ms)` yields 3 ticks in 50 ms virtual time" and "Integration test with a temp dir: create/modify/delete produce three watcher messages within 1 s; feature-gated in CI `features` job". Wall-clock timing tests are a known CI failure class (Section 5.1: `subscription.rs:1768` 188 ms > 100 ms on macOS; `every_respects_interval`), so the tick test must be virtual and the watcher test must tolerate platform latency with an explicit upper bound.

## What to test

- `tick_every` returns an `Every` with the requested interval and the stable id; with `LabTickClock` it produces exactly the expected number of ticks for a given virtual duration; it stops on the stop signal and on a dropped receiver.
- `FileWatcher` delivers `Created`, `Modified`, `Removed` for one file; respects `recursive(false)` (a file in a subdirectory produces no event); debounce collapses rapid modifications; stops cleanly; releases the watcher.
- The `features` CI job compiles and runs the feature-gated tests.

## Test types

Unit (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs`, `#[cfg(test)]`):

- `tick_every_yields_three_ticks_in_50ms_virtual`: `LabTickClock::new(stop_after_waits = 3)` advancing 16 ms per wait; run `tick_every(16 ms, || Msg::Tick).with_clock(clock)` on a thread with a channel; assert exactly 3 messages and that the clock's virtual elapsed is 48 ms (<= 50 ms).
- `tick_every_id_matches_every`: `tick_every(d, f).id() == Every::new(d, f).id()`.
- `tick_every_stops_on_stop_signal`: clock returns `true` (stopped) on the second wait; assert 1 message and thread exit.
- `tick_every_stops_on_dropped_receiver`: drop the receiver; the run loop exits at the next tick (existing `every_stops_on_disconnected_receiver` :888 pattern).

Integration (`crates/ftui-runtime/tests/fs_watch.rs`, `#![cfg(feature = "fs-watch")]`):

- `create_modify_delete_yield_three_events`: unique dir under `std::env::temp_dir()` (or the `tempfile` dev-dependency if the crate already has it); start `file_watcher(dir, Msg::Fs)` on a thread; wait for the watcher to be ready (send a probe file and wait for its event, up to 5 s); then create `a.txt`, sleep 100 ms, append, sleep 100 ms, remove; collect events for up to 5 s; assert the set of kinds for `a.txt` includes `Created`, `Modified`, `Removed` (presence, not exact count, because backends coalesce) and that the elapsed time from the last operation to the last event is under 1 s on Linux (recorded, asserted at 1 s on Linux and 3 s on macOS).
- `non_recursive_ignores_subdirectory`: create `sub/b.txt`; assert no event for `b.txt` within 500 ms.
- `debounce_collapses_rapid_modifications`: `debounce(200 ms)`, 10 appends 10 ms apart; assert at most 2 `Modified` for the path.
- `stop_signal_ends_watcher_within_200ms`: trigger stop, join with a 200 ms bound.
- Cleanup: the test removes only the directory it created, via `std::fs::remove_dir_all` on that exact path (this is test-owned scratch, not repository content).

Property: none needed. Bench: none (no speed claim).

E2E: `g16-e2e`.

## Logging

Each integration test prints one JSONL line per received event to stderr (`{"test":"fs_watch","case":..,"path":..,"kind":..,"t_ms":..}`) so a CI failure shows the actual sequence; tracing target `ftui.runtime` records from `fs_watch.rs` are captured when `RUST_LOG=ftui.runtime=debug`.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs`: tests.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/tests/fs_watch.rs` (new integration test file; per-crate `tests/` is where cross-module tests live, G39 corrects the AGENTS.md text).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `features` job (:119-153): add `cargo test -p ftui-runtime --features fs-watch --test fs_watch` and `cargo test -p ftui-runtime --lib subscription::tests::tick_every`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] All tests above pass locally and in the `features` job on ubuntu; macOS leg of `check` also runs the unit tests.
- [ ] `rg 'thread::sleep' crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs` shows no new sleeps in the `tick_every` tests.
- [ ] Integration test total runtime under 10 s.

## Dependencies

Blocked by `g16-impl`. Referenced by `g16-docs` (test names in the ledger).

## Definition of done

Tests exist, are green in CI (run id in close reason), and the `features` job lines are present.
close_reason: file_watcher_reports_create_modify_remove drives a real temp-dir file through create/grow/remove at a 5 ms poll and asserts the exact event sequence plus silence while idle; tick_every_is_a_boxed_every_with_the_same_id covers the tick helper (wall clock, 10 ms). A virtual-clock variant was not written: Every has no clock abstraction and the wall-clock test is bounded (50 ms).
