The "Table Theming System" table (:2176-2188) promises "Row striping ... configurable period", "Truncation: Ellipsis, clip, or wrap per column", "Alignment: Left/center/right per column", "Border variants: 9 built-in border styles per table edge", and shows `TableTheme::modern().with_stripe_period(2).with_header_style(..).with_selection_style(..)` (:2191-2194). The "Stylesheet System" (:2197-2208) shows `Stylesheet::new(); sheet.register(..); sheet.get("heading").unwrap_or_default()`. The "Widget Composition" section (:2210+) shows `frame.render_widget(w, area)` and `Layout::horizontal([Constraint::Percentage(30), ..]).split(frame.area())`.

The reality check rates V6 "80+ widgets" PARTIAL (57 production types), V39 "Table theming engine" PARTIAL/WRONG_API, V40 "Stylesheet" WRONG_API/no consumer, V41 "Widget composition helpers `render_widget`, `Layout`" WRONG_API, and Section 2.2.C has one row per promise above ("none of these exist"). The G06 decision table marks every one of them CODE (rows: `Frame::render_widget/area` -> G17.9, `Layout::horizontal` -> G17.9, `Stylesheet::register` -> DOC + CODE consumer G17.8, `TableTheme::modern().with_*` -> G17.7, 9 border styles -> G17.6, Input history/Textarea syntax hook/indeterminate Progress/JsonView folding/Sparkline markers -> G17). The plan's optimality pass chose "widgets are exercised rather than quarantined": a widget is library surface and needs a test, a snapshot and a showcase exercise, not deletion. A consumer who copies any of these README snippets today gets a compile error; that is the user-visible gap.

## Current state (evidence)

Verified 2026-09-01 (commit `ab07291f`):

- G17.1 `crates/ftui-widgets/src/progress.rs`: `ProgressBar { block, ratio, label, style, gauge_style }` (:17-23), `ratio()` clamps to 0..=1 (:41), `impl Widget` (:72); no indeterminate mode. `spinner.rs` `SpinnerState::tick()` (:97) is the phase pattern.
- G17.2 `json_view.rs`: `JsonToken` (:25), `JsonView` (:46), `formatted_lines()` (:141), `impl Widget for JsonView` (:332); no fold state or node ids.
- G17.3 `textarea.rs`: builders `with_line_numbers` (:292) .. `with_max_height` (:327); render styles graphemes at :1376-1392 from `base_style` and `selection_style`; no highlighter hook. `ftui-extras/src/syntax.rs` `Tokenizer` trait (:199), `SyntaxHighlighter` used by `markdown_live_editor.rs:19,235`.
- G17.4 `input.rs`: `TextInput` (:21), `handle_event` (:254), `handle_key` (:324) handles no Up/Down recall; the doc at :1278-1299 points to `ftui_runtime::undo::HistoryManager` (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/undo/history.rs:104`, undo/redo stacks, not recall).
- G17.5 `sparkline.rs`: `min` (:78), `max` (:87), `bounds` (:94), `impl Widget` (:202); no markers.
- G17.6 `borders.rs`: `BorderType` (:109-123) has SIX variants `Square, Ascii, Rounded, Double, Heavy, Custom(BorderSet)` (:121-122) — the plan document's "5" undercounts by the `Custom` variant; README says 9. `BorderSet` consts at :32-92.
- G17.7 `ftui-style/src/table_theme.rs`: fields (:418-445), builders `with_border .. with_preset_id` (:1184-1275, no `with_stripe_period`/`with_header_style`/`with_selection_style`), presets `aurora` (:1282) .. `terminal_classic` (:1498), `terminal_classic_for` (:1504), no `modern`; `ftui-widgets/src/table.rs` `Table { widths: Vec<Constraint>, theme, theme_phase }` (:80-87), `theme()` (:162), no per-column truncation/alignment.
- G17.8 `ftui-style/src/stylesheet.rs`: `StyleSheet` (:83), `define` (:151), `get -> Option<Style>` (:168), `get_or_default` (:174), `compose` (:220); consumers outside the module: only re-exports in `ftui-style/src/lib.rs:65` and `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs` (rg).
- G17.9 `ftui-render/src/frame.rs`: `width()` (:649), `height()` (:655), no `area()`/`render_widget`; `Widget`/`StatefulWidget` traits are in `ftui-widgets/src/lib.rs:423/:549` and ftui-render does not depend on ftui-widgets; `ftui-layout/src/lib.rs` `Flex::horizontal()` (:561), `constraints()` (:577), `split()` (:634), `Constraint::Percentage(f32)` (:165), 515 `Flex::horizontal()/vertical()` call sites in 67 files; `ftui-widgets/src/layout.rs:158` is an unrelated `Layout` grid widget.
- Snapshot infrastructure: 419 insta snapshots plus 7 goldens, `BLESS=1` honored (Section 2.1); `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh` (787 lines) runs build/tests/clippy/features/signatures/docs/snapshots/policy steps and leaks `FTUI_HARNESS_SEED=0` into `cargo test` (:113-114, G04.1).

## Target state

Every promise above is true in code: indeterminate `ProgressBar`, foldable `JsonView`, `TextArea::with_highlighter`, `TextInput` recall history, `Sparkline` min/max markers, `BorderType::Dashed` plus an exercised `Custom`, `TableTheme` stripe/header/selection builders and per-column truncation/alignment with a `modern` preset, `Block::styled`/`Table::with_stylesheet` reading a `StyleSheet`, and `Frame::area()`/`FrameExt::render_widget`/`Layout` alias. - [ ] README widget table rows, Table Theming rows and the Stylesheet/Composition snippets match the code (`g17-docs` plus G06 ledger rows).

Every sub-item is its own bead pair; no tests bead is shared (the items live in different files, so co-location does not apply).

## Dependencies and ordering

Code work is blocked by nothing (day-one track). DOC rows (`g17-docs`, and the README rewrite that names counts) depend on `g06-impl-ledger` (cluster A) because the claims ledger is where each row's proof is recorded; the code beads do not wait for it. `g17-e2e` depends on all nine impl beads; `g04-01-impl` (cluster B) must fix the seed leak in `widget_api_e2e.sh` before the script's unit-test step is trustworthy, but the new scenario step does not depend on it.

- Rejected: retracting the README rows (DOC-only). The plan's rule is CODE when the behaviour is user-visible value at <= M; every item here is S or M.
- Rejected: adding nine border variants to match "9"; the count is decorative, the code adds `Dashed` (useful) and the README states the real number.
- Rejected: changing `Flex::horizontal()` to take constraints (515 call sites); the alias plus `Frame::area()` gives a README example that compiles with the existing idiom.

- Risk: `ftui-widgets` must not depend on `ftui-extras` (G17.3); the highlighter is a closure type so the showcase builds it from `SyntaxHighlighter`.

title: feature(G17.1): ProgressBar indeterminate marquee mode driven by a phase counter
description:
# feature(G17.1): ProgressBar indeterminate marquee mode driven by a phase counter

## Context and why this matters

The README widget table (README.md:2158) promises for `Progress`: "Progress bars | Determinate/indeterminate". The reality check of 2026-09-01 (Section 2.2.C row "Input history; Textarea syntax hooks; Progress indeterminate; JsonView collapse/expand; Sparkline min/max markers") found that none of these exist: `ProgressBar` has no indeterminate mode at all. This bead is sub-item G17.1 of block G17 "Widget features the README promises — PARTIAL/WRONG_API -> WORKING (cluster of 9)", and the G06 CODE/DOC decision table marks "indeterminate Progress" as **CODE** (the promise is user-visible value and at most S complexity), so the code changes to match the README rather than the README retracting the claim.

Vision rows served: V6 ("80+ widgets", PARTIAL), V39-V41 (widget API rows, WRONG_API), Section 2.2.C editor/widget rows. User-visible consequence today: an app that needs to show "working, unknown duration" (a spawned process, a network request) has no widget for it and has to hack a `Spinner` next to an empty bar. Reachable-from-production definition of done applies: the mode must be rendered by a showcase screen and covered by a snapshot, not only by a unit test.

The README row itself is a **DOC** item owned by the claims ledger bead `g06-impl-ledger` (cluster A): that bead flips the ledger row from "missing" to "proved by test X" once this bead lands. The code work here has no dependency on the ledger.

## Current state (evidence)

Verified against `crates/ftui-widgets/src/progress.rs` on 2026-09-01 (commit `ab07291f`):

- `pub struct ProgressBar<'a> { block: Option<Block<'a>>, ratio: f64, label: Option<&'a str>, style: Style, gauge_style: Style }` at `progress.rs:17-23`. No mode field, no phase.
- `pub fn ratio(mut self, ratio: f64) -> Self` at `progress.rs:41` clamps to `0.0..=1.0` (NaN -> 0.0). This is the only way to drive the fill.
- `impl<'a> Widget for ProgressBar<'a>` at `progress.rs:72` (`fn render(&self, area, frame)` at `:73`): renders a fill proportional to `ratio` and an optional label. Stateless `Widget`, not `StatefulWidget`.
- `impl MeasurableWidget for ProgressBar<'_>` at `progress.rs:172`.
- `MiniBar` (`progress.rs:291`, builders `value` :319, `width` :326, `show_percent` :333, `filled_char` :347, `empty_char` :354, `thresholds` :361, `colors` :368, `render_string` :391, `impl Widget for MiniBar` :436) is a separate compact gauge and is not touched by this bead.
- Existing phase-driven animation pattern in the same crate: `crates/ftui-widgets/src/spinner.rs` `pub struct SpinnerState { pub current_frame: usize }` at `:90-93` with `pub fn tick(&mut self)` at `:97` (`wrapping_add(1)`), consumed by `impl StatefulWidget for Spinner` (`:103`). The showcase drives it from the runtime tick.
- Showcase: `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/widget_gallery.rs` has `fn render_display_widgets(&self, frame: &mut Frame, area: Rect)` at `:442` where the existing determinate bar is rendered. No indeterminate bar anywhere in the 45 screens.

## Target state

`ProgressBar` renders in one of two modes:

- **Determinate** (default, unchanged output): fill = `ratio * inner_width`, label as today.
- **Indeterminate**: a marquee segment sweeps across the bar. Segment width `seg = max(3, inner_width / 5)`; left edge `pos = phase % (inner_width + seg) - seg` (so the segment enters from the left, crosses, and leaves at the right before wrapping); cells inside `[pos, pos+seg)` intersected with `[0, inner_width)` use `gauge_style`, the rest use `style`; `ratio` is ignored; label still drawn (centered, over the bar, as determinate does).

Phase is supplied by the caller (the widget stays a stateless `Widget`, exactly like `Sparkline` and unlike `Spinner`): `ProgressBar::new().indeterminate(phase)`. The showcase widget gallery shows one indeterminate bar whose phase is its tick counter, so the marquee visibly moves and the snapshot at a fixed tick is deterministic.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/progress.rs`
   - Add `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)] pub enum ProgressMode { #[default] Determinate, Indeterminate { phase: u64 } }`.
   - Add field `mode: ProgressMode` to `ProgressBar` (`:17-23`); `Default` derive keeps `Determinate`.
   - Add builders next to `ratio()` (`:41`): `pub fn indeterminate(mut self, phase: u64) -> Self` (sets `Indeterminate { phase }`) and `pub fn mode(mut self, mode: ProgressMode) -> Self`. Add `pub fn is_indeterminate(&self) -> bool`.
   - In `Widget::render` (`:73`): after computing the inner area (block applied), branch on `self.mode`. Factor the fill computation into `fn marquee_span(inner_width: u16, phase: u64) -> Option<(u16, u16)>` (returns the visible `[start, end)` or `None` when width is 0) so tests can call it directly without a `Frame`. Determinate path must be byte-for-byte the same output as before (existing snapshot tests must not change).
   - `MeasurableWidget` (`:172`): unchanged; both modes measure identically.
   - Rustdoc on `indeterminate`: explain that the caller supplies the phase (tick count or frame index), typical usage with `Cmd::Tick`/`Every`, and that `ratio` is ignored in this mode.
2. `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/widget_gallery.rs`
   - In `render_display_widgets` (`:442`) add a second bar labelled "indeterminate" using `.indeterminate(self.tick_count)` (add a `tick_count: u64` field to the screen state if it does not already have one, incremented in its tick handler). Keep the existing determinate bar so the old snapshot rows stay recognisable.
3. Snapshots: three new insta snapshots in `crates/ftui-widgets` tests (see g17-01-tests) plus the re-blessed `widget_gallery` display-section snapshot in `crates/ftui-demo-showcase` (`BLESS=1 cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase`, review with `cargo insta review`).
4. Run `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` (nightly pin `nightly-2026-08-25` from `rust-toolchain.toml`), then `ubs crates/ftui-widgets/src/progress.rs crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/widget_gallery.rs` before committing.

What NOT to do: do not add a `ProgressBarState`/`StatefulWidget` variant (the caller already owns a tick counter; a second state type would be a parallel API); do not create `progress_v2.rs` or any file variant; do not touch `MiniBar`; do not change the determinate output; no compatibility shim for a `ratio(-1.0)` "magic" indeterminate value.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/progress.rs`: `ProgressMode`, `mode` field, `indeterminate()`/`mode()`/`is_indeterminate()`, `marquee_span()`, render branch, rustdoc.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/widget_gallery.rs`: indeterminate bar in `render_display_widgets` (`:442`), tick counter.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/lib.rs`: re-export `ProgressMode` alongside `ProgressBar` if the crate re-exports widget types there (check the existing `pub use progress::...` line; add only if one exists).
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/snapshots/*widget_gallery*display*.snap`: re-blessed.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-widgets progress::` passes with the new tests `indeterminate_marquee_wraps`, `indeterminate_ignores_ratio`, `determinate_unchanged_by_mode_default`, `indeterminate_width_one_and_zero` and the property test `marquee_span_always_inside_area` (named in g17-01-tests).
- [ ] Snapshots `progress_indeterminate_phase0_40x1`, `progress_indeterminate_phase3_40x1`, `progress_indeterminate_phase7_40x1` exist and show the segment at three distinct positions.
- [ ] `widget_gallery` snapshot shows a bar labelled "indeterminate" (re-blessed and reviewed, diff limited to the new row).
- [ ] `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh` scenario `g17_01_progress_indeterminate` (added by g17-e2e) passes and logs its JSONL line.
- [ ] Claims-ledger row for README.md:2158 "Determinate/indeterminate" updated to point at these tests (done in `g06-impl-ledger`, cluster A).

## Tests and logging

- Unit: `marquee_span` table tests (width 40, seg 8, phases 0/3/7/47/48 -> expected spans, wrap at `40 + 8 = 48`), plus render-through-`Frame` tests comparing cell styles.
- Property (proptest): for `width in 0..=200`, `phase in any::<u64>()`, the returned span is `None` iff width is 0, otherwise `start <= end <= width` and `end - start <= seg`.
- Snapshot: three phases at 40x1 using the harness snapshot helper used by the other `ftui-widgets` snapshot tests.
- E2E: scenario `g17_01_progress_indeterminate` in `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh` runs the showcase widget gallery under `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` for two ticks and asserts the "indeterminate" label is present in the canonicalized screen and that two captures at different ticks differ in the bar row. JSONL fields: `run_id`, `scenario`, `screen` (`WidgetGallery`), `seed`, `snapshot_hash`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`.
- Logging: none at runtime (pure render). Tracing span `widget_render` with `widget = "ProgressBar"` already exists under the `tracing` feature; add `mode` as a span field.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: nothing. Can start on day one.
- Unblocks: `g17-01-tests`, the `g17_01_progress_indeterminate` scenario in `g17-e2e`, and the README row in `g17-docs` / `g06-impl-ledger`.
- Parallel-safe with every other G17 sub-item (different files) except that `widget_gallery.rs` is also touched by G17.5 (Sparkline markers) and G17.8 (StyleSheet); coordinate through file reservations (`file_reservation_paths` with the bead id as reason).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- **Stateless phase vs. `StatefulWidget`**: rejected `StatefulWidget` because every caller already has a tick/frame counter and the `Sparkline`/`Table::theme_phase` precedent (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs:171`) passes phases by value. A stateful variant would need a second render path and a second snapshot fixture.
- **Segment sizing**: `max(3, width/5)` keeps the marquee visible at width 10 and proportional at width 200. Documented as an implementation detail, not a public constant, so it can be tuned later without an API change.
- **Determinism**: because phase is caller-supplied, snapshots are deterministic; no `Instant::now()` in the widget.
- **Risk**: the existing determinate snapshots in `ftui-widgets` and the showcase must not change; the render branch must keep the determinate code path identical (verify by diffing snapshot files: only the new rows may appear).
- **Rollback**: revert the single commit; no persisted state, no schema.

## Definition of done

Reachable from the production path (rendered by the showcase widget gallery, exported from `ftui-widgets`); the close reason names the unit tests, the three snapshot files, the re-blessed gallery snapshot and the passing `g17_01_progress_indeterminate` E2E scenario with its JSONL line; the claims-ledger row (README.md:2158) is updated in `g06-impl-ledger`; `main` is green after merge (`cargo check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `fmt --check`, `ubs` exit 0).

title: task(G17.5): Unit tests and snapshot for Sparkline min/max markers
description:
# task(G17.5): Unit tests and snapshot for Sparkline min/max markers

## Context

Companion test bead for `g17-05-impl` (Sparkline min/max markers). README.md:2159 promises `Sparkline` "Min/max markers"; on 2026-09-01 `crates/ftui-widgets/src/sparkline.rs` only had scaling bounds (`min` `:78`, `max` `:87`, `bounds` `:94`) and drew no markers in `render` (`:203`) or `render_to_string` (`:180`). The G06 table marks this CODE. These tests prove marker placement (first extreme wins), style merging, bounds independence, NaN handling, window clipping and text-mode output, and pin one snapshot. Vision rows V6, V39-V41; Section 2.2.C. Ledger row owned by `g06-impl-ledger` (cluster A).

## What to test

1. Placement: the min marker lands on the column of the first minimum sample; the max marker on the first maximum; ties choose the earliest index.
2. Style: the marker style merges over the column's computed style (base or gradient) without discarding the gradient background.
3. Bounds: explicit `bounds(0, 100)` changes bar heights but markers still follow the data extremes.
4. Single sample: both extremes coincide; the max marker is drawn (documented order).
5. Text mode: `render_to_string()` contains the marker glyphs at the same positions as the frame render.
6. Edge cases: empty data (no panic, no markers), all-NaN data (no markers), NaN mixed in (ignored for extremes), data longer than the area (only the visible window is considered for drawing; the extreme may be outside the window and then no marker is drawn).
7. No regression: without markers, output is byte-identical to before (existing `render_basic` `:420` and `render_empty_area` `:409` unchanged).

## Test types

Unit (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/sparkline.rs` `#[cfg(test)]`):

- `min_marker_placed_at_first_min`: data `[5, 1, 3, 1, 9]`, width 5, `with_min_marker('^', red)`; column 1 is `^` with red fg, column 3 is a bar.
- `max_marker_placed_at_first_max`: data `[9, 2, 9]`, `with_max_marker('v', blue)`; column 0 is `v`, column 2 is a bar.
- `markers_respect_explicit_bounds`: data `[10, 20, 30]` with `bounds(0, 100)`; bars are low but min marker at column 0 and max marker at column 2.
- `single_sample_gets_max_marker`: data `[4]` with both markers; the one column shows the max glyph and max style.
- `render_to_string_includes_markers`: same data as the snapshot; the string equals the expected 20-char row with `▴` and `▾` at the expected indices.
- `empty_data_no_panic`: `Sparkline::new(&[])` with markers renders nothing and returns an empty string.
- `nan_samples_are_not_extremes`: data `[f64::NAN, 1, 2]`; min marker at column 1, max at column 2; all-NaN yields no markers.
- `marker_outside_window_not_drawn`: 30 samples, width 10, the minimum at index 0: no min marker in the rendered row; the maximum inside the window is marked.
- `marker_style_merges_over_gradient`: `gradient(a, b)` plus `with_max_marker('v', Style::new().bold())`; the marked cell keeps the gradient fg and gains bold.
- `extreme_indices_pure_fn`: table tests on `extreme_indices` for ties, NaN, empty.

Property (proptest): random `Vec<f64>` (finite values, len 0..=64): `extreme_indices` returns `None` iff empty; otherwise `data[min_idx]` equals the minimum, `data[max_idx]` equals the maximum, and no earlier index holds the same value.

Snapshot (insta): `sparkline_markers_20x1` for data `[3, 7, 2, 9, 4, 1, 6, 8, 5, 7, 3, 9, 2, 6, 4, 8, 1, 5, 7, 3]` (min first at index 5, max first at index 3) with `▴`/`▾`.

title: feature(G17.6): Add BorderType::Dashed, exercise Custom(BorderSet), state the real border-style count
description:
# feature(G17.6): Add BorderType::Dashed, exercise Custom(BorderSet), state the real border-style count

## Context and why this matters

README.md:2151 promises, in the Core Widgets table: `Block` | Container with borders/title | **"9 border styles, title alignment"**. The Table Theming table at README.md:2183 repeats the number: **"Border variants | 9 built-in border styles per table edge"**. The reality check (2026-09-01, Section 2.2.C row "9 border styles") found that `BorderType` does not have nine variants, and the G06 decision table resolved this row as "DOC (5) unless G17.6 adds more", with the G17.6 decision being: "keep 5 ... or add `Thick`, `Dashed`, `Dotted`, `Custom(BorderChars)` to reach the documented breadth. Decision: add `Custom` and `Dashed` (useful), README states the real count."

This bead serves vision rows V6 ("80+ widgets", PARTIAL), V39 ("Table theming engine", PARTIAL / WRONG_API) and V41 ("Widget composition helpers", WRONG_API), and closes the "9 border styles" row of Section 2.2.C. The user-visible consequence today: a consumer who reads the README expects dashed or dotted borders, finds no such variant, and (worse) cannot tell from the README that a fully custom glyph set is already supported.

**Correction to the plan document, verified in code on 2026-09-01:** the plan says `BorderType` has 5 variants. It actually has **six**. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/borders.rs:109-123` declares `pub enum BorderType { Square (#[default]), Ascii, Rounded, Double, Heavy, Custom(BorderSet) }` — `Custom(BorderSet)` is at :121-122 and `to_border_set()` at :127-135 already maps `BorderType::Custom(set) => *set`. So the "add `Custom`" half of the G17.6 decision is already done; only `Dashed` is new, and the README count must state the real number after this bead.

The DOC half of this row (rewriting README.md:2151 and :2183 to the real count) is owned by the claims ledger work in `g06-impl-ledger` (cluster A) and recorded in `g17-docs`; the code work in this bead does not depend on it.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/borders.rs:5` `pub struct BorderSet` with fields for corners, edges and tees (`tee_down`, `tee_left`, `tee_right`, `cross` visible at :100-103 in the `HEAVY` const).
- `borders.rs:32` `BorderSet::ASCII`, `:47` `ROUNDED`, `:62` `SQUARE`, `:77` `DOUBLE`, `:92` `HEAVY` — five glyph sets.
- `borders.rs:109-123` `BorderType` enum: `Square` (default), `Ascii`, `Rounded`, `Double`, `Heavy`, `Custom(BorderSet)`; derives `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default`.
- `borders.rs:127-135` `to_border_set()` matches every variant; `:134` `BorderType::Custom(set) => *set`.
- `borders.rs:303` existing test asserts `BorderType::Custom(custom).to_border_set() == custom`; `:380` `border_set_tees_are_consistent`.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/block.rs:67` `Block::border_type(BorderType)`, `:80` `pub(crate) fn border_set(&self) -> BorderSet`, `:99` `title_alignment(Alignment)`, `:60` `border_style(Style)`.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/widget_gallery.rs:468` `render_borders` is the gallery section that shows border types.
- README.md:2151 says 9; README.md:2183 says 9. Code has 6 (5 named presets + `Custom`).

## Target state

- `BorderSet::DASHED` exists: horizontal edges `┄`, vertical edges `┆`, corners and tees taken from `SQUARE` (`┌ ┐ └ ┘ ┬ ┴ ├ ┤ ┼`).
- `BorderType::Dashed` exists and `to_border_set()` maps it to `BorderSet::DASHED`.
- Optional (decide during implementation, default yes if it costs under 20 lines): `BorderSet::HEAVY_DASHED` (`┅`, `┇`, heavy corners) and `BorderType::HeavyDashed`.
- `widget_gallery.rs` `render_borders` shows every `BorderType` variant including `Dashed` and one `Custom(BorderSet)` example built from ASCII-only glyphs, so the gallery snapshot is the visual proof.
- The README states the real count (6 with `Dashed`, 7 with `HeavyDashed`) and lists the variant names; that text change is a G06 ledger row (DOC) executed in `g17-docs`.
- Explicitly NOT done: padding the enum to nine variants (`Thick`, `Dotted`, ...) only to match the old number. `Heavy` already is "thick"; a dotted variant would be a second dashed style with no user pull.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/borders.rs`: after `HEAVY` (:92-104) add `pub const DASHED: Self = Self { top_left: '┌', top_right: '┐', bottom_left: '└', bottom_right: '┘', horizontal: '┄', vertical: '┆', tee_down: '┬', tee_up: '┴', tee_left: '┤', tee_right: '├', cross: '┼' }` using the exact field names of the struct at :5 (copy the field list from `SQUARE` at :62). If `HEAVY_DASHED` is added, base it on `HEAVY` with `┅`/`┇`.
2. Same file, `BorderType` (:109-123): add `/// Single line border with dashed edges.` `Dashed,` (and `HeavyDashed,` if chosen) before `Custom(BorderSet)`. Keep `Square` as `#[default]`.
3. Same file, `to_border_set()` (:127-135): add the arm(s) `BorderType::Dashed => BorderSet::DASHED`. Because the match is exhaustive, the compiler enforces this.
4. Search for every other exhaustive `match` on `BorderType` across the workspace (`rg -n 'BorderType::Heavy' crates -g '*.rs'` and follow the matches; known consumers are `block.rs:80 border_set()` which delegates to `to_border_set()`, the table theme gallery and the widget gallery) and add the new arms by hand. Do not use a script.
5. `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/widget_gallery.rs` `render_borders` (:468): add two more sample blocks, one `BorderType::Dashed` titled "Dashed" and one `BorderType::Custom(BorderSet { .. })` titled "Custom" using `+`, `-`, `|` glyphs (distinct from `Ascii`, which is also `+ - |`; use `#` corners so the difference is visible). Keep the section within 80x24 by shrinking sample widths if needed; re-bless the affected snapshot(s) with `BLESS=1 cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase`.
6. Add a doc comment on `BorderType` listing every variant and stating that `Custom` accepts any `BorderSet`; this comment is the source the claims ledger points at.
7. After code changes run `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, then `ubs crates/ftui-widgets/src/borders.rs crates/ftui-widgets/src/block.rs crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/widget_gallery.rs` before committing.
8. Do NOT: create a `borders_v2.rs`, keep both an old and a new enum, or delete any file. Do NOT change the README count here (that is `g17-docs`), but record the final variant count in this bead's close reason so the ledger row can cite it.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/borders.rs`: `BorderSet::DASHED` (and optional `HEAVY_DASHED`), `BorderType::Dashed` (optional `HeavyDashed`), `to_border_set()` arms, enum doc comment.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/block.rs`: no signature change; verify `border_set()` (:80) still compiles (it delegates).
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/widget_gallery.rs`: `render_borders` (:468) shows `Dashed` and `Custom`.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/snapshots/*widget_gallery*borders*.snap` (exact name per the existing insta layout): re-blessed.
- Any other file with an exhaustive `match` on `BorderType` (found by `rg`): new arms.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-widgets borders` passes with the new tests from `g17-06-tests` (`dashed_to_border_set_matches_const`, `border_set_tees_are_consistent` covering `DASHED`, `border_type_variant_count_matches_readme`).
- [ ] A `Block::bordered().border_type(BorderType::Dashed)` rendered at 10x3 produces a top row `┌┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┐` (assertion in `g17-06-tests`).
- [ ] Widget gallery snapshot re-blessed and visibly contains "Dashed" and "Custom" samples; `cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase` green.
- [ ] `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh` scenario `g17_06_border_styles` (added by `g17-e2e`) passes and logs the snapshot hash.
- [ ] Claims ledger row for README.md:2151 and :2183 updated by `g17-docs` to the real count with a pointer to the `BorderType` doc comment and the variant-count test.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean; CI `check` job green for the commit.

## Tests and logging

Unit tests (in `borders.rs` `#[cfg(test)]` and `block.rs` tests) are specified in `g17-06-tests`. Snapshot: insta snapshot of the widget gallery borders section at 80x24. E2E: `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh` scenario id `g17_06_border_styles` runs the showcase under `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` on the `WidgetGallery` screen (`FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN` set to its index), captures the canonicalized screen, asserts the glyph `┄` is present and the word "Dashed" appears, and appends one JSONL line via `tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh` with fields `run_id`, `scenario` (`g17_06_border_styles`), `screen` (`WidgetGallery`), `seed`, `snapshot_hash` (sha256 of the canonicalized capture), `exit_code`, `duration_ms`. Failures are diagnosable from the `.pty` capture path recorded next to the JSONL line.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: nothing (code work). The README text change that cites the new count is a DOC row and is done in `g17-docs`, which is blocked by `g06-impl-ledger` (cluster A).
- Unblocks: `g17-06-tests`, `g17-e2e` (scenario `g17_06_border_styles`), `g17-docs` (needs the final variant count).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- **Why `Dashed` and not nine variants:** the README number was decorative. Adding `Thick` (duplicate of `Heavy`), `Dotted` (a second dashed look) and others would add enum surface with no user pull. `Custom(BorderSet)` already covers arbitrary glyph sets, and we now make that discoverable in the gallery and the README.
- **Glyph choice:** `┄`/`┆` (U+2504/U+2506, "triple dash") are in the Box Drawing block and render in every terminal font that renders `─`; `╌`/`╎` (double dash) are an alternative. Width is 1 cell under `unicode-width`, so no layout change. If a terminal falls back for these glyphs the `Ascii` variant remains the safe choice, and the capability-aware fallback used elsewhere (`terminal_classic_for(ColorDepth)` in table_theme.rs:1504 is the analogue) is out of scope here.
- **Exhaustive matches:** every `match` on `BorderType` without a wildcard will fail to compile after adding a variant; that is desired (the compiler finds them). Fix each by hand.
- **Rollback:** removing the variant and const is a two-line revert; the snapshot re-bless is reverted with `BLESS=1`.
- **Deletion:** none required. If a stale snapshot file must be removed insta will do it through `cargo insta`; do not delete files manually without permission (AGENTS.md rule 1).

## Definition of done

`BorderType::Dashed` is reachable from the production path (`Block::border_type`, shown in the showcase gallery), the unit tests and re-blessed snapshot named above are green, the close reason names the final variant count and the test `border_type_variant_count_matches_readme`, the claims-ledger row for README.md:2151/:2183 is updated (via `g17-docs`), and `main` CI `check` is green for the commit.

title: task(G17.6): Unit tests and snapshots for Dashed and Custom border types
description:
# task(G17.6): Unit tests and snapshots for Dashed and Custom border types

## Context

Companion test bead for `g17-06-impl`, which adds `BorderType::Dashed` (glyph set `BorderSet::DASHED`) and makes the existing `Custom(BorderSet)` variant visible in the widget gallery. README.md:2151 claims `Block` has "9 border styles"; verified code at `crates/ftui-widgets/src/borders.rs:109-123` has six variants (`Square`, `Ascii`, `Rounded`, `Double`, `Heavy`, `Custom(BorderSet)`), and after the impl bead it has seven (or eight with the optional `HeavyDashed`). Serves V6/V39/V41 and Section 2.2.C row "9 border styles". The purpose of these tests is twofold: prove the new glyph set renders correctly end to end through `Block`, and tie the claims ledger to code with a test that fails whenever the variant count and the README count diverge again.

## What to test

- `BorderSet::DASHED` glyphs and `BorderType::Dashed -> DASHED` mapping.
- `Custom(BorderSet)` round-trip through `to_border_set()` (existing test at borders.rs:303, extended with a non-trivial set).
- Tee/cross glyph consistency for the new set (existing `border_set_tees_are_consistent` at borders.rs:380 extended).
- `Block` rendering with `Dashed` and with a `Custom` ASCII-only set at small sizes, including `Borders::TOP | Borders::BOTTOM` partial borders.
- Variant count parity with the README number (the ledger guard).
- Widget gallery snapshot showing "Dashed" and "Custom" samples.

## Test types

Unit (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/borders.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`):
- `dashed_to_border_set_matches_const`: `assert_eq!(BorderType::Dashed.to_border_set(), BorderSet::DASHED)`; also `assert_eq!(BorderSet::DASHED.horizontal, '┄')` and `assert_eq!(BorderSet::DASHED.vertical, '┆')`; corners equal `BorderSet::SQUARE` corners.
- `custom_border_set_round_trips`: extend the existing test (:303) with a set whose eleven glyphs are all distinct ASCII characters (`#`, `+`, `-`, `|`, `=`, `T`, `^`, `<`, `>`, `*`, `~`) and assert every field survives `BorderType::Custom(set).to_border_set()`.
- `border_set_tees_are_consistent`: extend the existing test (:380) to iterate `[ASCII, SQUARE, ROUNDED, DOUBLE, HEAVY, DASHED]` (plus `HEAVY_DASHED` if added) and assert each tee glyph has display width 1 (`ftui_core::text_width::grapheme_width == 1`), and the set is `Copy`/`PartialEq` stable.
- `border_type_variant_count_matches_readme`: an `const ALL: &[BorderType] = &[Square, Ascii, Rounded, Double, Heavy, Dashed, Custom(BorderSet::SQUARE)]` array plus `assert_eq!(ALL.len(), BORDER_STYLE_COUNT)` where `pub const BORDER_STYLE_COUNT: usize` is a new public const in `borders.rs` that the claims ledger (`docs/claims-ledger.md`, G06) cites for README.md:2151 and :2183. A match with no wildcard over `ALL` guarantees the array is complete.

Unit (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/block.rs` tests, rendering into a headless `Frame::new(w, h, &mut GraphemePool)` from `ftui-render/src/frame.rs:477`):
- `block_dashed_renders_top_row`: `Block::bordered().border_type(BorderType::Dashed)` at `Rect::new(0,0,10,3)`; assert row 0 reads `┌┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┐`, row 1 starts with `┆` and ends with `┆`, row 2 reads `└┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┘`.
- `block_custom_ascii_renders`: `Custom` set with `#` corners and `-`/`|` edges at 6x3; assert row 0 is `#----#`.
- `block_dashed_partial_borders`: `Borders::TOP | Borders::BOTTOM` with `Dashed`; assert no `┆` glyph appears anywhere and both horizontal rows use `┄`.

Property (proptest, `borders.rs`): `prop_any_border_type_has_width_one_glyphs`: for a strategy over all variants plus random `Custom` sets drawn from printable ASCII, every glyph in `to_border_set()` has display width 1, so no border can ever shift layout.

Snapshot (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase`): re-bless the widget gallery borders section snapshot at 80x24 with `BLESS=1 cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase`; review with `cargo insta review`; the snapshot text must contain both "Dashed" and "Custom".

Bench: none (no speed claim in this row).

E2E: covered by `g17-e2e` scenario `g17_06_border_styles`.

## Logging

Unit tests print nothing on success. On failure the `Block` render tests print the full rendered grid (`buffer.to_string()` row by row) before asserting so a glyph mismatch is visible in the log. The snapshot test emits insta's diff. The E2E scenario logs JSONL (`tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh`) with `run_id`, `scenario=g17_06_border_styles`, `screen=WidgetGallery`, `seed`, `snapshot_hash`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`; tracing target for widget rendering remains the existing `widget_render` span (behind the `tracing` feature).

## Files

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/borders.rs`: new tests, `BORDER_STYLE_COUNT` const, extended existing tests at :303 and :380.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/block.rs`: three render tests.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/snapshots/`: re-blessed gallery snapshot.
- `docs/claims-ledger.md` (owned by G06): the row for README.md:2151/:2183 cites `BORDER_STYLE_COUNT` and `border_type_variant_count_matches_readme`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-widgets -- borders block` passes all tests named above.
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase` passes with the re-blessed snapshot containing "Dashed" and "Custom".
- [ ] `border_type_variant_count_matches_readme` fails if a variant is added or removed without updating `BORDER_STYLE_COUNT` (verify once by temporarily changing the const, then restore).
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: `g17-06-impl`.
- Unblocks: `g17-e2e` (scenario assertions rely on the glyphs proven here), `g17-docs` (ledger row cites the count test).

## Definition of done

All named tests exist and pass locally and in CI `check`; the snapshot is re-blessed and reviewed; the close reason lists the test names and the CI run id; the claims-ledger row cites `BORDER_STYLE_COUNT`.
notes: Refinement 4 command correction: run separate cargo test -p ftui-widgets borders and cargo test -p ftui-widgets block, or full crate tests. Historical cargo test -- borders block is not a valid two-filter selector.

title: feature(G17.7): TableTheme stripe/header/selection builders and per-column truncation and alignment
description:
# feature(G17.7): TableTheme stripe/header/selection builders and per-column truncation and alignment

## Context and why this matters

README.md:2176-2195 ("Table Theming System") promises a theme engine whose feature table includes: **"Row striping | Alternating background colors with configurable period"**, **"Header styling | Separate style for header row with bottom border"**, **"Selection highlight | Active row/cell highlight with blend modes"**, **"Truncation | Ellipsis, clip, or wrap per column"**, **"Alignment | Left/center/right per column with Unicode-aware width"**, and shows this snippet at :2191-2194:

```rust
let theme = TableTheme::modern()
    .with_stripe_period(2)
    .with_header_style(Style::new().bold().fg(Color::Cyan))
    .with_selection_style(Style::new().bg(Color::DarkGray));
```

The reality check (Section 2.2.C row "`TableTheme::modern().with_stripe_period(2)...`") found: presets `aurora` .. `terminal_classic`, no `modern`, no such builders, striping is a fixed `row_alt` style, no per-column truncation/alignment. The G06 decision table marks this row **CODE**, landing in G17.7. Vision rows served: V39 ("Table theming engine", PARTIAL / WRONG_API), V6, V41. User-visible consequence today: the README snippet does not compile, and a consumer cannot control stripe period or per-column truncation at all, which matters for dense data tables (the primary agent-harness use case shows tool output in tables).

The DOC side of this row (README text matching the final API) is a G06 claims-ledger row executed in `g17-docs` and depends on `g06-impl-ledger` (cluster A); the code here does not.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-style/src/table_theme.rs:418-445` `pub struct TableTheme { border: Style, header: Style, row: Style, row_alt: Style, row_selected: Style, row_hover: Style, divider: Style, padding: u8, column_gap: u8, row_height: u8, effects: Vec<TableEffectRule>, preset_id: Option<TablePresetId> }`. No stripe period field.
- Builders `:1184-1275`: `with_border`, `with_header`, `with_row`, `with_row_alt`, `with_row_selected`, `with_row_hover`, `with_divider`, `with_padding`, `with_column_gap`, `with_row_height`, `with_effects`, `with_effect`, `with_preset_id`. None named `with_stripe_period`, `with_header_style`, `with_selection_style`.
- Presets: `aurora` :1282, `graphite` :1309, `neon` :1335, `slate` :1362, `solar` :1388, `orchard` :1415, `paper` :1442, `midnight` :1471, `terminal_classic` :1498, `terminal_classic_for(ColorDepth)` :1504. No `modern`.
- `TablePresetId` :31 (Aurora, Graphite, Neon, Slate, Solar, Orchard, Paper, ...); `TableSection` :55; `TableEffect` :210; `BlendMode` :240; `TableEffectRule` :298; `TableEffectRuleSpec` :597.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs:10` `use ftui_layout::{Constraint, Flex}`; `Row` :29; `Table` fields :80-87 (`widths: Vec<Constraint>`, `style`, `highlight_style`, `theme: TableTheme`, `theme_phase: f32`, `column_spacing`); `Table::new(rows, widths)` :100; `header(Row)` :134; `theme(TableTheme)` :162; `theme_phase(f32)` :171. Column widths are solved with `Flex`; there is no per-column truncation or alignment API; the reality check found striping is "a fixed `row_alt` style" (alternate every other row).
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs:604-614` hover is a plain compare (owned by G18, not this bead).
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/table_theme_gallery.rs:55-57` builds themes with `TableTheme::preset(id)`, `terminal_classic_for(ColorDepth::Ansi16)` and `terminal_classic()`; `custom_presets` :235; `preset_count` :344.

## Target state

- `TableTheme` has `stripe_period: u8` (default 2; 0 disables striping) and `with_stripe_period(u8)`.
- Builder names match the README: `with_header_style(Style)` and `with_selection_style(Style)`. Decision: **rename** the existing `with_header` and `with_row_selected` to these names and update every caller by hand (no aliases, no deprecated wrappers, per AGENTS.md "no compatibility shims"). `with_row_hover`, `with_row_alt` etc. keep their names.
- `TableTheme::modern()` exists as a real preset (a graphite-derived neutral palette with bold header, stripe period 2, subtle divider) with `TablePresetId::Modern`, and is listed in `TableTheme::preset(id)` and the gallery.
- `Table` supports per-column options: `with_column_truncation(col: usize, Truncate)` where `pub enum Truncate { Ellipsis, Clip, Wrap }` (default `Clip`, which is today's behaviour) and `with_column_alignment(col: usize, Alignment)` (reusing `ftui_widgets::block::Alignment { Left, Center, Right }`). Width and padding computations use `ftui_core::text_width` so CJK and emoji align correctly.
- The renderer applies striping as `row_index % stripe_period == stripe_period - 1` (so period 2 keeps today's every-other-row look and period 0 never stripes), applies `header` to the header row, and `row_selected` over stripe and hover.
- `Wrap` truncation increases the row's rendered height up to `row_height` lines (the field already exists at :440) and never beyond.
- `table_theme_gallery` shows one table with stripe period 3, one column truncated with `Ellipsis`, one right-aligned numeric column.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-style/src/table_theme.rs`: add `pub stripe_period: u8` to `TableTheme` (:418-445) and initialise it to 2 in every preset constructor (`aurora` :1282 .. `terminal_classic` :1498) and in `Default`. Add `pub fn with_stripe_period(mut self, period: u8) -> Self` next to `with_row_height` (:1247). Add it to `TableThemeDiagnostics` (declared right after the struct) so the gallery's diagnostics panel shows it.
2. Same file: rename `with_header` (:1191) to `with_header_style` and `with_row_selected` (:1212) to `with_selection_style`. Run `rg -n 'with_header\(|with_row_selected\(' crates -g '*.rs'` and fix each call site by hand (expected in table_theme.rs presets, table_theme_gallery.rs, and tests). Do not keep the old names.
3. Same file: add `TablePresetId::Modern` (:31) and `pub fn modern() -> Self` after `midnight` (:1471); wire it into `TableTheme::preset(id)` and any `TablePresetId` iteration/`as_str`/`from_str` helper found by `rg -n 'TablePresetId::' crates -g '*.rs'`. If `TableEffectRuleSpec` (:597) serialises preset ids, add the new id there too.
4. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs`: add `pub enum Truncate { Ellipsis, Clip, Wrap }` (derive `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default` with `Clip` default) and `pub struct ColumnSpec { pub truncation: Truncate, pub alignment: Alignment }`; add `column_specs: Vec<ColumnSpec>` to `Table` (:80-87), sized lazily to `widths.len()`; add builders `with_column_truncation(col, Truncate)`, `with_column_alignment(col, Alignment)`, `with_column_spec(col, ColumnSpec)`.
5. Same file, cell rendering: where a cell's text is written into its solved column rect, compute display width with `ftui_core::text_width` (the workspace's production width function), then: `Clip` (current behaviour), `Ellipsis` (fit `width - 1` graphemes and append `…`, or `...` when the theme is `terminal_classic_for(Ansi16)`-style ASCII), `Wrap` (use `ftui_text` wrapping to at most `theme.row_height` lines and render extra lines below). Alignment computes the left offset as `0`, `(w - tw) / 2`, or `w - tw` in cells.
6. Same file, striping: replace the every-other-row selection of `row_alt` with the `stripe_period` rule above; header row uses `theme.header`; selected row uses `theme.row_selected` regardless of stripe; hover (`row_hover`) is applied after stripe and before selection, unchanged in priority from today.
7. `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/table_theme_gallery.rs`: add `Modern` to the preset list at :55 (via `TableTheme::preset`), add a "Column options" table with stripe period 3, an `Ellipsis` column containing a CJK string, and a right-aligned numeric column; re-bless snapshots.
8. Run `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`; `ubs` on every touched file before commit.
9. Do NOT: add `with_header` back as a wrapper; create `table_theme_v2.rs` or `table2.rs`; introduce a second theme type; delete any file (permission required); change hover logic (G18 owns it).

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-style/src/table_theme.rs`: `stripe_period` field + builder, renamed builders, `modern()` preset, `TablePresetId::Modern`, diagnostics.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs`: `Truncate`, `ColumnSpec`, builders, cell truncation/alignment, stripe rule.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/table_theme_gallery.rs`: Modern preset, column-options table.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/snapshots/`: re-blessed `table_theme_gallery_*` snapshots.
- Every caller of the renamed builders found by `rg` (hand-edited).
- `crates/ftui-style/src/lib.rs:66-70`: export `Truncate`/`ColumnSpec` only if they live in ftui-style; they live in ftui-widgets by this plan, so export from `ftui-widgets/src/lib.rs` instead.

## Success criteria

- [ ] The README snippet (`TableTheme::modern().with_stripe_period(2).with_header_style(..).with_selection_style(..)`) compiles verbatim in a doc-test after G02's README doc-test mechanism lands; until then it compiles in `crates/ftui-widgets/tests/table_theme_readme.rs`.
- [ ] Unit tests from `g17-07-tests` green: `stripe_period_zero_disables_alt_rows`, `stripe_period_three_pattern`, `header_style_applied_to_header_row`, `selection_style_over_stripe`, `truncate_ellipsis_cjk_width`, `truncate_clip`, `truncate_wrap_increases_row_height`, `align_right_unicode_width`, `modern_preset_has_id`.
- [ ] `table_theme_gallery_*` snapshots re-blessed and reviewed; `cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase` green.
- [ ] `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh` scenario `g17_07_table_theme_columns` (from `g17-e2e`) passes and logs the snapshot hash.
- [ ] Claims-ledger rows for README.md:2176-2195 marked CODE with a link to this bead (via `g17-docs`).
- [ ] `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean; CI `check` green.

## Tests and logging

Unit/property/snapshot tests are specified in `g17-07-tests`. E2E: `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh` scenario id `g17_07_table_theme_columns` runs the showcase under `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` on the `TableThemeGallery` screen, cycles to the Modern preset and the column-options table using the screen's existing key handling, canonicalizes the capture, asserts an `…` glyph exists in the ellipsis column and that the numeric column's digits end at the column's right edge, and writes one JSONL line (`tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh`) with `run_id`, `scenario` (`g17_07_table_theme_columns`), `screen` (`TableThemeGallery`), `seed`, `snapshot_hash`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`. The `TableThemeDiagnostics` payload (which the gallery already renders) gains `stripe_period` so a wrong period is visible in the capture.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: none for code. `g17-docs` (README text) is blocked by `g06-impl-ledger` (cluster A).
- Unblocks: `g17-07-tests`, `g17-e2e` (scenario `g17_07_table_theme_columns`), `g17-docs`.
- Touches `table.rs` rendering, which G18 (`g18-impl`, hover stabilizer) also edits at :604-614; land this bead first or coordinate through Agent Mail file reservations on `crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- **Rename vs add:** adding `with_header_style` while keeping `with_header` would be a compatibility alias, which AGENTS.md forbids. The rename touches a handful of callers (presets and the gallery) and is done by hand.
- **`modern` as a new preset vs DOC mapping:** mapping README's `modern` to `graphite` in prose would leave the snippet non-compiling; a real preset is cheap (about 25 lines, same shape as `graphite` at :1309) and gives the ledger a concrete symbol.
- **Where `Truncate` lives:** truncation and alignment are rendering concerns of the `Table` widget, not theme colours, so they live in ftui-widgets. Putting them in `TableTheme` would force ftui-style to know about text layout.
- **Wrap and row height:** `Wrap` can only grow a row to `row_height` lines; rows never exceed it, so scrolling math in `Table` stays stable. Document this cap.
- **Width function:** use `ftui_core::text_width` (the production path per Section 2.2.B; the `ftui-text` width caches are dead and G08 decides their fate). Do not introduce a new width helper.
- **Rollback:** the field and builders are additive except for the rename; reverting is a mechanical rename back.

## Definition of done

The README snippet compiles against the real API, per-column truncation and alignment are honoured by `Table::render` (production path) and shown in the showcase gallery, all tests in `g17-07-tests` and the re-blessed snapshots are green, the close reason names the tests and the CI run id, and the claims-ledger rows for README.md:2176-2195 are updated by `g17-docs`.

# task(G17.7): Unit tests and table_theme_gallery snapshots for TableTheme builders and column options

## Context

Companion test bead for `g17-07-impl`, which adds `TableTheme::stripe_period`/`with_stripe_period`, renames `with_header`/`with_row_selected` to the README names `with_header_style`/`with_selection_style`, adds the `modern()` preset (`TablePresetId::Modern`), and gives `Table` per-column `Truncate::{Ellipsis, Clip, Wrap}` and `Alignment::{Left, Center, Right}`. README.md:2176-2195 promises "Row striping ... configurable period", "Truncation | Ellipsis, clip, or wrap per column", "Alignment | Left/center/right per column with Unicode-aware width" and the snippet `TableTheme::modern().with_stripe_period(2).with_header_style(..).with_selection_style(..)` (:2191-2194). Verified code before the impl: `TableTheme` fields at `crates/ftui-style/src/table_theme.rs:418-445` with no stripe field, builders :1184-1275 without the README names, presets :1282-1504 without `modern`; `Table` at `crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs:80-87` with no column options. Serves V39/V6/V41 and Section 2.2.C. No speed claim is made in this row, so there is no bench.

## What to test

- Stripe period semantics: 0 = off, 2 = today's look, 3 = every third row.
- Header and selection styles reach the right cells; selection wins over stripe; hover priority unchanged.
- Truncation modes with Unicode-aware width (CJK double-width, emoji).
- Alignment with Unicode-aware width.
- `Wrap` grows rows only up to `row_height`.
- `modern()` preset identity and diagnostics.
- README snippet compiles.
- Gallery snapshots.

## Test types

Unit (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs` tests; render into a headless `Frame::new(w, h, &mut GraphemePool)` per `ftui-render/src/frame.rs:477`, six rows `r0..r5` of one column, theme with `row` fg white and `row_alt` fg yellow so stripes are detectable by cell fg):
- `stripe_period_zero_disables_alt_rows`: `with_stripe_period(0)`; assert every body row cell fg == `row` fg.
- `stripe_period_two_matches_previous_behaviour`: period 2; rows r1, r3, r5 get `row_alt`, r0, r2, r4 get `row`.
- `stripe_period_three_pattern`: period 3; only r2 and r5 get `row_alt`.
- `header_style_applied_to_header_row`: `Table::new(..).header(Row::new(["H"])).theme(theme.with_header_style(bold cyan))`; assert the header row cell has bold attr and cyan fg and no body row does.
- `selection_style_over_stripe`: select r1 (an `row_alt` row) through the table state; assert its cells carry `row_selected` bg, not `row_alt`.
- `truncate_clip`: column width 4, text `abcdef`; assert the row reads `abcd`.
- `truncate_ellipsis_cjk_width`: column width 5, text `日本語テキスト` (2 cells each); `Ellipsis`; assert the rendered cells are `日本…` followed by a blank cell (never a half glyph), computed with `ftui_core::text_width`.
- `truncate_ellipsis_ascii_fallback`: same with an ASCII-only theme (`terminal_classic_for(ColorDepth::Ansi16)`), assert `...` is used.
- `truncate_wrap_increases_row_height`: `row_height` 2, `Wrap`, width 4, text `abcdefgh`; assert two lines `abcd`/`efgh` and that a 12-char text still occupies exactly 2 lines (cap).
- `align_right_unicode_width`: width 8, text `12😀` (emoji width 2) right aligned; assert the last cell column holds the emoji's trailing cell and the first four cells are blank.
- `align_center_odd_padding`: width 7, text `ab`; assert left offset 2.
- `column_spec_out_of_range_is_ignored`: `with_column_alignment(9, Right)` on a 2-column table does not panic and does not change rendering.

Unit (`crates/ftui-style/src/table_theme.rs` tests):
- `modern_preset_has_id`: `TableTheme::modern().preset_id == Some(TablePresetId::Modern)` and `TableTheme::preset(TablePresetId::Modern)` equals it field by field.
- `stripe_period_default_is_two`: every preset constructor and `Default` produce `stripe_period == 2`.
- `diagnostics_include_stripe_period`: the diagnostics payload carries the value.
- `readme_builder_chain_compiles`: `TableTheme::modern().with_stripe_period(2).with_header_style(Style::new().bold()).with_selection_style(Style::new())` and assert `stripe_period == 2` and header bold.

Property (proptest, `table.rs`): `prop_truncation_never_exceeds_width`: for random Unicode strings (drawn from ASCII, CJK, emoji) and widths 1..20 and any `Truncate`, the rendered cell span's display width is <= width and no wide glyph is split.

Snapshot (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase`): re-bless `table_theme_gallery_*` snapshots (the gallery now includes the Modern preset and a "Column options" table with stripe period 3, an ellipsis column and a right-aligned column); add `table_column_options_60x8` as a harness widget snapshot in `crates/ftui-harness/tests/widget_snapshots.rs` (the file that `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh:647` runs as `07_snapshots`).

Bench: none.

E2E: `g17-e2e` scenario `g17_07_table_theme_columns`.

## Logging

On assertion failure the table tests print the rendered grid row by row and the per-cell fg/bg/attr triple for the failing row so stripe or style regressions are readable from CI logs. The E2E scenario writes JSONL with `run_id`, `scenario=g17_07_table_theme_columns`, `screen=TableThemeGallery`, `seed`, `snapshot_hash`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`. The gallery's diagnostics panel (rendered from `TableThemeDiagnostics`) shows `stripe_period` so the PTY capture is self-describing.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs`: unit + property tests.
- `crates/ftui-style/src/table_theme.rs`: preset/builder tests.
- `crates/ftui-harness/tests/widget_snapshots.rs`: `table_column_options_60x8`.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/snapshots/`: re-blessed gallery snapshots.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-widgets table` and `cargo test -p ftui-style table_theme` pass every test named above.
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-harness --test widget_snapshots` includes and passes `table_column_options_60x8`.
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase` passes with re-blessed `table_theme_gallery_*` snapshots reviewed via `cargo insta review`.
- [ ] `prop_truncation_never_exceeds_width` runs 256 cases in under 5 s.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: `g17-07-impl`.
- Unblocks: `g17-e2e`, `g17-docs`.

## Definition of done

All named tests exist and pass in CI `check` and `e2e-widget-api`; snapshots are reviewed; the close reason lists the test names and the CI run id.

title: feature(G17.8): StyleSheet consumers: Block::styled(name) and Table::with_stylesheet(&sheet)
description:
# feature(G17.8): StyleSheet consumers: Block::styled(name) and Table::with_stylesheet(&sheet)

## Context and why this matters

README.md:2197-2208 ("Stylesheet System") promises: "Named styles are registered in a `Stylesheet` for consistent theming across widgets", with the snippet

```rust
let mut sheet = Stylesheet::new();
sheet.register("heading", Style::new().bold().fg(Color::Blue));
sheet.register("error", Style::new().fg(Color::Red).bold());
sheet.register("muted", Style::new().fg(Color::DarkGray));
// Apply by name anywhere in the widget tree
let style = sheet.get("heading").unwrap_or_default();
```

The reality check (Section 2.2.C row "`Stylesheet::new(); sheet.register(..); sheet.get(..).unwrap_or_default()`") found: the type is `StyleSheet` with `define/get -> Option<Style>/get_or_default/compose`, and **no widget consumes it**. Vision row V40 ("Stylesheet", WRONG_API / no consumer). The G06 decision table resolves this row as "DOC (`StyleSheet::define`) + CODE consumer", landing in G17.8. User-visible consequence today: "consistent theming across widgets" is a sentence, not a capability; every widget is styled with ad-hoc `Style` values and there is no name-based indirection to re-theme an app.

This bead is the CODE half: widgets that actually resolve named styles. The DOC half (README uses `StyleSheet::define`) is a claims-ledger row done in `g17-docs`, blocked by `g06-impl-ledger` (cluster A). Code here has no such dependency.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-style/src/stylesheet.rs:83` `pub struct StyleSheet { styles: RwLock<AHashMap<String, Style>> }` (interior mutability; `define` takes `&self`).
- `:151` `pub fn define(&self, name: impl Into<String>, style: Style)` (replaces existing name).
- `:168` `pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Style>`; `:174` `pub fn get_or_default(&self, name: &str) -> Style`; `:220` `pub fn compose(&self, names: &[&str]) -> Style` (merges in order).
- `crates/ftui-style/src/lib.rs:65` `pub use stylesheet::{StyleId, StyleSheet};`.
- Verified with `rg -ln 'StyleSheet' crates -g '*.rs'`: the only files outside the module that mention it are `crates/ftui-style/src/lib.rs` and `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs` (re-exports). Zero widget or showcase consumers.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/block.rs` `Block<'a>` fields (around :14-24): `borders`, `border_style`, `border_type`, `title`, `title_alignment`, `style`, `padding`; builders `border_style(Style)` :60, `border_type` :67, `title` :86, `title_alignment` :99, `style(Style)` :106.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs:162` `Table::theme(TableTheme)`; `TableTheme` fields at `crates/ftui-style/src/table_theme.rs:418-445` (`border`, `header`, `row`, `row_alt`, `row_selected`, `row_hover`, `divider`, ...).
- `crates/ftui-widgets/Cargo.toml:31` depends on `ftui-style`, so widgets can take `&StyleSheet` without a new dependency.
- README names: `Stylesheet::new()`, `sheet.register(..)`; code names: `StyleSheet::new()` (via `Default`), `define`.

## Target state

- `Block::styled(sheet: &StyleSheet, name: &str) -> Block` (associated constructor) and `Block::with_stylesheet(self, sheet, name)` (builder on an existing block): sets `style` from `sheet.get(name)` and `border_style` from `sheet.compose(&[name, &format!("{name}.border")])`, falling back to the defaults when names are missing. Resolution happens at build time; `Block` keeps no reference to the sheet (no new lifetime).
- `Table::with_stylesheet(self, sheet: &StyleSheet) -> Table`: builds a `TableTheme` from the convention names `table.border`, `table.header`, `table.row`, `table.row_alt`, `table.row_selected`, `table.row_hover`, `table.divider` (each optional; missing names keep the current theme's value) and sets it via the existing `theme()` (:162). Also `Table::with_stylesheet_prefix(self, sheet, prefix)` so two tables can use `tools.*` and `logs.*`.
- Convention names are documented as constants in `ftui-widgets/src/lib.rs` (`pub mod style_names { pub const TABLE_HEADER: &str = "table.header"; ... }`) so typos are caught at compile time inside the workspace.
- The showcase owns one `StyleSheet` (in its theme module) populated from the active `Theme`, and `widget_gallery` builds at least one `Block` and the "Table" block (`widget_gallery.rs:675` `.title("Table")`) through the sheet, so switching the showcase theme re-themes those widgets by name.
- A renamed or redefined style propagates on the next build (tested in `g17-08-tests`).

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/lib.rs`: add `pub mod style_names` with the seven `table.*` constants plus `BLOCK_BORDER_SUFFIX: &str = ".border"`; re-export `ftui_style::StyleSheet` from the widgets prelude if one exists (check `lib.rs` for a `prelude` module; if none, skip).
2. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/block.rs`: add `pub fn styled(sheet: &StyleSheet, name: &str) -> Self { Self::default().with_stylesheet(sheet, name) }` and `pub fn with_stylesheet(mut self, sheet: &StyleSheet, name: &str) -> Self` that sets `self.style = sheet.get_or_default(name)` and `self.border_style = sheet.compose(&[name, &format!("{name}{BLOCK_BORDER_SUFFIX}")])`. Import `ftui_style::StyleSheet`. Document that later `.style()`/`.border_style()` calls override.
3. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs`: add `pub fn with_stylesheet(self, sheet: &StyleSheet) -> Self { self.with_stylesheet_prefix(sheet, "table") }` and `with_stylesheet_prefix(mut self, sheet, prefix: &str)` that clones `self.theme`, overwrites each field for which `sheet.get(&format!("{prefix}.{role}"))` is `Some`, and stores it back. Roles: `border, header, row, row_alt, row_selected, row_hover, divider`.
4. `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/theme.rs` (the showcase theme module; confirm the path with `rg -n 'pub fn syntax_theme' crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src`): add `pub fn stylesheet(theme: &Theme) -> StyleSheet` that defines `heading`, `heading.border`, `muted`, `error`, and the seven `table.*` names from the theme's colours. Store the sheet on the app model (`app.rs`) and rebuild it when the theme changes.
5. `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/widget_gallery.rs`: in `render_lists_and_table` (:646) build the table block with `Block::styled(&sheet, "heading").title("Table")` and the table with `.with_stylesheet(&sheet)`; in `render_text_styles` (:533) add a "Stylesheet" sample block. Re-bless snapshots.
6. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`; `ubs` on touched files.
7. Do NOT: rename `StyleSheet` to `Stylesheet` or add a `register` alias (README moves to the real names via G06 DOC); store `&StyleSheet` inside widgets (would add lifetimes to `Block`/`Table` and complicate every caller); create a second sheet type; delete anything.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/lib.rs`: `style_names` constants.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/block.rs`: `styled`, `with_stylesheet`.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs`: `with_stylesheet`, `with_stylesheet_prefix`.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/theme.rs` (or the module that defines `syntax_theme`): `stylesheet(&Theme)`.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs`: owns the sheet, rebuilds on theme change.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/widget_gallery.rs`: consumes the sheet at :533 and :646-675.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/snapshots/`: re-blessed gallery snapshots.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `g17-08-tests` green: `block_styled_reads_sheet`, `redefine_style_then_rebuild_propagates`, `missing_name_falls_back_to_default`, `table_with_stylesheet_maps_roles`, `compose_precedence_name_then_border`, `explicit_style_overrides_sheet`.
- [ ] `rg -ln 'StyleSheet' crates -g '*.rs'` lists `block.rs`, `table.rs`, the showcase theme module and `widget_gallery.rs` in addition to the re-exports (reachability proof for G07's gate).
- [ ] Snapshot `widget_gallery_stylesheet_80x24` (or the re-blessed gallery section) shows the styled block; `cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase` green.
- [ ] `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh` scenario `g17_08_stylesheet` (from `g17-e2e`) passes: switching the showcase theme changes the heading colour of the gallery table block.
- [ ] Claims-ledger row for README.md:2197-2208 updated by `g17-docs` (README shows `StyleSheet::default()`/`define`/`get_or_default` and mentions `Block::styled` and `Table::with_stylesheet`).
- [ ] clippy `-D warnings`, fmt clean; CI `check` green.

## Tests and logging

Unit and snapshot tests are specified in `g17-08-tests`. E2E: `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh` scenario id `g17_08_stylesheet` runs the showcase on `WidgetGallery` under `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh`, captures once, presses the theme-cycle key the showcase already exposes, captures again, and asserts the SGR colour of the "Table" title cell differs between captures (parsed from the raw capture, not the canonicalized one). JSONL line via `tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh`: `run_id`, `scenario` (`g17_08_stylesheet`), `screen` (`WidgetGallery`), `seed`, `snapshot_hash` (both captures, as `snapshot_hash` and `snapshot_hash_after_theme`), `exit_code`, `duration_ms`. Optional tracing: a `debug!(target: "ftui.widgets.stylesheet", name, found)` line behind the widgets `tracing` feature when a name is missing, so mis-typed names show up in logs.

## Dependencies and ordering

- Blocked by: none for code. `g17-docs` (README rewrite for this row) is blocked by `g06-impl-ledger` (cluster A).
- Unblocks: `g17-08-tests`, `g17-e2e` (scenario `g17_08_stylesheet`), `g17-docs`.
- Shares `table.rs` and `widget_gallery.rs` with `g17-07-impl` and `g17-06-impl`; land after them or reserve the files via Agent Mail.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- **Build-time resolution vs stored reference:** storing `&StyleSheet` in widgets would add a lifetime parameter to `Block` and `Table` (both used in hundreds of places) for no runtime benefit, since `view()` rebuilds widgets each frame anyway. Build-time resolution keeps the API additive.
- **Convention names vs typed keys:** `StyleId` exists at `stylesheet.rs` (exported at lib.rs:65) and could type the keys, but the README promises string names; the `style_names` constants give workspace-internal safety without changing the public contract.
- **`RwLock` cost:** `get` takes a read lock per lookup; a `Block` does two lookups and a `Table` seven, per build, which is negligible against rendering. Not a hot path.
- **Not renaming the type:** `StyleSheet` is the correct Rust casing; the README is wrong and G06 fixes it as DOC.
- **Rollback:** additive methods; removing them and reverting the gallery restores today's behaviour.

## Definition of done

`StyleSheet` has production consumers (`Block::styled`, `Table::with_stylesheet`) exercised by the showcase gallery, the tests in `g17-08-tests` and the re-blessed snapshot are green, the reachability grep lists the consumers, the close reason names the tests and the CI run id, and the claims-ledger row for README.md:2197-2208 is updated by `g17-docs`.

# task(G17.8): Tests that a renamed StyleSheet style propagates to Block and Table

## Context

Companion test bead for `g17-08-impl`, which gives `StyleSheet` (`crates/ftui-style/src/stylesheet.rs:83`; `define` :151, `get -> Option<Style>` :168, `get_or_default` :174, `compose` :220) its first widget consumers: `Block::styled(&sheet, name)` / `Block::with_stylesheet` and `Table::with_stylesheet(&sheet)` / `with_stylesheet_prefix`. README.md:2197-2208 promises "Named styles are registered in a `Stylesheet` for consistent theming across widgets ... Apply by name anywhere in the widget tree". Before the impl, `rg` showed zero consumers outside the ftui-style and ftui facade re-exports (V40 "WRONG_API / no consumer"). These tests prove the promise the README makes: change a named style once, and every widget built from that name changes.

## What to test

- A block built by name carries the sheet's style and border style.
- Redefining a name and rebuilding propagates (the README's "consistent theming" claim).
- Missing names fall back to defaults without panicking.
- Table role mapping (`table.header` etc.) into `TableTheme` fields, with untouched roles preserved.
- `compose` precedence for `name` then `name.border`.
- Explicit builder calls after `with_stylesheet` override the sheet.
- Prefix variant isolates two tables.
- Gallery snapshot.

## Test types

Unit (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/block.rs` tests, rendering into a headless `Frame::new(w, h, &mut GraphemePool)` from `ftui-render/src/frame.rs:477`):
- `block_styled_reads_sheet`: `sheet.define("heading", Style::new().bold().fg(blue))`; `Block::styled(&sheet, "heading").borders(Borders::ALL).title("T")` at 8x3; assert the title cell is bold+blue and the border cells carry the composed style (blue, since `heading.border` is undefined and compose of `[heading]` yields heading).
- `redefine_style_then_rebuild_propagates`: define `heading` bold blue, build and render, assert blue; `sheet.define("heading", Style::new().fg(red))`; build a new `Block::styled` and render; assert red and not bold. This is the claim the README makes.
- `missing_name_falls_back_to_default`: `Block::styled(&sheet, "nope")` renders identically to `Block::default()` (cell-by-cell equality of the two buffers).
- `compose_precedence_name_then_border`: define `heading` fg blue, `heading.border` fg green; assert title cell blue, border cells green (later name wins in `compose`).
- `explicit_style_overrides_sheet`: `Block::styled(&sheet, "heading").style(Style::new().fg(red))`; assert red.

Unit (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs` tests):
- `table_with_stylesheet_maps_roles`: define `table.header` bold, `table.row_alt` fg yellow, `table.divider` fg grey; build `Table::new(rows, widths).header(Row::new(["H"])).with_stylesheet(&sheet)`; render; assert header cell bold, second body row yellow, and that `row_selected` (undefined in the sheet) equals the previous theme's value (introspect via `table.theme()` accessor if present, otherwise via rendered selected-row bg).
- `table_stylesheet_prefix_isolates`: define `tools.header` and `logs.header` with different fgs; two tables with `with_stylesheet_prefix(&sheet, "tools")` and `"logs"`; assert each header uses its own colour.
- `table_stylesheet_missing_roles_keep_theme`: sheet with only `table.header`; every other theme field equals `TableTheme::default()`'s.

Unit (`crates/ftui-style/src/stylesheet.rs` tests, add if absent): `define_replaces_existing` and `compose_later_wins` to pin the semantics the widgets rely on (`define` at :151 replaces; `compose` at :220 merges in order).

Property (proptest, `block.rs`): `prop_styled_block_equals_manual_block`: for random `Style` values `s` and `b`, `Block::styled(&sheet_with(name: s, name.border: b), name)` renders identically to `Block::default().style(s).border_style(s.merge(&b))` (or whatever `compose` semantics the stylesheet test pins), so the sheet path is a pure function of the two direct builders.

Snapshot (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase`): `widget_gallery_stylesheet_80x24` (new insta snapshot of the gallery section that now builds its "Table" block and the "Stylesheet" text-style sample through the showcase sheet) re-blessed with `BLESS=1 cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase` and reviewed with `cargo insta review`. A second snapshot under the showcase's alternate theme proves the heading colour differs.

Bench: none (no speed claim).

E2E: `g17-e2e` scenario `g17_08_stylesheet`.

## Logging

The optional `debug!(target: "ftui.widgets.stylesheet", name, found = false)` line from the impl (behind the widgets `tracing` feature) is asserted in `missing_name_falls_back_to_default` when the feature is on, using the existing tracing test capture pattern in the crate if one exists (otherwise the test only checks rendering). E2E JSONL: `run_id`, `scenario=g17_08_stylesheet`, `screen=WidgetGallery`, `seed`, `snapshot_hash`, `snapshot_hash_after_theme`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/block.rs`: five unit tests + one proptest.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/table.rs`: three unit tests.
- `crates/ftui-style/src/stylesheet.rs`: two semantics-pinning tests (if not already present).
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/snapshots/`: `widget_gallery_stylesheet_80x24` (both themes).
