title: epic(G23): make 'runs in a browser' reproducible from this repo (in-tree host, wasm32 CI)
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:1245-1247 answers "### Can it run in a browser?" with "Yes. `ftui-web` provides a WASM adapter that renders through the same Rust core. `ftui-showcase-wasm` is the WASM build target for the demo showcase." README.md:690-698 ("## Web/WASM Backend") says "FrankenTUI targets both native terminals and web browsers from a single Rust codebase" and lists `ftui-web` as "Web adapter with pointer/touch parity, DPR/zoom handling". This epic closes vision row V8 ("Web/WASM backend, runs in browser") and Section 5.2 of the audit. The user-visible consequence today: a reader who clones the repo cannot see anything run in a browser. `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/frankentui_showcase_demo.html` imports an out-of-tree `pkg/FrankenTerm.js` bundle that this repository does not build, `pkg/` does not exist in-tree, neither web crate has ever been compiled for `wasm32` in CI, and the "DPR/zoom handling" claim is a code comment.

Status arrow: PARTIAL -> WORKING (owner decision on scope). Complexity L. Would open beads close it? No.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-web/src/lib.rs:8`: "This crate intentionally does not bind to `wasm-bindgen` yet. The primary purpose is to provide backend building blocks that `frankenterm-web` can wrap with a stable JS API." The crate is 12,350 lines, has zero `web_sys`/`wasm_bindgen`/canvas references, and implements the `ftui-backend` traits (`WebBackend` at `:565`, `WebPresenter` at `:379`, `WebEventSource` at `:165`, `DeterministicClock` at `:116` per the audit). It is a host-driven patch producer: the host pushes input and time, the crate emits `WebPatchRun`s.
- DPR/zoom: the only mention is a comment at `crates/ftui-web/src/step_program.rs:352-353` ("Host-side fit/DPR/zoom transitions can require a repaint boundary even when cols/rows remain numerically unchanged"). No cell-metric or device-pixel code exists.
- Pointer/touch parity is real: `crates/ftui-web/src/pane_pointer_capture.rs` (1,684 lines), tests `pane_web_e2e.rs`, `pane_cross_host_parity.rs`.
- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm` (4,130 lines: `lib.rs` 1,326, `runner_core.rs` 1,661, `wasm.rs` 1,143): `wasm.rs:540-541` `#[wasm_bindgen] pub struct ShowcaseRunner`, 48 `#[wasm_bindgen]` items under `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]` (`lib.rs:11-15`), exporting `new`, `init`, `advanceTime`, `setTime`, `pushEncodedInput`, `resize`, `step`, `takeFlatPatches`, `prepareFlatPatches`/`flatCellsPtr`/`flatCellsLen`/`flatSpansPtr`/`flatSpansLen`, `takeLogs`, `patchHash`, `patchStats`, `frameIdx`, `isRunning`, plus the `panePointer*`/`pane*` family (`wasm.rs:629-1030`). This matches `docs/spec/wasm-showcase-runner-contract.md` section 6 (`:275-343`). `Cargo.toml`: `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`, `publish = false`, wasm32-only deps `js-sys 0.3.103`, `wasm-bindgen 0.2.126`, `getrandom 0.4.3 (wasm_js)`; `[package.metadata.wasm-pack.profile.release] wasm-opt = ["-Oz"]`.
- Patch format (contract section 3, `:133-172`): `takeFlatPatches()` returns `{ cells: Uint32Array, spans: Uint32Array }`; spans are `[offset, len, ...]` in row-major linear cell indices; cells are 4 `u32` per cell `[bg, fg, glyph, attrs]` with `bg`/`fg` packed `0xRRGGBBAA`, `glyph` a codepoint (`0` empty, `0x25A1` grapheme fallback), `attrs` bits 0-7 `StyleFlags`, bits 8-31 link id. First frame after `init` or `resize` is a single full span `[0, cols*rows]`. Inputs (contract section 1, `:36-60`) are JSON strings such as `{"kind":"key","phase":"down","code":"a","mods":0,"repeat":false}` passed to `pushEncodedInput`.
- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/frankentui_showcase_demo.html:333-345`: `import('../../pkg/FrankenTerm.js')` and `import('../../pkg/ftui_showcase_wasm.js')`, then `termMod.default('../../pkg/FrankenTerm_bg.wasm')` and `runnerMod.default('../../pkg/ftui_showcase_wasm_bg.wasm')`. No `pkg/` directory is checked in.
- `./build-wasm.sh` (repository root): requires `wasm-pack`; builds the external `frankenterm-web` only when `FRANKENTERM_WEB_CRATE_DIR` is set ("Skipping frankenterm-web: this checkout has no crates/frankenterm-web"); then `wasm-pack build crates/ftui-showcase-wasm --target web --out-dir ../../pkg --release`; it also temporarily rewrites the root `Cargo.toml` with `sed` to drop the ftui-extras opt-level override.
- CI `.github/workflows/ci.yml:2256-2290` job `wasm` ("WASM Build Check") only `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` for `ftui-core`, `ftui-render`, `ftui-style`, `ftui-layout`, `ftui-text`, `ftui-i18n`, `frankenterm-core`; never `ftui-web` or `ftui-showcase-wasm`. `docs/getting-started.md:62-74` tells readers to `cargo check -p ftui-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and run `./build-wasm.sh`.
- `frankenterm-core` (crates.io 0.2.0) resolves; `scripts/frankenterm_js_*.sh` run in-tree tests (four in CI).

## Target state

- Both web crates build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` in CI (`g04-13-impl` owns the `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p ftui-web -p ftui-showcase-wasm` step; this block adds `wasm-pack build` of the showcase on top).
- A minimal in-tree JS host with no bundler, `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/showcase-host.js`, drives `ShowcaseRunner` (init, requestAnimationFrame loop calling `advanceTime`/`step`/`takeFlatPatches`, keyboard/mouse/resize to `pushEncodedInput`/`resize`) and paints flat patches into a `<pre>` grid of `<span>` cells, so `frankentui_showcase_demo.html` works from `wasm-pack build` alone when `pkg/FrankenTerm.js` is absent.
- DPR/zoom: either implemented for that host (cell metrics from `getBoundingClientRect`, `window.devicePixelRatio` and `visualViewport.scale` observed via `ResizeObserver`; a metric change triggers `resize(cols, rows)` even when cols/rows are unchanged, which is exactly the repaint boundary `step_program.rs:352` anticipates) or the README claim is removed. Decided in `g23-decision`.
- A headless-browser CI step loads the page, advances 60 frames, and asserts the Dashboard title text is present in the grid.
- README web sections say "host-driven patch producer" until a renderer exists in-tree.

## Success criteria (block level)

- [ ] `wasm` job builds `ftui-web` and `ftui-showcase-wasm` for wasm32 and runs `wasm-pack build crates/ftui-showcase-wasm --target web` producing `pkg/ftui_showcase_wasm_bg.wasm` (g04-13-impl + g23-impl).
- [ ] `tests/e2e/web/showcase_host.spec.mjs` (Playwright, chromium headless) passes in the `wasm` job: 60 frames advanced, grid contains the Dashboard title (g23-e2e).
- [ ] `docs/spec/wasm-showcase-runner-contract.md` section 6 still matches the exports (already true; g23-tests adds a test that keeps it true).
- [ ] DPR/zoom either implemented with a Playwright test at `deviceScaleFactor: 2` and `1` or the README row reads "pointer/touch parity" only (g23-impl-dpr, g23-docs).

## Plan (children)

1. `g23-decision` (question, P1): how far to go (minimal `<pre>` host vs waiting for an in-tree renderer; DPR/zoom implement vs retract; whether `build-wasm.sh`'s Cargo.toml `sed` rewrite is acceptable).
2. `g23-impl`: in-tree host + wasm-pack build + headless-browser CI step.
3. `g23-impl-dpr`: DPR/zoom for the `<pre>` host, or retract.
4. `g23-tests`: unit tests for the host's patch decoder (node), export-contract test, wasm32 `wasm-bindgen-test` smoke.
5. `g23-e2e`: Playwright scenario with JSONL logging.
6. `g23-docs`: README/getting-started wording, claims-ledger rows.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-13-impl` (wasm32 build job) and `g23-decision`. Unblocks: `g42-impl` (Section 7.6 row V8: "headless-browser CI step").

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Why a `<pre>` host rather than porting FrankenTerm's WebGPU renderer: the goal of V8 is "runs in a browser, reproducible from this repo". A few hundred lines of DOM code make the claim true and testable; the WebGPU path remains available via `FRANKENTERM_WEB_CRATE_DIR` for people who have the adjacent crate.
- Risk: `wasm-pack` availability on runners (install via `cargo install wasm-pack --locked` or the `jetli/wasm-pack-action`); Playwright needs `npx playwright install chromium` (cache it).
- Risk: `build-wasm.sh` rewrites `Cargo.toml` with `sed` and restores it on exit; a crash mid-build leaves a `Cargo.toml.bak`. The decision bead asks whether to replace the rewrite with a `[profile.wasm-release]` cargo profile.
- Rollback: the host is additive; removing it restores the current state.

## Definition of done

Headless-browser step green in CI (run id in close reason), `pkg/` reproducible from `wasm-pack build`, README web wording matches the code, claims-ledger rows present.

title: question(G23): owner decides web host scope, DPR/zoom, build profile and browser test
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:1245-1247 says "Can it run in a browser? Yes." and README.md:690-698 credits `ftui-web` with "DPR/zoom handling". From this repository alone nothing runs in a browser: the demo page needs an out-of-tree `pkg/FrankenTerm.js` and an unbuilt `pkg/ftui_showcase_wasm.js`, CI never compiles the web crates for wasm32, and DPR/zoom is one comment. The G23 epic can make the claim true with a small in-tree host, but how far to go is the owner's call because it sets the scope of the web story for the README. Serves V8, Section 5.2.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-web/src/lib.rs:8`: "intentionally does not bind to `wasm-bindgen` yet"; 12,350 lines; no DOM/canvas code; implements `ftui-backend` traits.
- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/src/wasm.rs:540-1140`: 48 `#[wasm_bindgen]` exports on `ShowcaseRunner`, matching `docs/spec/wasm-showcase-runner-contract.md:275-343`.
- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/frankentui_showcase_demo.html:333-345`: hard imports of `../../pkg/FrankenTerm.js`, `../../pkg/FrankenTerm_bg.wasm` (out-of-tree bundle) and `../../pkg/ftui_showcase_wasm.js` (built by `./build-wasm.sh`, not checked in).
- `./build-wasm.sh`: needs `wasm-pack`; builds FrankenTerm only with `FRANKENTERM_WEB_CRATE_DIR`; rewrites root `Cargo.toml` via `sed` to drop `[profile.release.package.ftui-extras] opt-level = 3` and restores it via `trap`.
- `crates/ftui-web/src/step_program.rs:352-353`: the only DPR/zoom text is a comment.
- CI `wasm` job (`ci.yml:2256-2290`) checks six core crates plus `frankenterm-core` for wasm32; `ftui-web` and `ftui-showcase-wasm` are never built.
- The patch contract (`docs/spec/wasm-showcase-runner-contract.md:133-172`) is simple enough for a DOM host: spans `[offset,len]`, cells `[bg,fg,glyph,attrs]` as `u32`.

## The question for the owner

1. **Host scope.** (a) Minimal in-tree `<pre>`-grid host `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/showcase-host.js` (recommended: ~300 lines, no bundler, no WebGPU; renders glyphs and colors, ignores links/underline styles beyond CSS classes); the demo HTML falls back to it when `pkg/FrankenTerm.js` is missing. (b) Port enough of FrankenTerm-web into this repo to keep the WebGPU path (weeks; out of scope for this plan). (c) Retract "runs in a browser" to "host-driven patch producer; browser rendering requires the adjacent frankenterm-web crate" and skip the host. Plan default: (a).
2. **DPR/zoom.** (a) Implement for the `<pre>` host in `g23-impl-dpr`: observe `window.devicePixelRatio`, `visualViewport.scale` and the cell box from `getBoundingClientRect()`; recompute `cols/rows` from the container size; call `runner.resize(cols, rows)` on any metric change (including same cols/rows, which triggers the full-repaint boundary at `step_program.rs:352`); Playwright test at `deviceScaleFactor` 1 and 2. (b) Retract the README phrase "DPR/zoom handling". Plan default: (a) if 1(a) is chosen, else (b).
3. **`build-wasm.sh` Cargo.toml rewrite.** Keep the `sed`-and-restore, or replace with a dedicated cargo profile `[profile.wasm-release]` (inherits release, no per-package opt-level override) selected via `wasm-pack build --profile`? Plan default: replace; the rewrite mutates a tracked file during builds and violates the spirit of "no script-based code edits" (AGENTS.md).
4. **Where the headless test runs.** Playwright chromium in the `wasm` job (plan default) vs `wasm-bindgen-test` in node only (no DOM; cannot assert the grid text).

## Target state

A comment on this bead answering the four questions; close reason "Decided: host=<a|b|c>; dpr=<a|b>; build-profile=<keep|replace>; browser-test=<playwright|wbt>". `g23-impl` and `g23-impl-dpr` execute accordingly; `g23-docs` writes the README wording that matches.

## Implementation plan

1. Owner reads the evidence (complete above; no code reading needed) and answers.
2. If 1(c) is chosen, `g23-impl` shrinks to "wasm-pack build in CI" and `g23-impl-dpr` closes as retract; `g23-e2e` becomes a node-side `wasm-bindgen-test` smoke that constructs `ShowcaseRunner(80,24)`, calls `init()` and `step()` and asserts `takeFlatPatches().spans` equals `[0, 1920]`.

What NOT to do: no deletions (nothing here deletes), no `_v2` HTML file (the fallback goes into the existing `frankentui_showcase_demo.html`), no vendoring of FrankenTerm's bundle into `pkg/`.

## Files to change

None by this bead.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Decision recorded with all four answers.

## Tests and logging

Not applicable; tests live in `g23-tests`/`g23-e2e`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: nothing. Unblocks: `g23-impl`, `g23-impl-dpr`, `g23-docs`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Option 1(a) is the cheapest way to make the README sentence literally true and CI-verifiable; it also gives `ftui-web` its first in-tree consumer that renders, which the audit noted was missing ("no DOM/canvas code").
- Keeping FrankenTerm out-of-tree is consistent with AGENTS.md:330-333 ("those crates are not currently vendored inside this workspace. Treat them as adjacent/external").

## Definition of done

Decision comment present; no code changed by this bead.

title: G23: In-tree text host demonstration with actual browser tests
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:1245-1247: "Can it run in a browser? Yes. `ftui-web` provides a WASM adapter that renders through the same Rust core. `ftui-showcase-wasm` is the WASM build target for the demo showcase." Today that is not reproducible from this repository: the demo page imports an out-of-tree FrankenTerm bundle, `pkg/` is never built, and CI never compiles either web crate for wasm32. This bead adds the minimal in-tree JS host, the `wasm-pack` build in CI, and the headless-browser step, so the sentence becomes true and stays true. Serves V8 and Section 5.2; it is the primary implementation bead of G23.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/frankentui_showcase_demo.html:327-345`: `let termMod, runnerMod; ... const termJsUrl = '../../pkg/FrankenTerm.js?v=...'; const runnerJsUrl = '../../pkg/ftui_showcase_wasm.js?v=...'; [termMod, runnerMod] = await Promise.all([import(termJsUrl), import(runnerJsUrl)]); ... termMod.default(termWasmUrl), runnerMod.default(runnerWasmUrl)`. The page is 84 KB and drives FrankenTerm's WebGPU surface (`term.input`, `term.drainEncodedInputs`, `term.applyPatchBatchFlat`, `term.render` per contract "Architecture", `docs/spec/wasm-showcase-runner-contract.md:8-34`).
- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/src/wasm.rs`: exports (all under `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")`): constructor `new(cols, rows)` (`:573`), `init`, `advanceTime` (`:605`), `setTime` (`:611`), `pushEncodedInput` (`:618`), `resize`, `step`, `takeFlatPatches` (`:1036`), `prepareFlatPatches`/`flatCellsPtr`/`flatCellsLen`/`flatSpansPtr`/`flatSpansLen` (`:1051-1090`), `takeLogs` (`:1091`), `patchHash` (`:1102`), `patchStats` (`:1108`), `frameIdx` (`:1127`), `isRunning` (`:1133`), `setShakespeareText` (`:585`), `setSqliteSource` (`:594`), pane pointer family (`:629-1030`).
- Patch encoding (`docs/spec/wasm-showcase-runner-contract.md:133-172`): `spans = [offset, len, ...]`, `cells = [bg, fg, glyph, attrs, ...]`, `bg`/`fg` `0xRRGGBBAA`, `glyph` codepoint (`0` empty, `0x25A1` fallback), `attrs` bits 0-7 StyleFlags (bold/italic/underline/strikethrough/dim/inverse/hidden/blink), bits 8-31 link id; first frame after `init`/`resize` is one span `[0, cols*rows]`; empty batches valid.
- Input encoding (`:44-59`): JSON strings, e.g. `{"kind":"key","phase":"down","code":"a","mods":0,"repeat":false}`, `{"kind":"mouse","phase":"down","button":0,"x":10,"y":5,"mods":0}`, `{"kind":"wheel",...}`, `{"kind":"paste","data":"..."}`, `{"kind":"focus","focused":true}`.
- `./build-wasm.sh`: `wasm-pack build crates/ftui-showcase-wasm --target web --out-dir ../../pkg --release` after a `sed` rewrite of the root `Cargo.toml` (restored on exit).
- `ci.yml:2256-2290` `wasm` job: `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown` then `cargo check` of six core crates and `frankenterm-core`.
- `crates/ftui-web/sdk/` exists (`examples/`, `frankenterm-js-events.d.ts`), establishing `sdk/` as the place for JS host material.
- `g04-13-impl` adds `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p ftui-web -p ftui-showcase-wasm` to the `wasm` job.

## Target state

- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/showcase-host.js` (ES module, no bundler, no dependencies): `export async function mountShowcase({ container, wasmUrl, cols, rows, frames })`. It `import`s `../../pkg/ftui_showcase_wasm.js` (path parameterized), `await init(wasmUrl)`, constructs `new ShowcaseRunner(cols, rows)`, calls `init()`, builds a `<pre class="ftui-grid">` with `rows` lines of `cols` `<span>` cells, then runs a `requestAnimationFrame` loop: `runner.advanceTime(dt_ms)`, `const s = runner.step()`, `if (s.rendered) paint(runner.takeFlatPatches())`. `paint` decodes spans/cells per the contract and sets `span.textContent = String.fromCodePoint(glyph || 0x20)` and `span.style.color/backgroundColor` from the packed RGBA, toggling CSS classes for the 8 style bits. Keyboard (`keydown`/`keyup`), mouse (`mousedown`/`mouseup`/`mousemove`/`wheel` mapped to cell coordinates by dividing by the measured cell box), paste, and focus events are encoded to the contract's JSON and passed to `pushEncodedInput`. `resize(cols, rows)` is called when the container's cell capacity changes. The host exposes `window.__ftuiShowcase = { runner, frames: () => runner.frameIdx(), text: () => gridText, stats: () => runner.patchStats(), logs: () => runner.takeLogs() }` for tests. An optional `frames` argument stops the loop after N frames (deterministic tests use `setTime`).
- `frankentui_showcase_demo.html`: keep the FrankenTerm path; wrap the `import(termJsUrl)` in a probe (`fetch(termJsUrl, {method: 'HEAD'})` or `try/catch` on the dynamic import); on failure, `import('./sdk/showcase-host.js')` and call `mountShowcase({ container: document.getElementById('terminal') ... })`, showing a one-line banner "Rendering with the in-tree text host (FrankenTerm bundle not found)". No second HTML file.
- `build-wasm.sh`: per `g23-decision` question 3, either keep the sed/restore or add `[profile.wasm-release]` to the root `Cargo.toml` and pass `--profile wasm-release`; in both cases the script must succeed without `FRANKENTERM_WEB_CRATE_DIR` and print the serve instructions it already prints.
- CI `wasm` job: after `g04-13-impl`'s build step, add `cargo install wasm-pack --locked` (or `jetli/wasm-pack-action@v0.4.0`), `wasm-pack build crates/ftui-showcase-wasm --target web --out-dir ../../pkg --release`, upload `pkg/` as artifact `showcase-wasm-pkg`, then run the Playwright step defined in `g23-e2e` (`npx playwright test tests/e2e/web/showcase_host.spec.mjs`).

## Implementation plan

1. Write `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/showcase-host.js` as specified; keep it framework-free; document the contract sections it implements at the top of the file.
2. Add `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/showcase-host.css` (grid font, `white-space: pre`, class names for the 8 style bits) and reference it from the HTML fallback branch. (Two new files; both are genuinely new functionality with no existing home.)
3. Edit `frankentui_showcase_demo.html:327-345` to add the fallback branch; keep `ASSET_VERSION` cache-busting; keep progress messages.
4. `build-wasm.sh`: per decision; ensure `set -euo pipefail` still holds and the script exits 0 without the external crate.
5. `ci.yml` `wasm` job: install wasm-pack, build, upload artifact, run Playwright (`g23-e2e` supplies the spec and the `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` step).
6. `docs/getting-started.md:62-74`: replace "Optional: build the in-tree showcase WASM package with the repo helper" with the exact three commands (`rustup target add`, `./build-wasm.sh`, `python3 -m http.server 8080` then open `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/frankentui_showcase_demo.html`).
7. Run `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` (Rust untouched, but the CI edits and any `Cargo.toml` profile change must not break them); `ubs` on changed files.

What NOT to do: no bundler, no npm dependencies for the host, no copying of FrankenTerm code, no new HTML variants, no `pkg/` committed to git (add `pkg/` to `.gitignore` if it is not already).

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/showcase-host.js`: new host.
- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/showcase-host.css`: new styles.
- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/frankentui_showcase_demo.html`: fallback branch at :327-345.
- `build-wasm.sh`: profile handling per decision; works without the external crate.
- `Cargo.toml` (root): `[profile.wasm-release]` if chosen.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `wasm` job steps (wasm-pack build, artifact, Playwright).
- `docs/getting-started.md`: :62-74 commands.
- `.gitignore`: `pkg/` if missing.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `./build-wasm.sh` on a clean checkout without `FRANKENTERM_WEB_CRATE_DIR` exits 0 and produces `pkg/ftui_showcase_wasm.js` and `pkg/ftui_showcase_wasm_bg.wasm`.
- [ ] Opening the demo HTML via `python3 -m http.server` renders the Dashboard in the `<pre>` grid; `q`/Tab/number keys switch screens.
- [ ] CI `wasm` job: `wasm-pack build` step green, `showcase-wasm-pkg` artifact uploaded, Playwright step green (`g23-e2e`).
- [ ] `g23-tests` node tests for the patch decoder pass.

## Tests and logging

- Unit (node, `g23-tests`): `sdk/showcase-host.test.mjs` decodes a synthetic `{cells, spans}` batch and asserts grid text and colors; input encoder produces contract-conformant JSON.
- E2E (`g23-e2e`): Playwright spec; JSONL log per run with `run_id`, `frames`, `dirty_cells`, `patch_count`, `bytes_uploaded` (from `patchStats()`), `title_found`, `duration_ms`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-13-impl` (wasm32 build step; `wasm-pack` needs the target installed), `g23-decision`. Unblocks: `g23-impl-dpr`, `g23-e2e`, `g23-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- `takeFlatPatches` returns typed arrays copied from wasm memory; the zero-copy `prepareFlatPatches`/`flatCellsPtr` path exists (`wasm.rs:1051-1090`) but is unnecessary at 80x24..200x60 for a text host. Use the simple path.
- Grapheme clusters: the flat format carries one codepoint per cell with `0x25A1` fallback; the host renders exactly what the contract provides (no shaping). Document this limitation in `g23-docs`.
- Risk: `wasm-pack` version drift; pin (`cargo install wasm-pack --version 0.13.1 --locked` or the action's pinned version) and record it in the job.
- Alternative rejected: a `<canvas>` 2D host. More code for the same proof; can follow later.

## Definition of done

Host and fallback merged; `wasm-pack` build and headless step green in CI (run id in close reason); getting-started commands verified on a clean clone; `ubs` clean; main green.
notes: Refinement 2: proceed with the reversible in-tree host demonstration scoped explicitly as a text/patch host. Preserve the first-party WebGPU roadmap and out-of-tree ownership; no xterm.js dependency and no claim that a text host fulfills full renderer/IME/grapheme/GPU requirements. Real browser render/input/resize tests are mandatory for this host. Resolve non-mutating Cargo build/profile mechanics against actual tooling before implementation; do not rewrite tracked Cargo.toml from scripts.

title: task(G23): DPR/zoom handling in the in-tree host or retract the README claim
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:690-696 lists `ftui-web` as "Web adapter with pointer/touch parity, DPR/zoom handling". Pointer/touch parity is real (`crates/ftui-web/src/pane_pointer_capture.rs`, 1,684 lines; `pane_web_e2e.rs`, `pane_cross_host_parity.rs`). DPR/zoom handling does not exist: the only reference is a comment at `crates/ftui-web/src/step_program.rs:352-353` ("Host-side fit/DPR/zoom transitions can require a repaint boundary even when cols/rows remain numerically unchanged"). A browser at 200% zoom or on a HiDPI display changes the CSS pixel size of a monospace cell; a host that does not re-measure will either overflow its container or leave the grid too small. This bead either implements the handling in the in-tree host created by `g23-impl` or retracts the README phrase, per `g23-decision` question 2. Serves V8 and the Section 5.2 row "DPR/zoom handling: NOT_STARTED".

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-web/src/step_program.rs:348-356`: on a resize signal the program stores `prev_width/prev_height`, sets `self.dbl_buf = None` and `pending_geometry_transition = Some(GeometryTransition { from_cols, ... })`, i.e. the Rust side already treats any `resize(cols, rows)` call as a full-repaint boundary even when cols/rows are numerically unchanged. That is the hook a DPR-aware host needs; nothing on the JS side calls it for metric changes because no JS host exists in-tree.
- `ShowcaseRunner::resize(cols, rows)` (`wasm.rs`, contract `:299`) pushes a Resize event processed on the next `step()`; contract section 2 (`:112-132`) says the first frame after resize is a single full span.
- No `devicePixelRatio`, `visualViewport`, `ResizeObserver`, or `getBoundingClientRect` string exists anywhere under `crates/` (verified by the audit's grep: zero `web_sys`/canvas references).

## Target state

Implement route (decision 2(a)):
- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/showcase-host.js` gains a `CellMetrics` helper: measures one probe `<span>` containing `M` via `getBoundingClientRect()` to get `cellWidthCss`/`cellHeightCss`; reads `window.devicePixelRatio` and `window.visualViewport?.scale ?? 1`; computes `cols = floor(container.clientWidth / cellWidthCss)`, `rows = floor(container.clientHeight / cellHeightCss)`.
- A `ResizeObserver` on the container plus listeners on `window` `resize` and `visualViewport` `resize`/`scroll` call `recomputeMetrics()`; when any of `{cellWidthCss, cellHeightCss, dpr, scale, cols, rows}` changes, the host rebuilds the `<pre>` grid if cols/rows changed and always calls `runner.resize(cols, rows)` (forcing the repaint boundary), then logs `{event: "dpr_zoom", dpr, scale, cols, rows, cell_w, cell_h}` to `console.debug` under the `ftui.web.host` prefix and to the host's in-page JSONL buffer (`window.__ftuiShowcase.events`).
- Mouse coordinates use the measured `cellWidthCss`/`cellHeightCss`, so clicks land on the right cell at any zoom.
- README.md:696 keeps "DPR/zoom handling" with the qualifier "(in the in-tree text host)".

Retract route (decision 2(b)):
- README.md:696 row becomes "Web adapter with pointer/touch parity"; `docs/claims-ledger.md` records the retraction with the reason; no code change.

## Implementation plan (implement route)

1. In `showcase-host.js`, add `measureCell(container)` (probe span, `getBoundingClientRect`, remove probe), `computeGeometry()`, `installObservers()`; wire `mountShowcase` to call `computeGeometry()` before constructing the runner so the initial `cols/rows` match the container instead of fixed 80x24 (keep explicit `cols/rows` options as an override for tests).
2. Emit the `dpr_zoom` event into `window.__ftuiShowcase.events` (array of plain objects) and `console.debug`.
3. `g23-e2e` spec gains two Playwright contexts: `deviceScaleFactor: 1` and `2`, same viewport; assert both render the Dashboard title, `cols/rows` are equal across DPR at equal CSS viewport, and a `page.evaluate(() => window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize')))` after `page.setViewportSize` changes `cols` and produces a full-span patch (`patchStats().dirty_cells === cols*rows`).
4. Zoom emulation: Playwright cannot change browser zoom directly; emulate via `visualViewport` is read-only, so test zoom by CSS `document.body.style.zoom = '1.5'` (Chromium supports it) plus a `resize` dispatch, and assert `cellWidthCss` changed and `runner.resize` was called (spy via `window.__ftuiShowcase.events`).
5. Run `ubs` on changed files.

What NOT to do: no canvas rewrite; no changes to `ftui-web` Rust code (the repaint boundary already exists); no new HTML.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/showcase-host.js`: metrics, observers, events.
- `tests/e2e/web/showcase_host.spec.mjs`: DPR/zoom cases (owned by `g23-e2e`; this bead adds the cases).
- `README.md:696`: qualifier or retraction.
- `docs/claims-ledger.md`: row "DPR/zoom handling" with proof (test name) or retraction.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Implement route: Playwright cases `dpr_1_and_2_render_identical_grid_text`, `viewport_resize_changes_cols_and_full_repaints`, `css_zoom_triggers_runner_resize` pass in CI.
- [ ] Retract route: README row updated; ledger row says "retracted 2026-09; reason: no DOM host implements it".
- [ ] Either way: `rg -n "DPR/zoom" README.md` returns only truthful text.

## Tests and logging

- Unit (node): `computeGeometry()` pure function tested with synthetic metrics (`{clientWidth: 800, clientHeight: 480, cellW: 10, cellH: 20} -> {cols: 80, rows: 24}`; DPR does not change cols/rows for the same CSS size; zero-size container yields `cols: 1, rows: 1` minimum).
- E2E: cases above; JSONL per case with `run_id`, `case`, `dpr`, `zoom`, `cols`, `rows`, `cell_w`, `cell_h`, `dirty_cells`, `status`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g23-decision`, `g23-impl` (host must exist). Unblocks: `g23-docs` (final README wording), `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- `visualViewport.scale` reflects pinch-zoom on mobile; browser zoom (Ctrl+/-) changes `devicePixelRatio` and CSS pixel metrics instead. Measuring the probe span covers both.
- Risk: layout thrash if `recomputeMetrics()` runs every frame; run it only from observers/events and debounce to one call per animation frame.

## Definition of done

Implement: tests green in CI (run id in close reason) and README qualifier in place. Retract: README and ledger updated with the decision reference. Main green.

title: task(G23): wasm-bindgen-test smoke, export-contract test and host decoder node tests
description:
## Context

Companion test bead for `g23-impl` (in-tree `<pre>` host, wasm-pack build, headless CI step) and `g23-impl-dpr`. The promise is README.md:1245-1247 ("Can it run in a browser? Yes.") and the export contract in `docs/spec/wasm-showcase-runner-contract.md:275-343`. Today `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm`'s 48 `#[wasm_bindgen]` items are compiled only under `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")` (`lib.rs:11-15`) and no CI job builds that target, so the exports could silently drift from the contract or fail to compile without anyone noticing. Serves V8, Section 5.2.

## What to test

1. The wasm32 build of `ftui-showcase-wasm` compiles and the runner works in a JS engine (node via `wasm-bindgen-test`): construct, init, step, patch shape.
2. The exported API matches the contract document (names and `js_name`s), so the doc stays true.
3. The JS host's pure functions (patch decoding, input encoding, geometry) are correct without a browser.
4. Determinism: with `setTime`, two runs of N frames produce equal `patchHash()` sequences (the contract's determinism section, `:173-247`).

## Test types

wasm-bindgen-test (`crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/tests/wasm_runner_smoke.rs`, `#![cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]`, `wasm_bindgen_test_configure!(run_in_node)` or browser via `wasm-pack test --headless --chrome`):
- `runner_init_emits_full_span_first_frame`: `ShowcaseRunner::new(80, 24)`, `init()`, `step()` returns `rendered: true`; `take_flat_patches()` spans equal `[0, 1920]`; cells length equals `1920 * 4`.
- `resize_emits_full_span`: `resize(100, 30)`, `step()`, spans `[0, 3000]`.
- `push_encoded_input_accepts_contract_json`: `push_encoded_input(r#"{"kind":"key","phase":"down","code":"Tab","mods":0,"repeat":false}"#)` returns true; malformed JSON returns false; after `step()` the frame index advanced and the patch is non-empty (screen switch).
- `deterministic_patch_hash_under_set_time`: two runners, `set_time(0)`, 30 iterations of `set_time(i*16_000_000)` + `step()`, compare `patch_hash()` per frame; all equal.
- `pane_pointer_roundtrip_smoke`: `panePointerDownAt`/`panePointerMoveAt`/`panePointerUpAt` on the Layout Lab screen do not panic and `paneLayoutState()` returns JSON.

Contract-conformance unit test (`crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/src/wasm.rs` `#[cfg(test)]`, runs on the host target):
- `exports_match_contract_doc`: parse `include_str!("../../../docs/spec/wasm-showcase-runner-contract.md")` section 6 for `js_name = X` and `pub fn x(` names; compare with a hard-coded list of the exports in `wasm.rs` (kept next to the impl); assert set equality for the section-6 subset (`new, init, advanceTime, setTime, pushEncodedInput, resize, step, takeFlatPatches, takeLogs, patchHash, patchStats, frameIdx, isRunning, destroy`). This test compiles on the host because it only reads text.

Node unit tests for the host (`crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/showcase-host.test.mjs`, run with `node --test`):
- `decodes_cells_and_spans`: synthetic `spans = [0, 3]`, `cells = [0x000000FF, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x48, 0, ...]` renders "H.." with white-on-black styles.
- `encodes_key_event_per_contract`: `KeyboardEvent`-like object `{key: 'a', ctrlKey: false}` encodes to `{"kind":"key","phase":"down","code":"a","mods":0,"repeat":false}`; modifiers bitmask matches the contract's `mods` semantics (document the bit assignment in the host and in the test).
- `computeGeometry_is_dpr_invariant` (from `g23-impl-dpr`).
- `empty_batch_is_noop`: `spans = []` paints nothing and does not throw.

Bench: none (no speed claim in this block; `patchStats()` numbers are logged, not gated).

## Logging

- wasm tests print `PATCH_STATS {dirty_cells, patch_count, bytes_uploaded}` per frame via `console_log!` so a failing determinism test shows the diverging frame index.
- Node tests print one JSONL line per case `{"suite":"showcase-host","case":"...","status":"pass|fail","detail":...}`.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/tests/wasm_runner_smoke.rs`: new (wasm32-only).
- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/Cargo.toml`: `[target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dev-dependencies] wasm-bindgen-test = "0.3"` (pin the exact current version).
- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/src/wasm.rs`: `exports_match_contract_doc` test.
- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/showcase-host.test.mjs`: new.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `wasm` job: `wasm-pack test --node crates/ftui-showcase-wasm` and `node --test crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `wasm-pack test --node crates/ftui-showcase-wasm` green in the `wasm` job.
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-showcase-wasm exports_match_contract_doc` green on the host target.
- [ ] `node --test crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/` green.
- [ ] Removing `takeFlatPatches` from the contract doc makes `exports_match_contract_doc` fail (verified once, not committed).

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `g23-impl` (host exists), `g04-13-impl` (wasm32 target in CI). Unblocks: `g23-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Definition of done

All tests named above exist and run in CI; close reason cites the `wasm` job run id and test names.

title: task(G23): Playwright scenario loads the showcase page, advances 60 frames, asserts Dashboard
description:
## Context and why this matters

The G23 success criterion from the audit is a headless-browser CI step that "loads the page, advances 60 frames, and asserts the Dashboard title text is present in the grid". This is the only proof that README.md:1245-1247 ("Can it run in a browser? Yes.") holds from this repository alone. Unit tests in node prove the runner works in a JS engine; only a real browser proves the page, the module loading, the DOM host and input wiring work together. Serves V8; it is the Section 7.6 verification row "V8 web: headless-browser CI step (G23)".

## Current state (evidence)

- No browser test exists. `tests/e2e/lib/` has `frankenterm_event_ordering_check.mjs` and `frankenterm_markers_decorations_check.mjs` (node scripts for FrankenTerm parity), `ws_client.py` (websocket client whose `websockets` dependency is never installed in CI, G04.6), but no Playwright configuration.
- The demo page `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/frankentui_showcase_demo.html` needs `pkg/` (built by `g23-impl` in CI) and, after `g23-impl`, falls back to `sdk/showcase-host.js` when `pkg/FrankenTerm.js` is absent.
- `ShowcaseRunner` exposes `frameIdx()`, `patchStats()` (`{dirty_cells, patch_count, bytes_uploaded}`), `takeLogs()`, `isRunning()` (`wasm.rs:1091-1135`); the host (`g23-impl`) exposes `window.__ftuiShowcase = { runner, frames(), text(), stats(), logs(), events }`.
- Dashboard is screen 1 (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/cli.rs:26` "--screen=N Start on screen N, 1-indexed (default: 1)"); its title text is rendered by `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/dashboard.rs` (assert on the literal the screen draws; read it when writing the spec and record it in the spec's comment).

## Target state

- `tests/e2e/web/playwright.config.mjs` (chromium only, headless, `webServer` serving the repo root with `python3 -m http.server 8080`, 60 s timeout).
- `tests/e2e/web/showcase_host.spec.mjs` with cases:
  1. `page_loads_and_renders_dashboard`: open `http://localhost:8080/crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/frankentui_showcase_demo.html`, wait for `window.__ftuiShowcase`, poll until `frames() >= 60` (the host advances real time; use `runner.setTime` through `page.evaluate` to make it deterministic: 60 calls of `setTime(i*16_000_000); step()`), assert `text()` contains the Dashboard title literal, assert no console errors.
  2. `keyboard_switches_screen`: dispatch `page.keyboard.press('Tab')`, step 5 frames, assert `text()` differs and contains the second screen's title.
  3. `resize_full_repaint`: `page.setViewportSize({width: 1200, height: 800})`, dispatch resize, step, assert `stats().dirty_cells == cols*rows` for that frame.
  4. `dpr_1_and_2_render_identical_grid_text`, `css_zoom_triggers_runner_resize` (from `g23-impl-dpr`, only if implement route).
  5. `wasm_size_budget_logged`: read `pkg/ftui_showcase_wasm_bg.wasm` size and log it (no gate yet; budget decided in `g25-docs` if wanted).
- `scripts/wasm_showcase_e2e.sh`: builds `pkg/` if missing (`./build-wasm.sh`), runs `npx playwright test tests/e2e/web`, converts Playwright's JSON reporter output into the repo's JSONL format under `target/e2e/web/<run_id>.jsonl` and validates it with `python3 tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py --schema tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json`.
- CI `wasm` job runs the script after the wasm-pack build (`g23-impl` step 5) with `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` cached.

## Implementation plan

1. Add `tests/e2e/web/package.json` (devDependency `@playwright/test` pinned to the current 1.x) and `playwright.config.mjs`; no other npm deps.
2. Write the spec as above; use `page.evaluate` with `window.__ftuiShowcase.runner.setTime(...)`/`step()` for determinism; capture `console` messages and fail on `error`.
3. Write `scripts/wasm_showcase_e2e.sh` (bash, `set -euo pipefail`, sources `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh` and `logging.sh` for `jsonl_init`/`jsonl_run_start`/`jsonl_assert`/`jsonl_run_end`; runs Playwright; maps each test to a `jsonl_assert` line).
4. `ci.yml` `wasm` job: `actions/setup-node@v4` (node 20), `npm ci --prefix tests/e2e/web`, `npx --prefix tests/e2e/web playwright install --with-deps chromium`, run the script, upload `target/e2e/web/` and Playwright's `test-results/` (traces on failure) as artifacts with `if: always()`.
5. Verify once that a deliberately wrong title literal fails the job; revert.

What NOT to do: no Firefox/WebKit matrix (chromium is enough for the proof); no screenshot snapshots (text assertions are stable); no committed `pkg/` or `node_modules/`.

## Files to change

- `tests/e2e/web/package.json`, `tests/e2e/web/package-lock.json`, `tests/e2e/web/playwright.config.mjs`, `tests/e2e/web/showcase_host.spec.mjs`: new.
- `scripts/wasm_showcase_e2e.sh`: new.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `wasm` job steps.
- `.gitignore`: `tests/e2e/web/node_modules/`, `tests/e2e/web/test-results/`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `scripts/wasm_showcase_e2e.sh` exits 0 locally after `./build-wasm.sh`; JSONL validates against `e2e_jsonl_schema.json`.
- [ ] CI `wasm` job green with the Playwright step; artifacts uploaded (run id in close reason).
- [ ] `page_loads_and_renders_dashboard` asserts the exact title literal and `frames() >= 60`.

## Tests and logging

JSONL fields per case: `run_id`, `ts`, `scenario` (`wasm_showcase_host`), `case`, `browser` (`chromium <version>`), `dpr`, `cols`, `rows`, `frames`, `dirty_cells`, `patch_count`, `bytes_uploaded`, `wasm_bytes`, `console_errors` (count), `duration_ms`, `status`, `detail`. Playwright traces retained on failure. Driver: Playwright (browser); the PTY drivers do not apply here.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g23-impl` (host + pkg build in CI). Unblocks: `g42-impl` (Section 7.6 V8 row).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- `wasm-bindgen-test` in node cannot assert DOM text; that is why a browser is required for this bead while `g23-tests` covers the engine-level smoke.
- Risk: runner time (Playwright install ~1 min with cache). Acceptable inside the `wasm` job.
- Risk: flaky real-time frame counting; avoided by driving `setTime` explicitly.

## Definition of done

Spec and script merged; CI step green; JSONL artifact produced and validated; close reason cites run id and case names.

title: docs(G23): README/getting-started say host-driven patch producer plus in-tree text host
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:690-706 ("## Web/WASM Backend") says "FrankenTUI targets both native terminals and web browsers from a single Rust codebase" and describes `ftui-web` as "Web adapter with pointer/touch parity, DPR/zoom handling"; README.md:1245-1247 says "Can it run in a browser? Yes. `ftui-web` provides a WASM adapter that renders through the same Rust core." `docs/getting-started.md:51-74` tells readers to run `./build-wasm.sh`. The accurate description of `ftui-web` today is the one in its own header (`crates/ftui-web/src/lib.rs:3-12`): a host-driven, deterministic-time, no-threads backend that "intentionally does not bind to `wasm-bindgen` yet" and emits patches for a host to paint. This bead rewrites the web sections so they say exactly that plus whatever `g23-impl`/`g23-impl-dpr` delivered, and adds the claims-ledger rows that keep the text honest. Serves V8 and Section 2.2.C ("Web/WASM (G23 wording)" row of the G06 README plan).

## Current state (evidence)

- README.md:690-698 table: `ftui-web | Web adapter with pointer/touch parity, DPR/zoom handling`; `ftui-showcase-wasm | WASM build target for the demo showcase`.
- README.md:699-706: paragraph already admits "This checkout does not currently vendor local `crates/frankenterm-core` or `crates/frankenterm-web`"; "the in-tree browser surface today is `ftui-web` plus the `ftui-showcase-wasm` target".
- README.md:1245-1247 FAQ answer "Yes." without the precondition (an out-of-tree bundle or the in-tree host).
- README.md:220-228 "Backend & Platform" crate table rows for `ftui-web`/`ftui-showcase-wasm` (verify wording when editing).
- `docs/getting-started.md:51-74`: web section with `cargo check` commands and `./build-wasm.sh`; no mention that the page needs `pkg/` served over HTTP or of the in-tree host.
- `docs/spec/wasm-showcase-runner-contract.md` matches the exports (verified by `g23-tests` `exports_match_contract_doc`).
- `docs/adr/ADR-008-terminal-backend-strategy.md` (Status PROPOSED, 2026-02-08) frames the backend strategy "Replace Crossterm, Enable WASM, Unify Interfaces"; `docs/adr/ADR-009-webgpu-renderer-architecture.md` describes the FrankenTerm WebGPU renderer that lives out of tree. ADR status handling is `g34-impl`'s job; this bead supplies the web facts.

## Target state

- README "Web/WASM Backend": states the architecture in two sentences: `ftui-web` is a host-driven patch producer implementing the `ftui-backend` traits (`WebBackend`, `WebPresenter`, `WebEventSource`, `DeterministicClock`); `ftui-showcase-wasm` exports `ShowcaseRunner` via wasm-bindgen; rendering is done by a host: the in-tree text host `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/sdk/showcase-host.js` (always available) or the adjacent FrankenTerm WebGPU host (when `FRANKENTERM_WEB_CRATE_DIR` is provided to `./build-wasm.sh`). The table row for `ftui-web` reads "Host-driven web backend: pointer/touch parity" plus "DPR/zoom handling (in-tree text host)" only if `g23-impl-dpr` implemented it.
- README FAQ "Can it run in a browser?": "Yes, from this repository: `./build-wasm.sh && python3 -m http.server 8080`, then open `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/frankentui_showcase_demo.html`. CI runs a headless Chromium check of that page on every push (`wasm` job)."
- `docs/getting-started.md` web section: the three commands, the fallback-host note, the limitation that the text host renders one codepoint per cell (`0x25A1` fallback for multi-codepoint graphemes, per the contract `:151`).

title: epic(G03): Per-Program termination-signal state and nextest timeouts so the runtime test binary cannot hang
description:
## Context and why this matters

AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks (CRITICAL)" and "Testing" make `cargo test --workspace` a mandatory gate, and README.md:405-410 lists `cargo test --workspace` as the way to run tests. The 2026-09-01 reality check (commit `ab07291f`) ran `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 16,727 tests passed across 206 binaries, then the `ftui-runtime` lib test binary hung for more than ten minutes in `program::tests::run_pending_signal_skips_initial_render_and_subscription_start` (Section 1 evidence table). The same two tests hang in CI: the `Check (macos-latest, nightly)` job of run 33152820289 was killed at the 6-hour limit in `run_invokes_on_shutdown_before_returning_signal_error` and `run_pending_signal_skips_initial_render_and_subscription_start` (Section 5.1), and one `Check (ubuntu-latest, nightly)` job ran 8h35m before failing. Because there is no per-test timeout, one hang turns a CI job into a multi-hour failure that looks like runner starvation, which is why the hang has survived since March. This is root cause 3 of the reality check ("red CI normalized") and a design gap ("process-global signal state (test race)"). Vision row V70 ("Mandatory gates green": PARTIAL locally, RED in CI) and gap letter E depend on it. The plan document's Gate 4 ("cleanup") credibility rests on the runtime's signal handling being testable in parallel.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs:79-140` `pub mod shutdown_signal`: one `static PENDING_TERMINATION_SIGNAL: AtomicI32`; `record_pending_termination_signal(signal)` is a `compare_exchange(0, signal)` (first signal wins); `pending_termination_signal() -> Option<i32>`; `clear_pending_termination_signal()` is an unconditional `store(0)`; `with_test_signal_serialization(f)` takes a `OnceLock<Mutex<()>>` lock and clears before and after `f`. The module doc says the runtime "clears it to acknowledge completion back to the signal thread".
- Writers of the global: `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs:1312` (crossterm session signal thread) and `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs:335` (native backend signal thread).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `fn check_termination_signal() -> Option<i32>` (:110) and `fn clear_termination_signal()` (:116) wrap the globals; `Program::observed_termination_signal(&self)` (:5220) returns `check_termination_signal()` only when `self.intercept_signals`; the run loop polls it at :5254, :5269, :5286, :5297, :5321, :5441, :5467; `complete_lifecycle` clears the global unconditionally at :5490 before returning `SignalTerminationError { signal }`.
- Test helper `headless_program_with_resolved_config` (:11276) calls `clear_termination_signal()` at :11283 on every construction; `headless_program_with_config` (:11395) builds on it. Every headless test therefore clears the global.
- Only two runtime tests take the serialization lock: `run_invokes_on_shutdown_before_returning_signal_error` (:11933; lock at :11976; records signal 2 at :11984; asserts one `on_shutdown`, `signal_termination_from_error(&err) == Some(2)`, and the global is `None` afterwards) and `run_pending_signal_skips_initial_render_and_subscription_start` (:11994; lock at :12048; records 15 at :12057; asserts zero renders and zero subscription starts). Two ftui-core tests also take it: `terminal_session.rs:1504` `wait_for_shutdown_ack_immediate_after_explicit_teardown` and `:2609` `pending_termination_signal_round_trip`. No other crate uses `with_test_signal_serialization` (verified with `rg` across `crates/`).
- Race: test A records a signal and calls `run()`; test B (parallel, any headless test) constructs a program and clears the global; A's first `observed_termination_signal()` sees `None`, enters the headless event loop, and nothing ever wakes it. The lock only protects A from other lock-takers, not from the hundreds of headless tests that do not take it.
- No `.config/nextest.toml`, no nextest anywhere in the repo, no `timeout-minutes` on the `check` job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:23-85`; only `golden-trace-gates` :702 and `doctor-frankentui-verification` :1100 have 45-minute limits). The local isolated re-run attempt during the audit timed out waiting for the rch build queue (`hang_repro.log`, EXIT=124), so the static root cause plus the macOS CI log are the evidence.

## Target state

Signal state is owned per `Program` for headless/simulator constructors and shared with the process-global slot only for interactive constructors whose backend installs a signal thread. No test can clear another test's signal. `with_test_signal_serialization` is removed (not deprecated: AGENTS.md forbids wrapper functions for deprecated APIs). `Program::inject_termination_signal(signal)` is the documented test/harness way to simulate a signal. `.config/nextest.toml` sets `slow-timeout = { period = "60s", terminate-after = 2 }`; CI runs `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast`; a hanging test fails the job within 3 minutes with its name in the log. Twenty consecutive `cargo nextest run -p ftui-runtime --test-threads 16` runs pass.

## Implementation plan (block level)

1. `g03-impl`: `TerminationSignalSlot` in `ftui-core::shutdown_signal` (process-backed or owned), `Program.signal_slot`, `inject_termination_signal`, acknowledge-by-CAS in `complete_lifecycle`, headless constructors stop clearing the global, tests migrated, `with_test_signal_serialization` removed and its four call sites rewritten.
2. `g03-impl-nextest`: `.config/nextest.toml`, `check` job test step switched to nextest, AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks" gains the nextest command, local install note (rch workers need `cargo-nextest`).
3. `g03-tests`: concurrency test, acknowledge tests, 20-run soak with JSONL log, one-time hang-timeout verification.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs` (`shutdown_signal`), `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs` (two tests), `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` (slot, constructors, lifecycle, tests), `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs` (no change expected; the signal thread keeps writing to the process slot).
- `.config/nextest.toml` (new), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `check` job, `AGENTS.md`, `scripts/soak_runtime_tests.sh` (new, from `g03-tests`).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `two_concurrent_headless_programs_with_independent_pending_signals_both_terminate` green.
- [ ] `scripts/soak_runtime_tests.sh 20` (20 x `cargo nextest run -p ftui-runtime --test-threads 16`) all pass; JSONL log attached to `g03-tests` close reason.
- [ ] `.config/nextest.toml` present; `check` job uses `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast`; a scratch `loop {}` test fails CI in under 3 minutes (verified once, run id recorded).
- [ ] `rg -n with_test_signal_serialization crates` returns nothing.

## Tests and logging

See `g03-tests`. Tracing target `ftui.runtime.signal` events: `signal_observed { signal, source: "process" | "owned" }` and `signal_acknowledged { signal }` so PTY tests can see the path taken.

## Dependencies and ordering

No blockers. Unblocks `g04-12-impl` (job topology switches to nextest), the whole G04 cluster's credibility, `g13-impl` (lifecycle tests), `g32-impl` (SIGTSTP/SIGCONT work builds on the slot).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative: keep the global and make every headless test take the lock. Rejected: hundreds of tests, permanent serialization, and the next new test forgets the lock.
- Alternative: only add the nextest timeout. Rejected: it converts a hang into a flake; the race remains and the two tests would fail randomly.
- Risk: interactive constructors must keep sharing the process slot because the backend signal threads (`terminal_session.rs:1312`, `ftui-tty:335`) write there and `terminal_session.rs` waits for the clear as an acknowledgement; the design keeps that path byte-for-byte.
- Risk: nextest does not run doctests; the `docs` job already runs `cargo test --doc --workspace` (ci.yml:111).

## Definition of done

All three child beads closed with evidence; a green `check` job on main that used nextest (run id); soak log archived; AGENTS.md updated.

title: bug(G03): Per-Program termination-signal slot, inject_termination_signal, no global clears in headless tests
description:
## Context and why this matters

The `ftui-runtime` unit test binary can block forever: `cargo test --workspace` hung locally in `run_pending_signal_skips_initial_render_and_subscription_start` on 2026-09-01 and the macOS nightly CI job of run 33152820289 was killed at 6 hours in the same pair of tests. AGENTS.md makes `cargo test --workspace` a mandatory gate, so a gate that cannot finish means nothing else can be trusted (reality-check root cause 3, vision row V70, gap letter E). The bug is a design flaw, not a flaky test: termination-signal state is a single process-global `AtomicI32` that every headless test clears on construction, so any parallel test can erase another test's pending signal between `record` and the first poll. This bead moves ownership of the pending signal into `Program` for headless and simulator programs, keeps the process slot only where a real signal thread writes it, and gives tests an explicit `inject_termination_signal` API. It is the fix that makes `g03-impl-nextest`'s timeout a safety net rather than a flake generator.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs:79-140`:
  ```rust
  static PENDING_TERMINATION_SIGNAL: AtomicI32 = AtomicI32::new(0);
  pub fn record_pending_termination_signal(signal: i32) { let _ = PENDING_TERMINATION_SIGNAL.compare_exchange(0, signal, SeqCst, SeqCst); }
  pub fn pending_termination_signal() -> Option<i32> { match load { 0 => None, s => Some(s) } }
  pub fn clear_pending_termination_signal() { PENDING_TERMINATION_SIGNAL.store(0, SeqCst); }
  #[doc(hidden)] pub fn with_test_signal_serialization<R>(f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R { /* OnceLock<Mutex<()>>; clear; f(); clear */ }
  ```
  Module doc: "Signal handlers record the first pending termination signal here. The runtime polls it, performs graceful teardown, then clears it to acknowledge completion back to the signal thread."
- Writers: `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs:1312` (`crate::shutdown_signal::record_pending_termination_signal(signal)` in the crossterm session's signal thread) and `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs:335` (native backend signal thread). `terminal_session.rs` has a `wait_for_shutdown_ack` path (test at :1504 `wait_for_shutdown_ack_immediate_after_explicit_teardown`) that waits for the slot to be cleared.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `:110 fn check_termination_signal() -> Option<i32>`; `:116 fn clear_termination_signal()`; `:5220 fn observed_termination_signal(&self) -> Option<i32> { if self.intercept_signals { check_termination_signal() } else { None } }`; polls at :5254, :5269, :5286, :5297, :5321, :5441, :5467; `:5486-5495` in `complete_lifecycle`: `if let Some(signal) = termination_signal { clear_termination_signal(); let error = io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Interrupted, SignalTerminationError { signal }); debug_assert_eq!(signal_termination_from_error(&error), Some(signal)); ... }`.
- Tests: `:11276 fn headless_program_with_resolved_config` clears at `:11283`; `:11395 fn headless_program_with_config`; `:11933 run_invokes_on_shutdown_before_returning_signal_error` (lock :11976, uses `headless_signal_program_with_config(model, ProgramConfig::default().with_signal_interception(true))`, `record_pending_termination_signal(2)` :11984, asserts `shutdowns == 1`, `signal_termination_from_error(&err) == Some(2)`, `check_termination_signal() == None`); `:11994 run_pending_signal_skips_initial_render_and_subscription_start` (lock :12048, records 15 :12057, asserts zero render calls and zero subscription starts).
- ftui-core tests using the lock: `terminal_session.rs:1504` and `:2609` (`pending_termination_signal_round_trip`: clears, asserts `None`, records 2, records 15 (ignored because first wins), asserts `Some(2)`).
- No other crate references `with_test_signal_serialization` (`rg` over `crates/` on 2026-09-01: only the four sites above).

## Target state

- `ftui_core::shutdown_signal::TerminationSignalSlot`: `pub struct TerminationSignalSlot(Inner)` with `enum Inner { Process, Owned(Arc<AtomicI32>) }`; constructors `TerminationSignalSlot::process()` and `TerminationSignalSlot::owned()`; methods `record(&self, signal: i32)` (CAS 0 -> signal), `pending(&self) -> Option<i32>`, `acknowledge(&self, signal: i32) -> bool` (CAS signal -> 0; returns whether it was still pending), `is_process(&self) -> bool`. The three existing free functions stay as the process-slot API used by the signal threads (`record_pending_termination_signal`, `pending_termination_signal`, `clear_pending_termination_signal`), implemented over the same static. `with_test_signal_serialization` is deleted.
- `Program` gains `signal_slot: TerminationSignalSlot`. `Program::with_config` and `Program::with_native_backend` (interactive; their backends install signal threads that write the process slot) use `process()`. `headless_program_with_resolved_config`, `ProgramSimulator`, and every other non-interactive constructor use `owned()`. `observed_termination_signal` reads `self.signal_slot.pending()` when `self.intercept_signals`. `complete_lifecycle` calls `self.signal_slot.acknowledge(signal)` instead of an unconditional clear (so a signal recorded after the observed one is not erased; log a `tracing::warn!` if acknowledge returns false).
- `pub fn inject_termination_signal(&self, signal: i32)` on `Program` (documented "Test and harness API: records `signal` into this program's slot exactly as the OS signal thread would; for interactive programs this is the process slot") delegates to `self.signal_slot.record(signal)`.
- The two runtime tests use `program.inject_termination_signal(2)` / `(15)` with no lock. `headless_program_with_resolved_config` no longer touches the global.
- ftui-core tests: `pending_termination_signal_round_trip` is rewritten over `TerminationSignalSlot::owned()` (same assertions); `wait_for_shutdown_ack_immediate_after_explicit_teardown` tests the process path and keeps a test-module-local `static ACK_TEST_LOCK: Mutex<()>` shared only with any other ftui-core test that must touch the process slot (there is exactly one other today: none after the rewrite; if a second appears, both take the local lock). No exported lock.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs` `shutdown_signal`: add `TerminationSignalSlot` and `Inner` (above); implement `Process` variants over the static; implement `Owned` over `Arc<AtomicI32>`; `#[derive(Clone, Debug)]`; unit tests `owned_slots_are_independent`, `process_slot_reflects_free_functions`, `acknowledge_only_clears_matching_signal`. Remove `with_test_signal_serialization` and the `Mutex`/`OnceLock` imports it needed. Update the module doc to describe both paths.
2. `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs`: rewrite the two tests (:1504, :2609) as described; keep `record_pending_termination_signal` at :1312 unchanged.
3. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: add the field to `Program` (:4695 struct); set it in every constructor (search `Program {` literal constructions: `with_config` :4814 area, `with_native_backend` :5140 area, headless constructors in tests :11276 and :11395, `ProgramSimulator` construction, any `with_backend`/`with_event_source` constructors; `rg -n 'intercept_signals:' crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` finds every struct literal). Replace `check_termination_signal()` in `observed_termination_signal` (:5220) with `self.signal_slot.pending()`; replace `clear_termination_signal()` at :5490 with `acknowledge`; delete `clear_termination_signal` (:116) and `check_termination_signal` (:110) if no other caller remains (the test at :11989 asserts `check_termination_signal() == None`; rewrite it as `program.signal_slot_pending() == None` via a `pub fn pending_termination_signal(&self) -> Option<i32>` accessor on `Program`).
4. Add `inject_termination_signal` and `pending_termination_signal` accessors on `Program` (public, documented, `#[doc(alias = "record_pending_termination_signal")]`).
5. Rewrite the two hanging tests: drop the lock closure; construct with `with_signal_interception(true)`; call `program.inject_termination_signal(2)` / `(15)` before `run()`; keep every assertion; add `assert_eq!(program.pending_termination_signal(), None)` after run.
6. `headless_program_with_resolved_config` (:11283): delete the `clear_termination_signal();` line.
7. Emit tracing: `tracing::debug!(target: "ftui.runtime.signal", signal, source = if self.signal_slot.is_process() { "process" } else { "owned" }, "signal_observed")` where the loop first sees a signal, and `"signal_acknowledged"` in `complete_lifecycle`.
8. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`; then `cargo test -p ftui-core` and `cargo test -p ftui-runtime --lib` via rch (the runtime binary must now finish); `ubs` on the three changed source files.

What NOT to do: no deprecated wrapper for `with_test_signal_serialization` (AGENTS.md: "Never create wrapper functions for deprecated APIs"); no `#[ignore]` on the two tests; no global test mutex exported from ftui-core; no new file `signal_slot.rs` unless `shutdown_signal` outgrows lib.rs (it is ~60 lines today; keep it inline); no deletion of test functions, only rewrites; no script-based edits across the struct-literal sites (do them by hand or with parallel subagents).

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs`: `shutdown_signal` module.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs`: two tests.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: struct field, constructors, `observed_termination_signal`, `complete_lifecycle`, accessors, tests, helper removal.
- `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs`: none (verify the signal thread still compiles against the unchanged free functions).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-runtime --lib` completes (no hang) with `--test-threads 16`, ten times in a row locally via rch (log paths in the close reason; the 20-run nextest soak is `g03-tests`).
- [ ] `run_invokes_on_shutdown_before_returning_signal_error` and `run_pending_signal_skips_initial_render_and_subscription_start` pass without any lock.
- [ ] `rg -n 'with_test_signal_serialization|clear_termination_signal\(\)' crates` returns nothing.
- [ ] ftui-core unit tests `owned_slots_are_independent`, `process_slot_reflects_free_functions`, `acknowledge_only_clears_matching_signal` pass; `pending_termination_signal_round_trip` and `wait_for_shutdown_ack_immediate_after_explicit_teardown` pass.
- [ ] PTY sanity: `scripts/consumer_smoke_e2e.sh` (G01) or the showcase under `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` with `kill -TERM` sent after 1 s exits with code 143 (128+15) and restores the terminal (existing E2E `cleanup_*` scripts under `tests/e2e/scripts/` cover this; run `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh` filtered to `cleanup` and attach the JSONL).

## Tests and logging

Unit tests above; concurrency test in `g03-tests`. Tracing target `ftui.runtime.signal` with fields `signal`, `source`. E2E: existing `cleanup_*` PTY scenarios with their JSONL (`run_id`, `scenario`, `exit_code`, teardown sequence tallies).

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: nothing. Unblocks: `g03-tests`, `g03-impl-nextest` (can proceed in parallel but the soak needs this), `g04-12-impl`, `g13-impl`, `g32-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Why CAS-acknowledge instead of clear: a second OS signal arriving during teardown must not be lost; `acknowledge(signal)` leaves a different pending value in place and logs.
- Why the process slot stays for interactive programs: `terminal_session.rs` and `ftui-tty` signal threads cannot see a `Program`; they write the static, and `terminal_session.rs` waits for the clear as an ack. Changing that channel is out of scope (it belongs with `g13-impl`'s shared teardown extraction).
- Alternative: an `mpsc` channel per program instead of an atomic. Rejected: the loop polls from several points and needs a level-triggered, idempotent read.
- Rollback: revert; the free functions are unchanged so backends are unaffected.

## Definition of done

Reachable from production (interactive programs use the process slot through the same code). Close reason names the tests, the ten local runs, and the commit. No README claim changes; AGENTS.md text is `g03-impl-nextest`/`g06-docs-agents`.

title: task(G03): Add .config/nextest.toml slow-timeout kill, switch CI unit tests to nextest, document in AGENTS.md
description:
## Context and why this matters

The reality check found that a single hanging test in the `ftui-runtime` unit binary turned CI jobs into 6-8 hour failures (run 33152820289: `Check (macos-latest, nightly)` killed at the 6 h limit; `Check (ubuntu-latest, nightly)` failed after 8h35m) and that no per-test timeout exists anywhere: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `check` job (:23-85) has no `timeout-minutes` and runs `cargo test --workspace --lib` (:82-83) and `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (:85) with libtest, which has no timeout facility. Because a hang and a slow runner look identical, the signal-state race (`g03-impl`) went undiagnosed since March 2026. AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks" and "Testing" list only `cargo test` commands. This bead installs cargo-nextest with a slow-test termination policy so that any future hang fails fast with the test's name, switches the CI unit-test step to it, and records the command in AGENTS.md. It serves vision row V70 and gap letter E, and is the G03 half that G04.12 (`g04-12-impl`, job topology) builds on.

## Current state (evidence)

- `ls -la .config` -> "No such file or directory". `rg -i nextest` over the repo matches only `docs/planning/reality-check-2026-09-01.md`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:23-85` `check` job: matrix `os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]`, `rust: [stable, nightly]`, plus `windows-latest`/stable; steps: checkout, `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` with `toolchain: ${{ matrix.rust }}` (floating; pinning is `g04-10-impl`), cache, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, no-mock grep, `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --lib`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (nightly only). No `timeout-minutes`.
- `timeout-minutes: 45` exists only on `golden-trace-gates` (:702) and `doctor-frankentui-verification` (:1100).
- The `docs` job (:86-117) runs `cargo test --doc --workspace` (:111); nextest does not run doctests, so that step must remain.
- AGENTS.md:120-135 "Compiler Checks (CRITICAL)" lists `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`. AGENTS.md:150-169 "Unit Tests" lists `cargo test --workspace` and per-crate `cargo test -p ...`.
- AGENTS.md "RCH" section: cargo commands are offloaded to remote workers by a PreToolUse hook; `cargo nextest` must be installed on those workers or `rch` must fall back; `rch` "fails open" (runs locally) when unavailable.

## Target state

- `.config/nextest.toml` exists with a `default` profile (`slow-timeout = { period = "60s", terminate-after = 2 }`, `fail-fast = false`) and a `ci` profile (same timeout plus `grace-period = "10s"`, `retries = 0`, `failure-output = "immediate-final"`, `status-level = "slow"`, `final-status-level = "flaky"`, JUnit report at `target/nextest/ci/junit.xml`).
- CI `check` job runs `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast --profile ci` for the unit/integration step and `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --profile ci` for the all-features step (nightly), each step with `timeout-minutes: 45`, after installing nextest with `taiki-e/install-action@nextest` (pinned to a tag). `cargo test --doc --workspace` stays in the `docs` job. JUnit XML uploaded as artifact `nextest-junit-<os>-<rust>` always.
- A test that loops forever is killed after 120 s (60 s slow period x terminate-after 2) plus grace, the job fails, and the log line names the test (`TIMEOUT [ 120.0s] ftui-runtime program::tests::<name>`).
- AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks" includes `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` with a one-line install note; "Unit Tests" keeps `cargo test` for doctests and adds the nextest form; the RCH section notes that workers need `cargo-nextest`.

## Implementation plan

1. Create `.config/nextest.toml`:
   ```toml
   [profile.default]
   slow-timeout = { period = "60s", terminate-after = 2 }
   fail-fast = false

   [profile.ci]
   slow-timeout = { period = "60s", terminate-after = 2, grace-period = "10s" }
   retries = 0
   failure-output = "immediate-final"
   status-level = "slow"
   final-status-level = "flaky"

   [profile.ci.junit]
   path = "junit.xml"
   ```
   Confirm the schema against the installed nextest version's docs (search online per AGENTS.md "Third-Party Library Usage" if unsure); the `[profile.ci.junit]` table name and `path` are relative to `target/nextest/ci/`.
2. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `check` job: add step `uses: taiki-e/install-action@<pinned tag>` with `tool: nextest` after the toolchain step; replace `cargo test --workspace --lib` with `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast --profile ci` (drop `--lib` only if the job's runtime stays acceptable; otherwise keep `--lib` semantics with `--lib` is not a nextest flag: use `--workspace --lib` equivalents `--bins --lib`? Verify: nextest accepts the same target selection flags as cargo test, so `--lib` is valid); replace the all-features step similarly; add `timeout-minutes: 45` on both steps; add `- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7` with `if: always()`, `name: nextest-junit-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.rust }}`, `path: target/nextest/ci/junit.xml`. Do not add `continue-on-error`.
3. Coordinate with `g04-12-impl`: that bead splits `check` into `check`/`test-unit`/`test-all-features`; if it lands first, apply the nextest switch inside `test-unit`/`test-all-features`; if this lands first, `g04-12-impl` must carry the nextest steps over unchanged (write this in both beads' close notes).
4. AGENTS.md: in "Compiler Checks (CRITICAL)" append `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast   # per-test timeout: 60s slow, killed at 120s (.config/nextest.toml)`; in "Unit Tests" add `cargo nextest run -p ftui-runtime --test-threads 16` and the sentence "doctests still need `cargo test --doc --workspace`"; in "RCH" add "remote workers must have `cargo-nextest` installed (`cargo install cargo-nextest --locked`)". (The rest of the AGENTS.md rewrite is `g06-docs-agents`; keep this diff to these three insertions.)
5. Local verification via rch: `cargo nextest run -p ftui-runtime --test-threads 16` completes; if `rch` workers lack nextest, install there or run locally and note it.
6. One-time timeout verification (do this on a scratch branch, never on main): add `#[test] fn scratch_hang_for_timeout_verification() { loop { std::hint::spin_loop() } }` to `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs` tests, push, observe the `check` job fail within 3 minutes of reaching the test step with `TIMEOUT` and the test name, record run id and log excerpt in `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md` "Hang timeout gate" section, and remove the test on the branch (the branch itself is not deleted by the agent).

What NOT to do: no `continue-on-error`; no `retries > 0` in CI (retries would hide the race this block fixes); no per-test `#[timeout]` attributes; no removal of `cargo test --doc` from the `docs` job; no deletion of the scratch branch without permission.

## Files to change

- `.config/nextest.toml`: new.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `check` job steps (:80-85) and artifact upload.
- `AGENTS.md`: three insertions (Compiler Checks, Unit Tests, RCH).
- `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md`: "Hang timeout gate" section.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `check` job green on main using nextest (run id in the close reason) with JUnit artifacts present.
- [ ] Scratch `loop {}` test fails CI in under 3 minutes with the test name in the log (run id recorded in `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md`).
- [ ] `cargo nextest run -p ftui-runtime --test-threads 16` passes locally (via rch or local fallback) after `g03-impl`.
- [ ] AGENTS.md contains the nextest command in "Compiler Checks".

## Tests and logging

CI job log + JUnit XML per matrix cell; nextest `status-level = "slow"` prints `SLOW [ 60.0s]` lines for any test over the period, which is the early-warning signal for the next race. `g03-tests` consumes the JUnit files in the soak script.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: nothing (config and CI can land before the race fix; the soak in `g03-tests` needs both). Unblocks: `g03-tests`, `g04-12-impl`, `g06-docs-agents` (which references the command).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative: `timeout-minutes` on the job only. Rejected: a job-level kill loses the test name and still costs 45 minutes; nextest names the test in 2 minutes.
- Alternative: `cargo test -- --test-threads 1`. Rejected: hides the race, multiplies runtime.
- Risk: nextest runs each test in its own process, which changes semantics for tests relying on process-global state (exactly the class of test G03 removes); any remaining ones will surface as failures and must be fixed, not retried.
- Risk: 60 s may be tight for a few heavy tests on shared runners (e.g. `perf_corpus_1000_under_budget`, `g04-02-impl`); a per-test override `[[profile.ci.overrides]] filter = 'test(...)' slow-timeout = ...` is allowed with a comment naming the bead that will remove the need.

## Definition of done

Config and CI change on main, green run id, timeout verification recorded, AGENTS.md updated, JUnit artifact visible.
