CI proof pending the next green run (tracked by G04 e2e acceptance bead).

title: task(G03): Concurrency test for independent pending signals and a 20-run nextest soak with logs
description:
## Context

`g03-impl` replaces the process-global termination-signal slot with a per-`Program` `TerminationSignalSlot` (owned for headless/simulator programs, process-backed for interactive ones) and adds `Program::inject_termination_signal`. `g03-impl-nextest` adds a 120 s per-test kill. This bead proves both: a concurrency test that would have hung before the fix, acknowledge semantics tests, a 20-run soak protocol with machine-readable logs, and the record of the one-time hang-timeout verification. The evidence it produces is what the G03 epic and `g42-impl` cite. Background: on 2026-09-01 (`ab07291f`) `program::tests::run_pending_signal_skips_initial_render_and_subscription_start` blocked for more than ten minutes locally and the macOS nightly CI job was killed at 6 h in the same tests; the cause was any parallel headless test clearing the global between `record` and the first `observed_termination_signal()` poll.

## What to test

1. Two headless programs running concurrently with different injected signals both terminate with their own signal (the original race, now impossible).
2. A signal injected after `run()` has started still stops the loop promptly.
3. `complete_lifecycle` acknowledges only the signal it observed (CAS), never a later one.
4. Headless programs never touch the process-global slot.
5. Interactive constructors use the process slot (so real OS signals keep working).
6. Repeated full-binary runs with high parallelism never hang or exceed the slow threshold.

## Test types (unit, property, bench, E2E) with names and assertions

Unit tests in `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` `mod tests`:
- `two_concurrent_headless_programs_with_independent_pending_signals_both_terminate`: spawn two `std::thread`s; each builds a headless program via `headless_signal_program_with_config(model, ProgramConfig::default().with_signal_interception(true))` with a `ShutdownModel` counting `on_shutdown`; thread A calls `program.inject_termination_signal(15)` then `run()`; thread B injects `2` then `run()`; join both with a 10 s watchdog (`recv_timeout` on a channel each thread signals when done; a timeout is a test failure, not a hang, even without nextest); assert A's error maps to `Some(15)` and B's to `Some(2)` via `signal_termination_from_error`, each `shutdowns == 1`, each `program.pending_termination_signal() == None` after run, and `ftui_core::shutdown_signal::pending_termination_signal() == None` before and after.
- `inject_after_run_started_stops_loop_within_one_second`: headless program with a subscription that ticks every 10 ms; start `run()` on a thread; sleep 50 ms; `inject_termination_signal(15)` from the test thread (slot is `Clone`/`Send`; expose `program.signal_slot_handle()` returning a clone for this purpose, or inject through an `Arc<Program>`-free handle obtained before moving the program to the thread); assert the thread finishes within 1 s and the error carries 15; assert `on_shutdown` ran once.
- `complete_lifecycle_acknowledges_only_the_observed_signal`: owned slot; `record(15)`; simulate the loop observing 15; before `complete_lifecycle`, `record(2)` is ignored by CAS semantics (first wins) so this tests the ack: after `acknowledge(15)` the slot is `None`; then `record(2)`; `acknowledge(15)` returns false and leaves `Some(2)`.
- `headless_program_never_touches_process_slot`: build ten headless programs in a loop, inject and run each; assert `ftui_core::shutdown_signal::pending_termination_signal()` is `None` throughout (this test is only meaningful because no other test in the binary writes the process slot after `g03-impl`; document that invariant in the test's doc comment).
- `interactive_constructors_use_process_slot` (`#[cfg(feature = "crossterm-compat")]` or native, gated on a PTY being available; otherwise construct the slot the same way the constructor does and assert `is_process()`): asserts the constructor wiring by checking `Program::signal_slot.is_process()` through a `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate)` accessor.

ftui-core unit tests (from `g03-impl`, verified here): `owned_slots_are_independent`, `process_slot_reflects_free_functions`, `acknowledge_only_clears_matching_signal`, `pending_termination_signal_round_trip`, `wait_for_shutdown_ack_immediate_after_explicit_teardown`.

Soak (E2E of the test binary): new `scripts/soak_runtime_tests.sh [runs=20] [threads=16] [out_dir]`: loops `cargo nextest run -p ftui-runtime --test-threads $threads --profile ci` (via rch when available), captures each run's stdout, the JUnit XML (`target/nextest/ci/junit.xml`, copied per run), wall time, pass/fail counts, and every `SLOW`/`TIMEOUT` line; writes one JSONL record per run and a final summary; exit non-zero if any run fails or any `TIMEOUT` appears, or if any test exceeds 30 s (half the slow period) in more than 2 runs (early warning). Protocol for the close reason: run `scripts/soak_runtime_tests.sh 20 16 /data/tmp/claude-1000/soak_g03` (or the operator's scratch dir), attach `soak.jsonl` and the summary line.

Hang-timeout verification: recorded once by `g03-impl-nextest` (scratch `loop {}` test, run id in `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md`); this bead's close reason links to it.

No property tests or benches: no speed claim in this block. (A `proptest` over random interleavings of record/acknowledge on an owned slot is cheap and welcome: `proptest_slot_first_record_wins_and_ack_is_exact`, 256 cases.)

## Logging (structured JSONL fields, tracing targets)

- Soak JSONL per run: `{"schema":"soak_runtime.v1","run_id","run_index","command","threads","exit_code","passed","failed","skipped","duration_ms","slow_tests":[{"name","seconds"}],"timeouts":[...],"junit_path","stdout_path"}`; summary: `{"kind":"summary","runs","all_passed","max_test_seconds","max_test_name","total_duration_ms"}`.
- Tests enable `tracing` capture where available and assert on the `ftui.runtime.signal` events `signal_observed{signal,source}` and `signal_acknowledged{signal}` (from `g03-impl`) in `two_concurrent_...` when the `tracing` feature is on; otherwise assertions rest on return values.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: five tests (+ optional proptest; `proptest` is already a dev-dependency of ftui-runtime? verify; if not, skip the proptest rather than add a dependency for one test).
- `scripts/soak_runtime_tests.sh`: new.
- `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md`: "Runtime soak" subsection pointing at the script and the expected summary line.

## Success criteria

- [ ] All five runtime tests and the ftui-core tests green under `cargo nextest run -p ftui-runtime --test-threads 16` and under plain `cargo test -p ftui-runtime --lib`.
- [ ] `scripts/soak_runtime_tests.sh 20 16` summary: `runs=20 all_passed=true timeouts=0`, attached to the close reason with the JSONL path.
- [ ] `max_test_seconds` in the soak summary is below 30 s (records the slowest test name for `g04-02-impl` to consider).
- [ ] The hang-timeout verification run id (from `g03-impl-nextest`) is referenced.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `g03-impl` (slot and inject API), `g03-impl-nextest` (the soak uses nextest and the `ci` profile). Unblocks: `g04-12-impl` (green unit step), `g42-impl`.

## Definition of done

Tests on main, soak log archived and cited, playbook subsection added, close reason lists test names, soak summary line, and CI run id of a green `check` job that includes these tests.
close_reason: Tests landed: program::tests::two_concurrent_headless_programs_with_independent_pending_signals_both_terminate (SIGINT/SIGTERM in parallel plus a clean third program), inject_termination_signal_first_signal_wins; existing signal tests rewritten without the global serialization helper. 5 consecutive runs at --test-threads=16 green (5 passed each).

title: epic(G24): Asupersync lane resolves to its executor, Shadow policy records evidence
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:589-614 ("## Runtime Migration & Rollout Infrastructure") promises three execution lanes ("`Legacy` Available, `Structured` Active (current default), `Asupersync` Full Asupersync-native execution, Future"), an operator workflow "Off -> Shadow -> Evaluate -> Enable -> Monitor -> Rollback" driven by `ProgramConfig::default().with_lane(RuntimeLane::Structured).with_rollout_policy(RolloutPolicy::Shadow).with_env_overrides()`, and env vars `FTUI_RUNTIME_LANE` (`legacy|structured|asupersync`) and `FTUI_ROLLOUT_POLICY` (`off|shadow|enabled`). README.md:616-630 ("### Shadow-Run Validation") says shadow runs "prove rendering determinism across runtime migrations by running the same model through two independent execution paths and comparing frame checksums". README.md:2317-2319 ("## Queueing-Theoretic Scheduler (Deep Dive)") presents "The effect queue scheduler (1,900+ lines)" with SRPT, Smith's rule and aging as the effect scheduler. README.md:1221 (Known Limitations) already admits "Asupersync execution lane: Falls back to Structured; executor pending".

This epic closes vision rows V52 ("Runtime lanes + rollout + shadow-run: PARTIAL, Asupersync falls back; Shadow is a label") and V48 ("Queueing scheduler SRPT/Smith/aging: OPT-IN"). User-visible consequence today: selecting the Asupersync lane silently runs the Structured lane even when the `asupersync-executor` feature compiled a real executor; `RolloutPolicy::Shadow` changes nothing except one startup log line; and the queueing scheduler the README describes at length runs only when an app explicitly opts into the `EffectQueue` backend, while the default lanes spawn one OS thread per `Cmd::task`.

Status arrow: PARTIAL -> WORKING. Complexity M. Would open beads close it? No.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs:2713-2725` `pub enum RuntimeLane { Legacy, #[default] Structured, Asupersync }` with doc "Full Asupersync-native execution (reserved for future use). Falls back to Structured if Asupersync primitives are unavailable."
- `program.rs:2734-2746` `RuntimeLane::resolve()`: `Self::Asupersync => { tracing::info!(target: "ftui.runtime", requested = "asupersync", resolved = "structured", "Asupersync lane not yet available; falling back to structured cancellation"); Self::Structured }` unconditionally, regardless of the `asupersync-executor` feature.
- `program.rs:2778-2800` `RuntimeLane::task_executor_backend()`: `Legacy | Structured => TaskExecutorBackend::Spawned` (per-task `std::thread::spawn`, documented as the #78 input-lag regression fix); `Asupersync => { #[cfg(feature = "asupersync-executor")] TaskExecutorBackend::Asupersync; #[cfg(not(...))] TaskExecutorBackend::EffectQueue }`. Because `resolve()` runs first, the Asupersync arm is unreachable via the lane.
- `program.rs:3320-3326` `resolved_effect_queue_config()`: `self.effect_queue.clone().with_backend(self.runtime_lane.resolve().task_executor_backend())` (only when the app uses the legacy default backend; `EffectQueueConfig::with_backend` at `:2085` is the explicit override). `with_config` calls `config.runtime_lane.resolve()` at `:4818`.
- `program.rs:3579-3690` `AsupersyncTaskExecutor` (feature `asupersync-executor`): real pool with `AsupersyncRuntime`, `BlockingTaskHandle`s, `max_queue_depth` backpressure mirroring `EffectQueue`, `dropped` counter, `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT = 2 s`.
- `program.rs:2850-2863` `pub enum RolloutPolicy { #[default] Off, Shadow, Enabled }` with doc "Shadow-run comparison mode: run both lanes, emit evidence, use baseline"; `from_env()` reads `FTUI_ROLLOUT_POLICY` (`:2871`). Fields `ProgramConfig.runtime_lane` (`:2988`), `rollout_policy` (`:2994`); builders `with_lane` (`:3289`), `with_rollout_policy` (`:3296`), `with_env_overrides` (`:3307`).
- `program.rs:4904-4913`: the only use of `rollout_policy` at runtime is `tracing::info!(target: "ftui.runtime", requested_lane, resolved_lane, rollout_policy = config.rollout_policy.label(), "runtime startup: lane={}, rollout={}")`. No shadow run, no evidence.
- Shadow comparison exists only in the harness: `crates/ftui-harness/src/shadow_run.rs:207` `pub struct ShadowRun;` with `ShadowRunConfig` (`:57`), `ShadowVerdict` (`:134`), `ShadowRun::compare` (`:225`) running one model through two `LabSession`s (the README snippet at :619-629 is exact). `crates/ftui-harness/tests/perf_rollout_drills_e2e.rs` runs `ftui_harness::perf_rollout_drills::standard_drill_suite()` (shadow/canary/fallback/rollback/recovery, 8 reports) and prints `DRILL_REPORT {json}` for `scripts/perf_rollout_drills_e2e.sh`.
- Queueing scheduler: `crates/ftui-runtime/src/queueing_scheduler.rs` (2,891 lines; header "Queueing Theory Scheduler with SRPT/Smith-Rule Style Scheduling (bd-13pq.7)") is instantiated only in `effect_queue_loop` (`program.rs:3884` `QueueingScheduler::new(config.scheduler)`), which emits `effect_queue_select` evidence (`:3946-3949`) and runs one job per `scheduler.tick` (`:3951-3955`). `effect_queue_loop` runs only for `TaskExecutorBackend::EffectQueue`.
- `tests/baseline.json` row `runtime_effect_queue_drain` (p50 100 µs, p95 500 µs, p99 2 ms, p999 5 ms, threshold 15%) has no `criterion_name`, so `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh:297-306` skips it as `non_criterion_baseline`.
- `docs/adr/ADR-010-asupersync-targeted-adoption.md` (Status PROPOSED, 2026-03-12) scopes Asupersync to "runtime shell orchestration, effect execution, subscription/process lifecycle management, cancellation and deadline propagation" and explicitly not the render kernel.

## Target state

- With `asupersync-executor` on, `RuntimeLane::Asupersync.resolve()` returns `Asupersync` and `task_executor_backend()` returns `TaskExecutorBackend::Asupersync`; without the feature, `resolve()` logs a `warn!` (not `info!`) naming the missing feature and falls back to `Structured` (documented behavior).
- `RolloutPolicy::Shadow` in `Program` records per-frame checksums and lane metadata into the evidence sink (`shadow_frame` events) so `ftui-harness` `ShadowRun` can compare two recorded runs; README describes shadow-run as a harness workflow over recorded evidence.
- The default task executor backend is decided by benchmark: `runtime_effect_queue_drain` becomes a criterion bench with a `criterion_name`, plus a burst-of-200-tasks latency bench; either `EffectQueue` (with the queueing scheduler) becomes the default or the scheduler is documented as opt-in; the numbers live in `docs/perf/effect_backend_<date>.md`.

## Success criteria (block level)

- [ ] `asupersync_lane_resolves_to_asupersync_backend_when_feature_enabled` (feature-gated) and `asupersync_lane_falls_back_to_structured_without_feature` pass (g24-tests).
- [ ] `rollout_drills.rs` E2E compares two evidence files and yields `ShadowVerdict::Match` (g24-e2e).

1. `g24-impl`: lane resolution honoring the feature; Shadow policy recording (`shadow_frame` evidence with frame index, buffer checksum, lane label, rollout policy, task backend).
2. `g24-impl-executor-default`: two benches, decision doc, default flip or opt-in documentation.

Any default flip to `EffectQueue` must include a multi-worker or non-serializing configuration and must re-run that scenario (the bench below includes a "10 concurrent 10 ms pollers" case for this reason).

title: task(G24): RuntimeLane::resolve honors asupersync-executor; Shadow writes shadow_frame evidence
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:589-614 says `RuntimeLane::Asupersync` is "Full Asupersync-native execution" selectable via `FTUI_RUNTIME_LANE=asupersync`, and that `RolloutPolicy::Shadow` enables "Shadow-compare before enabling". In code the lane is a label: `RuntimeLane::resolve()` rewrites Asupersync to Structured unconditionally, so the real `AsupersyncTaskExecutor` (compiled under feature `asupersync-executor`) is unreachable through the lane; and `RolloutPolicy::Shadow` produces one log line and no evidence. This bead makes both honest: the lane resolves to the executor when it exists (and warns when it does not), and Shadow records the per-frame evidence that a shadow comparison needs. Serves V52; primary implementation bead of G24.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs:2734-2746`:
  ```rust
  pub fn resolve(self) -> Self {
      match self {
          Self::Asupersync => {
              tracing::info!(target: "ftui.runtime", requested = "asupersync", resolved = "structured",
                  "Asupersync lane not yet available; falling back to structured cancellation");
              Self::Structured
          }
          other => other,
      }
  }
  ```
- `program.rs:2778-2800` `task_executor_backend()`: `Legacy | Structured => Spawned`; `Asupersync => Asupersync` under `cfg(feature = "asupersync-executor")`, else `EffectQueue`. Unreachable via `resolve()`.
- `program.rs:3320-3326` `resolved_effect_queue_config()` calls `self.runtime_lane.resolve().task_executor_backend()`; `program.rs:4818` `let resolved_lane = config.runtime_lane.resolve();` in `with_config`.
- `program.rs:3579-3690` `AsupersyncTaskExecutor<M>` (feature-gated): fields `result_sender`, `evidence_sink`, `runtime: AsupersyncRuntime`, `handles: Vec<BlockingTaskHandle>`, `max_queue_depth`, `dropped`, `closed`; `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT = 2 s`.
- `program.rs:2850-2863` `RolloutPolicy { Off, Shadow, Enabled }`; `program.rs:4904-4913` the startup `tracing::info!` is the only runtime consumer of `rollout_policy`.
- Evidence sink API: `crates/ftui-runtime/src/evidence_sink.rs:144` `pub struct EvidenceSink`, `:200` `pub fn write_jsonl(&self, line: &str) -> io::Result<()>`; existing writers call e.g. `sink.write_jsonl(&evidence.to_jsonl("effect_queue_select"))` (`program.rs:3946-3949`).
- Frame checksum helper lives in the harness: `crates/ftui-harness/src/golden.rs:71` `pub fn compute_buffer_checksum(buf: &Buffer) -> String`. The runtime cannot depend on the harness.
- Harness comparison: `crates/ftui-harness/src/shadow_run.rs:57` `ShadowRunConfig`, `:134` `ShadowVerdict`, `:207` `ShadowRun`, `:225` `compare(...)` (two `LabSession`s in-process).

## Target state

1. `RuntimeLane::resolve()`:
   - `#[cfg(feature = "asupersync-executor")]`: `Asupersync => Asupersync` (no fallback).
   - `#[cfg(not(feature = "asupersync-executor"))]`: `Asupersync => { tracing::warn!(target: "ftui.runtime", requested = "asupersync", resolved = "structured", missing_feature = "asupersync-executor", "Asupersync lane requested but the `asupersync-executor` feature is not compiled; falling back to structured cancellation"); Structured }`.
   - The doc comment on the `Asupersync` variant drops "reserved for future use" and states the feature requirement.
2. `RuntimeLane::task_executor_backend()`: the `Asupersync` arm returns `TaskExecutorBackend::Asupersync` (only reachable with the feature now); the `#[cfg(not)]` arm becomes unreachable and is removed (no dead fallback to `EffectQueue`).
3. Shadow recording in `Program`:
   - New `pub fn buffer_checksum(buf: &Buffer) -> u64` in `crates/ftui-render/src/buffer.rs` (FNV-1a over each cell's 16 bytes in row-major order; `#[inline]`; documented as the shadow/golden checksum). `ftui_harness::golden::compute_buffer_checksum` is changed to format this function's result so both sides agree (no compatibility wrapper: update the harness call sites and snapshots if the string changes).
   - In `Program`, after each successful present (the site where `diff_decision` evidence is written in `terminal_writer.rs:1655`-area or the program-level frame loop; pick the program-level site that already has `frame_idx`), when `config.rollout_policy == RolloutPolicy::Shadow` and an evidence sink is configured, write `{"event":"shadow_frame","frame":<u64>,"checksum":<u64 as hex string>,"lane":"<resolved lane label>","requested_lane":"<label>","rollout_policy":"shadow","task_backend":"spawned|effect_queue|asupersync","cols":<u16>,"rows":<u16>,"ts_ns":<u128>}` via `EvidenceSink::write_jsonl`. Add `ShadowFrameEvidence { .. }` with `to_jsonl()` next to the other evidence structs in `program.rs` (or `evidence_sink.rs` if the sibling structs live there) and add the `shadow_frame` name to `telemetry_schema.rs` constants (coordinate with `g20-impl`, which is making all event names constants).
   - `RolloutPolicy::Enabled` is unchanged (lane is live).
4. Harness side: `ShadowRun::compare_recorded(baseline: &Path, candidate: &Path) -> ShadowRunResult` in `shadow_run.rs` reads two evidence JSONL files, filters `shadow_frame` lines, pairs by `frame`, compares `checksum`, and yields `ShadowVerdict::Match` / `Mismatch { first_divergent_frame, .. }` / the existing variants; `frames_compared` and match ratio reuse the existing accounting (`:195-198`).
5. Startup log at `program.rs:4904-4913` additionally logs `task_backend` and, for Shadow, the evidence path (`evidence_sink.path()` if available).

## Implementation plan

1. `program.rs:2734-2746`: rewrite `resolve()` with the two cfg arms; update the variant doc at `:2722-2724`.
2. `program.rs:2778-2800`: simplify `task_executor_backend()`.
3. `crates/ftui-render/src/buffer.rs`: add `buffer_checksum`; unit test with a known vector.
4. `crates/ftui-harness/src/golden.rs:71`: implement `compute_buffer_checksum` via `ftui_render::buffer::buffer_checksum` (format `{:016x}`); re-bless any golden checksum fixtures under `crates/ftui-harness/tests/golden/` that change (list them in the close reason; `BLESS=1` flow).
5. `program.rs`: `ShadowFrameEvidence` struct + `to_jsonl`; emit after present under `Shadow`; `telemetry_schema.rs`: `pub const EVENT_SHADOW_FRAME: &str = "shadow_frame";`.
6. `crates/ftui-harness/src/shadow_run.rs`: `compare_recorded`; reuse `ShadowVerdict`.
7. `program.rs:4904-4913`: extend the startup log.
8. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (with and without `--features asupersync-executor` for `ftui-runtime`), `cargo fmt --check`; `ubs` on changed files.

What NOT to do: no in-process dual-lane execution; no compatibility alias for the old `info!` message; no new `program_v2.rs`; do not touch `tests/baseline.json` here (G25 owns it; `g24-impl-executor-default` hands it the row).

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `RuntimeLane::resolve`, `task_executor_backend`, `ShadowFrameEvidence`, emission site, startup log.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/telemetry_schema.rs`: `EVENT_SHADOW_FRAME`.
- `crates/ftui-render/src/buffer.rs`: `buffer_checksum`.
- `crates/ftui-harness/src/golden.rs`: use the shared checksum.
- `crates/ftui-harness/src/shadow_run.rs`: `compare_recorded`.
- `crates/ftui-harness/tests/golden/*` : re-blessed if checksum format changed.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-runtime --features asupersync-executor asupersync_lane_resolves_to_asupersync_backend_when_feature_enabled` green; `cargo test -p ftui-runtime asupersync_lane_falls_back_to_structured_without_feature` green (asserts the `warn!` via a `tracing` test subscriber).
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-runtime shadow_policy_writes_shadow_frame_evidence` green: headless program with `RolloutPolicy::Shadow` and a temp-file sink; after 5 rendered frames the file has 5 `shadow_frame` lines with strictly increasing `frame` and 16-hex-digit `checksum`.
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-harness compare_recorded_matches_identical_runs` and `compare_recorded_reports_first_divergent_frame` green.
- [ ] `g24-e2e` yields `ShadowVerdict::Match` on two real recordings.

## Tests and logging

Details in `g24-tests`. Logging: `shadow_frame` JSONL as specified; tracing `warn!` on fallback; startup `info!` includes `task_backend`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: nothing. Coordinates with `g20-impl` (event-name constants; if `g20-impl` lands first, use its constant; if not, add the constant here and `g20-impl` keeps it). Unblocks: `g24-impl-executor-default` (needs the truthful lane mapping), `g24-tests`, `g24-e2e`, `g24-docs`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Per-frame checksum cost: FNV-1a over 80x24x16 = 30 KB per frame, ~10-20 µs; only under `Shadow`, never in `Off`/`Enabled`.
- Risk: golden fixture churn from the checksum change; keep the algorithm identical to the harness's current one if it is already FNV-1a over cell bytes (check `golden.rs:71` first and prefer moving the existing algorithm rather than inventing a new one).
- Alternative rejected: leaving `resolve()` as-is and documenting the fallback. The feature exists and the README table promises the lane; honoring it costs a cfg arm.

## Definition of done

Lane and Shadow behave as documented; tests above green with and without the feature; goldens consistent; evidence name registered; close reason lists test names; main green.
notes: Refinement 3: logging one checksum per live frame is a recording path, not dual execution. Explicitly distinguish record-and-compare from actual Shadow candidate evaluation. Complete shadow semantics against the documented contract; run pure/replayed effects in candidate mode so subprocess/network/clipboard/log effects execute once. Inject state divergence to prove detection.

title: task(G24): decide the default task executor backend by benchmark (spawned vs effect queue)
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:2317-2319 ("## Queueing-Theoretic Scheduler (Deep Dive)") says "The effect queue scheduler (1,900+ lines) implements multiple scheduling disciplines from queueing theory" (SRPT, Smith's rule, aging), and README.md:1700/1764 list "Smith's Rule + Aging | Queueing scheduler" among the math-driven components. That scheduler (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/queueing_scheduler.rs`, 2,891 lines) runs only when an app opts into `TaskExecutorBackend::EffectQueue`; the default lanes spawn one thread per `Cmd::task`. Vision row V48 is therefore OPT-IN. This bead decides the default backend by benchmark rather than by assertion, and either flips the default or documents the scheduler as opt-in. It also gives `runtime_effect_queue_drain` a real criterion bench so the perf gate stops skipping it. Serves V48 and V52.

## Current state (evidence)

- `program.rs:2757-2777` doc comment "Input-lag regression fix (#78)": `Structured` once returned `EffectQueue`, which "routed every `Cmd::Task` through a single `effect_queue_loop` worker thread with a Smith's-rule (SPT) scheduler, serializing all tasks. Apps that forward PTY output via per-pane `Cmd::task` polling loops (e.g. 10ms drains) then contended for one serialized worker, adding per-keystroke head-of-line latency versus v0.2.1, where each `Cmd::task` got its own `std::thread::spawn`." Hence `Legacy | Structured => TaskExecutorBackend::Spawned` (`:2785-2791`).
- `program.rs:3877-3955` `effect_queue_loop`: one thread; `QueueingScheduler::new(config.scheduler)`; `max_depth = config.max_queue_depth`; per iteration `scheduler.peek_next()`, writes `effect_queue_select` evidence, `scheduler.tick(job.remaining_time)`, runs completed jobs via `run_task_closure(task, "queued", ...)`, `record_queue_processed()`.
- `TaskExecutorBackend` enum at `program.rs:2016`; `EffectQueueConfig::with_backend` at `:2085`; `uses_legacy_default_backend` gate referenced at `:2775`.
- `tests/baseline.json` `runtime_effect_queue_drain`: description "Time to drain effect queue after shutdown signal", `category: user-visible`, budgets p50 100 µs / p95 500 µs / p99 2 ms / p999 5 ms, `threshold_pct: 15`, no `criterion_name`/`bench_file`, so `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh:297-306` prints `SKIP ... non_criterion_baseline`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/benches/` contains `ivm_bench.rs`, `pane_terminal_bench.rs`, `telemetry_bench.rs`, `tick_strategy_bench.rs`; none benchmarks task execution.
- `docs/perf/` exists (pane_* docs, `baseline_profiles.md`); no `effect_backend_*.md`.

## Target state

- `crates/ftui-runtime/benches/effect_backend_bench.rs` (criterion) with groups:
  - `runtime/effect_queue_drain/{spawned,effect_queue,asupersync}`: enqueue 50 trivial tasks, signal shutdown, measure time to drain (criterion name for the baseline row: `runtime/effect_queue_drain/<default backend>`).
  - `runtime/task_burst_200/{spawned,effect_queue,asupersync}`: submit 200 tasks of 100 µs simulated work in one update; measure p50/p99 latency from submit to result-message receipt, and total completion time.
  - `runtime/pollers_10x10ms/{spawned,effect_queue,asupersync}`: the #78 scenario: 10 concurrent tasks each sleeping 10 ms then re-submitting for 500 ms, plus a keystroke-echo task every 20 ms; measure echo latency p99 (this is the regression guard).
  - `asupersync` variants under `#[cfg(feature = "asupersync-executor")]`.
- Decision rule (stated up front so the outcome is not post-hoc): `EffectQueue` becomes the default for `Structured` only if (a) `pollers_10x10ms` echo p99 is within 1.2x of `spawned`, (b) `task_burst_200` p99 is at least 1.3x better than `spawned`, and (c) `effect_queue_drain` meets the baseline p99 (2 ms). Otherwise `Spawned` stays the default and the scheduler is documented as opt-in with the numbers.
- `docs/perf/effect_backend_<date>.md`: machine, commit, criterion output tables for the three groups, the rule above, the verdict.
- `tests/baseline.json`: `runtime_effect_queue_drain` gains `criterion_name: "runtime/effect_queue_drain/<default>"`, `bench_file: "effect_backend_bench"`, `crate: "ftui-runtime"` (hand this row to `g25-impl`, which edits the file; if `g25-impl` is not merged, add the row here and note it).
- If flipped: `RuntimeLane::task_executor_backend()` returns `EffectQueue` for `Structured` with `EffectQueueConfig.workers >= 2` (add a `workers` field so tasks are not serialized; `effect_queue_loop` spawns `workers` threads pulling from the scheduler under a mutex) and the #78 doc comment is rewritten to describe the new guard bench.

## Implementation plan

1. Write the bench file; use `ProgramSimulator` (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/simulator.rs:85`) or the headless constructor to drive `Cmd::task` submissions without a terminal; use `std::time::Instant` inside tasks to timestamp submit/receive (results carry the submit instant).
2. Run each group 3 times via `rch exec -- cargo bench -p ftui-runtime --bench effect_backend_bench -- --save-baseline <date>` (and with `--features asupersync-executor`); save criterion JSON under `target/criterion/`.
3. Write `docs/perf/effect_backend_<date>.md` from the JSON (hand-written tables; `scripts/render_perf_readme.py` from `g25-impl-readme-numbers` can be reused once it exists).
4. Apply the decision rule; implement the flip (with `workers`) or leave `Spawned`.
5. If flipped: rerun the full `ftui-runtime` test suite plus `scripts/e2e_test.sh --quick` and the pane PTY E2E (`crates/ftui-harness/tests/pane_input_pty_e2e.rs`) to guard #78 empirically; record numbers.
6. Update the baseline row (via `g25-impl` or directly); `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt`; `ubs`.

What NOT to do: do not flip the default without the three numbers; do not delete the `Spawned` backend; no hidden env-var default override.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-runtime/benches/effect_backend_bench.rs`: new bench (three groups).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml`: `[[bench]] name = "effect_backend_bench" harness = false`.
- `docs/perf/effect_backend_<date>.md`: new decision record.
- `tests/baseline.json`: `runtime_effect_queue_drain` criterion mapping (coordinate with `g25-impl`).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: only if flipped (`task_executor_backend`, `EffectQueueConfig.workers`, `effect_queue_loop` worker pool, #78 comment).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo bench -p ftui-runtime --bench effect_backend_bench` produces the three groups for `spawned` and `effect_queue` (and `asupersync` with the feature).
- [ ] `docs/perf/effect_backend_<date>.md` exists with tables and the verdict sentence "Default backend: <Spawned|EffectQueue> because <rule outcome>".
- [ ] `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh --check-only` no longer reports `runtime_effect_queue_drain` as `non_criterion_baseline`.
- [ ] If flipped: `pollers_10x10ms` echo p99 within 1.2x of spawned, recorded in the doc; pane PTY E2E green.

## Tests and logging

- Bench output is the evidence; criterion JSON kept as an artifact by the `perf-gate` job (`g25-impl`).
- Unit test `effect_queue_workers_do_not_serialize_independent_tasks` (only if flipped): two 50 ms tasks complete in < 80 ms total with `workers = 2`.
- Logging: bench prints one JSONL line per group `{bench, backend, p50_us, p99_us, total_ms}` to stderr for easy capture.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g24-impl` (truthful lane mapping so the `asupersync` variant is reachable). Coordinates with `g25-impl` (baseline row) and `g25-impl-benches` (bench conventions). Unblocks: `g24-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- The #78 regression is the strongest argument for keeping `Spawned`; the decision rule encodes it as a hard constraint (a) rather than leaving it to judgment.
- A `workers` pool changes scheduler semantics (SRPT across N workers is still well-defined: pop the highest-priority ready job per free worker); document it in the module header if implemented.
- Alternative rejected: making `EffectQueue` default for `Legacy` only. Legacy is the pre-migration lane and should not change behavior.

## Definition of done

Benches exist and run; decision doc committed; baseline row mapped; default state matches the doc; close reason quotes the three numbers and the verdict; main green.

title: task(G24): feature-gated lane resolution tests, shadow evidence tests, checksum tests
description:

title: task(G24): record two showcase runs under Shadow and compare to ShadowVerdict::Match
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:616-630 promises shadow-run validation that "prove[s] rendering determinism across runtime migrations by running the same model through two independent execution paths and comparing frame checksums", ending in `assert_eq!(result.verdict, ShadowVerdict::Match)`. After `g24-impl`, `RolloutPolicy::Shadow` records `shadow_frame` evidence and the harness can compare two recordings. This bead proves the whole loop end to end with the real showcase binary under a PTY: record a Structured run and a second run (Structured again, and Asupersync when the feature is compiled), compare the evidence files, and get `Match`. It is the Section 7.6 row "V52 lanes: feature-gated lane resolution tests; `rollout_drills.rs`".

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-harness/tests/perf_rollout_drills_e2e.rs` runs `ftui_harness::perf_rollout_drills::standard_drill_suite()` (8 reports: shadow/canary/fallback/rollback/recovery, clean and failure paths), prints `DRILL_REPORT {json}`, asserts `mechanism_ok`, byte-identical replay and operator guidance. `scripts/perf_rollout_drills_e2e.sh` harvests those lines. The drills are synthetic; no drill records or compares a real program's evidence.
- Showcase evidence: `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL` ("Path for evidence JSONL logs (diff/resize/budget)", `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/cli.rs:140`); deterministic runs via `FTUI_DEMO_DETERMINISTIC`, `FTUI_DEMO_SEED`, `FTUI_DEMO_TICK_MS`, `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_TICKS` (`cli.rs:111-114`); `--screen=N`/`FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN` (`cli.rs:26,:119`).

- PTY driver: `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` `pty_run <output_file> <cmd...>` with `PTY_TIMEOUT`; JSONL helpers in `tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh` (`jsonl_init`, `jsonl_run_start`, `jsonl_step_start/end`, `jsonl_assert`, `jsonl_artifact`, `jsonl_run_end`); schema `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json`; validator `tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py`.

## Target state

- `scripts/perf_rollout_drills_e2e.sh` gains a `shadow_recorded_compare` scenario (or a new sibling `scripts/shadow_run_e2e.sh` if the drills script's structure makes that cleaner; prefer extending):
  1. Build the showcase (`rch exec -- cargo build -p ftui-demo-showcase`).
  2. Run A: `FTUI_RUNTIME_LANE=structured FTUI_ROLLOUT_POLICY=shadow FTUI_DEMO_DETERMINISTIC=1 FTUI_DEMO_SEED=7 FTUI_DEMO_TICK_MS=16 FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_TICKS=120 FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL=$OUT/a.jsonl pty_run $OUT/a.pty <showcase> --screen=1 --screen-mode=alt`.
  3. Run B: identical env, `b.jsonl`.
  4. Run C (only if `cargo build -p ftui-demo-showcase --features ftui-runtime/asupersync-executor` succeeds; feature name verified in `crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml`): `FTUI_RUNTIME_LANE=asupersync`, `c.jsonl`.
  5. Compare with a tiny harness binary or test: `cargo test -p ftui-harness --test rollout_drills -- compare_recorded_cli` reading `SHADOW_BASELINE`/`SHADOW_CANDIDATE` env; or add `crates/ftui-harness/src/bin/shadow_compare.rs` (one new bin, prints the verdict JSON). Assert A vs B is `Match` with `frames_compared >= 100`; A vs C is `Match` (lanes must not change rendering) when C exists.
  6. Negative control: A vs A-with-one-line-edited (sed on a copy in `$OUT`, not on tracked files) yields a mismatch at the edited frame.
- `crates/ftui-harness/tests/rollout_drills.rs` (new integration test file named as the audit's success criterion): `shadow_compare_of_two_recorded_runs_matches` using two checked-in fixture evidence files under `crates/ftui-harness/tests/fixtures/shadow/{a,b}.jsonl` (generated once by the script, 20 frames each) and `shadow_compare_detects_divergence` using a fixture with frame 11 altered.

## Implementation plan

1. Confirm the showcase honors `FTUI_RUNTIME_LANE`/`FTUI_ROLLOUT_POLICY` (grep `with_env_overrides` in `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/`); add if missing.

4. Generate the fixtures once; write `crates/ftui-harness/tests/rollout_drills.rs`.
5. Wire into `ci.yml` `perf-rollout-gates`; upload artifacts `if: always()`.
6. Run locally three times to check stability; run `ubs` on changed files.

What NOT to do: no in-process dual-program "shadow"; no editing tracked fixtures with sed (copies only); no skipping the negative control.

- `crates/ftui-harness/src/bin/shadow_compare.rs`: new bin.
- `crates/ftui-harness/tests/rollout_drills.rs`: new integration test.

- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/main.rs`: `with_env_overrides()` if absent.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Script exit 0 locally; JSONL validates against `e2e_jsonl_schema.json`.
- [ ] A-vs-B verdict `Match`, `frames_compared >= 100`; A-vs-C `Match` when the feature builds; negative control mismatch at the edited frame.
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-harness --test rollout_drills` green.
- [ ] `perf-rollout-gates` job green with artifacts (run id in close reason).

## Tests and logging

JSONL per step: `run_id`, `ts`, `scenario` (`shadow_recorded_compare`), `step` (`run_a|run_b|run_c|compare_ab|compare_ac|negative_control`), `lane`, `rollout_policy`, `seed`, `ticks`, `frames_recorded` (count of `shadow_frame` lines), `verdict`, `frames_compared`, `first_divergent_frame`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, `pty_bytes`, `sync_pairs` (count of `\x1b[?2026h`/`l` pairs in the capture, to show the runs rendered), `status`. PTY driver: `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` `pty_run`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g24-impl` (evidence + comparison), `g24-tests`. Unblocks: `g42-impl` (Section 7.6 V52 row), `g24-docs` (cites the scenario).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Determinism relies on `FTUI_DEMO_DETERMINISTIC=1` and fixed `TICK_MS`; screen 1 (Dashboard) is the safest choice because it is fixture-driven. If A-vs-B ever mismatches, that is a real nondeterminism bug and must become a bead, not a loosened assertion.
- Asupersync run C only where the feature compiles; the script logs `skipped` with reason otherwise.

Scenario in CI with artifacts; fixture-based integration test green; close reason cites run id, verdicts and frame counts.

title: epic(G25): enforce performance budgets in CI and back README numbers with artifacts
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:2086-2094 ("### Benchmark Suite") prints "`diff/identical_100x50 time: [1.2 µs]`, `diff/sparse_5pct_100x50 time: [8.3 µs]`, `diff/dense_100x50 time: [45 µs]`" as the output of `cargo bench -p ftui-render`. README.md:1259-1261 (FAQ "What's the performance like?") and README.md:1527 ("## Math-Driven Performance") make speed a headline feature, and the original plan document (section 0.12) set budgets: present 80x24 p50 < 1 ms / p99 < 3 ms, 120x40 p50 < 2 ms / p99 < 6 ms, 200x60 p50 < 6 ms / p99 < 18 ms, input parse+dispatch < 100 µs per event, wrap 200 lines < 2 ms, bytes emitted O(changes), and allocations per frame tracked. README.md ("Frame arena in hot path", vision row V29) promises per-frame arena allocation on the hot path.

This epic closes vision rows V35 ("Property tests, snapshots, benches: WORKING; bench numbers unbacked"), V29 ("Frame arena in hot path: WORKING (light use)"), Section 2.2.E ("`tests/baseline.json` is consumed by `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh`, which no workflow invokes ... README performance numbers are not backed by any checked-in artifact") and Section 2.2.F ("Perf budgets at 120x40 / 200x60, input parse+dispatch under 100 µs, bytes-emitted O(changes), wrap 200 lines under 2 ms, allocations per frame: no gate enforces any of them"). User-visible consequence: the README quotes numbers for benchmarks that do not exist (`100x50`, `dense`), no CI job would catch a 2x regression in present latency, and the arena that is supposed to keep the hot path allocation-free is used by one widget.

Status arrow: UNPROVEN -> WORKING. Complexity L. Would open beads close it? No.

## Current state (evidence)

- `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh` (20 KB; header "Performance Regression Gate (bd-3fc.4)"): compares criterion results with `tests/baseline.json` p99 budgets; modes `--check-only`, `--quick`, `--json`, `--flamegraph`, `--update`; uses `rch exec -- cargo` when available; reads `slo.yaml` for `slo_metric` declarations. Lines 297-306: rows without `criterion_name`/`bench_file` are printed `SKIP` and logged `{"status":"skip","reason":"non_criterion_baseline"}`. No workflow invokes it (`grep -n perf_regression_gate .github/workflows/*.yml` returns nothing).
- `scripts/bench_budget.sh` (29 KB; "Performance Budget Enforcement Script (bd-3cwi)"): hard-coded `BUDGETS` map (e.g. `cell/compare/bits_eq_same 100 ns`, `buffer/new/alloc/80x24 100 µs`, `buffer/new/alloc/200x60 500 µs`); CI `benchmarks` job (`ci.yml:294-338`) runs `./scripts/bench_budget.sh --quick` (line 327) only on pushes to main, with the audit's noted 1.50x loosened dense envelopes.
- `tests/baseline.json` (`_updated: 2026-07-20`, `_presenter_color_depth: truecolor`): criterion rows `frame_render` (`pipeline/truecolor/diff_and_present/full/80x24@5%`, p50 500 µs, p95 1 ms, p99 2 ms, p999 5 ms, 10%), `layout_computation` (`layout/flex_split/horizontal/10`), `diff_strategy` (`diff/sparse_5pct/compute/80x24`), `diff_strategy_large` (`diff/sparse_5pct/compute/200x60`, p99 800 µs), `widget_render_block`, `widget_render_table`, `ansi_emit` (`present/truecolor/sparse_5pct/present/80x24`), `buffer_new_80x24`, `buffer_new_200x60`, `cell_bits_eq`; and four `category: user-visible` rows without criterion names: `runtime_shutdown_latency` (p99 5 ms), `runtime_first_frame` (p99 10 ms), `runtime_command_roundtrip` (p99 500 µs), `runtime_effect_queue_drain` (p99 2 ms).
- `crates/ftui-render/benches/diff_bench.rs` groups: `diff/identical`, `diff/sparse_5pct`, `diff/heavy_50pct`, `diff/full_100pct`, each over `(80,24), (120,40), (200,60)` with `BenchmarkId::new("compute", "{w}x{h}")`; `diff/runs` coalesce. No `100x50`, no `dense`. Other benches: `arena_bench.rs`, `buffer_bench.rs`, `cell_bench.rs`, `double_buffer_bench.rs`, `presenter_bench.rs`, `resize_storm_bench.rs`, `roaring_bench.rs`; `crates/ftui-core/benches/read_optimized_bench.rs` only (no input parser bench); `crates/ftui-text/benches/{cache_bench,search_bench,shaped_render_bench,width_bench}.rs` (no wrap bench); `crates/ftui-runtime/benches/{ivm_bench,pane_terminal_bench,telemetry_bench,tick_strategy_bench}.rs`.
- Checked-in results: `docs/profiling/opportunity_matrix_2026-02-03.md` (identical diff 1.81 µs at 80x24 per the audit), `docs/profiling/baseline_metrics_2026-02-03.jsonl`, `docs/perf/baseline_profiles.md`. No artifact backs 1.2/8.3/45 µs.
- `CountingWriter` lives at `crates/ftui-render/src/counting_writer.rs:34` (`bytes_written()`, `reset_counter()`), with `within_budget()` at `:164` using `expected_max_bytes(cells_changed, run_count)`; the harness re-exports/uses it (the audit placed it in ftui-harness; the definition is in ftui-render).
- `FrameArena` at `crates/ftui-render/src/arena.rs` (`BumpVec` alias `:35`, `DEFAULT_ARENA_CAPACITY = 256 KB` `:38`, `new` `:68`, `reset` `:84`, `alloc_str` `:92`, `alloc_slice` `:111`, `alloc` `:132`, `alloc_iter` `:140`, `new_vec` `:153`, `allocated_bytes` `:171`); `Frame.arena: Option<&'a FrameArena>` (`frame.rs:470`), `set_arena` (`:571`), `arena()` (`:579`); `Program.frame_arena` (`program.rs:4786`), reset before view (`:6562`, `:6629`) and `frame.set_arena(&self.frame_arena)` (`:6572`, `:6634`), memory guardrail counts `frame_arena.allocated_bytes()` (`:6124`). Consumers: `crates/ftui-widgets/src/input.rs:954-957` ("Use arena allocation when available") and the showcase dashboard only.
- Allocation sites the arena could absorb: `crates/ftui-text/src/wrap.rs:113` `pub fn wrap_text(...) -> Vec<String>` and `:128 wrap_with_options`, `:157 wrap_chars`, `:193 wrap_words` each return `Vec<String>`; `crates/ftui-layout/src/lib.rs:634` `Flex::split(&self, area: Rect) -> Rects` (and `:810 split_with_measurer`); `crates/ftui-render/src/diff.rs:1559` `pub fn runs(&self) -> Vec<ChangeRun>` plus `:1606 runs_into(&self, out: &mut Vec<ChangeRun>)` (already has an out-param variant; `:4372` uses a reusable `runs_buf`).

## Target state

- A `perf-gate` CI job runs `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh --quick --json` on pushes to main and nightly, uploads `target/regression-gate/regression_report.jsonl` and criterion JSON; no row is skipped as `non_criterion_baseline`.
- `tests/baseline.json` gains rows with criterion names: `present_80x24_sparse` (p50 < 1 ms, p99 < 3 ms), `present_120x40_sparse` (p50 < 2 ms, p99 < 6 ms), `present_200x60_sparse` (p50 < 6 ms, p99 < 18 ms), `input_parse_dispatch_event` (< 100 µs), `bytes_emitted_sparse_5pct` (bytes < 8 x changed cells + 64), `wrap_200_lines` (< 2 ms), `frame_allocations_ascii_scene` (0 allocations in the ASCII path), `text_width_non_ascii` (G08's row), and the four runtime rows mapped to real benches.
- New benches: `crates/ftui-core/benches/input_parser_bench.rs`, `crates/ftui-text/benches/wrap_bench.rs`, presenter sizes in `presenter_bench.rs`, bytes via `CountingWriter`, feature `alloc-count` with a counting `#[global_allocator]` in benches.
- `FrameArena` carries wrapped-line span vectors (`ftui-text` wrap), solved `Rect` lists (`Flex::split`), and `ChangeRun` vectors (diff) when `frame.arena` is present; `frame_allocations_ascii_scene` reaches zero and a non-ASCII scene drops by at least half.
- `scripts/render_perf_readme.py` writes `docs/perf/baseline_<date>.md` and the README "Benchmark Suite" block from the gate JSON; `check_readme_claims.py` verifies the block hash.

## Success criteria (block level)

- [ ] `perf-gate` job green on main with artifacts; `regression_report.jsonl` has zero `non_criterion_baseline` skips (g25-impl, g25-e2e).
- [ ] The eight new baseline rows exist with criterion names and pass (g25-impl, g25-impl-benches).
- [ ] `frame_allocations_ascii_scene == 0`; non-ASCII scene allocations at least halved vs the pre-arena number recorded in the bead (g25-impl-arena).
- [ ] README "Benchmark Suite" block regenerated from an artifact, with a ledger hash (g25-impl-readme-numbers, g25-docs).

## Plan (children)

1. `g25-impl`: perf-gate CI job + baseline rows (after `g04-12-impl` job topology).
2. `g25-impl-benches`: the new benches and the `alloc-count` feature.
3. `g25-impl-arena`: arena adoption in wrap/Flex/diff.
4. `g25-impl-readme-numbers`: generator script, dated report, README block, ledger hash.
5. `g25-tests`: bench-existence tests, gate self-tests, alloc-count unit tests.
6. `g25-e2e`: the gate job end to end, including a deliberate regression proving it fails.
7. `g25-docs`: README Benchmarks/Performance wording, `docs/perf/README` index, ledger rows.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-12-impl` (job topology: the gate must live in the advisory-vs-blocking split that block defines). Unblocks: `g06-impl-ledger`/`g06-docs-readme` (README numbers), `g11-impl` (needs the `frame_render` row unchanged under the conformal predictor), `g08-impl` (`text_width_non_ascii` row), `g42-impl` (Section 7.6 row V35: "`perf-gate` job artifact and `docs/perf/baseline_<date>.md`").

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Shared runners are noisy: the gate compares means to p99 budgets with `threshold_pct`; `--quick` sampling plus generous p99s (not p50s) is the right gate; p50 targets are recorded, not gated, on CI. Section 7.1 G04.2 moved wall-clock unit assertions here for the same reason.
- Allocation counting via a global allocator affects all benches in that binary; keep it behind `alloc-count` and only in bench targets, never in library code.
- Arena adoption must not change results: proptests assert wrap output equality with and without arena.
- Alternative rejected: deleting `bench_budget.sh` and its `benchmarks` job. Both scripts can coexist until the gate proves stable; then `g25-docs` records which one is canonical (the gate) and the `benchmarks` job may be folded (no file deletion without permission).

## Definition of done

Gate in CI with artifacts, baseline rows real, arena on the hot path with the allocation numbers proving it, README numbers generated from a checked-in artifact, ledger rows present, main green.
