title: task(G25): input_parser_bench, wrap_bench, presenter sizes, bytes via CountingWriter, alloc-count
description:
## Context and why this matters

The plan's performance budgets (present at 80x24/120x40/200x60, input parse+dispatch < 100 µs per event, wrap 200 lines < 2 ms, bytes emitted O(changes), allocations per frame) have no benches behind them: `crates/ftui-core/benches/` holds only `read_optimized_bench.rs`, `crates/ftui-text/benches/` has no wrap bench, `presenter_bench.rs` has the 80x24 sparse present but the baseline maps no other size, nothing measures bytes on the wire per frame, and nothing counts allocations. README.md:2086-2094 quotes `100x50` and `dense` benches that do not exist. This bead writes the benches with the exact criterion ids that `g25-impl` put into `tests/baseline.json`, and adds the `alloc-count` feature so allocation counts become a measurable, gate-able number (the acceptance metric for `g25-impl-arena`). Serves V35, Section 2.2.F.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-render/benches/diff_bench.rs:179-245`: groups `diff/identical`, `diff/sparse_5pct`, `diff/heavy_50pct`, `diff/full_100pct` over `(80,24),(120,40),(200,60)`; `:247-260` `diff/runs` coalesce at `80x24@5%`, `80x24@50%`, `200x60@5%`; helper at `:113-170` interleaves full/dirty measurements and records p50/p95.
- `crates/ftui-render/benches/presenter_bench.rs` (5 KB, 2026-07-22): produces `present/truecolor/sparse_5pct/present/80x24` and `pipeline/truecolor/diff_and_present/full/80x24@5%` (both referenced by `tests/baseline.json`).
- `crates/ftui-render/src/counting_writer.rs:34` `CountingWriter<W>` with `bytes_written()`, `reset_counter()`; stats type with `bytes_per_run()` and `within_budget()` (`:164`, budget from `expected_max_bytes(cells_changed, run_count)`); header says it is "used to verify O(changes) output size for diff-based rendering".
- Input parser: `crates/ftui-core/src/input_parser.rs` (README.md:1067 "Input Parser (3,200+ Lines)"); fuzz targets exist under `fuzz/`; no bench.
- Wrap: `crates/ftui-text/src/wrap.rs:113` `wrap_text(text, width, WrapMode) -> Vec<String>`, `:128 wrap_with_options`, `:933 wrap_text_optimal` (Knuth-Plass path via `kp_tokenize` `:713`).
- Runtime user-visible rows in `tests/baseline.json` (`runtime_first_frame` p99 10 ms, `runtime_shutdown_latency` p99 5 ms, `runtime_command_roundtrip` p99 500 µs, `runtime_effect_queue_drain` p99 2 ms) have no bench; `ProgramSimulator` (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/simulator.rs:85`) and the headless constructors can drive them.
- `FrameArena` bench exists: `crates/ftui-render/benches/arena_bench.rs` (1.4 KB).

## Target state

New/extended benches with these exact criterion ids:

1. `crates/ftui-core/benches/input_parser_bench.rs` (criterion, `harness = false`):
   - `input/parse_dispatch/mixed_event_stream/per_event`: a fixed byte corpus of 1,000 events (plain keys, CSI arrows, SS3 F-keys, kitty `CSI u` keys with modifiers, SGR mouse `\x1b[<0;10;5M`, bracketed paste of 2 KB, focus in/out, a 200-byte OSC reply); parse with the production parser and dispatch each `Event` through a minimal `Model::update` (a counter model) via the headless program's input path or the parser + a direct `update` call; `Throughput::Elements(1000)`; per-event time reported by criterion.
   - `input/parse/paste_64kb`: one 64 KB bracketed paste (guards pathological paste handling).
2. `crates/ftui-text/benches/wrap_bench.rs`:
   - `wrap/word/200_lines_80_cols`: 200 lines of mixed English prose (fixed corpus in the bench, ~60-120 chars each) wrapped at 80 with `WrapMode::Word`.
   - `wrap/word/200_lines_80_cols_unicode`: same with 30% CJK/emoji lines.
   - `wrap/optimal/200_lines_80_cols`: `wrap_text_optimal`.
3. `crates/ftui-render/benches/presenter_bench.rs` extended:
   - `present/truecolor/sparse_5pct/present/{80x24,120x40,200x60}` and `pipeline/truecolor/diff_and_present/full/{120x40,200x60}@5%` alongside the existing 80x24.
   - `present/bytes/sparse_5pct/{80x24,120x40,200x60}`: not a timing bench; at the end of the bench binary (`criterion_main` wrapper `fn main()` that runs criterion then the report), present one 5% frame through `CountingWriter`, compute `cells_changed`, `runs`, `bytes`, and write `target/regression-gate/bytes_report.json` `[{scene, cols, rows, cells_changed, runs, bytes, budget: 8*cells_changed+64, within_budget}]`. Also assert `within_budget()` from `CountingWriter` stats and print it.
4. `crates/ftui-runtime/benches/runtime_latency_bench.rs`:
   - `runtime/first_frame/headless_80x24`: time from headless `Program` construction to the first presented frame (measure with the existing evidence or a `CountingWriter` flush hook).
   - `runtime/shutdown_latency/headless`: quit message to `run()` return.
   - `runtime/command_roundtrip/cmd_msg`: `Cmd::msg` dispatch to model update completion (use `ProgramSimulator::inject_events` and step).
   - `runtime/effect_queue_drain/<backend>` is in `effect_backend_bench.rs` (`g24-impl-executor-default`); do not duplicate.
5. Allocation counting: feature `alloc-count` in `crates/ftui-render/Cargo.toml` and `crates/ftui-widgets/Cargo.toml` (bench-only): `crates/ftui-render/benches/alloc_count_bench.rs` registers a counting `#[global_allocator]` (wrapping `std::alloc::System`, `AtomicU64` counters for alloc/dealloc/realloc; safe code only) and renders two scenes into an 80x24 `Frame` with a `FrameArena` attached: `ascii_dashboard_80x24` (Block + Paragraph with 20 wrapped ASCII lines + a 10x3 Table + a status line) and `unicode_dashboard_80x24` (same with CJK/emoji text); counts allocations across `view + diff + present` per frame after a warm-up frame; writes `target/regression-gate/alloc_report.json` `[{scene, allocs_per_frame, bytes_per_frame, arena_bytes}]`; also runs the same scenes with `frame.arena = None` and records both so `g25-impl-arena`'s effect is visible in one report. `#[global_allocator]` is allowed under `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` (the `GlobalAlloc` impl delegates to `System`; implementing the trait requires `unsafe impl`, so this bench file carries `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` locally and is excluded from the crate's forbid by being a bench target with its own attribute; document this exception in the file header and in `g25-docs` since AGENTS.md says unsafe is forbidden; if the owner rejects the exception, use the `stats_alloc` crate or count via `FrameArena::allocated_bytes` plus a `Vec` capacity audit and record the substitute).
6. `Cargo.toml` `[[bench]]` entries with `harness = false` for each new file; `[features] alloc-count = []` where needed.

## Implementation plan

1. Write the corpora as `const` arrays inside each bench (no fixture files needed except the wrap prose, which can live in `crates/ftui-text/benches/fixtures/prose_200.txt`).
2. Implement the benches; run each via `rch exec -- cargo bench -p <crate> --bench <name> -- --quick`; confirm criterion ids match `tests/baseline.json` exactly (`ls target/criterion/`).
3. Implement the `bytes_report.json` and `alloc_report.json` writers; make paths overridable by `FTUI_PERF_REPORT_DIR`.
4. Run `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh --check-only` and fix id mismatches.
5. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` (benches compile under `--all-targets`), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`; `ubs` on the bench files.

What NOT to do: no `100x50`/`dense` benches invented to match the README (the README block is regenerated from real ids by `g25-impl-readme-numbers`); no unsafe outside the clearly-marked allocator bench; no benches in library `src/`.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-core/benches/input_parser_bench.rs`: new; `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml`: `[[bench]]`.
- `crates/ftui-text/benches/wrap_bench.rs` (+ `fixtures/prose_200.txt`): new; `crates/ftui-text/Cargo.toml`: `[[bench]]`.
- `crates/ftui-render/benches/presenter_bench.rs`: sizes + bytes report.
- `crates/ftui-render/benches/alloc_count_bench.rs`: new; `crates/ftui-render/Cargo.toml`: feature + bench.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/benches/runtime_latency_bench.rs`: new; `crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml`: `[[bench]]`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `ls target/criterion` after running all benches contains every `criterion_name` in `tests/baseline.json` (checked by `g25-tests` `baseline_criterion_ids_exist`).
- [ ] `target/regression-gate/bytes_report.json` shows `within_budget: true` for all three sizes; bytes for 80x24@5% under `8*96+64 = 832`.
- [ ] `target/regression-gate/alloc_report.json` has both scenes with and without arena (numbers recorded in the close reason as the pre-arena baseline).
- [ ] Per-event input dispatch mean under 100 µs on the CI runner (gate row passes).

## Tests and logging

- Bench binaries print one JSONL line per group to stderr `{bench, id, mean_ns, p50_ns, p99_ns}` (criterion estimates re-read from `target/criterion/<id>/new/estimates.json`) to make CI logs readable without the artifact.
- Unit tests in `g25-tests` cover the allocator counter (`counter_counts_box_alloc_and_free`) and the bytes budget formula.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: nothing (can start day one; `g25-impl` consumes its ids). Unblocks: `g25-impl`, `g25-impl-arena` (uses `alloc_report.json`), `g25-impl-readme-numbers`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- `CountingWriter::within_budget()` uses `expected_max_bytes`; the plan's budget `8 x changed cells + 64` is stricter and is the gate's formula; both are reported.
- Global-allocator counting is process-wide; the bench must run scenes single-threaded and subtract a measured baseline (empty frame) to avoid counting criterion's own allocations; report both raw and net.

## Definition of done

Benches exist with the exact ids, reports written, gate `--check-only` maps every row, pre-arena allocation numbers recorded, main green.

title: task(G25): FrameArena adoption for wrap spans, Flex rects and diff ChangeRun vectors
description:
## Context and why this matters

Vision row V29 ("Frame arena in hot path") is marked WORKING (light use): `FrameArena` is plumbed through `Frame` and reset by `Program` every frame, but only `TextInput` (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/input.rs:954-957`) and the showcase dashboard take storage from it. Meanwhile the three hottest per-frame temporary vectors (wrapped lines in `ftui-text`, solved rects in `Flex::split`, `ChangeRun` lists in the diff) still hit the system allocator every frame. The plan's "allocations per frame" budget therefore cannot reach zero for an ASCII scene. This bead adopts the arena in those three places, with the `alloc-count` bench from `g25-impl-benches` as the acceptance metric: `frame_allocations_ascii_scene` reaches 0 and a non-ASCII scene drops by at least half. Serves V29, V35, Section 2.2.F.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-render/src/arena.rs`: `pub type BumpVec<'a, T> = bumpalo::collections::Vec<'a, T>` (`:35`); `DEFAULT_ARENA_CAPACITY = 256 * 1024` (`:38`); `FrameArena::new(capacity)` (`:68`), `with_default_capacity` (`:75`), `reset` (`:84`, O(1), retains chunks), `alloc_str` (`:92`), `alloc_fmt` (`:100`), `alloc_slice<T: Copy>` (`:111`), `alloc_with` (`:119`), `alloc` (`:132`), `alloc_iter` (`:140`), `new_vec` (`:153`), `new_vec_with_capacity` (`:158`), `allocated_bytes` (`:171`), `as_bump` (`:187`).
- `crates/ftui-render/src/frame.rs:464-470` `pub arena: Option<&'a FrameArena>`; constructors set `arena: None` (`:489, :508, :533, :558`); `set_arena` (`:571`); `arena()` (`:579`).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs:4785-4786` `frame_arena: FrameArena`; `:6561-6572` reset then `frame.set_arena(&self.frame_arena)` before `view()`; `:6628-6634` same for the measurement pass; `:6124` memory guardrail adds `frame_arena.allocated_bytes()`; `:6150-6157` and `:6184-6190` rebuild the arena on memory alerts.
- Wrap: `crates/ftui-text/src/wrap.rs:113 pub fn wrap_text(text: &str, width: usize, mode: WrapMode) -> Vec<String>`; `:128 wrap_with_options(text, &WrapOptions) -> Vec<String>`; internal `split_lines_unwrapped` `:147`, `wrap_chars` `:157`, `wrap_words` `:193`, `split_words` `:331 -> Vec<&str>`, `kp_tokenize` `:713 -> Vec<KpWord>`, `wrap_text_optimal` `:933`. Every call allocates a `Vec<String>` plus one `String` per line. Consumers include `Paragraph` (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/paragraph.rs`, alignment at `:192`, render around `:358`) and the harness `minimal.rs`.
- Layout: `crates/ftui-layout/src/lib.rs:634 pub fn split(&self, area: Rect) -> Rects` and `:810 split_with_measurer`; `Rects` is the solved rect list (check its definition near `:600` when implementing; it wraps a `Vec<Rect>` or `SmallVec`).
- Diff: `crates/ftui-render/src/diff.rs:1246 pub struct ChangeRun`; `:1559 pub fn runs(&self) -> Vec<ChangeRun>`; `:1606 pub fn runs_into(&self, out: &mut Vec<ChangeRun>)`; `:4372` a reusable `runs_buf` in the presenter path. The diff itself is computed in `TerminalWriter` (runtime), which owns no arena reference today.
- Bench acceptance: `crates/ftui-render/benches/alloc_count_bench.rs` (`g25-impl-benches`) writes `target/regression-gate/alloc_report.json` with `allocs_per_frame` for `ascii_dashboard_80x24` and `unicode_dashboard_80x24`, with and without arena.

## Target state

1. Wrap: add arena-aware entry points that return borrowed slices instead of owned strings:
   - `pub fn wrap_text_in<'a>(arena: &'a FrameArena, text: &'a str, width: usize, mode: WrapMode) -> &'a [&'a str]` and `wrap_with_options_in<'a>(arena, text, &WrapOptions) -> &'a [&'a str]` in `wrap.rs`, implemented by the same algorithm producing `(start, end)` byte ranges into `text` collected in a `BumpVec<'a, &'a str>` (`arena.new_vec_with_capacity(estimated_lines)`), then `into_bump_slice()`. The existing `Vec<String>` functions become thin wrappers that map the slices to owned strings (they remain the API for callers without an arena; this is not a compatibility shim, it is the non-arena path). Word splitting (`split_words`, `kp_tokenize`) gets `_in` variants using `BumpVec` as well.
   - Because `ftui-text` depends on `ftui-render` only under the `markup` feature (`crates/ftui-text/Cargo.toml:17 markup = ["dep:ftui-render"]`), the arena type must not force that dependency: move `FrameArena` (and `BumpVec`) to `ftui-core` (`crates/ftui-core/src/arena.rs`, ftui-core already depends on `bumpalo` if `ftui-render` does; otherwise add it) and re-export from `ftui_render::arena` by `pub use ftui_core::arena::*` so `Frame.arena` keeps its type. `ftui-text` depends on `ftui-core` unconditionally (`Cargo.toml:26`).
   - `Paragraph::render` (`paragraph.rs`) uses `wrap_text_in` when `frame.arena()` is `Some`, else the owned path.
2. Layout: `Flex::split_in<'a>(&self, arena: &'a FrameArena, area: Rect) -> &'a [Rect]` (and `split_with_measurer_in`) building the solved list in a `BumpVec<Rect>`; `split` keeps returning `Rects` for arena-less callers. Widgets that call `Flex::split` inside `render` with a frame available (`Table`, `Block` children, the showcase dashboard, `Tabs`) switch to `split_in(frame.arena)` where an arena is present; do it in `Table` and `Paragraph`/`Block` first (they are in both bench scenes), then the dashboard.
3. Diff: `TerminalWriter` already keeps a reusable `runs_buf` on the presenter path (`diff.rs:4372`); make `BufferDiff::runs_into` the only path used per frame (no `runs()` allocation in production) and give `TerminalWriter` a persistent `Vec<ChangeRun>` cleared per frame (steady-state zero allocations without needing the arena, since the diff runs after `view()` and outside the `Frame` lifetime). If a `runs()` call remains on the present path, replace it.
4. Guardrail interplay: `program.rs:6124` counts `allocated_bytes()`; the arena grows with wrap output; set `DEFAULT_ARENA_CAPACITY` usage unchanged (256 KB) and verify the soft alert at `:6184` does not trip on the 200x60 unicode scene (log the number).
5. Acceptance: rerun `alloc_count_bench`; `ascii_dashboard_80x24` reports `allocs_per_frame == 0` with arena; `unicode_dashboard_80x24` at most half the pre-arena count recorded in `g25-impl-benches`'s close reason. Update `tests/baseline.json` rows `frame_allocations_ascii_scene` (budget 0) and `frame_allocations_unicode_scene` (budget = measured post-arena value + 10%).

## Implementation plan

1. Move `FrameArena` to `ftui-core` with re-export (one commit; run the workspace gates).
2. Implement `wrap_text_in` family with `BumpVec`; proptest equality with the owned path; wire `Paragraph`.
3. Implement `Flex::split_in`; wire `Table`, `Block`, `Tabs`, dashboard.
4. Diff: persistent runs buffer in `TerminalWriter`; remove per-frame `runs()`.
5. Run `alloc_count_bench` before/after each step; keep a table in the bead comments.
6. Snapshot suite (`cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase`, 419 insta snapshots + 7 goldens) must be unchanged; if any changes, that is a bug in the arena path, not a re-bless.
7. `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt`; `ubs`.

What NOT to do: no arena usage across frame boundaries (references die at `reset`); no `unsafe`; no changing wrap semantics; no re-blessing snapshots to hide differences; no deleting the owned-path functions.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-core/src/arena.rs` (moved from `crates/ftui-render/src/arena.rs`, via `git mv`) and `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs`, `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml` (`bumpalo`).
- `crates/ftui-render/src/arena.rs`: `pub use ftui_core::arena::*;` (or `lib.rs` re-export).
- `crates/ftui-text/src/wrap.rs`: `_in` variants.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/paragraph.rs`, `table.rs`, `block.rs`, `tabs.rs`: arena-aware wrap/split.
- `crates/ftui-layout/src/lib.rs`: `split_in`, `split_with_measurer_in`.
- `crates/ftui-render/src/diff.rs` / `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`: persistent runs buffer.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/dashboard.rs`: `split_in`.
- `tests/baseline.json`: allocation rows (coordinate with `g25-impl`).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `alloc_report.json`: `ascii_dashboard_80x24.allocs_per_frame == 0` (with arena); `unicode_dashboard_80x24` <= 50% of pre-arena.
- [ ] Proptests `wrap_in_equals_wrap_owned` and `flex_split_in_equals_split` pass (10k cases each).
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase` snapshots unchanged (no `.snap` diff in `git status`).
- [ ] `frame_render` and `present_*` gate rows do not regress (arena path should be faster; record deltas).

## Tests and logging

- Proptests above in `wrap.rs` and `ftui-layout/src/lib.rs` test modules; unit test `paragraph_uses_arena_when_present` (render with and without arena, buffer equality, `arena.allocated_bytes() > 0` in the arena case).
- Bench JSONL from `alloc_count_bench` per scene `{scene, arena: true|false, allocs_per_frame, bytes_per_frame, arena_bytes}`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g25-impl-benches` (acceptance metric). Unblocks: `g25-impl` baseline allocation rows finalization, `g25-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Moving `FrameArena` to `ftui-core` is the least invasive way to let `ftui-text` use it without a `markup`-feature dependency; alternative (feature-gating arena wrap behind `markup`) rejected because it would leave the default wrap path allocating.
- Lifetimes: `wrap_text_in` borrows `text` for `'a`; `Paragraph` owns its text for the frame, which is fine; callers that build strings on the fly must `arena.alloc_str` first.
- Risk: `bumpalo` `Vec` growth inside a 256 KB chunk for 200x60 unicode scenes; `allocated_bytes()` is logged and the guardrail rebuild path already exists.

## Definition of done

Zero allocations for the ASCII scene, halved for unicode, proptests and snapshots green, baseline rows set, numbers in the close reason, main green.
notes: Refinement 2: profile before expanding FrameArena adoption. Target measured allocations with observational parity and total-cost/peak-memory evidence; do not force arena usage into every listed data structure merely to make a call-count gate green. Reversible implementation and retained fallback satisfy scope without deleting code.

title: task(G25): render_perf_readme.py generates docs/perf/baseline_<date>.md and the README block
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:2086-2094 ("### Benchmark Suite") shows `cargo bench -p ftui-render` output "`diff/identical_100x50 time: [1.2 µs] throughput: [4.2 Mcells/s]`, `diff/sparse_5pct_100x50 time: [8.3 µs]`, `diff/dense_100x50 time: [45 µs]`". No such benchmark ids exist (`diff_bench.rs` uses `diff/identical/compute/80x24` etc., no 100x50, no `dense`), and the only checked-in results (`docs/profiling/opportunity_matrix_2026-02-03.md`, identical diff 1.81 µs at 80x24) do not match. Once the perf gate produces JSON artifacts (`g25-impl`), the README numbers must be generated from an artifact rather than typed, and the claims checker must detect when the block drifts from the artifact. This bead builds that pipeline. Serves V35, Section 2.2.C row "Benchmark numbers: regenerate (G25)".

## Current state (evidence)

- README.md:2086-2094 block (bash fence with three commented result lines).
- `docs/profiling/opportunity_matrix_2026-02-03.md` (19 KB, criterion + hyperfine tables at 80x24/120x40/200x60), `docs/profiling/baseline_metrics_2026-02-03.jsonl` (8.5 KB), `docs/perf/baseline_profiles.md` (19 KB): historical, hand-written.
- Gate artifact after `g25-impl`: `target/regression-gate/regression_report.jsonl` (per-row JSON: `run_id`, `ts`, `category`, `criterion_name`, `slo_metric`, `observed_mean_ns`, `baseline_p99_ns`, `threshold_pct`, `status`, `reason`), criterion estimates under `target/criterion/<id>/new/estimates.json` (`mean.point_estimate`, `median.point_estimate`, confidence intervals), plus `bytes_report.json` and `alloc_report.json` (`g25-impl-benches`).
- `scripts/check_readme_claims.py` (`g06-impl-ledger`) extracts backticked identifiers and numbers with units from README and requires ledger rows with proofs.
- `scripts/` naming convention: python helpers exist (`doctor_frankentui_replay_triage.py`, `doctor_frankentui_no_fake_gate.py`); `docs/perf/` holds dated markdown.

## Target state

- `scripts/render_perf_readme.py`: inputs `--report target/regression-gate/regression_report.jsonl --criterion-dir target/criterion --bytes target/regression-gate/bytes_report.json --allocs target/regression-gate/alloc_report.json --date YYYY-MM-DD --commit <sha> --machine "<runner label>"`; outputs (a) `docs/perf/baseline_<date>.md` with a header (date, commit, machine, toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml`, `cargo bench` command lines) and one table per group (present sizes p50/p99 vs budget, diff sizes, input dispatch, wrap, bytes per frame vs `8*cells+64`, allocations per scene with/without arena, runtime latencies); (b) the README block between markers `<!-- perf:begin -->` and `<!-- perf:end -->` rewritten in place with the same numbers (a `bash` fence showing real criterion ids and `time: [x µs]` lines, plus one line "Source: docs/perf/baseline_<date>.md, commit <sha>"); (c) a line `perf_block_sha256: <hash>` appended to `docs/claims-ledger.md`'s Benchmarks row (or a sidecar `docs/perf/README_BLOCK.sha256`) computed over the README block content.
- `scripts/check_readme_claims.py` verifies that the sha256 of the current README block equals the recorded hash and that `docs/perf/baseline_<date>.md` named in the block exists (so editing the block by hand fails CI).
- README markers inserted once by this bead around the Benchmark Suite block; the block content is generated.
- The generator is idempotent (running twice yields no diff) and refuses to run if the gate report has any `status: fail` row (numbers from a failing run must not be published).

## Implementation plan

1. Run the gate locally via rch to obtain a full artifact set (`./scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh --json`, not `--quick`, for publishable numbers).
2. Write `scripts/render_perf_readme.py` (stdlib only: `json`, `hashlib`, `argparse`, `pathlib`); it edits README only between the markers (this is a docs-block generator, not a code edit; AGENTS.md's script prohibition targets source code, and the block is machine-owned by design; state this in the script header).
3. Insert markers in README.md:2086-2094 replacing the fake numbers; run the generator; commit `docs/perf/baseline_<date>.md`.
4. Extend `check_readme_claims.py` with the hash check (coordinate with `g06-impl-ledger`; if that script is not merged, add `scripts/check_perf_block.py` with the same check and call it from the `docs` job; fold later).
5. Add a `perf-gate` job step (nightly only): run the generator in `--check` mode (regenerate to a temp file and diff against the README block; fail if they differ beyond a tolerance of 10% per number, which signals the published numbers are stale and should be regenerated by a human-reviewed PR).
6. `ubs` on the scripts.

What NOT to do: do not auto-commit README changes from CI; do not publish numbers from `--quick` runs; do not keep the 100x50/dense lines.

## Files to change

- `scripts/render_perf_readme.py`: new.
- `README.md`: markers at :2086-2094; generated block.
- `docs/perf/baseline_<date>.md`: generated report (first one committed by this bead).
- `docs/claims-ledger.md`: Benchmarks row with the block hash (or `docs/perf/README_BLOCK.sha256`).
- `scripts/check_readme_claims.py` (or `scripts/check_perf_block.py`): hash + existence check.
- `.github/workflows/perf.yml`: nightly `--check` step.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `python3 scripts/render_perf_readme.py ...` twice produces no diff the second time.
- [ ] README block lists only criterion ids that exist in `target/criterion/` (checked by `g25-tests` `readme_perf_block_ids_exist`).
- [ ] Hand-editing a number in the block makes `check_readme_claims.py` (or `check_perf_block.py`) fail (verified once, not committed).
- [ ] `docs/perf/baseline_<date>.md` committed; README block cites it and the commit.

## Tests and logging

- `scripts/render_perf_readme.py --self-test`: renders from fixture JSON under `tests/fixtures/perf/` (small report + estimates) into a temp README and compares to an expected block checked into the fixture dir; run by `g25-tests`.
- Logging: the script prints `{"rows": n, "groups": [...], "report": path, "readme_block_sha256": hash}` on success and a clear reason on refusal (failing gate rows).

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g25-impl` (gate artifact), `g25-impl-benches` (bytes/alloc reports). Coordinates with `g06-impl-ledger` (checker) and `g06-docs-readme` (README pass must keep the markers). Unblocks: `g25-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Publishing from a developer machine vs CI runner: numbers differ by hardware; the report header records the machine, and the README line says "on <machine>"; CI's nightly `--check` only flags drift beyond 10%, it does not overwrite.
- Alternative rejected: linking to criterion HTML reports as artifacts only. Artifacts expire; a dated markdown file in the repo is the durable proof the ledger needs.

## Definition of done

Generator, first dated report, README block with markers and hash, checker wired, nightly drift check in place; close reason cites the report path and hash.

title: task(G25): baseline/bench consistency, gate self-tests, arena transparency proptests
description:
## Context

Companion test bead for `g25-impl` (perf-gate job + baseline rows), `g25-impl-benches` (new benches, `alloc-count`), `g25-impl-arena` (arena adoption) and `g25-impl-readme-numbers` (generated README block). The promise under test is README.md:1259-1261/2086-2094 and the plan's budgets: present 80x24 p50 < 1 ms p99 < 3 ms, 120x40 p50 < 2 ms p99 < 6 ms, 200x60 p50 < 6 ms p99 < 18 ms, input parse+dispatch < 100 µs, wrap 200 lines < 2 ms, bytes O(changes), zero allocations on the ASCII path. Today `tests/baseline.json` rows can reference benches that do not exist without anything noticing, the gate script has no self-test, and nothing asserts that the README numbers come from an artifact. Serves V35, V29, Section 2.2.E/F.

## What to test

1. Baseline/bench consistency: every `criterion_name` in `tests/baseline.json` corresponds to a bench that exists (static check of bench sources plus a run-time check on `target/criterion`).
2. Gate script correctness: pass/fail/skip decisions on fixture inputs; `kind: bytes|allocs` rows; `pending_bead` reason; exit codes.
3. Allocation counter correctness and arena transparency (wrap/split equality with and without arena).
4. Bytes budget formula and `CountingWriter` accounting.
5. README block provenance (ids exist; hash matches; refusal on failing runs).

## Test types

Unit (Rust):
- `crates/ftui-render/src/counting_writer.rs`: `counting_writer_counts_and_resets` (exists? verify; add if missing), `within_budget_true_for_sparse_frame`, `bytes_budget_formula_8x_plus_64` (a helper `plan_bytes_budget(cells_changed) -> u64 = 8*cells+64` added next to `expected_max_bytes` and used by the bench).
- `crates/ftui-render/benches/alloc_count_bench.rs` (test module inside the bench or a small `#[cfg(test)]` in a `benches/support/alloc_counter.rs` shared file): `counter_counts_box_alloc_and_free` (one `Box::new` increments alloc by 1 and dealloc by 1), `counter_is_zero_for_stack_only_work`.
- `crates/ftui-text/src/wrap.rs`: proptest `wrap_in_equals_wrap_owned` (arbitrary unicode text up to 4 KB, width 1..200, all `WrapMode`s: `wrap_text_in(&arena, ..)` joined equals `wrap_text(..)`); `wrap_in_zero_heap_allocations_for_ascii` (under `alloc-count`, 200 ASCII lines, counter delta 0 apart from the arena's own chunk growth measured via `allocated_bytes`).
- `crates/ftui-layout/src/lib.rs`: proptest `flex_split_in_equals_split` (random constraint lists 0..16, random areas).
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/paragraph.rs`: `paragraph_uses_arena_when_present` (identical buffer output; `arena.allocated_bytes() > 0` only in the arena case).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`: `present_path_reuses_runs_buffer` (two consecutive presents; `runs_buf.capacity()` unchanged after the second; no `runs()` call on the path, asserted by a counter in test builds or by reviewing that `runs_into` is the only call site: `rg -n "\.runs\(\)" crates/ftui-runtime/src` returns nothing on the present path).

Static/script tests (`scripts/perf_gate_selftest.sh`, bash + python, run by the `check` job; small):
- `baseline_criterion_ids_exist`: for each `criterion_name` in `tests/baseline.json`, `rg -F "<group prefix>"` finds the group string in the named `bench_file` under `crates/<crate>/benches/` (prefix = text before the last `/` component; e.g. `present/truecolor/sparse_5pct/present` in `presenter_bench.rs`).
- `baseline_rows_have_declared_slo_metrics`: every `slo_metric` appears in `slo.yaml`.
- `gate_selftest_pass_fail_skip`: with a fixture `target/criterion` tree under `tests/fixtures/perf/criterion_ok/` (estimates below budget) the gate `--check-only` exits 0 and reports all `pass`; with `tests/fixtures/perf/criterion_regressed/` (one row 3x over p99) it exits 1 and the JSONL has exactly one `fail` naming that row; with a baseline row marked `_pending` the JSONL has `reason: pending_bead`.
- `gate_bytes_and_allocs_rows`: fixture `bytes_report.json`/`alloc_report.json` produce `pass` and, with `allocs_per_frame: 3` against budget 0, `fail`.
- `readme_perf_block_ids_exist`: every `<id> time:` line inside the README markers names an id present in `tests/baseline.json` or the fixture criterion tree.
- `render_perf_readme_selftest`: `python3 scripts/render_perf_readme.py --self-test` exits 0 (renders fixtures to a temp file and compares to `tests/fixtures/perf/expected_block.md`); `--report` with a failing row exits 2 with message "refusing to publish numbers from a failing gate run".

Bench (the gate itself): rows listed in `g25-impl`; the assertion is `observed_mean <= baseline_p99 * (1 + threshold_pct/100)` per row, `bytes <= 8*cells+64`, `allocs_per_frame <= budget`.

E2E: `g25-e2e` (job end to end with a deliberate regression).

## Logging

- Gate JSONL fields (per row): `run_id`, `ts`, `category`, `criterion_name`, `slo_metric`, `observed_mean_ns|bytes|allocs`, `baseline_p99_ns|budget`, `threshold_pct`, `status`, `reason`; summary line `SUMMARY total= passed= failed= skipped=`.
- Self-test prints one JSONL line per check `{"check","fixture","expected","actual","status"}`.
- Bench binaries emit `{bench, id, mean_ns, p50_ns, p99_ns}` per group to stderr.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-render/src/counting_writer.rs`, `crates/ftui-text/src/wrap.rs`, `crates/ftui-layout/src/lib.rs`, `crates/ftui-widgets/src/paragraph.rs`, `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`: tests above.
- `crates/ftui-render/benches/support/alloc_counter.rs` (+ tests): shared counter.
- `scripts/perf_gate_selftest.sh`: new.
- `tests/fixtures/perf/{criterion_ok,criterion_regressed}/**/estimates.json`, `bytes_report.json`, `alloc_report.json`, `expected_block.md`: fixtures.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `check` job: run `scripts/perf_gate_selftest.sh`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] All Rust tests above green (`cargo test -p ftui-render -p ftui-text -p ftui-layout -p ftui-widgets -p ftui-runtime`), with `--features alloc-count` for the allocation ones.
- [ ] `scripts/perf_gate_selftest.sh` exits 0 in the `check` job; the regressed fixture yields exactly one `fail`.
- [ ] `baseline_criterion_ids_exist` fails when a bogus `criterion_name` is added to `tests/baseline.json` (verified once, not committed).

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `g25-impl`, `g25-impl-benches`, `g25-impl-arena`, `g25-impl-readme-numbers`. Unblocks: `g25-e2e`, `g25-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Definition of done

Tests and self-test exist and run in CI; fixtures committed; close reason cites test names and the `check` job run id.

title: task(G25): perf_gate_e2e.sh proves a clean pass and a deliberate regression failure in CI
description:
## Context and why this matters

A perf gate that has never failed proves nothing. Section 2.2.E notes the current `benchmarks` job runs `bench_budget.sh --quick` only on main pushes with loosened envelopes, and `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh` is invoked by no workflow. `g25-impl` adds the `perf-gate` job; this bead proves it end to end: a clean run passes with a complete artifact, and a deliberately injected regression fails the job with a diagnosable report. It also verifies the artifact's JSONL against a schema so a "green" run cannot be an empty report. This is the Section 7.6 row "V35 perf: `perf-gate` job artifact and `docs/perf/baseline_<date>.md`".

## Current state (evidence)

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:294-338` `benchmarks` job: `run: ./scripts/bench_budget.sh --quick` (line 327), push-to-main only.
- `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh --json` writes `target/regression-gate/regression_report.jsonl` with rows `{run_id, ts, category, criterion_name, slo_metric, status, reason, ...}` (`:285-320`).
- No workflow runs the gate; no schema exists for its JSONL; `tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py` validates the E2E schema `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json` and can take a different schema file.
- `docs/perf/` holds dated markdown; no gate artifacts are archived.

## Target state

- `scripts/perf_gate_e2e.sh`:
  1. `clean` phase: runs `./scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh --quick --json` (via rch locally, plain cargo in CI); asserts exit 0; validates `regression_report.jsonl` against `tests/perf/regression_report_schema.json` (new schema: required fields per row, `status in {pass, fail, skip}`, `reason` required when `skip|fail`); asserts `SUMMARY failed=0` and `skipped` equals the count of `_pending` rows in `tests/baseline.json`; asserts `bytes_report.json` and `alloc_report.json` exist and validate.
  2. `regression` phase: copies `tests/baseline.json` to `$TMP/baseline_tight.json`, sets `present_80x24_sparse.p99_ns` to 1 (impossible budget), runs the gate with `BASELINE_FILE=$TMP/baseline_tight.json` (the script reads `BASELINE_FILE` from `PROJECT_ROOT`; add an env override `FTUI_PERF_BASELINE` to the script in `g25-impl` if it has none) in `--check-only` mode against the results from phase 1; asserts exit 1 and exactly one `fail` row for `present_80x24_sparse` with `observed_mean_ns > baseline_p99_ns`.
  3. `provenance` phase: `python3 scripts/render_perf_readme.py --check` (from `g25-impl-readme-numbers`) confirms the README block hash matches or reports drift (informational on PRs, failing nightly).
  4. Emits JSONL to `target/e2e/perf/<run_id>.jsonl` using `tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh` helpers and validates it with `validate_jsonl.py`.
- CI: the `perf-gate` job (from `g25-impl`) runs `scripts/perf_gate_e2e.sh` instead of calling the gate directly, so every run also exercises the failure path; artifacts: `target/regression-gate/`, `target/e2e/perf/`, criterion estimates.
- Archive: on nightly runs, the job commits nothing; `g42-impl` copies one artifact set into `docs/reports/reality-check-verification-<date>/`.

## Implementation plan

1. Write `tests/perf/regression_report_schema.json` (JSON Schema draft-07 subset understood by `validate_jsonl.py`; check its `TYPE_MAP` at `tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py:11-19`).
2. Add `FTUI_PERF_BASELINE` override to `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh` (one line at `:24`, `BASELINE_FILE="${FTUI_PERF_BASELINE:-$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/baseline.json}"`), if `g25-impl` did not.
3. Write `scripts/perf_gate_e2e.sh` (bash, `set -euo pipefail`, sources `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh` + `logging.sh`; no PTY needed).
4. Update the `perf-gate` job to call it; upload artifacts `if: always()`.
5. Run locally via rch; run in CI; capture run id.
6. `ubs` on the scripts.

What NOT to do: no modification of the tracked `tests/baseline.json` during the regression phase (copies only); no `continue-on-error`; no skipping the regression phase on PRs.

## Files to change

- `scripts/perf_gate_e2e.sh`: new.
- `tests/perf/regression_report_schema.json`: new.
- `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh`: `FTUI_PERF_BASELINE` override.
- `.github/workflows/perf.yml` (or the G04.12 advisory workflow): `perf-gate` job calls the E2E script.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `scripts/perf_gate_e2e.sh` exits 0 locally and in CI; phase 2 shows exactly one `fail` row for `present_80x24_sparse`.
- [ ] `target/e2e/perf/<run_id>.jsonl` validates; `regression_report.jsonl` validates against the new schema.
- [ ] `perf-gate` run id recorded in the close reason with the summary lines of both phases.

## Tests and logging

JSONL per phase/step: `run_id`, `ts`, `scenario` (`perf_gate`), `phase` (`clean|regression|provenance`), `step`, `rows_total`, `rows_passed`, `rows_failed`, `rows_skipped`, `failed_rows` (array of criterion names), `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, `artifact` (path), `status`. Driver: none (no PTY); the gate's own JSONL is the primary evidence; `validate_jsonl.py` output is captured in the log.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g25-impl`, `g25-impl-benches`, `g25-tests` (self-test fixtures reused for the schema). Unblocks: `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Running the regression phase in `--check-only` reuses phase-1 results, so the job cost is one bench run plus two script passes.
- Alternative rejected: a separate "prove it fails" workflow run only once. Exercising the failure path on every run guards the gate's own logic against drift.

## Definition of done

E2E script in the `perf-gate` job, both phases green, schemas committed, close reason cites run id and summary lines.

title: docs(G25): README benchmark/perf prose, docs/perf index, ledger rows, gate vs bench_budget
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:2086-2094 ("### Benchmark Suite") quotes benchmark ids and numbers that no bench produces; README.md:1259-1261 (FAQ "What's the performance like?") describes the degradation ladder with the wrong level names (Full -> SimpleBorders -> NoColors -> TextOnly; the code's `budget.rs` ladder is Full, SimpleBorders, NoStyling, EssentialOnly, Skeleton, SkipFrame per the audit's C-table; that row is owned by `g06-docs-readme`, but the performance FAQ paragraph is edited here); README.md:1527 ("## Math-Driven Performance") and the "Frame arena" claim (V29) describe the hot path. After `g25-impl`, `g25-impl-benches`, `g25-impl-arena` and `g25-impl-readme-numbers`, the truthful story is: a perf gate runs in CI against `tests/baseline.json`; the plan's budgets are rows in that file; README numbers are generated from a dated artifact; the arena carries wrap/layout/diff temporaries. This bead writes that into README, `docs/perf/README.md` (index), the claims ledger, and resolves the `bench_budget.sh` vs gate question in text. Serves V35, V29, Section 2.2.C (benchmark numbers row), 2.2.E, 2.2.F.

## Current state (evidence)

- README.md:2086-2094 block (fake `100x50`/`dense` ids; 1.2/8.3/45 µs).
- README.md:1259-1261 FAQ paragraph; README.md:1527-1650 "Math-Driven Performance" (mentions cost models, diff strategy, presenter cursor economy).

title: epic(G26): agent shell reference app: child process into scrollback under stable chrome
description:
## Context and why this matters

The original plan document (section 0.1) names one primary real-world target: a Claude Code / Codex-style agent harness session powered by ftui, where a child process streams output into scrollback while a stable chrome (status line, input box) stays put at the bottom of the terminal. README.md:49-53 (TL;DR) leads with "Inline mode with scrollback preservation and stable chrome", AGENTS.md:383 lists "Inline mode first: preserve scrollback while keeping chrome stable" as a key design decision, and `docs/tutorials/agent-harness.md:1-4` says "This tutorial shows how to build a Claude/Codex style agent harness using ftui" and points readers at `crates/ftui-harness/examples/minimal.rs` and `streaming.rs` "if you want working code right now". No in-tree application actually does what the target describes: `ftui-harness` is a test harness binary, `minimal.rs` is a 10-line `wrap_text` scratch, and `streaming.rs` pushes synthetic "Log line N" strings into a `LogViewer` widget inside the UI region instead of streaming a real child process into scrollback via `write_log`. This epic closes Section 2.2.F ("The primary real-world target ... has no in-tree consumer beyond `ftui-harness`, and no bead names one") and serves V1 (inline mode) by giving the flagship inline story a real consumer that the E2E suite hammers with 10,000 log lines.

Status arrow: PARTIAL -> WORKING. Complexity M. Would open beads close it? No.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui/` contains only `Cargo.toml` and `src/`; no `examples/` directory. `g01-impl` creates `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs` (the README Minimal API Example) and makes `App::new(m).run()` open a terminal under default features (today `AppBuilder::run()` returns `Err(Unsupported)` without `crossterm-compat`, `program.rs:7115`).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/process_subscription.rs:69` `pub struct ProcessSubscription<M: Send + 'static>` with fields `program`, `args`, `env`, `timeout`, `id`, `make_msg: Arc<dyn Fn(ProcessEvent) -> M>`; header: "wraps `std::process::Command` as a first-class runtime `Subscription`. It spawns a child process, captures stdout line-by-line, and sends messages to the model. When the subscription is stopped (via `StopSignal`), the child process is killed"; `ProcessEvent::Error(String)` variant at `:62`; builder `new(program, make_msg)` (`:106`), `.arg(..)`; `Command::new(&self.program)` at `:196`; reader join timeout 250 ms (`:83-84`).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs:2151` `pub fn write_log(&mut self, text: &str) -> io::Result<()>`: takes the one-writer lock, `sanitize(text)`, then `write_log_inline` for `Inline`/`InlineAuto` (scroll-region path parks the cursor at the region bottom so each LF scrolls only the log region and lines accumulate in scrollback, `:2185-2194`; overlay path erases and rewrites exactly one line, `:2196+`), and is a no-op in `AltScreen`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/log_sink.rs:40` `LogSink::new(&mut TerminalWriter<W>)` implements `Write`, buffers until `\n`, sanitizes each line and calls `write_log`.
- `crates/ftui-harness/examples/streaming.rs` (161 lines): `LogViewer`/`LogViewerState`, `StatusLine`, `Every` subscription, `ScreenMode`; synthetic lines, no child process.
- `scripts/e2e_test.sh` (invoked by no workflow; G04.14 wires it into `e2e-pty`): sources `tests/e2e/lib/{common,logging,pty}.sh`; scenarios large-screen (`run_large_case` `:749`), span-diff (`:845`), tile-skip (`:930`), selector-storm (`:1016`), budgeted refresh (`:1113`); flags `--quick`, `--no-large`, `--no-budget`, `--no-span`, `--no-tile`, `--no-selector`, `--trace-only`; uses `E2E_HARNESS_BIN`.
- Measured inline behavior under a PTY (kitty identity): DECSTBM set once, reset on exit, 25/25 sync pairs, cursor restored (audit Section 1); under most other identities no DECSTBM (owned by `g05-impl`).

## Target state

`crates/ftui/examples/agent_shell.rs`: an inline-mode app that spawns a command given on its command line (`cargo run -p ftui --example agent_shell -- <cmd> [args..]`, default `sh -c 'for i in $(seq 1 200); do echo line $i; sleep 0.01; done'`), streams the child's stdout and stderr into scrollback through `write_log` (sanitized by default; `--log-mode=sanitized|sgr-only|raw` selects `write_log`, `write_log_sgr_only`, `write_log_raw` from `g27-impl`), keeps a status line (child pid, lines received, bytes, elapsed, exit status) and a `TextInput` in a 3-row inline chrome, forwards typed lines to the child's stdin, forwards Ctrl-C to the child (SIGINT) and quits on a second Ctrl-C or `q` when the child has exited, handles resize, renders OSC 8 links for `http(s)://` tokens in the status line, and tears down cleanly (raw mode off, cursor shown, DECSTBM reset, no alt screen ever entered). The tutorial targets it and the README presents it as the flagship inline demo.

## Success criteria (block level)

- [ ] `scripts/e2e_test.sh` scenario `agent_shell_log_spam`: 10,000 log lines at full speed while the chrome stays stable; canonicalized transcript contains all 10,000 lines in order; zero `\x1b[2J`, `\x1b[3J`, `\x1b[?1049h` in the capture; teardown sequence present; JSONL log of frame counts and bytes (g26-e2e).
- [ ] Unit tests for the model (line accounting, Ctrl-C state machine, exit-status rendering) and a headless simulator test for the 10k-line update path (g26-tests).
- [ ] `docs/tutorials/agent-harness.md` Part 1 targets `agent_shell.rs`; README "Quick Example"/"Use Cases" name it (g26-docs).

## Plan (children)

1. `g26-impl`: the example (depends on `g01-impl` for a working `App::run()` under the facade's defaults and on `g27-impl` for the log modes).
2. `g26-tests`: unit + simulator tests.
3. `g26-e2e`: `agent_shell_log_spam` (and `agent_shell_injection`, shared with `g27-e2e` if that bead exists in the orchestrator's set; otherwise both scenarios live here).
4. `g26-docs`: tutorial retarget + README flagship.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g01-impl` (default backend), `g27-impl` (`write_log_raw`/`write_log_sgr_only`). Unblocks: `g42-impl` (Section 7.6 rows V1/V31/V49: "`agent_shell_log_spam` E2E").

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Why an example in `crates/ftui` rather than a new crate: the facade is what consumers depend on; an example there is compiled by `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, is doc-testable, and needs no new workspace member. `crates/ftui/examples/` is created by `g01-impl` for `minimal_inline.rs`; `agent_shell.rs` is the second file there, not a new variant of anything.
- Why not extend `ftui-harness/examples/streaming.rs`: it is a widget demo inside the UI region; the target requires scrollback streaming via `write_log`, which is a different path (`terminal_writer.rs:2185-2194`).
- Risk: stdin forwarding needs the child's stdin piped; `ProcessSubscription` captures stdout/stderr but may not expose stdin; if so, `g26-impl` adds `ProcessSubscription::with_stdin_channel()` (a `mpsc::Sender<String>` the model writes to) rather than a parallel process type.
- Risk: under the current identity policy (Section 2.2.D) the scroll-region path is inactive on WezTerm/iTerm2/xterm-256color; the E2E runs under the kitty identity so DECSTBM is exercised, and `g05-impl` widens that later.

## Definition of done

Example runs under the facade's default features, E2E scenario green in the `e2e-pty` job with JSONL artifacts, tests green, tutorial and README retargeted, claims-ledger rows present, main green.

title: feature(G26): crates/ftui/examples/agent_shell.rs with ProcessSubscription and Cmd::Log modes
description:
## Context and why this matters

The plan's primary target (section 0.1) is an agent-harness session: a child process streams into scrollback while a stable inline chrome holds a status line and an input box. README.md:49 leads with that story and `docs/tutorials/agent-harness.md:1-8` says working code exists in `crates/ftui-harness/examples/minimal.rs` and `streaming.rs`; neither spawns a process or writes to scrollback. This bead writes `crates/ftui/examples/agent_shell.rs`, the first in-tree consumer of the inline `write_log` path with a real child process, so the flagship promise is a program people can run and the E2E suite can hammer. Serves V1, Section 2.2.F; primary implementation bead of G26.

## Current state (evidence)

- Facade: `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs` (prelude; `g01-impl` adds `Widget`/`StatefulWidget` to the prelude and makes `App::new(m).screen_mode(..).run()` open the native backend on unix / crossterm elsewhere under default features; today `AppBuilder::run()` is a stub under `#[cfg(not(feature = "crossterm-compat"))]`, `program.rs:7115`). `crates/ftui/examples/` does not exist yet (created by `g01-impl`).
- Process subscription: `crates/ftui-runtime/src/process_subscription.rs:69-110`: `ProcessSubscription<M>` { `program`, `args`, `env`, `timeout`, `id`, `explicit_id`, `make_msg` }; `new(program, make_msg)`; `Command::new(&self.program)` at `:196`; stdout captured line by line; `ProcessEvent` variants include `Error(String)` (`:62`); child killed on `StopSignal`; reader join timeout 250 ms. Check whether `ProcessEvent` distinguishes stdout/stderr lines and exit status (read `:40-66`); add variants `Stdout(String)`, `Stderr(String)`, `Exited(i32)` if missing.
- Log path: `terminal_writer.rs:2151` `write_log(&mut self, text)` (sanitizes, one-writer lock, inline scroll-region or overlay, no-op in alt screen); `log_sink.rs:40` `LogSink` (line-buffered `Write` over `write_log`). `g27-impl` adds `write_log_raw`, `write_log_sgr_only`, `LogSink::raw()`.
- How a model reaches the writer for logs: the runtime exposes a log channel (`Cmd`/`Program` API; find the existing mechanism used by `ftui-harness/src/main.rs` for `FTUI_HARNESS_LOG_FILE` lines and by the showcase `inline_mode_story` screen; grep `write_log` callers in `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` and `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/inline_mode_story.rs` before writing the example). If no public `Cmd::log`-style path exists, add `Cmd::Log(LogText)` in `program.rs` with `LogText::{Sanitized(String), SgrOnly(String), Raw(String)}` dispatched to the three writer methods (this is the runtime API the example and the tutorial use; document it).
- Widgets: `TextInput` (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/input.rs`, arena-aware at `:954`), `StatusLine`/`StatusItem` (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/status_line.rs`, used by `streaming.rs:18`), `Block`, `Borders`; links via `Frame::register_link` (audit C-table) rendered as OSC 8 by the presenter.
- Ctrl-C: the runtime delivers `Event::Key` with `Modifiers::CTRL` + `'c'` when raw mode is on (verify in `crates/ftui-core/src/event.rs`); signals to the child need the pid: `std::process::Child::id()`; sending SIGINT without `unsafe` uses the `nix` or `rustix` crate already in the workspace (AGENTS.md "Key Dependencies" G06 row mentions `nix`/`rustix`); confirm which is a dependency of `ftui-runtime` and use `rustix::process::kill_process(Pid, Signal::Int)` or `nix::sys::signal::kill`.

## Target state

`crates/ftui/examples/agent_shell.rs` (~300 lines, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`):
- CLI: `agent_shell [--log-mode=sanitized|sgr-only|raw] [--ui-height=N] [--exit-when-child-exits] [--exit-after-ms=N] -- <cmd> [args..]`; defaults: `sanitized`, 3 rows, keep running after exit until `q`; env mirrors `FTUI_AGENT_SHELL_LOG_MODE`, `FTUI_AGENT_SHELL_EXIT_AFTER_MS` for E2E.
- Model `AgentShell { child: ChildState, lines: u64, bytes: u64, stderr_lines: u64, started: Instant, input: TextInputState, ctrl_c_armed: bool, log_mode: LogMode, last_error: Option<String>, links: Vec<String> }`; `ChildState::{Starting, Running { pid }, Exited { code, at }}`.
- `init()`: returns the `ProcessSubscription` for the command (stdout+stderr), `Every(250 ms)` tick for the elapsed clock; screen mode `Inline { ui_height }` with `.never_alt_screen()` if such a builder exists (assert in tests that no `1049h` is emitted).
- `update()`: `ProcessEvent::Stdout(line)` -> `Cmd::Log(mode.wrap(line))`, `lines += 1`, `bytes += line.len()+1`; `Stderr(line)` -> same with a dim `[stderr]` prefix in sanitized mode; `Exited(code)` -> status; `Key Enter` -> write the input line to the child's stdin (`ProcessSubscription::with_stdin()` returning a `Sender<String>`, added in `process_subscription.rs` if absent) and echo `> line` into scrollback; `Key Ctrl-C` while child running -> send SIGINT to the pid and set `ctrl_c_armed`; second Ctrl-C within 2 s or `q`/`Esc` when exited -> `Cmd::quit()`; `Resize` handled by the runtime.
- `view()`: row 1 status line (`pid`, `lines`, `bytes`, `elapsed`, `exit`, `mode`), with any `http(s)://` token from the last 200 lines registered as an OSC 8 link; row 2 `TextInput` in a `Block` with `Borders::TOP`; row 3 hint line (`Enter: send  Ctrl-C: interrupt child  q: quit`).
- Never clears the screen, never enters alt screen; teardown via the runtime's RAII.
- `Cargo.toml` of `crates/ftui`: `[[example]] name = "agent_shell" required-features = []` (must run under default features) and a `[dev-dependencies]` entry only if the example needs something the facade does not re-export (prefer re-exporting `ProcessSubscription`/`ProcessEvent` from `ftui::runtime` so the example uses `ftui::` paths only; that re-export is part of this bead).

## Implementation plan

1. Read `process_subscription.rs:1-260` and `program.rs` `Cmd` enum (`:325-373`); add `ProcessEvent::{Stdout, Stderr, Exited}` and `with_stdin()` if missing; add `Cmd::Log(LogText)` if no log command exists (tests in `g26-tests`).
2. Re-export `ProcessSubscription`, `ProcessEvent`, `LogText` from `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs` (`pub use ftui_runtime::{...}` in the `runtime` module).
3. Write the example; run `cargo run -p ftui --example agent_shell -- sh -c 'seq 1 200'` under the kitty identity in a PTY and by hand.
4. Verify teardown with `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` `pty_run` and grep for `\x1b[?25h`, `\x1b[r` (DECSTBM reset), absence of `\x1b[?1049h`.
5. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`; `ubs` on the new file and edited runtime files.

What NOT to do: no alt-screen mode option; no direct `stdout` writes from the model (one-writer rule, ADR-005); no `unsafe` for signals; no new crate; no `_v2` of `streaming.rs`.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui/examples/agent_shell.rs`: new example.
- `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`: `[[example]]`.
- `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`: re-exports.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/process_subscription.rs`: `Stdout/Stderr/Exited` events, `with_stdin()` (if absent).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `Cmd::Log(LogText)` (if absent) dispatching to `write_log`/`write_log_sgr_only`/`write_log_raw`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo run -p ftui --example agent_shell -- seq 1 10000` finishes with status `exit 0`, all 10,000 lines in scrollback (verified by `g26-e2e` canonicalized transcript), chrome intact.
- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui --example agent_shell` (unit tests inside the example, `g26-tests`) green.
- [ ] Under `FTUI_AGENT_SHELL_LOG_MODE=sanitized`, `printf '\x1b[2J'` from the child never reaches the wire (`g26-e2e`/`g27-e2e` injection scenario).
- [ ] No `\x1b[?1049h` in any capture; DECSTBM reset and cursor show present at exit.

## Tests and logging

- Unit tests: in `g26-tests` (line accounting, Ctrl-C state machine, status rendering, `LogText` wrapping per mode).
- Tracing: `target: "ftui.example.agent_shell"` info lines on spawn (`pid`), exit (`code`, `lines`, `bytes`), and Ctrl-C forwarding; `RUST_LOG=ftui.example.agent_shell=info` documented in the file header.
- E2E JSONL: `g26-e2e`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g01-impl` (facade default backend + `examples/` dir), `g27-impl` (log modes). Unblocks: `g26-tests`, `g26-e2e`, `g26-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Stdin forwarding via a channel keeps `ProcessSubscription` the single process abstraction; a separate writer thread owned by the subscription writes lines to the child's stdin and closes it on stop.
- If `Cmd::Log` already exists under another name (check `program.rs` and the showcase inline story), use it; do not add a duplicate.
- Rollback: the example is additive.

## Definition of done

Example merged and runnable under default features; runtime additions tested; E2E scenario green; close reason cites the E2E run id and test names; main green.

title: task(G26): agent shell model, process subscription and headless 10k-line tests
description:
## Context

Companion test bead for `g26-impl` (`crates/ftui/examples/agent_shell.rs` plus the runtime additions `ProcessEvent::{Stdout,Stderr,Exited}`, `ProcessSubscription::with_stdin()`, `Cmd::Log(LogText)`). The promise is the plan's primary target: a child process streams into scrollback under a stable inline chrome, with Ctrl-C forwarding and crash-safe teardown (README.md:49, AGENTS.md:383, `docs/tutorials/agent-harness.md:1-4`). Nothing in-tree tests that path today; `crates/ftui-harness/examples/streaming.rs` exercises a `LogViewer` widget, not `write_log` scrollback, and `process_subscription.rs` tests (if any) do not cover stdin or exit codes. 1. Model logic without a terminal: line/byte accounting, stderr tagging, exit-status transitions, Ctrl-C arming and quit rules, log-mode wrapping.
2. Runtime additions: `ProcessSubscription` delivers `Stdout`/`Stderr`/`Exited` in order and honors stdin writes; `Cmd::Log` reaches the writer's three methods.
3. Headless throughput: 10,000 `Stdout` events through `update()` under the `ProgramSimulator` complete within a budget and produce exactly 10,000 log commands.
4. Wire invariants (headless writer): with `ScreenMode::Inline`, the emitted bytes never contain `\x1b[2J`, `\x1b[3J`, `\x1b[?1049h` (the `inline_never_clears_screen` proptest from `g27-tests` covers the writer generically; here a targeted test covers this example's command stream).

## Test types

Unit (inside `crates/ftui/examples/agent_shell.rs` under `#[cfg(test)]`, run with `cargo test -p ftui --example agent_shell`):
- `stdout_line_increments_counters`: `update(ProcessEvent::Stdout("abc"))` -> `lines == 1`, `bytes == 4`, returns one `Cmd::Log(LogText::Sanitized("abc"))`.
- `stderr_line_is_tagged_in_sanitized_mode`: returns `LogText::Sanitized("[stderr] warn")` and `stderr_lines == 1`.
- `exit_event_sets_state_and_status_text`: `Exited(3)` -> `ChildState::Exited { code: 3, .. }`; `view()` into an 80x3 `Buffer` (headless `Frame`) shows `exit 3`.
- `ctrl_c_first_forwards_second_quits`: first Ctrl-C while `Running` returns a `Cmd` that calls the signal hook (inject a `Box<dyn Fn(u32)>` signal sender in the model for testability) and sets `ctrl_c_armed`; second within 2 s returns `Cmd::quit()`; a Ctrl-C after 2 s re-arms instead.
- `q_quits_only_after_child_exited`: `q` while running is forwarded to stdin as text; after `Exited`, `q` quits.
- `enter_sends_input_line_and_echoes`: input "ls" + Enter -> stdin sender receives "ls\n" and a `Cmd::Log(Sanitized("> ls"))` is returned; input cleared.
- `log_mode_wraps_correctly`: `LogMode::SgrOnly` -> `LogText::SgrOnly`, `Raw` -> `LogText::Raw`.
- `links_extracted_from_recent_lines`: a line containing `https://example.com/x` registers one link; the status view calls `frame.register_link` once (assert via the frame's link registry length).

Unit (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/process_subscription.rs`):
- `process_subscription_delivers_stdout_stderr_exit_in_order`: spawn `sh -c 'echo out; echo err 1>&2; exit 7'`; collect events until `Exited(7)`; assert `Stdout("out")`, `Stderr("err")`, `Exited(7)` (order between out/err may interleave; assert exit is last and both lines present).
- `process_subscription_forwards_stdin`: spawn `cat`; send "hello\n" via `with_stdin()` sender; expect `Stdout("hello")`; stop -> child killed, `Exited` or stop observed within 1 s.
- `process_subscription_kills_child_on_stop`: spawn `sleep 30`; stop; assert the pid is gone within 500 ms (`kill -0` via `rustix`/`nix`, no unsafe).

Unit (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`):
- `cmd_log_dispatches_to_writer_modes`: headless program with a `Vec<u8>` writer in `Inline { ui_height: 3 }`; `Cmd::Log(Sanitized("a\x1b[31mb"))` emits `ab` (escape stripped); `SgrOnly("a\x1b[31mb\x1b[2J")` emits `\x1b[31m` but not `\x1b[2J`; `Raw("\x1b[31mz")` emits it verbatim.

Simulator (`crates/ftui/tests/agent_shell_sim.rs`, uses the example's model via `#[path = "../examples/agent_shell.rs"] mod agent_shell;`):
- `ten_thousand_lines_headless_under_budget`: `ProgramSimulator` with the model; inject 10,000 `Stdout` events (as `Msg`), step; assert `lines == 10_000`, 10,000 log commands executed, wall clock < 2 s (informational on CI; hard assert < 10 s).
- `inline_writer_never_clears_screen_for_agent_shell_stream`: headless `TerminalWriter` over `Vec<u8>` (kitty capability profile), replay the 10,000 log lines plus 50 presents; assert no `\x1b[2J`, `\x1b[3J`, `\x1b[?1049h`; count DECSTBM set/reset (1 set, 1 reset at teardown).

Bench: none beyond `g25` rows (the E2E logs throughput).

E2E: `g26-e2e`.

## Logging

- Tests use `tracing_subscriber::fmt().with_test_writer()` with `RUST_LOG=ftui.example.agent_shell=debug,ftui.runtime=info`.
- The simulator test prints `{"test":"ten_thousand_lines_headless_under_budget","lines":10000,"elapsed_ms":n}`.
- Wire-invariant test prints escape tallies `{"clear_2j":0,"clear_3j":0,"alt_1049h":0,"decstbm_set":1,"decstbm_reset":1,"sync_pairs":n}` on failure.

## Files

- `crates/ftui/examples/agent_shell.rs`: `#[cfg(test)]` module.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/process_subscription.rs`: three tests.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `cmd_log_dispatches_to_writer_modes`.
- `crates/ftui/tests/agent_shell_sim.rs`: new.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui --example agent_shell`, `cargo test -p ftui --test agent_shell_sim`, `cargo test -p ftui-runtime process_subscription`, `cargo test -p ftui-runtime cmd_log_dispatches` all green.
- [ ] Wire-invariant tallies as above.
- [ ] Tests run under `cargo nextest` with the per-test timeout from `g03-impl` (none exceeds 60 s).

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `g26-impl`, `g27-impl` (writer modes). Unblocks: `g26-e2e`, `g26-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Definition of done

All named tests exist and pass in CI; close reason lists them with the run id.
