title: epic(G27): finish the untrusted-output policy: raw/SGR-only opt-in, adversarial PTY tests
description:
## Context and why this matters

`docs/adr/ADR-006-untrusted-output-policy.md` (Status: PROPOSED) decides "Sanitize by default: any text flowing through log paths or user-provided content is sanitized. Raw passthrough is explicitly opt-in", sketches the API as "`write_log(...)` / `Text::sanitized(...)` are safe by default; `write_raw(...)` / `Text::raw(...)` require explicit opt-in", names an "Optional semi-trusted mode (future): allow SGR-only", and sets a test plan: "PTY tests that feed adversarial sequences into logs and assert terminal invariants. Fuzz tests with random bytes for log paths. Tests ensuring no state leakage after malicious content." `docs/risk-register.md` R2 ("ANSI/OSC injection via untrusted content", Critical) lists "Explicit raw opt-in `write_raw()`: Designed" and "Adversarial PTY tests: Planned" while its summary table says R2 is "Mitigated". The kernel invariant "inline never clears the full screen" (plan-doc Definition of Done) has no named test. This epic closes Section 2.2.F rows "`write_raw()` / semi-trusted SGR passthrough: not started", "Adversarial escape-injection PTY tests: unit-level only", and "'Inline never clears full screen' invariant has no named test", and serves V1/V4 (inline mode, cleanup) and the README "Agent harness" use case where tool output and LLM streams are untrusted by definition. User-visible consequence today: an agent harness built on ftui cannot show colored tool output at all (everything is stripped), and nobody has demonstrated under a real PTY that a hostile child cannot clear the screen, retitle the window, or exfiltrate the clipboard through the log path.

Status arrow: PARTIAL -> WORKING. Complexity M. Would open beads close it? No.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs:2151-2172` `pub fn write_log(&mut self, text: &str) -> io::Result<()>`: `let _output_guard = terminal_output_lock();` then "Defense in depth: callers usually sanitize before logging, but the terminal writer is the final emission boundary and must never pass through escape/control injection payloads." `let sanitized = sanitize(text);` and dispatch to `write_log_inline` (`Inline`, `InlineAuto`) or `Ok(())` in `AltScreen`. `write_log_inline` (`:2179+`): scroll-region path (`scroll_region_active`, `position_cursor_for_log`, write bytes, flush) or overlay path (erase-and-rewrite one width-clamped line anchored on `last_inline_region`; "never emit an unscoped LF").
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/log_sink.rs:40-78` `LogSink<'a, W>`: `new(&mut TerminalWriter<W>)`; `Write::write` splits on `\n`, `sanitize(&line)`, `self.writer.write_log(&format!("{}\n", safe_line))`; `flush` sanitizes the partial line; `Drop` flushes.
- `crates/ftui-render/src/sanitize.rs`: header documents the threat model (cursor manipulation, persistent mode changes, fake prompts, exfiltrating queries, window title) and performance (memchr fast path, zero allocation when no ESC); `:69 pub fn sanitize(input: &str) -> Cow<'_, str>`; `:319 pub enum Text<'a>` with `sanitized` (`:331`), `trusted` (`:341`), `sanitized_owned`, `trusted_owned`, `as_str`, `is_sanitized`, `is_trusted`, `into_owned`. `Text::trusted` exists as a marker but the writer sanitizes regardless of it.
- `rg -n "write_raw|write_log_raw|sgr_only" crates --glob "*.rs"` returns nothing.
- Adversarial coverage is unit-level in `sanitize.rs` tests; no harness test feeds payloads through a PTY. `crates/ftui-harness/tests/` has `proptest_flicker_invariants.rs` (references `1049h`/`2J` for flicker invariants), `pty_terminal_lifecycle.rs` (2.9 KB), `e2e_flicker_free_round_trip.rs`, `no_flicker_fault_invariant.rs`, `sync_bracket_completeness_proof.rs`, `render_no_flicker_proof.rs`; none is named for the inline-never-clears invariant.
- `crates/ftui-render/src/terminal_model.rs` is the terminal state model used by presenter correctness tests (risk register R1 "Terminal model tests").
- Risk register R2 beads: bd-397 "Create adversarial tests for escape injection" (closed per the tracker's 2,732 closed beads, yet the register still says Planned).

## Target state

- `TerminalWriter::write_log_raw(&mut self, text: &str)` (explicit opt-in, documented as dangerous, still under the one-writer lock and still routed through the inline log region so the chrome rules hold) and `TerminalWriter::write_log_sgr_only(&mut self, text: &str)` (semi-trusted: keeps `CSI ... m` SGR sequences, strips everything else including OSC/DCS/APC/C1 and cursor CSIs); `LogSink::raw(&mut writer)` and `LogSink::sgr_only(&mut writer)` constructors; `sanitize_sgr_only(input) -> Cow<str>` in `ftui-render/src/sanitize.rs`; `Text::trusted` honored by a `write_log_text(&Text)` entry that dispatches on the marker.
- `crates/ftui-harness/tests/pty_injection_adversarial.rs` feeds ESC/CSI/OSC/DCS/APC/C1 payloads through each log mode under a PTY and asserts the terminal model is unchanged (title, modes, cursor position, alt screen, scroll region) and no full-clear sequences appear (sanitized and sgr-only modes).
- `inline_never_clears_screen` proptest over harness scenarios asserts no `\x1b[2J`, `\x1b[3J`, `\x1b[?1049h` in inline mode for arbitrary sequences of presents, resizes and log writes.
- ADR-006 status Accepted with the delivered API names; risk register R2 rows say Implemented with test names.

## Success criteria (block level)

- [ ] `write_log_raw`, `write_log_sgr_only`, `LogSink::raw`, `LogSink::sgr_only`, `sanitize_sgr_only` exist with unit tests (g27-impl, g27-tests).
- [ ] `crates/ftui-harness/tests/pty_injection_adversarial.rs` green on ubuntu and macos (g27-tests).
- [ ] `inline_never_clears_screen` proptest green (g27-tests).
- [ ] ADR-006 Accepted; risk register R2 rows updated (g27-docs).
- [ ] PTY-level scenario `agent_shell_injection` green (in `g26-e2e`).

## Plan (children)

1. `g27-impl`: the writer/sink/sanitizer additions.
2. `g27-tests`: unit + proptest + harness PTY adversarial test + fuzz target extension.
3. `g27-docs`: ADR-006 acceptance, risk register, README "Untrusted output" paragraph, ledger rows.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: nothing (day-one parallel track). Unblocks: `g26-impl` (agent shell log modes), `g34-impl` (ADR/risk-register truth depends on this landing), `g42-impl` (Section 7.6 row F: "`write_raw` tests").

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Naming: ADR-006 sketches `write_raw`; the delivered names are `write_log_raw`/`write_log_sgr_only` because they share `write_log`'s region discipline (the raw variant is raw with respect to sanitization, not with respect to where it writes). The ADR text is updated to the real names in `g27-docs`; the ledger records the rename.
- SGR-only allowlist must reject `CSI ? ... h/l` (DEC private modes), `CSI ... J/K` (clears), `CSI ... H/f` (cursor), OSC 0/2 (title), OSC 52 (clipboard), OSC 8 (links; decision: strip in sgr-only, since a hostile link target is a phishing vector; links come from the app's own `Frame::register_link`), DCS/APC/PM/SOS, and C1 8-bit introducers (`0x9B`, `0x9D`, `0x90`, `0x9F`).
- Raw mode is deliberately unpleasant to reach (a separate method name, a doc warning, no env var to enable it globally).

## Definition of done

API landed and tested, PTY adversarial and invariant tests green in CI, ADR-006 Accepted, risk register truthful, ledger rows present, main green.

title: feature(G27): write_log_raw, write_log_sgr_only, LogSink::raw/sgr_only, sanitize_sgr_only
description:
## Context and why this matters

ADR-006 ("Untrusted Output Policy", Status PROPOSED) promises "Raw passthrough is explicitly opt-in" via `write_raw(...)`/`Text::raw(...)` and an "Optional semi-trusted mode (future): allow SGR-only". Today only the sanitized half exists: `TerminalWriter::write_log` and `LogSink` strip every escape, and there is no opt-in at all (`rg "write_raw|sgr_only" crates` is empty). An agent harness (the plan's primary target, `g26-impl`) therefore cannot display a compiler's colored diagnostics or a test runner's green/red output without losing all styling. This bead adds the two opt-in modes and the SGR-only sanitizer, keeping the one-writer rule and the inline log-region discipline for every mode. Serves Section 2.2.F ("`write_raw()` / semi-trusted SGR passthrough: not started"), V1; primary implementation bead of G27.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs:2151-2172`:
  ```rust
  pub fn write_log(&mut self, text: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
      let _output_guard = terminal_output_lock();
      let sanitized = sanitize(text);
      let text = sanitized.as_ref();
      match self.screen_mode {
          ScreenMode::Inline { ui_height } => self.write_log_inline(ui_height, text),
          ScreenMode::InlineAuto { .. } => { let ui_height = self.effective_ui_height(); self.write_log_inline(ui_height, text) }
          ScreenMode::AltScreen => Ok(()),
      }
  }
  ```
  `write_log_inline(&mut self, ui_height, text)` at `:2179`: `visible_height = ui_height.min(self.term_height)`; returns `Ok(())` when the UI fills the terminal; scroll-region path (`self.scroll_region_active`: `position_cursor_for_log(visible_height)`, `write_all(text.as_bytes())`, `flush`); overlay path anchored on `self.ui_anchor`/`last_inline_region` erasing and rewriting one width-clamped line.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/log_sink.rs:34-78`: `LogSink { writer: &'a mut TerminalWriter<W>, buffer: Vec<u8> }`; `new`; `Write::write` sanitizes per line and calls `write_log(&format!("{}\n", safe_line))`; `flush` sanitizes the partial line; `Drop` flushes.
- `crates/ftui-render/src/sanitize.rs:69 pub fn sanitize(input: &str) -> Cow<'_, str>`; strategy STRIP; `Text<'a>` enum (`:319`) with `sanitized`/`trusted` constructors and `is_trusted` (`:380`); the writer never consults `Text`.
- ADR-006 "What Gets Sanitized": ESC and all CSI/OSC/DCS/APC; C0 except TAB/LF/CR.
- The overlay path width-clamps by display width; raw text containing escapes has display width smaller than byte length, so the clamp must operate on the sanitized-width or the raw path must skip clamping (decision below).

## Target state

1. `crates/ftui-render/src/sanitize.rs`:
   - `pub fn sanitize_sgr_only(input: &str) -> Cow<'_, str>`: same memchr fast path; in the slow path, keep sequences matching exactly `ESC [ <params> m` where `<params>` is `[0-9;:]*` (covers `38;2;r;g;b`, `38:2::r:g:b`, `4:3` underline styles) and at most 64 bytes; strip every other ESC-introduced sequence (CSI with any other final byte, OSC/DCS/APC/PM/SOS with ST or BEL terminators, single-char ESC sequences like `ESC 7`/`ESC c`), strip C1 controls (`0x80..=0x9F` as UTF-8 `U+0080..U+009F`), strip C0 except TAB/LF/CR. Return `Cow::Borrowed` when nothing is removed.
   - `pub enum SanitizeMode { Strip, SgrOnly, Raw }` and `pub fn sanitize_with(input, mode) -> Cow<str>` (Raw returns Borrowed unchanged) so callers and tests share one dispatch.
   - `Text<'a>` gains `Text::sgr_only(&str)` (marker) and `pub fn mode(&self) -> SanitizeMode` (`sanitized -> Strip`, `sgr_only -> SgrOnly`, `trusted -> Raw`).
2. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`:
   - Refactor `write_log` into `fn write_log_with_mode(&mut self, text: &str, mode: SanitizeMode)`; `write_log` = `Strip`; new `pub fn write_log_sgr_only(&mut self, text)` = `SgrOnly`; new `pub fn write_log_raw(&mut self, text)` = `Raw`, with a doc comment: "Bypasses sanitization. The caller asserts the text is trusted. Escape sequences in `text` can move the cursor, change modes, or clear the screen; the inline chrome guarantees no longer hold for this call. Prefer `write_log_sgr_only`." Also `pub fn write_log_text(&mut self, text: &Text<'_>)` dispatching on `text.mode()`.
   - Overlay-path clamping: compute the clamp on the display width of the sanitized (`Strip`) projection while emitting the mode's bytes, so SGR-only lines are clamped by visible width; for `Raw`, skip clamping and document it.
   - Every mode holds `terminal_output_lock()` and goes through `write_log_inline` (region discipline preserved); `AltScreen` remains a no-op for all modes.
   - Emit a `tracing::debug!(target: "ftui.runtime.log", mode = "raw", bytes = n)` on every raw write (so an operator can see raw usage in logs).
3. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/log_sink.rs`: `LogSink { writer, buffer, mode: SanitizeMode }`; `new` (Strip), `pub fn sgr_only(writer)`, `pub fn raw(writer)`; `write`/`flush` call `writer.write_log_with_mode(&line, self.mode)` (make `write_log_with_mode` `pub(crate)`); remove the double sanitization (`LogSink` currently sanitizes and then `write_log` sanitizes again; single pass at the writer is the boundary, per the writer's own "final emission boundary" comment).
4. `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`: re-export `SanitizeMode`, `Text` (if not already) so consumers reach them via `ftui::`.

## Implementation plan

1. `sanitize.rs`: implement `sanitize_sgr_only` and `sanitize_with` next to `sanitize`; reuse its scanner (factor the sequence-boundary parser into a private `fn next_sequence(bytes, i) -> (SeqKind, end)` used by both strip and sgr-only; keep the fast path).
2. `terminal_writer.rs`: refactor as above; keep `write_log`'s public signature.
3. `log_sink.rs`: add mode field and constructors; drop the redundant per-line `sanitize`.
4. Unit tests (`g27-tests`); run `cargo test -p ftui-render -p ftui-runtime`.
5. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`; `ubs` on the three files.

What NOT to do: no global env var that turns raw on for everything (`FTUI_LOG_RAW=1` would defeat the ADR); no `write_raw` that bypasses the log region (a raw write to arbitrary screen positions would break the one-writer discipline for the UI region too); no new file; no compatibility alias named `write_raw` (the ledger records the name).

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-render/src/sanitize.rs`: `sanitize_sgr_only`, `SanitizeMode`, `sanitize_with`, `Text::sgr_only`, `Text::mode`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`: `write_log_with_mode`, `write_log_sgr_only`, `write_log_raw`, `write_log_text`, clamp handling, raw tracing.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/log_sink.rs`: `mode`, `sgr_only()`, `raw()`.
- `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`: re-exports.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `sanitize_sgr_only("a\x1b[31mb\x1b[2Jc\x1b]0;t\x07d") == "a\x1b[31mbcd"`; `sanitize_sgr_only("plain")` is `Cow::Borrowed`.
- [ ] Headless writer tests: `write_log_sgr_only` emits SGR bytes and no `\x1b[2J`; `write_log_raw` emits `\x1b[2J` verbatim (documenting that raw is raw); `write_log` emits neither.
- [ ] `LogSink::sgr_only` over multi-line input with a split escape across two `write` calls still strips correctly (buffered per line).
- [ ] `g27-tests` PTY adversarial test and `inline_never_clears_screen` proptest green.

## Tests and logging

Details in `g27-tests`. Logging: `ftui.runtime.log` debug line per raw write (`mode`, `bytes`); no logging on the sanitized fast path (performance).

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: nothing. Unblocks: `g26-impl`, `g27-tests`, `g27-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- SGR-only still allows an attacker to set colors that persist until the next reset; the writer emits `\x1b[0m` after every sgr-only line (documented) so styling cannot leak into the chrome.
- Overlay clamping by visible width: compute `display_width(strip(text))` once per line; SGR bytes are zero-width.
- Alternative rejected: implementing SGR-only inside `LogSink` only. The writer is the emission boundary; every mode must live there.

## Definition of done

Three modes implemented at the writer, sink constructors present, tests green, `ubs` clean, close reason lists test names; main green.

title: task(G27): pty_injection_adversarial.rs, inline_never_clears_screen proptest, sgr-only fuzz
description:
## Context

Companion test bead for `g27-impl` (`write_log_raw`, `write_log_sgr_only`, `LogSink::{raw,sgr_only}`, `sanitize_sgr_only`). The promises under test are ADR-006's test plan ("PTY tests that feed adversarial sequences into logs and assert terminal invariants. Fuzz tests with random bytes for log paths. Tests ensuring no state leakage after malicious content"), the risk register R2 rows ("Adversarial PTY tests: Planned"), and the plan-doc kernel invariant "inline never clears the full screen", which the audit notes "has no named test" (Section 2.2.F). Today adversarial coverage is unit-level inside `crates/ftui-render/src/sanitize.rs`; `crates/ftui-harness/tests/proptest_flicker_invariants.rs` mentions `1049h`/`2J` for flicker, not for the log path. Serves V1, V4, Section 2.2.F.

## What to test

1. Sanitizer correctness for all three modes over a curated adversarial corpus and under fuzzing.
2. Writer behavior per mode in both inline paths (scroll-region active, overlay) and in alt screen (no-op).
3. Terminal-model invariance: after feeding payloads through the sanitized and sgr-only paths under a real PTY, the terminal's title, DEC private modes, scroll region, cursor visibility and alt-screen state equal a control run.
4. The inline-never-clears invariant across arbitrary present/resize/log sequences.
5. Sink line-buffering with escapes split across writes.

## Test types

Unit (`crates/ftui-render/src/sanitize.rs`):
- `sgr_only_keeps_sgr_strips_rest`: corpus table with expected outputs: `\x1b[31m` kept; `\x1b[38;2;1;2;3m` kept; `\x1b[4:3m` kept; `\x1b[2J`, `\x1b[3J`, `\x1b[H`, `\x1b[?1049h`, `\x1b[?25l`, `\x1b[r`, `\x1b[2;10r` stripped; `\x1b]0;evil\x07`, `\x1b]52;c;aGk=\x07`, `\x1b]8;;http://x\x1b\\` stripped; `\x1bP+q\x1b\\` (DCS), `\x1b_Gf=100\x1b\\` (APC), `\x1b^pm\x1b\\`, `\x1bXsos\x1b\\` stripped; `\x1b7`, `\x1bc` stripped; C1 `\u{9b}2J`, `\u{9d}0;t\u{9c}` stripped; C0 `\x07`, `\x08`, `\x0c` stripped, TAB/LF/CR kept; an SGR longer than 64 bytes stripped; an unterminated `\x1b[31` at end of input stripped.
- `sgr_only_fast_path_borrows`: no ESC -> `Cow::Borrowed`.
- Proptest `sanitize_modes_are_idempotent_and_ordered`: for arbitrary byte strings (as lossy UTF-8), `strip(strip(x)) == strip(x)`, `sgr(sgr(x)) == sgr(x)`, `strip(sgr(x)) == strip(x)`, and `strip(x)` contains no `0x1b`, no C1, no C0 except `\t\n\r`.
- Proptest `sgr_only_output_contains_only_sgr_escapes`: every `\x1b` in the output is followed by `[`, params `[0-9;:]*`, then `m`.

Fuzz (`fuzz/fuzz_targets/sanitize_sgr_only.rs`, new target beside the existing parser targets; built by the `fuzz` job after `g04-05-impl`): input bytes -> `sanitize_with(SgrOnly)`; asserts the two properties above; 60 s in the nightly fuzz run.

Unit (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`):
- `write_log_modes_headless_inline_scroll_region`: writer over `Vec<u8>` with a kitty capability profile (scroll region active after first present) in `Inline { ui_height: 3 }`; for each mode write the payload `"x\x1b[31my\x1b[2Jz\x1b]0;t\x07\n"`; assert the bytes between the log-position cursor sequence and the flush: Strip -> `xyz`, SgrOnly -> `x\x1b[31myz\x1b[0m`, Raw -> payload verbatim; assert `\x1b[2J` count is 0, 0, 1 respectively.
- `write_log_modes_headless_inline_overlay`: same with a profile without scroll region (overlay path); additionally assert the overlay line is width-clamped by visible width for SgrOnly (a 200-visible-char line with 100 bytes of SGR on an 80-col terminal emits 80 visible chars).
- `write_log_modes_alt_screen_noop`: all three modes emit nothing in `AltScreen`.
- `write_log_text_dispatches_on_marker`: `Text::sanitized`, `Text::sgr_only`, `Text::trusted` route to the three modes.
- `raw_write_emits_debug_trace`: tracing test subscriber sees one `ftui.runtime.log` debug event with `mode = "raw"`.

Unit (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/log_sink.rs`):
- `log_sink_sgr_only_handles_escape_split_across_writes`: write `"a\x1b[3"` then `"1mb\x1b[2J\n"`; output line is `a\x1b[31mb`.
- `log_sink_raw_passes_through`, `log_sink_default_strips`, `log_sink_flush_partial_line_uses_mode`.

Harness PTY test (`crates/ftui-harness/tests/pty_injection_adversarial.rs`, new; uses the harness's existing PTY helpers from `pty_terminal_lifecycle.rs` and the terminal model in `crates/ftui-render/src/terminal_model.rs`):
- Runs a small inline program (the harness binary or an in-test `Program` over the PTY slave) that writes the adversarial corpus through `write_log` and `write_log_sgr_only` (two runs) and a control run writing the stripped text; captures the master side; replays the capture into `TerminalModel`; asserts for the two sanitized runs: model title unchanged, `alt_screen == false`, DEC modes set equal the control's, scroll region equal the control's, cursor visible at exit, no `\x1b[2J`/`\x1b[3J`/`\x1b[?1049h` bytes in the capture, OSC 52 absent; asserts the visible text equals the control's visible text (sgr-only run may differ only in style attributes).
- `pty_injection_raw_mode_is_reachable_only_explicitly`: the raw run contains `\x1b[2J` (documenting the opt-in) and still tears down cleanly (`\x1b[?25h` last, raw mode restored via the PTY's termios read-back).
- Payload corpus shared with the sanitizer unit test via a `pub const ADVERSARIAL_PAYLOADS: &[&str]` in `crates/ftui-harness/src/lib.rs` (also used by `g26-e2e`'s injection scenario).

Proptest (`crates/ftui-harness/tests/inline_never_clears_screen.rs`, new):
- `inline_never_clears_screen`: strategy generating 1..200 operations from `{Present(random small frame), Resize(cols 20..200, rows 5..60), Log(random text with random escapes), LogSgrOnly(..), SetUiHeight(1..10)}`, applied to a headless `TerminalWriter` over `Vec<u8>` in `Inline`/`InlineAuto` with each capability profile (kitty, xterm-256color, tmux); asserts the emitted bytes contain no `\x1b[2J`, `\x1b[3J`, `\x1b[?1049h`, `\x1b[?47h`, and that any `\x1b[K`/`\x1b[J` emitted is scoped (`\x1b[0J`/`\x1b[J` only when the cursor is inside the UI region at the time, checked through the model). 2,000 cases; shrink output prints the operation sequence and escape tallies.
- `alt_screen_mode_is_the_only_path_to_1049h`: same generator in `AltScreen` shows `1049h` exactly once at session start.

Bench: `sanitize_sgr_only` added to the existing sanitize bench if one exists (`rg -n sanitize crates/ftui-render/benches`); no gate row (fast path is memchr).

E2E: PTY-level scenario `agent_shell_injection` lives in `g26-e2e`.

## Logging

- PTY test writes the capture and model dump to `target/pty_injection/<mode>.{raw,model.json}` on failure and prints escape tallies `{clear_2j, clear_3j, alt_1049h, osc, dcs, apc, c1, sgr_kept}`.
- Proptest prints the shrunk operation list with per-op emitted byte ranges.
- Tracing target `ftui.runtime.log` for raw writes.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-render/src/sanitize.rs`: unit + proptests.
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/sanitize_sgr_only.rs`, `fuzz/Cargo.toml`: new target.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`, `log_sink.rs`: unit tests.
- `crates/ftui-harness/src/lib.rs`: `ADVERSARIAL_PAYLOADS`.
- `crates/ftui-harness/tests/pty_injection_adversarial.rs`, `crates/ftui-harness/tests/inline_never_clears_screen.rs`: new.

## Success criteria

- [ ] All unit/proptests green: `cargo test -p ftui-render sanitize`, `cargo test -p ftui-runtime write_log_modes`, `cargo test -p ftui-runtime log_sink`, `cargo test -p ftui-harness --test pty_injection_adversarial`, `cargo test -p ftui-harness --test inline_never_clears_screen`.
- [ ] Fuzz target builds and runs 60 s without findings in the nightly fuzz job.
- [ ] PTY test green on ubuntu and macos runners (`e2e-pty` or `test-unit` job; run id in close reason).

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `g27-impl`. Coordinates with `g04-05-impl` (fuzz manifest) and `g26-e2e` (shared payload corpus). Unblocks: `g27-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Definition of done

Named tests exist and pass in CI; corpus shared; close reason lists test names and run id.

title: docs(G27): accept ADR-006 with the delivered API and make risk register R2 truthful
description:
## Context and why this matters

`docs/adr/ADR-006-untrusted-output-policy.md` has carried "Status: PROPOSED" since it was written even though the sanitize-by-default half has shipped (`terminal_writer.rs:2157`, `log_sink.rs:54`) and, after `g27-impl`, the opt-in half ships too. `docs/risk-register.md` R2 says "Explicit raw opt-in `write_raw()`: Designed", "Adversarial PTY tests: Planned" while the summary table says "Mitigated"; its Beads list cites bd-397 and bd-10i.8.5. Section 2.2.E of the audit flags exactly this drift ("`docs/risk-register.md` says all risks mitigated in its summary while its detail rows still say Planned/Designed; ADR-004/005/006/008/010 are still PROPOSED"). This bead accepts ADR-006 with the delivered API, makes R2 truthful, and documents the three log modes for consumers. Serves Section 2.2.E/F; ADR bookkeeping for the other ADRs is `g34-impl`'s job, which depends on this bead for ADR-006.

## Current state (evidence)

- ADR-006 sections: Context, Decision ("Sanitize by default... Raw passthrough is explicitly opt-in"), What Gets Sanitized (ESC + CSI/OSC/DCS/APC; C0 except TAB/LF/CR; "Optional semi-trusted mode (future): allow SGR-only"), Sanitization Strategy (STRIP), API Sketch (`write_log`/`Text::sanitized` safe; `write_raw`/`Text::raw` opt-in), Consequences, Test Plan (PTY adversarial, fuzz, no state leakage).
- Risk register R2 table rows: "Sanitize by default: Implemented", "Explicit raw opt-in: Designed", "Adversarial PTY tests: Planned", "C0 control filtering: Implemented"; Test Suites: "Adversarial tests: bd-397", "Fuzz tests", "State leakage tests"; Related ADRs: ADR-006.
- README: `rg -n "sanitiz|write_raw" README.md` (verify; the audit's C-table has no row for this, and the "Agent harness" use case text does not mention the policy). `docs/one-writer-rule.md` exists (README key docs) and may mention `write_log`.
- Delivered API (`g27-impl`): `TerminalWriter::write_log` (strip), `write_log_sgr_only`, `write_log_raw`, `write_log_text(&Text)`; `LogSink::new/sgr_only/raw`; `ftui_render::sanitize::{sanitize, sanitize_sgr_only, sanitize_with, SanitizeMode, Text}`; tests from `g27-tests` (`pty_injection_adversarial`, `inline_never_clears_screen`, `sgr_only_keeps_sgr_strips_rest`, fuzz target `sanitize_sgr_only`).

## Target state

- ADR-006: `Status: ACCEPTED (2026-09-xx)`; "Optional semi-trusted mode (future)" becomes "Semi-trusted mode: SGR-only (`write_log_sgr_only`); allowlist: `CSI [0-9;:]* m` up to 64 bytes; everything else stripped, including OSC 8"; API Sketch replaced by the real names with one line each; add "Decisions made during implementation": raw mode has no global switch; sgr-only appends `\x1b[0m` per line; raw writes emit a debug trace; Test Plan rows link the test names. Keep the original text under a "History" note rather than deleting it (no content loss).
- Risk register R2: rows read "Explicit raw opt-in (`write_log_raw`, `LogSink::raw`): Implemented (g27-impl)", "Adversarial PTY tests (`pty_injection_adversarial.rs`): Implemented", add row "Inline never clears screen (`inline_never_clears_screen` proptest): Implemented"; Beads list adds this block's bead ids; the summary table's "Mitigated" for R2 is now true. (The other risk rows R1/R3 remain for `g34-impl`.)
- README: a short "Untrusted output" paragraph under the agent-harness use case or the Inline Mode section: default strip, `sgr-only` for colored tool output, `raw` only for trusted sources, one code line per mode; link to ADR-006.
- `docs/one-writer-rule.md` (if it lists log APIs): mention the three modes.
- `docs/claims-ledger.md` rows: "sanitize by default" (proof: `write_log_modes_headless_inline_scroll_region`), "explicit raw opt-in" (proof: `pty_injection_raw_mode_is_reachable_only_explicitly`), "inline never clears" (proof: proptest name), "ADR-006 accepted" (proof: file status line).

## Implementation plan

title: epic(G29): i18n scoped truth: RTL via LocaleContext::direction and bidi, German, retract formatting
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:2304-2313 ("## Internationalization") claims: "The `ftui-i18n` crate provides locale-aware rendering: Locale context propagated through the runtime (`ProgramConfig::with_locale("fr")`); Number/date formatting respecting locale conventions; Text direction (LTR/RTL) integrated with the BiDi module in `ftui-text`; String table support for message translation. The `i18n_demo` screen demonstrates live locale switching between English, French, German, Japanese, and Arabic." README.md:1364-1368 ("### BiDi & Shaping") lists `bidi.rs` (1,100+ lines) for mixed LTR/RTL text. README.md:243 lists `ftui-i18n | Internationalization support | Implemented`. This epic closes vision row V47 ("i18n formatting/bidi/5 languages: PARTIAL (catalog + plurals only)") and the Section 2.2.C row "i18n: number/date formatting, LTR/RTL via ftui-text bidi, demo in EN/FR/DE/JA/AR | string catalog + plural rules only; no formatting; no bidi integration; demo has en/es/fr/ru/ar/ja". It also feeds G04.9: the PTY E2E failures include four `rtl_locale_not_selected` cases. User-visible consequence: an Arabic user switching the locale gets left-aligned, logically-ordered text; German is absent from the demo; and the README promises formatting that does not exist anywhere in the tree.

Status arrow: PARTIAL -> WORKING (scoped: two CODE items, one DOC retraction). Complexity M. Would open beads close it? No.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-i18n/src/` is 1,160 lines: `catalog.rs` 796, `plural.rs` 340, `lib.rs` 24. `lib.rs:18-24` exports `catalog::{CoverageReport, I18nError, LocaleCoverage, LocaleStrings, StringCatalog, StringEntry}` and `plural::{PluralCategory, PluralForms, PluralRule}`. `catalog.rs:28 pub type Locale = String;`; `:148 pub struct StringCatalog { locales: HashMap<Locale, LocaleStrings>, fallback_chain: Vec<Locale>, plural_rules: HashMap<Locale, PluralRule> }`; `:199 pub fn get(&self, locale: &str, key: &str) -> Option<&str>` walking the fallback chain. `plural.rs:71 pub enum PluralRule { English, Russian, Arabic, ... }` (CLDR-style groups plus a custom fn variant). No number, date, currency or unit formatting anywhere (`rg -n "format_number|format_date|NumberFormat|DateFormat" crates/ftui-i18n` is empty).
- Runtime: `crates/ftui-runtime/src/locale.rs:21 pub struct LocaleContext { current: Observable<Locale>, overrides: Rc<RefCell<Vec<Locale>>> }` with `new` (`:29`), `system` (`:39`), `global` (`:45`), `current_locale` (`:51`), `base_locale` (`:61`), `set_locale` (`:66`), `subscribe` (`:72`), `push_override` (`:78`), `version` (`:89`); `detect_system_locale` (`:114`); thread-local `GLOBAL_CONTEXT`. No `direction()` (`rg -n "fn direction|Direction" crates/ftui-runtime/src/locale.rs` is empty). `ProgramConfig::with_locale` at `program.rs:3164` sets `locale_context = LocaleContext::new(locale)`; `check_locale_change` around `program.rs:6844` re-renders on version change.
- Text: `crates/ftui-text/src/bidi.rs` (header: "Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX#9) support ... wrapping the `unicode_bidi` crate"; types `BidiSegment` (visual<->logical index mapping, cursor movement), `BidiRun`, `Direction` (Ltr/Rtl), `ParagraphDirection` (Auto/Ltr/Rtl); `reorder(text, ParagraphDirection) -> String`; `BidiSegment::new(text, None)`, `visual_pos`, `logical_pos`). Feature `bidi = ["dep:unicode-bidi"]` (`crates/ftui-text/Cargo.toml:18`, `unicode-bidi 0.3.18` optional at `:37`); enabled by no library crate; only `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml:19` enables `features = ["markup", "bidi"]`. `Paragraph` (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/paragraph.rs`) has `alignment(Alignment)` (`:192`, default `Alignment::Left` `:146`) and no bidi awareness; the wrap path (`ftui-text/src/wrap.rs`) is logical-order only.
- Demo: `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/i18n_demo.rs:32-68` `const LOCALES: &[LocaleInfo]` = en (English), es (Espanol), fr (Francais), ru (Russkij), ar (al-arabiya, `rtl: true`), ja (Nihongo); `LocaleInfo { tag, name, native, rtl }` (`:75`); `toggle_rtl` (`:350-353`) picks the first locale whose `rtl` differs; `current_info().rtl` consulted at `:271`; `Alignment::Center` used at `:478`. No German. The `rtl` flag is a demo-local bool, not a property of the runtime locale.
- E2E: `tests/e2e/scripts/test_bidi_voi_overlay.sh` contains the `rtl_locale` cases; `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/i18n_e2e.rs` exists; `tests/e2e/scripts/test_locale_context.sh` exists; harness env `FTUI_HARNESS_LOCALE_OVERRIDE` (`main.rs:306`), `FTUI_HARNESS_LOCALE_SWITCH_TO` (`:317`), `FTUI_HARNESS_LOCALE_SWITCH_TICKS/MS` (`:328-332`). Audit Section 5.1: `rtl_locale_not_selected` x4 among the 42/166 PTY failures on ubuntu.

## Target state

- CODE 1: `LocaleContext::direction() -> Direction` (Rtl for base languages `ar`, `he`, `fa`, `ur`, `yi`, `ps`, `sd`, `ug`, `dv`, `ku-Arab`; Ltr otherwise; overridable by `set_direction`), exposed to widgets through `Frame` (or a `RenderContext`) so `Paragraph` chooses its default alignment and, when the `bidi` feature is on in `ftui-text`, reorders each wrapped line visually via `bidi::reorder` and maps cursor movement in `TextInput`/`TextArea` through `BidiSegment`. `ftui-widgets` gains feature `bidi = ["ftui-text/bidi"]`; the facade `ftui` enables it by default (cost: one dependency, `unicode-bidi`).
- CODE 2: the demo adds German (`de`, "Deutsch") with translated strings for every key the i18n screen uses; the demo's `rtl` bool is replaced by `LocaleContext::direction()`.
- DOC: number/date formatting is retracted from README with the recorded decision "a full ICU dependency is out of scope; `ftui-i18n` provides catalog + plural rules; formatting is the app's responsibility"; README language list reads en/es/fr/de/ru/ar/ja.
- Proof: RTL snapshot of the i18n screen in Arabic; PTY `rtl_locale_*` cases green; German strings present.

## Success criteria (block level)

- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase i18n_demo_arabic_rtl_80x24` snapshot shows right-aligned, visually reordered Arabic (g29-tests).
- [ ] `tests/e2e/scripts/test_bidi_voi_overlay.sh` `rtl_locale_*` cases green on ubuntu and macos (g29-e2e; G04.9 cluster).
- [ ] `LocaleContext::direction()` unit tests and `Paragraph` bidi tests green (g29-tests).
- [ ] README i18n section truthful; ledger rows present (g29-docs).

## Plan (children)

1. `g29-impl`: direction API, Paragraph/TextInput/TextArea wiring under `bidi`, German strings, demo switch to runtime direction.
2. `g29-tests`: unit/proptest/snapshot tests.
3. `g29-e2e`: PTY `rtl_locale_*` cases and a locale-switch scenario with JSONL.
4. `g29-docs`: README retraction and language list; ledger rows; decision record.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: nothing (day-one). Unblocks: `g04-09-impl` (the `rtl_locale` failure cluster), `g42-impl` (Section 7.6 row C "every row" and V47).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Why retract formatting rather than implement: locale-aware number/date formatting done correctly is ICU-sized (`icu4x` pulls in data tables of several MB); the plan's rule ("CODE when user-visible value and at most M; DOC when decorative or larger") puts it on the DOC side. The decision is recorded in the ledger so it can be revisited.
- Bidi correctness scope: per-line reordering after wrapping is the standard terminal approach (like `mlterm`/`bidi-aware` emulators); we do not attempt paragraph-level reordering across wrapped lines beyond UAX#9's per-line rule L1-L4 as implemented by `unicode-bidi`.
- Risk: the `bidi` feature enabling by default in the facade adds `unicode-bidi` to every consumer; acceptable (small, pure Rust, `forbid(unsafe_code)` compatible; verify the crate's own unsafe usage is not a policy problem, since `unicode-bidi 0.3.18` is already a dependency of the showcase).

## Definition of done

Direction API on the runtime, bidi rendering under the feature, German in the demo, README truthful, snapshots and PTY tests green, ledger rows present, main green.

title: feature(G29): LocaleContext::direction, Frame.text_direction, bidi Paragraph/editors, German demo
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:2304-2313 promises "Text direction (LTR/RTL) integrated with the BiDi module in `ftui-text`" and a demo with German among its languages. In code, RTL is a demo-local boolean (`i18n_demo.rs:37-61`), `LocaleContext` has no notion of direction, `Paragraph` always lays out logical order left-aligned, and the `bidi` feature of `ftui-text` is enabled by no library crate. This bead wires text direction from the runtime locale into rendering and cursor movement, and adds German to the demo, which is the CODE half of G29. Serves V47, Section 2.2.C i18n row, and G04.9's `rtl_locale_not_selected` failures.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/locale.rs:15-95`: `LocaleContext { current: Observable<Locale>, overrides: Rc<RefCell<Vec<Locale>>> }`; `new`, `system`, `global`, `current_locale`, `base_locale` (`:61`), `set_locale`, `subscribe`, `push_override`, `version`; `detect_system_locale` (`:114`); free functions `set_locale` (`:121`), `current_locale` (`:127`). `Locale = String` (`ftui-i18n/src/catalog.rs:28`).
- `crates/ftui-text/src/bidi.rs` (feature `bidi`): `Direction` (Ltr/Rtl), `ParagraphDirection` (Auto/Ltr/Rtl), `reorder(text, ParagraphDirection) -> String`, `BidiSegment::new(text, Option<..>)` with `visual_pos(i)`/`logical_pos(i)` and cursor movement helpers, `BidiRun`.
- `crates/ftui-text/Cargo.toml:14-20` features: `default = []`, `bidi = ["dep:unicode-bidi"]`, `normalization`, `shaping`, `markup`, `thread_local_cache`.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/paragraph.rs`: `alignment: Alignment` field (`:110`), default `Alignment::Left` (`:146`), builder `alignment()` (`:192`), alignment offset applied at `:358`; wrapping via `ftui_text::wrap`.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/input.rs` (`TextInput`, arena-aware at `:954`) and `crates/ftui-text/src/editor.rs`/`cursor.rs` (TextArea cursor movement): logical-index cursor; Left/Right keys move by grapheme in logical order.
- `crates/ftui-render/src/frame.rs`: `Frame` carries `links`, `hit_grid`, `widget_signals`, `arena` (`:464-470`); no locale/direction.
- Demo `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/i18n_demo.rs:32-68` `LOCALES` (en, es, fr, ru, ar `rtl: true`, ja); `LocaleInfo { tag, name, native, rtl }` (`:75`); `:271 if self.current_info().rtl {..}`; `toggle_rtl` (`:350-353`); string tables for the screen live in the same file or a catalog (`rg -n "StringCatalog" crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/i18n_demo.rs`); `Alignment::Center` at `:478`.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml:19` enables `ftui-text` features `["markup", "bidi"]`.

## Target state

1. `ftui-runtime/src/locale.rs`:
   - `pub enum TextDirection { Ltr, Rtl }` (runtime-owned; converted to `ftui_text::bidi::Direction` when the feature is on) with `TextDirection::for_locale(&str) -> Self`: base language (before `-`/`_`, lowercase) in `["ar","he","fa","ur","yi","ps","sd","ug","dv","ckb"]` or script subtag `Arab`/`Hebr` -> Rtl.
   - `LocaleContext::direction(&self) -> TextDirection` (from `current_locale()` unless overridden), `set_direction(&self, Option<TextDirection>)` (explicit override stored alongside `current`; bumps `version`), and `subscribe` fires on direction changes as it does on locale changes.
2. Propagation to widgets: `Frame` gains `pub text_direction: TextDirection` (default Ltr; `ftui-render` defines a mirror enum `ftui_render::TextDirection` to avoid a render->runtime dependency; the runtime sets `frame.text_direction = config.locale_context.direction().into()` where it calls `frame.set_arena` at `program.rs:6572` and `:6634`). Widgets read `frame.text_direction`.
3. `Paragraph::render`: if the widget's alignment was not set explicitly (track `alignment: Option<Alignment>`), default to `Right` for Rtl; under `cfg(feature = "bidi")` in `ftui-widgets` (`bidi = ["ftui-text/bidi"]`), each wrapped line is passed through `ftui_text::bidi::reorder(line, ParagraphDirection::from(frame.text_direction))` before cell placement; without the feature, only alignment changes (documented).
4. `TextInput` and `TextArea` cursor: under `bidi`, Left/Right map through `BidiSegment::visual_pos`/`logical_pos` so the visual cursor moves in the direction the key points; Home/End respect direction. Without the feature, unchanged.
5. `ftui-widgets/Cargo.toml`: feature `bidi = ["ftui-text/bidi"]`; `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`: `default` includes `bidi` via `ftui-widgets/bidi` (state it in the features table of README per `g01-impl`'s feature docs).
6. Demo: add `LocaleInfo { tag: "de", name: "German", native: "Deutsch" }` and German strings for every key the screen renders (title, description, sample sentences, plural examples: "1 Datei"/"2 Dateien" with `PluralRule::English`-style one/other); remove the `rtl` field and `toggle_rtl`'s own flag in favor of `LocaleContext::direction()` (the toggle now calls `set_direction(Some(..))`/`None`); the E2E marker the PTY tests look for (`rtl_locale` in `test_bidi_voi_overlay.sh`) must be emitted from the runtime direction (read the script to learn the exact marker text before changing the screen).
7. Harness: `FTUI_HARNESS_LOCALE_OVERRIDE=ar` now also flips direction (no new env var).

## Implementation plan

1. `locale.rs`: `TextDirection`, `for_locale`, `direction`, `set_direction`; unit tests.
2. `ftui-render/src/frame.rs`: `text_direction` field + setter; `program.rs` sets it per frame.
3. `paragraph.rs`: `Option<Alignment>` and bidi reorder under the feature; `input.rs`, `editor.rs`/`cursor.rs`: cursor mapping under the feature.
4. Cargo features (`ftui-widgets`, `ftui`).
5. Demo: German strings; replace `rtl` bool; keep the toggle key.
6. Snapshot re-bless only for the i18n screen in `ar` (expected change) and `de` (new); any other snapshot change is a bug.
7. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (with and without `--features bidi` on `ftui-widgets`), `cargo fmt --check`; `ubs`.

What NOT to do: no number/date formatting (retracted in `g29-docs`); no reordering inside the wrap algorithm (reorder after wrap per line); no new locale crate; no `i18n_demo_v2.rs`; no deletion of existing demo locales.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/locale.rs`: `TextDirection`, `direction()`, `set_direction()`.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: set `frame.text_direction` (`:6572`, `:6634` area).
- `crates/ftui-render/src/frame.rs`: `text_direction` field.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/paragraph.rs`, `input.rs`; `crates/ftui-text/src/editor.rs` or `cursor.rs`: direction-aware behavior.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/Cargo.toml`, `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`: `bidi` feature.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/i18n_demo.rs`: German, runtime direction.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/snapshots/*i18n*`: re-blessed `ar`, new `de`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `TextDirection::for_locale("ar-EG") == Rtl`, `("en-US") == Ltr`, `("ku-Arab") == Rtl`, `("he") == Rtl` (unit tests).
- [ ] `Paragraph` with Arabic text in an Rtl frame renders right-aligned with visual order (snapshot `i18n_demo_arabic_rtl_80x24` and a widget-level test comparing against `unicode_bidi` reference output).
- [ ] German strings present for every key (`i18n_demo_german_80x24` snapshot; catalog coverage test says 100% for `de`).
- [ ] PTY `rtl_locale_*` cases green (`g29-e2e`).

## Tests and logging

Details in `g29-tests`. Tracing: `ftui.runtime.locale` info on direction change (`locale`, `direction`, `source: locale|override`).

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: nothing. Unblocks: `g29-tests`, `g29-e2e`, `g29-docs`, `g04-09-impl`, `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Putting `TextDirection` on `Frame` rather than a global: keeps widgets pure functions of frame state (consistent with `arena` and `links`), and headless tests can set it directly.
- `unicode-bidi` reorder per line handles neutrals and mirroring per UAX#9; box-drawing borders are not reordered because they are drawn by `Block`, not through `reorder`.

## Definition of done

Direction API, frame propagation, widget behavior under `bidi`, German demo strings, snapshots blessed with justification, gates green, close reason lists tests.

title: task(G29): direction inference, bidi rendering and cursor tests, Arabic/German snapshots
description:
## Context

Companion test bead for `g29-impl` (runtime `TextDirection`, `LocaleContext::direction()`, `Frame.text_direction`, `Paragraph`/`TextInput`/`TextArea` bidi behavior under the `bidi` feature, German demo strings). The README promise (README.md:2304-2313) is LTR/RTL "integrated with the BiDi module in `ftui-text`" and a demo in English, French, German, Japanese, Arabic. Today the only RTL logic is a demo bool and `ftui-text/src/bidi.rs` has unit tests of its own but no consumer. Serves V47 and the G04.9 `rtl_locale_not_selected` cluster.

## What to test

1. Direction inference from locale tags (base language, script subtag, overrides, version bumps).
2. Frame propagation: the program sets `frame.text_direction` from the locale context every frame and on locale change.
3. Paragraph rendering under Rtl: default alignment and visual reordering equal to `unicode_bidi` reference; LTR text unchanged; mixed text per-line correctness; feature-off behavior (alignment only).
4. Cursor movement in `TextInput`/`TextArea` under Rtl: Left/Right move visually; Home/End; round-trip visual<->logical mapping.
5. Demo: German coverage 100%; Arabic snapshot; locale switch re-renders with the new direction.

## Test types

Unit (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/locale.rs`):
- `direction_for_locale_table`: `("ar",Rtl)`, `("ar-EG",Rtl)`, `("he-IL",Rtl)`, `("fa",Rtl)`, `("ur",Rtl)`, `("ckb",Rtl)`, `("ku-Arab",Rtl)`, `("en",Ltr)`, `("de-DE",Ltr)`, `("ja",Ltr)`, `("",Ltr)`, `("AR_sa",Rtl)` (case/underscore normalization via `normalize_locale`).
- `set_direction_override_wins_and_bumps_version`: locale `en`, `set_direction(Some(Rtl))` -> `direction() == Rtl`, `version` increased, subscriber called once; `set_direction(None)` restores Ltr.
- `push_override_changes_direction`: `push_override("ar")` -> Rtl; dropping the guard -> Ltr.

Unit (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`):
- `frame_text_direction_follows_locale_context`: headless program with `with_locale("ar")`; capture the frame via a test model that records `frame.text_direction` in `view()`; assert Rtl; call `set_locale("en")`; next frame Ltr; `check_locale_change` triggered a re-render (frame count +1 without input).

Unit/proptest (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/paragraph.rs`, `#[cfg(feature = "bidi")]`):
- `paragraph_rtl_default_alignment_right`: Arabic sample in a 40x3 buffer with `text_direction = Rtl`; last cell column of the text equals width-1 (right-aligned); explicit `.alignment(Alignment::Left)` still wins.
- `paragraph_rtl_visual_order_matches_unicode_bidi`: for a fixed corpus of 20 strings (pure Arabic, Arabic with Latin brand names, numbers, punctuation, Hebrew), rendered row text equals `ftui_text::bidi::reorder(line, ParagraphDirection::Rtl)` padded/aligned; comparing against `unicode_bidi::BidiInfo` directly as an oracle.
- Proptest `paragraph_ltr_text_is_unchanged_by_direction_rtl`: arbitrary ASCII text renders identical glyph sequence (only alignment differs) under Ltr vs Rtl frames.
- `paragraph_wrap_then_reorder_per_line`: a 3-line wrapped Arabic paragraph reorders each line independently (line boundaries unchanged vs the logical wrap).
- Feature-off (`#[cfg(not(feature = "bidi"))]`): `paragraph_rtl_without_bidi_only_aligns_right`.

Unit (`crates/ftui-widgets/src/input.rs`, `crates/ftui-text/src/editor.rs` or `cursor.rs`, under `bidi`):
- `input_rtl_left_key_moves_visually_left`: Arabic text, cursor at logical 0 (visual right end); `Left` moves visual cursor left (logical +1); `Right` at logical 0 is a no-op at the visual right edge; `Home`/`End` go to visual left/right.
- Proptest `bidi_segment_visual_logical_roundtrip`: for arbitrary mixed strings, `logical_pos(visual_pos(i)) == i` for all grapheme indices (this belongs to `ftui-text` if not already present; add there).

Snapshot (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase`, insta):
- `i18n_demo_arabic_rtl_80x24`: screen `i18n_demo` after switching to `ar`; blessed once with a review note in the bead.
- `i18n_demo_german_80x24`: new.
- `i18n_demo_locale_switch_ar_to_en_80x24`: after `ar` then `en`, equals the existing English snapshot (no leftover RTL alignment).

Coverage (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/i18n_demo.rs` tests or `ftui-i18n` `CoverageReport`):
- `german_catalog_coverage_is_complete`: `StringCatalog::coverage()` (`LocaleCoverage`) reports 100% of keys for `de` relative to `en`; also for `es`, `fr`, `ru`, `ar`, `ja` (fix any gaps found; list them in the bead).

Bench: none (reorder cost is per wrapped line; if `g25` sees a `frame_render` regression with `bidi` on, add `wrap/word/200_lines_80_cols_rtl` to `wrap_bench.rs`).

E2E: `g29-e2e`.

## Logging

- Snapshot tests print the locale tag, direction and `version` on failure.
- Tracing target `ftui.runtime.locale` (`locale`, `direction`, `source`) asserted in `set_direction_override_wins_and_bumps_version` via a test subscriber.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/locale.rs`, `program.rs`: unit tests.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/paragraph.rs`, `input.rs`; `crates/ftui-text/src/{editor,cursor,bidi}.rs`: unit/proptests.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/i18n_demo.rs` + `snapshots/`: snapshot and coverage tests.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/Cargo.toml`: `[dev-dependencies] unicode-bidi` (oracle) under the feature.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-runtime locale`, `cargo test -p ftui-widgets --features bidi paragraph`, `cargo test -p ftui-widgets --no-default-features paragraph_rtl_without_bidi`, `cargo test -p ftui-text bidi`, `cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase i18n` all green.
- [ ] The `features` CI job includes `ftui-widgets` with and without `bidi`.
- [ ] Coverage test shows 100% for all seven locales.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `g29-impl`. Unblocks: `g29-e2e`, `g29-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Definition of done

All named tests exist and pass; snapshots blessed with justification; close reason lists test names and run id.

title: task(G29): PTY rtl_locale cases green plus locale-switch scenario with JSONL
description:
## Context and why this matters

The audit's CI root-cause table (Section 5.1, "PTY E2E ubuntu / macos") lists `rtl_locale_not_selected` (4 cases) among the 42/166 real PTY failures, and Section 7.1 G04.9 assigns that cluster to G29. The PTY scripts are the only proof that locale switching and RTL rendering work in a real terminal session rather than in a headless buffer. This bead makes the existing RTL cases pass against the runtime-driven direction from `g29-impl`, adds a locale-switch scenario with structured JSONL, and records the identity matrix results so `g04-09-impl` can close its cluster. title: epic(G30): runtime API names in README (persistence, macro player, checksum, SLO) as DOC rows
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md documents four runtime facilities with API shapes that do not exist: state persistence (README.md:2574-2585: `FileBackend`, `MemoryBackend`, `CustomBackend`, `PersistenceConfig::new().with_auto_save(true).with_backend(FileBackend::new("~/.config/myapp/state.json"))`), input macro playback (README.md:2550-2553: `MacroPlayer::new(macro_data)` then a loop calling `player.next()` yielding `(event, delay)` and `simulator.send_event(event)`), the headless simulator checksum (README.md:2663: `let hash = frame.checksum();`), and the SLO schema (README.md:2598-2616: `slo.yaml` with `objectives / budget_us / window_seconds / error_budget_pct` and "slo.yaml --parse--> SloSchema"). The features themselves work (vision rows V26 "State persistence: WORKING (API names wrong)", V27 "Input macro record/playback: WORKING (player API wrong)", V28 "Headless simulator: WORKING (`checksum` name wrong)") except V25 ("SLO schema + safe mode: WRONG_API / DEAD"), whose module is quarantined by G07. The audit resolved all four as DOC rows in the G06 decision table ("`frame.checksum()`, `MacroPlayer::next`, `sim.send_event`: DOC, this block"; "`PersistenceConfig`/`FileBackend` names: DOC, this block"; "`slo.yaml` schema: DOC + quarantine, G07") and listed G30 "so the vision checklist rows V25-V28 have an owner". This small epic exists only to parent `g30-docs`, the single bead that states the exact replacement names so the README rewrite (`g06-docs-readme`) can be done without reopening the code.

Status arrow: WRONG_API -> WORKING (DOC). Complexity S. Would open beads close it? No.

## Current state (evidence)

See `g30-docs` for the file:line table of real APIs. Summary: `PersistenceConfig::with_registry(Arc<StateRegistry>).auto_load(bool).auto_save(bool)` (`program.rs:1884-1952`), `FileStorage` (feature `state-persistence`, `state_persistence.rs:291`) and `MemoryStorage` (`:165`); `MacroPlayer::step/replay_all/replay_with_timing` (`input_macro.rs:243-315`); `ProgramSimulator::inject_events/inject_event` (`simulator.rs:169,:185`); `ftui_harness::golden::compute_buffer_checksum(&Buffer) -> String` (`golden.rs:71`); `slo.rs` hand-rolled parser with `regression_threshold` (default 0.10), `noise_tolerance`, `safe_mode_*`, `metrics: {metric_type, max_value, max_ratio, safe_mode_trigger}` (`slo.rs:53-150`); safe mode never enters `Program`.

## Target state

README sections rewritten to the real names, one worked snippet each that compiles as a doc-test (`g02-impl` mechanism), the SLO section moved to the "Experimental modules" section (G07) with its real schema, and four claims-ledger rows.

## Plan (children)

1. `g30-docs`: the replacement table and README edits, coordinated with `g06-docs-readme`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g06-impl-ledger` (ledger format), `g07-impl` (SLO quarantine status). Unblocks: `g42-impl`/`g42-docs` (vision rows V25-V28 flip to WORKING or EXPERIMENTAL with a documented decision).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- CODE alternative (add `frame.checksum()`, `MacroPlayer::next`, `send_event`, `FileBackend` aliases) rejected by the G06 rule: the README names are nicer names for the same thing, and AGENTS.md forbids compatibility wrappers.

## Definition of done

`g30-docs` closed with the claims check green; V25-V28 rows updated in the vision table by `g42-docs`.

title: docs(G30): replacement API names for persistence, MacroPlayer, simulator checksum and SLO rows
description:
## Context and why this matters

Four README sections describe runtime APIs by names that do not exist in the code. The features work; the names are wrong, so a reader who copies the snippet gets compile errors and concludes the feature is missing. The audit's G06 decision table resolves all four as DOC rows and G30 owns vision rows V25-V28. This bead lists the exact replacement identifiers with file:line evidence so `g06-docs-readme` (the README rewrite pass) can apply them verbatim, and it adds the claims-ledger rows that keep them true. It also moves the SLO section to the Experimental section per G07, since `slo.rs` is test-only and "safe mode never enters `Program`" (audit C-table).

## Current state (evidence): README text vs code

| README (line) | README says | Code has (file:line) |
|---|---|---|
| Persistence (README.md:2574-2585) | `FileBackend`, `MemoryBackend`, `CustomBackend`; `PersistenceConfig::new().with_auto_save(true).with_backend(FileBackend::new("~/.config/myapp/state.json"))` | `pub struct PersistenceConfig` (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs:1884`); constructor `PersistenceConfig::with_registry(registry: Arc<StateRegistry>) -> Self` (`:1929`); builders `auto_load(mut self, enabled: bool)` (`:1945`), `auto_save(mut self, enabled: bool)` (`:1952`); `ProgramConfig::with_registry(Arc<StateRegistry>)` (`:3231`); storage types `MemoryStorage` (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/state_persistence.rs:165`) and `FileStorage` (`:291`, behind feature `state-persistence`); custom storage is a trait impl (name the trait after reading `state_persistence.rs:100-165`; the audit calls the surface "StateRegistry, auto-load/save"). The registry owns the storage; there is no `with_backend` on the config. |
| Macro playback (README.md:2550-2553) | `let mut player = MacroPlayer::new(macro_data); while let Some((event, delay)) = player.next() { simulator.send_event(event); }` | `pub struct MacroPlayer<'a>` (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/input_macro.rs:243`); `MacroPlayer::step<M: Model>(...)` (`:282`), `replay_all<M: Model>(...)` (`:302`), `replay_with_timing<M: Model>(...)` (`:315`); a free `replay_with_timing` also at `:136`. The player drives a `Program`/simulator itself; there is no iterator `next()` and no `(event, delay)` tuple API. |
| Simulator input (README.md:2553) | `simulator.send_event(event)` | `ProgramSimulator<M: Model>` (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/simulator.rs:85`); `inject_events(&mut self, events: &[Event])` (`:169`), `inject_event(&mut self, event: Event)` (`:185`); construction `ProgramSimulator::with_registry(model, registry)` (`:146`) for persistence tests. |
| Frame checksum (README.md:2663) | `let hash = frame.checksum();` | `ftui_harness::golden::compute_buffer_checksum(buf: &Buffer) -> String` (`crates/ftui-harness/src/golden.rs:71`); after `g24-impl`, `ftui_render::buffer::buffer_checksum(&Buffer) -> u64` is the shared primitive. `Frame` has no `checksum` method. |
| SLO schema (README.md:2598-2616) | `slo.yaml` with `objectives: ... budget_us ... window_seconds: 60 ... error_budget_pct: 1.0`; "slo.yaml --parse--> SloSchema" | `crates/ftui-runtime/src/slo.rs`: hand-rolled parser; fields `regression_threshold: f64` (`:62`, default `0.10` at `:150`), `noise_tolerance: f64` (`:64`), `safe_mode_trigger: bool` (`:55`, `:118`), per-metric `max_ratio: Option<f64>` (`:53`), `max_value`, `metric_type`; the repo's `slo.yaml` is consumed by `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh` for `slo_metric` declarations; no `objectives`/`window_seconds`/`error_budget_pct` keys; safe mode is never entered by `Program` (module test-only; G07 quarantines it under `experimental`). |

## Target state

README (applied by `g06-docs-readme` using this table):
1. Persistence section: diagram row `FileStorage  MemoryStorage  <your impl of the storage trait>`; snippet:
   ```rust,no_run
   let registry = Arc::new(StateRegistry::new(FileStorage::new(path)?));
   let config = ProgramConfig::default()
       .with_registry(registry.clone());
   // or, explicitly: PersistenceConfig::with_registry(registry).auto_load(true).auto_save(true)
   ```
   with the feature note "`FileStorage` requires the `state-persistence` feature". Exact constructor signatures verified against `state_persistence.rs` when writing (do not guess `FileStorage::new`'s arguments; read `:291-330`).
2. Macro section: snippet using `MacroPlayer::new(&recording)` (verify the constructor at `input_macro.rs:243-281`) and `player.replay_all(&mut simulator)` or `replay_with_timing(&mut simulator, clock)`, plus `player.step(&mut simulator)` for stepwise control.
3. Simulator section: `simulator.inject_event(event)` / `inject_events(&events)`; checksum line becomes `let hash = ftui_harness::golden::compute_buffer_checksum(simulator.buffer());` (verify the buffer accessor name in `simulator.rs`).
4. SLO section: moved under "Experimental modules" (G07) with the real keys (`regression_threshold`, `noise_tolerance`, `safe_mode_*`, `metrics: {metric_type, max_value, max_ratio, safe_mode_trigger}`) and the sentence "safe mode is not wired into `Program`; the schema is consumed by `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh` for metric declarations".
5. All four snippets become doc-tests via the `g02-impl` mechanism (`no_run` where they open a terminal; `ignore` + "(fragment)" only if truly incomplete).

Claims ledger rows (four): "state persistence API" (proof: `program.rs:1929-1952` identifiers found by `rg` + a doc-test name), "macro player API" (proof: `input_macro.rs:282-315` + doc-test), "simulator inject/checksum" (proof: `simulator.rs:169` + `golden.rs:71`), "SLO schema" (status: EXPERIMENTAL, proof: `slo.rs:53-64` keys + G07 feature gate).

## Implementation plan

1. Verify the four constructor signatures named above by reading the cited ranges (this bead's implementer does the read; the table gives the lines).
2. Hand the final snippets to `g06-docs-readme` (comment on that bead with the snippets) or, if `g06-docs-readme` is already closed, apply the README edits directly in this bead.
3. Add the ledger rows.
4. Run `cargo test -p ftui --doc` and `scripts/check_readme_claims.py`.

What NOT to do: no alias methods (`frame.checksum()`, `MacroPlayer::next`, `send_event`, `FileBackend`) in code; no new docs file; no deletion of the SLO section (moved, not removed).

## Files to change

- `README.md`: :2550-2553, :2574-2585, :2598-2616, :2663 (via `g06-docs-readme` or directly).
- `docs/claims-ledger.md`: four rows.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `rg -n "FileBackend|MemoryBackend|player.next\(\)|send_event|frame.checksum\(\)|error_budget_pct" README.md` returns nothing.
- [ ] The four snippets compile under `cargo test -p ftui --doc`.
- [ ] Claims check passes with the four rows.

## Tests and logging

Docs-only; doc-tests and the claims check are the verification; outputs in the close reason.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g06-impl-ledger` (ledger exists), `g07-impl` (SLO quarantine feature name). Coordinates with `g06-docs-readme` (applies the text) and `g24-impl` (`buffer_checksum` primitive). Unblocks: `g42-docs` (V25-V28 rows).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- The G06 rule: CODE only when the promised behavior is user-visible value at most M; here the behavior exists and only names differ, so DOC.

## Definition of done
