title: epic(G31): Windows scoped truth: crossterm by default, windows-latest smoke, real matrix
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:1236-1239 (FAQ "Does it work on Windows?") says "Windows support is tracked in `docs/WINDOWS.md` and the deferred native-backend strategy is documented in `docs/spec/frankenterm-architecture.md` (Section 13.5)". `docs/WINDOWS.md` says "Last validated: 2026-02-03 (bd-31go)" and its CI matrix table marks `windows-latest | stable | Validated`, and `docs/adr/ADR-004-windows-v1-scope.md` (Status: PROPOSED) decides "Windows is supported in v1 with documented limitations" with a test plan "Windows CI build passes; minimal correctness tests run on Windows (raw mode lifecycle, basic input decode, resize)". Reality: the `Check (windows-latest, stable)` job has been red on every run since the Windows validation date (19 `dead_code` clippy errors in `ftui-tty`, audit Section 5.1; fix owned by `g04-03-impl`), `run_native()` errors on Windows, the crossterm path requires a feature the facade does not enable (`g01-impl`), and the native Windows backend is deferred (`docs/WINDOWS.md` "Deferred Native Backend Strategy (bd-lff4p.4.9)"). This epic closes vision row V67 ("Windows support: PARTIAL") with a scoped, honest target: Windows builds and runs the README example over crossterm by default, a PTY-less smoke runs on `windows-latest`, and the docs state the real matrix with run ids. User-visible consequence today: a Windows user following the README gets a clippy-red crate tree and an `Unsupported` error.

Status arrow: PARTIAL -> WORKING (scoped). Complexity M (after G01/G04.3). Would open beads close it? No.

## Current state (evidence)

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:23-34` `check` job matrix: `os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]`, `rust: [stable, nightly]`, `include: - os: windows-latest rust: stable`; steps `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (`:56-60`), then check/test. Windows fails at clippy (`ftui-tty` unix-only items not cfg-gated, `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs:217, 267, 597` per the audit).
- `docs/WINDOWS.md`: "Last validated: 2026-02-03 (bd-31go)"; matrix table (Linux/macOS/Windows "Validated"); "Automated Testing" bullets; "Supported Features (v1 target)"; "Known Limitations (v1)" (no DEC 2026 on Windows, OSC 8 Windows Terminal only, kitty keyboard absent, DECSTBM varies); Windows compatibility matrix (Windows Terminal / cmd.exe / ConHost / PowerShell); "Deferred Native Backend Strategy (bd-lff4p.4.9)" with a 5-phase plan (`ftui-win32` crate, `windows-sys`), "Scope Boundaries (Non-Blocking)".
- ADR-004: Status PROPOSED; Decision "Windows is supported in v1 with documented limitations"; Supported list (raw mode enter/exit and cleanup on panic; key input and resize; basic mouse; color); Best-effort list; Test Plan (Windows CI build passes; minimal correctness tests on Windows; `docs/windows.md` documents what works).
- Backends: `ftui-tty` is Unix-only (`#[cfg(unix)]` internals; `run_native` at `program.rs:7107` only with `native-backend` on unix); crossterm path via `Program::new`/`with_config` under `crossterm-compat` (`program.rs:4803-4814`); `g01-impl` makes the facade default select crossterm on non-unix and native on unix; `g04-03-impl` makes `ftui-tty` compile as an empty shell on Windows with `TtyBackend::open` returning `Unsupported`.
- Headless: `ProgramSimulator` (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/simulator.rs:85`) runs a `Model` without a terminal on any OS; `crates/ftui-harness` snapshot tests are platform-independent (`docs/WINDOWS.md` "Snapshot tests: Platform-independent golden snapshots").
- No ConPTY driver exists in the repo; `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` is a Python `pty` driver (Unix only).
- Windows Terminal detection: `WT_SESSION` treated as authoritative (`docs/WINDOWS.md` Configuration Recommendations; `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_capabilities.rs` per the audit).

## Target state

- With `g01-impl` and `g04-03-impl` landed: `cargo build -p ftui --examples` on `windows-latest` compiles `minimal_inline` and `agent_shell` with default features, and `App::run()` selects crossterm.
- A `windows-smoke` CI job on `windows-latest`: `cargo test -p ftui-runtime --lib simulator` (headless simulator suite), `cargo test -p ftui-harness --test widget_snapshots` (platform-independent snapshots), and a start/stop check: run `target\debug\examples\minimal_inline.exe` with `FTUI_EXIT_AFTER_MS=1500` (env honored by the example via `g01-impl`/`g35-impl` convention) under a plain console (`cmd /c`), assert exit code 0 within 10 s, stdout non-empty, and that `stderr` contains no `Unsupported`; plus `cargo run -p ftui-demo-showcase -- --screen=1` with `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS=1500` asserting exit 0.
- `docs/WINDOWS.md` "CI Validation Status" rewritten: a real matrix (job name, what it proves, last green run id and date), the sentence "PTY-based E2E tests do not run on Windows (no ConPTY driver in this repository)", and the crossterm-only decision.
- ADR-004 Accepted with "crossterm-only on Windows for v1; native `ftui-win32` deferred (bd-lff4p.4.9)".

## Success criteria (block level)

- [ ] `Check (windows-latest, stable)` green (after `g04-03-impl`) and `windows-smoke` green three consecutive runs (g31-impl, g31-tests).
- [ ] `docs/WINDOWS.md` matrix rows carry run ids; ADR-004 status ACCEPTED (g31-docs).
- [ ] README FAQ answer states the scope in one sentence (g31-docs).

## Plan (children)

1. `g31-impl`: crossterm-by-default on Windows via `g01-impl` (verify, do not duplicate), Windows-specific fixes surfaced by the smoke (path/console-mode issues), `FTUI_EXIT_AFTER_MS` support in the facade examples if `g01-impl` did not add it.
2. `g31-tests`: the `windows-smoke` job and its assertions (this is the block's CI/E2E bead; PTY-based E2E is impossible here, so the smoke is the tests bead).
3. `g31-docs`: `docs/WINDOWS.md`, ADR-004, README FAQ, ledger rows.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g01-impl` (default backend), `g04-03-impl` (Windows clippy). Unblocks: `g34-impl` (ADR-004 status), `g42-impl` (Section 7.6 row V67: "Windows CI job green; `docs/WINDOWS.md` run ids").

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- A ConPTY driver (Python `pywinpty` or a Rust `conpty` crate) would allow real E2E on Windows; deferred with the native backend because the value is low until a Windows backend exists beyond crossterm. Recorded in `docs/WINDOWS.md` "Future Improvements".
- Risk: GitHub Windows runners have no interactive console for `cargo run` of a TUI; crossterm's `enable_raw_mode` on a non-tty handle fails. The smoke therefore asserts either a clean run (if the runner console works) or a clean, specific `Unsupported`/not-a-tty error path with exit code 2 and no panic; `g31-tests` defines both acceptable outcomes precisely and logs which occurred.

## Definition of done

Windows check and smoke jobs green (run ids in the close reason), docs and ADR truthful, ledger rows present.

title: task(G31): Windows runs the facade example over crossterm; exit hook; not-a-console path
description:
## Context and why this matters

ADR-004 ("Windows v1 Scope") promises "core functionality works (raw mode lifecycle, basic input, resize, color where exposed)" over the crossterm backend, and `docs/WINDOWS.md` claims validation on 2026-02-03. Since then every `Check (windows-latest, stable)` run has failed (audit Section 5.1: 19 `dead_code` clippy errors in `ftui-tty`), `run_native()` cannot work on Windows, and the crossterm path needs a feature the facade does not enable. `g04-03-impl` fixes the clippy errors and `g01-impl` makes crossterm the default on non-unix; this bead makes sure the two combine into a Windows program that actually starts and stops, fixes whatever Windows-specific issues the smoke surfaces, and provides the deterministic exit hook the smoke needs. Serves V67; primary implementation bead of G31.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs:7107` `run_native()` exists only with `native-backend` on unix; `:7115-7124` `AppBuilder::run()` returns `Err(Unsupported, "enable crossterm-compat feature to use AppBuilder::run()")` without `crossterm-compat`; `Program::new`/`with_config` are `crossterm-compat`-gated (`:4803-4814`).
- `g01-impl` target: one `pub fn run(self)` dispatching `#[cfg(all(feature = "native-backend", unix))]` to native, else `#[cfg(feature = "crossterm-compat")]` to crossterm, else `Unsupported` naming the features; facade `default = ["runtime", "extras", "backend"]`, `backend = ["native-backend", "crossterm"]`.
- `g04-03-impl` target: `ftui-tty` compiles on Windows as an empty shell (`#![cfg(unix)]` on the implementation module, stub `TtyBackend::open` returning `Unsupported`).
- `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs` (crossterm session, RAII with panic hook at `:1194` per the audit) is the Windows session path; `terminal_capabilities.rs` treats `WT_SESSION` as authoritative (`docs/WINDOWS.md`).
- Showcase: `--screen=N`, `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS` (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/cli.rs:26,:121`), `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_TICKS` (`:114`).
- Harness: `FTUI_HARNESS_EXIT_AFTER_MS` (`crates/ftui-harness/src/main.rs:275,:594`).
- Facade examples (`crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs` from `g01-impl`, `agent_shell.rs` from `g26-impl`): exit hook convention not yet defined for examples.
- CI Windows runner: `windows-latest`, PowerShell default shell; `cargo run` of a TUI in a non-interactive console may fail at `enable_raw_mode` (crossterm returns an `io::Error` when the handle is not a console).

## Target state

1. On Windows with facade default features: `App::new(model).run()` reaches `Program::with_config` (crossterm). Verified by `g01-impl`'s `crates/ftui/tests/default_backend.rs` (`BACKEND == "crossterm"` on `cfg(windows)`); this bead adds the `cfg(windows)` assertion to that test if `g01-impl` wrote only the unix case.
2. Deterministic exit for examples: `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs` and `agent_shell.rs` honor `FTUI_EXIT_AFTER_MS` (documented in the file header) by returning an `Every`-driven quit; implemented as a small shared helper `ftui::runtime::exit_after_env("FTUI_EXIT_AFTER_MS") -> Option<Duration>` in the facade (or `ftui-runtime`) so all examples and the harness share one parser (the harness keeps its `FTUI_HARNESS_EXIT_AFTER_MS` name; the helper takes the var name).
3. Non-console handling: when `enable_raw_mode` fails because stdin/stdout is not a console, `Program::with_config` returns `io::ErrorKind::Unsupported` with message "stdin is not a console; run inside Windows Terminal, conhost, or use the headless simulator" and exit code 2 from `App::run` (no panic, no partial terminal state). Unit test with a redirected stdout on Windows (`cfg(windows)`), plus the smoke's second acceptable outcome (`g31-tests`).
4. Path and console-mode fixes discovered by the smoke (unknown until run): each fix is small and stays in the crate that owns it; if a fix is larger than S, file a child bead under `g31-epic` with the log.
5. `WT_SESSION` detection: unit test on all platforms that `WT_SESSION=...` yields the Windows Terminal profile (truecolor, OSC 8, SGR mouse, no sync output) matching the `docs/WINDOWS.md` matrix row.

## Implementation plan

1. Confirm `g01-impl` and `g04-03-impl` are merged; run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` on a Windows machine or via the CI job to establish the baseline.
2. Add `exit_after_env` helper and wire the two facade examples.
3. Add the not-a-console error path in `Program::with_config` (crossterm branch) and its test.
4. Add the `WT_SESSION` capability test in `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_capabilities.rs` tests.
5. Push; watch `Check (windows-latest, stable)` and the `windows-smoke` job from `g31-tests`; fix issues; repeat until green three times.
6. `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt` on Linux via rch; `ubs` on changed files.

What NOT to do: no native Windows backend work (deferred by design, bd-lff4p.4.9); no `cfg(windows)` forks of examples; no marking the Windows job `continue-on-error`; no ConPTY driver in this bead.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui/tests/default_backend.rs`: Windows assertion (if missing).
- `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs` or `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `exit_after_env` helper; not-a-console error path.
- `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs`, `crates/ftui/examples/agent_shell.rs`: `FTUI_EXIT_AFTER_MS`.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_capabilities.rs`: `WT_SESSION` test.
- Any Windows-specific fixes surfaced by the smoke (each cited in the close reason).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `Check (windows-latest, stable)` green (clippy + check + tests) on three consecutive main pushes (run ids).
- [ ] `windows-smoke` (g31-tests) green: examples build; start/stop check yields outcome A (exit 0, rendered) or outcome B (exit 2, "not a console" message, no panic), logged.
- [ ] `default_backend.rs` asserts `BACKEND == "crossterm"` under `cfg(windows)`.
- [ ] `WT_SESSION` capability test green on all three OSes.

## Tests and logging

Details in `g31-tests`. Tracing: `ftui.runtime` info at startup already logs backend and lane (`program.rs:4904-4913`); add `os = std::env::consts::OS` and `console = true|false` fields so the smoke log shows which outcome occurred.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g01-impl`, `g04-03-impl`. Unblocks: `g31-tests`, `g31-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- The "not a console" path is a real product improvement (today crossterm's raw error surfaces as a generic `io::Error`); the smoke's outcome B is acceptable only because it proves the clean failure path, not because the app ran.
- Alternative rejected: running the smoke under `winpty`/`conpty` wrappers; adds tooling for little proof until a native backend exists.

## Definition of done

Windows check green, smoke green three times, examples honor the exit hook, not-a-console path tested, close reason cites run ids and any surfaced fixes.

title: task(G31): windows-smoke CI job (simulator, snapshots, start/stop) and cross-platform unit tests
description:
## Context

Companion test bead for `g31-impl`; also the block's CI/E2E bead, because PTY-driven E2E is not possible on Windows in this repository (`tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` is a Unix Python `pty` driver; no ConPTY driver exists). ADR-004's test plan says "Windows CI build passes; minimal correctness tests run on Windows (raw mode lifecycle, basic input decode, resize)" and `docs/WINDOWS.md` claims "Validated (2026-02-03)" while `Check (windows-latest, stable)` has been red ever since (audit Section 5.1). This bead adds a `windows-smoke` job that proves the facade example and the showcase start and stop on `windows-latest`, runs the headless and snapshot suites there, and logs the outcome so `docs/WINDOWS.md` can cite run ids. Serves V67.

## What to test

1. Build: facade examples and showcase compile on Windows with default features.
2. Headless correctness on Windows: `ProgramSimulator` suite, snapshot suite, input decode unit tests (crossterm event mapping), resize handling in the simulator.
3. Start/stop: the example process exits cleanly under a deterministic timer, either rendering (outcome A) or failing with the documented not-a-console error (outcome B); never panics; never leaves a stray process.
4. Capability detection under `WT_SESSION`.

## Test types

CI job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, new job `windows-smoke`, `runs-on: windows-latest`, `timeout-minutes: 30`, toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml` per `g04-10-impl`, `shell: pwsh`):
- Step `build-examples`: `cargo build -p ftui --examples --locked`; asserts `target\debug\examples\minimal_inline.exe` and `agent_shell.exe` exist.
- Step `headless-suites`: `cargo test -p ftui-runtime --lib simulator --locked`, `cargo test -p ftui-harness --test widget_snapshots --locked`, `cargo test -p ftui-core --lib input_parser --locked`, `cargo test -p ftui-core --lib terminal_capabilities --locked`.
- Step `start-stop-minimal`: `$env:FTUI_EXIT_AFTER_MS=1500; $p = Start-Process -FilePath target\debug\examples\minimal_inline.exe -PassThru -NoNewWindow -RedirectStandardOutput out.txt -RedirectStandardError err.txt; $p | Wait-Process -Timeout 10`; asserts: process exited (not killed by timeout); exit code is 0 (outcome A) or 2 with `err.txt` containing `not a console` (outcome B); `err.txt` does not contain `panicked`; `out.txt` size > 0 for outcome A; record `outcome`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, first 200 bytes of each file into `smoke.jsonl`.
- Step `start-stop-showcase`: same with `target\debug\ftui-demo-showcase.exe --screen=1` and `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS=1500` (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/cli.rs:121`).
- Step `start-stop-agent-shell`: `agent_shell.exe --exit-when-child-exits -- cmd /c "echo hello"`; outcome A requires `hello` in `out.txt`.
- Step `upload`: `smoke.jsonl`, `out.txt`, `err.txt` as artifact `windows-smoke-<sha>`, `if: always()`.
- Step `summary`: append a table (step, outcome, exit code, duration) to `$env:GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.

Unit (`cfg(windows)` where noted):
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: `with_config_reports_not_a_console_cleanly` (`#[cfg(windows)]`): redirect stdout to a pipe (`std::process::Command` spawning the test binary itself with `--nocapture` is complex; instead call the internal console check function `console_available() -> bool` directly with a non-console handle and assert the error message and kind `Unsupported`); on unix the same function returns the `isatty` result (test with a pipe).
- `crates/ftui/tests/default_backend.rs`: `default_backend_is_crossterm_on_windows` (`#[cfg(windows)]`) and `default_backend_is_native_on_unix` (`#[cfg(unix)]`) reading the runtime's `BACKEND` constant from `g01-impl`.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_capabilities.rs`: `wt_session_profile_matches_windows_doc` (all OSes): with `WT_SESSION` set and `TERM` unset, capabilities report truecolor, OSC 8 true, SGR mouse true, sync output false, kitty keyboard false, matching `docs/WINDOWS.md`'s Windows Terminal column.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/input_parser.rs` (or the crossterm event mapping module): `crossterm_key_event_maps_to_ftui_key` table test (arrows, F-keys, Ctrl+C, Enter, Backspace, modifiers) compiled on all OSes (crossterm types are cross-platform).
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/simulator.rs`: `simulator_resize_reflows_view` runs everywhere and is explicitly included in the Windows headless step.
- `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs` (or wherever `exit_after_env` lives): `exit_after_env_parses_ms_and_rejects_garbage`.

Property: none new (platform-independent proptests already run on Windows through `cargo test` in the `check` job).

Bench: none.

E2E: the `windows-smoke` job is the E2E for this block; PTY E2E explicitly not applicable (documented in `g31-docs`).

## Logging

`smoke.jsonl` rows: `run_id` (GitHub run id), `ts`, `os` (`windows-latest` image version from `$env:ImageOS`), `step`, `binary`, `outcome` (`A_rendered|B_not_console`), `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, `stdout_bytes`, `stderr_excerpt`, `status`. The runtime startup `info!` line (with `os` and `console` fields from `g31-impl`) is captured in `err.txt` when `RUST_LOG=ftui.runtime=info` is set in the job.

## Files

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `windows-smoke` job.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`, `crates/ftui/tests/default_backend.rs`, `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_capabilities.rs`, `crates/ftui-core/src/input_parser.rs` (or event mapping), `crates/ftui-runtime/src/simulator.rs`, `crates/ftui/src/lib.rs`: tests above.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `windows-smoke` green three consecutive runs on main (run ids in close reason); `smoke.jsonl` shows the outcome for each binary.
- [ ] All listed unit tests green on ubuntu, macos and windows in the `check` job.
- [ ] If outcome B occurs for every binary on every run, `g31-docs` states "CI proves the clean not-a-console path; interactive rendering on Windows is manually validated" and records the manual validation (terminal, date, person) rather than claiming CI rendering.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `g31-impl`, `g01-impl`, `g04-03-impl`, `g26-impl` (agent_shell example). Unblocks: `g31-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Definition of done

Job merged and green, unit tests green cross-platform, JSONL artifact produced, close reason cites run ids and outcomes.

title: epic(G32): SIGTSTP/SIGCONT suspend-resume (bd-d4dtr implements; design note and PTY test here)
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md's design decisions (AGENTS.md:379 "RAII terminal state restoration: guaranteed on any exit path, even crashes"; README "RAII cleanup even on panic", vision row V4) promise that the terminal is always restored. The audit verified this empirically for normal exit, `q`, SIGTERM and panic (Section 2.1 "RAII teardown restores raw mode, alt screen, mouse, paste and cursor (verified empirically, including panic hook installation)") but found one hole: job control. `kill -TSTP` (or Ctrl-Z) suspends the process with raw mode and the alt screen still active, so the user's shell prompt appears inside a raw-mode terminal and `fg` resumes into a stale screen (Section 2.2.F "SIGTSTP/SIGCONT: open bead bd-d4dtr; `kill -TSTP` leaves the shell in raw mode"; vision row V4 "WORKING (gap: SIGTSTP)"). This is the one gap in Section 7 that an existing open bead already covers: **bd-d4dtr** ("SIGTSTP/SIGCONT suspend-resume handling for inline sessions", P3, feature, open since 2026-08-22, split off from bd-kdn7n) is the implementation bead. This epic exists to (a) declare bd-d4dtr the implementation bead so the orchestrator links it as a dependency of this epic and of `g42-impl`, (b) add the PTY test the audit asks for ("Add a PTY test that sends `SIGTSTP` then `SIGCONT` and asserts the mode transitions"), and (c) supply the safe re-raise design note that bd-d4dtr itself says it lacks ("design needed before implementation").

Status arrow: NOT_STARTED -> WORKING. Complexity S-M. Would open beads close it? Yes (bd-d4dtr), once the design and the PTY test exist.

## Current state (evidence)

- `br show bd-d4dtr` (2026-09-01): "Split off from bd-kdn7n's closing note: no SIGTSTP/SIGCONT handling today: `kill -TSTP` suspends with raw mode + alt screen active, leaving an unusable shell after `fg`. Proper fix needs a safe (`forbid(unsafe_code)`) re-raise strategy: restore cooked state on SIGTSTP, reset disposition to default and raise so the kernel actually stops the process, then on SIGCONT re-arm raw mode/scroll regions/kitty/mouse per saved flags and force a full repaint. signal-hook disposition juggling makes this non-trivial; design needed before implementation." Type feature, P3, owner ubuntu.
- Signal plumbing today: `ftui_core::shutdown_signal` process-global `AtomicI32` (`crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs:79-140` per the audit; `record_pending_termination_signal`, `clear_pending_termination_signal`), consumed by `Program` (`observed_termination_signal()`, `complete_lifecycle` at `program.rs:5490`); `g03-impl` moves per-program signal state into `Program` (`pending_signal: Arc<AtomicI32>`, `inject_termination_signal`) and keeps the global only for the OS handler.
- Teardown stacks: `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs` (crossterm session; RAII drop and panic hook around `:1178-1197`) and `crates/ftui-tty` `RawModeGuard` (`:365-399`, its own hook at `:312`); `g13-impl` extracts a shared `ftui-core::session_teardown` (ordered cleanup, panic-hook chaining, kitty pop-once latch).
- Existing PTY cleanup cases: `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh` (`cleanup_normal`, `cleanup_cursor_visible`, `cleanup_sigterm`, `cleanup_mouse_disabled`, `cleanup_bracketed_paste_disabled`, `cleanup_altscreen_exit`, `cleanup_altscreen_mouse_focus`) drive `E2E_HARNESS_BIN` with `FTUI_HARNESS_EXIT_AFTER_MS` and grep the capture for `\x1b[?25h` etc.; `cleanup_sigterm` is the template for a signal case.
- `signal-hook` is the sanctioned safe signal crate (bd-d4dtr text); confirm it is already a dependency of `ftui-core`/`ftui-runtime` (`rg -n signal-hook crates/*/Cargo.toml`) before designing.
- Every crate is `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` (AGENTS.md:55; V33).

## Target state

- bd-d4dtr implemented per the design note in `g32-impl-design`: on SIGTSTP the runtime restores cooked mode, shows the cursor, leaves the alt screen or resets DECSTBM and parks the cursor below the inline UI, disables mouse/paste/kitty, flushes, then stops itself with the default disposition; on SIGCONT it re-enters raw mode, re-applies the saved flags in the same order the session used at startup, and forces a full repaint; both transitions are logged as evidence.
- PTY test `cleanup_tstp_cont` in `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh` (and a Rust harness variant) asserts the mode transitions on the wire and via the PTY's termios.

## Success criteria (block level)

- [ ] `g32-impl-design` merged as `docs/spec/suspend-resume.md` and referenced from bd-d4dtr (comment on the bead).
- [ ] bd-d4dtr closed with the implementation and the design note cited.
- [ ] `cleanup_tstp_cont` PTY case green on ubuntu and macos (g32-tests).

## Plan (children)

1. `g32-impl-design`: design note (safe re-raise with `signal-hook`, ordering, interaction with `g03`/`g13`).
2. bd-d4dtr (existing; the orchestrator adds `br dep add bd-d4dtr <g32-impl-design>` and `br dep add <g32-tests> bd-d4dtr`, and links bd-d4dtr under `g32-epic`).
3. `g32-tests`: PTY TSTP/CONT test with JSONL, harness-level Rust test, unit tests for the state machine.

## Dependencies and ordering

`g32-impl-design` blocked by: nothing (can be written now; should be consistent with `g03-impl`'s per-program signal state and `g13-impl`'s shared teardown, so it references both and the implementer of bd-d4dtr reconciles). bd-d4dtr blocked by: `g32-impl-design` (its own text says design first). `g32-tests` blocked by: bd-d4dtr. `g42-impl` lists `g32-tests`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Why not just ignore SIGTSTP: ignoring it (SIG_IGN) breaks job control, which agent-harness users rely on (`Ctrl-Z` to get a shell, `fg` to return). The correct behavior is cooperative suspend.
- Safe re-raise under `forbid(unsafe_code)`: `signal-hook` provides `signal_hook::low_level::emulate_default_handler(SIGTSTP)` and `signal_hook::low_level::raise` in safe Rust, plus `signal_hook::flag::register` for the SIGCONT flag; the design note pins the exact calls.
- Risk: the handler must never do terminal I/O from the signal context; the design moves all I/O to the main loop by having the handler set a flag and wake the event loop (self-pipe or the existing signal thread), then the main loop restores the terminal and calls the re-raise.

## Definition of done

Design note merged, bd-d4dtr implemented and closed with test names, PTY case green in CI (run id), README/AGENTS RAII claims annotated (`g34-impl`/ledger) with "including SIGTSTP/SIGCONT".

title: task(G32): docs/spec/suspend-resume.md safe re-raise design for bd-d4dtr
description:
## Context and why this matters

Open bead bd-d4dtr ("SIGTSTP/SIGCONT suspend-resume handling for inline sessions") states: "Proper fix needs a safe (`forbid(unsafe_code)`) re-raise strategy: restore cooked state on SIGTSTP, reset disposition to default and raise so the kernel actually stops the process, then on SIGCONT re-arm raw mode/scroll regions/kitty/mouse per saved flags and force a full repaint. signal-hook disposition juggling makes this non-trivial; design needed before implementation." Nobody has written that design, which is why the bead has sat open since 2026-08-22 while `kill -TSTP` still leaves the shell in raw mode (audit Section 2.2.F; vision row V4 "WORKING (gap: SIGTSTP)"). This bead produces the design note as `docs/spec/suspend-resume.md` so bd-d4dtr's implementer has an unambiguous, unsafe-free plan that is consistent with the per-program signal ownership from `g03-impl` and the shared teardown from `g13-impl`.

## Current state (evidence)

- Signal ownership today: `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs:79-140` process-global `AtomicI32` for termination signals (`record_pending_termination_signal` CAS from 0; `clear_pending_termination_signal` store); `Program::complete_lifecycle` clears it (`program.rs:5490`); a signal thread installs the OS handler for interactive constructors. `g03-impl` gives each `Program` its own `pending_signal: Arc<AtomicI32>` and keeps the global only for the OS handler.
- Teardown order (as verified by the audit's PTY captures and `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh` cases): kitty keyboard pop, mouse off (`?1000l`/`?1002l`/`?1006l`), bracketed paste off (`?2004l`), focus events off, cursor show (`?25h`), DECSTBM reset (`\x1b[r`) in inline mode or alt-screen leave (`?1049l`), then raw mode off (termios). `g13-impl` centralizes this as `ftui-core::session_teardown` with a kitty pop-once latch and panic-hook chaining; `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs` (crossterm) and `crates/ftui-tty` `RawModeGuard` (`:365-399`) are the two stacks.
- Inline geometry: `TerminalWriter` tracks `last_inline_region`, `ui_anchor`, `scroll_region_active` (`terminal_writer.rs:2179-2200`); a full repaint after resume needs the writer to forget its diff baseline (the same mechanism a resize uses) and re-establish DECSTBM.
- `signal-hook` capabilities (safe API): `signal_hook::flag::register(SIGCONT, Arc<AtomicBool>)`, `signal_hook::iterator::Signals` (a thread-based iterator, likely what the current signal thread uses), `signal_hook::low_level::emulate_default_handler(signal) -> io::Result<()>` (performs the default action for the signal in a safe wrapper: for SIGTSTP it stops the process), `signal_hook::low_level::raise(signal)`, `signal_hook::consts::{SIGTSTP, SIGCONT, SIGTTIN, SIGTTOU}`. Verify the exact function set in the vendored `signal-hook` version (`Cargo.lock`) when writing the note.
- All crates `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` (AGENTS.md:55).

## Target state

`docs/spec/suspend-resume.md` with these sections, each concrete enough to implement without further design:

1. **Scope.** Unix only (`cfg(unix)`); both backends (`ftui-tty` native, crossterm); inline and alt-screen modes; Ctrl-Z from the terminal (ISIG is off in raw mode, so Ctrl-Z arrives as a key event, not a signal: the runtime must translate `Ctrl-Z` key into a self-suspend request; `kill -TSTP` from outside arrives as a real signal) and `SIGTTIN`/`SIGTTOU` (treated like TSTP).
2. **State machine.** `Running -> SuspendRequested(source: Key|Signal) -> Suspended -> Resuming -> Running`; invariants: terminal I/O happens only in `Running`/`SuspendRequested`/`Resuming` on the main loop, never in a signal handler; exactly one teardown and one re-arm per cycle; a termination signal during `Suspended` (e.g. SIGTERM while stopped, delivered on CONT) takes precedence and runs the normal exit path.
3. **Handler design (safe).** Register SIGTSTP/SIGTTIN/SIGTTOU with the existing signal thread (`signal_hook::iterator::Signals`) or a `flag::register` into `Program.pending_suspend: Arc<AtomicI32>` (the signal number), plus a wake of the event loop (the existing wake channel the input thread uses; if none, a `mpsc` sentinel `Event::Internal(Suspend)`); register SIGCONT with `flag::register(SIGCONT, resume_flag)`. The handler does no I/O.
4. **Main-loop suspend sequence.** On observing `pending_suspend != 0`: (a) stop input polling thread or mark it paused; (b) call `session_teardown::suspend(&mut session)`: kitty pop, mouse off, paste off, focus off, cursor show, in inline mode `\x1b[r` and move the cursor to the row below the UI region (so the shell prompt appears under the app's output), in alt-screen mode `?1049l`; flush; termios cooked (`tcsetattr` via `rustix`/`nix`/crossterm safe APIs, whichever the backend uses); (c) log evidence `suspend {signal, mode, cols, rows, ts}`; (d) clear `pending_suspend`; (e) stop the process with the default action: `signal_hook::low_level::emulate_default_handler(SIGTSTP)` (preferred: it restores the default disposition, raises, and re-installs the handler; document its exact semantics from the crate docs) or, if unavailable, the two-step "reset to default via `signal_hook::low_level::unregister` of our handler + `raise(SIGTSTP)` + re-register" (still safe API); (f) execution continues at (g) only after SIGCONT.
5. **Resume sequence.** (g) after return from the stop: read `resume_flag`; re-arm in startup order: raw mode on, alt screen (`?1049h`) if that mode, kitty push, mouse on, paste on, focus on, cursor hide, inline: recompute geometry (`ioctl TIOCGWINSZ` via the existing size query) and re-set DECSTBM; (h) invalidate the writer's diff baseline (the resize path's "full repaint" flag) and mark the model dirty; (i) log `resume {ts, cols, rows, size_changed}`; (j) resume input polling. If the terminal size changed while suspended, deliver a `Resize` event first.
6. **Ctrl-Z as a key.** With ISIG off, `Ctrl-Z` is `Event::Key(Char('z'), CTRL)`; the runtime's default keymap maps it to `SuspendRequested(Key)` unless the app has bound it (G14 keymap priority), then runs the same suspend sequence; document the `ProgramConfig::with_job_control(bool)` switch (default true in interactive constructors, false in headless/simulator).
7. **Interaction with `g03-impl`.** `pending_suspend` lives on `Program` like `pending_signal`; the OS handler writes through the same process-global slot only for interactive constructors; tests inject via `inject_suspend_signal()`.
8. **Interaction with `g13-impl`.** `session_teardown` gains `suspend()`/`resume()` as the reversible subset of `teardown()`; the kitty pop-once latch resets on resume.
9. **Failure modes.** If `tcsetattr` fails on resume (terminal gone), exit with the normal error path; if SIGCONT arrives without a prior TSTP (external `kill -CONT`), it is a no-op; if TSTP arrives during teardown, coalesce.
10. **Test plan.** Unit: state machine transitions (table); harness: headless writer emits the suspend sequence bytes in order and the resume sequence bytes in order (golden byte sequences per backend); PTY: `cleanup_tstp_cont` (in `g32-tests`), asserting termios `icanon`/`echo` after TSTP and their absence after CONT, `?25h` after TSTP, `?25l` after CONT, DECSTBM reset then re-set in inline mode, `?1049l` then `?1049h` in alt mode, and a full repaint (`2026h/l` pair with the whole UI rewritten) after CONT.
11. **Evidence.** Event names `suspend`/`resume` under tracing target `ftui.runtime.signal` and as evidence-sink JSONL (register in `telemetry_schema.rs` via `g20-impl`).

## Implementation plan

1. Read the current signal thread and teardown code paths (`ftui-core/src/lib.rs:79-140`, `terminal_session.rs:1150-1210`, `ftui-tty` `RawModeGuard`), the `signal-hook` version in `Cargo.lock` and its docs for `emulate_default_handler`.
2. Write `docs/spec/suspend-resume.md` with the eleven sections; include the exact byte sequences for both modes (copy from the existing teardown code, not from memory).
3. Comment on bd-d4dtr with the path and a two-line summary; the orchestrator links the dependency.
4. No code changes in this bead.

What NOT to do: no `unsafe`; no `libc::signal`/`sigaction` calls; no handler-side terminal I/O; no new signal thread if the existing one can be extended; no separate design file variants.

## Files to change

- `docs/spec/suspend-resume.md`: new design note.

## Success criteria

- [ ] The note answers every question in bd-d4dtr's text (cooked restore, default disposition + raise, re-arm order, full repaint) with concrete API calls and byte sequences.
- [ ] Reviewed against `g03-impl` and `g13-impl` designs (comment from those beads' owners or a note that they were consulted).
- [ ] bd-d4dtr references the note.

## Tests and logging

Not applicable (design bead); the test plan section feeds `g32-tests`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: nothing. Unblocks: bd-d4dtr (orchestrator link), `g32-tests`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- `emulate_default_handler` vs manual reset/raise/re-register: prefer the single safe call; the manual path is documented as the fallback if the vendored version lacks it.
- Ignoring Ctrl-Z entirely (rejected): breaks the shell workflow the agent-harness target depends on.

## Definition of done

Design note merged; bd-d4dtr comment posted; `g32-tests` can be written from the note alone.

title: task(G32): PTY TSTP/CONT cases, golden suspend/resume sequences, state-machine unit tests
description:
## Context

Test bead for the SIGTSTP/SIGCONT work implemented by the existing open bead **bd-d4dtr** (design in `g32-impl-design`, `docs/spec/suspend-resume.md`). The promise is README/AGENTS "RAII terminal state restoration: guaranteed on any exit path" (V4) extended to job control: after `Ctrl-Z`/`kill -TSTP` the shell must be usable (cooked mode, cursor visible, no alt screen, no scroll region), and after `fg`/`SIGCONT` the app must be fully re-armed and repainted. The audit asked specifically for "a PTY test that sends `SIGTSTP` then `SIGCONT` and asserts the mode transitions" (Section 7.3 G32). Today `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh` covers `cleanup_sigterm` but nothing covers suspend/resume.

## What to test

1. State machine transitions and coalescing (unit).
2. Byte sequences emitted on suspend and resume for both backends and both screen modes (headless writer, golden sequences).
3. Real PTY: termios flags and wire sequences across TSTP -> CONT, inline and alt-screen, native and crossterm backends; Ctrl-Z key path; size change while suspended; SIGTERM delivered while stopped.
4. Evidence events `suspend`/`resume`.

## Test types

Unit (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs` `#[cfg(test)]`, using `inject_suspend_signal()` from bd-d4dtr):
- `suspend_state_machine_transitions`: `Running -> SuspendRequested(Signal) -> Suspended -> Resuming -> Running`; a second TSTP during `SuspendRequested` is coalesced (one teardown); SIGCONT without prior TSTP is a no-op.
- `termination_during_suspended_takes_precedence`: inject TSTP then SIGTERM; on resume the program exits with `SignalTerminationError(SIGTERM)` after one resume re-arm (or without re-arm, per the design note's failure-modes section; assert whichever the note specifies).
- `ctrl_z_key_maps_to_suspend_when_job_control_enabled`: `Event::Key(Char('z'), CTRL)` -> suspend requested; with `with_job_control(false)` it is delivered to the model as a key.
- `headless_and_simulator_ignore_suspend`: headless constructors never register the handler; `inject_suspend_signal` is a no-op with a warning.

Golden byte sequences (`crates/ftui-harness/tests/suspend_resume_sequences.rs`, headless `TerminalWriter` over `Vec<u8>` per backend session type):
- `inline_suspend_sequence_native`, `inline_suspend_sequence_crossterm`: bytes equal the sequence documented in `docs/spec/suspend-resume.md` section 4 (kitty pop if pushed, `?1000l ?1002l ?1006l`, `?2004l`, `?1004l`, `?25h`, `\x1b[r`, cursor move below the UI region, flush); assert order with index comparisons and print the escape tally on failure.
- `inline_resume_sequence_*`: `?25l`, DECSTBM set for the current geometry, mouse/paste/focus on, kitty push, then a full repaint (`?2026h` ... whole UI ... `?2026l`).
- `altscreen_suspend_and_resume_sequences_*`: `?1049l` on suspend, `?1049h` on resume, full repaint.
- `resize_while_suspended_delivers_resize_first`: geometry changed between suspend and resume -> a `Resize` event precedes the repaint and DECSTBM uses the new rows.

PTY E2E (`tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh`, new cases following `cleanup_sigterm`'s pattern; driver `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` `pty_run`, which must gain a way to send signals mid-run: add `PTY_SIGNAL_SCRIPT="sleep 1; TSTP; sleep 1; CONT; sleep 1"` support to the Python driver, or use the existing mechanism `cleanup_sigterm` uses, extended to a sequence):
- `cleanup_tstp_cont_inline`: harness inline (`FTUI_HARNESS_SCREEN_MODE=inline FTUI_HARNESS_UI_HEIGHT=5 FTUI_HARNESS_EXIT_AFTER_MS=4000`), kitty identity; after TSTP: `stty -a` on the PTY (driver records termios at each phase via `pty_record_metadata`) shows `icanon` and `echo`; capture up to that point ends with `?25h` and `\x1b[r`; process state is `T` (stopped) in `/proc/<pid>/stat` on Linux or `ps -o stat` on macOS; after CONT: termios shows `-icanon -echo`; capture contains `?25l`, a DECSTBM set, and a sync pair enclosing a repaint of all 5 UI rows; final exit 0 with normal teardown.
- `cleanup_tstp_cont_altscreen`: `FTUI_HARNESS_SCREEN_MODE=alt`; `?1049l` after TSTP, `?1049h` after CONT.
- `cleanup_ctrl_z_key_inline`: send the byte `\x1a` instead of the signal; same assertions (the app suspends itself).
- `cleanup_tstp_then_sigterm`: TSTP, then SIGTERM while stopped, then CONT; process exits with the SIGTERM path and the terminal is restored (termios cooked, `?25h` last).
- `cleanup_tstp_cont_resize`: change the PTY size while stopped (driver `TIOCSWINSZ`), CONT; the repaint uses the new size (canonicalized frame has the new width).
- Each case runs for both backends when the harness exposes a backend switch (`FTUI_HARNESS_BACKEND=native|crossterm` if present; otherwise native only and a note).

Evidence: `evidence_contains_suspend_and_resume_events` (harness test with a temp evidence sink; fields `event`, `signal`, `mode`, `cols`, `rows`, `ts`, `size_changed`).

Bench: none.

## Logging

- PTY cases write per-phase JSONL via `jsonl_case_step_start/end` and `jsonl_assert`: `run_id`, `ts`, `scenario`, `identity` (`kitty`), `backend`, `screen_mode`, `phase` (`running|after_tstp|after_cont|exit`), `termios_icanon`, `termios_echo`, `proc_state`, `esc_tallies` {`cursor_show`, `cursor_hide`, `decstbm_reset`, `decstbm_set`, `alt_enter`, `alt_leave`, `mouse_off`, `mouse_on`, `sync_pairs`}, `cols`, `rows`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, `status`, `detail`; captures saved under `target/e2e/cleanup/<run_id>/`.
- Tracing target `ftui.runtime.signal` (`suspend`/`resume` info lines) captured in unit tests via a test subscriber.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: unit tests.
- `crates/ftui-harness/tests/suspend_resume_sequences.rs`: new.
- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh`: five new cases in `ALL_CASES`.
- `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` (and its Python driver): mid-run signal sequence and `TIOCSWINSZ` support (small, reusable; used later by `g05`'s identity matrix).

## Success criteria

- [ ] All unit and golden tests green (`cargo test -p ftui-runtime suspend`, `cargo test -p ftui-harness --test suspend_resume_sequences`).
- [ ] `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh` all cases `passed` on ubuntu and macos in the `e2e-pty` job (run id in close reason); JSONL validates.
- [ ] After `cleanup_tstp_cont_inline`, `stty -a` shows cooked flags while stopped and raw flags after resume (values logged).

## Dependencies

Blocked by: bd-d4dtr (implementation; orchestrator links it), `g32-impl-design`. Coordinates with `g03-impl` (signal injection API) and `g13-impl` (shared teardown). Unblocks: `g42-impl` (listed explicitly in its deps).

## Definition of done

All cases green in CI, driver extension merged, close reason cites run id, termios values and escape tallies.

title: epic(G33): ftui-simd implement-or-unpublish and yank stale ftui-demo-showcase 0.1.1
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:244 lists `ftui-simd | SIMD acceleration | Reserved` in the workspace table, README.md:303-309 ("### Crates.io (Published So Far)") counts it among the 17 published library crates, README.md:1780-1798 ("16-byte Cell ... SIMD-friendly 128-bit equality via `bits_eq()` ... compare 4 x 128-bit cells <- SIMD-friendly") sells SIMD as part of the cell design, and AGENTS.md:319 lists `ftui-simd/ # SIMD acceleration`. The original plan document had a SIMD chapter. `crates/ftui-simd/src/lib.rs` is 17 lines of documentation ("a sandbox for safe, performance-oriented code paths ... should be wired in via feature flags") with no code, no dependencies and no dependents, yet it is published on crates.io at 0.6.0 and is the first crate `release.yml` publishes (Layer 0). Separately, `ftui-demo-showcase` 0.1.1 sits on crates.io although the crate is `publish = false` (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml:5`) and at 0.6.0 in-tree, so crates.io shows a stale showcase that cannot be updated. This epic closes Section 2.2.F ("SIMD chapter: `ftui-simd` is a 17-line doc-only crate that nothing depends on (yet it is published on crates.io at 0.6.0)") and the release-hygiene half of V66/V41. User-visible consequence: a crates.io user who adds `ftui-simd` gets nothing; a user who finds `ftui-demo-showcase 0.1.1` gets a stale, unmaintained artifact; and every release run must publish an empty crate first.

Status arrow: WRONG_APPROACH -> WORKING. Complexity S (decision) / L (implement route) / S (unpublish route). Would open beads close it? No.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-simd/src/lib.rs` (17 lines): `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` plus the module doc ("Optional optimization crate ... This crate is optional and should be wired in via feature flags ... Note: This project currently forbids unsafe code. This crate exists to host safe optimizations behind feature flags"). No items.
- `crates/ftui-simd/Cargo.toml`: `name = "ftui-simd"`, `version = "0.6.0"`, `edition = "2024"`, `description = "Optional safe SIMD-friendly optimizations for FrankenTUI."`, `[lints] workspace = true`, `[dependencies]` empty.
- Root `Cargo.toml:18` lists `"crates/ftui-simd"` as a member; `rg -n "ftui-simd|ftui_simd" --glob Cargo.toml .` finds only the member line and its own manifest; `rg -n ftui_simd crates --glob "*.rs"` finds nothing.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:78-80`: `# Layer 0: no internal deps` / `publish ftui-simd` / `publish ftui-i18n`; the `publish()` function greps for "already uploaded" but the last two release runs failed on `ftui-simd@0.6.0 already exists on crates.io` (audit Section 5.1; idempotency fix owned by `g04-11-impl`).
- Cell equality: `Cell::bits_eq` (README.md:1785 "Single 128-bit comparison via `bits_eq()`"), benched as `cell/bits_eq/equal` (`tests/baseline.json` row `cell_bits_eq`, p99 10 ns) in `crates/ftui-render/benches/diff_bench.rs`/`cell_bench.rs`; the diff uses row-skip and 4-cell blocks (audit Section 2.1). ASCII width fast path lives in `ftui_core::text_width` (audit G08).
- Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` pins `nightly-2026-08-25`; `std::simd` (`#![feature(portable_simd)]`) is available on nightly and is safe Rust.
- `ftui-demo-showcase`: `Cargo.toml:2-5` `name = "ftui-demo-showcase"`, `version = "0.6.0"`, `publish = false`; crates.io has 0.1.1 (audit Section 7.3 G33). README.md:1221 says "crates.io publishing: 17 of 20 crates (all libraries); Showcase targets stay workspace-local".
- Yank/unpublish requires the crates.io owner token (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` secret in `release.yml`); crates.io does not delete versions, `cargo yank` marks them unusable for new resolutions.

## Target state

- **Implement:** `ftui-simd` gains real, safe `std::simd` paths behind feature flags: `bits_eq_rows(&[Cell], &[Cell]) -> bool` / first-mismatch index over 16-byte cells (u8x16/u64x2 lanes), and `ascii_width_fast(&[u8]) -> Option<usize>` (all-ASCII detection via lane masks); consumed by `ftui-render` diff row compare and `ftui-core` width fast path under `feature = "simd"`; criterion benches compare against the scalar paths; the crate stays published with content.
- **Unpublish:** `cargo yank --version 0.6.0 ftui-simd` (owner action), remove the crate from the workspace and `release.yml` (deletion of `crates/ftui-simd/` needs explicit written permission per AGENTS.md rule 1), README/AGENTS rows removed, the "SIMD-friendly" prose kept only where it describes the scalar `bits_eq` layout.

## Success criteria (block level)

- [ ] Decision recorded with the crates.io actions the owner performed (yank output pasted) (g33-decision).
- [ ] Implement route: `simd` feature paths wired with benches showing the gain and proptests showing equality with scalar (g33-impl-simd, g33-tests); or unpublish route: crate gone from workspace/release loop/docs with permission recorded (g33-impl-unpublish).
- [ ] `release.yml` no longer fails on `ftui-simd` (g04-11-impl idempotency plus this block's outcome).
- [ ] README/AGENTS rows truthful (in the impl beads; ledger rows).

## Plan (children)

1. `g33-decision` (question, P1): implement vs unpublish; showcase 0.1.1 yank vs deprecated 0.6.0; deletion permission wording.
2. `g33-impl-simd` (implement route; blocked by decision).
3. `g33-impl-unpublish` (unpublish route; blocked by decision and `g04-11-impl`).
4. `g33-tests`: proptests + benches for the implement route; workspace/workflow assertions for the unpublish route.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g33-decision`; unpublish route also by `g04-11-impl` (release loop edits should land once). Unblocks: `g41-impl` (release checklist references the crate list), `g42-impl` (listed as `g33-decision`).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- The implement route is only worth it if the benches show a gain: `bits_eq` is already 2-10 ns; a SIMD row compare wins on long identical rows (200x60 identical diff is 3.13 µs per `docs/profiling/opportunity_matrix_2026-02-03.md` numbers for alloc; check the diff table there) but the diff already skips identical rows via dirty tracking. The decision bead states the bar: at least 25% faster `diff/identical/compute/200x60` and `diff/sparse_5pct/compute/200x60`, else unpublish.
- Yanking is not deletion of code; removing `crates/ftui-simd/` from the tree is, and needs permission.

Decision executed, crates.io state matches the docs, release loop clean, tests/benches or workspace assertions green, ledger rows present.

title: question(G33): owner decides ftui-simd route, deletion permission and showcase yank
description:
## Context and why this matters

`ftui-simd` is a 17-line documentation-only crate (`crates/ftui-simd/src/lib.rs`: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` plus module docs; no items, no deps, no dependents) that is nonetheless published on crates.io at 0.6.0, listed in README.md:244 as "SIMD acceleration | Reserved", counted among the published libraries at README.md:303-309, and published first by `.github/workflows/release.yml:78-80`. `ftui-demo-showcase` is `publish = false` at 0.6.0 (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/Cargo.toml:5`) but crates.io still serves 0.1.1. The audit (Section 7.3 G33) asks the owner to choose: give `ftui-simd` real safe SIMD paths, or unpublish/yank it and remove it from the workspace (deletion needs permission); and yank the stale showcase or publish a deprecated README-only version. Both crates.io actions require the owner's token, so this is necessarily an owner decision. Serves Section 2.2.F (SIMD chapter) and V66/V41 (release hygiene).

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-simd/Cargo.toml`: version 0.6.0, description "Optional safe SIMD-friendly optimizations for FrankenTUI.", no dependencies; root `Cargo.toml:18` member; zero references from any crate (`rg -n ftui_simd crates --glob "*.rs"` empty).
- `release.yml:78-80` publishes it in Layer 0; last two release runs failed with `ftui-simd@0.6.0 already exists` (idempotency fix in `g04-11-impl`).
- SIMD-relevant hot paths: `Cell::bits_eq` (16-byte cells, README.md:1780-1798), diff row compare with 4-cell blocks (`crates/ftui-render/src/diff.rs`), ASCII fast path in `ftui_core::text_width` (audit G08). Baseline `cell_bits_eq` p99 10 ns; diff rows `diff_strategy` (80x24 sparse p99 200 µs), `diff_strategy_large` (200x60 sparse p99 800 µs).
- Nightly toolchain (`rust-toolchain.toml` `nightly-2026-08-25`) permits `#![feature(portable_simd)]` / `std::simd` in safe code.
- crates.io: `cargo yank --version 0.6.0 ftui-simd` and `cargo yank --version 0.1.1 ftui-demo-showcase` need `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`; yanked versions remain visible but are excluded from new resolutions.

## The question for the owner

1. **`ftui-simd` route.** (a) Implement: `std::simd` row-compare and ASCII-detect kernels behind `feature = "simd"` in `ftui-render`/`ftui-core`, keep publishing (with content). Bar for keeping it after implementation: at least 25% improvement on `diff/identical/compute/200x60` and `diff/sparse_5pct/compute/200x60` and no regression on 80x24, measured by `g33-tests` benches; if the bar is missed, fall back to (b). (b) Unpublish: yank 0.6.0, remove the workspace member, remove from `release.yml`, README, AGENTS. Plan default: (a) with the bar; the audit rates implement as L, unpublish as S.
2. **Deletion permission (route b).** Removing `crates/ftui-simd/` (two files: `Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`) is a file deletion. If the owner chooses (b), the owner must write here: "I authorize deleting crates/ftui-simd/Cargo.toml and crates/ftui-simd/src/lib.rs". Without that sentence, route (b) keeps the directory in the tree with `publish = false` and removes only the workspace member line and the release step.
3. **`ftui-demo-showcase 0.1.1`.** (a) Yank 0.1.1 (owner runs `cargo yank`); README.md:1221 keeps "Showcase targets stay workspace-local". (b) Publish a README-only 0.6.0 with description "Deprecated: the showcase is workspace-local; run it from the repository" (requires temporarily flipping `publish = false`, which contradicts the crate's intent). Plan default: (a).
4. **Who runs the crates.io commands.** The owner (token holder). The implementer records the command output in the bead.

## Target state

A comment on this bead answering 1-4, with the yank command outputs pasted, and (for route b) the deletion permission sentence verbatim or an explicit "no deletion".

## Implementation plan

1. Owner reads this bead (evidence complete) and answers.
2. Orchestrator unblocks `g33-impl-simd` or `g33-impl-unpublish` and closes the other with reason "not chosen (g33-decision)".

What NOT to do: no yank without the owner; no removal of the crate directory without the permission sentence; no `ftui-simd2` crate.

## Files to change

None by this bead.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Decision recorded with the four answers and command outputs.

## Tests and logging

Not applicable.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: nothing. Unblocks: `g33-impl-simd`, `g33-impl-unpublish`, `g33-tests`, `g41-impl` (release checklist crate list), `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Keeping an empty published crate "reserved" has a cost every release and misleads crates.io users; both routes fix that.

## Definition of done

Decision comment present; crates.io actions performed by the owner and pasted; no code changed by this bead.

title: task(G33): safe std::simd row-compare and ASCII kernels behind a simd feature with benches
description:
## Context and why this matters

Implement route of G33 (chosen in `g33-decision` option 1(a)). README.md:1780-1798 describes the 16-byte `Cell` as "SIMD-friendly" with "single 128-bit comparison via `bits_eq()`" and AGENTS.md:319 calls `ftui-simd` "SIMD acceleration", but the crate has no code and no consumer. This bead gives it real, safe `std::simd` kernels for the two hot loops where lane-parallel work can win (row equality / first-mismatch in the diff; all-ASCII detection for the width fast path), wires them behind a `simd` feature so the scalar paths remain the default until the benches prove the gain, and keeps the crate published with content. Serves Section 2.2.F (SIMD chapter), V35 (bench-backed claims).

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-simd/src/lib.rs`: docs only; `Cargo.toml` no deps; nothing depends on it.
- Diff: `crates/ftui-render/src/diff.rs` compares cells with `Cell::bits_eq` (16-byte compare) in 4-cell blocks with per-row dirty tracking (audit Section 2.1: "diff with row-skip, 4-cell blocks, per-row dirty-span union and `ChangeRun` coalescing"); `runs_into` at `:1606`; SAT at `:789-805` (G28). Benches `diff/identical|sparse_5pct|heavy_50pct|full_100pct/compute/{80x24,120x40,200x60}` in `benches/diff_bench.rs:179-245`.
- Width: `ftui_core::text_width::grapheme_width` ASCII fast path then `unicode_display_width` (audit G08); `crates/ftui-text/benches/width_bench.rs` exists.
- `Cell` is 16 bytes with a compile-time size assertion (`crates/ftui-render/src/cell.rs`; content 4 + fg 4 + bg 4 + `CellAttrs(u32)` 4 per the audit's C-table); a `&[Cell]` row can be viewed as `&[u128]`/`&[u64]` only via `bytemuck`-style casts or by exposing `Cell::as_bits() -> u128` (check the existing `bits_eq` implementation for the accessor it uses; the audit calls it "branchless").
- Toolchain nightly (`nightly-2026-08-25`); `std::simd` requires `#![feature(portable_simd)]` at the crate root of the crate using it.

## Target state

1. `crates/ftui-simd/src/lib.rs`: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)] #![feature(portable_simd)]`; public safe functions:
   - `pub fn first_mismatch_u128(a: &[u128], b: &[u128]) -> Option<usize>`: processes 4 lanes at a time as `u64x8` (two u64 per cell) or `u8x64`, mask-compare, `first_set` lane index; scalar tail.
   - `pub fn rows_equal_u128(a: &[u128], b: &[u128]) -> bool`.
   - `pub fn all_ascii(bytes: &[u8]) -> bool`: `u8x64` lanes, `(v & 0x80).reduce_or() == 0`; scalar tail.
   - `pub fn ascii_width(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<usize>` (Some(len) if all ASCII printable, None otherwise; C0 handling documented).
   - Each with a `#[inline]` scalar twin `*_scalar` for tests and benches.
2. `crates/ftui-render`: `[features] simd = ["dep:ftui-simd"]`; in `diff.rs`, the row compare uses `ftui_simd::first_mismatch_u128` on `Cell::as_bits()` slices under `cfg(feature = "simd")`, scalar otherwise; `Cell::as_bits(&self) -> u128` (or `row_bits(&[Cell]) -> &[u128]`, only if achievable without unsafe; otherwise copy into a stack buffer per 64-cell chunk, which is still branch-free) added in `cell.rs`.
3. `crates/ftui-core`: `[features] simd = ["dep:ftui-simd"]`; `text_width` ASCII fast path uses `ftui_simd::all_ascii` under the feature.
4. `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`: `simd = ["ftui-render/simd", "ftui-core/simd"]` (not default until the bar is met; `g33-decision` sets the bar).
5. Benches: `crates/ftui-simd/benches/simd_bench.rs` (`simd/first_mismatch/{scalar,simd}/{80,200,1000}_cells`, `simd/all_ascii/{scalar,simd}/{64,1024,65536}_bytes`); `crates/ftui-render/benches/diff_bench.rs` runs with and without the feature in the perf gate (two criterion baselines `scalar`/`simd`).
6. `release.yml`: unchanged order (Layer 0) since `ftui-render`/`ftui-core` now depend on it; `Cargo.toml` of `ftui-simd` gains `keywords`/`description` reflecting content.
7. Docs (this bead): README.md:244 row "`ftui-simd` | Portable-SIMD row compare and ASCII detection (feature `simd`) | Implemented"; README.md:1780-1798 gains "with `--features simd`, row comparison uses `std::simd` lanes (see `docs/perf/baseline_<date>.md` for the measured gain)"; AGENTS.md:319 same wording; ledger row "SIMD acceleration" (proof: `simd_matches_scalar` proptest + bench ids).

## Implementation plan

1. Read `cell.rs` `bits_eq` and `diff.rs` row compare; design the `u128` view without unsafe (stack chunk copy if needed).
2. Implement the four kernels + scalar twins with unit tests; `cargo test -p ftui-simd`.
3. Wire `ftui-render` and `ftui-core` under the feature; `cargo test -p ftui-render --features simd`.
4. Run benches via rch with and without the feature; record numbers in the bead and in `docs/perf/baseline_<date>.md` (via `g25-impl-readme-numbers`'s generator).
5. Apply the bar from `g33-decision`: if met, flip the facade feature to default and update docs; if missed, leave opt-in and document, or hand over to `g33-impl-unpublish` per the decision text.
6. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (both feature states), `cargo fmt --check`; `ubs`.

What NOT to do: no `unsafe` (no `transmute`, no raw pointer casts; use `std::simd::Simd::from_slice`/`from_array` on copies if necessary); no `target_feature` intrinsics; no changes to the diff's algorithm beyond the compare kernel; no `_v2` diff.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-simd/src/lib.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, `benches/simd_bench.rs`: kernels, benches.
- `crates/ftui-render/src/cell.rs`, `diff.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, `benches/diff_bench.rs`: feature wiring.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/text_width` (inline module), `Cargo.toml`: feature wiring.
- `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml`: `simd` feature.
- `README.md` (:244, :1780-1798), `AGENTS.md` (:319), `docs/claims-ledger.md`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Proptests `first_mismatch_simd_equals_scalar`, `all_ascii_simd_equals_scalar` (in `g33-tests`) green.
- [ ] Bench numbers recorded; bar from `g33-decision` evaluated in the close reason (met or missed, with numbers).
- [ ] Workspace gates green in both feature states; `features` CI job includes `--features simd`.
- [ ] README/AGENTS/ledger rows updated; `release.yml` publishes a non-empty crate.

## Tests and logging

Details in `g33-tests`. Bench JSONL lines per group to stderr as in `g25-impl-benches`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g33-decision`. Coordinates with `g25-impl` (baseline rows for `simd` variants). Unblocks: `g33-tests`, `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Copying 64 cells into a `[u128; 64]` stack buffer costs ~1 KB memcpy per chunk; measure; if it eats the gain, expose a safe `&[u128]` view by storing row cells as `u128` internally (a larger change; only if the bench justifies it, and as its own bead).
- Risk: `portable_simd` API churn on nightly; the toolchain is pinned, and `g04-10-impl` keeps CI on the pin.

## Definition of done

Kernels wired under the feature, equality proptests green, benches recorded against the bar, docs updated, main green.
notes: Refinement 4: implement safe experimental SIMD kernels and compare to scalar without deleting/yanking anything; this reversible route does not need the combined deletion/yank question .38.1 first. Promotion requires measured benefit and parity; retaining scalar fallback is mandatory.

title: task(G33): remove ftui-simd from release loop/workspace/docs after owner yank (permission)
description:
## Context and why this matters

Deleting `crates/ftui-simd/` requires the owner's explicit written permission (AGENTS.md rule 1); without it the directory stays with `publish = false`.
