title: feature(G05): FTUI_SYNC_OUTPUT / FTUI_SCROLL_REGION env overrides and capability_decision evidence lines
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:363-389 ("Evidence Logs (JSONL Diagnostics)") promises that runtime decisions are explainable through evidence lines, and README.md:818-833 ("Bayesian Capability Detection") promises that capability evidence is combined from environment and probes. Today a user whose terminal gets no sync output has no switch to force it and no log line saying why it was disabled: the only override is `FTUI_TEST_PROFILE` (`terminal_capabilities.rs:1030`), the `capability_override.rs` module is a thread-local test helper that reads no environment, and no `capability_decision` event exists. With G05 adding three new decision sources (identity profiles, the DECRPM probe, the DECSTBM self-test), the policy must be both overridable and observable, otherwise the next regression in the matrix is as invisible as the last one. This bead adds `FTUI_SYNC_OUTPUT`, `FTUI_SCROLL_REGION` (and documents `FTUI_CAPS_PROBE` from `g05-impl`) and makes every capability decision emit a `capability_decision` evidence line with its source. It serves V31, V51 (evidence sink categories), V64 and gap D.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-core/src/capability_override.rs`: `pub struct CapabilityOverride` (:71) with builder setters (`color_depth`, `mouse_sgr`, ...), `apply_to(&self, caps) -> TerminalCapabilities` (:335), `pub struct OverrideGuard` (:401), `push_override` (:430), `with_capability_override` (:455), `current_capabilities` (:468), `has_active_overrides` (:484), `clear_all_overrides` (:498), and `impl TerminalCapabilities { pub fn with_overrides() -> Self (:514); pub fn with_overrides_from(self, base) -> Self (:520) }`. Thread-local stack; RAII guards; documented as "for testing (bd-k4lj.3)". No `std::env` access.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_capabilities.rs:1030`: `env::var("FTUI_TEST_PROFILE")` selects a profile wholesale; no per-capability env override. `use_sync_output()` (:1233) and `use_scroll_region()` (:1246) compute from fields; no override slot.
- Both constructors call `TerminalCapabilities::with_overrides()` (`program.rs:4820` and `:5144`), so `with_overrides()` is the single choke point where env overrides belong.
- Evidence sink: `Program` writes `diff_decision`, `budget_decision`, `guardrail_snapshot`, `fairness_decision`, `decision`/`decision_evidence`/`regime_transition`, `effect_queue_select`, `certificate_decision`, `task_executor_*`, `widget_refresh` (reality check Section 2.2.B and G20). No `capability_decision`. `rg -n capability_decision crates` is empty.
- `caps_probe.rs:1020 CapabilityLedger` (log-BF ledger, `EvidenceSource`, `record`, weights `DECRPM_CONFIRMED 4.6` / `DECRPM_DENIED -4.6`) is built only by the demo screen; `g28-impl` makes it the production combiner.
- The showcase E2E (`scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh`) already validates JSONL against `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json`.

## Target state

- Env overrides, read once in `TerminalCapabilities::with_overrides()` after detection and thread-local overrides: `FTUI_SYNC_OUTPUT=0|1`, `FTUI_SCROLL_REGION=0|1`, `FTUI_CAPS_PROBE=0|1` (default 1; consumed by `g05-impl`'s gating), `FTUI_HYPERLINKS=0|1` (cheap to add alongside, same mechanism; optional). Values other than `0`/`1` are ignored with a `tracing::warn!`. Stored as `sync_output_override: Option<bool>`, `scroll_region_override: Option<bool>` fields; `use_sync_output()`/`use_scroll_region()` return the override when `Some` (an explicit `1` wins even inside a mux, because the user said so; the doc says this loudly), else the existing logic.
- Precedence, documented in one table in `terminal_capabilities.rs` module docs and README (via `g05-docs`): `env_override` > `self_test` (scroll region only) > `probe` > `identity` (`detect_from_inputs`) > `profile` (`FTUI_TEST_PROFILE` / `from_profile`).
- `pub struct CapabilityDecision { capability: &'static str, value: bool, source: DecisionSource, detail: String, log_bf: Option<f64> }` with `pub enum DecisionSource { Profile, Identity, Probe, SelfTest, EnvOverride }`; `TerminalCapabilities` carries `decisions: Vec<CapabilityDecision>` appended by `detect_from_inputs` (identity), `from_profile` (profile), `refine_from_probe` (probe), the env layer (env_override), and the writer's self-test (self_test, appended through `Program`); at startup `Program` writes one `capability_decision` evidence line per entry with fields `capability, value, source, detail, log_bf, profile, in_any_mux` and a tracing event on `ftui.core.capabilities`. When `g28-impl` has landed, `log_bf` comes from `CapabilityLedger`; until then it is `null`.
- Capabilities covered by decisions: `sync_output`, `scroll_region`, `true_color`/`color_depth`, `osc8_hyperlinks`, `kitty_keyboard`, `in_any_mux` (as `mux` with detail naming which marker matched). Each capability gets exactly one line per source that touched it (so a probe-confirmed sync shows two lines: identity false, probe true).

## Implementation plan

1. `terminal_capabilities.rs`: add `CapabilityDecision`, `DecisionSource` (with `as_str`), the two override fields, the `decisions` vec (not part of `PartialEq` if the struct derives it; check derives and use a manual `PartialEq` that ignores `decisions` or store decisions beside the struct in a `DetectedCapabilities { caps, decisions }` return type from `with_overrides()`; prefer the latter if `TerminalCapabilities` is `Copy`/`const`-constructed anywhere: the profile constructors are `const fn`, so a `Vec` field is impossible there. Decision: keep `TerminalCapabilities` `const`-constructible and return decisions separately: `pub fn with_overrides_and_decisions() -> (Self, Vec<CapabilityDecision>)`, with `with_overrides()` discarding them for callers that do not care). Record identity decisions inside `detect_from_inputs` by returning `(Self, Vec<CapabilityDecision>)` from a new inner function and keeping the old signature as a thin caller (not a compatibility shim: the two functions have different purposes).
2. `capability_override.rs`: add `pub fn apply_env_overrides(caps: &mut TerminalCapabilities, decisions: &mut Vec<CapabilityDecision>)` reading the four variables; call it at the end of `with_overrides_and_decisions()`. Keep the thread-local test stack as is.
3. `use_sync_output()` / `use_scroll_region()`: consult the override fields first. Update their rustdoc.
4. `caps_probe.rs` `refine_from_probe`: take `&mut Vec<CapabilityDecision>` (new signature `refine_from_probe_with_decisions`; the existing name keeps working by passing a throwaway vec is a shim, so instead change the signature and update the single production caller in `program.rs` and the tests).
5. `program.rs`: both constructors call `with_overrides_and_decisions()`, pass the vec through `probe_and_refine` (from `g05-impl`) and the DECSTBM self-test (from `g05-impl-decstbm-selftest`), then write one `capability_decision` evidence line per entry through the existing evidence sink right after the sink is initialised (before the first present), plus `tracing::info!(target: "ftui.core.capabilities", ..)`.
6. `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json`: add the `capability_decision` event shape (fields above) so strict validation in `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh` accepts it; `docs/spec/telemetry-events.md` entry if that file exists by then (`g20-impl`), else a rustdoc block on `CapabilityDecision`.
7. Tests (`g05-tests`): `env_override_1_forces_sync_even_in_mux`, `env_override_0_disables_sync_on_kitty`, `invalid_env_value_is_ignored_with_warning`, `decisions_record_identity_then_probe_for_sync`, `precedence_env_over_self_test_over_probe_over_identity`. Env-reading tests must not use the process env (parallel tests): `apply_env_overrides` takes an `impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>` lookup so tests pass a closure over a `HashMap`.
8. Gates and `ubs`.

What NOT to do: no reading of env vars at `use_sync_output()` call time (hot path; read once at construction); no second evidence sink; no `FTUI_*` names that collide with the showcase's `FTUI_DEMO_*` or the harness's `FTUI_HARNESS_*` families; no compatibility wrapper for the old `refine_from_probe` signature; no deletion.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_capabilities.rs`: types, fields, decisions, overrides in `use_*`, module-doc precedence table.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/capability_override.rs`: `apply_env_overrides`.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/caps_probe.rs`: `refine_from_probe` signature and decision recording.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: decision plumbing and evidence emission.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`: self-test verdict appended as a `SelfTest` decision (hand back through `Program`).
- `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json`: event shape.

## Success criteria

- [ ] The five unit tests above green.
- [ ] `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh` JSONL (strict validation) contains `capability_decision` lines with `source` in `{profile, identity, probe, self_test, env_override}` and at least one line each for `sync_output` and `scroll_region`.
- [ ] `g05-e2e` rows `kitty_force_sync_off` (`FTUI_SYNC_OUTPUT=0`): `count_2026h == 0` and a `capability_decision{capability:"sync_output", value:false, source:"env_override"}` line; `tmux_force_sync_on` (`FTUI_SYNC_OUTPUT=1` in tmux identity): `count_2026h > 0` with the env_override line; `xterm256_force_scroll_region_off`: no DECSTBM, strategy overlay.
- [ ] README (via `g05-docs`) documents the three variables and the precedence table; claims-ledger rows added.

## Tests and logging

Unit tests with injected env lookup. Evidence event `capability_decision` (fields listed in Target state). Tracing target `ftui.core.capabilities`. E2E via `g05-e2e` and `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g05-impl` (probe decisions), `g05-impl-identities` (identity decisions and profiles). Related: `g05-impl-decstbm-selftest` contributes the `self_test` source (if it lands later it appends to the vec; if earlier, this bead wires its verdict). Optional: `g28-impl` supplies `log_bf`. Unblocks: `g05-tests`, `g05-e2e`, `g05-docs`, `g20-impl` (which lists real event names; `capability_decision` must be in its schema).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Why `1` overrides mux gating: an operator debugging a mux passthrough problem needs to force the mode; the danger is theirs and the README says so. `FTUI_TEST_PROFILE` remains the way to simulate whole terminals.
- Alternative: a config-file override. Rejected for now (policy-config is feature-gated and not on the consumer path); env vars are what the rest of the FTUI_* family uses.
- Risk: `const fn` profile constructors cannot hold a `Vec`; hence decisions travel beside the struct, not inside it.
- Rollback: unset the variables; revert restores the previous signatures.

## Definition of done

Overrides effective in both constructors; evidence lines present in showcase E2E JSONL under strict validation; tests green; close reason cites test names and a JSONL excerpt; claims-ledger rows "FTUI_SYNC_OUTPUT / FTUI_SCROLL_REGION overrides" and "capability_decision evidence" proven.
close_reason: FTUI_SYNC_OUTPUT / FTUI_SCROLL_REGION parsed by capability_override::apply_env_policy_overrides{,_with} (1/true/on/yes, 0/false/off/no; junk ignored), applied at detection and re-applied after the live probe so the operator beats a positive reply; an explicit 1 lifts the WezTerm identity gate, never tmux/screen/zellij evidence. The functions return PolicyOverrides so the capability_decision evidence row records the switch (operator source, +/-9.2). Tests: env_policy_override_forces_sync_output_on_and_lifts_wezterm_gate, env_policy_override_never_lifts_real_multiplexer_evidence, env_policy_override_forces_off_and_ignores_unset_or_junk, env_policy_override_reports_which_switches_applied, operator_override_dominates_the_ledger; matrix rows wezterm_operator_opt_in, operator_opt_out, operator_opt_out_beats_probe PASS.

Tests env_policy_*; matrix rows wezterm_operator_opt_in, operator_opt_out, operator_opt_out_beats_probe, probe_disabled PASS.

title: task(G05): Unit tests for DECRPM reply parsing, identity table, override precedence and DECSTBM self-test
description:
## Context

G05 changes four layers of the terminal-capability policy: the DECRPM 2026 and CPR probes (`g05-impl`), identity profiles including the WezTerm-mux rule reversal (`g05-impl-identities`), the runtime DECSTBM self-test with fallback (`g05-impl-decstbm-selftest`), and env overrides plus `capability_decision` evidence (`g05-impl-overrides`). Each layer has a measured failure today (2026-09-01, `ab07291f`: 0 sync brackets on WezTerm, iTerm2, Apple Terminal, VS Code, `TERM=alacritty`, `xterm-256color`; Hybrid identical to ScrollRegion; no probe on truecolor terminals). This bead is the unit/property test bead for all four implementation beads. The PTY matrix is `g05-e2e`. All tests here are hermetic: no process env, no `/dev/tty`, no real terminal; replies are byte slices and injected closures.

## What to test

1. DECRPM reply parsing and the `probe_sync_output` verdict for every status value, other modes, timeout and garbage.
2. CPR reply parsing.
3. Deadline handling across multiple probes.
4. `refine_from_probe` upgrade-only semantics for `sync_output` and `color_depth`.
5. The identity table: every measured identity and the five new ones map to the expected `profile`, `sync_output`, `use_sync_output()`, `use_scroll_region()`, `probe_sync`, `in_any_mux`.
6. Profile name round trips.
7. Override precedence and invalid values.
8. DECSTBM self-test verdicts and fallback behaviour, evidence emission, Hybrid re-verification on resize, override skipping the self-test.
9. `capability_decision` records: which sources appear for each capability.
10. Property: `InlineStrategy::select` and the writer never emit DECSTBM when `use_scroll_region()` is false, and never emit `?2026h` when `use_sync_output()` is false, for arbitrary capability combinations.

## Test types (unit, property, bench, E2E) with names and assertions

`crates/ftui-core/src/caps_probe.rs` (`#[cfg(test)]`, feature `caps-probe`):
- `decrpm_2026_status_1_2_3_is_supported`: `parse_decrpm_response(b"\x1b[?2026;1$y") == Some((2026, 1))`, likewise 2 and 3; `verdict_from_decrpm((2026, s)) == Some(true)` for s in {1,2,3}.
- `decrpm_2026_status_0_and_4_is_unsupported`: `;0$y` and `;4$y` -> `Some(false)`.
- `decrpm_other_mode_is_ignored`: `\x1b[?2004;1$y` -> `None` from the 2026 verdict.
- `decrpm_timeout_is_none`: `probe_sync_output_with(reader_that_never_returns, 20ms) == None` and elapsed < 60 ms.
- `decrpm_garbage_is_none`: inputs `b"\x1b[?2026;$y"`, `b"\x1b[?;1$y"`, `b"garbage"`, `b"\x1b[?2026;1$x"`, empty.
- `decrpm_reply_with_leading_noise_is_parsed`: `b"\x1b[I\x1b[?2026;2$y"` (a focus-in event before the reply) -> `Some((2026, 2))`.
- `cpr_parse_row_col`: `b"\x1b[24;80R"` -> `Some((24, 80))`; `b"\x1b[24R"` -> `None`; `b"\x1b[24;80H"` -> `None`.

`crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs` (writer over `Vec<u8>`, capabilities by hand, injected `cpr_reply_source`):

- `self_test_honoured_keeps_scroll_region`: reply `(21, 1)` for region bottom 21 -> strategy unchanged, DECSTBM set after the self-test, `scroll_region_verified == Some(true)`.
- `self_test_absolute_row_report_is_honoured`: reply row == region height (DECOM-relative) also honoured.

title: task(G05): pty_identity_matrix.py asserts sync/DECSTBM per identity in CI and generates docs/compat-matrix.md
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:1214-1224 ("Known Limitations") lists "Formal compatibility matrix | In progress | Yes", and README.md:1935 promises "No partial frames ever visible". The only way the 2026-09-01 reality check could tell that the promise was off on WezTerm, iTerm2, Apple Terminal, VS Code, `TERM=alacritty` and `xterm-256color` was a throwaway Python `pty` driver that forked the showcase with a scrubbed environment, set one identity at a time, sent `q` after two seconds and counted escape sequences. Nothing in CI does this: `.github/workflows/emulator_compat_matrix.yml` simulates four profiles through `FTUI_TEST_PROFILE` inside `cargo test -p ftui-harness --test conformance_matrix_e2e` and never runs a binary under a PTY, so it cannot see `TERM_PROGRAM`, probes, or the writer's real output. This bead productizes the audit driver as `scripts/pty_identity_matrix.py`, gives it the ability to answer DECRPM and CPR queries so probe and self-test paths are testable without real emulators, asserts an expectations table per identity, emits JSONL, runs in CI, and generates `docs/compat-matrix.md`. It is the proof for G05 (V1, V31, V49, gap D) and is reused by `g01-e2e` (tallies), `g26-impl` (agent shell scenario) and `g42-impl` (final verification row "V1 inline mode, V31 sync output, V49 strategies").

## Current state (evidence)

- No `scripts/pty_identity_matrix.py`, no `docs/compat-matrix.md`, no `tests/e2e/identity_matrix_expectations.json`.
- Audit driver behaviour (scratchpad, 2026-09-01): removed `TMUX`, `STY`, `ZELLIJ`, every `WEZTERM_*`, `TERM_PROGRAM`, `KITTY_WINDOW_ID` from the child env; set the identity variables per row; `pty.fork()` at 100x30; ran the showcase binary; wrote `q` after 2 s; read until exit; counted regexes `\x1b\[\?1049[hl]`, `\x1b\[\?2026[hl]`, `\x1b\[>\d*u` / `\x1b\[<u` (kitty keyboard push/pop), `\x1b\[\?100[0236][hl]` (mouse modes), `\x1b\[\?2004[hl]` (bracketed paste), `\x1b\[\?1004[hl]` (focus), `\x1b\[\?25[lh]` (cursor), `\x1b\[\d+;\d+r` (DECSTBM set), `\x1b\[r` (DECSTBM reset), DA1 `\x1b\[c`, DA2 `\x1b\[>c`, DECRPM `\x1b\[\?\d+\$p`, OSC 8 `\x1b\]8;`. Raw captures saved as `demo_nomux_kitty_alt.raw`, `demo_nomux_kitty_inline.raw`, `demo_nomux_xterm256_inline.raw` (kitty inline: 25/25 sync pairs, DECSTBM set once and reset on exit).
- Showcase controls: `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN_MODE=alt|inline|inline-auto` (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/cli.rs:115`), `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN=<n>` (:119), `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS` (used in `screens/dashboard.rs:2937`), `--screen`, `--screen-mode`. Binary built by `cargo build -p ftui-demo-showcase` (default features enable both backends and `caps-probe`).
- `tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py` with `--schema tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json --registry tests/e2e/lib/e2e_hash_registry.json --strict` is the JSONL gate used by `e2e-widget-api` (ci.yml:412-425).
- `emulator_compat_matrix.yml`: `on: push/pull_request` with a `paths:` filter (`crates/ftui-harness/**`, `crates/ftui-render/**`, `crates/ftui-widgets/**`, `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_capabilities.rs`) plus `workflow_dispatch`; job `compat-matrix` (matrix xterm-256color, screen, kitty, modern; `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`; artifact `compat-results-<profile>` from `/tmp/ftui_conformance_e2e/*.jsonl`) and `compat-summary` (writes a pass/fail table to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`).
- Identity expectations after G05 land: see `g05-epic` table and `g05-impl-identities` target state.

## Target state

`scripts/pty_identity_matrix.py`:
- CLI: `--binary PATH` (default `target/debug/ftui-demo-showcase`), `--rows/--cols` (30/100), `--send q --send-after-ms 2000`, `--screen-mode inline|alt|both` (default both), `--screen N` (fixed screen for determinism, default the dashboard), `--identity NAME` (repeatable; default all), `--expectations tests/e2e/identity_matrix_expectations.json`, `--out DIR`, `--jsonl PATH`, `--summary-md docs/compat-matrix.md`, `--reply-decrpm none|0|1|2|3|4` (when not `none`, the driver watches child output for `\x1b[?2026$p` and writes `\x1b[?2026;<n>$y` into the pty), `--cpr-mode honor|ignore|timeout` (answers `\x1b[6n` with the row the child would see if DECSTBM+DECOM were honoured (`honor`), with the screen bottom row (`ignore`), or never (`timeout`); to compute `honor`, the driver tracks the last DECSTBM top/bottom it saw), `--env KEY=VALUE` (extra), `--keep-raw`.
- Identity rows (name -> env): `kitty` (`TERM=xterm-kitty`, `KITTY_WINDOW_ID=1`), `ghostty` (`TERM=xterm-ghostty`, `TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty`), `alacritty_term_program` (`TERM=xterm-256color`, `TERM_PROGRAM=Alacritty`), `alacritty_term` (`TERM=alacritty`), `wezterm_term_program` (`TERM=xterm-256color`, `TERM_PROGRAM=WezTerm`), `wezterm_term_program_with_pane` (+ `WEZTERM_PANE=0`), `wezterm_term` (`TERM=wezterm`), `wezterm_socket_no_term_program` (`TERM=xterm-256color`, `WEZTERM_UNIX_SOCKET=/tmp/x`), `iterm2` (`TERM=xterm-256color`, `TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app`, `LC_TERMINAL=iTerm2`), `apple_terminal` (`TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal`), `vscode` (`TERM_PROGRAM=vscode`), `xterm256_truecolor` (`TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`), `xterm256` (no COLORTERM), `tmux` (`TERM=tmux-256color`, `TMUX=/tmp/tmux-1/default,1,0`), `screen` (`TERM=screen-256color`, `STY=1.pts-0.host`), `zellij` (`ZELLIJ=0`), `dumb` (`TERM=dumb`). Variants generated by flags: `<identity>__decrpm<n>`, `<identity>__cpr_ignore`, `<identity>__cpr_timeout`, `<identity>__sync_off` (`FTUI_SYNC_OUTPUT=0`), `<identity>__sync_on`, `<identity>__scroll_off`, `<identity>__probe_off` (`FTUI_CAPS_PROBE=0`).
- Expectations file: per scenario `{ "sync_pairs": ">0" | "0", "decstbm_set_inline": ">0" | "0" | "1", "strategy": "scroll_region"|"hybrid"|"overlay_redraw", "alt_screen_in_inline": 0, "exit_code": 0, "queries": {"decrpm": 0|1, "da1": 0, "da2": 0, "cpr": 0|1}, "teardown": {"cursor_shown": true, "decstbm_reset": ">=set"} }`. Initial content mirrors the identity table in `g05-tests`: kitty/ghostty/alacritty (both)/wezterm (three non-mux rows) -> sync >0, decstbm >0, no decrpm query; `wezterm_socket_no_term_program`, tmux, screen, zellij -> 0/0, overlay, no queries; `iterm2`, `vscode`, `xterm256_truecolor`, `xterm256` -> sync 0 with no reply, decstbm >0 (hybrid), `decrpm: 1`; `*__decrpm2` and `__decrpm1/3` on those -> sync >0; `__decrpm0/4` -> 0; `apple_terminal` -> sync 0, decstbm >0, `decrpm: 0` even with `__decrpm2`; `kitty__cpr_ignore` -> `decstbm_set_inline: 1`, strategy overlay_redraw, evidence `inline_strategy_fallback`; `kitty__cpr_timeout` same; `kitty__sync_off` -> sync 0; `tmux__sync_on` -> sync >0; `xterm256__scroll_off` -> decstbm 0; `dumb` -> exit 0, no queries, no DECSTBM.
- Strategy observation: the driver reads the evidence JSONL the showcase writes (set `FTUI_EVIDENCE_PATH` or whatever env the sink uses; read `README.md:363-389` and `program.rs` for the variable) and extracts `capability_decision` and `inline_strategy_fallback` lines; `strategy_observed` comes from a startup evidence line `inline_strategy_selected { strategy }` (add it in `g05-impl-decstbm-selftest` if absent).
- Output: one JSONL record per scenario and screen mode, a summary record, exit code 1 on any mismatch, and `docs/compat-matrix.md` with a table (identity, screen mode, sync, DECSTBM, strategy, probe, verdict) plus a "How to read this" paragraph and the generation command; the file is committed when it changes (the CI job uploads it; the implementer commits the first version; the `docs` claims checker verifies the file's header date is within 30 days of the newest `capability` code change or the row `compat matrix fresh` fails: see `g06-impl-checker`).
- CI: new job `pty-identity-matrix` in `emulator_compat_matrix.yml` (ubuntu-latest and macos-latest; nightly from `rust-toolchain.toml`; python 3.11; `cargo build -p ftui-demo-showcase`; run the script with `--screen-mode both`; validate JSONL with `validate_jsonl.py --strict`; upload `pty-identity-matrix-<os>` with JSONL, raw captures, and the generated markdown; fail on mismatch). Extend the workflow's `paths:` filter to include `crates/ftui-core/src/caps_probe.rs`, `crates/ftui-core/src/inline_mode.rs`, `crates/ftui-core/src/capability_override.rs`, `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`, `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`, `scripts/pty_identity_matrix.py`, `tests/e2e/identity_matrix_expectations.json`, or drop the filter so the matrix runs on every push (preferred; the job takes a few minutes). Add the job to `compat-summary`'s table.

## Implementation plan

1. Write `scripts/pty_identity_matrix.py` (Python 3.11, stdlib only: `pty`, `os`, `select`, `re`, `json`, `argparse`, `time`, `signal`); structure: `IDENTITIES` dict, `Scenario` dataclass, `run_scenario()` (fork, env scrub + set, resize via `TIOCSWINSZ`, output pump with optional DECRPM/CPR responders, timed `q`, drain, waitpid with a hard timeout of 15 s and SIGKILL fallback logged as a failure), `tally()` (regex counts above plus `count_osc8`, `count_2J`, `count_3J`), `read_evidence()`, `evaluate(expectations)`, `write_jsonl()`, `write_summary_md()`.
2. Write `tests/e2e/identity_matrix_expectations.json` with the rows above; include a top-level `"_comment"` pointing to `g05-tests`'s identity table test and explaining the update procedure (update both, never one).
3. Add `inline_strategy_selected` evidence at writer construction if `g05-impl-decstbm-selftest` did not.
4. Workflow changes; `compat-summary` reads the new artifact and appends rows.
5. Run locally on Linux (rch is not involved: the script runs the built binary; build via rch first) and, before closing, once on a real WezTerm and a real kitty by the owner or an agent with a terminal, recording the JSONL in the close reason (real emulators can differ from the driver's synthetic replies; those runs are the ground truth for the "real terminal" column that `docs/compat-matrix.md` marks separately).
6. Document usage at the top of the script and in README "E2E Scripts" (via `g05-docs`).

What NOT to do: no deletion of the existing simulated `compat-matrix` job (it tests rendering determinism per profile; keep both); no mocks named as such (CI no-mock grep); no reliance on `/tmp` when `RUNNER_TEMP` or `--out` is given; no editing of showcase code from the script; the script must never leave the controlling terminal in raw mode (it owns a fresh pty, so the developer's terminal is untouched).

## Files to change

- `scripts/pty_identity_matrix.py`: new.
- `tests/e2e/identity_matrix_expectations.json`: new.
- `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json`: `pty_identity_matrix.v1` record shape.
- `.github/workflows/emulator_compat_matrix.yml`: job, paths, summary.
- `docs/compat-matrix.md`: generated, committed.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`: `inline_strategy_selected` evidence if missing.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `python3 scripts/pty_identity_matrix.py --screen-mode both` exits 0 locally after all G05 impl beads; every scenario `ok: true`.
- [ ] `pty-identity-matrix` job green on ubuntu and macos (run ids); artifacts contain JSONL, raw captures, and `compat-matrix.md`.
- [ ] `xterm256__decrpm2` shows `count_2026h > 0`; `xterm256` (no reply) shows `count_2026h == 0`; both show `count_decrpm_query == 1`.
- [ ] `kitty__cpr_ignore` shows `count_decstbm_set == 1`, `strategy_observed == "overlay_redraw"`, evidence `inline_strategy_fallback`.
- [ ] Every scenario: `count_1049h == 0` in inline mode; `count_25h >= 1` at teardown; `count_decstbm_reset >= count_decstbm_set` when any set occurred; `exit_code == 0`.
- [ ] `docs/compat-matrix.md` committed and linked from README "Synchronized Output" (`g05-docs`).

## Tests and logging

The script is the test. JSONL per scenario: `schema, kind, run_id, scenario, identity, env (the identity vars only), screen_mode, decrpm_reply, cpr_mode, binary_sha256, exit_code, duration_ms, bytes, count_1049h, count_1049l, count_2026h, count_2026l, count_25l, count_25h, count_decstbm_set, count_decstbm_reset, count_kitty_push, count_kitty_pop, count_mouse_on, count_mouse_off, count_2004h, count_2004l, count_1004h, count_1004l, count_da1_query, count_da2_query, count_decrpm_query, count_cpr_query, count_osc8, count_2J, count_3J, strategy_observed, capability_decisions (list), fallback_events (list), expected, mismatches (list), ok, raw_path`. Summary: `{kind:"summary", scenarios, passed, failed, duration_ms, matrix_md}`. The script prints one human line per scenario (`[ok] kitty inline sync=25/25 decstbm=1/1 strategy=scroll_region`).

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g05-impl-identities`, `g05-impl-decstbm-selftest`, `g05-impl-overrides` (all scenarios exercise them; `g05-impl` is transitively required). Unblocks: `g05-docs` (matrix link), `g42-impl`, `g26-impl` (reuses the driver), `g41-impl` (release checklist "compat matrix green").

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative: run real emulators headless in CI (xterm under Xvfb, kitty, wezterm). Rejected for now: heavy, flaky, and the synthetic replies test the same code paths; real-terminal ground truth is captured manually and marked as such in the matrix. A follow-up bead can add xterm under Xvfb as one real row.
- The showcase is the binary under test because it exercises the full production path (both backends, probe, writer); the consumer example (`g01-e2e`) covers the facade defaults.
- Risk: timing. Two seconds before `q` is enough for the probe budget (300 ms) plus first frames; the driver records `duration_ms` and fails a scenario that exceeds 15 s.
- Risk: macOS runners' `pty` behaves slightly differently (buffering); the driver's drain loop uses `select` with a 200 ms idle timeout as the audit driver did.

## Definition of done

Script and expectations on main, job green on both OSes, matrix committed and linked, real-terminal runs recorded, claims-ledger row "Formal compatibility matrix" proven with the job name and the generated file.

title: docs(G05): Rewrite README Synchronized Output and Inline Mode with preconditions and link the compat matrix
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md:1925-1935 ("Synchronized Output") states an unconditional guarantee ("No partial frames ever visible, eliminating flicker even on slow terminals"), README.md:2033 states "Theorem 1 (Sync Bracket Completeness): Every byte emitted by Presenter is wrapped in DEC 2026 sync brackets" and points at `no_flicker_proof.rs` (the file is `crates/ftui-harness/tests/render_no_flicker_proof.rs`), README.md:2369-2397 ("Inline Mode") says Hybrid "falls back to overlay-redraw when capability probing detects an unreliable DECSTBM implementation. This is the default.", README.md:1200-1204 (Troubleshooting "output flickers") says "Inline mode uses synchronized output where supported", and README.md:1214-1224 lists "Formal compatibility matrix | In progress". After the G05 implementation beads, each of these has a precise, testable truth: sync output is on when identity is known-good or DECRPM confirms, off in muxes, overridable; DECSTBM is verified at startup with a fallback; the matrix is generated in CI. This bead writes that truth into README and AGENTS.md and registers every statement in the claims ledger so `g06-impl-checker` keeps it honest. It is the DOC half of the G06 decision rows "Inline Hybrid with fallback | CODE | G05.4" and "Theorem 1 file name" and closes gap D's documentation.

## Current state (evidence)

- README.md:1925-1935: mechanism diagram (`CSI ? 2026 h ... CSI ? 2026 l`) and the unconditional guarantee; no preconditions, no identity list, no mention of DECRPM, muxes, or overrides.
- README.md:2030-2040: "The codebase includes formal proof sketches in `no_flicker_proof.rs`" and Theorems 1-4. Real file: `crates/ftui-harness/tests/render_no_flicker_proof.rs` (Section 3 row V34 "WORKING (file names differ)").
- README.md:2369-2397: Strategy A (DECSTBM diagram), B (overlay), C (Hybrid "This is the default"). Selection truth after G05: mux -> Overlay; scroll region and sync -> ScrollRegion; scroll region only -> Hybrid (self-tested, re-verified on resize); else Overlay; `FTUI_SCROLL_REGION` override.

## Context and why this matters

README.md:93-97 ("## Quick Example") says `FTUI_HARNESS_VIEW=dashboard cargo run -p ftui-demo-showcase` and `FTUI_HARNESS_VIEW=visual_effects cargo run -p ftui-demo-showcase` to "pick a specific demo view". README.md:486-504 ("## Configuration") lists nine `FTUI_HARNESS_*` variables as the harness configuration, and README.md:1192-1197 ("no mouse events") says `FTUI_HARNESS_ENABLE_MOUSE=true cargo run -p ftui-harness`. The facts: `crates/ftui-harness/examples/minimal.rs` is a 10-line `wrap_text` debugging scratch that never opens a terminal; the showcase ignores `FTUI_HARNESS_VIEW` entirely (it uses `--screen=N` / `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN`, `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/cli.rs:26,:119`, and `FTUI_DEMO_MOUSE` for mouse, `cli.rs:110`); the nine harness variables are real (all read in `crates/ftui-harness/src/main.rs`) but the README does not say they apply to the harness binary only. This epic (G35, "Harness and showcase usage docs: WRONG_API -> WORKING") makes the hello world a hello world and the configuration text true. It serves Section 2.2.A item 5, the G06 decision-table row "`FTUI_HARNESS_VIEW ... ftui-demo-showcase`: DOC, G35", and vision row V5/A (onboarding). User-visible consequence today: the first command a newcomer runs prints two `Vec<String>` debug lines and exits, and the second command silently ignores the variable.

Status arrow: WRONG_API -> WORKING. Complexity S. Would open beads close it? No.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-harness/examples/minimal.rs` (10 lines): `use ftui_text::wrap::{WrapMode, wrap_text}; fn main() { let text = "123 \u{00A0}\u{00A0}\u{00A0}foo"; let lines = wrap_text(text, 6, WrapMode::Word); println!("wrapped lines 1: {:?}", lines); ... }`. Other examples: `counter.rs` (94 lines), `layout.rs` (90), `modal.rs` (183), `streaming.rs` (161; uses `ftui_runtime::{App, Cmd, Every, Model, ScreenMode, Subscription}`, `LogViewer`, `StatusLine`, `Block`, `Borders`, `Flex`).

The nine README variables (`SCREEN_MODE`, `UI_HEIGHT`, `VIEW`, `ENABLE_MOUSE`, `ENABLE_FOCUS`, `LOG_LINES`, `LOG_MARKUP`, `LOG_FILE`, `EXIT_AFTER_MS`) are all real.
- Showcase CLI (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/cli.rs`): `--screen-mode=MODE` (`:22`; alt|inline|inline-auto), `--screen=N` (`:26`; 1-indexed), env `FTUI_DEMO_MOUSE` (`:110`), `FTUI_DEMO_DETERMINISTIC` (`:111`), `FTUI_DEMO_SEED` (`:112`), `FTUI_DEMO_TICK_MS` (`:113`), `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_TICKS` (`:114`), `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN_MODE` (`:115`), `FTUI_DEMO_UI_HEIGHT/MIN/MAX` (`:116-118`), `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN` (`:119`), `FTUI_TABLE_THEME_REPORT_PATH` (`:120`), `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS` (`:121`), `FTUI_DEMO_TOUR*` (`:124-126`), `FTUI_DEMO_PANE_WORKSPACE` (`:127`), `FTUI_DEMO_VFX_*` (`:128-139`), `FTUI_DEMO_EVIDENCE_JSONL` (`:140`). Screen numbers 1-9,0 switch screens 1-10 (`:94`); Tab cycles (`:95`).
- README lines: :93-97 (wrong var), :398-404 (examples), :486-504 (config), :1192-1197 (mouse), :477-484 ("Troubleshooting map"); `docs/tutorials/agent-harness.md:6-8,:17-20`.

title: task(G35): rewrite ftui-harness examples/minimal.rs as an inline hello world

`crates/ftui-harness/examples/minimal.rs` (target 30-40 lines), header comment "Minimal hello world: inline mode, 3 rows, tick counter; `q` or Ctrl-C quits. Run: `cargo run -p ftui-harness --example minimal`. Set `FTUI_HARNESS_EXIT_AFTER_MS=<ms>` to auto-exit (used by the E2E smoke)."; model `Hello { ticks: u64 }`; `Model::init` returns `Cmd::none()`; `subscriptions` returns `Every(Duration::from_millis(250))` mapped to `Msg::Tick` plus, when `FTUI_HARNESS_EXIT_AFTER_MS` parses, a one-shot quit after that duration (reuse the harness's existing helper if `main.rs:594` exposes one via `ftui_harness::`; otherwise `Every` with a counter); `update` handles `Tick` (increment) and `Key` (`q`, `Esc`, Ctrl-C -> `Cmd::quit()`); `view` renders `Paragraph::new(format!("Hello from FrankenTUI  ticks: {}  (q to quit)", self.ticks))` inside a `Block` with `Borders::ALL` and title "minimal"; `main` runs `App::new(Hello::default()).screen_mode(ScreenMode::Inline { ui_height: 3 }).run()` and maps the `io::Result` to exit code. Rendered text contains the literal `Ticks:`-style token the E2E asserts (`ticks:`).

The NBSP wrap check moves to a unit test `wrap_word_groups_nbsp_with_following_word` in `crates/ftui-text/src/wrap.rs` (two assertions from the old file), so the knowledge is kept without an example file.

title: task(G35): PTY smoke for the minimal example and README env-var attribution checker
description:
## Context

Companion test bead for `g35-impl` (hello-world `minimal.rs`) and `g35-docs` (README configuration truth). The promises: README.md:398-404 `cargo run -p ftui-harness --example minimal` is a runnable example; README.md:486-504 lists the environment variables that configure the harness; README.md:93-97 and :1192-1197 tell users how to pick a showcase screen and enable mouse. Today no test runs the example and nothing checks that a documented variable is actually read by the binary the README attributes it to (the `FTUI_HARNESS_VIEW=... ftui-demo-showcase` line is exactly that kind of error). Serves Section 2.2.A item 5, V5/A.

## What to test

1. The example starts, renders, and tears down cleanly under a PTY, both with `q` and with the auto-exit variable.
2. Every environment variable the README attributes to a binary is read by that binary's source (static attribution check), and every variable the binary reads that affects user-facing behavior is documented or explicitly listed as internal.
3. The showcase honors `--screen=N` and `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN` (already tested? verify in `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/`; add if missing) and ignores `FTUI_HARNESS_VIEW` (negative test proving the README fix was needed).
4. The moved wrap expectation.

## Test types

PTY E2E (`tests/e2e/scripts/test_examples.sh`, new, following `test_cleanup.sh`'s `run_case` pattern; driver `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` `pty_run`):
- `minimal_example_auto_exit`: build `cargo build -p ftui-harness --example minimal`; `FTUI_HARNESS_EXIT_AFTER_MS=800 PTY_TIMEOUT=5 pty_run $OUT/minimal.pty target/debug/examples/minimal`; assert exit 0; capture contains `Hello from FrankenTUI` and `ticks:`; escape tallies: `?25l` >= 1, `?25h` last cursor sequence, `1049h` == 0, `2026h` count == `2026l` count (kitty identity), DECSTBM set >= 1 and reset == 1.
- `minimal_example_quit_key`: no auto-exit; driver sends `q` after 500 ms (`PTY_INPUT_SCRIPT` or the existing key-send facility used by other scripts, e.g. `test_inline.sh`); same assertions plus duration < 2 s.
- `minimal_example_ctrl_c`: sends `\x03`; exit 0 (or the documented signal exit code; assert whichever the runtime defines) and clean teardown.
- JSONL per case via `logging.sh` helpers; included in `run_all.sh --quick`.

Static attribution check (`scripts/check_env_docs.py`, new, stdlib only; runs in the `check` job):
- Parses README.md "## Configuration" and "## Troubleshooting" blocks and the Quick Example, extracting `(binary, VAR)` pairs from lines like `FTUI_X=... cargo run -p <crate>` and from the code block under each "configured via" sentence (the README will tag blocks with an HTML comment `<!-- env:ftui-harness -->` / `<!-- env:ftui-demo-showcase -->` added by `g35-docs`).
- For each pair, asserts `rg -n "\"<VAR>\"" crates/<crate>/src` finds a read (`std::env::var`), else fails with the README line number.
- Inverse: lists `FTUI_HARNESS_*` and `FTUI_DEMO_*` variables read in `crates/ftui-harness/src/main.rs` and `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/cli.rs` that are absent from README and from an allowlist `docs/env-internal-allowlist.txt` (for test-only knobs like `FTUI_HARNESS_MINIMIZE_*`, `FTUI_HARNESS_FLICKER_*`, `FTUI_DEMO_VFX_*`); fails on undocumented, unallowlisted variables.
- Self-test with fixtures under `tests/fixtures/env_docs/`.

Unit (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase`):
- `cli_screen_flag_and_env_select_screen`: `Cli::parse_from(["x", "--screen=3"])` -> `start_screen == 3`; env `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN=5` (with the crate's env-serialization helper) -> 5; `--screen` wins over env (or env wins; assert the documented precedence from `cli.rs:119` "Override --screen": env overrides the flag, so assert that).
- `harness_view_env_is_ignored_by_showcase`: with `FTUI_HARNESS_VIEW=dashboard` set, `Cli::parse_from(["x"])` -> `start_screen == 1` and no field references the variable (grep-level assertion in the static check as well).
- `mouse_env_parses_on_off_auto`: `FTUI_DEMO_MOUSE` values.

Unit (`crates/ftui-text/src/wrap.rs`): `wrap_word_groups_nbsp_with_following_word` (from `g35-impl`): `wrap_text("123 \u{00A0}\u{00A0}\u{00A0}foo", 6, WrapMode::Word)` and the spaced variant produce the line splits the old example demonstrated (record the exact expected vectors after running once; assert them).

Bench: none.

## Logging

- PTY cases: JSONL fields `run_id`, `ts`, `scenario` (`minimal_example_*`), `identity`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, `esc_tallies` {`cursor_hide`, `cursor_show`, `alt_1049h`, `sync_h`, `sync_l`, `decstbm_set`, `decstbm_reset`}, `text_found` (bool), `status`, `detail`.
- `check_env_docs.py` prints one JSONL line per pair `{"binary","var","readme_line","found_in":path|null,"status"}` and a summary.

## Files

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_examples.sh`: new; `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh`: include.
- `scripts/check_env_docs.py`, `docs/env-internal-allowlist.txt`, `tests/fixtures/env_docs/*`: new.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `check` job: run `check_env_docs.py`.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/cli.rs` (tests) or `tests/cli_env.rs`: unit tests.
- `crates/ftui-text/src/wrap.rs`: unit test.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `tests/e2e/scripts/test_examples.sh` all cases `passed` on ubuntu and macos (`e2e-pty` job; run id in close reason).
- [ ] `scripts/check_env_docs.py` exits 0 on main and exits 1 when the README line `FTUI_HARNESS_VIEW=dashboard cargo run -p ftui-demo-showcase` is reintroduced (verified once, not committed).
- [ ] Showcase CLI unit tests green.

title: epic(G38): plan-doc leftovers decided: SSH extra dropped, TLA+ wording, execution tracker
description:
## Context and why this matters

The original plan documents (`docs/planning/plan-to-create-frankentui-opus.md`, 152 KB, and `plan-to-create-frankentui-codex.md`) promised a few things that were never built and never formally dropped, so they keep resurfacing as "gaps" in every audit: an SSH extra (`plan-to-create-frankentui-opus.md:121` "Markdown, syntax highlighting, forms, SSH/PTY integration, export (HTML/SVG), images (optional)" and `:169` "Markdown, syntax highlighting, export, SSH, forms, etc."), formal TLA+ specifications (`:765` "### 2.1 Terminal State Machine (TLA+-style)"; `docs/spec/state-machines.md:3` calls itself "the formal-ish specification backbone for FrankenTUI"), and an execution tracker (`docs/main-todo-bead-map.md:4` "It is the execution tracker so we do not need to reopen the plan to see intent", unmaintained). This small epic exists to parent `g38-docs`, which records those decisions where a future reader will look, so the next reality check does not rediscover them.

Status arrow: NOT_STARTED -> DECIDED. Complexity S. Would open beads close it? No.

## Current state (evidence)

- SSH: no crate, feature, module or bead mentions an SSH extra (`rg -n -i "ssh" crates --glob "*.rs"` is expected to return only unrelated hits; verify and record the count). The bead tracker recorded silent scope cuts in closing notes (audit Section 4) but not for SSH.
- TLA+: `docs/spec/state-machines.md` (bead bd-10i.13.1) is prose + tables, explicitly "formal-ish"; no `.tla` files exist (`find . -name "*.tla"`); the plan's section title says "TLA+-style".

- README "Limitations" (README.md:1206-1224 "What FrankenTUI Doesn't Do (Yet)" and "Known Limitations") is the reader-facing place for dropped scope; README.md:1269-1300 "Key Docs" lists spec documents.

- TLA+ wording: `docs/spec/state-machines.md` header states "This is an informal (prose + tables) specification; no TLA+/Alloy models exist. Invariants are enforced by the tests named in each section" and each state machine section links its tests (terminal lifecycle: `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh`, `pty_terminal_lifecycle.rs`; presenter: `proptest_terminal_model_invariants.rs`, `render_no_flicker_proof.rs`); the plan's "Decisions since the plan" block notes "formal TLA+ specs: not pursued; `docs/spec/state-machines.md` is the formal-ish backbone".

1. `g38-docs`: the three decision records and the test links.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g34-decision` (tracker outcome to reference). Unblocks: `g42-docs` (vision-delivery table cites decided rows).

- Building an SSH extra is a real feature (a `russh`/`ssh2`-based session that pipes a remote PTY into `ProcessSubscription`-like streams); the plan's target user (agent harness) runs locally; dropping is the honest call, reversible by a future bead.

title: G45: Correct unavailable conformal quantile ranks and configuration boundaries
description:
crates/ftui-runtime/src/conformal_predictor.rs computes ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha)) then clamps the index to n-1. At n=20, alpha=.01 the required 21st residual is absent; a finite observed maximum has only 20/21 marginal coverage for continuous exchangeable samples, not 99%. Default runtime now uses this predictor, so merely moving prose to experimental is insufficient. Represent unavailable bounds as unbounded/defer or enforce an explicit sufficient-sample contract, and propagate the outcome through budget/degradation APIs without nonfinite arithmetic or silent confidence inflation. Validate alpha and nonfinite observations; handle separate Mondrian bucket counts, ties, reset and warmup. Do not promise conditional/drift coverage from marginal exchangeability.

Verification contract (companion task):
Use a mathematically independent order-statistic oracle over small n and alpha grids, including exactly attainable n/(n+1) and unattainable ranks. Test empty and single sample, ties, extreme/NaN/infinite alpha or timings, distinct bucket sizes and reset. Verify runtime warmup/degrade/recover consumes the unavailable-bound state correctly. Add seeded exchangeable coverage experiments with binomial uncertainty and separate drift/assumption-break cases; passing empirical samples do not replace the exact rank proof. Record sample counts, alpha, rank, coverage, seeds and runtime decision logs.

title: epic(G06): Claims ledger, README-claims CI checker, and one truthful rewrite of README.md and AGENTS.md
description:
## Context and why this matters

README.md is the product's contract with users and AGENTS.md is the contract with the agents that maintain it. The 2026-09-01 reality check (commit `ab07291f`) found at least 25 places where README describes APIs, constants, counts, defaults, event names, file names and architecture that do not match the code (Section 2.2.C), and several more in AGENTS.md (architecture diagram says "TerminalSession (crossterm)" although crossterm is optional and labelled legacy; "Cross-component integration tests live in the workspace `tests/` directory" although that directory holds no Rust files; "46 screens" and "80+ widgets" in the workspace tree). The front-page numbers are wrong in the same direction every time: "850K+ lines" (actual 1,053,170 in 967 files), "80+ widgets" (57 production `Widget`/`StatefulWidget` implementors outside `#[cfg(test)]`), "46 demo screens" in seven places (45: `ScreenId` has 45 variants and `all_screens_count` asserts 45 at `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs:679` and `:7068`), `ftui = "0.5"` (crates.io has 0.6.0). A prior truth pass (bead bd-1zmo3, epic bd-i80el, 2026-04-09) fixed the same class of drift and regressed within weeks because nothing checks README against code. This is reality-check root cause 1 ("no truth mechanism between README and code") and the root of most of Section 2.2.B and all of 2.2.C. It serves every C row and vision rows V6 (80+ widgets), V39 (table theming), V40 (stylesheet), V41 (widget composition helpers), V42 (hyperlinks API), V43 (focus API), V44 (modal API), V45 (time-travel API), V51 (evidence sink categories), V65 (46 screens), V69 (AGENTS.md `tests/` claim).

The mechanism this block installs is a checked-in claims ledger plus a CI script: every tracked number and backticked identifier in README.md and AGENTS.md must have a ledger row, and every ledger row's proof (test name, path, identifier, command, CI job) must still exist. Then README and AGENTS.md are rewritten once against the ledger. The rule for each mismatch is CODE when the promised behaviour is user-visible value and the change is at most M in complexity, DOC when the promise was decorative (bit layouts, illustrative numbers, nicer names for the same thing).

## Current state (evidence)

- README.md is 2,700+ lines with 31 ```rust fences (G02) and about 60 `##`/`###` sections (headings at lines 25, 49, 55, 73, 89, 102, 124, 131, 137, 194, 204, 248, 277, 320, 336, 349, 363, 390, 486, 507, 546, 560, 589, 690, 709, 733-1167 (alien-artifact subsections), 1169, 1206, 1226, 1269, 1302, 1329, 1388, 1417, 1458, 1498, 1523, 1527-1660, 1889, 1925, 1997, 2086, 2143, 2172, 2369, 2440+).
- Wrong counts: `850K+`/`850,000+` at README.md:16 and :1257; `46` at :16, :23 (badge), :69, :102, :104, :235, :262, :575, :1234, :1257 and AGENTS.md:310; `80+` at :16, :64, :217, :261, :1219, :1257, :2143, :2145 and AGENTS.md:324; `ftui = "0.5"` at :314; `docs/getting-started.md:18` and `:167-168` say only three crates are published.
- Benchmark block README.md:2086-2094 quotes `diff/identical_100x50 1.2 µs`, `sparse_5pct_100x50 8.3 µs`, `dense_100x50 45 µs`; no 100x50 or `dense` bench exists; checked-in 2026-02-03 results are 80x24/120x40/200x60 (identical 1.81 µs).
- README.md:2440-2455 credits `scripts/solve_sos_barrier.py`, which never existed in git history.
- README.md:2030 names `no_flicker_proof.rs`; the file is `crates/ftui-harness/tests/render_no_flicker_proof.rs`.
- AGENTS.md:57-65 Key Dependencies lists `crossterm | Terminal backend (events, raw mode, ANSI)`; AGENTS.md:272-297 architecture diagram "TerminalSession (crossterm) -> Event"; AGENTS.md:148 and :187 and :326 claim `tests/` holds cross-component integration tests (it holds shell E2E scripts and fixtures only); AGENTS.md:216-254 doctor_frankentui verification block describes CI jobs that have never executed a gate (both workflows die at VHS install; Section 5.1).
- No `docs/claims-ledger.md`, no `scripts/check_readme_claims.py`, no allowlist file. The `docs` CI job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:86-117`) runs rustdoc tests and builds harness examples; nothing reads README.

Status-label rows (not API mismatches but claims that must carry a label after G07): every "Alien Artifact" subsection gets "wired by default", "opt-in", "demo-only", or "experimental" per Section 2.2.B, owned by `g06-docs-readme` with the module status supplied by `g07-impl` (quarantine list) and the wiring beads (`g08-impl` width cache, `g09-impl` a11y, `g10-impl` VirtualizedList, `g11-impl` conformal, `g12-impl` BOCPD, `g13-impl` controllers, `g14-impl` keybindings, `g18-impl` gesture/hover, `g19-impl` hint ranker, `g20-impl` evidence, `g28-impl` SAT and caps ledger, `g24-impl` lanes/scheduler, `g23-impl` web).

## Target state

`docs/claims-ledger.md` maps every tracked claim (the 37 rows above, the status-label rows, and the 71 vision rows) to a proof and a status; `scripts/check_readme_claims.py` runs in the `docs` job and fails when README.md or AGENTS.md contains a tracked number or backticked identifier without a ledger row, or when a ledger row's proof no longer exists; README.md and AGENTS.md are rewritten once against the ledger, in the order Installation and Quick Start (G01), Minimal API Example (G02), Workspace Overview, Demo Showcase Gallery, Widget System, Table Theming, Alien Artifact sections, Performance Engineering, Runtime Migration, Web/WASM, Synchronized Output (G05), Benchmarks (G25), FAQ counts; an "Experimental modules" README section lists G07's quarantined modules with the feature flag.

## Implementation plan (block level; one child bead each)

1. `g06-decision`: owner confirms (or amends) the decision table; default "accept as listed".
2. `g06-impl-ledger`: write the ledger seeded from the table and the 71 vision rows.
3. `g06-impl-checker`: the script, the allowlist, CI wiring, and hooks for G02 (example identity), G20 (telemetry literals), G25 (benchmark block hash), G05 (compat matrix freshness).
4. `g06-tests`: self-tests proving the checker fails on a seeded broken claim.
5. `g06-docs-readme`: the README rewrite in the fixed order, DOC rows enumerated with replacement text direction.
6. `g06-docs-agents`: AGENTS.md truth.
7. `g06-docs-getting-started`: getting-started consistency pass.

## Files to change

`docs/claims-ledger.md` (new), `docs/claims-allowlist.txt` (new), `scripts/check_readme_claims.py` (new), `scripts/tests/test_check_readme_claims.py` (new), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`docs` job), `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/getting-started.md`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `scripts/check_readme_claims.py` runs in the `docs` job; it extracts every backticked identifier and every number with a unit or count noun from README.md and AGENTS.md, requires a ledger row, and verifies each row's proof exists (`cargo test -- --list` output for test names; `test -e` for paths; `rg` for identifiers in `crates/*/src`).
- [ ] Ledger has 100% coverage of the 37 rows above with each row marked CODE (linking the closing bead) or DOC (linking the README diff), plus the 71 vision rows.
- [ ] README doc-tests (G02) green after the rewrite.
- [ ] A seeded broken claim fails the checker (`g06-tests`), verified in CI once.
- [ ] `rg -n '46 (interactive )?(demo )?screens|80\+ (direct )?widget|850K|850,000' README.md AGENTS.md` returns nothing.

## Tests and logging

Checker self-tests (`g06-tests`); the checker's `--report` output (counts of claims, proven, unproven, allowlisted) printed to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` on every `docs` run; README doc-tests.

## Dependencies and ordering

- `g06-impl-ledger` and `g06-decision` can start immediately (pure DOC rows need no code).
- `g06-docs-readme` is blocked by `g06-decision`, `g06-impl-ledger`, `g06-impl-checker`, `g01-docs`, `g02-impl`, `g05-docs`, `g07-impl` (to know what is experimental), `g25-impl` (numbers).
- Unblocks: `g34-impl` (governance docs refresh), `g42-impl` (which requires the ledger at 100% with proofs).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative: generate README from code. Rejected: README is prose with judgment; a ledger plus a checker keeps prose human while making claims machine-verified.
- Risk: the checker becomes noisy on prose numbers ("three strategies"); the allowlist with a reason column and a rule that only numbers adjacent to unit/count nouns are tracked keeps it sane.
- Risk: CODE rows land over months and README must stay true at every commit; therefore the rewrite describes only what exists at merge time and each CODE bead updates its row and README line when it lands (written into each CODE bead's definition of done via the ledger's "owner" column).
- No deletion: sections are rewritten, never removed; modules named in README that become experimental move to the "Experimental modules" section instead of disappearing.

## Definition of done

All seven child beads closed; `docs` job green with the checker (run id); ledger 100% with proofs; README and AGENTS.md rewritten; `g42-impl` can cite the ledger report.

Expect on the order of 150-300 N rows; split the work across parallel subagents by README section (AGENTS.md rule: no script-based edits of the docs, but the ledger itself is data and may be appended by the checker's `--append-missing` mode, which writes rows with `status: unproven` for a human to fill).

What NOT to do: no line-number-only locations (text anchors are required for re-location); no proofs of the form `manual:` for anything a test or path can prove; no deletion of README text from this bead (the ledger records, the docs beads edit); no second ledger file per crate.

## Files to change

- `docs/claims-ledger.md`: new.
- `docs/claims-allowlist.txt`: initial prose-number entries discovered in step 5 (shared with `g06-impl-checker`, which owns the format).
