- [ ] `scripts/check_readme_claims.py --check` reports zero tracked claims without a row (after the N rows/allowlist) and lists `pending-*` rows without failing on them (they fail only when their owning bead is closed and the proof is still missing).
- [ ] `scripts/check_readme_claims.py --report` shows `proven >= 60%` of rows at ledger creation (WORKING rows), with the remainder `pending-code`/`pending-doc`.
- [ ] The file's proof grammar section is the same text the checker prints in `--help`.

## Tests and logging

The checker's self-tests (`g06-tests`) include a case that parses the real ledger and asserts column integrity (unique ids, valid enums, every CODE row has an owner). Report JSON `target/claims/report.json` with `{rows, proven, pending_code, pending_doc, retracted, allowlisted, unproven, missing_rows: [...]}` uploaded by the `docs` job.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: nothing (decision outcomes from `g06-decision` are folded in when known; rows default to the proposed table). Unblocks: `g06-impl-checker` (needs the file format to exist), `g06-docs-readme`, `g06-docs-agents`, `g06-docs-getting-started`, `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative: YAML/JSON ledger. Rejected: a markdown table is readable in the repo and on GitHub and is still trivially parseable with fixed columns.
- Risk: a large ledger goes stale. The `last_verified` stamp and the checker's CI run make staleness visible; `g37-impl`'s monthly reality-check job diffs the ledger.
- Risk: `bead:<slug>` proofs let CODE rows sit pending forever; the checker fails a `bead:` proof once the bead is closed (read-only `br show` or `.beads/issues.jsonl`) so closing a CODE bead without landing its proof breaks the `docs` job, which is the intended enforcement of "reachable from production" as definition of done.

## Definition of done

Ledger on main, checker green on it, coverage numbers in the close reason, `g06-epic` and `g06-decision` consistent with the `decision`/`owner` columns.
notes: Refinement 4 supersedes proven>=60% as an acceptance requirement. Ledger completeness and truthful classification matter; a target percentage incentivizes false proof. Path/identifier/test-name existence establishes only presence, while behavioral claims need actual scoped passing results and artifact identity. Preserve pending/experimental/external status and all 71 goals plus new obligations; map formatting and real renderer to their new concrete tasks.

title: task(G06): scripts/check_readme_claims.py with allowlist, proof verification and docs-job CI wiring
description:
## Context and why this matters

Nothing fails when README.md or AGENTS.md drift from the code. That is why the April 2026 truth pass (bd-1zmo3) regressed and why the 2026-09-01 reality check (`ab07291f`) found 37 mismatch rows, wrong counts in a dozen places, benchmark numbers no bench produces, a credited script that never existed, and a proof file with the wrong name. The ledger (`g06-impl-ledger`) records what each claim's proof is; this bead writes the script that enforces it in the `docs` CI job and provides the hooks other blocks rely on: README example byte-identity (G02), telemetry string-literal grep (G20: no `"ftui."` literal outside `telemetry_schema.rs`), benchmark block hash (G25: README "Benchmark Suite" block must equal what `scripts/render_perf_readme.py` produced), compat-matrix freshness (G05), widget and line counts (rows C31, C32), and crates.io version (C33). It closes reality-check root cause 1 mechanically and is required by `g42-impl` ("claims-ledger report" in the verification archive).

## Current state (evidence)

- No `scripts/check_readme_claims.py`, no `docs/claims-allowlist.txt`, no `scripts/tests/` directory (`ls scripts | rg check_readme` empty).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `docs` job (:86-117): checkout, nightly toolchain, cache, `cargo test --doc --workspace` (:111), `cargo build --examples -p ftui-harness` (:117). Python is not set up in this job (the `e2e-widget-api` job at :389-392 uses `actions/setup-python@v6` with 3.11).
- README.md claims to track (examples): counts (`850K+`, `20 crates`, `80+`, `46`, `57`, `419 insta snapshots`, `17 library crates`, `16-byte Cell`, `13K+ line program.rs`, `9K+ lines`, `1,900+ Lines`, `3,200+ Lines`, `257 lines`), badges (`img.shields.io/badge/crates-20-blue`, `widgets-80%2B`, `demo_screens-46`), identifiers in backticks (`ScreenMode::Inline { ui_height: 10 }`, `BufferDiff::compute(&prev, &next)`, `TerminalWriter`, `TerminalSession`, `PaneTree`, `PaneDragResizeMachine`, `ShadowRun::compare()`, `FTUI_HARNESS_VIEW`, `BLESS=1`, ...), paths (`docs/getting-started.md`, `scripts/pane_e2e.sh`, `no_flicker_proof.rs`), and benchmark numbers with units (`1.2 µs`, `4.2 Mcells/s`).
- README Minimal API Example is at README.md:139-190 and must be byte-identical to `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs` (created by `g01-impl-facade`).
- `cargo test -- --list` prints `<path>: <name>: test` lines per binary; `cargo nextest list` (after `g03-impl-nextest`) prints `<binary> <name>`; either can feed the `test:` proof kind.
- `rg` is available locally and, after `g04-06-impl`, on CI runners; the script must fall back to Python regex search when `rg` is missing (and say so).
- Production widget count method used by the audit: Python count of distinct `impl Widget for X` / `impl StatefulWidget for X` outside `#[cfg(test)]` under `crates/ftui-widgets/src` -> 57 (names in the audit's `prod_impls.txt`: Align, Badge, Block, Budgeted, CachedWidget, ClickableList, Columns, CommandPalette, ConstraintOverlay, CustomErrorBoundary, DebugOverlay, DebugOverlayStateful, DecisionCard, Dialog, DialogContent, DragPreview, DriftVisualization, Emoji, ErrorBoundary, FallbackWidget, FancyProgressBar, FilePicker, Group, Help, HistoryPanel, InspectorOverlay, JsonView, KeybindingHints, Layout, List, LogViewer, MiniBar, Modal, MyWidget, NotificationStack, Padding, Paginator, Panel, Paragraph, Pretty, ProgressBar, ReceiptVerifierPanel, Rule, Scrollbar, Sparkline, Spinner, StatusLine, Stopwatch, Table, Tabs, TextArea, TextInput, Timer, Toast, Tree, ValidationErrorDisplay, VirtualizedList, VoiDebugOverlay; note `MyWidget` and `Layout` look like doc-example or helper types and the counting rule must exclude rustdoc code blocks and `examples/` so the final number is defensible and stated in the ledger with the rule).
- Rust line count method: `find crates -name '*.rs' | xargs wc -l` -> 1,053,170 in 967 files.

## Target state

`scripts/check_readme_claims.py` (Python 3.11, stdlib only; `rg` optional):
- `--check` (default): parse `docs/claims-ledger.md` (fixed columns), extract claims from `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` (and `docs/getting-started.md`, `docs/compat-matrix.md` when `--docs` is given), require a ledger row or allowlist entry for each, verify every row's proof, print a summary, exit 1 on: missing row, failed proof of a `proven` row, `bead:` proof whose bead is closed, expired `manual:` proof, allowlist entry without a reason, ledger column error.
- Extraction rules: (a) backticked spans that match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_:!<>()\[\]., &'*=-]*$` and contain a Rust identifier of length >= 3 or a path with `/` or an env var `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{3,}=?`; (b) numbers adjacent (within 2 tokens) to a unit or count noun from a fixed list (`lines?, crates?, widgets?, screens?, tests?, snapshots?, goldens?, targets?, scripts?, bytes?, ms, µs, us, ns, s, Mcells/s, Kcells/s, %, K\+, M\+, x`), including `K+`/`,000+` forms and shields.io badge values; (c) markdown links to repo paths. Claims are normalised (whitespace, trailing punctuation) into a key; the ledger's `claim` column is matched by exact normalised key or by a `match:` regex in the row.
- Proof verifiers: `test:<crate>::<name>` -> present in `target/claims/test-list.txt` (produced by a CI step `cargo nextest list --workspace > target/claims/test-list.txt` or `cargo test --workspace -- --list`; the script also accepts `--test-list PATH`); `path:` -> exists; `ident:` -> found in `crates/*/src/**/*.rs` outside `#[cfg(test)]` modules (heuristic: lines before the first `#[cfg(test)]` in each file) via `rg -n --fixed-strings` or Python fallback; `cmd:` -> `subprocess.run(shell=True)` exit 0 with a 60 s timeout; `job:<workflow.yml>:<job>` -> job key exists in the YAML (simple regex, no PyYAML); `count:<expr>` -> evaluated in a restricted namespace exposing `read(path, start, end)`, `count_lines(glob)`, `re`, `len`; `manual:<date>:<who>` -> date within 90 days; `bead:<slug>` -> slug present in `.beads/issues.jsonl` with status not closed (read-only; never invokes `br` mutations).
- Subcommands/hooks: `--example-identity` (README fence after `## Minimal API Example` vs `crates/ftui/examples/minimal_inline.rs`, byte-exact after stripping the fence line; also used by `g01-e2e`); `--count-widgets [--expect N]` (rule: distinct type names in `impl (Widget|StatefulWidget) for <Type>` under `crates/ftui-widgets/src`, excluding matches inside rustdoc ``` blocks, `#[cfg(test)]` regions, and files under `examples/`; prints the sorted list); `--count-lines [--min N]`; `--telemetry-literals` (fail if a string literal starting with `"ftui.` appears in `crates/*/src/**/*.rs` outside `crates/ftui-runtime/src/telemetry_schema.rs`; wired by `g20-impl`, off by default until then); `--bench-block-hash` (sha256 of the README "Benchmark Suite" fenced block equals the hash recorded in `docs/perf/baseline_<date>.md` front matter; wired by `g25-impl`); `--compat-matrix-fresh` (the `Generated:` date in `docs/compat-matrix.md` is newer than the last git commit touching `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_capabilities.rs`, `caps_probe.rs`, `inline_mode.rs`, `crates/ftui-runtime/src/terminal_writer.rs`; wired by `g05-e2e`); `--crates-io <crate> --min-version X` (network; skipped with a warning when offline or `--offline`); `--extract` (print extracted claims as JSON for ledger seeding); `--append-missing` (append `N` rows with `status: unproven`); `--report` (markdown table for `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`) and `--json target/claims/report.json`; `--stamp` (write `last_verified`); `--verify-owners` (every CODE row's owner slug exists in `.beads/issues.jsonl`).
- `docs/claims-allowlist.txt`: one entry per line `<literal>\t<reason>\t<added-by-bead>`; the checker rejects entries without a reason; allowlisted literals are reported with counts so growth is visible.
- CI: `docs` job gains `actions/setup-python@v6` (3.11), a step producing `target/claims/test-list.txt`, `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'` (self-tests from `g06-tests`), then `python3 scripts/check_readme_claims.py --check --docs --report >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY --json target/claims/report.json`, and an `actions/upload-artifact@v7` step (`claims-report`, always). AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks" gains the command (via `g06-docs-agents`).

## Implementation plan

1. Write the script with a small module layout inside one file: `Ledger` (parse/validate/stamp), `Extractor`, `Proofs` (one function per kind), `Hooks` (the subcommands), `main`. Keep it under ~900 lines; no third-party packages.
2. Write `docs/claims-allowlist.txt` with the format header and the first entries from the ledger seeding run (dates like `2026-02-03`, version numbers like `0.6.0`, ordinal prose like "three strategies" only if they escape the unit rule, ADR numbers, `Rust 2024`, `128 + signal`).
3. Wire the `docs` job steps; make the first CI run in `--report`-only mode is not allowed (no `continue-on-error`); instead land the script together with a ledger that passes (`g06-impl-ledger` step 5 has already produced the N rows and allowlist), i.e. this bead's CI wiring merges in the same PR as the ledger seeding finish or immediately after it on a green run.
4. Add the hooks' wiring points as no-ops that print "not enabled" until their owning beads flip them (`--telemetry-literals`, `--bench-block-hash`, `--compat-matrix-fresh` are enabled by a `[hooks]` section in the ledger header listing which are active, so the owning beads enable them by editing the ledger, not the script).
5. Document usage in the script's module docstring and in `docs/claims-ledger.md` header (same grammar text; `g06-tests` asserts they match).
6. Run locally: `python3 scripts/check_readme_claims.py --check` against the current README to seed; `--example-identity` fails until `g01-impl-facade` (expected; the hook is enabled by the ledger `[hooks]` list once that bead lands).

What NOT to do: the script must never modify README.md/AGENTS.md (AGENTS.md "No Script-Based Changes"; it only reads docs and may append rows to the ledger under `--append-missing`, which is data, and even that is off in CI); no PyYAML or other dependencies; no `rm`; no network in `--check` unless `--crates-io` is explicitly requested; no `continue-on-error` in CI.

## Files to change

- `scripts/check_readme_claims.py`: new.
- `docs/claims-allowlist.txt`: new.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `docs` job steps (python setup, test list, self-tests, checker, artifact).
- `docs/claims-ledger.md`: `[hooks]` header section (coordinate with `g06-impl-ledger`).

## Success criteria

- [ ] `python3 scripts/check_readme_claims.py --check --docs` exits 0 on main after the ledger and rewrite land; `docs` job green (run id).
- [ ] Seeded broken claim fails: `g06-tests` case `seeded_broken_count_fails` and one real CI verification (a scratch branch restoring "46 screens" in README turns the `docs` job red with the claim and line printed; run id recorded in `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md` "Claims gate" section).
- [ ] `--example-identity` green after `g01-impl-facade`; `--count-widgets --expect 57` green (or the number the documented rule yields, recorded in ledger row C31 with the rule); `--count-lines --min 1000000` green.
- [ ] `--report` shows counts; `target/claims/report.json` uploaded.
- [ ] Runtime under 60 s in CI excluding the test-list step.

## Tests and logging

Self-tests in `scripts/tests/test_check_readme_claims.py` (`g06-tests`). Report JSON fields: `{"generated", "commit", "files": [...], "claims_total", "claims_matched", "claims_missing": [{"file","line","claim"}], "rows_total", "proven", "pending_code", "pending_doc", "retracted", "allowlisted", "unproven", "failed_proofs": [{"id","proof","reason"}], "hooks": {"example_identity": "ok|fail|disabled", ...}}`. Human summary lines prefixed `[claims]`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g06-impl-ledger` (file format and seed). Unblocks: `g06-tests`, `g06-docs-readme`, `g06-docs-agents`, `g06-docs-getting-started`, and the hook consumers `g20-impl`, `g25-impl`, `g05-e2e`, `g02-tests` (which cites `--example-identity`), `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Alternative: a Rust binary in `ftui-harness`. Rejected: the check must run in seconds in the `docs` job without a build; Python stdlib is enough.
- Risk: false positives on prose. Mitigated by the unit/count-noun rule, the allowlist with reasons, and `--extract` for review before enabling.
- Risk: `cmd:` proofs run arbitrary shell in CI; restrict to commands starting with `rg`, `python3 scripts/`, `test`, `!`, `grep`, `wc`, `find` (a fixed prefix allowlist in the script) and document it.
- Rollback: remove the CI step; the ledger remains useful as documentation.

## Definition of done

Script, allowlist and CI steps on main; green run id; red verification run id; hooks documented; AGENTS.md command added (`g06-docs-agents`).
notes: Refinement 4: checker must distinguish presence proof, compile proof, behavioral/host evidence and statistical claims. Reject mismatched evidence kind, unavailable/failed/stale test run, closed bead without actual proof, and hard-coded count games. Resolve current inventory and supported features; native release mandatory rows fail if pending, diagnostic reports retain honest incomplete status.

title: task(G06): Checker self-tests: seeded broken claims fail, allowlist honored, proofs verified, example identity
description:
## Context

`g06-impl-checker` adds `scripts/check_readme_claims.py`, which fails the `docs` CI job when README.md or AGENTS.md contain a tracked claim without a ledger row or when a ledger row's proof no longer exists. A gate that has never failed proves nothing (the same reasoning as `g02-tests` for doc-tests and `g03-impl-nextest` for timeouts). This bead writes the checker's self-tests (stdlib `unittest`, run in the `docs` job before the checker) and records the one-time real-CI verification that a seeded broken claim turns the job red. It also pins the counting rules (widgets, lines, screens) so the numbers in README are reproducible, and asserts the ledger's structural integrity so that `g06-impl-ledger`'s data cannot rot silently.

## What to test

1. Extraction: backticked identifiers, unit/count numbers, badge values, path links are found with file and line; prose numbers without unit nouns are not.
2. Matching: exact normalised key and `match:` regex rows; allowlist entries with reasons; allowlist entries without reasons are rejected.
3. Proof verifiers: `test:` (against a test-list file), `path:`, `ident:` (outside `#[cfg(test)]`), `cmd:` (prefix allowlist; timeout), `job:`, `count:` (restricted namespace), `manual:` (expiry), `bead:` (closed bead fails).
4. Hooks: `--example-identity`, `--count-widgets`, `--count-lines`, `--telemetry-literals`, `--bench-block-hash`, `--compat-matrix-fresh` (enabled/disabled via the ledger `[hooks]` section).
5. Exit codes and report JSON shape.
6. Ledger integrity on the real `docs/claims-ledger.md`: unique ids, valid enums, CODE rows have an owner, proof grammar in the ledger header equals the script's `--help` grammar text.
7. Seeded broken claim: a temp copy of the real README with "46 screens" restored fails with the claim and line reported.

## Test types (unit, property, bench, E2E) with names and assertions

`scripts/tests/test_check_readme_claims.py` (`unittest`; imports the script as a module via `importlib` from `scripts/`; every test builds its fixtures in `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()`; no network; no `rg` dependency: tests run with the Python fallback and, when `rg` is present, again with it by parametrising `use_rg`):
- `test_extracts_backticked_identifiers_and_paths`: README fixture with `` `BufferDiff::compute(&prev, &next)` ``, `` `docs/getting-started.md` ``, `` `FTUI_SYNC_OUTPUT=1` ``; assert three claims with correct line numbers and kinds (`api`, `file`, `env`).
- `test_extracts_numbers_with_unit_nouns_only`: "45 screens", "1.81 µs", "16-byte Cell", "419 insta snapshots", `badge/demo_screens-45-blue` extracted; "three strategies" and "Section 2" not.
- `test_missing_row_fails_with_location`: one claim, empty ledger -> exit 1, `claims_missing` contains `{file, line, claim}`.
- `test_allowlist_requires_reason`: allowlist line without a reason -> exit 1 with the allowlist line number; with a reason -> claim is `allowlisted`.
- `test_match_regex_row`: ledger row with `match:^\d+ screens$` matches "45 screens".
- `test_proof_test_kind_uses_test_list`: row `test:ftui-demo-showcase::all_screens_count`; test-list file with and without the name -> pass/fail.
- `test_proof_path_kind`: existing and missing paths.
- `test_proof_ident_kind_ignores_cfg_test`: a fixture crate file where the identifier appears only after `#[cfg(test)]` -> fail; before -> pass.
- `test_proof_cmd_kind_prefix_allowlist_and_timeout`: `cmd:rg -n foo file` passes/fails by exit code; `cmd:curl ...` rejected as disallowed prefix; a `cmd:python3 scripts/...` that sleeps past the timeout fails with `timeout` reason (use a 1 s timeout override in tests).
- `test_proof_job_kind_parses_workflow_yaml`: fixture workflow with `jobs:\n  docs:\n` -> `job:ci.yml:docs` passes; `job:ci.yml:nope` fails.
- `test_proof_count_kind_restricted_namespace`: `count:len(read('a.rs',1,10))>0` passes; `count:__import__('os')` rejected.
- `test_proof_manual_expires_after_90_days`: date 91 days ago fails; 89 passes.
- `test_proof_bead_kind_fails_when_closed`: fixture `.beads/issues.jsonl` with the slug open -> pass; closed -> fail with reason `bead closed but proof missing`.
- `test_example_identity_hook`: README fixture with a `## Minimal API Example` fence and an example file: identical -> ok; one byte differs -> fail with a unified diff in the reason.
- `test_count_widgets_rule`: fixture `crates/ftui-widgets/src/{a.rs,b.rs}` with `impl Widget for A`, `impl StatefulWidget for B`, a rustdoc fence containing `impl Widget for Fake`, and a `#[cfg(test)]` region with `impl Widget for T` -> count 2 and sorted names `[A, B]` (the fixture must avoid the words mock/fake/stub in file names to keep the CI no-mock grep quiet; use `Sample`).
- `test_count_lines_rule`: two files, known line counts.
- `test_telemetry_literals_hook`: `"ftui.render"` literal in a fixture file outside `telemetry_schema.rs` -> fail when enabled; pass when disabled via `[hooks]`.
- `test_bench_block_hash_hook` and `test_compat_matrix_fresh_hook`: fixture files with matching/mismatching hash and dates.
- `test_report_json_shape`: keys `generated, commit, files, claims_total, claims_matched, claims_missing, rows_total, proven, pending_code, pending_doc, retracted, allowlisted, unproven, failed_proofs, hooks` present.
- `test_real_ledger_integrity` (runs against the repo's `docs/claims-ledger.md`; skipped with a message if the file is absent): unique ids; `kind`, `decision`, `status` in their enums; every `decision == CODE` row has `owner != '-'`; header proof grammar equals `checker.PROOF_GRAMMAR`.
- `test_seeded_broken_claim_fails_on_real_readme` (skipped if README lacks the ledgered form): copy `README.md` to a temp dir, replace the first occurrence of the ledgered screen count line with "46 screens", run `--check` with the real ledger -> exit 1 and the missing/failed claim names "46 screens" with the line number.
- `test_cli_exit_codes`: `--check` clean -> 0; missing row -> 1; failed proof -> 1; `--report` never changes the exit code.

CI verification (one-time, recorded): on a scratch branch, change README's screen count back to 46 (or add a backticked `NoSuchType` identifier), push, observe the `docs` job fail at the checker step with the claim and line, record the run id and log excerpt in `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md` "Claims gate" section, remove the change on the branch (branch not deleted by the agent).

No bench; property-style coverage of the extractor via a table of 30 prose lines with expected extraction results (`test_extractor_table`).

## Logging (structured JSONL fields, tracing targets)

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py' -v` output in the `docs` job log; failures print the fixture directory listing and the checker's stderr.
- The checker's `--json` report from the seeded-failure test is attached to the close reason.

## Files

- `scripts/tests/__init__.py` (empty) and `scripts/tests/test_check_readme_claims.py`: new.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `docs` job: the unittest step precedes the checker (wired by `g06-impl-checker`; this bead adds `-v` and a failure artifact upload of `scripts/tests` output if desired).
- `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md`: "Claims gate" section (run ids, procedure).

## Success criteria

- [ ] All tests above green locally (`python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`) and in the `docs` job (run id).
- [ ] `test_seeded_broken_claim_fails_on_real_readme` green (i.e. the real README plus real ledger catch a restored wrong count).
- [ ] Real-CI red verification recorded with run id in `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md`.
- [ ] `test_real_ledger_integrity` green on main.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `g06-impl-checker` (the module under test) and transitively `g06-impl-ledger`. Unblocks: `g06-docs-readme` (the rewrite lands on a proven gate), `g42-impl`.

## Definition of done

Tests on main and in CI; seeded-failure verification recorded; close reason lists the test names, the green `docs` run id and the red verification run id.

title: docs(G06): Rewrite README.md against the claims ledger: counts, APIs, layouts, defaults, diagram, labels
description:
## Context and why this matters

description:
## Context and why this matters

AGENTS.md is read by every agent before it touches the tree, so an untrue AGENTS.md propagates errors into code and beads. The 2026-09-01 reality check (`ab07291f`) found: the Key Dependencies table (AGENTS.md:57-65) presents `crossterm` as "Terminal backend (events, raw mode, ANSI)" although `crossterm` is optional and labelled legacy in `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml` and the native `ftui-tty` backend is the stated preference (after G01 both are enabled by the facade's `backend` default); the architecture diagram (:272-297) says "TerminalSession (crossterm) -> Event (ftui-core)"; the Testing Policy (:148), Test Categories row (:187) and Workspace Structure (:326) say cross-component integration tests live in the workspace `tests/` directory, which contains shell E2E scripts and fixtures and no Rust files (vision row V69 WRONG); the tree lists "46 screens" (:310) and "80+ widgets" (:324); the `doctor_frankentui` verification block (:216-254) describes a CI job (`doctor-frankentui-verification`) that has never executed a doctor gate because both workflows die at VHS install (`ci.yml:1147` `find ... | head` under `set -euo pipefail`; `doctor_frankentui_extended.yml:85` installs `/tmp/vhs` while the tarball extracts to `/tmp/vhs_0.10.0_Linux_x86_64/vhs`; 68 of 79 steps skipped; scheduled runs red every day since 2026-08-06); Compiler Checks (:120-135) lacks the nextest command (G03), the claims check (G06) and the facade doc-tests (G02); "Landing the Plane" (:785-796) has no link to a green run. This bead makes AGENTS.md true and adds the new gates so agents run them. It closes V69 and the AGENTS.md half of decision-table row C29, and gives `g37-impl` (process guardrails) a truthful base.

## Current state (evidence)

Verify each against `Cargo.toml` files before rewriting (e.g. whether `unicode-width` is still the width source: the production width path is `ftui_core::text_width::grapheme_width`; check `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml` for the crate actually used).

## Context and why this matters

integration tests, fuzz targets exist, 74 E2E scripts exist", and AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks (CRITICAL)"
(AGENTS.md:120-136) makes `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
-- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` mandatory after every change. The reality-check of 2026-09-01
(vision rows V70 "Mandatory gates green (check/clippy/fmt/tests)" = PARTIAL locally, RED in CI; V68
"doctor_frankentui verification stack" = daily CI failure; Section 2.2 letter E "CI, test health, and
process") found that **no `ci.yml` run on `main` has been green in the last 40 runs (all failures since
2026-07-08)** and that the nightly `doctor_frankentui Extended Verification` workflow has been red on
30 of 30 runs since 2026-08-06. Red CI is normalized, so failures carry no signal: the runtime test hang
(G03) survived since March because nothing distinguished it from runner starvation, and a Windows clippy
break, a fuzz manifest break, and several env-leak bugs all shipped silently.

The user-visible consequence: a contributor (or the owner) cannot tell whether a change broke anything;
release confidence is zero; and every other block of the reality-check plan (G01 default backend, G05
sync-output probing, G06 claims ledger, G25 perf gates, G42 final verification) needs a green baseline to
prove itself against. This cluster is therefore on the critical path for the whole bridge plan
(Section 7.5: `G03 --> G04 --> G42`; `G04.3 --> G01`; `G04.7 --> G22`; `G04.12 --> G25`; `G04.13 --> G23`).

title: bug(G04.1): Stop E2E seed env vars leaking into cargo test (Widget API E2E, Demo Showcase)
description:
# bug(G04.1): Stop E2E seed env vars leaking into `cargo test` (Widget API E2E, Demo Showcase jobs)

## Context and why this matters

README.md promises deterministic E2E runs ("Use deterministic fixtures for stable hashes and reproducible
logs: `E2E_DETERMINISTIC=1 E2E_SEED=0 ...`", README.md:415-421) and AGENTS.md lists
`./scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh` and `./scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh` as the E2E gates (AGENTS.md:206-209).
Vision rows served: V70 (mandatory gates green) and V35 (property tests, snapshots); Section 2.2 letter E.
Today both CI jobs are red for the same reason: the E2E scripts export seed variables meant for the PTY
binaries into the whole shell, then run `cargo test`, so unit tests and insta snapshots that have their
own default seed see the E2E seed instead. The user-visible consequence is two permanently red jobs
("Widget API E2E" 98788563849 and "Demo Showcase" 98788563924 in run 33152820289) that hide any real
widget/showcase regression.

## Current state (evidence)

- `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh:54-64` `e2e_seed_init` defaults `E2E_SEED` to `E2E_DEFAULT_SEED:-0` when
  `E2E_DETERMINISTIC` (default 1) is set. `common.sh:95-105` `e2e_export_deterministic_env` then
  `export`s `FTUI_TEST_DETERMINISTIC=1`, `FTUI_DEMO_DETERMINISTIC=1`, `FTUI_SEED`, `FTUI_HARNESS_SEED`,
  `FTUI_DEMO_SEED`, `FTUI_TEST_SEED` all `= $seed` (0). `common.sh:181-198` `e2e_fixture_init` calls it.
- `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh:99` `e2e_fixture_init "widget_api"`; :113-114
  `SEED="${E2E_SEED:-${FTUI_HARNESS_SEED:-0}}"; export FTUI_HARNESS_SEED="${FTUI_HARNESS_SEED:-$SEED}"`;
  :477 `cargo build --workspace`; :481 `cargo test --workspace --lib -- --test-threads=4` (Step 2
  "Running unit tests") inherits every exported seed.
- `crates/ftui-harness/src/determinism.rs:517-524` `fixture_seed(default_seed)` reads `FTUI_TEST_SEED`,
  `FTUI_SEED`, `FTUI_HARNESS_SEED`, `E2E_SEED`, `E2E_CONTEXT_SEED` in that order before the default;
  `:36-38` `DeterminismFixture::new(prefix, default_seed)` calls it; `:234-236`
  `TestJsonlLogger::new(prefix, default_seed)` wraps it. Test `:639-647`
  `jsonl_logger_emits_core_fields` does `TestJsonlLogger::new("jsonl_logger", 99)` and asserts the line
  contains `"seed":99`; under the script it contains `"seed":0`. (Sibling tests `:650`
  `jsonl_logger_includes_context` and `:659` `lab_scenario_reports_deterministic_metadata` use seeds 7
  and 4242 through the same path.)
- `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh:95` `e2e_fixture_init "demo_showcase"`; :356 `run_step "Unit + snapshot
  tests" ... cargo test -p "$PKG" -- --test-threads=4 || true` — the `|| true` only masks the shell status;
  `run_step` (:150-163) records `exit_code=1` and `FAIL_COUNT` makes the script exit non-zero (:2601-2608).
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/determinism.rs:52-54` `demo_seed(default)` reads `FTUI_DEMO_SEED`,
  `FTUI_SEED`, `E2E_SEED`; `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/determinism_lab.rs:41`
  `const DEFAULT_SEED: u64 = 7;` and `:238` `seed: determinism::demo_seed(DEFAULT_SEED)`. Snapshot
  `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/snapshots/determinism_lab_initial_80x24.snap:1` reads
  `Determinism Lab  Seed: 7  Frame: 0 ...` (also `app_determinismlab_80x24.snap:3` and
  `determinism_lab_fault_120x40.snap:1`); test `tests/screen_snapshots.rs:2249-2256`
  `determinism_lab_initial_80x24`. Under the script the screen renders `Seed: 0`.
- The CI jobs (`ci.yml:376-436` `e2e-widget-api`, `:438-526` `demo-showcase`) run the scripts with
  `E2E_JSONL_VALIDATE=1`; the separate `cargo test ... screen_snapshots` step at `:490-491` is fine because
  step environments do not leak — only the in-script `cargo test` invocations are affected.

## Target state

Seed variables are scoped to the PTY invocations that need them and never reach `cargo test`; the tests
that assert a specific seed are robust even if a seed variable is present; both CI jobs are green and a
unit test proves the scoping rule.

## Implementation plan

1. `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh`: split `e2e_export_deterministic_env` into (a) `e2e_deterministic_env_args`
   which *prints* the `KEY=VALUE` pairs (for use as `env $(e2e_deterministic_env_args) <bin>` or as
   inline prefixes) and (b) the existing exporter, which stays for scripts that only run PTY binaries.
   Add `e2e_cargo_test_env_guard`: a function that runs its arguments with `env -u FTUI_SEED -u
   FTUI_HARNESS_SEED -u FTUI_DEMO_SEED -u FTUI_TEST_SEED -u E2E_SEED -u E2E_CONTEXT_SEED -u
   FTUI_TEST_TIME_STEP_MS -u E2E_TIME_STEP_MS` so any `cargo test` inside an E2E script is hermetic, and
   logs a `jsonl_assert "cargo_test_env_hermetic" "pass" "unset=<list>"` line.
2. `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh`: remove the global `export FTUI_HARNESS_SEED` at :113-114; keep `SEED` as
   a plain variable; wrap the `cargo test --workspace --lib` step (:481) and the snapshot step (:647) in
   `e2e_cargo_test_env_guard`; pass the seed to PTY runs explicitly (`FTUI_HARNESS_SEED="$SEED" pty_run
   ...`), following the existing inline-prefix style used at `tests/e2e/scripts/test_inline.sh:51-55`.
3. `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh`: wrap Step 4 (:356) in `e2e_cargo_test_env_guard`; keep
   `FTUI_DEMO_SEED="$E2E_SEED"` on the `pty_run` lines (already done that way in
   `tests/e2e/scripts/test_bidi_voi_overlay.sh:140-150`).
4. `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/determinism_lab.rs`: add `DeterminismLab::with_seed(seed: u64)`
   (or make the existing constructor take the seed explicitly and have `Default`/`new` call
   `demo_seed(DEFAULT_SEED)`); `tests/screen_snapshots.rs` determinism-lab cases construct the screen with
   `with_seed(7)` so snapshots do not depend on process environment. Do not add `cfg(test)` env reading
   hacks: tests must not mutate process env (racy under parallel tests).

title: task(G04.6): Install runner tooling (ripgrep, python websockets) and fail fast on missing tools
description:
# task(G04.6): Install runner tooling (ripgrep, python websockets) and fail fast on missing tools

## Context and why this matters

README.md and AGENTS.md present the PTY E2E suite (`tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh`, 74 scripts) and the
FrankenTerm conformance/WebSocket gates as release-blocking gates. Vision rows V70 (gates green) and
V61 (input parser E2E); Section 2.2 letter E; Section 5.1 rows "FrankenTerm Conformance/WS gates" and
"PTY E2E ubuntu / macos". Both jobs fail partly for a reason unrelated to the code: the runners lack
`rg` and the python `websockets` package, and the scripts do not check their prerequisites, so the
failures surface as opaque per-case failures (`rg: command not found` swallowed by `|| return 1`) and
mask the real assertion failures that G04.9 must triage. Until tooling is fixed, the 42/166 PTY
failures cannot be separated into "environment" and "bug".

## Current state (evidence)

- `ci.yml:528-562` `e2e-pty` job (ubuntu-latest, macos-latest): steps checkout, `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`
  nightly, `setup-python@v6` 3.x, cache, `./tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh`. No apt/brew step. By contrast
  `ci.yml:1121-1124` (doctor job) does `sudo apt-get install -y jq ripgrep ffmpeg`.
- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_inline.sh:57-58, 118-119, 135-140` use `rg -a -q "..." "$output_file" ||
  return 1`; under `set -euo pipefail` a missing `rg` exits 127 and the case fails as if the assertion
  failed. It is the only script under `tests/e2e/scripts/` that calls `rg` (grep on 2026-09-01); the
  others use `grep -a`. `ci.yml:600` (repro-bundle step) also uses `rg --files`.
- `ci.yml:63-71` (`check` job "Enforce no-mock policy"): `if rg -n -i '\b(mock|fake|stub)s?\b' crates
  tests ...; then ... exit 1; fi`. If `rg` is absent, the `if` condition is false (exit 127) and the gate
  silently passes — the policy is unenforced on any runner without ripgrep.
- `tests/e2e/lib/ws_client.py:43-47`: `try: import websockets except ImportError: print("ERROR:
  'websockets' package not available", file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(1)`;
  `tests/e2e/scripts/test_ws_protocol_compliance.sh:45-47` runs `ws_client.py --self-test` first and
  fails with `[FAIL] ws_client self-tests failed`; :58-69 embeds a second python program that also
  `import websockets`. `ci.yml:2147-2200` (`frankenterm-conformance-gates`) sets up python 3.x but never
  `pip install`s anything. Job 98788563820 failed with exactly the :46 message.
- `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh:24-30` already has `require_cmd <cmd>` (single command, prints "Missing
  required command: X"); nothing calls it from `run_all.sh`.

## Target state

Every workflow job that runs shell E2E installs its tools explicitly (ripgrep, jq, python `websockets`);
every E2E entry script checks all prerequisites up front and prints one line listing every missing tool
(exit code 2, distinct from test failure 1) and a JSONL `tools_missing` event; the no-mock policy step
fails loudly when `rg` is missing.

## Implementation plan

1. `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh`: add `require_tools <cmd>...` that collects all missing names, prints
   `Missing required tools: a b c (install: apt-get install ripgrep jq | brew install ripgrep jq; pip
   install websockets)` and returns 2; add `require_python_module <module>` using
   `"$E2E_PYTHON" -c "import <module>"`; if `logging.sh` is sourced, emit
   `jsonl_assert "tools_present" fail "missing=<list>"` before returning. Keep `require_cmd`.
2. `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh`: call `require_tools bash python3 jq rg awk sed xxd sha256sum` (verify
   `xxd`/`shasum` usage per OS: ci.yml:648 uses `xxd`; `sha256_file` in scripts — read `logging.sh` for
   the actual helper) right after `e2e_fixture_init "e2e"` (:36) and before building. Exit 2 on failure.
3. `tests/e2e/scripts/test_ws_protocol_compliance.sh`: `require_python_module websockets` at the top
   (after sourcing `common.sh`).
4. `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh`, `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh`, `scripts/e2e_test.sh`,
   `scripts/pane_e2e.sh`: same `require_tools` call with each script's real tool list (grep each script
   for `rg`, `jq`, `python3`, `xxd`, `ffmpeg` before writing the list).
5. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
   - `e2e-pty`: add step "Install E2E tooling" — ubuntu: `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y
     ripgrep jq xxd`; macos: `brew install ripgrep jq` (guard with `if: runner.os == ...`). Add
     `python -m pip install websockets` where the job runs ws tests.
   - `frankenterm-conformance-gates`: after setup-python add `python -m pip install --upgrade pip
     websockets` and a `python -c "import websockets; print(websockets.__version__)"` line; pin the
     version (`websockets>=12,<14` — check `tests/e2e/lib/ws_client.py` for API usage such as
     `websockets.connect(..., origin=...)` at :249, which changed in 13.x; choose the version that the
     client code targets and record it in the bead).
   - `check` job no-mock step: prepend `command -v rg >/dev/null || { echo "ripgrep missing"; exit 1; }`
     and add ripgrep to an "Install tooling" step on all three OSes (windows: `choco install ripgrep` or
     skip the no-mock step on windows with an explicit `if: runner.os != 'Windows'` and a comment).
   - `e2e-widget-api`, `demo-showcase`, `golden-trace-gates`: same tooling step where the scripts need it.
6. Document the tool list in `docs/testing/e2e-playbook.md` ("Prerequisites" section; file exists).
7. `ubs` on touched shell files; `shellcheck` if available.

## Files to change

- `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh`: `require_tools`, `require_python_module`.
- `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh`, `tests/e2e/scripts/test_ws_protocol_compliance.sh`,
  `scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh`, `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh`, `scripts/e2e_test.sh`,
  `scripts/pane_e2e.sh`: prerequisite checks.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: tooling steps in `check`, `e2e-pty`, `frankenterm-conformance-gates`,
  `e2e-widget-api`, `demo-showcase`, `golden-trace-gates`.
- `docs/testing/e2e-playbook.md`: prerequisites.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `ci.yml` job "FrankenTerm Conformance/Differential/WS Gates" green; log shows the websockets
      version line.
- [ ] `ci.yml` job "PTY E2E (ubuntu-latest)" and "(macos-latest)": no case fails with `rg: command not
      found`; the remaining failures are the real ones handed to `g04-09-impl` (count them in the close
      reason: expected 42 -> N where N are all assertion failures).
- [ ] Running `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin ./tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh` on a machine without `rg` prints
      `Missing required tools: rg` and exits 2 within one second (no cargo build attempted).
- [ ] The no-mock step fails when `rg` is absent (verified once by temporarily renaming it in a scratch
      run; evidence pasted in the bead comment).

## Tests and logging

`g04-06-tests`. JSONL: `assert` event `tools_present` (pass/fail with `missing=`), emitted before
`run_start` when possible or as the first `assert` of the run; exit code 2 for missing tools.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none. Unblocks: `g04-09-impl` (triage needs a clean tool baseline), `g04-14-impl` (the
ungated scripts need the same tooling), `g04-e2e`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: replacing `rg` with `grep` in `test_inline.sh` only. It fixes one file but leaves the repro
  bundle and no-mock steps silently broken; the tooling step is the real fix. Do both if trivial.
- Rejected: `pip install` inside `ws_client.py`. Scripts must not install packages at runtime.
- Risk: `brew install` on macOS runners can take minutes; cache is not worth it for two packages. Use
  `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`.

## Definition of done

Both jobs green or reduced to real assertion failures (with counts) on `main`; `require_tools` in place;
close reason cites run id, the new function names and the websockets version pinned.

# task(G04.6): Tests for `require_tools` and verification of runner tooling in CI

## Context

Companion to `g04-06-impl`. Run 33152820289: job "PTY E2E (ubuntu-latest)" 98788564023 failed cases in
`tests/e2e/scripts/test_inline.sh` (rg at :57, :118, :135 missing on the runner); job "FrankenTerm
Conformance/Differential/WS Gates" 98788563820 failed at `tests/e2e/lib/ws_client.py:46` ("'websockets'
package not available"). The `check` job's no-mock step (`ci.yml:63-71`) is an `if rg ...` that passes
silently when `rg` is missing. This bead tests the new prerequisite checks and proves the runners now
have the tools.

## What to test

1. `require_tools` reports every missing tool at once, exit 2, and emits the JSONL assert.
2. `require_python_module` detects a missing module.
3. Entry scripts exit 2 before building when a tool is missing.
4. CI jobs have the tools (log evidence) and the no-mock gate fails loudly without `rg`.

Shell self-tests (extend the existing `E2E_SELF_TEST=1` path in `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh:167-179`, and
add `tests/e2e/lib/common_self_test.sh` only if the existing hook cannot host them — prefer the hook):
- `require_tools_reports_all_missing`: `require_tools definitely_missing_a definitely_missing_b bash`
  returns 2 and prints `Missing required tools: definitely_missing_a definitely_missing_b`.
- `require_tools_passes_when_present`: `require_tools bash sh` returns 0 and prints nothing.
- `require_python_module_missing`: `require_python_module no_such_module_xyz` returns 2.
- `jsonl_tools_present_event`: with `logging.sh` sourced and `E2E_JSONL_FILE` set to a temp file, a
  failing `require_tools` appends one `assert` line with `"assertion":"tools_present"`,
  `"status":"fail"` and `missing=` details; validate the file with
  `python3 tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py <file> --schema tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json`.

Entry-script behaviour:
- `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin ./tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh` on a host without `rg`: exit 2, elapsed < 2 s
  (measure with `time`), no `cargo` invocation (check `target/` mtime unchanged).
- `E2E_PYTHON=python3 ./tests/e2e/scripts/test_ws_protocol_compliance.sh` in a venv without websockets:
  exit 2 with `Missing python module: websockets`.

  and `jq --version`; `run_all.sh` summary (`/tmp/ftui_e2e_*/results/summary.json`, uploaded as

- `check` job: no-mock step log begins with `rg <version>` (add `rg --version` to the step) and the gate

## Logging

JSONL `assert` event `tools_present`; details `missing=<space-separated names>`; the summary JSON's per-case
`error` field must never contain `command not found` after this bead (grep in the CI validation step:
`jq '.tests[] | select(.error != null and (.error | test("command not found")))' summary.json` must be
empty; add this to the "Validate PTY E2E JSONL logs" step).

## Files

- `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh` (self-tests), `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh`,
  `tests/e2e/scripts/test_ws_protocol_compliance.sh`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

Section 5.4 ("Neither of its CI workflows has ever executed a doctor gate (both die at VHS install)").
The user-visible consequence: the biggest crate in the repo (192K lines) has had zero CI coverage of its
gates for weeks; 68 of 79 steps of the per-push job are skipped every run; the nightly has been red 30
of 30 times since 2026-08-06; and the G22 owner decision on the crate's scope cannot be made on evidence
until the gates actually run.

## Current state (evidence)

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1138-1154` step "Install VHS (pinned)" in job `doctor-frankentui-verification`
  (`:1097-1100`, `timeout-minutes: 45`): under `set -euo pipefail` (:1140) it downloads
  `vhs_0.10.0_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz` (:1141-1142), extracts to `/tmp` (:1146), then
  `:1147 vhs_bin="$(find /tmp -maxdepth 3 -type f -name vhs -perm -u+x 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"`.
  `find` exits 1 whenever it meets an unreadable directory under `/tmp` (stderr is silenced but the
  status is not); with `pipefail` the pipeline status is 1, and because the line is a bare assignment its
  exit status is the substitution's, so `set -e` aborts the step in about 0.5 s (job 98788564055). The
  comment at :1143-1145 shows the author knew the tarball has a versioned directory.
- `.github/workflows/doctor_frankentui_extended.yml:80-86` step "Install VHS (pinned)": same download,
  `tar -xzf /tmp/vhs.tar.gz -C /tmp`, then `:85 sudo install -m 0755 /tmp/vhs /usr/local/bin/vhs` —
  but the archive extracts to `/tmp/vhs_0.10.0_Linux_x86_64/vhs`, so `install` fails ("cannot stat").
  Schedule `:12-14 cron '23 6 * * *'`, `timeout-minutes: 120` (:37); 30/30 runs red since 2026-08-06.
- Both workflows also install `ttyd` by hand (`ci.yml:1121-1136`, extended `:62-77`) with the same
  duplicated logic.
- No `.github/actions/` directory exists (verified `ls .github` on 2026-09-01: only `workflows/`).
- Downstream steps that never ran: the ci.yml doctor job's 30+ `cargo test -p doctor_frankentui --lib
  <gate>` steps (:1181-1790), the E2E scripts (:1847-1863), and the artifact map writer
  (:1945-2073, `artifact_map.txt`/`.json`); the extended workflow mirrors them (:171-1017).

## Target state

A composite action `.github/actions/install-vhs/action.yml` (inputs: `vhs-version` default `0.10.0`,
`vhs-sha256` required, `ttyd-version` default `1.7.7`, `ttyd-sha256`) downloads to a private
`mktemp -d`, verifies `sha256sum -c`, installs from the real extracted path, and prints `vhs --version`
and `ttyd --version`. Both workflows use it; the 68 skipped steps execute; both upload `artifact_map.txt`.

## Implementation plan

1. Obtain the release checksums: `curl -fsSL
   https://github.com/charmbracelet/vhs/releases/download/v0.10.0/checksums.txt` (VHS publishes one) and
   the ttyd 1.7.7 `SHA256SUMS`; record both hashes in the action defaults and in this bead.
2. Create `.github/actions/install-vhs/action.yml` (composite, `runs.using: composite`): steps
   `Download VHS` (curl to `$RUNNER_TEMP/vhs.tar.gz`), `Verify VHS checksum` (`echo "<sha>  vhs.tar.gz" |
   sha256sum -c -`), `Extract` (`tar -xzf` into `$RUNNER_TEMP/vhs`), `Install`
   (`sudo install -m 0755 "$RUNNER_TEMP/vhs/vhs_${VER}_Linux_x86_64/vhs" /usr/local/bin/vhs`), `Install
   ttyd` (apt if available else pinned binary with checksum), `Report` (`vhs --version`, `ttyd --version`,
   written to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`). No `find | head`; no `/tmp` globbing; `set -euo pipefail` kept.
3. `ci.yml` doctor job: replace :1121-1154 with `- uses: ./.github/actions/install-vhs` (keep `jq ripgrep
   ffmpeg` apt install as its own step).
4. `doctor_frankentui_extended.yml`: replace :62-86 the same way.
5. Run both workflows via `workflow_dispatch` (the extended one has it, :15; add `workflow_dispatch: {}`
   to ci.yml if absent) and inspect: the doctor gates execute; record which of the formerly skipped steps
   now fail on their own merits (those become follow-up beads under `g22-epic`, not this bead).
6. `docs/testing/e2e-playbook.md`: one paragraph "VHS/ttyd are installed by
   `.github/actions/install-vhs`; bump versions and checksums there".

## Files to change

- `.github/actions/install-vhs/action.yml`: new composite action (the only new file; it replaces two
  duplicated shell blocks).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: doctor job uses the action.
- `.github/workflows/doctor_frankentui_extended.yml`: uses the action.
- `docs/testing/e2e-playbook.md`: note.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `ci.yml` job "doctor_frankentui Verification": step "Install VHS" green with `vhs version v0.10.0`
      in the log; the step count executed rises from 11 to 79 (compare `gh run view --job <id>`);
      artifact containing `artifact_map.txt` uploaded (`:2072-2081`).
- [ ] `doctor_frankentui Extended Verification` (`workflow_dispatch` run, then the next three scheduled
      nights): install step green; `artifact_map.txt` uploaded (`:1017`).
- [ ] A deliberately wrong sha256 in a scratch branch fails the action at "Verify VHS checksum" (verified
      once; run id pasted into the bead).
- [ ] `g04-07-tests` verification satisfied.

## Tests and logging

`g04-07-tests`. The action writes `vhs`/`ttyd` versions and sha256 results to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`;
the doctor jobs' existing JSONL/artifact map is the downstream evidence.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none. Unblocks: `g22-impl`/`g22-decision` (doctor scope decision needs running gates),
`g04-e2e` (Extended Verification green three nights is a cluster acceptance criterion).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: `set +e` around the `find`. It keeps the fragile `/tmp` scan and the two divergent copies.
- Rejected: `go install github.com/charmbracelet/vhs@v0.10.0`. Slower (needs Go toolchain), and not
  checksum-pinned.
- Risk: once VHS installs, the doctor gates will expose their own failures (the crate has never run in
  CI). That is the point; triage them under G22, keep this bead scoped to the install.
- Risk: GitHub composite actions cannot use `runs-on`; all steps are `shell: bash` — fine for
  ubuntu-only jobs.

## Definition of done

Both workflows pass the install step and execute the gates; run ids (one ci.yml run, one dispatch run of
the extended workflow, then three scheduled nights) in the close reason; action file checksummed.

title: bug(G04.8): Surface and fix the frankenterm_js_parser_hooks_compat failure in Golden Trace Gates
description:
# bug(G04.8): Surface and fix the `frankenterm_js_parser_hooks_compat` failure in Golden Trace Gates

## Context and why this matters

README.md's Web/WASM and FrankenTerm sections promise xterm.js-compatible host APIs proven by
"release-blocking" harnesses, and `ci.yml`'s "Golden Trace Gates" job is the gate for the advanced host
API compatibility manifest (parser hooks, markers, runtime options, event/IME ordering). Vision rows V8
(web) and V70 (gates green); Section 2.2 letter E; Section 5.1 row "Golden Trace Gates:
`frankenterm_js_parser_hooks_compat` test exit 101 (output only in /tmp)". The consequence: a real test
failure has been invisible for weeks because the harness writes the test output to a `/tmp` file that is
never uploaded, and the job's later evidence-bundle steps then fail on a missing directory, so the
signal is doubly hidden.

## Current state (evidence)

- `ci.yml:699-760` job `golden-trace-gates` (`timeout-minutes: 45`): step "Advanced host API
  compatibility harness (release gate)" runs `./scripts/frankenterm_js_advanced_api_compat.sh` (:737-745).
- `scripts/frankenterm_js_advanced_api_compat.sh:43` `LOG_DIR=/tmp/ftui-frankenterm-js-advanced-api-${TIMESTAMP}`;
  `:58-75 run_subsystem` runs `( cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && "$@" -- --nocapture ) >"$raw" 2>&1 || rc=$?`
  and on failure prints only `parser_hooks  FAIL  (exit 101)  cells=N`; the raw log is shown only when
  `$VERBOSE` (`:70`). `:118-119` `run_subsystem parser_hooks FTUI_ADVANCED_API_COMPAT -- cargo test -p
  ftui-extras --features terminal --test frankenterm_js_parser_hooks_compat || true`.
- The test file `crates/ftui-extras/tests/frankenterm_js_parser_hooks_compat.rs` (14 KB; eight
  `#[test]`s at :153, :185, :207, :243, :269, :314, :339, :371) prints one `FTUI_ADVANCED_API_COMPAT
  {json}` line per cell (:10, :141); exit 101 means at least one `#[test]` panicked. The panic message
  is in the raw log under `/tmp` only.
- Upload steps: `:1075-1083` uploads `/tmp/ftui_schedule_trace_e2e/` only; `:1085-1092` uploads
  `/tmp/frankenterm_release_gates/remote_typography_rescale/` with `if-no-files-found: error` and `if:
  always()` — when the advanced-API step fails, the typography step (:812-822) never runs, the directory
  does not exist, and the upload step fails too (the "missing
  `/tmp/frankenterm_release_gates/remote_typography_rescale/`" error in job 98788563897).
- Sibling harnesses in the same job (`frankenterm_js_addon_parity_compat.sh`,
  `frankenterm_js_sdk_contract_compat.sh`, :746-768) share the same hide-the-output pattern.

## Target state

Any failing subsystem prints the tail of its raw log inside a `::group::` block in the job log; the whole
`LOG_DIR` and `/tmp/frankenterm_release_gates` are uploaded on every run; the missing-directory upload
cannot fail the job when an earlier step already failed; and the parser-hooks test itself passes (root
cause captured in this bead once visible).

## Implementation plan

1. `scripts/frankenterm_js_advanced_api_compat.sh` (and the two sibling scripts if they share the
   function): in `run_subsystem`, on `rc != 0` or `count == 0` always print
   `echo "::group::${subsystem} raw log (tail -80)"; tail -80 "$raw"; echo "::endgroup::"`; also print
   `grep -n "panicked at\|FAILED\|failed" "$raw" | head -20` so the failing `#[test]` name and panic
   location are the first thing visible. Keep `$VERBOSE` for the full log.
2. `ci.yml` `golden-trace-gates`: add an upload step `if: always()` for
   `/tmp/ftui-frankenterm-js-advanced-api-*/`, `/tmp/ftui-frankenterm-js-addon-parity-*/` (check the
   sibling scripts' `LOG_DIR` names) and `/tmp/frankenterm_release_gates/` with `if-no-files-found:
   ignore`; change `:1091 if-no-files-found: error` to `warn` (a missing directory is already reported by
   the failing step that should have produced it).
3. Reproduce the failure: `rch exec -- cargo test -p ftui-extras --features terminal --test
   frankenterm_js_parser_hooks_compat -- --nocapture`; copy the failing test name, the panic message and
   the `FTUI_ADVANCED_API_COMPAT` cell that failed into this bead's "Root cause" comment.
4. Fix the root cause in the code under test (`crates/ftui-extras/src/terminal/...` parser hooks; locate
   via the test's `use` lines) or, if the test encodes an outdated expectation against the vendored
   `frankenterm-core` 0.2.0 (see `crates/ftui-extras/Cargo.toml` deps), fix the expectation with a
   comment citing the upstream change. Do not `#[ignore]` the test.
5. `ubs` on touched files; `cargo clippy -D warnings`; `cargo fmt --check`.

## Files to change

- `scripts/frankenterm_js_advanced_api_compat.sh` (+ `frankenterm_js_addon_parity_compat.sh`,
  `frankenterm_js_sdk_contract_compat.sh` if they share the pattern): failure tail in the job log.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: upload steps; `if-no-files-found` softened for the dependent upload.
- `crates/ftui-extras/tests/frankenterm_js_parser_hooks_compat.rs` and/or the parser-hook
  implementation: the actual fix (file named once reproduced).

## Success criteria

- [ ] Local reproduction log attached as a bead comment (test name + panic message).
- [ ] `ci.yml` job "Golden Trace Gates" green on `main` (run id in close reason); artifact
      `frankenterm-advanced-api-logs` (new name) present on every run.
- [ ] A scratch-branch run with a deliberately failing cell shows the `::group::parser_hooks raw log`
      block with the panic line in the job log (verified once; run id pasted).
- [ ] `g04-08-tests` satisfied.

## Tests and logging

`g04-08-tests`. Evidence lines: `FTUI_ADVANCED_API_COMPAT {"subsystem":"parser_hooks","scenario":...}`
per cell; the manifest under `$LOG_DIR/manifest.jsonl` (see script :134 `REQUIRED = {"parser_hooks",
"markers", "runtime_options", "events_ime"}`); job-log groups per failing subsystem.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none. Unblocks: `g04-e2e`. Related: `g23-impl` (web host) relies on this gate staying green.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: `continue-on-error` on the harness step. Hides the failure again.
- Rejected: dropping the parser-hooks subsystem from `REQUIRED`. It is the README's "release-blocking"
  claim.
- Risk: the root cause may be an upstream frankenterm-core behaviour change; then the fix belongs in the
  vendored dependency pin and the close reason must say so.

## Definition of done

Root cause recorded; fix merged; Golden Trace Gates green; artifacts uploaded on every run; close reason
names the failing test, the fix commit and the run id.
close_reason: parser_hooks_compat test passes (8/8, verified); closed the observability hole that hid it — harnesses now echo a ::group:: tail of the failing raw log inline, CI uploads all three harness LOG_DIRs + the release-gates tree always, and the typography upload no longer hard-fails on a missing dir (21c06d0a).

  - macOS-only: `vsearch_screen_load` (`test_virtualized_search.sh:203`; siblings :229-309),
    `inline_story_*` (`test_inline_story.sh`, `run_case` :100), `dashboard_typewriter`
    (`test_text_effects_sweep.sh:119,138`), bidi and voi cases. Child: `g04-09-impl-macos` (owners
    `g10-impl` for vsearch, `g29-impl` for bidi).
- The exact failing case names per cluster are in the uploaded artifacts `e2e-pty-summary-ubuntu-latest`
  / `-macos-latest` (`/tmp/ftui_e2e_*/results/summary.json`, `jq '.tests[] | select(.status=="failed") |
  .name'`) and the failure bundle `e2e-pty-failure-bundle-<os>` (`minimal_repros.md`, per-test log
  excerpts and `.pty` hex heads; built by ci.yml:586-660). Download them with `gh run download
  33152820289 -n e2e-pty-summary-ubuntu-latest` at triage start and paste the lists into each child.
- Infrastructure: `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` (Python-`pty` driver, `pty_run`), `tests/e2e/lib/logging.sh`
  (`jsonl_*` helpers, `log_test_*`), `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh` (fixtures), schema
  `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json`, validator `tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py`.

## Target state

`./tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh` reports 166/166 (0 failed; skips only with a logged reason) on
`ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest`; JSONL and `summary.json` archived as artifacts on every run; each
child bead's close reason names the root cause and the fix commit; the PTY jobs are green for three
consecutive `main` runs.

## Implementation plan

1. After `g04-06-impl` merges, download the summaries of the first post-tooling run; recount the
   failures; distribute the exact case names to the six children (edit their descriptions via
   `br update`).
2. For each child: reproduce locally with the case's script (`bash -x tests/e2e/scripts/test_<suite>.sh`
   with `E2E_LOG_DIR` set) under the same identity the runner uses (`TERM=xterm-256color`, no
   `KITTY_WINDOW_ID`); classify as (a) test expectation stale, (b) real bug in the owning block, (c)
   environment (identity/capability gating, Section 2.2.D). For (b) the child is blocked by the owning
   block's impl bead and re-verifies after it lands; for (a) fix the script with a comment citing the
   behaviour change; for (c) make the script select the identity explicitly (`FTUI_*` overrides) and
   log it.
3. Keep `run_all.sh` as the single entry; do not add per-OS suites. Where a case must skip on one OS,
   use the existing skip path (`log_test_skip`, `logging.sh:1498`) with a reason string that names the
   bead.
4. Extend the CI validation step (ci.yml:567-584) to fail when `summary.json` has `failed > 0`
   (`run_all.sh` already exits non-zero, but the explicit jq check documents the gate) and to print the
   failed names in the job log.
5. Close the umbrella only when both PTY jobs are green three times in a row (run ids).

## Files to change

- Per child (see children). Umbrella-level: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (validation step prints failed
  names), `docs/testing/e2e-playbook.md` (triage recipe: download summary, jq filter, repro command).

## Success criteria

- [ ] Six children closed with root causes.
- [ ] `run_all.sh` 166/166 on ubuntu and macOS in three consecutive `main` runs (run ids in close reason).
- [ ] Artifacts `e2e-pty-jsonl-<os>` validated by `validate_jsonl.py --strict` (existing step).

## Tests and logging

`g04-09-tests` plus each child's own. JSONL fields per case (schema `assert`/`case_step_*`): `run_id`,
`scenario`/case id, `mode`, `cols`, `rows`, `seed`, `hash` (sha256 of the `.pty` capture), `duration_ms`,
`error` label (e.g. `rtl_locale_not_selected`), `screen`; `summary.json` with `passed/failed/skipped`
counts and per-test `status`/`error`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-06-impl` (tooling) and by its six children (`g04-09-impl-cleanup`, `-keybind`, `-voi`,
`-rtl`, `-mouse-paste`, `-macos`). Children are in turn blocked by the owning block impls where the
failure is a real bug (`g03-impl`, `g14-impl`, `g10-impl`, `g20-impl`, `g29-impl`). Unblocks `g04-e2e`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: marking failing suites `--quick`-only or skipping them in CI. The suite's value is precisely
  the failures it finds; skipped cases must carry a bead-named reason.
- Rejected: rewriting assertions to match current output without root-causing. Stale expectations are
  fixed only with a comment explaining the behaviour change.
- Risk: some clusters depend on L-sized blocks (G14 keybindings, G10 VirtualizedList, G29 i18n). The
  umbrella will therefore close late; that is acceptable — `g04-e2e` records green-main using the
  post-G04.6 baseline and re-asserts after this umbrella closes.

166/166 on both OSes three runs running; children closed with evidence; run ids and summary counts in
the close reason.

comments.text: Root cause found for the report-export steps of scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh (steps 12-17: terminal caps, i18n, widget builder, determinism lab, hyperlink playground, command palette) and the 11x screen sweeps: keystrokes were delivered with (sleep; printf keys > /dev/tty) & inside the script(1) session. A write to /dev/tty from inside the session lands on the pty OUTPUT side (what script records), never on the program input, so no key ever reached the showcase; verified with script -qec "(sleep .3; printf e > /dev/tty) & bash -c read" which reads nothing, while feeding script stdin reads the key. run_in_pty now takes a keys spec (delay_ms:keys|...) fed through a FIFO held open as script stdin (no stray EOF/^D); every site converted. Full E2E rerun in progress.

comments.text: Follow-up on the /dev/tty finding: a FIFO-based run_in_pty that feeds keys into scripts stdin (the pty master) instead of /dev/tty does deliver keys (verified: the terminal-caps report step went no_report -> PASS, and steps 12-17 receive their keys).
