title: bug(G04.9): PTY E2E cluster cleanup_* (4 of 7 cases fail on ubuntu) — root-cause and fix
description:
# bug(G04.9): PTY E2E cluster `cleanup_*` (4 of 7 cases fail on ubuntu) — root-cause and fix

## Context and why this matters

README.md promises "RAII cleanup even on panic" and a clean terminal on every exit path (vision row V4,
WORKING with the SIGTSTP gap); the `cleanup` suite is the only end-to-end proof that the harness
restores cursor visibility, disables mouse/bracketed paste, leaves the alt screen and survives SIGTERM.
Four of its seven cases fail on `ubuntu-latest` in run 33152820289 (job 98788564023), which means the
teardown guarantee is currently unproven on Linux CI. Parent umbrella: `g04-09-impl`.

## Current state (evidence)

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh`: cases registered at :198-204 — `cleanup_normal` (:56),
  `cleanup_cursor_visible` (:70), `cleanup_sigterm` (:90), `cleanup_mouse_disabled` (:113),
  `cleanup_bracketed_paste_disabled` (:133), `cleanup_altscreen_exit` (:153),
  `cleanup_altscreen_mouse_focus` (:173). Each runs `pty_run "$output_file" "$E2E_HARNESS_BIN"` (the
  `ftui-harness` binary, `run_all.sh:100-105`) and greps the raw PTY capture, e.g. `grep -a -F -q
  $'\x1b[?25h'` (cursor show), `grep -a -P -q '\x1b\[\?1000'` (mouse mode toggled), `grep -a -q
  "Welcome"` after the SIGTERM case (PTY timeout kills the process, comment at :47).
- Which four failed is recorded in artifact `e2e-pty-summary-ubuntu-latest` of run 33152820289
  (`jq '.tests[] | select(.status=="failed") | .name' summary.json`) and the failure bundle
  `e2e-pty-failure-bundle-ubuntu-latest` (`minimal_repros.md`, `*_excerpt.log`, `*_pty_head.hex`).
  Download at bead start; paste the four names here.
- Candidate root causes, in the order to check:
  1. Signal-state race (G03): `ftui_core::shutdown_signal` is a process-global `AtomicI32`
     (`crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs:79-140`); `Program::complete_lifecycle` clears it
     (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs:5490`). If the harness receives SIGTERM from the PTY driver
     while the lifecycle is mid-teardown, the cleanup sequence may be skipped or emitted twice.
     `cleanup_sigterm` is the direct probe.
  2. Identity/capability gating (Section 2.2.D): under `TERM=xterm-256color` without `KITTY_WINDOW_ID`
     the harness may never enable mouse/paste (so the "disable" sequences the tests grep for are never
     emitted). Check `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_capabilities.rs:1233 use_sync_output()` and the
     mouse/paste enable conditions in `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs` (`MOUSE_ENABLE` :54,
     `MOUSE_DISABLE` :57) and `terminal_session.rs`.
  3. Two teardown stacks (G13): `ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs` (crossterm, panic hook :1194) vs
     `ftui-tty` `RawModeGuard` (:365-399, hook :312). The harness picks one via features; the expected
     byte order differs (`write_cleanup_sequence` :1621).
  4. Stale expectation: the grep patterns may predate the mux-safe mouse sequences (`:55-58`).

## Target state

All seven `cleanup_*` cases pass on ubuntu and macOS; the teardown byte sequence for the harness under
`xterm-256color` is asserted explicitly (cursor show `\x1b[?25h`, mouse off `\x1b[?1000;1002;1006l...`,
paste off `\x1b[?2004l`, alt-screen leave `\x1b[?1049l`, kitty pop `\x1b[<u` when enabled) in the order
the code emits it; the root cause is recorded.

## Implementation plan

1. Download the artifacts, list the four failing names, reproduce locally:
   `E2E_LOG_DIR=/data/tmp/... TERM=xterm-256color bash -x tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh` after
   `cargo build -p ftui-harness --bin ftui-harness` (rch). Inspect the `.pty` capture with `xxd`.
2. Classify each failure against the four candidates. If (1): the fix is `g03-impl` (per-Program signal
   slot); this bead re-runs after it lands and adds `cleanup_sigterm_twice` (send SIGTERM during teardown
   via `PTY_SEND_SIGNAL_AFTER_MS`, a new `pty.sh` knob) to prove idempotent teardown. If (2): make the
   test declare its identity explicitly (`FTUI_CAPS_PROBE=0`, `TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty` or the G05 override
   `FTUI_SYNC_OUTPUT=1` once it exists) and assert the enable sequence too, so the test proves a
   round-trip rather than assuming enablement. If (3): align the expectation with the backend the harness
   actually uses and open/link `g13-impl`'s `teardown_sequence_identical_native_vs_crossterm` test. If
   (4): update the regex with a comment citing `ftui-tty/src/lib.rs` line numbers.
3. Add a shared helper `assert_teardown_sequence <pty_file>` in `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` that checks the
   ordered sequence above and logs a JSONL `assert` with `teardown_order=<found order>` and per-sequence
   counts (`1049l=1 25h=1 2004l=1 1000l>=1`), used by all cleanup cases.
4. No deletion of cases; no `|| true`.

## Files to change

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_cleanup.sh`: identity declaration; use `assert_teardown_sequence`.
- `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh`: `assert_teardown_sequence`, optional `PTY_SEND_SIGNAL_AFTER_MS`.
- Code fix location depends on classification (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`,
  `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs`, or `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs`); name it in the close reason.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Four failing case names and their classification recorded in a bead comment.
- [ ] `test_cleanup.sh` 7/7 locally under `TERM=xterm-256color` and under the kitty identity.
- [ ] CI "PTY E2E (ubuntu-latest)" and "(macos-latest)" show `cleanup` suite: all cases passed (run id).
- [ ] JSONL `assert` lines with `teardown_order` present and validated.

## Tests and logging

JSONL: per case `assert` with `teardown_order`, escape-sequence tallies, exit code, `duration_ms`; PTY
driver `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh`; capture files `<case>.pty` archived in `e2e-pty-logs-<os>`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-06-impl` (tooling baseline), `g03-impl` (signal state; the SIGTERM case cannot be
trusted before it). Related, not blocking: `g13-impl` (teardown unification), `g05-impl` (identity
overrides). Unblocks: `g04-09-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: loosening greps to "any of the sequences". The order matters for terminal state.
- Risk: the SIGTERM case depends on PTY driver timing; assert on sequence presence, not timing.

## Definition of done

Root cause and fix commit in the close reason; 7/7 on both OSes with run id; helper in `pty.sh`.

title: bug(G04.9): PTY E2E cluster keybind_* (3 of 8 cases fail) — root-cause; owner block G14
description:
# bug(G04.9): PTY E2E cluster `keybind_*` (3 of 8 cases fail) — root-cause; owner block G14

## Context and why this matters

README.md "Keybinding System (1,900+ Lines)" and `docs/spec/keybinding-policy.md` section 6.1 define
priorities for Ctrl-C, Esc, Esc-Esc, Ctrl-D and Ctrl-Q in the agent harness; the `keybinding` PTY suite
is the only proof those keys behave as documented. Vision row V62 (keybinding system: NOT_STARTED as
described) and V70. Three cases fail on ubuntu in run 33152820289 (job 98788564023). The keybinding
implementation is being rebuilt by G14 (`g14-impl`: real keymap with priorities, chords, conflict
report, serde), so this bead's job is to root-cause the three failures now, fix them if they are
harness/test defects, and otherwise re-verify after `g14-impl` lands. Parent: `g04-09-impl`.

## Current state (evidence)

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_keybinding.sh`: `run_case` (:98-124) records `keybinding assertion failed`
  as the error label for every failure (no per-assertion detail — the first fix is diagnosability).
  Cases (:126-276): `keybind_ctrl_c_clears_input`, `keybind_ctrl_c_cancels_task`,
  `keybind_esc_clears_input`, `keybind_esc_cancels_task`, `keybind_esc_esc_toggles_tree`,
  `keybind_esc_closes_tree`, `keybind_ctrl_d_soft_quit`, `keybind_ctrl_q_hard_quit`. Example
  (:213-231): sends `\x1b\x1b` with `PTY_SEND_DELAY_MS=300`, `FTUI_HARNESS_EXIT_AFTER_MS=2000`,
  `FTUI_HARNESS_SUPPRESS_WELCOME=1`, expects `(Tree view opened)` in the capture; comment says the
  double-Esc window is 250 ms.
- Runtime side: `crates/ftui-core/src/keybinding.rs:308-416` `SequenceDetector`/`SequenceConfig`
  (Esc-Esc only; env `FTUI_DISABLE_ESC_SEQ`); widgets' `Keybinding`/`KeybindingHints` are display-only
  (`help_registry.rs:55`, `help.rs:1088`); `pane_keymap` in ftui-runtime hardcodes pane keys.
- Which three fail: artifact `e2e-pty-summary-ubuntu-latest` (`jq` filter) and the failure bundle's
  `*_excerpt.log`/`*_pty_head.hex`. Download and paste at bead start.
- Candidate root causes: (a) Esc-Esc timing — the test's 300 ms send delay is *longer* than the 250 ms
  detector window mentioned in the comment, so on a slow runner the second Esc may arrive late (timing
  bug in the test or the detector's clock source); (b) the harness's Esc handling depends on the
  kitty keyboard protocol being enabled, which under `xterm-256color` identity it is not (Section
  2.2.D), so Esc arrives as a bare `\x1b` ambiguous with a CSI introducer and the parser's
  `PARSER_TIMEOUT_GRACE` (`ftui-tty/src/lib.rs:226`, 50 ms) resolves it late; (c) messages such as
  `(Tree view opened)` changed text.

## Target state

All eight keybinding cases pass on both OSes; failures report which assertion failed; the Esc-Esc
timing in the test is derived from the detector's configured window (read from a single constant
exposed by the harness, e.g. `FTUI_HARNESS_PRINT_CONFIG=1` printing `esc_seq_window_ms=250`) rather
than duplicated; after `g14-impl`, the suite is extended by `test_keybinding_chords.sh` (owned by G14).

## Implementation plan

1. Download artifacts; list the three failing names; reproduce locally with `bash -x` under
   `TERM=xterm-256color` and again with `TERM=xterm-kitty KITTY_WINDOW_ID=1` to test hypothesis (b).
2. `test_keybinding.sh`: replace the single `keybinding assertion failed` label with per-assertion
   labels (`expected_text_missing:<text>`, `pty_exit_<code>`) so the summary is diagnosable; log the
   send delay and window in the JSONL (`send_delay_ms`, `esc_window_ms`).
3. Hypothesis (a): set `PTY_SEND_DELAY_MS` below the window (e.g. 100 ms) and/or send both Escs in one
   write; if the detector uses wall-clock `Instant` between reads, the fix belongs in
   `SequenceDetector` (use the event timestamp, not read time) — file it under `g14-impl` and block on it.
4. Hypothesis (b): if bare-Esc disambiguation is the cause, the test must state the identity it runs
   under and the harness should enable kitty keyboard when supported; record the finding for `g05-impl`
   and `g36-impl` (input parser gaps).
5. Hypothesis (c): update the expected strings with a comment citing the harness source line.
6. After `g14-impl` lands, re-run the suite; if any case is still red, the umbrella stays open.

## Files to change

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_keybinding.sh`: error labels, timing derivation, identity declaration.
- Possibly `crates/ftui-core/src/keybinding.rs` (timestamp source) — coordinate with `g14-impl`.
- `crates/ftui-harness/src/main.rs`: `FTUI_HARNESS_PRINT_CONFIG` (only if needed for step 2).

## Success criteria

- [ ] Three failing names + classification in a bead comment.
- [ ] `test_keybinding.sh` 8/8 locally under both identities.
- [ ] CI PTY E2E jobs show `keybinding` suite fully passed (run id).
- [ ] JSONL per-case `error` labels are specific (no `keybinding assertion failed` generic label remains).

## Tests and logging

JSONL fields: case id, `send_delay_ms`, `esc_window_ms`, `identity` (TERM/TERM_PROGRAM), `error` label,
`hash` of the capture, `duration_ms`; capture `.pty` files in the artifact.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-06-impl`; `g14-impl` where the failure is in the keybinding implementation (hypothesis
a). Related: `g05-impl`, `g36-impl`. Unblocks: `g04-09-impl`, and `g14-e2e`'s `test_keybinding_chords.sh`
builds on the fixed suite.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: increasing `FTUI_HARNESS_EXIT_AFTER_MS` blindly. Fix the cause of late detection.
- Risk: G14 is L-sized; if all three failures are (a), this bead waits. Record the wait explicitly in
  the umbrella.

## Definition of done

Root cause per case, fix commit(s), 8/8 on both OSes with run id in the close reason.

title: bug(G04.9): PTY E2E cluster voi_marker_missing (4 cases) — root-cause; owners G10/G20
description:
# bug(G04.9): PTY E2E cluster `voi_marker_missing` (4 cases) — root-cause; owners G10/G20

## Context and why this matters

README.md presents VOI (value-of-information) sampling as how the runtime decides when to remeasure
expensive things, and the demo's VOI overlay screen is where a user would see it. Vision row V11 (VOI:
PARTIAL, inline_auto only) and V51 (evidence sink: `voi_sample` never written); Section 2.2.B "VOI
sampling: used only for `inline_auto` height remeasure". The four `voi_*` PTY cases assert that the
overlay renders a `VOI` marker; all four fail in run 33152820289 on ubuntu (job 98788564023) and the
VOI cases also fail on macOS (98788563987). Either the demo screen no longer shows the marker (a real
regression of the showcase) or the script targets the wrong screen. G10 (`g10-impl`) rewires
VirtualizedList's Bayesian machinery including a `RemeasurePolicy` (Beta-VOI) and G20 (`g20-impl`)
adds the `voi_sample` evidence event; this bead root-causes the E2E failure and coordinates with them.
Parent: `g04-09-impl`.

## Current state (evidence)

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_bidi_voi_overlay.sh`: `VOI_SCREEN=32` (:219), `run_case "voi" "$VOI_SCREEN"
  "$mode" "$cols" "$rows" "" 0` for `modes=(alt inline)` x `sizes=(80x24 120x40)` (:225-238) -> cases
  `voi_alt_80x24`, `voi_inline_80x24`, `voi_alt_120x40`, `voi_inline_120x40`. The demo binary is run
  with `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN=$screen`, `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN_MODE=$mode`, `FTUI_DEMO_UI_HEIGHT`,
  `FTUI_DEMO_DETERMINISTIC=1`, `FTUI_DEMO_SEED=$E2E_SEED`, `FTUI_DEMO_TICK_MS=$E2E_TIME_STEP_MS`,
  `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS=1600`, `PTY_TIMEOUT=6` (:140-150); assertion at :175-177: `command grep -a -q
  "VOI" "$output_file"` else `error="voi_marker_missing"`. Also fails if the capture is under 200 bytes
  (`output_too_small`, :161-164).
- The showcase has 45 screens (`ScreenId` in `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs:679`,
  `all_screens_count` asserts 45 at `:7068`); README says 46. Screen indices in the script (31 for bidi,
  32 for VOI; virtualized search uses 23 in `test_virtualized_search.sh:20`) are positional, so any
  reordering or removal of a screen silently retargets the E2E cases. This is the first hypothesis.
- Second hypothesis: the VOI overlay is drawn only after a remeasure decision that never fires under
  deterministic ticks (`FTUI_DEMO_TICK_MS`), so the marker text is absent within 1600 ms.
- Third: the marker text changed (e.g. `VoI`, `Value of Information`).

## Target state

The four `voi_*` cases pass on both OSes; the script addresses screens by stable slug
(`FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN=<slug>` accepted by the showcase, or a lookup from the `ScreenId` list via
`ftui-demo-showcase --list-screens`) instead of positional index; the overlay's marker is asserted
together with a `voi_sample` evidence line once `g20-impl` lands.

## Implementation plan

1. Reproduce: `cargo build -p ftui-demo-showcase` (rch), then `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN=32
   FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN_MODE=alt FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS=1600 tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh`-driven run; inspect the
   capture; compare the screen title with `ScreenId` order in `app.rs:679`.
2. If retargeted: add `--list-screens` (prints `index<TAB>slug<TAB>title`) and accept slugs in
   `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN` (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs` where `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN` is parsed, see
   `:657`); switch the script (and `test_virtualized_search.sh`, `test_bidi_voi_overlay.sh`) to slugs;
   add a unit test `screen_slug_lookup_round_trips` in the showcase.
3. If the marker never renders under deterministic ticks: coordinate with `g10-impl` (`RemeasurePolicy`
   pushes `WidgetSignal::Remeasure { index, voi, cost }`) so the overlay renders the marker from the
   policy's decision, and make the demo force one decision within the first N ticks in deterministic
   mode; assert the marker plus the `voi_sample` JSONL line (`alpha, beta, voi, sample_cost, decision`)
   from `g20-impl` in the E2E.
4. If the text changed: update the grep with a comment citing the screen source line.
5. Extend the case JSONL (`emit_case_jsonl` :76) with `screen_slug` and `marker_found`.

## Files to change

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_bidi_voi_overlay.sh`: slug addressing, richer JSONL.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs`: `--list-screens`, slug parsing (if needed).
- Coordinated with `g10-impl`/`g20-impl` for the marker/evidence path.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Root cause recorded (which hypothesis) with the capture excerpt.
- [ ] `voi_alt_80x24`, `voi_inline_80x24`, `voi_alt_120x40`, `voi_inline_120x40` pass on ubuntu and macOS
      (run id).
- [ ] Screen addressing by slug; `screen_slug_lookup_round_trips` green.
- [ ] After `g20-impl`: the E2E asserts a `voi_sample` line in `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh` JSONL.

## Tests and logging

JSONL per case: `scenario=voi`, `mode`, `cols`, `rows`, `screen_slug`, `marker_found`, `hash`,
`duration_ms`, `error`; PTY driver `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-06-impl`; `g10-impl` and `g20-impl` where the marker depends on the rewired VOI
policy/evidence. Unblocks: `g04-09-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: hardcoding a new index. Positional indices are the suspected cause.
- Risk: the VOI overlay may be demo-only decoration with no runtime backing; if so, say it in the close
  reason and let `g10-impl` decide what the overlay shows.

## Definition of done

Four cases green on both OSes with run id; root cause and fix commit in the close reason.

title: bug(G04.9): PTY E2E cluster rtl_locale_not_selected (4 cases) — root-cause; owner G29
description:
# bug(G04.9): PTY E2E cluster `rtl_locale_not_selected` (4 cases) — root-cause; owner G29

## Context and why this matters

README.md claims i18n with "LTR/RTL via ftui-text bidi" and a demo in several languages; the reality
check found `ftui-i18n` is a string catalog plus plural rules with no bidi integration (vision row V47:
PARTIAL; Section 2.2.C i18n row; G29 scopes the claim and adds `LocaleContext::direction()` driving
`Paragraph` alignment under the `bidi` feature). The four `bidi_*` PTY cases expect the demo's bidi
screen to show `Locale: Arabic` after four Right-arrow presses; all four fail on ubuntu (job
98788564023) and on macOS (98788563987) in run 33152820289. This bead root-causes the failure (script
targeting, locale cycling, or a real bug) and hands real bugs to `g29-impl`. Parent: `g04-09-impl`.

## Current state (evidence)

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_bidi_voi_overlay.sh`: `BIDI_SCREEN=31` (:218), `RIGHT=$'\x1b[C'`,
  `BIDI_SEND="${RIGHT}${RIGHT}${RIGHT}${RIGHT}"` (:221-222), `run_case "bidi" "$BIDI_SCREEN" "$mode"
  "$cols" "$rows" "$BIDI_SEND" 300` over `alt|inline` x `80x24|120x40` (:225-238) -> cases
  `bidi_alt_80x24`, `bidi_inline_80x24`, `bidi_alt_120x40`, `bidi_inline_120x40`. Assertion at
  :169-172: `command grep -a -q "Locale: Arabic" "$output_file"` else `error="rtl_locale_not_selected"`.
  Send delay 300 ms, exit after 1600 ms (:140-150).
- Demo languages are en/es/fr/ru/ar/ja (Section 2.2.C); four Right presses from `en` reach `ar` only if
  the order is exactly en, es, fr, ru, ar and the screen starts at `en` and Right cycles languages (the
  i18n screen's key handling is in `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/` — locate the screen at
  index 31 via `ScreenId` in `app.rs:679` and read its `update` for `KeyCode::Right`).
- Same positional-index fragility as `g04-09-impl-voi` (45 screens, README says 46; index 31 may no
  longer be the i18n/bidi screen).
- Under `xterm-256color` identity without kitty keyboard, arrow keys arrive as `\x1b[C` CSI sequences —
  fine — but if the app enables application cursor mode (`\x1b[?1h`) the terminal would send `\x1bOC`;
  the PTY driver sends raw bytes so this is not the cause unless the parser only accepts SS3 in that mode.

## Target state

The four `bidi_*` cases pass on both OSes; the script selects the locale deterministically (either a
`FTUI_DEMO_LOCALE=ar` env override honoured by the i18n screen in deterministic mode, or a slug-addressed
screen plus a documented key sequence); once `g29-impl` lands, the case additionally asserts an RTL
rendering property (right-aligned Arabic line via `Paragraph` alignment) not just the label.

## Implementation plan

1. Reproduce locally (build demo via rch; run the case with `bash -x`; inspect the capture with
   `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh`'s canonicalizer `pty_canonicalize` if built (`pty.sh:16-40`)).
2. Determine the screen at index 31 and its Right-key semantics; if the index drifted, move the script
   to slug addressing (shared change with `g04-09-impl-voi`; do it once, in whichever child lands first).
3. Add `FTUI_DEMO_LOCALE` (read via `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/determinism.rs` env helpers) so the
   i18n screen starts in the requested locale under deterministic mode; keep the Right-arrow cycling
   test as a second case `bidi_cycle_to_arabic` so both the override and the key path are covered.
4. Update the assertion to `Locale: Arabic` plus, after `g29-impl`, a right-aligned Arabic sample line
   (assert the first non-space column of that row is >= cols/2 in the canonicalized screen).
5. JSONL: add `locale_selected` and `rtl_detected` fields to `emit_case_jsonl` (:76).

## Files to change

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_bidi_voi_overlay.sh`: locale override, second case, JSONL fields.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/determinism.rs` and the i18n screen: `FTUI_DEMO_LOCALE`.
- Coordinated with `g29-impl` for the RTL rendering assertion.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Root cause recorded with capture excerpt.
- [ ] `bidi_alt_80x24`, `bidi_inline_80x24`, `bidi_alt_120x40`, `bidi_inline_120x40` (+ `bidi_cycle_to_arabic`)
      pass on both OSes (run id).
- [ ] Unit test `i18n_screen_honours_locale_override` in the showcase.
- [ ] After `g29-impl`: RTL alignment assertion added and green; `g29-impl`'s snapshot for the Arabic
      i18n screen referenced.

## Tests and logging

JSONL per case: `scenario=bidi`, `mode`, `cols`, `rows`, `screen_slug`, `locale_selected`,
`rtl_detected`, `hash`, `duration_ms`, `error`; PTY driver `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-06-impl`; `g29-impl` for the RTL rendering half. Unblocks: `g04-09-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: asserting only the `Locale: Arabic` label forever. A label is not proof of RTL rendering;
  the reality check exists because labels were taken as proof.
- Risk: `ru` may be absent or ordered differently in the catalog; the override path removes the
  dependence on order.

## Definition of done

Cases green on both OSes; override implemented and unit-tested; root cause and commit in the close
reason.

title: bug(G04.9): PTY E2E cluster mouse SGR + bracketed paste — root-cause and fix
description:
# bug(G04.9): PTY E2E cluster mouse SGR + bracketed paste — root-cause and fix

## Context and why this matters

README.md's input parser claims (CSI/SS3/DCS/OSC/APC, SGR mouse, bracketed paste; vision row V61:
WORKING with gaps) are proven end-to-end only by the `mouse_sgr` and `paste` PTY suites, which drive the
harness binary with raw escape sequences and grep the canonicalized screen for `Mouse: Down(Left)` /
`Paste: hello paste`. Both suites have failing cases on ubuntu in run 33152820289 (job 98788564023).
Because the same parser backs every consumer app, an input-path regression here is user-facing.
Parent: `g04-09-impl`.

## Current state (evidence)

- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_mouse_sgr.sh`: 11 cases (:97-302) — `mouse_left_click_release`,
  `mouse_middle_click`, `mouse_right_click`, `mouse_move_event`, `mouse_drag_left`,
  `mouse_scroll_events`, `mouse_coordinates`, `mouse_large_coords`, `mouse_shift_click`,
  `mouse_ctrl_click`, `mouse_alt_click`; each `pty_run`s `$E2E_HARNESS_BIN` with `PTY_SEND` set to SGR
  sequences (`\x1b[<0;10;5M` style) and greps a canonicalized file (`$canonical_file`) for
  `Mouse: Down(Left)` / `Mouse: Up(Left)` (:110-112 in the file's numbering shown as :55-56 of the
  excerpt). The canonical file comes from `pty_canonicalize` (`tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh:16-40`, binary
  `target/debug/pty_canonicalize`, built only when `PTY_CANONICALIZE=1`).
- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_paste.sh`: 6 cases (:67-175) — `paste_basic` (`PTY_SEND=$'\x1b[200~hello
  paste\x1b[201~'`, expects `Paste: hello paste`), `paste_multiline`, `paste_large`, `paste_unicode`,
  `paste_embedded_escape`, `paste_dos_limit`; same canonical-file grep pattern.
- Which cases failed: artifact `e2e-pty-summary-ubuntu-latest` + failure bundle of run 33152820289;
  paste the names at bead start (the audit summary lists "mouse SGR" and "paste" as clusters, not counts).
- Candidate root causes: (a) the harness never enables mouse/paste reporting under the runner identity
  (`xterm-256color`, no `KITTY_WINDOW_ID`), and the harness only *displays* mouse/paste events when the
  corresponding mode is on — check `crates/ftui-harness/src/main.rs` event display and
  `terminal_capabilities.rs` gating for `mouse_sgr`/`bracketed_paste`; (b) `pty_canonicalize` is not
  built on the runner (`PTY_CANONICALIZE` unset) so `$canonical_file` is empty or the raw capture is
  used and the expected text is split across diff updates; (c) the parser's ambiguous-sequence grace
  (`ftui-tty/src/lib.rs:226 PARSER_TIMEOUT_GRACE = 50 ms`) plus `PTY_SEND_DELAY_MS=300` interplay; (d)
  DoS limit case expectations (`paste_dos_limit`) tightened in code (`ftui-core` paste cap) without
  updating the test.

## Target state

All 11 mouse and 6 paste cases pass on both OSes; the tests state the identity/capabilities they need
and assert the enable sequences (`\x1b[?1006h`, `\x1b[?2004h`) were emitted before sending input; the
canonicalizer is built deterministically by `run_all.sh` before the suites run; JSONL carries the
escape-sequence tallies so a future failure is diagnosable from the artifact alone.

## Implementation plan

1. Download artifacts; list failing cases; reproduce locally (build `ftui-harness` and
   `pty_canonicalize` via rch; run each suite with `bash -x`).
2. `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh`: build `pty_canonicalize` once up front (`cargo build -p ftui-pty --bin
   pty_canonicalize` or wherever the bin lives — `rg -n "pty_canonicalize" crates/*/Cargo.toml`) and
   export `PTY_CANONICALIZE=1 PTY_CANONICALIZE_BIN=...`; fail fast if it is missing (uses
   `require_tools` from `g04-06-impl`).
3. In both suites add a precondition assert per case: capture contains `\x1b[?1006h` (mouse) or
   `\x1b[?2004h` (paste) before the input is sent; if absent, the error label is
   `mouse_mode_not_enabled` / `paste_mode_not_enabled` (not a generic failure). If the harness gates
   enabling on capabilities, declare the identity explicitly in the test (`TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty` or the
   G05 overrides) and document why.
4. For (c): send the whole SGR sequence in one write (already the case) and keep `PTY_SEND_DELAY_MS`
   >= 2x `PARSER_TIMEOUT_GRACE`; if the parser drops a well-formed sequence, that is a parser bug —
   add a unit test in `crates/ftui-core/src/input_parser.rs` reproducing the byte stream and fix it.
5. For (d): read the current paste cap in `ftui-core` (search `paste` limit constants) and align the
   test's payload size with a comment.
6. JSONL: add `seq_1006h`, `seq_2004h`, `events_seen` counts to each case's `log_jsonl`.

## Files to change

- `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh`: canonicalizer build + export.
- `tests/e2e/scripts/test_mouse_sgr.sh`, `test_paste.sh`: precondition asserts, labels, JSONL fields.
- Possibly `crates/ftui-core/src/input_parser.rs` (+ unit test) or `crates/ftui-harness/src/main.rs`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Failing case names + classification in a bead comment.
- [ ] `test_mouse_sgr.sh` 11/11 and `test_paste.sh` 6/6 locally and in both CI PTY jobs (run id).
- [ ] Any parser fix has a named unit test in `input_parser.rs` reproducing the exact bytes.
- [ ] JSONL per case includes `seq_1006h`/`seq_2004h`/`events_seen`.

## Tests and logging

PTY driver `tests/e2e/lib/pty.sh` (+ canonicalizer); JSONL fields above plus `run_id`, `identity`,
`duration_ms`, `exit_code`, `hash`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-06-impl`. Related: `g36-impl` (SGR-pixels 1016; do not fold it in here), `g05-impl`
(identity overrides). Unblocks: `g04-09-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: grepping the raw capture instead of the canonicalized screen. The canonicalizer exists
  precisely so diff updates do not split text.
- Risk: enabling mouse reporting in a PTY without a real terminal is harmless (the driver ignores the
  DECSET) but the harness must not wait for a reply.

## Definition of done

Both suites fully green on both OSes with run id; root cause, fix commit and any new unit test named in
the close reason.

title: bug(G04.9): PTY E2E macOS-only failures (vsearch_*, inline_story_*, dashboard_typewriter, bidi, voi)
description:
# bug(G04.9): PTY E2E macOS-only failures (`vsearch_*`, `inline_story_*`, `dashboard_typewriter`, bidi, voi)

## Context and why this matters

README.md promises the same terminal behaviour on Linux and macOS (FAQ; `docs/WINDOWS.md:15-19` matrix
lists macOS as validated), and the `e2e-pty` matrix runs the whole PTY suite on `macos-latest` for that
reason. Vision rows V1 (inline mode), V11 (VOI), V47 (bidi), V70; Section 5.1 row "PTY E2E macos:
vsearch_screen_load, inline_story_*, dashboard_typewriter, bidi, voi". macOS adds failures that ubuntu
does not have, which usually means timing (slower runners, different PTY buffering), BSD tool
differences (`grep -P`, `date +%s%3N`, `sha256sum` vs `shasum`), or virtualized-list behaviour that G10
is rewiring. Parent: `g04-09-impl`.

## Current state (evidence)

- Run 33152820289 job "PTY E2E (macos-latest)" 98788563987: failing clusters `vsearch_screen_load`
  (`tests/e2e/scripts/test_virtualized_search.sh:203`; siblings `vsearch_focus_search` :229,
  `vsearch_query` :256, `vsearch_navigation` :283, `vsearch_jump_bottom` :309), `inline_story_*`
  (`test_inline_story.sh:100 run_case`, cases `inline_story_80x24_ui<h>`, `inline_story_120x40_ui<h>`,
  `inline_story_200x50_ui<h>` at :269-271), `dashboard_typewriter` (`test_text_effects_sweep.sh:119`
  `"dashboard_typewriter|2|dashboard|Typewriter"`, :138), plus the bidi and voi cases handled by
  `g04-09-impl-rtl` / `g04-09-impl-voi` (macOS re-verification happens there).
- `vsearch_screen_load` (:203-231): runs the demo with `FTUI_VSEARCH_DETERMINISTIC=true`,
  `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN_MODE=inline`, `FTUI_DEMO_UI_HEIGHT=20`, `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN=23`,
  `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS=1200`; asserts capture > 300 bytes and `Virtualized Search` and `Items` in
  the assert file. Section 2.2.B: `virtualized_search.rs:613` keeps its own vectors and does not use
  `VirtualizedList`; G10 rewrites it on `VirtualizedList` and re-blesses its snapshots — expect the
  screen's text to change then.
- `inline_story` cases assert scrollback preservation with region hashes (`hash_region` :72,
  `hash_tail_region` :86) under `FTUI_DEMO_SCREEN_MODE=inline`, `FTUI_DEMO_DETERMINISTIC=1`,
  `FTUI_DEMO_SEED`, `FTUI_DEMO_TICK_MS` (:130-136); JSONL `case_step` events (:117).
- macOS specifics to check: `date +%s%3N` is unsupported by BSD `date` (used in
  `test_keybinding.sh:102`); `grep -a -P` (PCRE) is unavailable in BSD grep (used in `test_cleanup.sh`
  mouse case); `xxd`/`sha256sum` availability; PTY driver buffering in Python `pty` on macOS.
- Common infrastructure: `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh` `e2e_now_ms`/`e2e_timestamp` helpers exist for
  portable timing — scripts that bypass them are suspects.

## Target state

`run_all.sh` on `macos-latest` reports the same pass set as ubuntu (166/166); every script uses the
portable helpers (`e2e_now_ms`, `sha256_file`, `grep -a -E` instead of `-P`); timing-sensitive cases
derive their waits from `E2E_TIME_STEP_MS` and the demo's `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS` rather than fixed
sleeps; root causes recorded per cluster.

## Implementation plan

1. Download `e2e-pty-summary-macos-latest` and the failure bundle from run 33152820289; list the exact
   failing names; diff against the ubuntu list to isolate macOS-only ones.
2. Portability sweep (mechanical but done by hand, per AGENTS.md "No Script-Based Changes"): replace
   `date +%s%3N` with `e2e_now_ms`, `grep -P` with `grep -E` equivalents, `sha256sum` with the existing
   `sha256_file` helper, in every script under `tests/e2e/scripts/` that uses them (list them with `rg
   -n "date \+%s%3N|grep -a -P|sha256sum" tests/e2e/scripts`). Each change cites the BSD incompatibility
   in a comment.
3. `vsearch_screen_load`: if the failure is timing (capture < 300 bytes), raise `FTUI_DEMO_EXIT_AFTER_MS`
   proportionally to `E2E_TIME_STEP_MS` and assert on the first full frame instead of byte count; if it
   is content, wait for `g10-impl` (which re-blesses the screen) and re-verify; record which.
4. `inline_story_*`: compare the region hashes between OSes; if they differ only by PTY chunking, hash
   the canonicalized screen (`pty_canonicalize`) instead of raw regions; if DECSTBM/sync behaviour
   differs by identity, declare the identity explicitly (`TERM=xterm-256color`, `FTUI_CAPS_PROBE=0`).
5. `dashboard_typewriter`: text effects are tick-driven; ensure `FTUI_DEMO_TICK_MS` is honoured on macOS
   (compare the `emit_textfx_hash_jsonl` :150 hashes against ubuntu); fix the sweep's expected hash
   source if the effect uses wall time anywhere (`rg -n "Instant::now" crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/
   text_effects*`).
6. Add a CI step on the macOS leg printing `bash --version`, `grep --version`, `date --version || date`
   and `python3 --version` for future triage.

## Files to change

- `tests/e2e/scripts/*.sh` (portability edits, each cited), `test_virtualized_search.sh`,
  `test_inline_story.sh`, `test_text_effects_sweep.sh`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: tool version echo on macOS.
- Possibly `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/*` where wall time leaks into deterministic mode.

## Success criteria

- [ ] macOS-only failing names + classification in a bead comment.
- [ ] "PTY E2E (macos-latest)" summary: `failed: 0`, same `passed` count as ubuntu (run id).
- [ ] No `date +%s%3N` / `grep -P` / bare `sha256sum` left in `tests/e2e/scripts` (rg evidence).
- [ ] Any wall-time leak in deterministic demo mode fixed with a unit test in the showcase
      (`text_effects_deterministic_under_fixed_ticks`).

## Tests and logging

JSONL per case (`case_step_start/end`, `assert`) with `os`, `identity`, `hash`, `duration_ms`,
`tick_ms`; macOS tool-version lines in the job log.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-06-impl`; `g10-impl` (virtualized search rewrite changes the screen text);
`g29-impl` for the bidi re-verification on macOS. Unblocks: `g04-09-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: `if: runner.os != 'macOS'` skips. The macOS leg exists to catch exactly these differences.
- Risk: macOS runners are slower and shared; every remaining wait must scale with `E2E_TIME_STEP_MS`.

## Definition of done

macOS PTY job green three runs running (ids in the close reason); portability sweep evidence; root
causes per cluster.

title: task(G04.10): Pin every CI job to the channel in rust-toolchain.toml (no floating nightly)
description:
# task(G04.10): Pin every CI job to the channel in `rust-toolchain.toml` (no floating nightly)

## Context and why this matters

`rust-toolchain.toml` says, in its own header: "Pinned by DATE, deliberately — do not revert this to a
bare `channel = "nightly"`. A floating nightly means an upstream rustc regression lands here with no
warning and no reproducible green build." It cites the clippy-driver ICE "unexpected rigid alias in
layout_of after normalization" seen on nightlies around 2026-08-22/23 in three sibling repositories and
pins `nightly-2026-08-25` (commits `9f05e519` 2026-08-25 pinned nightly-2026-08-20, `b572f690`
2026-08-27 moved to 2026-08-25). AGENTS.md "Toolchain: Rust & Cargo" (:48-66) and the README badge
`rust-nightly` (README.md:19) describe a nightly project. Vision row V70 (gates green) and Section 2.2
letter E ("CI jobs use floating `nightly` despite the dated pin"). The consequence: CI does not
reproducibly build what developers build; a green (or red) run cannot be attributed to code vs
toolchain; cache keys are wrong; and the `stable` legs of the `check` matrix are mislabelled (see
evidence) so their results mean something different from what the job name says.

## Current state (evidence)

- `rust-toolchain.toml`: `[toolchain] channel = "nightly-2026-08-25" profile = "minimal" components =
  ["rustfmt", "clippy"]`; the file has existed since `aadc5679` (2026-01-31).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: every job uses `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` with an explicit input —
  `toolchain: ${{ matrix.rust }}` in `check` (:40-42, matrix `rust: [stable, nightly]` :30-33) and
  `toolchain: nightly` in `docs` (:95-97), `features` (:128-130), `coverage` (:170-172), `benchmarks`
  (:304-306), `docs-build` (:348-350), `e2e-widget-api` (:385-387), `demo-showcase` (:447-449), `e2e-pty`
  (:541-543), `golden-trace-gates` (:709-711), `doctor-frankentui-verification` (:1110-1112), `fuzz`
  (:2092-2094), `frankenterm-conformance-gates` (:2156-2158), `msrv` (:2245-2248, comment "Using nightly
  as MSRV since project requires edition 2024"), `wasm` (:2265-2267), `pane-perf-artifacts`
  (:2310-2312), `perf-rollout-gates` (:2489-2491). `release.yml:70` uses `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly`;
  `emulator_compat_matrix.yml:47` uses `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` with no input (= stable);
  `doctor_frankentui_extended.yml:44-46` `toolchain: nightly`. Cache keys embed `matrix.rust`/`nightly`.
- How `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` works (action.yml fetched 2026-09-01): it runs `rustup toolchain install
  <toolchain> --profile minimal --no-self-update` (:91-92) and then `rustup default <toolchain>` (:97-98,
  `continue-on-error: true`). It does not set `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` and does not read
  `rust-toolchain.toml`. Rustup's override precedence is `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` env > directory override >
  `rust-toolchain.toml` > `rustup default`, so every `cargo` invoked inside the checkout very likely
  resolves to `nightly-2026-08-25` from the file (auto-installed on first use) regardless of the
  `toolchain:` input. Consequences to verify in the first PR (add a `rustup show active-toolchain`
  step): the "stable" matrix legs are probably running the pinned nightly (which also explains how
  `.cargo/config.toml`'s `[build] rustflags = ["-Z", "threads=4"]` — a nightly-only flag — compiles on
  the "stable" legs), the installed `nightly`/`stable` toolchains are dead weight (about 1-2 min per
  job), and the `-${{ matrix.rust }}-` cache keys do not distinguish anything real.
- `scripts/fuzz_campaign_e2e.sh:33 NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN="${NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN:-nightly}"` runs `cargo
  +nightly fuzz` explicitly (a real floating use).

## Target state

One source of truth: the channel in `rust-toolchain.toml`. Every workflow job installs exactly that
channel (parsed by a tiny step), asserts it is active before building, and uses it in cache keys. The
`check` matrix has an OS axis only (the misleading `rust` axis is removed; the `--all-features` step
moves to the `test-all-features` job created by G04.12). Scripts that call `cargo +nightly` use the
pinned channel. The pin-check job (G04.15) guards the file format.

## Implementation plan

1. Add a reusable step (copy into each job — GitHub composite actions cannot set job-level matrix, but
   a composite action `.github/actions/rust-pin` is allowed and preferred to 17 copies):
   `.github/actions/rust-pin/action.yml` with steps: `Parse pin` (`channel=$(sed -nE
   's/^channel = "([^"]+)"/\1/p' rust-toolchain.toml); echo "channel=$channel" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`;
   fail if empty or if it does not match `^nightly-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$`), `Install`
   (`uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master` with `toolchain: ${{ steps.pin.outputs.channel }}` and
   `components: rustfmt, clippy` plus optional `targets:` input), `Assert active` (`rustup show
   active-toolchain | grep -F "$channel"` — fails loudly if the file and the installed toolchain
   disagree), `Report` (`rustc -Vv`, `cargo -V` to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`). Outputs: `channel`.
2. `ci.yml`: replace each `Install Rust toolchain` block with `- id: rust; uses: ./.github/actions/rust-pin`
   (with `targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown` in `wasm`, `components: llvm-tools-preview` in `coverage`);
   change cache keys from `-${{ matrix.rust }}-`/`-nightly-` to `-${{ steps.rust.outputs.channel }}-`;
   in `check` remove the `rust` axis (`matrix: os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]`) and
   the `if: matrix.rust == 'nightly'` on the all-features step (G04.12 moves that step; until then
   leave it unconditional on ubuntu only via `if: runner.os == 'Linux'`).
3. `release.yml:70`, `emulator_compat_matrix.yml:47`, `doctor_frankentui_extended.yml:44-46`: same action.
4. `scripts/fuzz_campaign_e2e.sh:33`: default `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` to the parsed channel
   (`sed -nE ... rust-toolchain.toml`), falling back to `nightly` only if the file is absent; `fuzz/README.md`
   examples use `cargo fuzz` without `+nightly` (the file pins it).
5. AGENTS.md "Toolchain: Rust & Cargo" (:48-56): one sentence "CI installs exactly the channel in
   `rust-toolchain.toml` via `.github/actions/rust-pin`; bump the pin there, nowhere else" (keep the
   `g06-impl` rewrite consistent).
6. `ubs` on touched files. No deletion of workflows; the `msrv` job is handled by `g04-15-impl`.

## Files to change

- `.github/actions/rust-pin/action.yml`: new composite action (single source of the install logic).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: 17 install blocks, cache keys, `check` matrix.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.github/workflows/emulator_compat_matrix.yml`,
  `.github/workflows/doctor_frankentui_extended.yml`: install blocks.
- `scripts/fuzz_campaign_e2e.sh`, `fuzz/README.md`: pinned channel.
- `AGENTS.md`: toolchain sentence.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Every job log contains `active toolchain: nightly-2026-08-25-<host>` from the assert step; no job
      installs `stable` or bare `nightly` (grep the run logs: `gh run view <id> --log | grep -c
      "rustup toolchain install nightly "` = 0 for the bare word).
- [ ] The first PR's "Assert active" step documents whether the old "stable" legs were really stable
      (paste the `rustup show active-toolchain` output from before/after in a bead comment).
- [ ] Changing the pin in `rust-toolchain.toml` alone changes what CI builds (verified once in a scratch
      branch by pinning to the previous date and observing the version in the summary).
- [ ] `g04-10-tests` satisfied.

## Tests and logging

`g04-10-tests`. Logging: `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` line `toolchain: nightly-2026-08-25 (rustc <ver> <hash>)`
per job; cache key visible in the cache step.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none. Unblocks: `g04-15-impl` (pin-check job reuses the action), `g04-12-impl` (topology
builds on the OS-only matrix), `g04-e2e`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: omitting the `toolchain:` input and relying on `rust-toolchain.toml` implicitly.
  `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master` requires the input, and an explicit assert is the only way to prove the
  pin is honoured; the composite action makes it explicit and cheap.
- Rejected: keeping a `stable` leg "for signal". The workspace uses `-Z threads=4` in
  `.cargo/config.toml` and edition-2024 nightly features; a genuine stable build is a separate decision
  (README badge says nightly). If the owner wants stable compatibility, that is a new bead, not a
  mislabelled matrix leg.
- Risk: `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master` is unpinned; pin it to a commit SHA in the action for
  reproducibility (note the SHA in the bead).

## Definition of done

All workflows use the action; assert step green everywhere; evidence of the old/new active toolchain in
the bead; run id in the close reason; AGENTS.md sentence added.

description:
# task(G04.1): Tests proving E2E seed variables no longer leak into `cargo test`

## Context

Companion to `g04-01-impl`. The Widget API E2E job (98788563849) and Demo Showcase job (98788563924) of
run 33152820289 failed because `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh:95-105` exports `FTUI_SEED`, `FTUI_HARNESS_SEED`,
`FTUI_DEMO_SEED`, `FTUI_TEST_SEED` (all 0) and the scripts then run `cargo test`
(`scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh:481`, `scripts/demo_showcase_e2e.sh:356`). `crates/ftui-harness/src/determinism.rs:517-524`
and `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/determinism.rs:52-54` read those variables, so
`determinism::tests::jsonl_logger_emits_core_fields` (expects `"seed":99`) and snapshot
`determinism_lab_initial_80x24` (expects `Seed: 7`, from `determinism_lab.rs:41 DEFAULT_SEED = 7`) fail.
This bead makes the regression impossible to reintroduce silently.

## What to test

1. The harness seed resolution order and default, without touching process env.
2. The showcase determinism-lab screen renders the seed it was constructed with, regardless of env.
3. The E2E scripts run `cargo test` with the seed variables unset (shell-level test).
4. The CI jobs are green.

## Test types

Unit (Rust):
- `crates/ftui-harness/src/determinism.rs` `fixture_seed_prefers_env_then_default`: with an injected
  reader returning `FTUI_TEST_SEED=5` assert 5; `FTUI_SEED=6` only -> 6; `FTUI_HARNESS_SEED=1`,
  `E2E_SEED=2` -> 1 (order); nothing -> default 99.
- `crates/ftui-harness/src/determinism.rs` `jsonl_logger_explicit_seed_wins_over_env`: build
  `TestJsonlLogger::new_with("x", 99, true, 100)` and assert `"seed":99` — this is the rewritten
  `jsonl_logger_emits_core_fields`; keep the assertions on `"event"`, `"run_id"`, `"deterministic"`,
  `"schema_version":1` (:642-646).
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/determinism_lab.rs` `with_seed_renders_that_seed`: construct
  `DeterminismLab::with_seed(11)`, render 80x24 into a `Buffer`, assert the header row contains
  `Seed: 11`.
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/determinism.rs` `seed_from_env_with` already has an injectable reader
  (`:52-54` calls `seed_from_env_with`); add `demo_seed_default_when_unset` asserting default 7 through it.

Shell (E2E lib self-test):
- `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh` gains `e2e_cargo_test_env_guard`; add a case to the existing
  `E2E_SELF_TEST=1` path (`common.sh:167-179`, `e2e_fixture_self_test`) that runs
  `e2e_cargo_test_env_guard env` and asserts none of `FTUI_SEED FTUI_HARNESS_SEED FTUI_DEMO_SEED
  FTUI_TEST_SEED E2E_SEED E2E_CONTEXT_SEED` appear in the output; emit
  `jsonl_assert "cargo_test_env_guard_self_test" pass|fail "leaked=<names>"`.

E2E (CI):
- `ci.yml` job `Widget API E2E`: step "Run Widget API E2E tests" green; JSONL validated by the existing
  "Validate Widget API E2E JSONL logs" step (`ci.yml:409-424`, `validate_jsonl.py --strict`).
- `ci.yml` job `Demo Showcase`: steps "Run demo showcase E2E tests" and "Run snapshot tests" green.

## Logging

JSONL (schema `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json`, events `run_start`, `step_start`/`step_end`,
`assert`, `run_end`): the guard emits an `assert` event named `cargo_test_env_hermetic` with details
`unset=FTUI_SEED,...` and the step name; the harness test logger line carries `run_id`, `seed`,
`deterministic`, `schema_version`. Tracing targets: none new.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-harness/src/determinism.rs` (tests module)
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/determinism_lab.rs` (tests module)
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/determinism.rs` (tests module)
- `tests/e2e/lib/common.sh` (self-test case)

## Success criteria

- [ ] The four unit tests above pass under `E2E_SEED=0 FTUI_HARNESS_SEED=0 FTUI_DEMO_SEED=0 FTUI_TEST_SEED=0
      cargo test -p ftui-harness -p ftui-demo-showcase determinism` (run through `rch exec`).
- [ ] `E2E_SELF_TEST=1 ./scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh` prints `cargo_test_env_guard_self_test pass`.
- [ ] CI run on `main` after merge: jobs 'Widget API E2E' and 'Demo Showcase' green; the log line
      `test determinism::tests::jsonl_logger_explicit_seed_wins_over_env ... ok` and
      `test determinism_lab_initial_80x24 ... ok` present. Cite the run id in the close reason.

Blocked by `g04-01-impl`. Unblocks `g04-e2e`.

title: task(G04.10): Verification that CI builds exactly the pinned toolchain
description:
# task(G04.10): Verification that CI builds exactly the pinned toolchain

## Context

Companion verification bead for `g04-10-impl` (S-sized). `rust-toolchain.toml` pins
`nightly-2026-08-25` with an ICE rationale, but every job in `ci.yml` passes `toolchain: nightly` or
`${{ matrix.rust }}` (stable/nightly) to `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` (e.g. :40-42, :95-97, :2245-2248),
`release.yml:70` uses `@nightly`, `emulator_compat_matrix.yml:47` uses `@stable`. The action only runs
`rustup toolchain install` + `rustup default` (action.yml:91-98), so which toolchain `cargo` actually
uses inside the checkout is decided by rustup's override precedence, not by the workflow. The fix adds
`.github/actions/rust-pin` that parses the file, installs that channel and asserts it is active.

## What to test

1. The pin parser rejects malformed/floating channels and accepts the dated form.
2. Every job's active toolchain equals the file's channel.
3. Changing the file changes CI's toolchain (and nothing else does).
4. Cache keys carry the channel.

## Test types

Shell unit test for the parser (run locally and as the first step of the pin-check job, `g04-15-impl`):
- `scripts/ci/parse_toolchain_pin.sh` (the same one-liner the action uses, kept in a script so it can be
  tested): given a temp file with `channel = "nightly-2026-08-25"` prints `nightly-2026-08-25`, exit 0;
  with `channel = "nightly"` exits 1 with `floating channel not allowed`; with no `channel` line exits 1;
  with `channel = "1.89.0"` exits 1 (this workspace is nightly-only; adjust if the owner later allows
  stable). Test cases in `scripts/ci/parse_toolchain_pin_test.sh` (bash, asserts exit codes and output).

Workflow verification:
- In the first run after merge, for every job: `gh run view <run-id> --log | grep "active toolchain"`
  shows `nightly-2026-08-25` on every line (count of lines == number of jobs that ran).
- Before/after comparison: in a scratch branch prior to the change, add only the `rustup show
  active-toolchain` step to the `check (stable)` leg and record its output; paste both outputs in the bead
  comment (this settles whether the old stable legs were really stable).
- Scratch-branch experiment: set `channel = "nightly-2026-08-20"` and confirm `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` shows
  that date in every job; revert.
- Negative: set `channel = "nightly"` in a scratch branch; the action's "Parse pin" step fails with
  `floating channel not allowed` (run id pasted).

Cache verification:
- The cache step logs a key containing `nightly-2026-08-25` (grep `Cache restored from key` /
  `cache-<os>-...-nightly-2026-08-25-`).

## Logging

`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` per job: `toolchain: <channel> (rustc <version> <commit-hash> <date>)`; the
assert step prints `rustup show active-toolchain`.

## Files

- `.github/actions/rust-pin/action.yml`, `scripts/ci/parse_toolchain_pin.sh`,
  `scripts/ci/parse_toolchain_pin_test.sh` (new, minimal; the `scripts/ci/` directory is new — keep it to
  these two files), all workflow files.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Parser test script passes (4 cases) locally; it also runs in the pin-check job.
- [ ] Every job in one green `main` run shows the pinned channel (run id + count).
- [ ] Before/after outputs for the old stable legs recorded.
- [ ] Negative and scratch-pin experiments cited by run id.

## Dependencies

Blocked by `g04-10-impl`. Unblocks `g04-15-impl` (pin-check job), `g04-e2e`.

## Definition of done

Evidence items above in the close reason; parser test committed.

title: bug(G04.11): Make the crates.io publish loop in release.yml idempotent and dry-runnable
description:
# bug(G04.11): Make the crates.io publish loop in `release.yml` idempotent and dry-runnable

## Context and why this matters

README.md "Installation" says all 17 library crates are published on crates.io (README.md:305-311) and
`release.yml` is the only mechanism that publishes them ("Publishes all workspace crates to crates.io on
version tags. Crates are published in dependency order with delays between each", release.yml:1-4).
Vision row V66 (crates.io: WORKING, but the release pipeline is red); Section 2.2 letter E; Section 5.1
row "release.yml (last two runs): `ftui-simd@0.6.0 already exists on crates.io` (publish loop not
idempotent)". The consequence: any re-run of a release (after a transient crates.io error, a rate limit,
or a partial publish) fails on the first already-published crate and never reaches the later ones, so a
half-published version can only be completed by hand. G41 (release checklist) depends on this.

## Current state (evidence)

- `.github/workflows/release.yml:59-131` job `publish-crates` (needs `verify`, `timeout-minutes: 30`,
  skipped for pre-release tags :64-65): `publish()` (:77-94) runs `cargo publish -p "$crate"`, and on
  failure only recognises the text `already uploaded` (:84 `elif echo "$output" | grep -q "already
  uploaded"`) as a skip; any other failure exits 1 (:86-90). Recent cargo/crates.io report the condition
  as `crate ftui-simd@0.6.0 already exists on crates.io index`, so the skip branch never matches and the
  loop dies at the first crate (`publish ftui-simd`, :97). `sleep 20` between publishes (:93).
- Publish order (:96-129): ftui-simd, ftui-i18n | ftui-core | ftui-render, ftui-pty, ftui-a11y |
  ftui-layout, ftui-style, ftui-backend | ftui-text, ftui-tty | ftui-runtime | ftui-widgets |
  ftui-extras, ftui-harness, ftui-web | ftui (17 crates).
- `verify` job (:27-54) compares the tag (`v*`, or the `workflow_dispatch` `tag` input) with the first
  `^version` line of the root `Cargo.toml` (:47; the workspace version is `Cargo.toml:27-28
  [workspace.package] version = "0.6.0"`).
- No dry-run mode exists; `workflow_dispatch` requires a real tag (:12-17).
- `ftui-simd` is a 17-line doc-only crate (Section 2.2.F) that nothing depends on; it is nevertheless
  first in the loop. Whether it should be published at all is the G33 owner decision (`g33-decision`).

## Target state

Re-running the release workflow on the same tag is safe: each crate is checked against crates.io
before publishing, already-published versions are logged as `skip` and the loop continues; every
outcome is logged as one structured line; a `dry_run` input runs `cargo publish --dry-run` per crate
without a token; the final step prints a table of `crate | version | published|skipped|failed`.

## Implementation plan

1. `release.yml` `publish()`: before `cargo publish`, query
   `https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/<crate>/<version>` with `curl -fsS -A "frankentui-release
   (github-actions)"` (crates.io requires a User-Agent); HTTP 200 -> `echo "::notice::<crate>@<version>
   already on crates.io, skipping"` and `skipped=$((skipped+1))`, continue without sleeping; 404 ->
   publish. Alternative when the API is unreachable: fall through to `cargo publish` and treat both
   texts `already uploaded` and `already exists on crates.io index` as skip (keep the text match as the
   second line of defence).
2. Log each outcome to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` as a markdown table row and to `release_log.jsonl`
   (`{"crate":..,"version":..,"status":"published|skipped|failed","elapsed_s":..}`) uploaded as an artifact.
3. Add `workflow_dispatch` input `dry_run` (boolean, default false). When true: skip the token check,
   run `cargo publish -p <crate> --dry-run` for each crate in the same order, and mark rows
   `dry-run-ok`. Note in a comment that `--dry-run` fails for a crate whose path dependencies are not yet
   on crates.io at the new version, so the dry run is only fully meaningful for a version bump that has
   not been published yet; that is acceptable and documented in `docs/release-checklist.md` (G41).
4. After the loop, verify: for every crate, the API returns 200 for the version; print the table; exit 1
   if any `failed`.
5. Keep `sleep 20` only after a real publish; use `cargo publish --no-verify`? No — keep verification
   (it catches packaging errors); the 30-minute job timeout may need raising to 45 for 17 verified
   builds (measure in the first real run and record).
6. `ubs .github/workflows/release.yml`; validate YAML with `actionlint` if available.

## Files to change

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: `publish()` idempotency, `dry_run` input, summary table, artifact.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` with `tag: v0.6.0`, `dry_run: false` on the current `main` completes green with
      17 `skipped` rows (nothing new to publish) — this is the idempotency proof (run id in close reason).
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` with `dry_run: true` completes without `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` and prints 17
      `dry-run-ok` (or documents the expected path-dependency dry-run limitation).
- [ ] The `release_log.jsonl` artifact validates as JSONL and has 17 rows.
- [ ] `g04-11-tests` satisfied.

## Tests and logging

`g04-11-tests`. Logging: summary table, `release_log.jsonl` artifact, `::notice::` annotations for skips,
`::error::` for failures with the cargo output.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none. Unblocks: `g41-impl` (release preflight builds on the idempotent loop), `g04-e2e`.
Related: `g33-decision` (whether `ftui-simd` stays in the publish list), `g10-impl` uses none.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: `continue-on-error` on the publish step. It would hide real publish failures.
- Rejected: `cargo publish --workspace` (newer cargo) as the single command. It changes ordering
  semantics and error handling in one go; revisit when the toolchain pin moves past a cargo that supports
  it, as a separate bead.
- Risk: crates.io API rate limits; one GET per crate is fine, and the text-match fallback covers outages.

## Definition of done

Idempotent re-run green on the current tag; dry-run mode green; artifact uploaded; run ids in the close
reason; `docs/release-checklist.md` (G41) references the dry-run input.
