title: task(G04.11): Verification of the idempotent release loop (re-run on published tag, dry run, artifact)
description:
# task(G04.11): Verification of the idempotent release loop (re-run on published tag, dry run, log artifact)

## Context

Companion verification bead for `g04-11-impl` (S-sized). `release.yml:77-94` `publish()` treats only
the text `already uploaded` as a skip; the last two release runs failed with `crate ftui-simd@0.6.0
already exists on crates.io index` at the first crate (`:97 publish ftui-simd`). The fix queries
crates.io per crate/version, logs `published|skipped|failed`, adds a `dry_run` input and an artifact.
There is no Rust code to unit-test; the shell function is small enough to test in isolation.

## What to test

1. The skip decision for an already-published version (API 200) and the fallback text match.
2. The loop continues past skips and stops on a real failure.
3. Dry-run mode needs no token and reports per crate.
4. The artifact and summary table are produced and complete.

## Test types

Shell unit tests (extract the `publish()` logic into `scripts/ci/release_publish.sh` so it can be run
outside Actions; the workflow sources it):
- `scripts/ci/release_publish_test.sh`: stub `curl` and `cargo` with functions on `PATH` (a temp dir
  with two shell scripts) to simulate (a) API 200 -> expects `status=skipped`, no `cargo publish` call;
  (b) API 404 + cargo success -> `status=published`, one call, `sleep` stubbed; (c) API 404 + cargo output
  `already exists on crates.io index` -> `status=skipped`; (d) API 404 + cargo error `failed to verify
  package tarball` -> `status=failed`, loop exits 1 after logging; (e) `DRY_RUN=1` -> `cargo publish
  --dry-run` invoked, `status=dry-run-ok`. Assert the JSONL rows written to `release_log.jsonl`.

Workflow verification (real crates.io, no new publishing):
- `gh workflow run release.yml -f tag=v0.6.0 -f dry_run=false` on `main`: job "Publish to crates.io"
  green; summary table shows 17 rows all `skipped`; artifact `release-log` contains 17 JSONL rows with
  `"status":"skipped"`; total runtime recorded.
- `gh workflow run release.yml -f tag=v0.6.0 -f dry_run=true`: green without the registry token; rows
  `dry-run-ok` (or the documented path-dependency limitation with the exact cargo message pasted).
- `verify` job still rejects a mismatched tag (`-f tag=v9.9.9` -> "Tag 9.9.9 does not match Cargo.toml
  0.6.0", exit 1) — run id pasted.

## Logging

`release_log.jsonl` fields: `crate`, `version`, `status`, `elapsed_s`, `attempt`, `message` (first line of
cargo output on failure); `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` table; `::notice::`/`::error::` annotations.

## Files

- `scripts/ci/release_publish.sh`, `scripts/ci/release_publish_test.sh` (new, small), `.github/workflows/release.yml`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Five shell test cases pass locally (`bash scripts/ci/release_publish_test.sh`).
- [ ] Idempotent re-run, dry-run and tag-mismatch runs cited by run id with the 17-row evidence.
- [ ] Artifact validated with `python3 -c 'import json,sys; rows=[json.loads(l) for l in open(sys.argv[1])];
      assert len(rows)==17'`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by `g04-11-impl`. Unblocks `g41-impl`, `g04-e2e`.

## Definition of done

Tests committed and green; three workflow runs cited; artifact evidence in the close reason.

title: task(G04.12): Split the check matrix into check / test-unit / test-all-features with 45-minute timeouts
description:
# task(G04.12): Split the `check` matrix into check / test-unit / test-all-features with 45-minute timeouts

## Context and why this matters

AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks (CRITICAL)" and "Testing" make check, clippy, fmt and the full test suite
mandatory gates; README.md claims "16.7K unit and integration tests" pass. Vision row V70 (mandatory
gates: RED in CI), Section 2.2 letter E and Section 2.3 item 3 ("Red CI normalized ... the hang has
survived since March because nothing distinguishes it from runner starvation"). Today one job does
everything (fmt, clippy, build, `--lib` tests, and on nightly the `--all-features` tests) and has no
timeout, so: a hung test holds a runner for the GitHub default of 6 hours (macOS nightly, job
98788563806) or 8h35m (Section 1); the all-features build fills the runner disk (ubuntu nightly
98788563823 and Coverage 98788563807: "No space left on device"); and advisory jobs (coverage,
benchmarks) sit in the same required workflow so their red masks code failures. The consequence for a
contributor: a PR's status is unreadable for hours and then red for reasons unrelated to the change.
G25 (perf gates) depends on this topology (`G04.12 --> G25`).

## Current state (evidence)

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:23-84` job `check` — matrix `os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]` x
  `rust: [stable, nightly]` + `windows-latest/stable` (:26-33); steps: fmt (:55-56), clippy `-D warnings`
  (:58-59), no-mock policy (:61-71), `cargo build --workspace` (:73-74), `cargo test --workspace --lib`
  (:76-77), `cargo test --workspace --all-features` only when `matrix.rust == 'nightly'` (:79-81). No
  `timeout-minutes` (the only ones in the file are :702 and :1100, both 45). Cache (:44-52) stores
  `~/.cargo/registry`, `~/.cargo/git` and the whole `target/` keyed by `matrix.rust` + `Cargo.lock`.
- `:161-200` job `coverage`: `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --all-targets --all-features --lcov` (disk
  exhaustion, job 98788563807), then a per-crate threshold gate.
- `:294-337` job `benchmarks`: `if: push && ref == main`, `./scripts/bench_budget.sh --quick`, uploads
  an artifact. Section 2.2.E: "loosened 1.5x envelopes; startup/first-frame/shutdown budgets are skipped
  as non_criterion_baseline"; `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh` is run by no workflow (G25).
- The hang: `ftui-runtime` lib tests `run_invokes_on_shutdown_before_returning_signal_error`
  (`crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs:11933`) and
  `run_pending_signal_skips_initial_render_and_subscription_start` (:11994) block on the process-global
  signal slot; fixed by `g03-impl`; per-test timeouts (`.config/nextest.toml`, `slow-timeout = { period =
  "60s", terminate-after = 2 }`) and the CI command `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` are
  owned by `g03-impl-nextest` (cluster A). `.config/` does not exist yet (verified 2026-09-01).
- `.cargo/config.toml`: `[build] rustflags = ["-Z", "threads=4"]` (nightly parallel front-end);
  `[target.wasm32-unknown-unknown] rustflags = ['--cfg', 'getrandom_backend="wasm_js"']`.
- Workspace size: 1,053,170 Rust lines in 967 files (Section 1); an all-features debug `target/` plus a
  restored cache of the previous `target/` is what exhausts the 14 GB free on `ubuntu-latest`.

## Target state

`ci.yml` is the required, code-only workflow: `check` (fmt, clippy, no-mock, `cargo check --workspace
--all-targets`) on three OSes; `test-unit` (`cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast`, per-test
timeout from `g03-impl-nextest`) on three OSes; `test-all-features` on ubuntu only with disk hygiene;
every job `timeout-minutes: 45`; no `continue-on-error`. Coverage and benchmarks move to
`.github/workflows/advisory.yml` (push to main + nightly schedule + dispatch) so their red never masks
a code failure but they still run and upload artifacts. A scratch `loop {}` test fails `test-unit` in
under 3 minutes.

## Implementation plan

1. `ci.yml` `check` job: after `g04-10-impl` (OS-only matrix, `.github/actions/rust-pin`), reduce to
   fmt -> clippy -> no-mock (with the `rg` guard from `g04-06-impl`) -> `cargo check --workspace
   --all-targets`; drop `cargo build` and both `cargo test` steps; `timeout-minutes: 45`.
2. New job `test-unit` (`needs: check`? No — run in parallel; a clippy failure should not hide a test
   failure): matrix `os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]`; install nextest with
   `taiki-e/install-action@nextest` (pin SHA); `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` exactly as
   documented by `g03-impl-nextest`; env `FTUI_TEST_TIME_SCALE: 4` (`g04-02-impl`), `CARGO_INCREMENTAL:
   0`; upload `target/nextest/default/junit.xml` (enable junit in the nextest config if
   `g03-impl-nextest` did not) as artifact `nextest-junit-<os>`; `timeout-minutes: 45`.
3. New job `test-all-features` (ubuntu only): step "Free runner disk" (remove `/usr/share/dotnet`,
   `/usr/local/lib/android`, `/opt/ghc`, `/usr/local/share/boost`, `$AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY`; print `df -h
   /` before and after — this is the standard 25-30 GB reclaim on ubuntu images); env
   `CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0`, `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only` (halves `target/` for a debug
   build; document that this differs from local builds); cache only `~/.cargo/registry` and
   `~/.cargo/git` (never `target/` for this job); `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features
   --no-fail-fast`; final step `du -sh target` logged; `timeout-minutes: 45`.
4. Move `coverage` and `benchmarks` verbatim into `.github/workflows/advisory.yml` with `on: push:
   branches: [main]`, `schedule: cron '41 4 * * *'`, `workflow_dispatch`; both `timeout-minutes: 45`;
   coverage gets the same disk-hygiene step and `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only`. Keep their
   artifacts and the coverage threshold gate unchanged (the gate still fails the advisory workflow —
   that is visible without blocking PRs).
5. Add `timeout-minutes: 45` to every remaining job in `ci.yml` (docs, features, docs-build,
   e2e-widget-api, demo-showcase, e2e-pty, fuzz, frankenterm-conformance-gates, msrv/pin-check, wasm,
   pane-perf-artifacts, perf-rollout-gates; golden-trace and doctor already have it). If a job genuinely
   needs more (doctor: 79 steps), record its measured duration and set the smallest value with margin
   (max 60), noting it in the bead.
6. Verify the hang detection once: in a scratch branch add `#[test] fn scratch_hang() { loop {} }` to
   `crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs` tests, push, and confirm `test-unit` fails within 3 minutes with the
   test name in the log (`nextest` prints `TIMEOUT [ 120.0s]`); revert. Paste the run id.
7. Branch protection: after three green runs (`g04-e2e`), the owner sets required checks to `check`,
   `test-unit`, `test-all-features` and the E2E jobs (owner action; note in `g04-e2e`).
8. `ubs` on the YAML; `actionlint` if available.

## Files to change

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: job split, timeouts, cache scope.
- `.github/workflows/advisory.yml`: new workflow hosting `coverage` and `benchmarks` (moved, not copied;
  the originals are removed from `ci.yml`).
- `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md` ("CI Alignment" :50-58): coverage now runs in `advisory.yml`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `ci.yml` has no job without `timeout-minutes` and no `continue-on-error` (grep evidence pasted).
- [ ] `test-all-features` completes on `ubuntu-latest` with `df -h` showing >= 5 GB free at the end and
      no "No space left on device" across three consecutive `main` runs.
- [ ] Scratch `loop {}` test fails `test-unit` in < 3 minutes (run id).
- [ ] `advisory.yml` runs on push to main and uploads `coverage`/`bench` artifacts; its status is not a
      required check.
- [ ] `g04-12-tests` satisfied.

## Tests and logging

`g04-12-tests`. Logging: `df -h` before/after, `du -sh target`, nextest junit artifacts per OS, job
durations recorded in the bead (baseline for future regressions).

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g03-impl` (the hang must be fixed or the split only shortens the pain), `g03-impl-nextest`
(config and command), `g04-10-impl` (OS-only matrix and pin action). Unblocks: `g25-impl` (perf-gate job
slots into the advisory/required split), `g04-e2e`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: `continue-on-error` for coverage/benchmarks inside `ci.yml`. A separate workflow keeps them
  visible without polluting the required status.
- Rejected: dropping `--all-features` tests. They are the only run that compiles the optional
  intelligence-layer modules (G07 quarantine relies on this job including the `experimental` feature).
- Rejected: caching `target/` for the all-features job. Restoring a multi-GB cache is what fills the
  disk; the registry cache alone keeps builds acceptable.
- Risk: three OS x two test jobs doubles runner minutes; mitigated by dropping the fake `stable` legs
  (`g04-10-impl`) which halves them again.

## Definition of done

Topology merged; timeouts everywhere; hang detection proven; three green runs of the new layout
(ids in the close reason); `docs/testing/coverage-playbook.md` updated.

title: task(G04.12): Verification of the new CI topology (timeouts, disk, hang detection, advisory split)
description:
# task(G04.12): Verification of the new CI topology (timeouts, disk, hang detection, advisory split)

## Context

Companion to `g04-12-impl`. Run 33152820289: Check ubuntu nightly (98788563823) and Coverage
(98788563807) died with "No space left on device" during `--all-features` builds; Check macos nightly
(98788563806) hung for the 6 h default limit in the ftui-runtime signal tests (`program.rs:11933`,
`:11994`). The fix splits `check` into `check` / `test-unit` (nextest, per-test timeout owned by
`g03-impl-nextest`) / `test-all-features` (disk hygiene), gives every job `timeout-minutes: 45`, and moves
coverage/benchmarks to `advisory.yml`. This bead defines the checks that prove each property.

## What to test

1. Static properties of the workflow files (timeouts, no continue-on-error, job set, cache scope).
2. Disk headroom on the all-features job across three runs.
3. A hung test fails fast with its name in the log.
4. Advisory workflow runs independently and is not a required check.
5. Test counts do not drop across the split (nothing silently stops running).

## Test types

Static (script `scripts/ci/workflow_lint.sh`, new, small; run in the `check` job and locally):
- `yq '.jobs[] | select(has("timeout-minutes") | not) | key' .github/workflows/ci.yml` prints nothing
  (fallback to `python3 -c` with PyYAML if `yq` is absent).
- `grep -c "continue-on-error" .github/workflows/ci.yml` == 0.
- Job keys of `ci.yml` include `check`, `test-unit`, `test-all-features` and exclude `coverage`,
  `benchmarks`; `advisory.yml` includes exactly those two.
- The `test-all-features` cache `path:` does not contain `target`.
- `actionlint` (if installed) exit 0.

Dynamic (CI):
- `test-all-features`: log shows `df -h` before/after the "Free runner disk" step with >= 20 GB
  reclaimed, and the final `df -h` with >= 5 GB free; three consecutive `main` runs green.
- Hang detection (scratch branch, once): `scratch_hang` test -> `test-unit` fails with nextest's
  `TIMEOUT` line naming `scratch_hang` in < 3 minutes wall time (`gh run view --job <id> --json
  startedAt,completedAt`). Run id pasted; branch never merged.
- `advisory.yml`: a push to `main` triggers it; `gh run list --workflow advisory.yml --limit 1` shows the
  run; the coverage artifact `lcov.info` and bench artifact exist; `gh api repos/.../branches/main/protection`
  (owner-run) does not list its jobs as required.

Counts:
- Compare the number of tests executed before/after: old `cargo test --workspace --lib` summary lines
  vs nextest's `Summary [ ... ] N tests run` on the same commit; N(new `test-unit` + `test-all-features`)
  >= N(old) (paste both).

## Logging

`df -h`/`du -sh target` lines; nextest junit artifacts `nextest-junit-<os>`; job durations table in
the bead comment (baseline for later drift).

## Files

- `scripts/ci/workflow_lint.sh` (new), `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/advisory.yml`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `workflow_lint.sh` passes locally and in CI.
- [ ] Three consecutive green `test-all-features` runs with disk evidence (ids).
- [ ] Hang-detection run id with the `TIMEOUT` line.
- [ ] Advisory run id and artifact names; test-count comparison pasted.

## Dependencies

Blocked by `g04-12-impl`. Unblocks `g25-impl` (uses the same lint for its `perf-gate` job), `g04-e2e`.

## Definition of done

All evidence in the close reason; lint script committed and running in `check`.

title: task(G04.13): Build ftui-web and ftui-showcase-wasm for wasm32 in the wasm CI job
description:
# task(G04.13): Build `ftui-web` and `ftui-showcase-wasm` for wasm32 in the `wasm` CI job

## Context and why this matters

README.md says "Web/WASM backend: Same Rust core renders in browser-oriented environments — in-tree
`ftui-web` + `ftui-showcase-wasm`" (README.md:66), lists `ftui-showcase-wasm` as "Implemented" (:227,
:697, :704, :717) and answers the FAQ "Can it run in a browser? Yes" (:1247). Vision row V8 (web: see
Section 5.2, UNPROVEN for the showcase crate); Section 5.1 "the `wasm` job only `cargo check`s core
crates for wasm32 and never builds `ftui-web` or `ftui-showcase-wasm`"; Section 5.2 "`#[wasm_bindgen]`
under `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")`; never built for wasm32 in CI: UNPROVEN". The consequence: the
two crates that carry the browser claim can break for wasm32 without any signal, and G23 (in-tree JS
host, headless-browser step) has no build to start from (`G04.13 --> G23`).

## Current state (evidence)

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:2256-2291` job `wasm` ("WASM Build Check"): `rustup target add
  wasm32-unknown-unknown`, then `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p <crate>` for
  `ftui-core`, `ftui-render`, `ftui-style`, `ftui-layout`, `ftui-text`, `ftui-i18n`, `frankenterm-core`
  (:2281-2290). Green in run 33152820289 — but it proves nothing about the web crates.
- `crates/ftui-web/Cargo.toml`: `default = []`; features `input-parser` (serde, serde_json) and
  `tracing`; deps `ftui-backend`, `ftui-core`, `ftui-layout`, `ftui-render`, `ftui-runtime` with
  `default-features = false`; dev-dep `wasm-bindgen-test = "0.3.76"`; no `wasm-bindgen` runtime dep
  (Section 5.2: "intentionally does not bind to wasm-bindgen yet", `lib.rs:8`).
- `crates/ftui-showcase-wasm/Cargo.toml`: `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`; deps `ftui-web` (feature
  `input-parser`), `ftui-demo-showcase` (`default-features = false`), `ftui-layout`, `serde_json`;
  `[target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dependencies] js-sys 0.3.103, wasm-bindgen 0.2.126, getrandom
  0.4.3 (wasm_js)`; `[package.metadata.wasm-pack.profile.release] wasm-opt = ["-Oz"]`;
  `src/lib.rs:11,14,18` `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]` / `#[cfg(any(target_arch = "wasm32", test))]`.
- `.cargo/config.toml`: `[target.wasm32-unknown-unknown] rustflags = ['--cfg',
  'getrandom_backend="wasm_js"']` (required by getrandom 0.4 on wasm) — note target-specific rustflags
  replace `[build] rustflags = ["-Z", "threads=4"]` for that target (cargo does not merge them), which is
  fine.
- Root `build-wasm.sh` (2026-09-01: exists at repo root, not `scripts/`): requires `wasm-pack`, patches
  `Cargo.toml` to drop the `ftui-extras` opt-level override, sets
  `CARGO_TARGET_WASM32_UNKNOWN_UNKNOWN_RUSTFLAGS` with `+bulk-memory,...,+multivalue`, optionally builds an
  out-of-tree `frankenterm-web` via `FRANKENTERM_WEB_CRATE_DIR`. `docs/spec/wasm-showcase-runner-contract.md`
  matches the `ShowcaseRunner` exports (Section 5.2).

## Target state

The `wasm` job (kept name) checks `ftui-web` for wasm32 with and without features and builds the
`ftui-showcase-wasm` cdylib in release for wasm32, logging the `.wasm` size as a JSON line and uploading
it as an artifact; a size regression guard exists (advisory threshold recorded, enforced later by G23 once
a real host exists); `wasm-pack build` and the headless-browser step are G23's, not this bead's.

## Implementation plan

1. `ci.yml` `wasm` job: use `.github/actions/rust-pin` with `targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown`
   (`g04-10-impl`); keep the seven existing checks; add:
   - `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p ftui-web`
   - `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p ftui-web --features input-parser,tracing`
   - `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p ftui-demo-showcase --no-default-features`
     (the showcase-wasm dependency shape)
   - `cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p ftui-showcase-wasm`
   - `ls -l target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/ftui_showcase_wasm.wasm` and
     `echo "{\"event\":\"wasm_size\",\"crate\":\"ftui-showcase-wasm\",\"bytes\":$(stat -c%s ...)}"` to the
     log and `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`; upload the `.wasm` as artifact `ftui-showcase-wasm` (retention 7).
   - `timeout-minutes: 45`.
2. Add `scripts/ci/wasm_size_guard.sh <file> <max_bytes>` that fails when the artifact exceeds the
   budget; call it with an initial budget of the first measured size x 1.25 (record the measured size in
   this bead and in `tests/baseline.json` as `wasm_showcase_release_bytes` so `g25-impl` can pick it up).
3. Do not run `build-wasm.sh` in CI yet (it mutates `Cargo.toml` and needs `wasm-pack`); note in
   `g23-impl` that the script's `Cargo.toml` patching should become a cargo profile
   (`[profile.wasm-release]`) so CI can use it without sed.
4. `docs/spec/wasm-showcase-runner-contract.md`: add a "CI" line naming the job and artifact.
5. `ubs` on YAML/scripts.

## Files to change

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `wasm` job steps, artifact, timeout.
- `scripts/ci/wasm_size_guard.sh`: new, small.
- `tests/baseline.json`: `wasm_showcase_release_bytes` row (advisory).
- `docs/spec/wasm-showcase-runner-contract.md`: CI note.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `wasm` job green with the four new steps; `wasm_size` JSON line in the log; artifact
      `ftui-showcase-wasm` downloadable (run id).
- [ ] Local reproduction via rch: `cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p
      ftui-showcase-wasm` succeeds; size recorded (bytes) in the bead.
- [ ] `wasm_size_guard.sh` fails on a budget below the measured size (verified once, output pasted).
- [ ] `g04-13-tests` satisfied.

## Tests and logging

`g04-13-tests`. Logging: `wasm_size` JSON line; `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` table `crate | bytes | budget`.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none (uses `g04-10-impl`'s action when available; otherwise `rustup target add`). Unblocks:
`g23-impl` (web host + headless browser step), `g04-e2e`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: running `wasm-pack build` now. It adds a toolchain install and `Cargo.toml` mutation for no
  proof beyond what `cargo build` gives until a host exists (G23).
- Rejected: `wasm-bindgen-test` in node now. `ftui-web` has the dev-dep but no browser-facing tests are
  known to be runnable headlessly yet; G23 decides.
- Risk: `getrandom` cfg must come from `.cargo/config.toml`; if the pin action or a future cargo ignores
  it, the build error names `getrandom_backend` — keep the config line documented.

## Definition of done

Job green with artifact and size line; budget row recorded; run id and measured size in the close
reason; G23 note added.

title: task(G04.13): Verification of wasm32 builds for ftui-web and ftui-showcase-wasm
description:
# task(G04.13): Verification of wasm32 builds for `ftui-web` and `ftui-showcase-wasm`

## Context

Companion verification bead for `g04-13-impl` (S-sized). The `wasm` job (`ci.yml:2256-2291`) only
`cargo check`s seven core crates for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`; `ftui-web` (host-driven backend, features
`input-parser`/`tracing`) and `ftui-showcase-wasm` (cdylib with `wasm-bindgen 0.2.126`, `js-sys`,
`getrandom` wasm_js; `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]` at `src/lib.rs:11,14,18`) are never built for
wasm32, so the README's "runs in a browser" claim (README.md:66, :1247) has no CI proof. The fix adds
checks/builds, a size line, an artifact and a size guard.

## What to test

1. Both crates compile for wasm32 (all feature combinations that exist).
2. The release cdylib is produced and its size is logged and bounded.
3. The artifact is uploaded and the guard script behaves (pass/fail).
4. The existing `ShowcaseRunner` export contract still matches (doc spec).

## Test types

Local (rch, wasm32 target installed):
- `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p ftui-web` exit 0.
- `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p ftui-web --features input-parser,tracing` exit 0.

description:
# task(G04.14): Run `scripts/e2e_test.sh` and `scripts/pane_e2e.sh` as CI gates (smoke mode) or stop listing them as gates

## Context and why this matters

README.md presents both scripts as the project's E2E entry points: "Deterministic E2E Runs:
`E2E_DETERMINISTIC=1 E2E_SEED=0 E2E_TIME_STEP_MS=100 ./scripts/e2e_test.sh`" (README.md:415-419), the
"E2E Scripts" list `./scripts/e2e_test.sh`, `./scripts/widget_api_e2e.sh`, `./scripts/pane_e2e.sh --mode
smoke`, `./scripts/pane_e2e.sh --mode full`, `./tests/e2e/check_pane_traceability.sh` (:432-438), and
"The pane system ... has dedicated E2E tests (`scripts/pane_e2e.sh`)" (:575). AGENTS.md "End-to-End
Testing" (:204-213) lists `./scripts/e2e_test.sh` first. Vision rows V7 (pane workspaces) and V70;
Section 2.2.E / 5.1 "scripts/e2e_test.sh and scripts/pane_e2e.sh are invoked by no workflow"; Section
2.3 item 1 (no truth mechanism between docs and code). The consequence: readers believe the render-perf
and pane suites gate merges; they do not, and both can rot silently (the reality check's rule: a script
is a gate only if a workflow runs it and its red blocks).

## Current state (evidence)

- `scripts/e2e_test.sh` (sources `tests/e2e/lib/{common,logging,pty}.sh`): options `--verbose`,
  `--quick` ("Run only core tests (inline + cleanup)", :57), `--trace-only`, `--no-large`,
  `--no-budget`, `--no-span`, `--no-tile`, `--no-selector` (:53); toggles `RUN_BASELINE`, `RUN_LARGE`,
  `RUN_BUDGETED`, `RUN_SPAN`, `RUN_TILE`, `RUN_SELECTOR` (:17-22) — it is the render-path E2E (baseline,
  large frames, budgeted degradation, span/tile diff, strategy selector) with JSONL output.
- `scripts/pane_e2e.sh`: modes `smoke` ("fast terminal + web sanity checks"), `full`, `stress`
  (:7-9, :41, :89-93); `PANE_E2E_MODE` default `full` (:29); "emits deterministic JSONL diagnostics and
  pane artifact bundles for failures, and uses rch for cargo-based checks when available" (:10-12).
- `rg -n "e2e_test.sh|pane_e2e.sh|check_pane_traceability" .github/workflows/` returns nothing
  (verified 2026-09-01). `tests/e2e/check_pane_traceability.sh` (13 KB) is also listed in README but
  check whether `pane-perf-artifacts` (`ci.yml:2301-2479`) runs it before touching it.
- README:418 recommends `E2E_SEED=0` for the whole script; after `g04-01-impl` the seed only reaches PTY
  runs, which is what the README means.

## Target state

Decision (default for this bead, unless the measured runtime makes it unreasonable): both scripts run
in CI. `e2e_test.sh --quick` and `pane_e2e.sh --mode smoke` run as steps of the `e2e-pty` ubuntu leg
(or a new `e2e-render-pane` job if they add more than 10 minutes), with strict JSONL validation and
artifact upload, and their `--full`/`stress` modes run in `advisory.yml` nightly. README and AGENTS.md
state exactly which mode CI runs. If the owner prefers de-listing instead, README/AGENTS say "local
only" and this bead records that decision.

## Implementation plan

1. Measure: run both scripts locally through rch with `time` (`--quick` and `--mode smoke`) and record
   durations, JSONL paths (`E2E_JSONL_FILE`) and artifact directories in the bead.
2. `scripts/pane_e2e.sh`: make sure the rch detection (:11-12) falls back to plain `cargo` when `rch`
   is absent (CI has no rch) and logs which path it took (`jsonl_assert "cargo_runner" pass
   "runner=cargo|rch"`); add `require_tools` (`g04-06-impl`).
3. `scripts/e2e_test.sh`: same `require_tools`; ensure `--quick` exits non-zero on any failure (read the
   summary code path) and writes `results/summary.json` like `run_all.sh`.
4. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `e2e-pty` (ubuntu leg only, `if: runner.os == 'Linux'`): steps "Render
   E2E (quick)" `E2E_JSONL_VALIDATE=1 E2E_JSONL_VALIDATE_MODE=strict ./scripts/e2e_test.sh --quick`, "Pane
   E2E (smoke)" `... ./scripts/pane_e2e.sh --mode smoke`, then validate their JSONL with
   `tests/e2e/lib/validate_jsonl.py --strict` and upload `/tmp/<their log dirs>` as `e2e-render-logs` /
   `e2e-pane-logs` (`if: always()`). If the combined time exceeds 10 minutes, create job
   `e2e-render-pane` instead (same steps, `timeout-minutes: 45`).
5. `.github/workflows/advisory.yml` (`g04-12-impl`): nightly `./scripts/e2e_test.sh` (full) and
   `./scripts/pane_e2e.sh --mode full`; `stress` stays manual (`workflow_dispatch` input).
6. README.md:415-438 and :575, AGENTS.md:204-213: state "CI runs `e2e_test.sh --quick` and `pane_e2e.sh
   --mode smoke` on every PR (job `e2e-pty`), full modes nightly (`advisory.yml`)"; add
   `tests/e2e/scripts/run_all.sh` to the list (it is the main gate and is absent from README's list).
   These are docs-truth lines that `g06-impl`'s ledger must keep (`claims-ledger.md` rows "E2E scripts").
7. `ubs` on shell and YAML.

## Files to change

- `scripts/e2e_test.sh`, `scripts/pane_e2e.sh`: `require_tools`, runner fallback, summary/exit codes.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: steps in `e2e-pty` (or new job); `.github/workflows/advisory.yml`: nightly
  full modes.
- `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`: E2E sections.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Both scripts run green in `ci.yml` on `main` (run id) with JSONL validated and artifacts uploaded;
      durations recorded.
- [ ] Nightly full modes run in `advisory.yml` (first run id).
- [ ] README/AGENTS lines match the workflow (quote them in the close reason).
- [ ] `g04-14-tests` satisfied.

## Tests and logging

`g04-14-tests`. JSONL from both scripts (`run_start`, `step_*`, `assert`, `run_end` with `run_id`,
`seed`, `mode`, per-case hashes) validated strictly; artifacts named above.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-06-impl` (tooling + `require_tools`). Related: `g04-12-impl` (advisory workflow),
`g26-impl` (its `agent_shell_log_spam` scenario lands in `e2e_test.sh`). Unblocks: `g04-e2e`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: leaving the scripts listed without running them. That is the exact docs-vs-reality drift
  the reality check found.
- Rejected: running `--mode full`/`stress` on every PR (too slow; nightly is enough for stress).
- Risk: `pane_e2e.sh` "web" checks may need node/playwright; if so, gate those steps on tool presence
  with a logged skip reason until `g23-impl` provides the host.

## Definition of done

Scripts gate PRs in smoke/quick mode with artifacts; nightly full mode; docs match; run ids in the close
reason.

title: task(G04.15): Replace the fake msrv job with a toolchain-pin-check job (pin format, lockfile)
description:
# task(G04.15): Replace the fake `msrv` job with a `toolchain-pin-check` job that asserts the pin and the lockfile

## Context and why this matters

The README badge says `rust-nightly` (README.md:19) and `rust-toolchain.toml` pins a dated nightly with
a written rationale; AGENTS.md "Toolchain: Rust & Cargo" (:48-66). Vision row V70; Section 5.1 "the
`msrv` job installs floating `nightly` and runs `cargo check` (not an MSRV check)". The job's name
promises a minimum-supported-Rust-version guarantee that the project does not have and cannot have
while it depends on nightly flags; a green "MSRV Check" is therefore a false claim in the CI summary,
the same kind of drift as the README API rows (Section 2.3 item 1). The useful thing a small extra job
can do is guard the pin file's format and the lockfile — neither is checked by any other job today.

## Current state (evidence)

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:2236-2253` job `msrv` ("MSRV Check"): `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` with
  `toolchain: nightly` and the comment "Using nightly as MSRV since project requires edition 2024"
  (:2246-2248); step "Check MSRV": `cargo check --workspace` (:2250-2251). Edition 2024 has been stable
  since Rust 1.85, so the comment's premise is stale; the real nightly dependencies are
  `.cargo/config.toml` `[build] rustflags = ["-Z", "threads=4"]` and any `#![feature(...)]` in crates
  (verify with `rg -n '#!\[feature' crates` and record the list in the bead).
- No `rust-version` key exists in `Cargo.toml` or `crates/ftui/Cargo.toml` (grep 2026-09-01).
- No job passes `--locked` to cargo (`rg -n -- "--locked" .github/workflows/ci.yml` empty), so a stale
  `Cargo.lock` would be silently updated on the runner.
- `rust-toolchain.toml` history: bare `nightly` from 2026-01-31 (`aadc5679`) until `9f05e519`
  (2026-08-25, nightly-2026-08-20), then `b572f690` (2026-08-27, nightly-2026-08-25).

## Target state

Job `toolchain-pin-check` (replacing `msrv`): asserts `rust-toolchain.toml` has a dated channel matching
`^nightly-\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` and the documented components; asserts the active toolchain equals it
(`.github/actions/rust-pin`); runs `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` and `git diff
--exit-code Cargo.lock`; runs the parser test script from `g04-10-tests`; `timeout-minutes: 45`. The
README badge stays `rust-nightly`; no MSRV claim anywhere. If the owner later wants stable support, that
is a new block (record the option in the bead, do not implement).

## Implementation plan

1. `ci.yml`: rename `msrv` -> `toolchain-pin-check` (name "Toolchain pin check"); steps: checkout;
   `bash scripts/ci/parse_toolchain_pin_test.sh` (unit tests of the parser, from `g04-10-tests`);
   `uses: ./.github/actions/rust-pin` (installs + asserts active); "Pin file components" —
   `grep -q 'components = \["rustfmt", "clippy"\]' rust-toolchain.toml`; "Locked check" — `cargo check
   --workspace --all-targets --locked`; "Lockfile unchanged" — `git diff --exit-code Cargo.lock`;
   "Nightly feature inventory" — `rg -n '#!\[feature' crates || true` printed to the step summary (so
   the day the list is empty someone can consider stable); `timeout-minutes: 45`.
2. Remove the stale MSRV comment; add a comment block explaining what the job guards and linking
   `rust-toolchain.toml`'s header.
3. `README.md`: no change to the badge; if any sentence mentions "MSRV", correct it (grep first — none
   found on 2026-09-01).
4. `docs/testing/e2e-playbook.md` or AGENTS.md toolchain section: one line naming the job.
5. `ubs`/`actionlint` on the YAML.

## Files to change

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: job rename and steps.
- `AGENTS.md`: one line in "Toolchain: Rust & Cargo".

## Success criteria

- [ ] Job "Toolchain pin check" green on `main` (run id); summary shows the channel and the feature
      inventory.
- [ ] Negative (scratch, once): `channel = "nightly"` fails at the parser step; a modified `Cargo.lock`
      (bump a dependency without committing the lock) fails at "Lockfile unchanged" (run ids).
- [ ] No job named `msrv` remains; `ci.yml` has no "MSRV" string.
- [ ] `g04-15-tests` satisfied.

## Tests and logging

`g04-15-tests`. Logging: `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` with channel, rustc version, feature inventory,
`--locked` result.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-10-impl` (pin action and parser script). Unblocks: `g04-e2e`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: deleting the job outright. The lockfile and pin-format guards are cheap and catch real
  drift (the pin file was floating for seven months).
- Rejected: adding `rust-version` to `Cargo.toml`. It would be a lie for a nightly-only workspace.
- Risk: `--locked` will fail immediately if `Cargo.lock` is already stale on `main`; fix the lockfile in
  the same PR and say so.

## Definition of done

Job renamed and green; negative controls cited; AGENTS.md line added; run ids in the close reason.

title: bug(G04.2): Remove wall-clock assertions from unit tests (Check ubuntu/macos stable)
description:
# bug(G04.2): Remove wall-clock assertions from unit tests (Check ubuntu/macos stable)

## Context and why this matters

AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks (CRITICAL)" and "Testing" (AGENTS.md:120-170) make `cargo test --workspace` a
mandatory gate, and README.md claims the suite passes ("16.7K unit and integration tests"). Vision row
V70 (mandatory gates green) is RED in CI partly because a handful of unit tests assert wall-clock
durations measured on shared GitHub runners. On a 2-vCPU `ubuntu-latest` / `macos-latest` runner under
load these fail nondeterministically, so the `check` matrix is red even when the code is right, and
real failures cannot be told apart from noise (Section 2.2.E "Red CI normalized"). Section 2.3 item 3.

## Current state (evidence)

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/command_palette/scorer.rs:3486-3515` `perf_corpus_1000_under_budget`: builds
  `BayesianScorer::fast()`, a 1,000-item corpus, `measure_stats_us(20, ...)`, prints one JSONL line
  (`"event":"palette_corpus_1000"` with a hard-coded `"ts":"2026-02-04T00:00:00Z"`, :3498-3505) and
  asserts `stats.p95_us <= budget` where `budget = coverage_budget_us(CORPUS_1000_BUDGET_US)`;
  `:3321 CORPUS_1000_BUDGET_US = 5_000`; `:3326 COVERAGE_BUDGET_MULTIPLIER = 5` applied only when
  `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE`/`CARGO_LLVM_COV` is set (:3328-3345). CI (job 98788564084, ubuntu stable):
  p95 5794 µs > 5000 µs.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs:1721-1775` `lifecycle_reconcile_removal_uses_parallel_stop`:
  three `SlowStopSub`s, `mgr.reconcile(vec![])`, asserts `elapsed < 100ms` (:1768-1771,
  "reconcile removal took {elapsed:?}, expected < 100ms with parallel stop"). CI (job 98788564122,
  macos stable): 188 ms.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs:907-935` `every_respects_interval`: `Every` at 50 ms, sleeps
  160 ms, asserts `msgs.len() >= 2` (:926-930 "Expected at least 2 ticks, got {}") and `<= 4`. CI: 1 tick.
- Other wall-clock assertions in the same crate that will fail next: `subscription.rs:823`
  (`elapsed < 100ms`), `:1324-1325` (`stop_all ... < 800ms`), `:1703-1704` (`parallel stop_all ... <
  150ms`), `:1867` (`< 400ms`); `render_thread.rs:760` (`< 1s`); `process_subscription.rs:899`
  (`kill_elapsed < 500ms`). The macOS job log lists four failing wall-clock tests; copy the remaining two
  names from job 98788564122 into this bead when starting.
- A virtual clock exists: `crates/ftui-core/src/cx.rs:74-92` `Cx` Lab mode with `LabClock` ("All `Cx`
  instances sharing the same `LabClock` see the same time"). No `FTUI_TEST_TIME_SCALE` variable exists
  anywhere in `crates/`, `tests/` or `scripts/` (verified by grep on 2026-09-01).

## Target state

No unit test in the workspace fails because a shared runner is slow. Throughput claims are measured by
criterion benches with baseline rows (consumed by the perf gate, G25); ordering/liveness properties of
timers and parallel stop are proven with a virtual clock or with assertions that do not depend on
elapsed wall time; the residual few tests that must sleep use a CI multiplier and assert generous bounds.
Twenty consecutive green `check` runs on `macos-latest`.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/command_palette/scorer.rs`: turn `perf_corpus_1000_under_budget` into a
   correctness test (`perf_corpus_1000_scores_and_sorts`: asserts result count, ordering, no NaN) that
   still prints the JSONL timing line with a real timestamp, and move the p95 <= 5 ms budget to
   `crates/ftui-widgets/benches/command_palette_bench.rs` (create if absent; check `ls
   crates/ftui-widgets/benches` first and extend an existing palette bench if one exists) as criterion
   bench `palette_corpus_1000_scan`; add the row `palette_corpus_1000_scan` to `tests/baseline.json` with
   `p95_us: 5000` so `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh` (G25) enforces it. Delete nothing; the test keeps
   its name in the JSONL event for continuity of logs.
2. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs`:
   - `every_respects_interval`: drive `Every` with `LabClock` (add `Every::with_clock(Cx)` or an
     internal `now: Arc<dyn Fn() -> Instant>` hook if `Every` cannot take a `Cx` yet) and assert exactly
     3 ticks after advancing 160 ms of virtual time; keep a smoke variant `every_ticks_at_least_once`
     that sleeps 3x the interval and asserts `>= 1` (liveness only).
   - `lifecycle_reconcile_removal_uses_parallel_stop`: replace the elapsed bound with an observable
     property: record per-subscription `stop()` start timestamps in the `SlowStopSub` counter and assert
     that all three starts happen before the first completes (parallel), which holds regardless of
     scheduling delays; keep the elapsed as a logged value, not an assertion.
   - `:823`, `:1324`, `:1703`, `:1867`: same treatment (property first; when a bound is genuinely the
     property, multiply it by `test_time_scale()`).
3. Add `pub fn test_time_scale() -> u32` in `crates/ftui-core/src/cx.rs` (or a small `test_support`
   module) reading `FTUI_TEST_TIME_SCALE` (default 1; CI sets 4) once via `OnceLock`; export it for
   the runtime tests; `ci.yml` `check`/`test-unit` jobs set `FTUI_TEST_TIME_SCALE: 4` in `env:`.
4. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/render_thread.rs:760` and `process_subscription.rs:899`: multiply by the
   scale; these bounds are liveness limits (1 s, 500 ms) and stay assertions.
5. Document the rule in `docs/testing/no-mock-policy.md` (a short "Timing assertions" paragraph: virtual
   clock for ordering, benches for throughput, `FTUI_TEST_TIME_SCALE` for liveness bounds) — it already
   governs test style and is linked from `ci.yml:64-71`.
6. `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt`, `ubs` on touched files. No script-based edits; the rewrites are
   per-test by hand.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/command_palette/scorer.rs`: test rewrite; JSONL line keeps `palette_corpus_1000`.
- `crates/ftui-widgets/benches/<palette bench>.rs`: `palette_corpus_1000_scan`.
- `tests/baseline.json`: new row.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs`: six tests.
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/render_thread.rs`, `process_subscription.rs`: scaled bounds.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/cx.rs`: `test_time_scale()`; `Every` clock hook in `subscription.rs`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `FTUI_TEST_TIME_SCALE: 4` on the test jobs.
- `docs/testing/no-mock-policy.md`: timing paragraph.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-runtime subscription` and `cargo test -p ftui-widgets command_palette` pass 20
      times in a row under `taskset -c 0 nice -n 19` (simulated slow runner) locally via rch; log kept.
- [ ] `ci.yml` `Check (macos-latest, ...)` green on 20 consecutive runs (count `gh run list --workflow
      ci.yml --branch main --limit 20`), recorded in `g04-02-tests`.

unchanged`, `Nightly feature inventory` all `success`; summary contains `channel: nightly-2026-08-25`.

  unchanged` with cargo's "lock file needs to be updated but --locked was passed".

All run ids and the parser test output in the close reason.

# task(G04): Green-main acceptance — three consecutive green `ci.yml` runs, streak script, AGENTS.md link ## Context and why this matters The G04 cluster's success criterion, in the reality-check plan's words: "three consecutive green `ci.yml` runs on `main`; `doctor_frankentui Extended Verification` green three nights running (or demoted per G22); the 'Landing the Plane' section of AGENTS.md links the green run id". This bead is that acceptance. It exists separately from the fifteen sub-item beads because green-main is a property of the whole, not of any fix, and because the April 2026 reality-gap epic (bd-i80el) "restored green gates and doc truth for one day; nothing kept them true" (Section 2.2.E). Vision rows V70 and V68; Section 7.6 row "V70 gates: three consecutive green ci.yml runs; nextest timeouts". `g42-impl` (final verification) and the monthly reality-check job (`g37-impl`) reuse the streak script defined here. ## Current state (evidence) - `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main --limit 40` on 2026-09-01: no green run; all failures since 2026-07-08 (Section 5.1); the last 60 also contain none (Section 1). Reference failing run 33152820289 on `ab07291f` (14 of 22 job instances failed or were cancelled). - `gh run list --workflow doctor_frankentui_extended.yml`: red every day 2026-08-27..2026-09-01 and 30/30 since 2026-08-06. - AGENTS.md "Landing the Plane (Session Completion)" (:785-796) lists five steps (file issues, run quality gates, update issue status, `br sync --flush-only`, hand off) and links no CI evidence. - No script computes a green streak; `scripts/` has no `ci/` directory yet (`g04-10-tests`, `g04-11-tests`, `g04-12-tests` add `scripts/ci/*.sh`). ## Target state `scripts/ci/green_streak.sh` prints the current consecutive-success streak for a workflow on `main` as JSONL and a one-line summary; the first three consecutive green `ci.yml` runs (and three green Extended Verification nights, or the G22 demotion decision) are recorded here and in AGENTS.md; the required-checks set is documented for the owner to apply in branch protection. ## Implementation plan 1. `scripts/ci/green_streak.sh [--workflow ci.yml] [--branch main] [--limit 40] [--min 3]`: uses `gh run list --workflow --branch
--limit --json databaseId,conclusion,headSha,createdAt,event` (filter `event == push`), walks newest-first, counts leading `success`, emits one JSONL line per run `{"run_id":..,"conclusion":..,"head_sha":..,"created_at":..}` to `--out ` and prints `streak= newest= oldest_green=`; exit 0 when `k >= min`, else 1. Requires `gh` (use `require_tools`-style check). Also prints the list of failed job names for the newest non-green run (`gh run view --json jobs`), which is the triage entry point for the monthly job. 2. After every G04 sub-item lands, run it; when it reports `streak=3` for `ci.yml`, record the three run ids and `head_sha`s in a bead comment, and the same for `doctor_frankentui_extended.yml` (or link `g22-decision` if the owner demoted the workflow). 3. AGENTS.md "Landing the Plane": add step 6 "Confirm main is green: `scripts/ci/green_streak.sh` must report streak >= 1 before you hand off; if red, file a bead naming the failing job" and a "Green baseline" line: "First green streak after the 2026-09 reality check: runs , , ()". Keep it to three lines; `g06-impl`'s AGENTS.md rewrite must preserve them. 4. Record in this bead the required-checks list for branch protection (`check`, `test-unit`, `test-all-features`, `PTY E2E (ubuntu-latest)`, `PTY E2E (macos-latest)`, `Widget API E2E`, `Demo Showcase`, `Documentation`, `Docs (rustdoc + examples)`, `Golden Trace Gates`, `FrankenTerm Conformance/Differential/WS Gates`, `Fuzz Build Check`, `WASM Build Check`, `Toolchain pin check`, `doctor_frankentui Verification`, `Feature Combinations`, `Pane Perf Replay Artifacts`, `Perf Rollout Gates`) and ask the owner to apply it (owner action; AGENTS.md rule 0 — do not change repository settings yourself). 5. `ubs` on the script. ## Files to change - `scripts/ci/green_streak.sh`: new. - `AGENTS.md`: Landing the Plane step 6 + Green baseline line. ## Success criteria - [ ] `scripts/ci/green_streak.sh --workflow ci.yml --min 3` exits 0; its JSONL output (three `success` rows with ids and shas) pasted into the close reason. - [ ] `scripts/ci/green_streak.sh --workflow doctor_frankentui_extended.yml --min 3` exits 0, or `g22-decision` is closed with the demotion decision and cited. - [ ] AGENTS.md contains the Green baseline line with the three run ids. - [ ] Required-checks list delivered to the owner (bead comment with the list; owner reply recorded). ## Tests and logging E2E: the script itself run against the live repository (read-only `gh` calls). JSONL fields: `run_id`, `conclusion`, `head_sha`, `created_at`, `event`, and for the newest failure `failed_jobs` (array of job names). Unit-ish: `scripts/ci/green_streak_test.sh` feeds a fixture JSON (via `GREEN_STREAK_FIXTURE=` bypassing `gh`) with sequences `S,S,S,F` -> streak 3, `F,S,S` -> 0, `S,F,S,S,S` -> 1, and asserts exit codes for `--min 3`. ## Dependencies and ordering Blocked by: `g03-impl` (hang) and every G04 sub-item impl: `g04-01-impl` .. `g04-08-impl`, `g04-09-impl`, `g04-10-impl` .. `g04-15-impl`. Unblocks: `g42-impl`, `g37-impl` (monthly job uses the streak script), `g41-impl` (release preflight requires a green run on the tag's commit). ## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected - Rejected: counting "green except advisory" runs. After `g04-12-impl` the advisory workflow is separate, so a `ci.yml` success is unambiguous. - Risk: the streak can break the day after it is recorded; that is why AGENTS.md makes the streak check a hand-off step and `g37-impl` re-checks monthly. ## Definition of done Three green run ids for `ci.yml` (and the Extended Verification outcome) in the close reason and in AGENTS.md; streak script committed with its fixture test; owner has the required-checks list.

# task(G04.2): Tests and bench for the de-flaked timing tests (virtual clock, baseline row, 20-run soak)

## Context

Companion to `g04-02-impl`. Run 33152820289 jobs Check ubuntu stable (98788564084) and Check macos stable
(98788564122) failed on `crates/ftui-widgets/src/command_palette/scorer.rs:3508` (p95 5794 µs > 5000 µs)
and `crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs:1768` ("reconcile removal took 188ms, expected < 100ms"),
`subscription.rs:926-930` `every_respects_interval` ("Expected at least 2 ticks, got 1"). This bead
specifies the replacement tests, the criterion bench and the soak that proves the flake is gone.

## What to test

- Timer semantics of `Every` under a virtual clock (exact tick count, no wall time).
- Parallelism of `SubscriptionManager::reconcile` removal as an ordering property, not a duration.
- The palette scorer's correctness on a 1,000-item corpus; its speed as a bench with a baseline row.
- `FTUI_TEST_TIME_SCALE` is honoured by every remaining sleep-based bound.
- 20 consecutive green `check` runs on macOS.

## Test types

Unit:
- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs`
  - `every_respects_interval_virtual_clock`: `LabClock` (`crates/ftui-core/src/cx.rs:87`) advanced by
    160 ms in 10 ms steps; assert exactly 3 `TestMsg::Tick` messages and that tick i arrives at
    virtual time 50*i ms (+-0).
  - `every_ticks_at_least_once_wall`: interval 20 ms, sleep `60 ms * test_time_scale()`, assert `>= 1`.
  - `reconcile_removal_stops_subscriptions_in_parallel`: `SlowStopSub` records `(id, start_ns, end_ns)`
    of `stop()` into a shared `Mutex<Vec<_>>`; assert all three `start_ns` are less than the minimum
    `end_ns` (overlap) and that `stop_count == 3`; log elapsed via `eprintln!` JSON line
    `{"event":"reconcile_removal","elapsed_ms":..}`.
  - Rewrites for `:823`, `:1324`, `:1703`, `:1867` following the same pattern; each keeps its original
    name suffixed `_property` so the old names disappear from the log (grep-able change).
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/command_palette/scorer.rs`
  - `perf_corpus_1000_scores_and_sorts`: 1,000 items, query "git co"; assert results are sorted
    descending by score, all scores finite and > 0, and the top result contains "git co"-matching text;
    print the `palette_corpus_1000` JSONL line with `ts` from `std::time::SystemTime`.
- `crates/ftui-core/src/cx.rs`
  - `test_time_scale_defaults_to_one` and `test_time_scale_parses_env` (through an injected reader, no
    env mutation).

Bench:
- `crates/ftui-widgets/benches/<palette bench>.rs` `palette_corpus_1000_scan` (criterion, 1,000 items,
  `BayesianScorer::fast()`); baseline row `palette_corpus_1000_scan` in `tests/baseline.json` with
  `p95_us: 5000`, `noise_tolerance` per the file's existing schema (`scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh`
  parses it; check its expected keys before adding the row).

Soak (E2E on CI):
- After merge, `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main --limit 20 --json conclusion,databaseId`
  shows 20 consecutive `success` for the macOS `check` job (or `test-unit` after G04.12). Record the
  first and last run ids.
- Local pre-merge soak: `for i in $(seq 20); do rch exec -- cargo test -p ftui-runtime subscription
  -- --test-threads=16 || exit 1; done` with the log saved to the scratchpad and summarised in the
  close reason.

## Logging

- Rust: `eprintln!` JSON lines with `event`, `elapsed_ms`, `ticks`, `scale` so `--nocapture` logs stay
  greppable; no new tracing targets.
- CI: `FTUI_TEST_TIME_SCALE=4` visible in the job `env:` block; the soak commands and counts pasted into
  the bead comment.

## Files

- `crates/ftui-runtime/src/subscription.rs`, `render_thread.rs`, `process_subscription.rs`
- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/command_palette/scorer.rs`, `crates/ftui-widgets/benches/`
- `crates/ftui-core/src/cx.rs`
- `tests/baseline.json`

## Success criteria

- [ ] All new/renamed tests pass under `taskset -c 0 nice -n 19 cargo test -p ftui-runtime -p ftui-widgets`
      20/20 locally (via rch).
- [ ] Bench runs and `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh --json` reports the new row.
- [ ] 20 consecutive green macOS check/test-unit runs on `main` (run ids in the close reason).
- [ ] No remaining `assert!(elapsed < Duration::...)` in `crates/ftui-runtime/src` without a
      `test_time_scale()` factor (verified by `rg "elapsed < Duration" crates/ftui-runtime/src`).

## Dependencies

Blocked by `g04-02-impl`. Related: `g25-impl` (perf gate consumes the baseline row).

## Definition of done

Tests and bench exist and are green; soak evidence and run ids in the close reason.
notes: Refinement 1: September 4 full suite failed focus p95 2112us >2000us and inspector p95 27048us >15000us. Isolated inspector passed (p95 3114us), focus failed again (7327us). Investigate worker load, debug/release profile and algorithm cost; do not merely loosen limits. Keep logical timing under a virtual clock and meaningful measured performance in a controlled gate. The historical 20 consecutive macOS runs is supporting stability evidence, not a replacement for exact-candidate checks.

title: bug(G04.3): Make ftui-tty compile clean under clippy on Windows (Check windows stable)
description:
# bug(G04.3): Make `ftui-tty` compile clean under clippy on Windows (Check windows stable)

## Context and why this matters

README.md FAQ says Windows is supported and `docs/WINDOWS.md:9-19` says the Windows CI matrix was
"Validated" on 2026-02-03; AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks" requires `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
-- -D warnings` to pass. Vision rows V67 (Windows support: PARTIAL) and V70 (gates green: RED); Section
2.2 letter E and Section 5.3 ("`ftui-tty`: real, Unix-only, opt-in via `native-backend`; fails Windows
clippy because unix-only helpers are not cfg-gated"). The user-visible consequence: the only Windows CI
leg has been red since the crate grew unix-only helpers, so Windows regressions are invisible, and G01
(default backend selection on the `ftui` facade, which must enable `native-backend` on unix and compile
to an empty shell elsewhere) cannot land until `ftui-tty` builds on Windows.

## Current state (evidence)

- Run 33152820289, job `Check (windows-latest, stable)` 98788563906 failed at step "Run clippy" with 19
  `dead_code` errors under `-D warnings`.
- `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs` is one 133 KB file. Some items are gated (`#[cfg(unix)]` on imports at
  :22, :36-38 and on fns at :228, :234, :241, :248, :276, :283, :304, :319, :364, :370, :397, :467, :474,
  :504) but these are not: constants :216-221 (`CLEAR_SCREEN`, `CURSOR_HOME`, `READ_BUFFER_BYTES`,
  `MAX_DRAIN_BYTES_PER_POLL`, `INFERRED_PIXEL_WIDTH_PER_CELL`, `INFERRED_PIXEL_HEIGHT_PER_CELL`), :226
  `PARSER_TIMEOUT_GRACE`, :267 `const fn cleanup_features_for_capabilities`, :519 `pub struct
  TtyEventSource` with :567 `impl TtyEventSource` whose :597 `fn live(...)` opens `/dev/tty`, and the
  later public surface :1191 `impl BackendEventSource for TtyEventSource`, :1322 `pub struct
  TtyPresenter`, :1407 `pub struct TtyBackend`, :1538/1575/1595 impls, :1621 `pub fn
  write_cleanup_sequence`, :1632 `write_cleanup_sequence_with_sync_end`. On Windows the gated callers
  vanish and the ungated private items become dead code.
- `crates/ftui-tty/Cargo.toml:23-25` already scopes `nix` and `rustix` to `[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]`.
- Consumers: `crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml:34-35,69` `native-backend = ["dep:ftui-tty"]`;
  `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs:5139-5140` `#[cfg(unix)] pub fn with_native_backend(...)`; :7107 and
  :7140 `run_native` variants.
- `docs/WINDOWS.md:146` still shows "[x] Windows tests passing (CI: windows-latest)".

## Target state

`cargo clippy -p ftui-tty --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the whole workspace clippy pass on
`windows-latest`. On non-unix targets the crate compiles to a documented shell: the public types exist
(`TtyBackend`, `TtySessionOptions`, `TtyClock`) and `TtyBackend::open(...)`/`TtyBackend::new(...)` return
`io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Unsupported, "ftui-tty native backend is unix-only; use the
crossterm-compat feature on Windows")`. `docs/WINDOWS.md` states what is actually validated, with the
green run id.

## Implementation plan

1. `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs`: gate every unix-only item with `#[cfg(unix)]`, following the file's
   existing per-item style (do not split the file into new modules — AGENTS.md "No File Proliferation";
   a module move would also destroy `git blame` on 130 KB). Concretely: the constant block :216-226, the
   fn at :267, `TtyEventSource` (:519) and its impls (:567, :1191), `TtyPresenter` (:1322) if it uses
   unix-only I/O, `TtyBackend` impls that touch termios/signals, `write_cleanup_sequence*` only if
   unused off-unix (they are pure `Write` helpers; keep them cross-platform if they compile).
2. Add a `#[cfg(not(unix))]` block at the end of `lib.rs` defining the shell: `pub struct TtyBackend;`
   with `pub fn open(_: TtySessionOptions) -> io::Result<Self>` returning `Unsupported` (match the real
   constructor's name and signature — read the real `impl TtyBackend` at :1407-1537 first), plus
   `pub const BACKEND_AVAILABLE: bool = cfg!(unix);` exported on all targets so G01's runtime dispatch can
   report `"native"`/`"crossterm"`/`"none"`.
3. Crate doc comment (:1-17) gains a "Platform support" paragraph: unix implemented, Windows returns
   `Unsupported`, see `docs/WINDOWS.md`.
4. `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`: no behaviour change; confirm `with_native_backend` stays
   `#[cfg(unix)]` and that `cargo check -p ftui-runtime --features native-backend --target
   x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` passes (use `rustup target add x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `cargo check
   --target`, which works cross-platform for check-only; run via rch).
5. `docs/WINDOWS.md`: replace "Last validated: 2026-02-03" and the "Validated" matrix rows with the real
   status: "Build + clippy + `--lib` tests: validated by ci.yml run <id> (windows-latest, stable)";
   "Native backend: not available (returns Unsupported); crossterm path requires the `crossterm` feature
   until G01 lands"; tick or untick :146 accordingly.
6. `cargo check/clippy -D warnings/fmt`; `ubs crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs`.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-tty/src/lib.rs`: cfg gates; non-unix shell; `BACKEND_AVAILABLE`.
- `docs/WINDOWS.md`: validation status with run id.
- (verify only) `crates/ftui-runtime/src/program.rs`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `ci.yml` `Check (windows-latest, stable)` step "Run clippy" green (run id in close reason).
- [ ] `cargo check -p ftui-tty --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `cargo clippy -p ftui-tty --target
      x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass from Linux via rch (log attached).
- [ ] Unit test `non_unix_backend_reports_unsupported` (cfg(not(unix))) and
      `backend_available_matches_cfg` (all targets) pass; see `g04-03-tests`.
- [ ] `docs/WINDOWS.md` cites the run id.

## Tests and logging

`g04-03-tests`. No runtime logging change; the `Unsupported` error message is the observable.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none. Unblocks: `g01-impl` (facade default features must compile on Windows), `g31-impl`
(Windows scoped validation), `g04-e2e`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: `#![cfg(unix)]` at crate level. It would make the crate an empty compilation unit on Windows
  and break `ftui-runtime`'s `dep:ftui-tty` feature wiring and G01's dispatch constant.
- Rejected: `#![allow(dead_code)]` on Windows. It hides the problem and violates the `-D warnings` gate.
- Risk: the 19 errors may include items used only by tests on unix; gate the tests too
  (`#[cfg(all(test, unix))]`).

## Definition of done

Windows check job green; `docs/WINDOWS.md` updated with the run id; `BACKEND_AVAILABLE` exported and
consumed later by `g01-impl`; close reason names the tests and run id.

Close when Check (windows-latest) is green on a run id.

## Context and why this matters

README.md links docs.rs for every published crate and `ci.yml` has a dedicated "Documentation" job
(`docs-build`, `ci.yml:339-374`) that builds rustdoc with warnings denied so broken intra-doc links never
ship to docs.rs. Vision row V70 (gates green); Section 2.2 letter E. The job is red (98788563855 in run
33152820289) because of two rustdoc lints in one widget file, which means every other rustdoc regression
(and G02's README doc-tests, which will run in the docs job) is currently invisible.

## Current state (evidence)

- Job "Documentation" 98788563855: rustdoc `-D warnings` reports an unresolved intra-doc link
  `ReceiptVerdict` and redundant explicit link targets in `crates/ftui-widgets/src/receipt_verifier_panel.rs`.
- In that file: the module doc at :7 reads "takes a parsed [`ReceiptVerdict`] (build it from the
  verifier's JSON"; the type is defined at :145 `pub struct ReceiptVerdict`; further links at :188
  ("renders a [`ReceiptVerdict`] inside a bordered"), :194-196 (doc example `use
  ftui_widgets::receipt_verifier_panel::{ReceiptVerifierPanel, ReceiptVerdict}; let verdict =
  ReceiptVerdict::skeleton("rcpt-001", true);`), :250 ("in [`ReceiptVerdict::posterior_snapshot`]").
  The exact offending spans are in the job log; reproduce locally with
  `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p ftui-widgets --no-deps` (via rch) and copy the two warnings
  into this bead before editing.
- Likely causes (verify, do not guess): the `//!` module doc at :7 sits before the `use` lines and
  references an item that may only exist under a feature (`#[cfg(feature = ...)]`) so rustdoc for the
  default feature set cannot resolve it; the "redundant explicit link target" lint fires on the pattern
  `` [`Foo`](Foo) `` or `` [`Foo`](crate::path::Foo) `` where the target equals the text.
- `ci.yml:86-117` `docs` job runs `cargo test --doc --workspace` and builds harness examples;
  `:339-374` `docs-build` is the failing "Documentation" job (read its exact `cargo doc` command and
  `RUSTDOCFLAGS` when starting).

## Target state

`RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` is clean; the "Documentation" job is green;
a local one-liner in AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks" lets agents catch rustdoc lints before pushing.

## Implementation plan

1. Reproduce with `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p ftui-widgets --no-deps` (rch); record the
   two warning texts with line numbers in the bead.
2. `crates/ftui-widgets/src/receipt_verifier_panel.rs`: fix the unresolved link by using the fully
   qualified path (`` [`ReceiptVerdict`](crate::receipt_verifier_panel::ReceiptVerdict) `` only if the
   item is behind a feature; otherwise the plain `` [`ReceiptVerdict`] `` must resolve — if it does not,
   check whether the module is declared with `#[cfg(feature = ...)]` in `crates/ftui-widgets/src/lib.rs`
   and whether `cargo doc` runs without that feature; the fix is then `#[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(...)))]`
   plus documenting the feature, not deleting the link). Remove the redundant explicit targets by
   writing `` [`Name`] `` alone.
3. Run `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` to confirm nothing else is pending.
4. AGENTS.md "Compiler Checks (CRITICAL)" (:120-136): add
   `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` as the fourth command with a one-line
   note that the "Documentation" CI job enforces it (this is a docs-truth edit; the `g06-impl` AGENTS.md
   rewrite must keep it).
5. `ubs` on the file; `cargo clippy -D warnings`; `cargo fmt --check`.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-widgets/src/receipt_verifier_panel.rs`: doc links at :7, :188, :250 (and any others the
  reproduction reveals).
- `AGENTS.md`: Compiler Checks gains the rustdoc command.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` exits 0 locally (rch log).
- [ ] `ci.yml` job "Documentation" green on `main` (run id in close reason).
- [ ] `g04-04-tests` verification: the docs job log contains `Documenting ftui-widgets v0.6.0` with no
      `warning: unresolved link` / `redundant explicit link target` lines.

## Tests and logging

No unit tests apply (rustdoc lint). Verification bead `g04-04-tests` names the CI job and log lines.
Optional guard: `cargo test -p ftui-widgets --doc receipt_verifier_panel` runs the doc example at
:194-196, proving the linked API exists.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none. Unblocks: `g02-impl` (README doc-tests run in the docs job and need a green baseline),
`g04-e2e`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: `#![allow(rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links)]`. It would hide future breakage on docs.rs.
- Rejected: removing the doc links. The links are useful; they only need the right target.
- Risk: the docs job may surface more warnings once these two are gone; fix them in the same PR and list
  them in the close reason.

## Definition of done

Documentation job green; AGENTS.md command added; close reason cites the run id and the exact warnings
fixed.

title: bug(G04.5): Fix the fuzz crate manifest so cargo fuzz build works outside the workspace
description:
# bug(G04.5): Fix the fuzz crate manifest so `cargo fuzz build` works outside the workspace (Fuzz Build Check)

## Context and why this matters

README.md lists fuzz targets among the quality gates ("fuzz targets exist") and AGENTS.md's workspace
tree shows `fuzz/ # Fuzz testing (excluded from workspace)` (AGENTS.md:328). `fuzz/README.md` documents
11 targets covering the input parser, VT parser, text, layout and widget rendering. Vision rows V61
(input parser) and V70 (gates green); Section 2.2.F ("fuzz targets already cover the parser"). The
"Fuzz Build Check" job (98788563967 in run 33152820289) fails before any fuzzing happens because the fuzz
package inherits workspace lints while being excluded from the workspace, so the fuzz safety net has
been off since the `[lints]` table was added. G39 adds a nightly fuzz job on top of this fix.

## Current state (evidence)

- `fuzz/Cargo.toml:11-12`: `[lints] workspace = true`. Root `Cargo.toml:25`: `exclude = ["fuzz"]`. Cargo
  refuses `workspace = true` inheritance for a package that is not a member of the enclosing workspace
  (the manifest parse error is the first line of the failing "Build fuzz targets" step; copy it
  verbatim into the bead when starting).
- Root `Cargo.toml:53-61` `[workspace.lints.clippy]`: `needless_range_loop = "allow"`,
  `type_complexity = "allow"` (with comments). Nothing else is inherited.
- `fuzz/Cargo.toml` declares 11 `[[bin]]` targets (:39-118): `fuzz_input_parser`,
  `fuzz_input_parser_structured`, `fuzz_input_parser_long_seq`, `fuzz_vt_parser`,
  `fuzz_text_cluster_map`, `fuzz_text_shaped_layout`, `fuzz_text_wrap`, `fuzz_text_width`,
  `fuzz_text_hyphenation`, `fuzz_layout_constraints`, `fuzz_widget_render`; a 12th source file
  `fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_grid_mutations.rs` is deliberately unregistered (:67-69 note: "old
  frankenterm-core grid/cursor API is no longer vendored"). `fuzz/Cargo.lock` is a separate lockfile;
  `fuzz/artifacts/fuzz_text_cluster_map/` exists (a prior crash artifact directory, gitignored per
  `fuzz/README.md:38`).
- `ci.yml:2083-2141` `fuzz` job: `cargo install cargo-fuzz`, `cargo fuzz build`, then 20 s per target for
  10 targets (`fuzz_vt_parser` is missing from the quick list :2112-2122), then
  `FUZZ_DURATION_SECS=20 ./scripts/fuzz_campaign_e2e.sh` and artifact upload (`fuzz/artifacts/`,
  `/tmp/fuzz_campaign_e2e_*/`). `scripts/fuzz_campaign_e2e.sh:33` uses `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN=nightly`
  (floating; G04.10 pins it).

## Target state

`fuzz/Cargo.toml` is a self-contained single-package workspace with the same clippy allowances as the
root; `cargo fuzz build` builds all 11 targets; the CI quick run covers all 11; the job is green. The
nightly 60 s/target campaign with corpus artifacts is `g39-impl`.

## Implementation plan

1. `fuzz/Cargo.toml`: add
   ```toml
   [workspace]            # standalone: the root workspace excludes ./fuzz
   [workspace.lints.clippy]
   needless_range_loop = "allow"
   type_complexity = "allow"
   ```
   (mirror of root `Cargo.toml:53-61`, with a comment pointing at the root so the two stay in sync) and
   keep `[lints] workspace = true`. Alternative if cargo-fuzz's generated layout objects to a nested
   `[workspace]`: replace `[lints] workspace = true` with an inline `[lints.clippy]` table with the same
   two entries. Decide by running `cargo fuzz build` (rch) and record which form was used.
2. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `fuzz` job: add `cargo fuzz run fuzz_vt_parser -- -max_len=4096
   -max_total_time=20` to the quick list; pass `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` from the pinned channel (see
   `g04-10-impl`; until it lands, keep `nightly`); keep `cargo fuzz build` as the first step.
3. `fuzz/README.md`: note the standalone workspace and that lints mirror the root.
4. Add a repo-level guard so the two lint tables cannot drift: a tiny test in the root workspace is
   overkill; instead `scripts/check_readme_claims.py` (G06) or the monthly reality-check job (G37) diffs
   the two tables. Record this as a follow-up line in `g37-impl`, not in this bead.
5. `ubs fuzz/Cargo.toml`; no code changes to fuzz targets.

## Files to change

- `fuzz/Cargo.toml`: `[workspace]` + mirrored lints.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `fuzz` job quick list (+`fuzz_vt_parser`).
- `fuzz/README.md`: one paragraph.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `cd fuzz && cargo +nightly-2026-08-25 fuzz build` succeeds locally (rch) for all 11 targets;
      `cargo fuzz list` prints the 11 names.
- [ ] `ci.yml` job "Fuzz Build Check" green on `main`; the "Quick fuzz run" step runs 11 targets; the
      campaign step's JSONL (`/tmp/fuzz_campaign_e2e_*/fuzz_campaign_e2e.jsonl`) has one `target_done`
      line per target with `crashes: 0`.
- [ ] `g04-05-tests` verification satisfied.

## Tests and logging

`g04-05-tests`. The campaign script already emits JSONL (`scripts/fuzz_campaign_e2e.sh:36`,
`emit_event`) with `run_id`, `nightly_toolchain`, per-target durations, `existing_crash_artifacts`,
`artifacts_dir`; keep those fields.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none. Unblocks: `g39-impl` (nightly fuzz job), `g04-e2e`, `g36-impl` (input parser fuzz
extensions for SGR-pixels 1016).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: making `fuzz` a workspace member. cargo-fuzz packages are conventionally excluded because
  `libfuzzer-sys` and `-Zsanitizer` flags must not leak into the main build, and `fuzz/Cargo.lock` is
  intentionally separate.
- Rejected: deleting `[lints]` from the fuzz manifest. It would let clippy lint families that the root
  deliberately allows fail on the fuzz build.
- Risk: `fuzz/artifacts/fuzz_text_cluster_map/` may contain a real crash reproducer; the campaign script
  reports `existing_crash_artifacts` — if non-zero, open a follow-up bug bead naming the artifact path
  (do not delete it).

## Definition of done

Fuzz job green with 11 targets; run id and `cargo fuzz list` output in the close reason; `fuzz/README.md`
updated.
close_reason: Fuzz manifest parses as standalone workspace (verified: cargo metadata + cargo check building all 11 targets, exit 0); added the missing fuzz_vt_parser to the CI quick-run list so all 11 are exercised. cargo-fuzz not installed locally so cargo fuzz build itself not run; CI Fuzz Build Check green owned by that job.
