title: epic(G37): Process guardrails — evidence-bearing close reasons, Landing the Plane, monthly reality check
description:
# epic(G37): Process guardrails — evidence-bearing close reasons, Landing-the-Plane update, monthly reality check

## Context and why this matters

The reality check of 2026-09-01 found the tracker reporting 2,732 of 2,734 beads closed and 144/144
epics closed while the README's front-page example does not compile and `main` has not been green in
40 CI runs (Section 0). Section 2.3 names the causes: "No truth mechanism between README and code"
(item 1), "No 'reachable from production' definition of done — hundreds of beads were closed on 'module
+ unit tests exist'" (item 2), and "Bead count as the progress metric — 99.9% closure with the
front-page example broken is the 'bead completion illusion' this workflow exists to catch" (item 6).
Section 4: "190 closed beads have a null close reason; 663 say only 'done'"; "silent scope cuts recorded
only in closing notes" (Windows backend "defer implementation", FRP "NOT implemented", CI E2E gate
"environmentally unmeetable"); the April reality-gap epic bd-i80el "closed the same day it was opened ...
All three regressed". AGENTS.md itself teaches the bad habit: its two `br close` examples read `br close
123 --reason "Completed"` (AGENTS.md:471) and `br close <id> --reason "Completed"` (:742), and "Landing
the Plane" (:785-796) asks for "Run quality gates" without naming them or requiring evidence. Vision rows
V70 (gates), V69/V71 (AGENTS.md truth); Section 2.2 letter E; Section 7.3 block G37: "`br` pre-close
check (`scripts/br_close_guard.sh`): refuse closing a bead whose reason lacks a test name, CI run id, or
PR/commit; AGENTS.md 'Landing the Plane' requires it; monthly reality-check job re-runs Section 1
commands and diffs the claims ledger."

The user-visible consequence of the gap: the owner cannot trust "closed" to mean "works", and every
future audit must redo the whole reality check from scratch because nothing records evidence at close
time or re-checks it later.

## Current state (evidence)

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` (2026-09-01, computed by a one-off Python pass over the file): 2,732 closed;
  188 with `close_reason` null; 851 whose reason is only "done"/"completed" (case-insensitive); the plan
  document counted 190 and 663 with a narrower filter. Fields present: `status`, `closed_at`,
  `close_reason`.
- `br 0.5.7` (installed) supports close-time policy natively via `.beads/policy.yaml`
  (beads_rust `src/close_policy.rs:27 POLICY_FILE_NAME`): `close_policy.require_close_reason {enabled,
  min_length (default 20), regex}` (:84-86, :2008-2027), `require_acceptance_criteria_satisfied` (:87-89;
  scans a `## Acceptance Criteria` section for unchecked `- [ ]`, :2335-2348),
  `forbid_self_close_after_in_progress`, `forbid_close_with_deferred_dependents` (#303),
  `require_typed_references {enabled, required_kinds}` with built-in kinds `commit`, `pr`, `reviewer`,
  `investigation`, `agent-mail`, `dashboard` and custom kinds when listed (:1968-1996); top-level
  `allow_bypass` (default true; `br close --bypass-policy --bypass-reason` is rejected when false,
  `br close --help`). Unknown keys are warned, not fatal (#302). `.beads/` currently has no
  `policy.yaml` (`ls .beads` 2026-09-01: `config.yaml`, `issues.jsonl`, `beads.base.jsonl`, `metadata.json`,
  db files).
- No `scripts/br_close_guard.sh`, no monthly workflow; workflows present: `ci.yml`,
  `doctor_frankentui_extended.yml`, `emulator_compat_matrix.yml`, `release.yml`.
- Section 1 commands that a monthly job should replay: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo
  clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, the full test suite (nextest
  after `g03-impl-nextest`), the demo under a PTY per identity (the driver becomes
  `scripts/pty_identity_matrix.py` in `g05-impl`), CI run status, bead stats, README counts (screens 45
  vs badge 46 `README.md:23`; widgets 57 vs badge `80+` :22; crates badge `20` :21; `ftui = "0.5"` :313
  vs workspace `0.6.0` `Cargo.toml:28`).

## Target state

- Closing a bead without evidence is impossible by default: `.beads/policy.yaml` enforces a minimum
  reason length and at least one typed reference (`test:`, `ci-run:`, `commit:`, `pr:`, `bench:`,
  `e2e:`, `decision:`, `docs:`); `allow_bypass: false`.
- `scripts/br_close_guard.sh` wraps `br close` with a friendlier pre-check and offers `--audit` over the
  JSONL for closes that slipped through (older `br`, `--no-db` edits), used by CI and the monthly job.
- AGENTS.md "Landing the Plane" names the exact gates, the reason format and the streak check; its two
  `br close` examples show real evidence.
- `.github/workflows/reality_check.yml` runs monthly (and on dispatch), replays the Section 1 commands,
  recomputes the README counts, runs the claims-ledger check when it exists (G06), audits close reasons
  since the previous run, uploads a JSONL+markdown report, and opens/updates a tracking issue on drift.

## Implementation plan

1. `g37-impl`: policy file, guard script, monthly workflow.
2. `g37-tests`: shell tests for the guard (temp beads dir), policy behaviour via `br` in a temp project,
   workflow dispatch verification.
3. `g37-docs`: AGENTS.md (Landing the Plane, close-reason format, examples), README contributor note,
   `fuzz`/lint drift one-liner placement.

## Success criteria (block)

- [ ] `br close <id> --reason "done"` is rejected in this repository with the policy message; `br close
      <id> --reason "test:foo_bar ci-run:123456 commit:abc1234 ..."` succeeds.
- [ ] `scripts/br_close_guard.sh --audit --since 2026-09-01` reports zero violations on `main`.
- [ ] First monthly run uploaded `reality_check_<YYYY-MM>.jsonl` and the markdown summary; drift issue
      created or "no drift" recorded.
- [ ] AGENTS.md updated; both `br close` examples carry evidence.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by nothing at the epic level. `g37-impl` uses `scripts/ci/green_streak.sh` from `g04-e2e` and
`scripts/check_readme_claims.py` from `g06-impl` when present (skips with a logged reason until then);
`g37-docs` is blocked by `g37-impl`; `g37-tests` by `g37-impl`. Unblocks: `g42-impl` (final
verification cites the first monthly report), `g34-impl` (governance docs regenerate from the same
counts).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: a git pre-commit hook that parses `.beads/issues.jsonl`. `br` already has the policy
  engine; a hook would duplicate it and be bypassed by `--no-verify`.
- Rejected: `require_acceptance_criteria_satisfied` on day one. The bead template uses `## Success
  criteria`, not `## Acceptance Criteria`; enabling the gate before the headings agree would enforce
  nothing. `g37-impl` evaluates it after a dry audit and records the decision.
- Risk: `allow_bypass: false` blocks the owner too; the owner can edit the file (rule 0) — say so in
  AGENTS.md.
- Risk: agents may write fake references (`commit:none`). The audit cross-checks `commit:`/`pr:` values
  with `git cat-file -e` / `gh pr view` and `ci-run:` with `gh run view` — reported, not enforced, in
  the monthly job.

## Definition of done

All three children closed with evidence; the first monthly report exists; the claims-ledger row for
"Landing the Plane" (G06) links the guard.

title: task(G37): .beads/policy.yaml, scripts/br_close_guard.sh, and the monthly reality_check.yml workflow
description:
# task(G37): `.beads/policy.yaml`, `scripts/br_close_guard.sh`, and the monthly `reality_check.yml` workflow

## Context and why this matters

AGENTS.md "Landing the Plane" (:785-796) says "Close finished work" and "Run quality gates" but names no
evidence; its `br close` examples use `--reason "Completed"` (:471, :742). The reality check found 188
null close reasons and 851 "done/completed"-only reasons among 2,732 closed beads (`.beads/issues.jsonl`,
2026-09-01), silent scope cuts hidden in closing notes (Section 4), and a prior truth-restoration epic
that regressed within weeks with nothing to notice (Section 2.2.E). Section 2.3 items 1, 2 and 6. This
bead installs the mechanism: `br`'s native close policy, a guard script for humans/agents and audits,
and a monthly job that re-runs the audit's Section 1 commands so drift is detected within a month
instead of at the next crisis.

## Current state (evidence)

- `br 0.5.7`: `br close` options include `-r/--reason`, `--bypass-policy` ("Only honoured when
  `.beads/policy.yaml` has `allow_bypass: true`"), `--bypass-reason`; policy schema in beads_rust
  `src/close_policy.rs`: `close_policy.require_close_reason {enabled, min_length, regex}`,
  `require_typed_references {enabled, required_kinds}` (built-ins `commit`, `pr`, `reviewer`,
  `investigation`, `agent-mail`, `dashboard`; custom kinds must be listed; matcher accepts any contiguous
  `kind:value` token, :1971-1996), `require_acceptance_criteria_satisfied`, `forbid_self_close_after_in_progress`,
  `forbid_close_with_deferred_dependents`, `attribution {tier: off|capture, fields}`, top-level
  `allow_bypass`. Example YAML in the crate's tests (:3405-3420).
- `.beads/policy.yaml` absent; `.beads/config.yaml` (92 B) and `metadata.json` present.
- JSONL fields per bead: `id`, `status`, `closed_at`, `close_reason` (verified with `head -c 1500
  .beads/issues.jsonl`).
- No monthly/scheduled truth job; `emulator_compat_matrix.yml` and `doctor_frankentui_extended.yml` are
  the only scheduled workflows.
- README counts to re-check monthly: badges `crates-20`, `widgets-80+`, `demo_screens-46`
  (README.md:21-23) vs 20 workspace members (`ls crates` = 20 dirs incl. doctor_frankentui,
  ftui-demo-showcase, ftui-showcase-wasm), 57 production widget types, 45 `ScreenId` variants
  (`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs:679`; `all_screens_count` at `:7068`); `ftui = "0.5"`
  (README.md:313) vs `Cargo.toml:28 version = "0.6.0"`.

## Target state

Evidence-bearing closes enforced by `br`; a guard script with `close` and `--audit` modes; a monthly
workflow that replays the reality-check commands and reports drift as an artifact and a GitHub issue.

## Implementation plan

1. `.beads/policy.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   # Close-time gates (beads_rust close_policy). Rationale: reality-check 2026-09-01, Section 2.3.
   close_policy:
     require_close_reason:
       enabled: true
       min_length: 40
     require_typed_references:
       enabled: true
       # At least one of these kind:value tokens must appear in --reason.
       required_kinds: ["test", "ci-run", "commit", "pr", "bench", "e2e", "decision", "docs"]
     require_acceptance_criteria_satisfied:
       enabled: false   # see g37-impl comment: enable once bead bodies use "## Acceptance Criteria"
     forbid_self_close_after_in_progress:
       enabled: false   # single-agent sessions would be blocked
     forbid_close_with_deferred_dependents:
       enabled: true
     attribution:
       tier: capture
       fields: ["agent_name", "harness", "model"]
   allow_bypass: false
   ```
   Verify the exact key names against the installed `br` (`br close --help`, and `br --version`), and
   that unknown keys only warn (#302). Commit the file (it is inside `.beads/`, which is tracked).
2. `scripts/br_close_guard.sh`:
   - `close <id>... --reason "<text>" [extra br args]`: validates locally (length >= 40; at least one
     `kind:value` from the list; for `commit:` values runs `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}`; for `ci-run:`
     values checks `^[0-9]{8,}$`; for `test:` values optionally checks the name exists with `rg -n "fn
     <name>\b" crates tests` and warns if not found), prints a precise message listing what is missing
     with an example reason, then `exec br close "$@"`. Never edits JSONL directly.
   - `--audit [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--out report.jsonl]`: reads `.beads/issues.jsonl`, selects
     `status == "closed"` with `closed_at >= since`, flags reasons that are null, shorter than 40 chars,
     or lack a typed reference; writes one JSONL row per flagged bead (`id`, `closed_at`, `reason`,
     `violations`) and a summary line; exit 1 if any violations. Uses `python3` for JSON parsing (no jq
     dependency for the audit path). Default `--since` = 2026-09-01 (policy start).
   - `--audit-refs`: additionally verifies `commit:`/`pr:`/`ci-run:` values exist (`git cat-file`,
     `gh pr view`, `gh run view`); reported as warnings.
3. `.github/workflows/reality_check.yml`: `on: schedule: cron '0 7 1 * *'`, `workflow_dispatch`;
   `permissions: contents: read, issues: write`; one job `reality-check` (`timeout-minutes: 60`):
   checkout; `./.github/actions/rust-pin`; steps each writing a JSONL row to
   `reality_check_$(date +%Y-%m).jsonl` via a tiny `record` shell function (`{"check":..,"status":..,
   "detail":..,"elapsed_s":..}`): `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`; `cargo clippy --workspace
   --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast`
   (command from `g03-impl-nextest`); `scripts/ci/green_streak.sh --workflow ci.yml --min 3` (from
   `g04-e2e`); `scripts/br_close_guard.sh --audit --since <first day of previous month>`; README counts
   (`scripts/reality_counts.sh`, new: prints screens/widgets/crates/version from code vs README badges
   and the crates.io version of `ftui` via `curl https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/ftui`); `python3
   scripts/check_readme_claims.py` if the file exists else `record ledger skipped "g06-impl pending"`;
   `python3 scripts/pty_identity_matrix.py --smoke` if it exists else record skipped (`g05-impl`); the
   fuzz-lint drift diff from `g04-05-tests`; then a summary step that renders `reality_check.md` from the
   JSONL, uploads both as artifact `reality-check-<YYYY-MM>`, and if any row has `status: fail`, finds
   or creates the issue titled `Monthly reality check: drift detected` (`gh issue list --search
   "in:title \"Monthly reality check\"" --state open`), appending the summary as a comment; if none, adds
   a comment "no drift" to the open issue if one exists.
   The job must not `cargo` on the runner if `rch` semantics matter — it does not; the runner builds
   directly (same as `ci.yml`).
4. Run the audit once over history (`--since 2026-01-01`) and attach the counts to this bead (expected
   about 1,039 flagged); do not rewrite history — the policy applies from 2026-09-01.
5. `ubs` on the shell/YAML; `shellcheck` if available.

## Files to change

- `.beads/policy.yaml`: new (tracked).
- `scripts/br_close_guard.sh`: new.
- `scripts/reality_counts.sh`: new (small; reused by `g06-impl`'s ledger check and `g34-impl`).
- `.github/workflows/reality_check.yml`: new workflow.

## Success criteria

- [ ] In this repo: `br close <scratch-id> --reason "done"` fails with the policy message; the same
      with `--reason "test:foo_bar ci-run:33152820289 commit:ab07291f verified locally and in CI"`
      succeeds (use a throwaway bead created for the test, then close it with real evidence text).
- [ ] `scripts/br_close_guard.sh --audit --since 2026-09-01` exits 0 on `main`; `--since 2026-01-01`
      exits 1 with the historical count.
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` of `reality_check.yml` completes; artifact contains the JSONL and markdown;
      the issue was created/commented (link in the close reason).
- [ ] `g37-tests` satisfied.

## Tests and logging

`g37-tests`. JSONL: guard audit rows (`id`, `closed_at`, `reason`, `violations[]`); monthly rows
(`check`, `status`, `detail`, `elapsed_s`, `run_id`); artifact and issue links.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none (uses `g04-e2e`'s streak script, `g03-impl-nextest`'s command, `g06-impl`'s ledger
check and `g05-impl`'s identity driver when present; each step skips with a logged reason until then,
and this bead's follow-up comment lists which skips remain). Unblocks: `g37-docs`, `g37-tests`,
`g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: a regex-only reason gate (`regex: "^Fix: "` style). Typed references are queryable and are
  what the audit needs.
- Rejected: enforcing `forbid_self_close_after_in_progress`. It assumes multi-actor review that this
  repo does not have.
- Risk: the monthly job's full test run is long (the local run took hours); use nextest with the
  per-test timeout and the same disk hygiene as `test-all-features` (`g04-12-impl`), and cap the job at
  60 minutes — a timeout is itself a recorded drift row.

## Definition of done

Policy active; guard and counts scripts committed; first dispatch run of the monthly workflow with
artifact and issue links in the close reason; historical audit numbers recorded.
notes: Refinement 2: a syntactically valid test:/ci-run:/commit: reference proves nothing about verdict or source identity. Consume actual result/receipt evidence when enforcing completion, reject stale/failed/missing mandatory results, and distinguish diagnostic incomplete reports. No new external issues/comments/messages or release dispatch are authorized by this audit; prove local behavior first and leave external automation to an explicitly authorized deployment.

description:
# task(G37): Tests for the close-reason guard, the br policy, and the monthly reality-check workflow

## Context

Companion to `g37-impl`. The guard (`scripts/br_close_guard.sh`), the policy (`.beads/policy.yaml`,
enforced by `br 0.5.7`'s close-policy engine) and the monthly workflow (`reality_check.yml`) are process
code; if they are wrong they either block all closes or enforce nothing. 188 null and 851 trivial close
reasons exist today (`.beads/issues.jsonl`, 2026-09-01). This bead specifies the tests that prove the
guard's decisions, the policy's behaviour in a throwaway beads project, and the workflow's output.

## What to test

1. Guard `close` mode: accepts evidence-bearing reasons, rejects missing/short/untyped ones, verifies
   `commit:` existence, never touches JSONL.
2. Guard `--audit`: flags the right rows from a fixture JSONL; exit codes; JSONL report shape.
3. Policy: `br` rejects/accepts closes in a temp project with the same `policy.yaml`.
4. Workflow: dispatch run produces the artifact and issue; each check row has a status.
5. `scripts/reality_counts.sh` prints the five counts and compares with README.

## Test types

Shell tests (`scripts/br_close_guard_test.sh`, bash; uses a temp dir; no writes to `.beads/`):
- `close_rejects_short_reason`: `--reason "done"` -> exit 2, message lists `min_length 40` and the
  required kinds.
- `close_rejects_untyped_reason`: 60-char prose without `kind:value` -> exit 2, message shows an
  example reason.
- `close_accepts_typed_reason`: `--reason "test:jsonl_logger_explicit_seed_wins_over_env ci-run:33152820289
  commit:ab07291f fixed seed leak"` with `br` stubbed on `PATH` (a script that records its argv) ->
  exit 0 and the stub received `close <id> --reason ...` unchanged.
- `close_warns_on_unknown_commit`: `commit:deadbeef` (not in repo) -> exit 2 with `commit not found`
  (strict for commits; `test:` unknown names only warn).
- `audit_flags_fixture_rows`: fixture JSONL with five closed beads (null reason; "done"; 45-char prose
  without refs; valid `test:`; valid `commit:`) and one open bead -> report has 3 rows, exit 1;
  `--since` after all `closed_at` -> 0 rows, exit 0.
- `audit_report_is_jsonl`: every line of `--out` parses; keys `id`, `closed_at`, `reason`,
  `violations`.

Policy behaviour (`scripts/br_policy_test.sh`, uses `br` in a temp dir: `br init` there, copy
`.beads/policy.yaml`, `br create --title t --type task --priority 3`, then):
- `br close <id> --reason "done"` -> non-zero, stderr mentions `require_close_reason` or
  `require_typed_references` (copy the exact wording into the test once observed).
- `br close <id> --reason "test:x_y ci-run:1 verified in CI run and local nextest"` -> exit 0.
- `br close <id> --bypass-policy --bypass-reason x` -> rejected because `allow_bypass: false`.
- Unknown key added to a copy of the policy -> `br close` still works and prints a warning (#302
  behaviour), so a typo cannot lock the project.

Counts script: `scripts/reality_counts.sh --json` prints `{"screens":45,"widgets":57,"crates":20,
"workspace_version":"0.6.0","readme_version":"0.5","cratesio_version":"0.6.0", ...}`; a unit-style
check asserts `screens` equals the value asserted by `all_screens_count`
(`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs:7068`).

Workflow: `gh workflow run reality_check.yml`; the run uploads `reality-check-<YYYY-MM>`; the JSONL has
one row per check (`cargo_check`, `clippy`, `fmt`, `nextest`, `green_streak`, `close_audit`,
`readme_counts`, `claims_ledger`, `identity_matrix`, `fuzz_lint_drift`) each with `status` in
`pass|fail|skipped`; the issue comment/creation happened (link).

## Logging

Guard: human message on stderr + JSONL report file; audit summary line `audit: flagged=<n>
scanned=<m> since=<date>`. Workflow: JSONL rows with `check`, `status`, `detail`, `elapsed_s`,
`run_id`; markdown summary; issue link.

## Files

- `scripts/br_close_guard_test.sh`, `scripts/br_policy_test.sh` (new, run locally and in the `check`
  job's lint step), `scripts/reality_counts.sh`, `.github/workflows/reality_check.yml`.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Guard test script: 6/6 pass; policy test: 4/4 pass (outputs pasted).
- [ ] Counts script output pasted and matches code.
- [ ] Dispatch run id, artifact name, issue link in the close reason.

## Dependencies

Blocked by `g37-impl`. Unblocks `g42-impl`.

## Definition of done

All tests committed and green; workflow evidence in the close reason.

title: docs(G37): AGENTS.md Landing the Plane — named gates, evidence-bearing close reasons, monthly check
description:
# docs(G37): AGENTS.md "Landing the Plane" — named gates, evidence-bearing close reasons, monthly check

## Context and why this matters

AGENTS.md is the contract every agent reads first. Today its "Landing the Plane (Session Completion)"
section (:785-796) says: 1 file issues, 2 "Run quality gates (if code changed) - Tests, linters,
builds", 3 "Update issue status - Close finished work", 4 `br sync --flush-only`, 5 hand off. Its two
worked `br close` examples read `br close 123 --reason "Completed"` (:471) and `br close <id> --reason
"Completed"` (:742). The reality check (Section 2.3 items 2 and 6; Section 4: 190 null and 663 "done"
reasons) shows this is exactly the habit that produced 2,732 closed beads with a broken front page.
Vision rows V69-V71 (AGENTS.md truth); Section 7.3 G37 "AGENTS.md 'Landing the Plane' requires it".
With `g37-impl` the policy is enforced by `br`; this bead makes the documentation say so, so an agent
learns the format before hitting the error.

## Current state (evidence)

- AGENTS.md:120-136 "Compiler Checks (CRITICAL)": check, clippy, fmt (rustdoc added by `g04-04-impl`).
- AGENTS.md:438-488 "Beads (br)": typical flow with `br close 123 --reason "Completed"` (:471).
- AGENTS.md:724-783 "Beads Workflow Integration": essential commands (:742 example), "Session Protocol"
  (:762-772), "Best Practices" (:775-781).
- AGENTS.md:785-796 "Landing the Plane": five steps, no gate names, no evidence requirement, no CI
  link (the `g04-e2e` bead adds the streak step and the Green baseline line; keep both).
- AGENTS.md:579-618 "UBS": `ubs <changed-files>` before every commit (already present; must be listed in
  the gates).

## Target state

AGENTS.md states, in one place, the exact gate commands, the close-reason format with the accepted
`kind:value` references, the guard script, the streak check, and the monthly job; both `br close`
examples carry real evidence; a short "Why" sentence links the reality check so the rule survives the
next rewrite (`g06-impl` rewrites AGENTS.md and must keep these blocks verbatim).

## Implementation plan

1. AGENTS.md "Landing the Plane": rewrite the five steps into:
   1. File beads for remaining work (`br create ...`), each with success criteria.
   2. Run the gates and keep the output: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy
      --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo
      doc --workspace --no-deps`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` (or the affected
      crates), `ubs <changed files>`; for E2E-affecting changes the relevant `tests/e2e/scripts/*.sh`.
   3. Close finished beads with evidence: `scripts/br_close_guard.sh close <id> --reason "test:<name>
      ci-run:<id> commit:<sha> <one sentence of what was verified>"` — reasons need >= 40 characters and
      at least one of `test:`, `ci-run:`, `commit:`, `pr:`, `bench:`, `e2e:`, `decision:`, `docs:`;
      `.beads/policy.yaml` enforces this and `--bypass-policy` is disabled (the owner may edit the file).
   4. `br sync --flush-only`, `git add .beads/`, commit.
   5. Confirm `main` is green: `scripts/ci/green_streak.sh --workflow ci.yml --min 1`; if red, file a
      bead naming the failing job before handing off.
   6. Hand off with the bead ids and the run id.
   Plus the "Green baseline" line from `g04-e2e` and one sentence: "Why: the 2026-09-01 reality check
   found 99.9% bead closure with a broken front-page example; evidence at close time is the fix."
2. Replace the two example reasons at :471 and :742 with evidence-bearing ones (e.g. `--reason
   "test:default_backend_opens_terminal ci-run:<id> commit:<sha> facade defaults open a PTY"`).
3. Add a "Monthly reality check" paragraph under "Landing the Plane" or "Testing": the workflow
   `reality_check.yml` runs on the 1st, uploads `reality-check-<YYYY-MM>`, and files/updates the issue
   "Monthly reality check: drift detected"; whoever picks up the issue creates beads per drift row.
4. README.md: if a contributor section exists (grep "Contributing"), add one line pointing to AGENTS.md
   "Landing the Plane"; otherwise no README change.
5. `docs/testing/e2e-playbook.md`: link the guard's `--audit` mode as the "did we really finish" check.

## Files to change

- `AGENTS.md`: Landing the Plane; examples at :471 and :742; monthly paragraph.
- `README.md`: one contributor line (only if a section exists).
- `docs/testing/e2e-playbook.md`: audit link.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `rg -n 'reason "Completed"' AGENTS.md` returns nothing; `rg -n "br_close_guard.sh" AGENTS.md`
      returns the step-3 line.
- [ ] The six steps and the Why sentence present; `scripts/check_readme_claims.py` (G06) treats the
      commands as ledger rows (each command in the section must exist and run: verified by
      `g06-impl`'s script or, until then, by running each command once and pasting the exit codes).
- [ ] `g06-impl`'s AGENTS.md rewrite keeps the blocks (note added to `g06-impl` as a comment).

## Tests and logging

Docs bead: verification is the two `rg` checks above plus running each listed command once (exit codes
in the close reason). No runtime logging.

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g37-impl` (the guard, policy and workflow must exist before AGENTS.md describes them —
documenting a job that does not exist yet is the disease this plan treats). Related: `g04-e2e` (streak
step), `g06-impl` (AGENTS.md rewrite must preserve). Unblocks: `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: a separate `docs/process/close-reasons.md`. AGENTS.md is what agents read; a second file
  proliferates and drifts (AGENTS.md "No File Proliferation").
- Risk: verbosity. Keep the section under 40 lines; commands, not prose.

## Definition of done

AGENTS.md updated with the exact commands and format; examples fixed; `rg` evidence and command exit
codes in the close reason.

title: epic(G39): AGENTS.md tests/ claim is false; fuzzing has no nightly cadence — WRONG -> WORKING
description:
# epic(G39): AGENTS.md `tests/` claim is false; fuzzing has no nightly cadence — WRONG -> WORKING

## Context and why this matters

AGENTS.md tells every agent where integration tests live: "Cross-component integration tests live in
the workspace `tests/` directory" (AGENTS.md:148), the Test Categories table row "`tests/` (workspace) |
Cross-component integration, E2E viewport tests" (:187), and the workspace tree "`├── tests/ #
Cross-component integration tests`" (:326). The reality check (Section 2.2.F: "The `tests/` workspace
directory that AGENTS.md says holds cross-component integration tests contains no Rust files (shell E2E
scripts and fixtures only)"; vision row V69: WRONG) verified `find tests -name "*.rs" | wc -l` = 0 on
2026-09-01. An agent following AGENTS.md would create Rust files under `tests/` that cargo never runs
(no workspace-level `tests/` is compiled unless a package declares it), silently losing tests — the
worst kind of doc drift. Separately, README.md lists fuzz targets among its quality gates and
`fuzz/README.md` documents 11 targets, but the only fuzzing is a 20-second-per-target smoke in `ci.yml`
(:2111-2122) with no scheduled campaign, so the parser/text/layout fuzzers never get the hours they
need (Section 7.3 G39: "add the nightly fuzz job (G04.5)"; vision rows V61, V70).

## Current state (evidence)

- `tests/` contains: `artifacts/`, `baseline.json`, `compat/`, `e2e/` (`check_pane_traceability.sh`,
  `fixtures/`, `lib/`, `scenarios/`, `scripts/`, `pane_a11y_compliance_matrix.json`,
  `pane_discoverability_checklist.json`, `pane_traceability_matrix.json`), `fixtures/`, `repro/`. Zero
  `.rs` files.
- Real cross-crate integration tests live in per-crate `tests/` directories, e.g.
  `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/baseline_capture.rs`, `crates/ftui-harness/tests/render_no_flicker_proof.rs`
  (Theorems 1-4), `crates/ftui-extras/tests/frankenterm_js_parser_hooks_compat.rs`,
  `crates/ftui-web/tests/pane_web_e2e.rs`, `crates/ftui-layout/tests/pane_determinism_matrix.rs`
  (run by `ci.yml:2351`).
- Fuzz: `fuzz/Cargo.toml` 11 `[[bin]]` targets; `ci.yml:2083-2141` `fuzz` job (20 s per target for 10
  targets + `scripts/fuzz_campaign_e2e.sh` with `FUZZ_DURATION_SECS=20`); the campaign script supports
  `FUZZ_DURATION_SECS`, `FUZZ_MAX_LEN`, `FUZZ_JOBS`, `FUZZ_ARTIFACT_ROOT`, JSONL logging, and reports

configurable duration (default 60 s per target, dispatch input up to 3600), persists the corpus across
runs, uploads crash artifacts, and files an issue on a crash. `fuzz/README.md` documents the cadence.

2. `g39-docs`: AGENTS.md text (three places) and `fuzz/README.md` cadence section, after the job

- Rejected: fuzzing for hours on every PR. Nightly with a persisted corpus is the standard cadence.
- Risk: the corpus cache grows; cap with `-max_len` per target (values in `ci.yml:2113-2122`) and prune

# task(G39): Nightly fuzz campaign workflow with persisted corpus and crash-artifact issues

## Context and why this matters

README.md counts "fuzz targets exist" among the quality gates and `fuzz/README.md` lists 11 targets
(input parser x3, VT parser, text x5, layout constraints, widget render). Vision rows V61 (input
parser: WORKING with gaps) and V70; Section 2.2.F ("Fuzz targets already cover the parser; extend with
1016 sequences" — G36) and Section 7.3 G39 ("add the nightly fuzz job"). Today the only fuzzing is the
`ci.yml` `fuzz` job's 20 s per target (`:2111-2122`) plus a 20 s campaign (`:2124-2130`); with no
persisted corpus every run restarts from scratch, so the fuzzers never reach deep states. A nightly
campaign with a growing corpus is how the parser claims (CSI/SS3/DCS/OSC/APC, kitty keyboard, paste,
SGR mouse) get real adversarial coverage. Parent: `g39-epic`.

## Current state (evidence)

- `scripts/fuzz_campaign_e2e.sh`: env `FUZZ_DURATION_SECS` (default 30; "CI: 300+"), `FUZZ_MAX_LEN`
  (4096), `FUZZ_JOBS` (1), `LOG_DIR` (`/tmp/fuzz_campaign_e2e_<ts>`), `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` (default
  `nightly`; `g04-10-impl` pins it), `RUN_ID`, `FUZZ_TARGET_FILTER`, `FUZZ_ARTIFACT_ROOT`
  (`fuzz/artifacts`), `FUZZ_INJECT_CRASH_TARGET` (deliberate failure injection for testing the script);
  JSONL at `$LOG_DIR/fuzz_campaign_e2e.jsonl` (:36); checks the nightly toolchain (:134-148, emits
  `nightly_toolchain_missing` and SKIPs if absent — a nightly job must treat that as failure, not skip);
  reports `existing_crash_artifacts` (:293-325).
- `fuzz/Cargo.toml`: 11 targets; `fuzz/README.md:20-33` run instructions; `fuzz/artifacts/` and
  `fuzz/corpus/` gitignored; local `fuzz/artifacts/fuzz_text_cluster_map/` exists (possibly a real
  reproducer — `g04-05-impl` files a bug bead if the campaign reports it).
- `ci.yml` `fuzz` job uploads `fuzz-campaign-artifacts` (`/tmp/fuzz_campaign_e2e_*/`, `fuzz/artifacts/`)
  with `actions/upload-artifact@v4` (:2132-2140; the rest of the file uses `@v7` — align).
- No scheduled fuzz workflow exists.

## Target state

`.github/workflows/fuzz_nightly.yml`: cron nightly + dispatch (`duration_secs` input, default 60, max
3600; `target` filter input), pinned toolchain, `cargo-fuzz` pinned, corpus restored from and saved to
a cache keyed by target set, all 11 targets run for the duration, JSONL + corpus + artifacts uploaded,
crash -> GitHub issue with reproducer path and `cargo fuzz fmt` output, `timeout-minutes: 45` at 60 s
(dispatch runs may set up to 90 via an input).

## Implementation plan

1. `.github/workflows/fuzz_nightly.yml`: `on: schedule: cron '17 3 * * *'`, `workflow_dispatch: inputs:
   duration_secs (default "60"), target (default ""), timeout_minutes (default "45")`; `permissions:
   contents: read, issues: write`; job `fuzz-nightly` (ubuntu-latest, `timeout-minutes: ${{ inputs.timeout_minutes || 45 }}`):
   checkout; `./.github/actions/rust-pin`; `cargo install cargo-fuzz --version <pinned>` (or
   `taiki-e/install-action` with a pinned version; record it); `actions/cache` for `fuzz/corpus` with key
   `fuzz-corpus-${{ hashFiles('fuzz/Cargo.toml') }}-${{ github.run_id }}` and `restore-keys:
   fuzz-corpus-${{ hashFiles('fuzz/Cargo.toml') }}-` (so each run restores the newest corpus and saves
   a new one); registry cache; `FUZZ_DURATION_SECS=<input or 60> FUZZ_TARGET_FILTER=<input>
   NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN=<pinned channel> ./scripts/fuzz_campaign_e2e.sh`; make the script's
   "nightly toolchain missing -> SKIPPED" path exit non-zero when `FUZZ_REQUIRE_TOOLCHAIN=1` (set in
   this workflow); upload `fuzz-nightly-<date>` with the JSONL, `fuzz/artifacts/`, and a `corpus_stats.txt`
   (`du -sh fuzz/corpus/*`).
2. Crash handling step (`if: failure()`): parse the JSONL for `crashes > 0` rows; for each, run `cargo
   fuzz fmt <target> <artifact>` to render the input; create or comment on an issue titled `fuzz crash:
   <target>` with the artifact path, the stack excerpt from the campaign log, and the run link (`gh
   issue list --search "in:title \"fuzz crash: <target>\"" --state open` to dedupe).
3. `scripts/fuzz_campaign_e2e.sh`: add `FUZZ_REQUIRE_TOOLCHAIN`; write the corpus under
   `fuzz/corpus/<target>` explicitly (`cargo fuzz run <target> fuzz/corpus/<target> -- ...`) so the cache
   path is deterministic; emit a `corpus_size` field per target in the JSONL.
4. `ci.yml` `fuzz` job: leave as the 20 s PR smoke; align its upload action version; add a comment
   pointing to the nightly workflow.
5. `ubs`/`actionlint`.

## Files to change

- `.github/workflows/fuzz_nightly.yml`: new.
- `scripts/fuzz_campaign_e2e.sh`: `FUZZ_REQUIRE_TOOLCHAIN`, explicit corpus dir, `corpus_size`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: fuzz job comment + upload version.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Dispatch run with `duration_secs=10` green; artifact contains JSONL with 11 target rows and
      `corpus_size` fields; corpus cache saved (log line `Cache saved with key fuzz-corpus-...`).
- [ ] Second run shows `Cache restored from key fuzz-corpus-...` and larger `corpus_size` for at least
      one target.
- [ ] Negative (dispatch with `FUZZ_INJECT_CRASH_TARGET=fuzz_text_wrap` via a temporary env in a scratch
      branch): the crash step creates an issue with the reproducer path; issue closed afterwards with a
      note (run id and issue link pasted).
- [ ] Three consecutive scheduled runs green (ids).

## Tests and logging

Campaign JSONL (`run_id`, `nightly_toolchain`, per-target `target`, `duration_secs`, `crashes`,
`corpus_size`, `existing_crash_artifacts`, `artifacts_dir`); `corpus_stats.txt`; issue body with
reproducer path and `cargo fuzz fmt` output. Verification of the script change: run
`FUZZ_REQUIRE_TOOLCHAIN=1 NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN=nope ./scripts/fuzz_campaign_e2e.sh` -> exit 1 with
`nightly_toolchain_missing` (paste).

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: `g04-05-impl` (fuzz manifest must build). Related: `g04-10-impl` (pinned channel),
`g36-impl` (adds 1016 sequences to the parser targets). Unblocks: `g39-docs`, `g42-impl`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: running the campaign inside `ci.yml` on PRs with a long duration. PR feedback must stay
  fast; the corpus persists nightly.
- Rejected: committing the corpus to git. It is binary churn; the cache plus artifact retention is the
  standard approach; a periodic `cargo fuzz cmin` keeps it bounded.
- Risk: cache size limit (10 GB per repo); `-max_len` bounds inputs; monitor `corpus_stats.txt`.

## Definition of done

Workflow merged; two dispatch runs (positive, negative) and three scheduled runs cited; script changes
verified; `fuzz/README.md` updated by `g39-docs`.

title: epic(G40): verify_no_regression is order-dependent and stale-file-sensitive — WRONG_APPROACH -> WORKING
description:
# epic(G40): `verify_no_regression` is order-dependent and stale-file-sensitive — WRONG_APPROACH -> WORKING

## Context and why this matters

README.md's "Performance Engineering" and the plan's Gate 4 rely on performance baselines; the demo
showcase's `baseline_capture.rs` is described in its own header as "Baseline p50/p95/p99 capture for
FrankenTUI hot paths (bd-3jlw5.1)" and is run by the "Demo Showcase" CI job (`ci.yml:502-503 cargo test
-p ftui-demo-showcase --test baseline_capture -- --nocapture`). The reality check's own full test run
had exactly one failing test: `verify_no_regression` (Section 1, row "The 1 failing test": "Reads a
gitignored `tests/baseline_results.json` that a stale local copy lacked `terminal_color_depth` for;
order-dependent on `capture_baselines` writing it first. Environment artifact, but a design smell";
Section 2.2.E: "`verify_no_regression` depends on a gitignored file that another test in the same
binary writes: order-dependent and stale-file-sensitive"). Vision rows V35 (benches: numbers unbacked)
and V70. The consequence: a developer with an old local file gets a red suite for a reason unrelated to
their change; in CI the two tests race on the file; and — worse — the "regression check" never fails
on a regression, so the file gives false comfort.

## Current state (evidence)

`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/baseline_capture.rs` (414 lines):
- `:255-258 baseline_path()` = `<CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR>/tests/baseline_results.json`; the root
  `.gitignore:54` ignores `baseline_results.json`.
- `:284-315 #[test] capture_baselines`: measures frame pipeline, diff engine, layout (`capture_*`),
  builds JSON with `version`, `generated_at`, `terminal_color_depth` (`BASELINE_COLOR_DEPTH =
  ColorDepth::TrueColor`, :28), `warmup_iters` 50, `measure_iters` 500, `hot_paths`; writes the file when
  `CAPTURE_BASELINE` is set **or the file does not exist** (:309-312).
- `:318-352 #[test] verify_no_regression`: returns early if the file is missing (:320-323); parses it
  (`expect("invalid JSON")`); `validate_baseline_color_depth` (:260-271) panics with "baseline missing
  terminal_color_depth provenance (expected truecolor)" or "mismatch" on a stale file; measures again;
  `check_regressions(..., 0.10, ...)` (:340, :382-414) collects p99 increases > 10% — and then only
  `eprintln!`s them (:342-351). There is no `assert!`/`panic!` on regressions: the test cannot fail on a
  performance regression, only on file problems.
- Both tests live in one binary; `cargo test` runs them on parallel threads by default, so
  `verify_no_regression` may read a half-written file (`invalid JSON` panic), skip (file not yet
  written), or verify — nondeterministic by construction.
- `:354-375` unit tests for the provenance validator exist.
- Related: `tests/baseline.json` + `scripts/perf_regression_gate.sh` (the real, unrun perf gate; G25),
  `scripts/bench_budget.sh --quick` in the `benchmarks` job.

## Target state

One test captures and verifies in-process; the gitignored file is an optional cache with provenance
(`version`, `terminal_color_depth`, `git_sha`, `hostname`, `generated_at`); a stale or invalid cache is
ignored with a logged JSON reason, never a panic; the file is written atomically; a `BASELINE_STRICT=1`
mode turns regressions into failures for the perf gate (G25) while the default stays advisory but
prints machine-readable lines; the CI job runs it deterministically.

## Implementation plan

`g40-impl` (code) and `g40-tests` (tests). See those beads.

## Success criteria (block)

- [ ] `cargo test -p ftui-demo-showcase --test baseline_capture` is deterministic under `--test-threads
      1` and default parallelism, with and without a pre-existing stale file (three runs each).
- [ ] A synthetic regression (env `BASELINE_SYNTHETIC_SLOWDOWN_PCT=50`) fails under `BASELINE_STRICT=1`
      and prints an advisory line otherwise.
- [ ] JSONL lines per hot path (`event: baseline_measure`, `p50_us`, `p95_us`, `p99_us`) in the CI log.

## Dependencies and ordering

None blocking. Related: `g25-impl` (perf gate may consume the JSONL or replace this test with criterion
rows), `g04-e2e` (Demo Showcase job must be green).

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

- Rejected: `#[serial]`/ordering attributes. They keep the file coupling; in-process capture+verify
  removes it.
- Rejected: committing `baseline_results.json`. Numbers vary per machine; provenance-checked cache is
  the right shape.
- Risk: making regressions hard failures by default would reintroduce runner-noise flakiness
  (`g04-02-impl`); hence strict mode is opt-in for the perf gate only.

## Definition of done

Children closed; Demo Showcase job green with the JSONL lines; close reason cites test names and run id.

title: bug(G40): Make baseline_capture.rs capture-and-verify in one process with a provenance-checked cache
description:
# bug(G40): Make `baseline_capture.rs` capture-and-verify in one process with a provenance-checked cache

## Context and why this matters

`crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/baseline_capture.rs` is run by the "Demo Showcase" CI job
(`ci.yml:502-503`) and was the single failing test in the reality check's full suite run (Section 1)
because a stale local `tests/baseline_results.json` lacked `terminal_color_depth`. Section 2.2.E calls
the design "order-dependent and stale-file-sensitive". Vision rows V35, V70. Beyond the flake, the test
cannot detect a regression at all: it only prints them. This bead fixes the design so the test is
deterministic, informative, and optionally strict. Parent: `g40-epic`.

## Current state (evidence)

- `baseline_capture.rs:255-258` `baseline_path()` -> `tests/baseline_results.json` (gitignored,
  `.gitignore:54`).
- `:284-315 capture_baselines` writes the file when `CAPTURE_BASELINE` is set or the file is missing;
  JSON keys `version "1.0.0"`, `generated_at "unix:<secs>"`, `terminal_color_depth "truecolor"`,
  `warmup_iters`, `measure_iters`, `hot_paths.{frame_pipeline,diff_engine,layout}`.
- `:318-352 verify_no_regression`: early return if missing; `expect("invalid JSON")`;
  `validate_baseline_color_depth` (`:260-271`) panics on missing/mismatched depth; re-measures;
  `check_regressions` (`:382-414`, recursive over `p99_us`, threshold 0.10); prints regressions with the
  hint "To update: CAPTURE_BASELINE=1 cargo test ..." — no assertion.
- `:39-67 measure()` returns `p50_us/p95_us/p99_us/max_us/iterations` per closure; `:26-27` 50 warmup /
  500 measured iterations; helpers `capture_frame_pipeline`, `capture_diff_engine`, `capture_layout`
  (`make_pair` at :70).
- Parallel test threads race on the file (both tests in one binary).

## Target state

- Single test `baseline_capture_and_verify`: measures once; loads the cache if present and valid
  (provenance: `version == "2.0.0"`, `terminal_color_depth == truecolor`, `git_sha` equal to
  `git rev-parse HEAD` when available, `hostname` equal to the current host); if invalid, logs one JSON
  line `{"event":"baseline_cache_ignored","reason":"missing|invalid_json|missing_provenance|depth_mismatch|host_mismatch|version_mismatch","path":..}`
  and treats it as absent; compares; prints per-hot-path JSON lines
  `{"event":"baseline_measure","path":"frame_pipeline/...","p50_us":..,"p95_us":..,"p99_us":..,"baseline_p99_us":..,"ratio":..}`;
  then writes the cache atomically (temp file + rename) with the new provenance unless
  `BASELINE_READONLY=1`.
- Regressions (> 10% p99): advisory by default (`{"event":"baseline_regression","path":..,"pct":..}`);
  with `BASELINE_STRICT=1` the test panics listing them (used by the perf gate, G25).
- `BASELINE_SYNTHETIC_SLOWDOWN_PCT=<n>` inflates the measured numbers by n% (test-only hook, documented)
  so the strict path can be exercised in `g40-tests`.
- Keep `capture_baselines` as a thin alias that calls the same function with `CAPTURE_BASELINE` semantics
  (so `docs`/scripts that reference the name keep working) — no second file, no second code path.

## Implementation plan

1. `baseline_capture.rs`: add `struct Provenance { version, terminal_color_depth, git_sha: Option<String>,
   hostname: Option<String>, generated_at }`; `fn load_cache(path) -> Result<Value, IgnoreReason>` (enum
   with the reasons above, each with `Display`); `fn write_cache_atomic(path, &Value)` using
   `tempfile`-free approach (`path.with_extension("json.tmp")` + `std::fs::rename`); `fn
   compare_and_report(baseline: Option<&Value>, current: &Value) -> Vec<Regression>` reusing
   `check_regressions`; `fn emit_measure_lines(current)`.
2. Replace the two tests with `baseline_capture_and_verify` + alias `capture_baselines` (calls the same
   fn with `force_write = env CAPTURE_BASELINE`); keep `baseline_color_depth_provenance_*` tests
   (:354-375) and extend them for the new reasons.
3. Provenance sources: `git_sha` via `std::process::Command::new("git").args(["rev-parse","HEAD"])`
   (None on failure); `hostname` via `std::env::var("HOSTNAME")` or `gethostname` through
   `Command::new("hostname")` (None on failure); mismatches are `IgnoreReason`s, not panics.
4. Header doc (:1-14): update the Run/Regenerate commands and document `BASELINE_STRICT`,
   `BASELINE_READONLY`, `BASELINE_SYNTHETIC_SLOWDOWN_PCT`.
5. `ci.yml:502-503`: keep the command; add `BASELINE_READONLY: "1"` on PR runs (no cache on runners
   anyway) — optional.
6. `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`, `ubs` on the file.

## Files to change

- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/baseline_capture.rs`: the redesign (single file; no new test file).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: env on the baseline step (optional).

## Success criteria

- [ ] With a stale file lacking `terminal_color_depth`: test passes and prints
      `baseline_cache_ignored ... missing_provenance` (three runs).
- [ ] With a half-written/invalid file: passes with `invalid_json` reason.
- [ ] `BASELINE_STRICT=1 BASELINE_SYNTHETIC_SLOWDOWN_PCT=50` with a valid cache: test fails listing the
      regressed paths; without `BASELINE_STRICT`: passes and prints `baseline_regression` lines.
- [ ] Default parallel run and `--test-threads 1` run give identical outcomes (no file race).
- [ ] "Demo Showcase" job green with `baseline_measure` lines in the log (run id).

## Tests and logging

`g40-tests`. JSON lines: `baseline_cache_ignored`, `baseline_measure`, `baseline_regression`,
`baseline_cache_written` (with path and provenance).

## Dependencies and ordering

Blocked by: none. Related: `g25-impl` (perf gate may call the strict mode or replace the test with
criterion rows; either way the JSON lines are the contract), `g04-e2e`.

## Considerations, risks, alternatives rejected

## Context

Companion to `g40-impl`. `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/tests/baseline_capture.rs` had two tests sharing a
gitignored file (`capture_baselines` :284-315 writes it; `verify_no_regression` :318-352 reads it,

## What to test

1. Cache loading decisions for every `IgnoreReason`.
2. Atomic write (no partial file observable) and provenance content.
3. Regression comparison logic and strict/advisory behaviour, driven by synthetic numbers.
4. Determinism across parallelism and pre-existing file states.

- `load_cache_invalid_json` (write `{` to a temp path) -> `Err(InvalidJson)`.
- `load_cache_missing_provenance` (`{"hot_paths":{}}`) -> `Err(MissingProvenance)`.
- `load_cache_depth_mismatch` (`terminal_color_depth: "ansi256"`) -> `Err(DepthMismatch)`.

title: epic(ftui): Universal Split-Pane Workspace (terminal + web)
description:
Background
- We need production-grade, click-drag resizable panes in both native terminal and web/wasm runtimes, with identical behavior semantics and first-class performance.
- Existing layout and hit-testing primitives are strong, but there is no unified pane workspace subsystem that guarantees parity between hosts.

North-Star Outcome
- A single shared pane engine powers both runtimes.
- Users can split, resize, collapse, reorder, and persist complex pane workspaces with mouse/touch/keyboard parity.
- Interaction remains deterministic, smooth, and robust under heavy UI load.

Why this matters
- Pane workspaces are the core interaction model for advanced TUIs and browser-hosted shells.
- Delivering this well improves usability, discoverability, and composability across all advanced screens/tools.

Design Principles
1. One canonical pane model in Rust; host adapters must not fork behavior.
2. Deterministic math and event handling for replay/debug.
3. Bounded cost per frame and bounded memory growth.
4. Inline-mode safety in terminal (scrollback-preserving defaults).
5. Accessibility and keyboard parity are built-in, not bolted on.

Hard Invariants
- Split tree remains acyclic and structurally valid after every operation.
- Min/max constraints are always respected after resize.
- Drag semantics are deterministic for equivalent event streams.
- Rendering cannot cause terminal state corruption or web pointer deadlocks.

Scope
- Shared pane core (split tree, constraints, operations, history).
- Shared interaction contract (drag lifecycle, snapping, thresholds).
- Terminal adapter implementation.
- Web/wasm adapter implementation.
- UX polish (handles, overlays, discoverability).
- Persistence and recovery.
- Full testing matrix (unit/property/PTY/browser perf+soak).

Out of Scope
- Arbitrary floating windows beyond the split-tree model (separate future epic).
- Remote multi-user collaborative editing of pane layouts (future epic).

Success Metrics
- 60+ FPS sustained on modern web hardware for representative demos.
- Terminal drag updates feel immediate and stable (no jitter/flicker).
- Parity scorecard: terminal vs web behavior diffs are empty for canonical scenarios.
- Deterministic replay reproduces layout state and frame hashes.

Execution Strategy
- Build this through child features/tasks below, each with strict dependencies and explicit quality gates.
- No bead should depend on this markdown outside Beads; every child contains full context for implementers.
design:
Program architecture
- Implement as one shared Rust pane engine with host adapters for terminal and web/wasm.
- Enforce deterministic interaction semantics via semantic event contract + replay harness.
- Keep correctness, accessibility, performance, and observability as co-equal release dimensions.

Test strategy mandate
- Every implementation task must land with focused unit tests.
- Cross-host behavior must be validated by deterministic replay + PTY/browser E2E.
- All validation paths must emit structured, searchable logs + reproducible artifact bundles.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Feature-complete split-pane workflows exist for terminal and web with semantic parity.
2) Comprehensive test pyramid exists: unit/property/fuzz + PTY/browser E2E + parity + soak.
3) E2E runner scripts are standardized and emit detailed diagnostics/artifacts by default.
4) Release gates for correctness/perf/a11y/parity are explicit and enforced.
notes:
Execution phases
1) Core model + solver + operations + invariants
2) Unified semantic interaction contract
3) Host adapters (terminal + web) with coordinate/hit-testing correctness
4) Rendering affordances + discoverability
5) Persistence/history/recovery
6) A11y parity and adaptive UX
7) Validation/perf hardening
8) Rollout docs + release gates

Key risks to manage
- Host divergence: terminal and web semantics drift unless parity runner remains authoritative.
- Input ambiguity: modifier/keymap precedence and drag lifecycle interruptions can produce non-deterministic behavior if contract is underspecified.
- Performance regressions: repeated resize and deep-tree operations can quietly exceed frame budgets without continuous profiling + CI gates.

Decision criteria
- Prefer shared Rust core logic to host-specific forks.
- If forced to diverge for host constraints, divergence must be explicit, documented, and covered by tests.
- Release only when correctness/parity/perf/a11y gates are all green.

Program execution schedule (optimized for parallel agents)
Assumed capacity
- 6 implementation agents + 1 integration/release agent.
- Time estimates are in minutes on each bead; schedule is dependency-gated and preemption-friendly.

Track A — Core/Contract backbone (Agent A)

- In parallel when unblocked: bd-2tp51 -> bd-1fix5 -> bd-2g4bw -> bd-ylfkz -> bd-2r1yi

Track B — Terminal adapter (Agent B)

Track C — Web adapter + rendering (Agent C)

- Perf: bd-2bav7 -> bd-1y0ph -> {bd-1k7ek, bd-25wj7} -> bd-1pvzq

Track E — Validation/observability spine (Agent E)

title: Async Task Manager E2E: Golden Schedule Trace + Isomorphism Proof
description:
## Goal
Guarantee scheduling behavior stays unchanged across refactors by validating a deterministic golden trace.

## Core Idea (Extreme Optimization)
- Record a canonical schedule trace (task start/stop, wakeups, yields, cancellations).
- Hash the trace into golden checksums.
- Require isomorphism proof for any performance change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Trace deterministic under fixed seed and scripted input.
- Golden checksum matches on CI.
- If checksum changes, require explicit isomorphism justification.

## Tests (REQUIRED)
- unit_trace_ordering: ordering rules are stable and documented.
- unit_trace_hash_stable: hashing stable across platforms.

## E2E (REQUIRED)
- Run scripted workload; emit trace + checksum; compare to golden.
- Log: scheduler decisions + queue lengths + wakeup latencies.

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.


## Testing Plan
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures.
- Property tests: invariants (idempotence, monotonicity, determinism) where applicable.
- Fuzz tests: parsers/state machines and any input-facing logic.
- Determinism: fixed seeds/time-freeze; snapshot fixtures must be stable.

title: Terminal engine: handle unimplemented Action variants (charset, DECALN, REP, SoftReset)
description:
Implement engine-side handling for parsed-but-unhandled Action variants in frankenterm-core:

1. **Character set switching** (DesignateCharset + SingleShift2/SS3):
   - Add G0-G3 character set slots to Cursor/SavedCursor
   - Implement DEC Graphics charset (0x5f-0x7e → line-drawing chars)
   - Apply charset translation during Print action
   - SingleShift2/3: temporary switch to G2/G3 for next char only

2. **DECALN (ScreenAlignment)**:
   - Fill entire screen with 'E' character
   - Reset margins and cursor position

3. **REP (RepeatChar)**:
   - Repeat the last printed character N times
   - Track last printed char in Grid/Cursor state

4. **DECSTR (SoftReset)**:
   - Reset cursor style, charset, modes, margins
   - Preserve screen content and scrollback

5. **AnsiSet/AnsiRst**:
   - Handle standard ANSI modes (IRM insert mode, etc.)

Tests: unit tests for each handler + conformance fixtures.
Quality gates: fmt, check, clippy, test.

title: Mermaid Terminal Diagram Engine (TME)
description:
Goal
- Build a world-class Mermaid-to-terminal diagram engine that produces beautiful, deterministic Unicode diagrams with ASCII fallback, adaptive to screen size and terminal constraints.

Why
- Current Mermaid support is raw-code display; we need real rendering to showcase FrankenTUI's rendering kernel and layout capabilities.
- Terminal constraints make layout beauty non-trivial; this epic formalizes the pipeline, algorithms, and integration.

Non-Goals
- No graphical raster output; terminal-only.
- No non-deterministic heuristics; all choices must be reproducible from inputs.
- No executing Mermaid JS; only safe, deterministic parsing.

Success Criteria
- Mermaid fenced blocks render as diagrams, not raw code.
- Output is deterministic for given input + size + config + capability profile.
- Diagrams scale: dense and detailed on large screens; readable on small screens.
- Unicode-first with ASCII fallback; capability policy chooses safely.
- Styling directives (classDef/style/linkStyle) and init directives are honored as far as terminal allows.
- Comprehensive tests (unit, property, snapshots, PTY E2E) + JSONL logs covering warnings, guard triggers, and config snapshots.

Key Design Principles
- Determinism, explainability, and layout beauty over strict spec fidelity.
- Unicode-first with ASCII fallback and width-calibrated glyph policy.
- Explicit layout objectives and constraints; no hidden heuristics.
- Graceful degradation under complexity guards; never crash on oversized inputs.

title: bug(doctor): supervised_orchestration Capture mode never drains child pipes while running (deadlock >64KB output, misreported as TimedOut)
description: supervised_orchestration.rs:762-863: SubprocessStdio::Capture pipes both streams but spawns no reader threads; wait_timeout polls with pipes unread, so a child writing >~64KB blocks on write() until the deadline, is killed, and reported TimedOut with output discarded (deadline break skips the post-exit drain). Fix: spawn reader threads after spawn() (see process_subscription.rs:241-258 for the correct in-tree pattern), use drained buffers on ALL exit paths. ALSO :855-867: timeout/cancel paths retain the PREVIOUS attempt's last_exit/last_stdout as evidence — reset per attempt.
close_reason: Capture mode now drains both pipes via concurrent reader threads (joined on every exit path incl deadline/cancel/wait-error); per-attempt evidence reset so timed-out retries never report a prior attempt's exit code/output. 2 real-subprocess regression tests (516KB output completes promptly; stale-evidence retry). doctor lib 2300 green, clippy -D clean

title: task(render-perf): implement certified dirty-region skipping in buffer and diff paths
description:
Background:
Once the certificate model is defined, the next step is to cash it out where it matters: avoiding buffer/diff work that the system can prove is unnecessary. This is where the abstract correctness story must become a practical, debuggable implementation with conservative fallback.

Goal:
Implement the first certified work-elimination path for render-stage skipping.
design:
Work packages:
- Wire certificate checks into the relevant render and diff seams.
- Ensure the implementation emits enough trace data to explain why work was skipped or forced.
- Preserve conservative fallback when evidence is missing, invalid, or conflicting.
- Scope the implementation so one primary work-elimination lever is being introduced rather than multiple intertwined optimizations.
- Define the expected replay and snapshot evidence that must pass before the change is trusted.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The implementation bead has a clear, singular objective: safely eliminate certified unnecessary work.
2. Behavioral preservation requirements and fallback triggers are explicit.
3. The task text makes it clear how reviewers should judge whether the implementation stayed within scope.
4. The implementation is incomplete without targeted unit/property tests for certificate logic plus integration/E2E replay evidence and detailed skip-vs-fallback logging.
notes: This bead should be kept narrow even if more ideas surface during implementation. The discipline matters because certificate logic is powerful and easy to overextend.
close_reason: Implemented DiffSkipHint enum and compute_certified_into method in ftui-render/src/diff.rs. Three hint levels: FullDiff (standard path), SkipDiff (certified buffer identity → zero work), NarrowToRows (certified clean rows → selective diff). Tracing events for skip/narrow evidence. 7 new tests covering skip, full-parity, narrow-to-rows, clean-row skip, out-of-bounds safety, and hint labels. Pre-existing tile_builder test failure is unrelated.

title: Internationalization (i18n) Foundation
description:
## Overview
Provide infrastructure for multi-language and RTL (right-to-left) text support in FrankenTUI applications.

## Rationale
- Global user base needs localized interfaces
- RTL languages (Arabic, Hebrew) require proper text rendering and layout mirroring
- String externalization enables translation workflows
- Locale-aware formatting (dates, numbers) improves UX

## Core Components
1. **String Catalog System**: Externalized string storage with key-based lookup
2. **RTL Layout Mirroring**: Automatic flex/grid direction reversal for RTL locales
3. **Unicode BiDi Algorithm**: Proper bidirectional text rendering in cells
4. **Locale Context**: Thread-local or model-level locale state
5. **Pluralization Rules**: ICU-style plural forms for different languages

## Implementation Strategy
- Create ftui-i18n crate (optional feature-gated dependency)
- Integrate with ftui-text for BiDi text segment handling
- Modify ftui-layout to respect text direction context
- Provide macro for compile-time string extraction

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests for BiDi text rendering (Arabic, Hebrew mixed with English)
- Layout tests for RTL flex/grid mirroring
- Snapshot tests comparing LTR vs RTL layouts
- Integration tests with demo showcase in multiple locales

## Success Criteria
- Applications can switch locale at runtime without restart
- RTL layouts render correctly with proper alignment
- No performance regression for LTR-only applications

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.


## E2E Plan
- Provide/extend an E2E script that exercises the feature end-to-end in PTY (where applicable).
- Logging: verbose JSONL with env/capabilities + per-step timings + seed + checksums; include a summary at end.
- On failure: print reproduction command and point to artifacts directory.
close_reason: All 6 subtasks closed: String Catalog System (.1), Locale Context Provider (.2), RTL Layout Mirroring (.3), BiDi Text Rendering (.4), i18n Demo and Extraction (.5), i18n E2E Test Suite (.6). Full i18n foundation with StringCatalog, PluralRules, FlowDirection/LogicalAlignment/LogicalSides RTL support, coverage/extraction API, I18nDemo screen, and 46 E2E tests.

title: Demo UX: Mouse-first interactivity + shortcut expansion
description:
Background
- Demo showcase already has a strong screen catalog, Screen Registry, command palette, and a Guided Tour.
- Mouse support exists but is currently shallow: tab bar click-switching is wired via the hit grid, and a handful of screens register hit regions, but most screens do not respond to mouse in an intuitive 'click what you see' way.
- Many screens have keyboard shortcuts, but lots of interaction is either hidden or passive; the demo should feel alive and exploratory.

Goals
- Make every screen in `ftui-demo-showcase` meaningfully mouse-friendly:
  - Clickable controls/widgets respond as users expect.
  - Scroll wheel scrolls the thing under the pointer (lists, panels, editors).
  - Drag interactions work where appropriate (kanban, drag-drop, timeline scrubbing, sliders).
  - Hover affordances are visible (focus/active state, subtle highlight, status hints).
- Add more keyboard shortcuts that *do things* (not just navigation):
  - Consistent global shortcuts (help, palette, perf HUD, inspector, toggle mouse).
  - Per-screen shortcuts for toggling modes, adjusting knobs, and triggering demos.
- Upgrade the Guided Tour storyboard to include the 'best stuff' and explicitly demonstrate:
  - Inline mode value (scrollback preserved; chrome stable).
  - Determinism + checksums + evidence ledgers.
  - Hit testing + hyperlinks + inspector overlays.
  - Performance HUD + budgets + degradation behavior.

Hard Constraints / Invariants (non-negotiable)
- Preserve Inline Mode scrollback as a first-class property:
  - Default behavior must not silently steal terminal scrollback unless user opts in.
  - Mouse capture policy must be explicit and documented in the demo UI and CLI.
- Keep one-writer rule / terminal lifecycle correctness intact.
- Determinism: fixed seeds + time-freeze remain deterministic across mouse/keyboard interactions.
- Performance: hit testing and hover updates must not materially regress frame time; coalesce high-frequency mouse move events.

Scope Notes
- This epic is about demo UX and interaction plumbing. It may require small changes in `ftui-core`/`ftui-widgets` (e.g., semantic mouse events or richer hit regions) when needed, but avoid large API churn.
- Prefer building shared primitives (clickable list/table/scrollbar/etc.) once, then applying to screens.

Success Criteria
- Every screen under `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/` has:
  - At least one meaningful mouse interaction (click/scroll/drag/hover) that changes state.
  - At least 3-5 screen-specific shortcuts that are discoverable in the help overlay.
- Guided Tour v2 covers the highest-signal screens and interactions.
- Test coverage exists:
  - Unit tests for mouse dispatch + focus/hover rules.
  - Deterministic integration tests per interaction category.
  - PTY/E2E validation where feasible.

- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/chrome.rs` (HitId ranges for chrome/panes)
- `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs` (mouse capture enable/disable)
- `crates/ftui-core/src/semantic_event.rs` (semantic click/drag abstractions)

title: Demo Input: mouse capture policy + inline scrollback preservation
description:
Background
- Mouse capture is currently available (see `ftui-core` terminal session enable/disable and the demo's `--no-mouse` CLI flag), but we must not compromise FrankenTUI's core value proposition: Inline Mode preserves native terminal scrollback.
- In many terminals, enabling mouse reporting steals the scroll wheel from the terminal's scrollback. That is acceptable in AltScreen mode, but it is a footgun in Inline mode unless it is explicit and opt-in.

Goal
- Define and implement a clear, explicit mouse capture policy for the demo showcase that:
  - Preserves native scrollback in Inline mode by default.
  - Still allows a 'full mouse' experience in AltScreen mode by default.
  - Provides an obvious, discoverable toggle and CLI/env config.

Design / Policy (proposed)
- Introduce a demo-level `MouseMode` concept (names are bikesheddable):
  - `Off`: no mouse capture; scroll wheel is terminal scrollback.
  - `On`: mouse capture enabled (click/scroll/drag/hover routed to UI).
- Defaults:
  - AltScreen: `On`.
  - Inline: `Off` (unless user explicitly opts in).
- UI affordances:
  - Status bar shows `Mouse: OFF (scrollback)` vs `Mouse: ON (UI scroll)`.
  - Help overlay documents toggle.
- Controls:
  - Keybinding: `M` toggles mouse mode.
  - CLI: keep `--no-mouse`; add `--mouse=on|off` (or env) if needed for determinism in tests.

Key Constraints
- No surprise scrollback theft in Inline mode.
- Must not violate one-writer rule or terminal teardown invariants.
- Deterministic: mode toggles are explicit inputs; no terminal-dependent heuristics.

Acceptance Criteria
- Inline mode demo retains native scrollback by default (wheel scrolls scrollback).
- AltScreen demo remains fully mouse interactive by default.
- Mouse toggle is visible/discoverable (status + help), and is logged in JSONL if demo logging is enabled.

Tests / Validation
- Unit tests for CLI/env parsing and default selection based on screen mode.
- PTY E2E smoke: Inline mode launch asserts mouse capture is disabled by default; AltScreen asserts enabled.

Key References
- `crates/ftui-core/src/terminal_session.rs` (Enable/Disable mouse capture)
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/cli.rs` (mouse flags)
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs` (event routing)

title: Demo Input: central mouse dispatcher (hit grid + semantic events)
description:
Background
- The demo already enables hit testing (`Frame::enable_hit_testing`) and caches a hit grid for tab-bar navigation.
- Today, only the tab bar click path is routed (`handle_mouse_tab_click`). Many screens already register hit regions (panes, links, etc.) but they are not wired to input.

Goal
- Build a central, deterministic mouse dispatch layer in the demo app that routes mouse events to the right target:
  - Chrome (tabs, category tabs, status bar toggles).
  - Overlays (command palette, help overlay, tour overlay, modal stacks).
  - Active screen content.

Scope / Work Items
- Standardize the input pipeline:
  - Raw `Event::Mouse(MouseEvent)` -> (optional) semantic gestures -> dispatch.
  - Decide click activation edge: prefer `MouseUp` for buttons (prevents accidental drags) unless explicitly needed.
- Hit test on every relevant mouse event:
  - Use `(HitId, HitRegion, HitData)` from the cached hit grid.
  - Provide a consistent mapping from hit targets to actions.
- Add hover tracking:
  - Mouse move updates a `hover_hit` state (coalesced) to support hover highlight + status hints.
- Drag handling:
  - Minimal drag state machine for screens needing drag (kanban, drag-drop, sliders, timeline scrub).
  - Use existing `ftui-core` semantic event primitives if/when helpful.

Determinism / Performance Considerations
- Coalesce mouse move events aggressively (existing event coalescer already helps).
- Avoid per-frame allocations for routing; keep hit ids stable.
- Never introduce wall-clock time dependencies in gesture recognition unless time-freeze is part of determinism mode.

Acceptance Criteria
- Clicking any registered hit region produces exactly one deterministic action.
- Hover state updates do not cause flicker and are coalesced.
- Drag interactions have a well-formed lifecycle and can be cancelled.
- Mouse interactions stop the guided tour consistently (like tab clicks already do).

Tests / Validation
- Unit tests for routing priority (palette > help > chrome > screen) and for hit mapping.
- Deterministic integration test: simulate a sequence of mouse events and assert resulting state transitions.

Key References
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs` (hit grid cache + current mouse handling)
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/chrome.rs` (HitId ranges)
- `crates/ftui-core/src/semantic_event.rs` (click/drag semantics)
- `crates/ftui-render/src/frame.rs` (hit grid API)
close_reason: done

title: task(perf-foundation): build golden-output, replay, and behavior-preservation proof oracles
description:
Background:
Many of the highest-value optimizations in this project involve skipping work or changing scheduling. Those are exactly the sorts of changes that can accidentally alter visible output, timing-sensitive semantics, or failure artifacts. We therefore need behavior-preservation oracles that are strong enough to block bad speedups.

Goal:
Create the golden-output and replay verification layer that later optimization beads must satisfy before they can be considered valid.
design:
Work packages:
- Define what constitutes equivalence for render output, runtime behavior, and doctor artifacts.
- Specify golden-output capture, checksum strategy, and replay commands for counterexample reproduction.
- Add an isomorphism-proof template covering ordering, tie-breaking, visible output, randomness, and any allowed differences.
- Distinguish presentation-only differences from semantic differences so reviewers know what must match exactly.
- Ensure failed proof attempts produce artifacts that make root-cause diagnosis fast.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Future optimization work has a concrete, reusable proof contract for behavioral preservation.\n2. Counterexample artifacts are actionable and replayable rather than vague test failures.\n3. The bead makes clear which dimensions of equivalence are strict and which can be intentionally relaxed with evidence and justification.
notes: This bead is the antidote to speedups that quietly corrupt determinism, terminal behavior, or triage evidence.
close_reason: Behavior-preservation proof oracles in proof_oracle.rs: 10 equivalence dimensions across 4 domains (Render, Runtime, Doctor, Performance). 9 strict + 1 relaxed. Includes BehaviorProof template with validation, RelaxedDimension justification tracking, DifferenceClass taxonomy (Semantic/PresentationOnly/PerformanceOnly), replay command generation, and proof completeness validator. Builds on existing golden.rs and shadow_run.rs. 15/15 tests pass.

title: Terminal Capability Simulator
description:
## Overview
Provide testing infrastructure that simulates various terminal capabilities for comprehensive compatibility testing.

## Rationale
- Real terminal testing requires many different terminals
- CI environments cannot run every terminal emulator
- Capability degradation paths need verification
- Helps developers test edge cases without hardware

## Core Components
1. **Virtual Terminal**: In-memory terminal that tracks state
2. **Capability Profiles**: Predefined profiles (xterm-256, vt100, dumb, etc.)
3. **Capability Override**: Runtime capability injection for testing
4. **Behavior Simulation**: Simulate quirks of specific terminals
5. **Recording/Playback**: Record real terminal sessions for replay

## Implementation Strategy
- Extend ftui-pty with VirtualTerminal that implements terminal traits
- Create capability profiles as static configurations
- Add CapabilityOverride to ftui-core for testing
- Integrate with snapshot testing in ftui-harness

## Predefined Profiles
- xterm-256color: Full features
- xterm: 16 colors only
- vt100: No colors, basic cursor
- dumb: Minimal capabilities
- screen: tmux/screen quirks
- windows-conhost: Windows Console Host behavior

## Testing Requirements
- Meta-tests: verify simulator matches real terminals
- Degradation tests: app behavior with reduced capabilities
- Cross-profile snapshot comparisons

## Success Criteria
- Can run full test suite without real terminal
- Capability detection code is thoroughly tested
- CI catches capability-related regressions

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.


## Testing Plan
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures.
- Property tests: invariants (idempotence, monotonicity, determinism) where applicable.
- Fuzz tests: parsers/state machines and any input-facing logic.
- Determinism: fixed seeds/time-freeze; snapshot fixtures must be stable.


## E2E Plan
- Provide/extend an E2E script that exercises the feature end-to-end in PTY (where applicable).
- Logging: verbose JSONL with env/capabilities + per-step timings + seed + checksums; include a summary at end.
- On failure: print reproduction command and point to artifacts directory.
