title: terminal_session teardown design gaps: kitty double-pop, signal-thread one-writer race, exit-vs-signal hang, remaining panic-boundary suppression sites
description: From exploration-audit round 7 (terminal_session.rs review). (1) Kitty keyboard pushed once (CSI >15u) but popped 2-3x on fatal-panic path: hook best_effort_cleanup pops, Drop cleanup pops again (kitty_keyboard_enabled still true), best_effort_cleanup_for_exit callers pop a third time; CSI <u is stack-based so an enclosing tty context's kitty entry is lost. Fix: global 'best-effort ran' flag consulted by cleanup(), or track pop-count. (2) SignalGuard thread writes teardown bytes to stdout concurrently with the render thread on SIGINT/SIGTERM (one-writer violation): a frame flush in progress interleaves with ESC[r/1049l and the frame remainder lands on the cooked main screen; deliberate restore-first tradeoff but worth a mutex/handshake with the writer. (3) Race: SIGTERM after the loop's last signal check on normal quit -> cleanup() joins signal thread which sits in wait_for_shutdown_ack ~2s then process::exit(128+sig) mid-Drop, skipping remaining destructors. (4) Recoverable panic boundaries still missing with_panic_cleanup_suppressed (fixed 2026-07-07 in program.rs run_task_closure + subscription.rs thread wrapper): ftui-extras/src/terminal/parser.rs:361, ftui-demo-showcase/src/app.rs:1608 + visual_effects.rs:4970 (HOOK-PROTECTED files — edit via python/git show per project rules). Also note: no SIGTSTP/SIGCONT handling (kill -TSTP suspends with raw mode + alt screen active).

S3-FIFO (Yang 2023 SOSP) replaces LRU/TinyLFU. EV=80.0 (highest). 3 FIFO queues (small/main/ghost), atomic bit access, no list reordering. description: Implement S3-FIFO: small VecDeque (10%), main VecDeque (80%), ghost VecDeque (10%), HashMap index. Insert to small. On eviction from small: if accessed, promote to main; else check ghost (if in ghost, insert to main). Eviction from main: FIFO with freq counter (max 3). Ghost stores keys only. Access = set bit (no reordering). Must be generic over K: Hash+Eq, V.

title: task(e2e): E2E test suite for S3-FIFO Cache
description:
## E2E Integration Test: S3-FIFO Cache (EV=80)

### Scope
Full integration test rendering 48 demo screens with S3-FIFO cache enabled for layout, width, and style caches. Exercises cache warm-up, steady-state hit rates, eviction under memory pressure, and visual correctness across all widget types.

### Test Scenario
1. Initialize FrankenTUI with S3-FIFO cache (small/main/ghost queues) replacing W-TinyLFU/LRU.
2. Render all 48 demo screens sequentially, each for 10 frames.
3. On each frame, capture golden-frame hash and compare to baseline (rendered with W-TinyLFU).
4. Inject cache pressure by cycling through screens rapidly (cache thrashing scenario).
5. Verify ghost queue promotion logic under realistic access patterns.

### JSONL Structured Logging Specification
Each frame emits one JSONL line with fields:
```json
{
  "event": "s3fifo_frame",
  "ts_ns": u64,
  "frame_id": u64,
  "screen": "string",
  "cache_hits": u32,
  "cache_misses": u32,
  "evictions_small": u32,
  "evictions_main": u32,
  "ghost_promotions": u32,
  "hit_rate": f64,
  "queue_sizes": { "small": u32, "main": u32, "ghost": u32 },
  "frame_hash": "hex_string",
  "baseline_match": bool
}
```

### Success Criteria
- All 48 screens render with zero visual regression vs baseline (frame_hash matches).
- Hit rate converges to >= 85% after warm-up (first 3 screens).
- No panics, no unsafe code violations (#![forbid(unsafe_code)]).
- Ghost queue correctly promotes frequently re-accessed entries.
- JSONL log file is parseable and schema-compliant for every frame.
- Total test runtime < 30s on CI.

title: feature(perf-foundation): measurement, replay, and optimization governance
description:
Background:
The optimization program needs a stable foundation before any subsystem-specific tuning is trustworthy. Without a shared baseline harness, hotspot extraction, golden outputs, and policy gates, the project will regress into anecdotal profiling and hand-wavy claims.

Goal:
Build the measurement, replay, and governance substrate that every later performance bead depends on.
design:
Feature scope:
- Inventory observables, invariants, and high-value fixtures.
- Capture deterministic baselines and profiler artifacts.
- Build golden-output and isomorphism-proof oracles.
- Define the comprehensive validation matrix and detailed logging contract that later lanes must satisfy.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Context

The demo showcase has genuinely impressive full-screen visual effects (metaballs, plasma, fire, matrix, etc.) implemented directly inside:
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/visual_effects.rs`

Right now these effects are *demo-owned* algorithms. They render via:
- `ftui_extras::canvas::{Painter, Canvas}` (Braille/sub-cell rasterization)

This is great for a wow-factor demo, but it prevents reuse inside real UI components (markdown panels, dashboards, forms) where we want:
- alpha-correct compositing behind widgets
- predictable contrast/legibility guarantees
- zero-flicker and deterministic presentation
- insanely high performance (no per-frame allocations, cache-friendly loops)

## Goal

Turn “demo visual effects” into **library-grade, trivially composable primitives** in `ftui-extras`:
- Effects can render as a **cell-background backdrop** behind arbitrary widgets (markdown, panels, lists).
- Effects can optionally also render as **high-resolution canvas output** for full-screen screensaver-like demos.
- Composition must be correct: use alpha blending and preserve scrollback/inline mode invariants.

Initial extraction scope:
- Metaballs + Plasma (because they are visually strong and structurally simple).

## Why This Serves FrankenTUI’s Core Goals

FrankenTUI’s differentiators are correctness + determinism + composability. Background effects are a perfect stress-test:
- If the API makes backdrops easy to layer correctly, *everything* becomes easier to compose.
- If the rendering model enforces zero surprise (no terminal corruption; no implicit I/O), it aligns with the one-writer rule.

We already have key low-level primitives:
- `PackedRgba::over()` implements Porter-Duff SourceOver.
- `Buffer::push_opacity()` + background compositing in `Buffer::set()` enable layered blending.

## Architectural Direction (High-Level)

We introduce a “backdrop render target” alongside the existing canvas target:

1) Backdrop target (cell-space):
- effect computes a `w*h` array of `PackedRgba` backgrounds
- widget writes those colors into `frame.buffer` as background-only pixels

2) Canvas target (sub-cell space):
- effect computes sub-pixel intensity/color into a `Painter` (Braille/blocks)
- `Canvas` renders it as glyphs

The critical composability primitive is the **Backdrop widget** (background-only), because it composes under any widget without affecting glyphs.

## Proposed Public API Sketch (Subject To Iteration)

```rust
pub enum FxQuality {
    Full,
    Reduced,
    Minimal,
}

pub trait BackdropFx {
    /// Fill `out` (len = w*h) with background colors in cell-space.
    ///
    /// Design constraints:
    /// - No per-call allocations (caller owns buffers).
    /// - Deterministic output given inputs.
    /// - Must tolerate tiny areas.
    fn render_bg(
        &mut self,
        out: &mut [PackedRgba],
        w: u16,
        h: u16,
        t: f32,
        theme: &ThemeInputs,
        quality: FxQuality,
    );
}

pub struct Backdrop<E> { /* effect + opacity + base fill + scrim policy */ }

impl<E: BackdropFx> Widget for Backdrop<E> { /* writes only cell.bg */ }
```

Theme input is an explicit decision point (see tasks):
- likely accept either `ftui_style::ResolvedTheme` (preferred stable surface)
- or a small `ThemeInputs` struct derived from `ftui-extras::theme::ThemePalette`

## Legibility / Contrast Policy

Backdrops must be safe behind text.
We achieve this by default through:
- an explicit opaque base fill (theme bg)
- effect composited with configurable opacity (usually 0.15–0.40)
- optional scrim overlay (theme overlay) under text-heavy regions

This creates a reliable invariant: text widgets can remain “transparent bg” and still be readable.

## Performance Non-Negotiables

- Zero allocations on the render hot path.
- Cache-friendly scanning (row-major), minimize branching.
- Avoid per-frame `Painter::for_area()` allocations in showcase; reuse buffers.
- Map `Frame.buffer.degradation` -> `FxQuality` so heavy effects degrade gracefully.

## Optional GPU Backend (Feature-Gated)

If a GPU is available, it should be used *only* as an internal accelerator and must:
- never panic or error to the user
- silently fall back to CPU forever if init fails
- be deterministic enough for interactive use (snapshot tests should default to CPU)

Planned implementation shape:
- `fx-gpu` feature using `wgpu`
- `FxBackend::Auto` with cached “GPU available” decision via `OnceLock`
- GPU computes the same `PackedRgba` cell-space buffer; terminal emission remains CPU

## Deliverables

- `ftui-extras`: new visual-fx/backdrop module(s) with stable-ish API
- extracted `MetaballsFx` + `PlasmaFx` using the new API
- demo showcase refactor to use the extracted library code
- tests for blending correctness + determinism, and perf sanity checks

## Non-Goals (For This Epic)

- extracting every single demo effect immediately (metaballs/plasma first)
- requiring GPU (GPU is optional and must never break CPU-only builds)
- changing terminal output/presenter mechanics

title: Visual FX API Spec: BackdropFx, Theme Inputs, Quality/Degradation
description:
## Purpose
Define the stable, library-grade contract for **cell-background visual FX backdrops** in `ftui-extras`.

This is the spec bead that all implementation beads (Backdrop widget, extracted effects, canvas adapters, GPU backend) must align to.

## Key Decisions (Lock These Down)

1) **Render target + ownership**
- Primary target is **cell-space backgrounds**.
- Effects write into a caller-owned `&mut [PackedRgba]` where `len == (w*h)`.
- No per-frame allocations required by the trait.

2) **Determinism contract**
- Output must be deterministic given the explicit inputs (dims, time, theme, params, quality).
- No hidden globals, no internal RNG unless explicitly seeded.

3) **Time semantics**
- Pass absolute time `t` (seconds, `f32` or `f64`) into render calls.
- If an effect needs internal state, it can keep it, but must still be deterministic under a fixed input sequence.

4) **Theme boundary**
- FX consumes a small resolved `ThemeInputs` (slots expressed in `PackedRgba`).
- Conversions from `ftui_style::ResolvedTheme` and `ftui_extras::theme::ThemePalette` are separate work (bd-l8x9.1.2).

5) **Quality / degradation**
- Define `FxQuality` and an explicit mapping from `ftui_render::budget::DegradationLevel`.
- Decorative FX must be able to go `Off` at low budgets.

6) **Composition semantics**
- Backdrop writes **background only** (`cell.bg`) and must never emit glyphs.
- Default composition should be predictable:
  - start from an **opaque base fill** (theme bg/surface)
  - composite effect color at configured opacity
  - optional scrim policy for legibility
  - child widget renders normally above

## Output Artifacts
- Spec comments + examples here.
- A short reference doc: `docs/concepts/visual-fx.md` (module path + invariants + examples).
- Downstream tasks reference this bead for naming + semantics (not re-deciding ad hoc).

## Non-Goals (This Epic)
- Extracting every showcase effect immediately (metaballs/plasma first).
- GPU bit-identical determinism across drivers (CPU remains the reference for tests).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A clear, minimal public API in `ftui-extras` for backdrop effects.
- [ ] A documented mapping from render budget degradation → FX quality.
- [ ] Theme integration boundary decided and documented (with conversions).
- [ ] No per-frame allocations required by the trait (caller-owned buffers).
- [ ] API supports deterministic output and tiny-area correctness.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
- Public type names + module paths are explicitly stated and consistent (aligned with bd-l8x9.1.1 + bd-l8x9.1.4).
- `BackdropFx` contract includes: buffer ownership, no-alloc expectation, determinism expectations, tiny-area safety.
- `ThemeInputs` required slots are listed and justified (what each is used for).
- `FxQuality` levels + `DegradationLevel -> FxQuality` mapping are explicit and documented.
- Composition ordering (base fill -> effect -> scrim -> child) is spelled out so users get predictable results.
- Spec includes a concrete test obligation list (unit tests + E2E script coverage) without requiring per-frame logging.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Problem

We need a library-grade API for visual effects that:
- can render behind arbitrary widgets (cell-background target)
- can optionally render at sub-cell resolution (canvas target)
- remains composable, deterministic, and fast

The API must minimize coupling and avoid pulling heavy deps unless feature-gated.

## Decisions To Lock Down

### 1) Theme Input Type

We currently have *two* theme-ish systems:
- `ftui-style::Theme` / `ResolvedTheme` (intended public surface)
- `ftui-extras::theme::ThemePalette` (lots of tokens used by demos)

We must choose an input type for FX that is:
- stable and ergonomic
- cheap to pass
- supports both dark/light and semantic slots

Options:
A) Accept `ftui_style::ResolvedTheme` (preferred long-term; stable surface)
B) Accept a small `ThemeInputs { base_bg, surface_bg, accent1, accent2, ... }` derived from either system
C) Accept raw `PackedRgba` params only (max decoupling, but less composable)

Recommendation: B) `ThemeInputs` as the FX boundary, with conversions from `ResolvedTheme` and from `ThemePalette`.
This avoids forcing FX to depend on the entire theme system while still enabling deep integration.

### 2) Backdrop FX Trait Shape

We need a single "cell-space" contract:
- caller owns reusable buffers
- effect fills `out` (len = w*h) with `PackedRgba` background colors
- effect may keep internal state (for animations / noise) but must not allocate per frame

Key constraint: effect must tolerate tiny areas and be deterministic given inputs.

### 3) Quality / Degradation Mapping

We already have runtime degradation levels (`ftui_render::budget::DegradationLevel`) that widgets use.
We need to map that to `FxQuality`:
- `Full` -> full resolution / full iterations
- reduced -> fewer iterations / lower frequency detail
- minimal -> very cheap fallback (e.g., simple gradient/noise)

We should explicitly state: effects may choose to render nothing at `EssentialOnly` / `Skeleton` if they are decorative.

### 4) Canvas Target (Optional)

The showcase uses `Painter` + `Canvas` (Braille). The library should support this without requiring it for backdrops.
We need to decide:
- separate trait `CanvasFx` OR
- adapter layer where an effect can implement both targets

Recommendation: keep backdrop API primary; add canvas rendering later as a separate trait to avoid bloating the core.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A clear, minimal public API in `ftui-extras` for backdrop effects.
- [ ] A documented mapping from render budget degradation -> FX quality.
- [ ] Theme integration boundary decided and documented (with conversions).
- [ ] No per-frame allocations required by the trait (caller-owned buffers).
- [ ] API supports deterministic output and tiny-area correctness.

## Output Artifact

This issue is "done" when its decisions are codified as:
- an API sketch in description/comments AND
- concrete type names + module path chosen for implementation tasks.

title: API Spec Subtask: Theme Boundary + Conversions (ResolvedTheme / ThemePalette)
description:
## Goal
Define the **theme boundary** for visual FX:
- FX consumes a small resolved `ThemeInputs` (slots as `PackedRgba`)
- conversions from existing theme systems are explicit and cheap
- no cyclic deps / no global theme lookup from FX code

## Scope

1) **ThemeInputs slot list** (what FX needs, and why)
- `bg_base` / `bg_surface`: opaque fills so Backdrop output is deterministic and doesn’t depend on previous cell.bg.
- `bg_overlay`: scrim color.
- `fg_primary` / `fg_muted`: used by contrast helpers.
- `accent_primary` / `accent_secondary` (+ a small `accent_slots` array): used for palettes/presets.

2) **Conversions**
- `impl From<ftui_extras::theme::ThemePalette> for ThemeInputs`
- `impl From<ftui_style::ResolvedTheme> for ThemeInputs`
  - requires a stable `ftui_style::Color -> PackedRgba` mapping.

3) **Caching guidance**
- Conversions should be cacheable at the app/screen level (e.g., recompute on theme change, not per cell).
- Backdrop render calls take `&ThemeInputs` to keep costs explicit.

## Non-Goals
- No new global theme registry.
- No "compatibility shims": once the semantic design system lands (bd-3vbf.1), update the mapping directly.

## Tests / Validation
- Unit tests: conversions are deterministic and produce opaque backgrounds where required.
- Unit tests: missing/None theme slots fall back to sensible defaults (documented).
- Unit tests: `ThemeInputs` stays within byte bounds and never produces NaN/inf (trivial for u8 RGBA).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] FX code can be used with either theme system.
- [ ] No dependency cycle introduced.
- [ ] ThemeInputs is small and cheap to pass by reference.
- [ ] ThemeInputs is sufficient for Metaballs/Plasma without hardcoding demo palettes.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
- ThemeInputs is the only theme boundary for FX modules (no global theme lookups).
- Conversions exist for both `ResolvedTheme` and `ThemePalette` without introducing crate cycles.
- Defaults/fallbacks are documented and tested.
- Works today and remains compatible with future design system improvements (bd-3vbf.1 is related, not blocking).

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Context

FX needs theme-aware colors (base background, overlay, accents) but should not hard-depend on any single theme implementation.

We have:
- `ftui_style::Theme` / `ResolvedTheme` using `ftui_style::Color`
- `ftui_extras::theme::ThemePalette` using `PackedRgba`

## Proposal: ThemeInputs (FX boundary)

Define a small struct in the FX module:

```rust
pub struct ThemeInputs {
    pub bg_base: PackedRgba,
    pub bg_surface: PackedRgba,
    pub bg_overlay: PackedRgba,
    pub fg_primary: PackedRgba,
    pub fg_muted: PackedRgba,
    pub accent_primary: PackedRgba,
    pub accent_secondary: PackedRgba,
    pub accent_slots: [PackedRgba; 4], // keep small; effects can derive more
}
```

Then provide conversions:
- `impl From<ftui_extras::theme::ThemePalette> for ThemeInputs`
- `impl From<ftui_style::ResolvedTheme> for ThemeInputs`
  - requires a tiny `Color -> PackedRgba` conversion (likely via `ftui_style` -> `ftui_render` mapping).

## Dependency / Cycle Considerations

- FX lives in `ftui-extras`, which already has optional deps on `ftui-style` and `ftui-render`.
- Keep conversions feature-gated (e.g., `visual-fx` enables `ftui-render`; theme conversions can be behind `dep:ftui-style` if needed).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] FX code can be used with either theme system.
- [ ] No dependency cycle introduced.
- [ ] ThemeInputs is small and cheap to pass by reference.
- [ ] ThemeInputs is sufficient for Metaballs/Plasma without hardcoding demo palettes.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Dependency Tweak (Plan Optimization)

This task was originally blocked by `bd-3vbf.1` (the full semantic design system).

That was overly constraining: we can define `ThemeInputs` *now* with a small set of semantically named slots (bg_base/bg_surface/bg_overlay/accents/etc.) and provide best-effort conversions from the **current** theme surfaces.

Then, when `bd-3vbf.1` lands, we can refine/expand the mapping without changing the FX public API. The stable boundary is `ThemeInputs`, not the upstream theme implementation.

Action:
- Changed `bd-l8x9.1.2 -> bd-3vbf.1` from `blocks` to `related`.

Rationale:

- Preserves the intention to align with the final design system.
- Avoids “compatibility shims”: the mapping can be corrected directly once the semantic palette exists.

title: API Spec Subtask: FxQuality + Mapping From DegradationLevel
description:
## Goal
Define `FxQuality` and the explicit mapping from `ftui_render::budget::DegradationLevel` so decorative backdrops degrade gracefully without surprises.

## Scope

1) `FxQuality` levels (recommended)
- `Full`: normal detail
- `Reduced`: fewer iterations / simplified math
- `Minimal`: very cheap fallback (lower frequency, fewer trig ops)
- `Off`: render nothing (decorative)

2) Mapping from `DegradationLevel`
- `Full` -> `Full`
- `SimpleBorders` / `NoStyling` -> `Reduced` (or `Minimal` for expensive FX)
- `EssentialOnly` / `Skeleton` / `SkipFrame` -> `Off`

3) Area-based overrides
- On huge areas (e.g., 240x80), allow clamping `Full -> Reduced` even if budget is `Full`.

## Tests / Validation
- Unit tests cover every `DegradationLevel` variant.
- Unit tests cover area-based override boundaries (document the threshold constants).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Mapping is explicit, stable, and documented in code (table + function).
- Backdrops can become `Off` at low budgets (never blocks essential UI).
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
- `FxQuality` variants are final and used across metaballs/plasma/backdrop widget.
- `DegradationLevel -> FxQuality` mapping exists and is unit tested.
- Thresholds for size-based clamping (if any) are constants with tests.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Context

FX backdrops are decorative. They must degrade gracefully when:
- terminal is huge
- CPU is under load
- runtime budget degrades frame quality (`DegradationLevel`)

## Proposed Quality Levels

```rust
pub enum FxQuality {
    Full,        // full iterations/detail
    Reduced,     // fewer iterations / lower frequency
    Minimal,     // very cheap fallback
    Off,         // render nothing
}
```

## Proposed Mapping

- `DegradationLevel::Full` -> `FxQuality::Full`
- `SimpleBorders` -> `FxQuality::Reduced`
- `NoStyling` -> `FxQuality::Reduced` (or `Minimal` depending on effect cost)
- `EssentialOnly` -> `FxQuality::Off` (background is non-essential)
- `Skeleton` -> `FxQuality::Off`
- `SkipFrame` -> `FxQuality::Off`

## Effect-Specific Overrides

Some effects may choose:
- `Reduced` -> `Minimal` on very large areas
- `Minimal` -> simple static gradient using theme accents

## Acceptance Criteria

title: GPU Backend Spike: wgpu Compute for FX (Silent Fallback to CPU)
description:
## Goal
Decide whether a `wgpu` compute backend is worth it for FX generation, while guaranteeing **silent CPU fallback** on any failure.

## Scope
- Prototype a minimal compute pipeline that generates a `w*h` RGBA8 buffer for *one* effect (metaballs first).
- Measure overhead vs CPU at realistic sizes (e.g., 120x40, 240x80).
- Identify the real risks:
  - init latency
  - readback cost
  - device lost / transient failures
  - determinism differences

## Non-Negotiables
- No panics in normal use.
- No user-visible errors/noise: fallback must be silent.
- If GPU init or dispatch fails once, permanently disable GPU for the process.

## Validation
- Compile-check: `cargo check -p ftui-extras --features fx-gpu,visual-fx`.
- Parity sanity: compare CPU vs GPU for a small set of sample points / small buffers within a tolerance (do **not** require bit-identical output).
- Failure path: test-only hook (env var) to force GPU init failure and assert CPU path still renders.

## Deliverable
A short conclusion:
- go/no-go for GPU backend
- expected speedups and where it helps
- proposed API shape for backend selection + fallback guarantees

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] GPU backend is fully optional and cannot break CPU builds or runtime.
- [ ] Any init/dispatch failure triggers silent CPU fallback and permanently disables GPU for the process.
- [ ] Measurements compare CPU vs GPU on realistic sizes and include overhead (init + dispatch + readback).
- [ ] Tests cover failure injection and verify CPU correctness under forced GPU failure.
close_reason: done

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Goal

Optional acceleration only: use GPU *if available* to speed up heavy FX computations, but never break CPU builds or runtime.

## Hard Requirements

- Must never panic in normal use.
- Must never surface runtime errors to users (silent fallback).
- If GPU init fails once, disable GPU for the rest of the process.
- Output must remain “good enough” and stable; snapshot tests should remain CPU-based.

## Likely Approach

- Add `fx-gpu` feature in `ftui-extras`.
- Use `wgpu` compute pipeline:
  - inputs: time, params, theme inputs, target dims
  - output: `w*h` RGBA8 buffer
- On startup/first use:
  - try adapter/device init
  - if fails: cache `GpuUnavailable` and always use CPU

## Determinism Concerns

GPU floating point and driver differences can cause subtle output differences.
Policy:
- GPU output must be visually correct, but we should not rely on bit-identical output.
- Any tests should be CPU-only or tolerant.

## Deliverable

A short written conclusion + a minimal proof-of-concept implementation plan:
- whether it is worth it
- what the public API looks like
- how we guarantee silent fallback

title: Implement Backdrop Widget: Cell-Background FX + Scrim + Composition
description:
## Goal
Implement the core composability primitive: a `Backdrop` widget that renders **cell background colors only** (no glyphs) from a `BackdropFx`, with base fill + opacity + optional scrim for legibility.

## Scope

1) Background-only rendering
- Writes `cell.bg` in `frame.buffer` and never writes glyph content.
- Default base fill should be **opaque** (theme surface) so output is deterministic regardless of existing buffer state.

2) Effect buffer ownership
- Backdrop owns/reuses a `Vec<PackedRgba>` sized to `area.width * area.height` (grow-only).
- Calls the effect to fill the slice (no per-frame allocations required by the effect contract).

3) Composition knobs
- Base fill color (usually theme surface)
- Effect opacity (scales alpha before compositing)
- Optional scrim policy (solid / gradient / vignette)

4) Ergonomics
- Provide a 1-liner wrapper for "child over backdrop" (tracked in bd-l8x9.2.3).
- Provide multi-layer composition with one buffer apply (tracked in bd-l8x9.2.5).

5) Runtime quality
- Backdrop reads `frame.buffer.degradation` and maps to `FxQuality` (tracked in bd-l8x9.2.4 + bd-l8x9.1.3).

## Deliverables
- Backdrop widget lives under `crates/ftui-extras/src/visual_fx/`.
- Public API is exported from `ftui_extras` behind the `visual-fx` feature.

## Tests / Validation
- Unit tests (bd-l8x9.8): background-only invariant + alpha correctness + determinism + tiny areas.
- E2E (bd-l8x9.8.1/8.2): demo showcase runs that exercise VisualEffects + markdown-over-backdrop paths with actionable logs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Backdrop renders only backgrounds (no accidental glyphs).
- [ ] Composition wrapper works (background + child widget in same area).
- [ ] Scrim option exists and demonstrably improves legibility.
- [ ] No per-frame allocations required by Backdrop (buffers owned/cached).
- [ ] Works correctly with scissor/opacity stacks.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Goal

Create the composability primitive that makes visual FX usable behind *real widgets*.

A Backdrop must:
- write only `cell.bg` (background)
- never write glyphs or corrupt text/layout
- support alpha blending via `PackedRgba::over()` / `Buffer::set()`
- support legibility with an optional scrim
- be fast enough to run every frame

## Implementation Sketch

### Rendering Model

For each cell in `area`:
1) start with an explicit opaque base background (theme surface/base)
2) composite effect color (with configured opacity) over base
3) optionally composite scrim (overlay) to guarantee readability
4) write a Cell with:
   - `content = EMPTY` (so we do not emit glyphs)
   - `fg = TRANSPARENT` (irrelevant)
   - `bg = computed_bg`

Because `Buffer::set()` already composites background over existing, the Backdrop must be careful about ordering:
- if we want Backdrop to be the "bottom" layer, it should render early (before foreground widgets).
- when used as a Widget wrapper, Backdrop renders first, then child widget.

### Composition Wrapper

Provide a wrapper like:

```rust
struct WithBackdrop<B, W> { backdrop: B, child: W }

impl<B: Widget, W: Widget> Widget for WithBackdrop<B, W> {
  fn render(&self, area: Rect, frame: &mut Frame) {
    self.backdrop.render(area, frame);
    self.child.render(area, frame);
  }
}
```

This makes “markdown over animated background” trivial.

### Scissor + Opacity

Use `frame.buffer.push_scissor(area)` and `push_opacity(opacity)` where appropriate.
Avoid nested opacity mistakes:
- Backdrop should generally manage its own opacity rather than relying on callers.

### Legibility Defaults

Default policy should be safe:
- base fill = theme.bg_surface (opaque)
- effect opacity default ~0.25
- scrim default Off (caller opts in), OR enable scrim automatically when used with text-heavy components.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Backdrop renders only backgrounds (no accidental glyphs).
- [ ] Composition wrapper works: background + child widget in same area.
- [ ] Scrim option exists and demonstrably improves legibility.
- [ ] No per-frame allocations required by Backdrop (buffers owned/cached).
- [ ] Works correctly with scissor/opacity stacks.

## Tests Needed

- background-only invariant (cells content unchanged when backdrop applied)
- alpha correctness vs `PackedRgba::over()` expectations
- determinism: same inputs -> same output
- tiny areas: 0x0, 1x1, narrow/short rectangles do not panic

title: Backdrop Internals: Buffer Caching + Zero-Alloc Render Path
description:
## Goal
Ensure Backdrop rendering is **zero-alloc in steady state** by caching and reusing internal buffers.

## Scope
- Backdrop owns `Vec<PackedRgba>` buffers sized to `area.width * area.height`.
- Grow-only policy: reallocate only when capacity is insufficient.
- Never use per-frame `vec![..]` or `push` patterns in the hot path.

## Tests / Validation
- Unit test: capacity does not change across many renders at a stable size.
- Unit test: resize to larger size grows once; resize smaller does not shrink.
- Unit test: buffer is fully written each frame (no stale pixels).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Backdrop steady-state render performs 0 vector growth operations.
- Resize path reallocates at most once per growth event.
close_reason: Implementation complete: zero-alloc buffer caching with grow-only policy. All 9 tests pass: capacity stable across renders, resize larger grows once, resize smaller does not shrink, buffer fully written with no stale pixels.

## Strategy

Backdrop rendering must not allocate every frame.

Implementation idea:
- Backdrop widget owns a `Vec<PackedRgba>` buffer sized to `area.width * area.height`.
- On resize, reallocate only when capacity is insufficient; otherwise reuse.

- plasma at 0.10 opacity
- scrim under text

…without paying O(layers * w*h) buffer writes to the frame.

## Proposed API Shapes (pick one)

A) `BackdropStack` widget
- owns:
  - `Vec<PackedRgba>` main buffer
  - `Vec<PackedRgba>` scratch buffer
- renders:
  - fill base
  - for each layer:
    - effect renders into scratch
    - apply layer opacity -> composite scratch over main
  - apply main to frame once

B) `CompositeFx` implementing `BackdropFx`
- wraps multiple `BackdropFx` and composes them into a caller-provided dst
- still needs scratch (owned by wrapper) but integrates cleanly with existing `Backdrop` widget

C) Tuple impls (advanced)
- implement `BackdropFx` for `(A, B)` / `(A, B, C)` to avoid trait objects
- may still need scratch; keep it explicit

## Performance Rules

- No per-frame allocations (buffers reused).
- No `Box<dyn BackdropFx>` unless we can prove it doesn’t matter (prefer generics).
- Composition must be stable/deterministic.

## Tests To Add

- unit: 2-layer composition equals sequential rendering + Buffer::set semantics
- unit: no-alloc steady-state
- unit: ordering matters and is documented (A over B vs B over A)

## Acceptance

- [ ] stacking multiple effects requires only a single pass of `buf.set` over cells
- [ ] API is ergonomic enough to use in `bd-l8x9.7` (markdown-over-backdrop)
- [ ] layering is deterministic and well-documented

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Implementation Notes

Target file:
- `crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/visual_effects.rs`

Current anti-pattern:
- `Painter::for_area(...)` per frame (allocates `pixels` + `colors` vectors every frame).

  - if dims grew: reallocate once, then reuse

title: Canvas Adapter Subtask: Shared Core Sampling API (Target-Agnostic)
description:
## Goal
Define a tiny, target-agnostic sampling surface so metaballs/plasma math has a **single source of truth** and can render to:
- cell-space backdrops (w*h)
- `ftui_extras::canvas::Painter` (sub-cell)
- future GPU compute (conceptually the same sampling function)

## Proposed Shape
- A pure sampling function (or small trait) like:
  - `sample(x_norm, y_norm, t, theme, quality, params) -> PackedRgba`

Where:
- `x_norm`/`y_norm` are stable normalized coordinates (define exact convention: [0,1] at centers).
- `t` is explicit.
- No hidden globals.

description:
## Goal
Add a Rust-based PTY integration test that drives the VisualEffects screen with real key input and asserts the app never panics.

## Why Rust/PTY (Not Bash)
The demo reads real terminal events via crossterm; sending complex input sequences from bash is fragile.

`ftui-pty` already exists to provide deterministic PTY automation.

## Test Outline
- Spawn `ftui-demo-showcase` on VisualEffects (`--screen=12`).
- Send key inputs with small delays:
  - space / left / right (cycle effects)
  - 'p' (cycle plasma palette when plasma is active)
- Quit cleanly ('q') and assert exit success.

## Logging Requirements
- On failure, print:
  - which key was last sent
  - captured stderr
  - a trimmed tail of captured output

## Acceptance Criteria
- Test runs deterministically in CI (no interactive requirements).
- Proves VFX input handling survives rapid switches without panics.

comments.text:

The demo reads real terminal events via crossterm. Sending keystrokes reliably from bash is fragile.

`ftui-pty` already exists to provide deterministic PTY automation; use it to:

  - left/right arrows (escape sequences)

## Logging

On failure, dump:
- captured stderr

- which key was last sent

title: InlineAuto height change + write_log before next present writes log inside displayed UI region
description: Found by exploration-audit round 5 (terminal_writer.rs review). set_auto_ui_height/clear_auto_ui_height (terminal_writer.rs ~930-966) invalidate prev_buffer but the OLD region is still physically on screen; write_log's InlineAuto arm (~2135-2150) positions using the NEW effective_ui_height() and ignores last_inline_region. Sequence: InlineAuto{min:1,max:8}, 80x24, UI displayed rows 17-24; request_ui_height_remeasure() drops effective height to min=1; a Cmd::Log before the next render computes log_row = 23 → log written INSIDE the on-screen UI; next present repaints rows 17-24, destroying the log line (never reaches scrollback). Same chain for plain shrink 6→3. Fix: position logs against the last DISPLAYED region (last_inline_region) rather than the effective height, or defer logs until after the next present when the region changed. Also consider (P3, emulator-dependent): set_size keeps stale last_inline_region from old geometry, and clear_inline_region_diff then erases old-geometry coordinates that may hold reflowed scrollback content on kitty/iTerm-style resize.
close_reason: Fixed: log positioning anchors against last_inline_region (displayed) rather than effective height, so remeasure/shrink between presents cannot land logs inside on-screen UI; set_size now also clears last_inline_region so post-resize geometry can't steer positioning or shrink-erasure. Regression test: inline_auto_shrink_positions_log_against_displayed_region. Note: diff-strategy posterior reset removed (was compensating for log-induced scrolling that no longer happens); test renamed to log_write_without_scroll_region_preserves_diff_strategy.

title: FrankenTerm.WASM: full custom terminal stack (replace crossterm + xterm.js)
description:
Vision
- Build FrankenTerm: a first-party, Rust-first terminal engine and renderer that runs natively and as `frankenterm.wasm`.
- Replace BOTH Crossterm (native) and xterm.js (web) so we control correctness, latency, and UX end-to-end.

North-Star Outcomes
- Web: `ftui-demo-showcase` runs fully client-side inside FrankenTerm at interactive framerates and feels like a native app.
- Web (terminal-class): FrankenTerm can connect to a real PTY bridge and run scripted remote sessions (bidirectional protocol, not just rendering).
- Native: a first-party backend with better lifecycle semantics + better perf than Crossterm.

Hard Constraints (Non-negotiable)
- Safe Rust in-tree (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in our crates; deps may use unsafe internally).
- Determinism where requested: seeded demos, explicit time sources, record/replay.
- Extreme Optimization discipline: baseline/profile/prove/one-lever/gates.
- Accessibility: keyboard-only usability + screen-reader strategy (even with WebGPU/canvas rendering).
- Security for remote mode: explicit threat model, origin/auth controls, no accidental command-exec in prod.

Success Criteria
- Builds:
  - `cargo test` green for workspace
  - `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds for web crates
- Correctness:
  - Golden trace replay gates are green (native + web)
  - Native PTY E2E suite (`tests/e2e/scripts/*`) stays green with detailed JSONL logs
- UX:
  - Web terminal supports: selection+copy/paste, scrollback, OSC 8 hyperlinks, resize storms, search, and a11y modes
- Performance:
  - 120x40 steady-state rendering at 60fps on modern hardware for representative workloads
  - Keystroke-to-photon latency budgets defined and measured for remote sessions

title: Web: frankentui_showcase_demo.html runs ftui-demo-showcase in browser (FrankenTermWeb, no xterm.js)
description:
Background
- FrankenTUI already has a full reference application (`ftui-demo-showcase`) and a first-party web terminal surface (`frankenterm-web`) that explicitly avoids xterm.js.
- What we do *not* yet have in this repo is a single, obvious, runnable artifact that proves the whole stack works end-to-end in the browser: inputs → model update → view/frame → diff/patch → FrankenTermWeb render.

User-Facing Outcome
- A standalone `frankentui_showcase_demo.html` (in this repo) that runs the *entire* showcase app client-side using our WASM-powered terminal engine/rendering (`frankenterm-web`), with interactive keyboard + mouse input, resize handling, and deterministic stepping where requested.

Why This Matters
- This is the fastest way for humans (and future-us) to validate correctness + UX without needing the Next.js website repo.
- It also becomes a high-signal E2E test harness for the web pipeline: record/replay input streams, compare frame hashes, and emit rich JSONL evidence logs.

Constraints / Non-Negotiables
- No xterm.js. The HTML demo must use `crates/frankenterm-web` and the ftui-web patch path.
- Do not weaken lint/quality gates.
- Determinism where requested: the demo must support seeded runs / fixed timestep playback for trace-based tests.

Deliverables
- `frankentui_showcase_demo.html` with JS glue to load wasm modules, initialize `FrankenTermWeb`, forward normalized input events, apply patch batches, and render each frame.
- A minimal WASM runner API for `ftui-demo-showcase` (wasm-bindgen boundary) that can be stepped/driven by the HTML host.
- Comprehensive unit tests + browser E2E tests with detailed logging (JSONL + console capture) to verify correctness and prevent regressions.

High-Level Architecture
- Browser host:
  - Captures DOM events → calls `FrankenTermWeb.input(...)` → drains encoded inputs (`drainEncodedInputs()`).
  - Feeds encoded inputs into the showcase WASM runner.
  - Receives patch batches in the `applyPatchBatchFlat(spans, cells)` format and applies them to `FrankenTermWeb`.
  - Calls `FrankenTermWeb.render()` / present loop (requestAnimationFrame).
- Showcase WASM runner:
  - Wraps `ftui-web::StepProgram<AppModel>` (or equivalent) and exposes: init, resize, apply_inputs, step, drain_patches.
  - Owns deterministic time source + optional fixed timestep mode for replay tests.

title: Design: JS/WASM contract for showcase runner (inputs, resize, patches, determinism)
description:
Goal
- Define the exact JS/WASM contract between:
  1) the browser host (HTML+JS),
  2) `FrankenTermWeb` (web terminal surface; `crates/frankenterm-web`), and
  3) the showcase WASM runner (host-driven wrapper around `ftui-demo-showcase` + `ftui-web::StepProgram`).

Why This Is Its Own Bead
- Locking down these formats makes downstream work (runner impl, HTML glue, E2E traces) mechanical and reviewable.

---

Contract v1 (Code-Backed)

1) Terminal Surface (FrankenTermWeb)
- Constructor: `new FrankenTermWeb()`
- Init (async): `await term.init(canvas, options?)`
  - Implemented in `crates/frankenterm-web/src/wasm.rs`.
  - `options` (partial):
    - `cols`/`rows` (u16) default `80x24`
    - `cellWidth`/`cellHeight` (u16) default `8x16`
    - `dpr` (f32) default `1.0`
    - `zoom` (f32) default `1.0`
    - `screenReader|screen_reader`, `highContrast|high_contrast`, `reducedMotion|reduced_motion`, `focused`
    - input encoder features + link open policy + text shaping config (see wasm.rs parsing)

- Geometry / Resize:
  - `term.fitToContainer(containerWidthCssPx: u32, containerHeightCssPx: u32, dpr: f32) -> geometry`
    - returns deterministic snapshot `{ cols, rows, pixelWidth, pixelHeight, cellWidthPx, cellHeightPx, dpr, zoom }`
  - `term.resize(cols: u16, rows: u16)` also exists for direct grid resize.

- Input normalization:
  - `term.input(eventObj)` accepts a normalized, deterministic InputEvent-shaped JS object (NOT a raw DOM event).
  - `term.drainEncodedInputs() -> Array<string>` returns canonical JSON strings (stable for record/replay).
  - `term.drainEncodedInputBytes() -> Array<Uint8Array>` is the VT-bytes path (remote/PTY mode), not used for showcase runner.

- Patch application:
  - `term.applyPatchBatchFlat(spans: Uint32Array, cells: Uint32Array)` is the fast path.

2) Browser Host → FrankenTermWeb InputEvent Object Shape
(Parsed by `parse_input_event()` in `crates/frankenterm-web/src/wasm.rs`.)

Common
- `kind: "key"|"mouse"|"wheel"|"touch"|"composition"|"paste"|"focus"|"accessibility"`
- `mods` may be any of:
  - preferred: `mods: number` (u8 bitset) with SHIFT=1, ALT=2, CTRL=4, SUPER=8
  - or: `mods: { shift, ctrl, alt, super/meta }`
  - or: top-level boolean flags: `shift|shiftKey`, `ctrl|ctrlKey`, `alt|altKey`, `meta|metaKey|super|superKey`

Key
- `{ kind:"key", phase:"down"|"up"|"keydown"|"keyup", key:<DOM key>, code:<DOM code>, repeat?:boolean, mods?:... }`

Mouse (cell coordinates; 0-indexed)
- `{ kind:"mouse", phase:"down"|"up"|"move"|"drag", x:u16, y:u16, button?:u8, mods?:... }`
  - `button` uses: 0=Left, 1=Middle, 2=Right, 3+=Other

Wheel (cell coordinates; deterministic *step* deltas, not pixels)
- `{ kind:"wheel", x:u16, y:u16, dx:i16, dy:i16, mods?:... }`
  - Sign convention matches SGR mouse wheel encoding in `crates/frankenterm-web/src/input.rs`:
    - `dy > 0` = scroll down, `dy < 0` = scroll up
    - `dx > 0` = scroll right, `dx < 0` = scroll left
  - Host MUST quantize DOM wheel input to deterministic i16 steps.
    - Recommended simplest deterministic mapping for the demo: `dx = sign(deltaX)`, `dy = sign(deltaY)` (0 if |delta|==0).

Paste
- `{ kind:"paste", data:string }` (UTF-8; max 786432 bytes enforced)

Focus
- `{ kind:"focus", focused:boolean }`

Composition
- `{ kind:"composition", phase:"start"|"update"|"end"|"cancel"|DOM synonyms, data?:string }`

Touch
- `{ kind:"touch", phase:"start"|"move"|"end"|"cancel", touches:[{id:u32,x:u16,y:u16},...], mods?:... }`

Accessibility
- `{ kind:"accessibility", screenReader?:bool, highContrast?:bool, reducedMotion?:bool, announce?:string }`

3) FrankenTermWeb → Host Encoded Input JSON (drainEncodedInputs)
- Canonical JSON is produced by `InputEvent::to_json_string()` in `crates/frankenterm-web/src/input.rs`.
- It is stable for record/replay (explicit field ordering, compact encoding).
- Shape is `InputEventJson` with `serde(tag="kind", rename_all="snake_case")`.

Examples (illustrative)
- Key: `{ "kind":"key", "phase":"down", "code":"Enter", "mods":0, "repeat":false }`
- Mouse: `{ "kind":"mouse", "phase":"down", "button":0, "x":10, "y":5, "mods":0 }`
- Wheel: `{ "kind":"wheel", "x":10, "y":5, "dx":0, "dy":1, "mods":0 }`
- Paste: `{ "kind":"paste", "data":"hello" }`

4) Encoded Input JSON → Runner → ftui_core::event::Event Mapping
Runner parses each string using the same schema, then converts to `ftui_core::event::Event`.

Canonical mapping (deterministic):
- `kind=key`
  - Map normalized key code (InputEventJson `code`) into `ftui_core::event::KeyCode` (Char/Enter/Escape/...; unknown => KeyCode::Null).
  - `phase=down`:
    - if `repeat=true` => `KeyEventKind::Repeat`
    - else => `KeyEventKind::Press`
  - `phase=up` => `KeyEventKind::Release`
  - `mods` bitset maps 1:1 to `ftui_core::event::Modifiers`.

- `kind=mouse`
  - Map x/y to `Event::Mouse(MouseEvent { x, y, modifiers, kind })`.
  - `phase=move` => `MouseEventKind::Moved`
  - `phase=down/up/drag` uses `button` mapping to `ftui_core::event::MouseButton`.

- `kind=wheel`
  - Map to repeated `Event::Mouse(MouseEventKind::Scroll*)` events.
  - Steps: `steps = max(abs(dx), abs(dy))`, clamped to 0..=16.
  - Direction:
    - if `dy != 0`: `dy > 0 => ScrollDown`, `dy < 0 => ScrollUp`
    - else: `dx > 0 => ScrollRight`, `dx < 0 => ScrollLeft`

- `kind=paste`
  - `Event::Paste(PasteEvent::new(data, /*bracketed=*/false))`

- `kind=focus`
  - `Event::Focus(focused)`

- `kind=composition`
  - `phase=end` with `data` => `Event::Paste(PasteEvent::new(data, /*bracketed=*/false))`
  - other phases => ignored (no-op) for now (still parseable + loggable).

- `kind=touch`
  - For demo compatibility, map to synthetic left-mouse events using the lowest touch id:
    - start => Mouse Down(Left)
    - move => Mouse Drag(Left)
    - end/cancel => Mouse Up(Left)

- `kind=accessibility`
  - Host applies directly to `FrankenTermWeb` via its dedicated APIs (rendering/mirror behavior).
  - Runner may currently ignore, or optionally forward as a custom app message later.

5) Runner → Host Patch ABI (Flat Path)
Runner emits patch batches compatible with `FrankenTermWeb.applyPatchBatchFlat(spans, cells)`.

Source of truth:
- Emission: `ftui-web` (`WebOutputs::flatten_patches_u32()` in `crates/ftui-web/src/lib.rs`)
- Decoding: `cell_patches_from_flat_u32()` in `crates/frankenterm-web/src/renderer.rs`

Invariants
- `spans: Uint32Array` in `[offset, len, offset, len, ...]` order.
  - `offset` is linear row-major cell offset (`row * cols + col`).
  - `len` is measured in CELLS (not u32 words).
  - spans are non-overlapping and ordered by increasing offset.

- `cells: Uint32Array` in `[bg, fg, glyph, attrs, ...]` order.
  - Exactly 4 u32 words per cell.
  - Must be fully consumed by spans (`sum(len) * 4 == cells.length`).

Cell packing
- `bg` / `fg`: packed RGBA as u32 (R in high byte, A in low byte).
- `glyph`: Unicode codepoint (`0` = empty/continuation). Graphemes use a fixed fallback codepoint (see `ftui-web` `cell_to_patch`).
- `attrs`: low 8 bits = style flags, bits 8..31 = hyperlink id.

Empty batches
- Allowed. `spans.length==0 && cells.length==0` means no-op.

6) Resize / Geometry Sync Rules
- The host MUST keep runner size and FrankenTermWeb size in lockstep.
  - After `fitToContainer()` returns `{cols, rows, ...}`, do:
    - `term.resize(cols, rows)` ONLY if you did not call `fitToContainer` (it already updates internal geometry).
    - `runner.resize(cols, rows)` (pushes `Event::Resize`).
- Patch offsets are only meaningful if both sides agree on `cols`.

7) Determinism / Time-Stepping
- Runner uses `ftui-web::StepProgram` deterministic clock (`advance_time(Duration)` / `set_time(Duration)`).
- Two supported host modes:
  1) realtime: per-frame `dt_ms = performance.now() - last_now` (clamped), `advance_time(dt)`, then `step()`.
  2) fixed-step: constant `dt_ms` (e.g. 16) and deterministic seeded replay.

8) JSONL Logging (Recommended; aligns with `e2e-jsonl-v1`)
- Prefer the existing schema used by `frankenterm-web` harness (`crates/frankenterm-web/src/frame_harness.rs`).

Minimum record types for showcase traces:
- `record_type: "showcase_input"`:
  - include: `schema_version`, `timestamp`, `run_id`, `seed`, `event_idx`, and `input_json` (the exact string from `drainEncodedInputs`).
- `record_type: "showcase_step"`:
  - include: `timestamp`, `run_id`, `seed`, `step_idx`, `dt_ms`, `events_processed`, `rendered`, `running`, `frame_idx`, `cols`, `rows`.
  - if rendered: include patch stats + `patch_hash` from `WebOutputs`.
- `record_type: "frame"`:
  - after applying patches, host may call `term.snapshotResizeStormFrameJsonl(run_id, seed, timestamp, frame_idx)` to emit stable frame hashes + geometry for postmortem.

---

Acceptance Criteria
- This description is implementable against current code:
  - `crates/frankenterm-web/src/wasm.rs` (JS surface)
  - `crates/frankenterm-web/src/input.rs` (canonical encoded JSON)
  - `crates/ftui-web/src/step_program.rs` + `crates/ftui-web/src/lib.rs` (runner + patches)
  - `crates/frankenterm-web/src/renderer.rs` (flat patch decoder)
- Downstream beads can reference this contract verbatim.
close_reason: done

title: Fix WASM build: ftui-core tracing feature must compile on wasm32
description:
Background
- The web showcase demo requires building a subset of the ftui stack for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- `ftui-core` has a `tracing` feature that is used by higher layers for instrumentation.
- Current issue: enabling `ftui-core` `tracing` on `wasm32-unknown-unknown` fails to compile because the optional `tracing` dependency is placed under a unix-only target dependency section in `crates/ftui-core/Cargo.toml`.

Root Cause (Expected)
- Optional deps for the `tracing` feature must be available on wasm targets too (or the feature must be cfg-gated).
- Today the feature compiles on unix but not on wasm because the dependency is not in scope for the wasm target.

What "Done" Means
- `ftui-core` compiles on wasm when `--features tracing` is enabled, without weakening the feature model.

Repro
- `cargo check -p ftui-core --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features tracing`

Fix Sketch
- Move `tracing` (and any required optional deps) into normal `[dependencies]` with `optional = true`, and keep platform-specific extras behind appropriate cfgs.
- Ensure `ftui-core/src/logging.rs` compiles cleanly on wasm with `tracing` enabled (may require `cfg` around subscriber setup if any).

Validation
- `cargo check -p ftui-core --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features tracing`
- `cargo check -p ftui-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (sanity)
- Follow-on: `cargo check -p ftui-demo-showcase --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` once the runner crate exists.

Notes
- This bead is a hard prerequisite for the browser showcase runner and for CI to gain a wasm check job.
close_reason: Fixed: moved tracing and tracing-subscriber from cfg(unix) target dependencies to platform-independent [dependencies] section in ftui-core/Cargo.toml. Verified: cargo check -p ftui-core --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features tracing succeeds, as does --features tracing-json, plus native builds and all 834 lib tests pass.

description:
Goal

Key Requirement

Change

- hyperfine (test binary): mean ~101.9ms (1.22x faster)
- strace -c: ~2 poll + ~539 read syscalls

Isomorphism proof
- Ordering preserved: yes (bytes parsed in-order; we only pull more bytes earlier).
- Tie-breaking unchanged: N/A
- Floating-point: N/A
- RNG: N/A
- Golden outputs: cargo test -p ftui-tty ✓

title: Alien Artifact: failing-trace minimizer (delta debugging + VOI)
description:
Goal
- When a golden trace fails (checksum mismatch), automatically minimize it to the smallest repro trace that still fails.

Why (User Value)
- Makes regressions debuggable in minutes: a minimized trace is actionable and can be attached to issues/PRs.

Techniques (Alien Artifact)
- Start with classic delta debugging (ddmin) on the event stream.
- Upgrade with Value-of-Information (VOI) heuristics to pick the next reduction step that maximizes expected information gain per replay cost.
- Maintain an evidence ledger: each reduction attempt logs (candidate size, replay time, pass/fail, inferred minimality bounds).

Deliverables
- CLI/API to minimize a trace given a predicate ("replay mismatches").
- Produces a new trace file + a minimization report (JSON/JSONL).

Acceptance Criteria
- On a representative failing trace, produces >=10x size reduction while preserving the failure.
- Deterministic: repeated minimization yields identical minimized trace on same build.
- Integrates into CI failure artifacts (minimized trace attached when feasible/time-bounded).

2. PROFILE: CPU + allocations + (web) GPU timing when available
3. OPPORTUNITY MATRIX: Score = Impact x Confidence / Effort; implement only Score >= 2.0
4. IMPLEMENT: exactly one lever per commit; no behavior changes mixed in
5. PROVE: golden outputs + explicit isomorphism proof (ordering/ties/FP/RNG)
6. VERIFY: trace replay + sha256/checksum gates
7. REPEAT: re-profile (hotspots shift)

Deliverables
- Repeatable harnesses
  - Core parser/grid: `cargo bench -p frankenterm-core` + realistic byte-stream corpus
  - Web renderer: in-browser harness that emits machine-readable JSON (frame_time histogram, time_to_first_frame, steady-state memory)
  - Native backend: PTY harness + present-time metrics + syscall profile (e.g. `strace -c`)
- Golden artifact strategy
  - JSONL traces (reuse/extend `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json`)
  - Frame/patch checksums stored in an append-only registry
- Templates
  - Opportunity matrix table + scoring rubric
  - Isomorphism proof template for every perf-related change
  - Regression threshold policy (when CI should fail)

Acceptance Criteria
- For each subsystem (core/web/native) we can run: baseline -> profile -> replay -> gate.
- Every optimization PR includes before/after numbers + a single-lever diff + isomorphism proof + golden verification.
notes: Drafted docs/profiling/extreme-optimization-loop.md (baseline/profile/opportunity matrix/one-lever/isomorphism proof/regression thresholds + harness sketches) and linked it from docs/operational-playbook.md.

title: Spec: Correctness strategy for terminal engines (invariants, fuzz, golden traces)
description:
Goal
- Specify correctness guarantees strong enough to justify replacing BOTH Crossterm and xterm.js.

Correctness Model
- Treat the terminal engine as a deterministic state machine driven only by explicit inputs:
  - output byte streams (VT/ANSI) and/or patches
  - input events (keyboard/mouse/touch/IME)
  - resize events
  - ticks/time (explicitly injected; never implicit global time)

Must Include
- Formal-ish invariants (written down, then enforced):
  - parser state machine safety (no panic, bounded memory growth, valid transitions)
  - grid mutations (cursor bounds, width invariants, no invalid placeholder cells)
  - scrollback correctness (capacity, wrap/reflow policy, viewport invariants)
  - selection semantics (spans scrollback+viewport; stable under resize where specified)
  - hyperlink semantics (OSC 8 lifetime + mapping)
- Proptest strategy
  - generators for byte streams, events, and resize storms
  - shrinking strategy that yields minimal repros
- Fuzzing strategy
  - entrypoints + corpora + crash triage protocol
  - every crash becomes a regression fixture
- Golden artifacts
  - conformance fixtures (byte stream -> expected grid snapshots)
  - golden trace corpus (event log -> expected checksums)
  - renderer goldens (framebuffer/patch checksums for key scenes)
- Differential testing (high-value)
  - compare FrankenTerm state against reference emulators for the same byte streams

E2E & Logging Requirements
- Native: `tests/e2e/scripts/*` must remain green and emit detailed JSONL.
- Web: a trace runner must replay the same golden traces and verify checksums.
- JSONL must conform to `tests/e2e/lib/e2e_jsonl_schema.json` (extend schema if needed, never break silently).
- Every run logs: run_id, build_id/git_sha, seed, size, caps/profile, perf counters, and checksums.

Acceptance Criteria
- A concrete test matrix mapping each user-facing feature to unit/property/fuzz/e2e coverage.
- CI hooks exist for: wasm build checks, proptest, fuzz smoke, trace replay, and checksum gates.
- A "never regress" list exists (copy/paste, selection, OSC8, resize, IME/composition, focus/mouse modes) with golden artifacts.
notes: Drafted docs/spec/frankenterm-correctness.md (invariants/proptest/fuzz/goldens + coverage matrix + CI hook checklist) and linked it from README Key Docs.

title: task(perf-rollout): script shadow, canary, fallback, and rollback drills for performance-sensitive changes
description:
Background:
A sound optimization program needs operational drills just as much as it needs benchmarks. When a performance change causes trouble, the team should know how to compare old and new behavior, canary the change, fall back, roll back, and preserve enough evidence to learn from the incident.

Goal:
Create the rollout-drill suite that operationalizes the performance evidence program.
design:
Work packages:
- Define the drill scenarios for shadow comparison, narrow canarying, fallback, rollback, and recovery after a failed optimization.
- Require each drill to emit structured evidence and clear operator guidance.
- Explain how these drills connect back to the evidence ledger and scorecard.
- Make sure the drills exercise real failure paths rather than only the clean success story.
- Capture what future operators should do when artifacts disagree or when tail monitors trip unexpectedly.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The project gains executable operational drills rather than aspirational prose.
2. The bead links rollout actions to the artifact contract and go/no-go policy cleanly.
3. Future self can understand not just what to do, but why each drill exists and what risk it is controlling.
4. The drill suite is incomplete without scripted end-to-end runs, operator-readable summaries, and detailed machine-readable logs/artifacts for shadow, canary, fallback, rollback, and recovery paths.

title: task(runtime-perf): build non-interference gauntlets for load, cancellation, shutdown, and terminal safety
description:
Background:
Runtime performance work is only a success if the user-facing semantics stay intact, especially around cancellation, shutdown, and terminal ownership. The project needs a dedicated gauntlet that proves performance work does not regress those properties under pressure.

Goal:
Create the runtime validation suite that enforces non-interference across the most failure-prone lifecycle edges.
design:
Work packages:
- Define gauntlet scenarios for load spikes, cancellation races, shutdown task draining, subscription churn, terminal-safety interactions, and adversarial challenge cases where runtime control policy is most likely to behave badly.
- Require focused unit/property tests for governor policy, hysteresis boundaries, and recovery semantics before E2E load scripts run.
- Require detailed logs and replay artifacts for failures so the team can tell whether the regression is semantic, scheduling, observability-related, degraded-mode UX related, or challenge-fixture fragility.
- Capture both correctness verdicts and performance metrics under the same scenarios.
- Explain what must remain invariant versus what can intentionally differ under a new control policy.
- Make the suite durable enough to guard future runtime changes beyond the first implementation wave.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Runtime optimization work gains a standing non-interference safety net with unit/property, integration, and scripted E2E stress coverage.
2. The bead clearly ties performance work back to user-visible correctness, degraded-mode clarity, and operator confidence.
3. Future implementers do not need an external plan to understand why these scenarios matter or what logs must be emitted.
4. The suite explicitly includes challenge and negative-control scenarios so runtime policy wins must survive more than idealized stress cases.
notes: This bead keeps the runtime lane honest by forcing it to prove that 'faster' did not quietly become 'weirder.'

title: task(doctor-perf): eliminate duplicate subprocess and comparison work in high-cost doctor paths
description:
Background:
Recent review work already showed how easy it is for capture/observe paths to duplicate app launches or split observation from the intended target. More broadly, doctor workflows can burn large amounts of time by redundantly launching, comparing, or re-deriving information that should be shared.

Goal:
Implement the first doctor optimization lever by removing provably redundant workflow work while preserving artifact quality and replayability.
design:
Work packages:
- Use the workflow cost map to identify the highest-value redundant subprocess or comparison patterns.
- Keep the implementation centered on one primary redundancy-elimination lever at a time.
- Require explicit reasoning about how the change preserves captured evidence, summary correctness, and replay commands.
- Define conservative fallback behavior when the deduplication conditions are not met.
- Record what before/after artifacts should prove the savings and the preserved semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The bead has a tight scope centered on removing redundant work, not broadly making doctor faster.
2. Evidence quality and replayability are explicit review criteria.
3. The task text gives future reviewers enough context to judge whether a proposed implementation stayed aligned with project goals.
4. The implementation is incomplete without focused unit/integration tests plus scripted failure-path E2E evidence and detailed logs proving when deduplication did or did not apply.
notes: This bead should favor clarity over cleverness. A slightly smaller win that preserves operator trust is better than an aggressive dedupe strategy that makes failures harder to understand.

title: task(perf-foundation): build deterministic macrobenchmark and replay fixture suites
description:
Background:
The program needs repeatable workloads that are representative of real use rather than tiny microbenchmarks. These fixtures should exercise render-heavy screens, runtime stress paths, and doctor workflows in ways that can be replayed consistently and compared across revisions.

Goal:
Create the canonical fixture suites and replay assets used by baseline capture, profiling, parity checks, and tail-latency gauntlets.
design:
Work packages:
- Translate the inventory bead into concrete fixture families for render, runtime, and doctor lanes.
- Partition fixtures into canonical regression suites and adversarial/challenge suites so the project gets both deterministic repeatability and robustness coverage.
- Ensure fixtures capture representative state transitions such as sparse updates, large invalidations, resize churn, subscription churn, cancellations, timeouts, degraded I/O, and artifact-heavy diagnostic runs.
- Define reproducibility rules: seeds, timing controls, host fingerprints, and fixture versioning.
- Specify artifact naming so baseline/profile/replay/challenge data can be compared over time.
- Include explicit notes on why each fixture exists, which user/operator pain it approximates, and whether it is expected to demonstrate wins, graceful fallback, or negative-control stability.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The project has deterministic fixtures that future performance work can reuse without reinventing workloads.
2. Each fixture is traceable to an explicit optimization question or invariant from the inventory bead.
3. Fixture metadata is rich enough to support profiling, shadow comparison, and later rollout scorecards.
4. The suite explicitly includes adversarial challenge fixtures and negative-control cases so optimizations cannot quietly overfit to a narrow curated benchmark set.
notes: Planning correction: the fixture layer now explicitly distinguishes canonical regression fixtures from challenge fixtures. That protects users from benchmark-specialized optimizations that would otherwise look excellent in curated runs but regress rarer real-world regimes.

title: task(perf-foundation): automate hotspot extraction across CPU, allocation, and syscall pressure
description:
Background:
Optimization choices should be driven by a ranked understanding of where time and resources are actually being spent. In FrankenTUI that likely spans CPU-heavy render code, allocation-heavy text/layout work, syscall-heavy presentation paths, and subprocess-heavy doctor workflows.

Goal:
Create the profiling and hotspot extraction lane that converts raw profiler output into a stable, comparable set of candidate bottlenecks.
design:
Work packages:
- Define profiling modes appropriate to the workspace: CPU, allocation, syscall, and workflow-level timing.
- Normalize profiler outputs into a common hotspot table with stage, location, percent contribution, and category labels.
- Require artifact linkage from hotspot records back to fixture IDs and baseline IDs.
- Document when hotspots are likely measurement artifacts versus genuine EV opportunities.

title: task(perf-foundation): define the comprehensive validation matrix and logging contract for performance work
description:
Background:
The current graph already includes several gauntlet and replay beads, but the validation obligations are still distributed across many tasks. That creates a planning risk: future implementation might satisfy local tests while missing the full matrix of unit, property, integration, E2E, soak, replay, and logging requirements that make performance work trustworthy.

Goal:
Define the canonical validation and logging matrix for the entire performance-control-plane program so every lane has explicit proof obligations and artifact expectations before implementation begins.
design:
Work packages:
- Map every performance lane and task class to the minimum required unit, property, integration, E2E, soak, replay, and shadow-comparison coverage.
- Reuse and align with existing observability/schema work so this matrix inherits stable IDs, event names, and failure-signature vocabulary rather than redefining them in parallel.
- Define the required logging schema for each layer, including stable IDs, reason codes, timing fields, mismatch categories, and replay pointers.
- Specify which tests are lane-local versus cross-lane, and which are gating versus informative.
- Require test scripts and gauntlets to emit human-readable summaries plus machine-readable artifact ledgers.
- Record failure-artifact standards so a broken optimization attempt is diagnosable without ad hoc debugging.
- Explicitly cover negative assertions and graceful-fallback cases so the matrix proves not only what should improve, but also what must not regress, what should remain stable, and what may intentionally degrade only within declared bounds.
- Require each lane to define minimum failure-forensics output, including how an operator distinguishes semantic regressions, observability gaps, benchmark overfitting, and expected challenge-fixture fallback behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Future implementers can read this bead alone and know the minimum validation and logging obligations for any performance change.
2. Unit/property tests and E2E/soak/replay scripts are all treated as first-class requirements, not optional extras.
3. The resulting matrix is detailed enough to drive the gauntlet, ledger, and scorecard beads directly.
4. The matrix is incomplete unless it explicitly covers negative assertions, graceful-fallback envelopes, challenge-fixture expectations, and lane-specific failure-forensics requirements.
notes: This bead exists because performance work often fails in the gaps between local tests and system-level reality. Making the full matrix explicit is cheaper than rediscovering those gaps during rollout. Planning refinement: the matrix now needs to define not just success evidence, but also how to prove that expected no-op behavior, bounded degradation, and failure diagnosis still work.
close_reason: Implemented validation_matrix.rs: 16 validation obligations across render/runtime/doctor/cross-lane with gating/informative classification, negative assertions, failure forensics, logging contracts with common fields + lane-specific events/reason codes, and 18 unit tests. Also fixed pre-existing clippy issues.

title: Mermaid Parser Core (Tokenizer + AST)
description:
Background
- We must parse Mermaid fenced blocks into a deterministic AST.
- Mermaid syntax varies by diagram type; a shared tokenizer + AST core prevents drift.

Scope
- Implement tokenizer: keywords, identifiers, arrows, brackets, directives, strings, comments.
- Parse Mermaid init directives (%%{init: {...}}%%) into AST nodes.
- Parse comments/annotations and ignore or retain for diagnostics.
- Build AST for all supported diagram types (flowchart, sequence, state, gantt, class, ER, mindmap, pie).
- Parse subgraph/cluster blocks and diagram direction directives.
- Parse styling directives (classDef/class/style/linkStyle) as AST nodes.
- Parse link/click directives into metadata (even if degraded at render).
- Robust error reporting with source spans (line/col) and expected tokens.
- Error recovery: resynchronize at line boundaries to continue AST build when possible.
- Deterministic normalization of whitespace + line endings.

Considerations
- Avoid parser generators unless already used; keep dependencies minimal.
- Avoid allocations in hot loops (use slices/indices).
- Parser must never panic on malformed input.

Tests / Validation
- Unit tests for lexing + parsing per diagram type.
- Golden AST fixtures for canonical samples.
- Error-case tests asserting span + error kind.
- Seeded fuzz tests for tokenizer + parser to ensure no panics.

Success Criteria
- AST captures nodes, edges, labels, directives, and diagram type.
- Parser errors are structured and location-aware; recovery yields partial AST when possible.
- Parser returns identical AST for semantically equivalent whitespace.
close_reason: Mermaid core parser: directives/comments/subgraph/style/link + error recovery + tests

Background:
doctor_frankentui spends time in orchestration, subprocess management, artifact generation, comparison, and reporting. Optimizing it effectively requires a workflow-level view of cost and redundancy, not just a list of hot functions.

title: Flaky test: inline_render_emits_tracing_span_fields races the tracing callsite interest cache under parallel runs
description: terminal_writer.rs test inline_render_emits_tracing_span_fields uses tracing::subscriber::set_default (thread-local dispatcher) but span callsite interest caches are process-global: when parallel tests register/unregister dispatchers concurrently, the info_span!("inline.render") callsite can be cached as not-enabled by a neighboring thread's state and the SpanChecker never sees new_span. Observed: fails ~1 in N in full multi-crate parallel runs (also the single failure in the 2026-07-07 round-5 combined run), passes in isolation and in per-suite runs. Fix options: call tracing::callsite::rebuild_interest_cache() after set_default in the test; or mark the test serial; or use a global subscriber guard shared by all tracing-dependent tests.

Process-global callsite interest is re-evaluated under the test's dispatcher instead of staying cached as not-enabled by a racing parallel test.

title: task(perf-rollout): define the unified performance evidence ledger and artifact contract
description:
Background:
By the time multiple optimization lanes are active, the project needs one place where baseline IDs, hotspot IDs, proof artifacts, replay commands, gauntlet runs, and rollout verdicts can be joined coherently. Without that, the optimization program will generate evidence faster than humans can understand it.

Goal:
Create the shared artifact contract and evidence ledger that all performance lanes feed into and all rollout decisions consume.
design:
Work packages:
- Define the canonical identifiers and file/report schema linking workflow inventory, baselines, profiles, proofs, implementations, gauntlets, rollout decisions, and validation-matrix outputs.
- Reuse and extend the existing artifact-manifest, retention, redaction, and failure-signature planning beads rather than inventing a second artifact vocabulary.
- Explain how render, runtime, and doctor artifacts map into the same ledger without losing lane-specific detail.
- Specify required versus optional fields so missing evidence becomes a visible defect.
- Include explicit schema for detailed logs: stable IDs, reason codes, mismatch classes, artifact references, and replay commands.
- Record how humans and CI should navigate from a failed verdict to the relevant artifacts and replay commands.
- Treat this bead as an early information-architecture contract: it should be definable before every artifact-producing implementation bead is complete, while still being rich enough to absorb their outputs later without churn.
acceptance_criteria:

description:
# v1 Definition of Done (Ship Checklist)

## Background
Plan Section 0.11 defines when ftui "v1" is done. This is the comprehensive checklist that must be completed before tagging v1.0.0.

## Definition of Done Criteria

### 1. Inline Mode Default is Stable
- [ ] Streaming logs + UI chrome does not corrupt scrollback
- [ ] Streaming logs + UI chrome does not corrupt cursor placement
- [ ] PTY tests confirm behavior on normal exit
- [ ] PTY tests confirm behavior on panic
- [ ] Tested on: Linux (xterm-like), macOS Terminal, tmux, screen
- [ ] No flicker under sustained log output
- [ ] Resize during logging re-anchors correctly

**Verified by:** bd-2gx Gate 1, bd-fbp, bd-10i.11.2

### 2. Diff/Presenter Correctness Validated
- [ ] Terminal-model tests for supported sequences pass
- [ ] Property tests with random buffers pass
- [ ] Output size baselines for representative workloads documented
- [ ] Style state never leaks across runs
- [ ] OSC 8 links properly managed (open/close)

**Verified by:** bd-2gx Gate 2, bd-10i.11.1, bd-10i.4.3

### 3. Unicode Width Correctness Proven
- [ ] Corpus tests cover ZWJ sequences
- [ ] Corpus tests cover emoji
- [ ] Corpus tests cover combining marks
- [ ] No off-by-one wrapping errors
- [ ] Truncation at correct grapheme boundaries

**Verified by:** bd-2gx Gate 3, bd-16k, bd-2uk

### 4. Style System is Deterministic and Documented
- [ ] Explicit masks documented
- [ ] Inheritance rules documented
- [ ] Style merge is deterministic (same input = same output)
- [ ] Theme resolution documented
- [ ] No "heisenbug" style flickers

**Verified by:** bd-10x, bd-22q

### 5. Runtime Supports Required Features
- [ ] update/view loop works

- [ ] Batch commands work

- [ ] Deterministic simulator works
- [ ] Snapshot tests work

**Verified by:** bd-10i.8.2, bd-10i.8.3

### 6. Core Widgets for Harness UIs Exist and Tested

### 8. Quality Gates Pass (All Four)

- [ ] Gate 4: Terminal cleanup

**Verified by:** bd-2gx

- [ ] Coverage meets thresholds
- [ ] Benchmarks run and tracked
- [ ] Release workflow configured
- [ ] Dependabot configured

**Verified by:** bd-xn2

## Ship Process
1. Create v1 tracking issue listing all criteria
2. Verify all beads above are closed
3. Run full test suite on all platforms
4. Update CHANGELOG.md with v1 release notes
5. Tag v1.0.0

title: task(runtime-perf): implement a conservative load governor with hysteresis and safe fallback modes
description:
Background:
A policy is only useful if it is compiled into runtime behavior that remains stable under noisy measurements and shifting loads. The runtime therefore needs a governor that changes behavior carefully, exposes its mode changes, and falls back safely rather than oscillating or hiding overload.

Goal:
Implement the first runtime load governor that applies the approved admission/coalescing policy under measured stress.
design:
Work packages:
- Turn the policy bead into concrete state transitions, thresholds, hysteresis, and logging.
- Ensure the governor announces mode changes, reasons, and fallback triggers in stable, replayable ways.
- Keep the implementation scoped to one primary control lever or one tightly coupled policy family.
- Define when the governor must defer to strict semantics rather than taking performance-saving action.
- Record what evidence must prove the governor improved behavior instead of merely hiding work.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The bead explains the intended runtime behavior under healthy, stressed, and fallback conditions clearly enough to review implementation against it.
2. Hysteresis and conservative fallback semantics are explicit.
3. The task stays within a single primary control objective rather than bundling multiple scheduler rewrites.
4. The implementation is not complete without focused unit/property tests, integration coverage, and scripted stress/E2E evidence showing user-visible degraded-mode and recovery semantics.
notes: The core risk is an unstable controller that makes the runtime less predictable. This bead therefore treats observability and fallback as part of the functionality, not an afterthought.
