title: write_log OverlayRedraw cannot scroll: bottom-anchor overwrites one row; top-anchor pushes UI rows into scrollback
description: Found by exploration-audit round 5 (terminal_writer.rs review). In OverlayRedraw strategy (basic terminals AND all mux environments incl. tmux), position_cursor_for_log (terminal_writer.rs ~2165-2188) parks the cursor at the bottom of the LOGICAL log region (term_height - ui_height) with no scroll region active. Bottom anchor: an LF there just moves down, so every subsequent write_log repositions to the SAME row and overwrites the previous log line (no EL first, so shorter lines leave remnants: 'okarting build...'); logs never reach scrollback, contradicting the module contract ('logs scroll normally above'). Top anchor: log_row = term_height IS the screen bottom, so each text\r\n scrolls the WHOLE screen (no DECSTBM), pushing a copy of the UI's top row into scrollback per log line. Test write_log_multiple_writes_position_each_time pins repositioning but not accumulation. Fix needs design: overlay-mode log scroll semantics without DECSTBM (options: whole-screen scroll + repaint with scrollback-safe LF at bottom row; or emit EL before each line as a minimum honesty fix). Related: bd for InlineAuto remeasure log race.
close_reason: Fixed: overlay-mode write_log never emits unscoped LF (root cause of both overwrite-remnants and top-anchor UI-scroll corruption); emits SAVE+CUP+EL+width-clamped-single-line+RESTORE anchored one row above the uppermost of displayed/pending regions. Scroll-region path unchanged (DECSTBM accumulation into scrollback preserved). Regression tests: overlay_write_log_emits_single_erased_line_no_lf, overlay_top_anchor_write_log_never_scrolls, overlay_write_log_clamps_to_terminal_width.

title: task(doctor-perf): optimize artifact manifests, replay helpers, and evidence economy without weakening triage
description:
Background:
Doctor workflows can become expensive not only because they run too much code, but also because they emit bulky, repetitive, or poorly structured artifacts. The right goal is not to minimize artifacts indiscriminately; it is to make each emitted artifact earn its place by improving replay, triage, or operator comprehension.

Goal:
Refine the artifact contract so doctor outputs stay rich and useful while avoiding wasteful duplication and confusion.
design:
Work packages:
- Identify artifact classes that are redundant, overly verbose, or hard to navigate.
- Define the minimum artifact set that still supports replay, triage, comparison, and operator explanation.
- Preserve or improve summary, manifest, and helper quality even when volume is reduced.
- Explain how artifact changes should be validated against failure and replay workflows, not just happy-path runs.
- Make clear how this work interacts with CI artifact contracts and future rollout scorecards.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The bead defines evidence economy in a way future implementers can apply without consulting a separate document.
2. Artifact reductions are justified in terms of preserved or improved operator value.
3. The task leaves room for rich failure evidence while removing wasteful duplication.
4. The implementation must include unit/integration coverage, replay/E2E artifact validation, and detailed logging showing why each artifact class was kept, changed, or omitted.
notes: The danger here is optimizing for smaller output instead of better evidence. The bead text intentionally pushes back on that failure mode.

title: Sub-Cell Canvas Diagram Rendering
description:
## Goal
Render Mermaid diagrams using FrankenTUI's existing Canvas system (Braille 2×4, Block 2×2, HalfBlock 1×2) instead of cell-by-cell line-drawing characters. This gives 2-8x spatial resolution, enabling smooth diagonal edges, recognizable geometric shapes (real circles/diamonds/hexagons), proper arrowhead triangles, and filled regions.

## Why This Is Transformative
- The Canvas system ALREADY EXISTS (canvas.rs) with Painter, line/circle/rect/fill primitives, and 3 rendering modes.
- Currently the mermaid renderer writes line-drawing chars one cell at a time — max 1:1 pixel resolution.
- Sub-cell rendering turns diagrams from "ASCII art" to "terminal graphics" — a qualitative visual leap.
- Naturally solves shape rendering (circles become actual circles in Braille mode).
- Solves curved edges for free (Painter draws lines at arbitrary angles).
- Deterministic (no floating-point variance), fits FrankenTUI's correctness philosophy.

## Implementation Strategy
1. Add CanvasMermaidRenderer alongside existing cell-based MermaidRenderer in mermaid_render.rs.
2. Reuse Viewport transform (layout coords → canvas coords).
3. Use Painter for: filled rects (nodes), lines (edges), circles (round nodes), polygons (diamonds/hexagons), triangles (arrowheads).

- Arrowheads are triangular, not just > characters.
- Node shapes (circle, diamond, hexagon, etc.) are geometrically correct.

description:
## What
Implement Canvas-based rendering for all 8 NodeShape variants using Painter primitives from canvas.rs.

## Shape Mapping
- Rect → Painter::rect (filled rectangle with border)
- Rounded → Painter::rect with corner radius (approximate with arcs or short diagonals)
- Stadium → Painter::rect with semicircle ends (half-circles at left/right)
- Subroutine → Double-bordered rect (two nested rectangles)
- Diamond → Painter polygon: 4 vertices at (cx, top), (right, cy), (cx, bottom), (left, cy)
- Hexagon → Painter polygon: 6 vertices (flat-top or pointy-top orientation)
- Circle → Painter::circle centered on node, radius = min(width, height) / 2
- Asymmetric → Painter polygon: flag shape (rect with pointed right side)

## Implementation Details
- Each shape gets a dedicated fn: canvas_draw_rect, canvas_draw_diamond, canvas_draw_circle, etc.
- Fill interior with node's theme background color via Painter::fill
- Draw border in node's theme border color via Painter::line or Painter::polygon
- Scale from layout units to canvas pixel coordinates via Viewport transform
- Padding between border and label text must account for shape geometry (diamond has less usable interior than rect)

description:
## What
Composite text labels (node labels, edge labels, cluster titles) on top of canvas-rendered shapes. Canvas draws geometry in sub-cell dots; text must be rendered in the cell layer on top.

## Implementation
- Canvas rendering writes to a CanvasLayer (Braille/Block/HalfBlock dots).
- Text rendering writes to the Buffer cell layer (standard Cell writes).
- When compositing: cells with text take priority over canvas dots in the same cell. This is how canvas.rs already works — Painter writes to a separate pixel grid that gets merged into Buffer cells, and explicit cell writes override.
- Center node labels within the shape's usable interior area (accounting for shape geometry — diamond has triangular corners, circle has curved edges).
- Edge labels: position at midpoint of edge, write text centered.
- Wrap long labels using existing wrap_text function.

## Key Design Decision
- Do NOT try to render text as Braille dots. Cell-based text is always more readable.
- Background color under text should match the node fill for readability.

description:
## What
Render arrowheads as filled triangles at edge endpoints using Painter polygon fill, instead of '>' / '<' / 'v' / '^' characters.

title: Implement ASCII width fast-path optimization
description:
# Implement ASCII Width Fast-Path Optimization

## Background
The plan emphasizes that ASCII must dominate common workloads:
- Section 0.12: "ASCII fast-path must remain allocation-free and dominate common workloads"
- Section 4.3: ASCII width is a major optimization opportunity

Most harness/log output is ASCII. For ASCII:
- display width == byte length
- no grapheme segmentation needed
- no Unicode tables needed

## Scope
- Provide a fast, allocation-free `ascii_width` / `display_width` helper.
- Integrate it into text measurement / wrapping / truncation hot paths.

## Design
### Core API
```rust
/// Returns Some(width) if s is pure ASCII; otherwise None.
#[inline]
pub fn ascii_width(s: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    let bytes = s.as_bytes();
    if bytes.iter().all(|&b| b < 0x80) {
        Some(bytes.len())
    } else {
        None
    }
}

#[inline]
pub fn display_width(s: &str) -> usize {
    ascii_width(s).unwrap_or_else(|| unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr::width(s))
}
```

### Performance notes
- ASCII detection is O(n) but extremely cheap (tight loop over bytes).
- Optional micro-optimizations (still safe): use `memchr` or portable SIMD via `std::simd` if available.
- **Repo policy: unsafe is forbidden**, so any SIMD path must be safe or it is out of scope.

## Integration points
- Segment/Text measurement
- Wrapping/truncation (byte-fast for ASCII)
- Viewport/log viewer rendering

## Tests
- Pure ASCII returns correct width
- Mixed ASCII/Unicode returns None from `ascii_width`
- Empty string returns Some(0)
- Integration tests: wrapping/truncation correctness unchanged

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ascii_width` and `display_width` exist.
- [ ] ASCII path is allocation-free.
- [ ] Non-ASCII path matches `unicode_width`.
- [ ] Integrated into the ftui-text measurement code paths.

title: feature(doctor-perf): optimize doctor_frankentui orchestration and evidence economy
description:
Background:
doctor_frankentui is both a performance consumer and a confidence engine. It launches subprocesses, captures evidence, writes artifacts, and helps operators understand failures. Performance work here must therefore reduce redundant work without weakening evidence quality or replayability.

Goal:
Profile and optimize the most expensive doctor workflows while preserving or improving the quality of summaries, manifests, replay helpers, and failure triage artifacts.
design:
Feature scope:
- Profile workflow-level cost centers across capture, replay, report, and failure handling.
- Remove duplicate subprocess, artifact, and comparison work.
- Tighten artifact contracts so evidence stays rich but no longer bloated or repetitive.
- Validate with soak, shadow, and deterministic replay suites.

Guiding principle:
The output of doctor work must stay useful to humans during failure, not merely become cheaper to compute.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Optimization decisions are grounded in workflow-level evidence rather than isolated function timings.
2. Artifact quality, replayability, and operator clarity remain first-class acceptance criteria.
3. The resulting doctor lane improves both throughput and the usability of failure evidence.
4. The lane is incomplete without focused unit/integration coverage, scripted failure-path and soak E2E runs, and detailed logging/manifests that explain every mismatch or fallback.
notes: Doctor work is easy to accidentally optimize in the wrong direction by deleting valuable evidence or making failure modes less intelligible. The bead text therefore makes evidence economy, not artifact austerity, the target.
close_reason: Feature verified: all 4 children shipped and in-tree — bd-qbbkv doctor_cost_profile.rs 5-stage workflow cost model (+ e2e), bd-mn4a0 deduplicated suite/report run_meta loading with proof logs, bd-tsgb4 run artifact manifests + replay helpers (19 refs in report.rs), bd-zmcvz shadow-comparison suite + CI artifact map. Evidence economy preserved: manifests/replay/triage artifacts are richer, not thinner (doctor E2E artifact contract in CI)

title: Text Effects: Character Reveal Modes
description:
## Background
The typewriter effect is limited to left-to-right reveal. A comprehensive reveal system enables dramatic text appearances for titles, announcements, and onboarding.

## Implementation

Add RevealMode enum (used as parameter, not nested in TextEffect):
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub enum RevealMode {
    #[default]
    LeftToRight,    // Classic typewriter
    RightToLeft,    // Reverse typewriter  
    CenterOut,      // Expand from middle
    EdgesIn,        // Converge to center
    Random,         // Random order (deterministic with seed)
    ByWord,         // Word at a time
    ByLine,         // Line at a time (for multi-line)
}
```

Add TextEffect variant (consistent structure with others):
```rust
TextEffect::Reveal {
    mode: RevealMode,
    progress: f64,      // 0.0 = hidden, 1.0 = fully revealed
    seed: u64,          // For Random mode determinism
}

// Separate variant for gradient mask (different parameters)
TextEffect::RevealMask {
    angle: f64,         // Sweep angle in degrees (0 = left-to-right)
    progress: f64,      // Mask position 0.0-1.0
    softness: f64,      // Edge softness 0.0 (hard) to 1.0 (gradient)
}
```

### Visibility Calculation by Mode:

| Mode | Visible When |
|------|--------------|
| LeftToRight | char_idx < progress * total_chars |
| RightToLeft | char_idx >= (1-progress) * total_chars |
| CenterOut | distance_from_center < progress * max_distance |
| EdgesIn | distance_from_edge < progress * max_distance |
| Random | hash(seed, idx) < progress * total_chars |
| ByWord | word_idx < progress * total_words |
| ByLine | line_idx < progress * total_lines |
| RevealMask | rotated_position > threshold (with softness fade) |

### Usage:
```rust
// Simple left-to-right reveal
StyledText::new("Hello World")
    .effect(TextEffect::Reveal { 
        mode: RevealMode::LeftToRight, 
        progress: 0.5,
        seed: 0,
    })

// Dramatic gradient mask sweep
StyledText::new("WELCOME")
    .effect(TextEffect::RevealMask {
        angle: 45.0,
        progress: 0.5,
        softness: 0.3,
    })
```

## Files

## Unit Tests (REQUIRED)
- test_reveal_ltr_first_chars_first: progress=0.5 shows first half
- test_reveal_rtl_last_chars_first: progress=0.5 shows last half

- test_reveal_edges_in_edges_first: Edge chars visible first
- test_reveal_random_deterministic: Same seed = same reveal order
- test_reveal_random_all_chars_reveal: progress=1 shows all
- test_reveal_by_word_whole_words: Partial progress shows complete words
- test_reveal_by_line_whole_lines: Lines reveal atomically
- test_reveal_mask_angle_0: Left-to-right sweep
- test_reveal_mask_angle_90: Top-to-bottom sweep  
- test_reveal_mask_softness_0: Hard edge (binary visible/hidden)
- test_reveal_mask_softness_1: Gradient fade across chars

title: task(render-perf): map the end-to-end cost surface of view -> buffer -> diff -> present -> write
description:
Background:
The render pipeline is where the clean architectural seams offer the biggest opportunity, but we need to know which stages dominate under which fixtures before deciding whether to target view invalidation, buffer writes, diff work, presenter state churn, or terminal writes.

Goal:
Produce the definitive stage-level render cost map that informs every later render optimization bead.
design:
Work packages:
- Reuse the existing reusable-buffer diff+present macrobenchmark work for demo screens as the seed benchmark path rather than creating a separate render benchmark universe.
- Break down render costs by stage, workload, and update shape.
- Track not only wall-clock time but also touched cells, changed regions, emitted bytes, and other stage-relevant counters.
- Identify workload classes where sparse-change assumptions hold and those where they fail.
- Highlight whether average cost or tail spikes are the bigger problem in each stage.
- Explain which findings point toward work-elimination opportunities versus low-level inner-loop tuning.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Later render beads can cite a concrete cost map instead of guessing which stage matters most.\n2. The bead explicitly distinguishes scenarios where skip certificates are likely high-EV from scenarios where they are not.\n3. The resulting analysis is detailed enough to justify prioritization between diff, presenter, and cache-related work.
notes: This bead is where render optimization stops being generic advice and becomes FrankenTUI-specific engineering.
close_reason: Implemented cost_surface.rs: CostSurfaceAnalyzer maps render pipeline stages (CellMutation, BufferDiff, PresenterEmit, FramePipeline) from BaselineRecord, computing pipeline fractions, tail ratios, skip-certificate EV, dominance detection, primary concern classification, and CostComparison for cross-fixture dominance shift analysis. 13 unit tests.

title: Demo Showcase: Theme Studio / Live Palette Editor
description:
## Background

Themes are the fastest way to make a TUI feel "impossibly premium". FrankenTUI already has:
- a semantic token system (fg/bg/accent/status/priority)
- alpha-aware overlays
- WCAG-aware contrast helpers

This screen turns the theme engine into an interactive instrument:
- inspect presets
- edit palette values live
- validate contrast
- export for real terminal emulators

## UX / Core Interactions

- Preset list (Cyberpunk Aurora, Darcula, Lumen Light, Nordic Frost, plus any future presets).
- Token inspector:
  - show each semantic token swatch
  - show computed contrast ratio for fg/bg pairs
- Live editor:
  - adjust hue/chroma/lightness or RGB
  - lock constraints (e.g., "keep WCAG AA")
  - preview immediately across the app

Suggested keybindings:
- Ctrl+T: cycle presets (global convention)
- Enter: edit selected token
- Esc: cancel edit
- E: export

## Export Targets (Impressive + Practical)

- Export current theme to:
  - FrankenTUI theme JSON (for reproducible bug reports)
  - Ghostty theme config snippet (user-visible win)
  - optional: other formats later

## Architecture Notes

- Core theme logic must live in library code (ftui-style / ftui-extras::theme), not in the demo.
- Theme Studio is a UI over that API.
- Cache derived semantic styles (semantic swatches) per theme to keep toggles O(1).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Live updates are immediate (no restart) and deterministic.
- Contrast validation is shown in the UI and enforced in tests.
- Export produces stable output with a versioned schema.

Additionally (project-wide standards):
- Alien Artifact: define invariants + failure modes; if heuristics exist, specify an explainable decision rule (evidence ledger / Bayes factors where applicable)
- Extreme Optimization: baseline -> profile -> opportunity matrix; for each perf change include an isomorphism proof + golden output checksums
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures; add property tests for core invariants where applicable
- E2E: scripts with verbose JSONL logging (env, capabilities, timings, seed, checksums) + deterministic mode
- Visual rigor: enforce contrast bounds + deterministic rendering under fixed seeds; include snapshot fixtures and log theme IDs

## Alien Artifact Upgrades (Concrete)

- Constraint-based palette editing:
  - treat "edit a token" as a constrained optimization problem in perceptual space (OKLCH)
  - enforce minimum contrast constraints while minimizing perceptual delta from the user's intent
  - surface a tiny evidence ledger when the solver adjusts the requested color

## Extreme Optimization

- Theme switching and editing must not allocate on the hot path.
- Add a toggle-latency regression test (bd-vu0o.2).

title: Comprehensive Unit Test Suite with Detailed Logging
description:
# Comprehensive Unit Test Suite with Detailed Logging

## Background
Plan Section 13.1 requires property tests and unit tests for all kernel components. The user specifically requested "comprehensive unit tests and e2e test scripts with great, detailed logging so we can be sure that everything is working perfectly after implementation."

## Scope
Every module in ftui must have a corresponding test module with:
1. Unit tests for all public APIs
2. Property tests for invariant preservation
3. Detailed logging of test execution for debugging

## Test Logging Requirements
All tests MUST use structured logging (tracing) with:
- Test name and module path
- Input parameters (for property tests, show the generated inputs)
- Expected vs actual values on failure
- Timing information for performance-sensitive code
- Stack traces on failure

## Per-Module Test Coverage (MANDATORY)

### ftui-core Tests
- [ ] TerminalSession: enter/exit raw mode, panic cleanup, mode tracking
- [ ] TerminalCapabilities: detection from environment variables
- [ ] Event types: serialization, comparison, conversion from backend

### ftui-render Tests
- [ ] Cell: 16-byte layout assertion, bits_eq correctness
- [ ] CellContent: char encoding, grapheme encoding, width calculation
- [ ] PackedRgba: RGBA packing, Porter-Duff over operation, opacity
- [ ] CellAttrs: flag packing, link ID encoding
- [ ] Buffer: bounds checking, scissor stack invariants, opacity stack invariants
- [ ] GraphemePool: intern/lookup, refcount correctness, slot reuse
- [ ] LinkRegistry: register/lookup, deduplication
- [ ] BufferDiff: change detection, run grouping correctness
- [ ] Presenter: ANSI output correctness, style tracking, link handling

### ftui-style Tests
- [ ] Style: merge semantics, mask handling, property inheritance
- [ ] Color: parsing, downgrade (truecolor→256→16→mono)
- [ ] Theme: slot resolution, preset correctness

### ftui-text Tests
- [ ] Text/Span: construction, styling, width measurement
- [ ] Wrapping: word wrap, character wrap, no mid-grapheme breaks
- [ ] Truncation: ellipsis placement, width correctness
- [ ] Measurement: min/max width calculation

### ftui-layout Tests
- [ ] Rect: intersection, containment, inner margin
- [ ] Sides: CSS-like tuple conversion
- [ ] Layout algorithms: flex, grid constraints

### ftui-runtime Tests
- [ ] Program: event dispatch, command handling
- [ ] Cmd: batch, sequence, tick scheduling
- [ ] Simulator: deterministic replay, snapshot capture

## Test Harness Requirements

### Logging Setup
```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use tracing::{info, debug, error};
    use tracing_test::traced_test;
    
    #[traced_test]
    #[test]
    fn test_cell_bits_eq() {
        info\!("Testing Cell::bits_eq with identical cells");
        let cell_a = Cell::new('A', Style::default());
        let cell_b = Cell::new('A', Style::default());
        debug\!(cell_a = ?cell_a, cell_b = ?cell_b, "Comparing cells");
        assert\!(cell_a.bits_eq(&cell_b), "Identical cells should be equal");
        info\!("Cell bits_eq test passed");
    }
}
```

### Property Test Logging
```rust
#[cfg(test)]
proptest\! {
    #[test]
    fn buffer_diff_roundtrip(buffer1 in arb_buffer(80, 24), buffer2 in arb_buffer(80, 24)) {
        info\!(width = 80, height = 24, "Property test: buffer diff roundtrip");
        debug\!(buffer1_hash = ?hash(&buffer1), buffer2_hash = ?hash(&buffer2), "Input buffers");
        
        let diff = BufferDiff::compute(&buffer1, &buffer2);
        info\!(change_count = diff.len(), "Diff computed");
        
        // Apply diff and verify
        let mut result = buffer1.clone();
        apply_diff(&mut result, &buffer2, &diff);
        
        for y in 0..24 {
            for x in 0..80 {
                prop_assert_eq\!(
                    result.get(x, y), buffer2.get(x, y),
                    "Cell mismatch at ({}, {})", x, y
                );
            }
        }
        info\!("Property test passed");
    }
}
```

## Test Categories with Counts

| Module | Min Test Count | Notes |
|--------|----------------|-------|
| Cell/CellContent | 15+ | Layout, encoding, width |
| Buffer | 20+ | Bounds, scissor, opacity, clear |
| GraphemePool | 10+ | Intern, refcount, reuse |
| BufferDiff | 15+ | Detection, runs, edge cases |
| Presenter | 25+ | All ANSI sequences, state tracking |
| InputParser | 30+ | All key codes, mouse, paste |
| Style | 15+ | Merge, mask, inheritance |
| Text | 20+ | Width, wrap, truncate |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every public API has at least one test
- [ ] Property tests cover all invariants from plan Section 2.3
- [ ] All tests use tracing for logging
- [ ] Test output includes timing information
- [ ] cargo test --all produces clear, structured output
- [ ] Test coverage > 80% for kernel crates

## Dependencies
- Requires: bd-10i.3 (Phase 1 types exist)
- Blocks: bd-2gx (Quality Gates)

## Test Framework Stack
- Unit tests: built-in #[test]
- Property tests: proptest
- Logging: tracing + tracing-test
- Coverage: cargo-llvm-cov
- Timing: criterion for perf-sensitive

## CI Requirements
- All tests run on every PR
- Test failure shows full log output
- Coverage report generated
- Test timing tracked for regression

title: Gradients: LUT + Memoization + SIMD Hot Path
description:
## Goal
Make gradient sampling effectively free at render time using precomputed lookup tables and tight hot paths.

## Core Idea (Extreme Optimization)
- Precompute t values per row/col and store in SmallVec or Vec<u16> (fixed-point).
- Precompute gradient samples into a LUT keyed by (gradient_id, size, mode).
- Use SIMD-friendly loops for applying sampled colors to glyph runs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Per-character gradient sampling is O(1) with no trig or division in hot path.
- LUT reuse across frames when size/gradient unchanged.
- No allocations during steady-state rendering.

## Tests (REQUIRED)
- unit_lut_reuse_same_size: cache hit for same dimensions.
- unit_lut_invalidate_resize: cache miss on size change.
- unit_fixed_point_accuracy: fixed-point t within epsilon of float.
- perf_gradient_hotpath: measure p50/p95 vs baseline; include logs.

## Isomorphism Proof
- Output colors identical to reference float implementation (golden checksums).

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.


## Testing Plan
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures.
- Property tests: invariants (idempotence, monotonicity, determinism) where applicable.
- Fuzz tests: parsers/state machines and any input-facing logic.
- Determinism: fixed seeds/time-freeze; snapshot fixtures must be stable.


## E2E Plan
- Provide/extend an E2E script that exercises the feature end-to-end in PTY (where applicable).
- Logging: verbose JSONL with env/capabilities + per-step timings + seed + checksums; include a summary at end.
- On failure: print reproduction command and point to artifacts directory.
close_reason: Implemented gradient LUT optimization with O(1) sampling, fixed-point t-value caching, binary search for stop lookup, and batch sampling methods. All unit tests pass.

title: Interactive Diagram Node Navigation + Edge Highlighting
description:
## Goal
Add keyboard-driven navigation within rendered Mermaid diagrams. Users can select nodes, follow edges, and see connection details — turning diagrams from static pictures into navigable data structures.

## Why This Matters
- Leans into FrankenTUI's terminal-native advantage: interactivity that a static PNG cannot provide.
- The demo-showcase already has keybinding framework, metrics panel, and sample navigation.
- Directly useful for debugging/ops: "show me the service dependency graph and let me Tab through it."
- Makes large diagrams actually useful — you can explore them instead of just squinting.

## Features
1. Node Selection: Tab/Shift-Tab cycles through nodes in layout order (left→right, top→bottom). Selected node gets highlighted border (accent color) + optional glow effect.
2. Edge Following: Arrow keys move to connected node in spatial direction. Left/Right follow edges horizontally. Up/Down follow edges vertically. If multiple neighbors in that direction, choose nearest.
3. Edge Highlighting: When a node is selected, all edges connected to it render in accent color. Incoming edges: one color. Outgoing edges: another.
4. Detail Panel: When a node is selected, show in a side panel: node ID, label, shape type, cluster membership, incoming edge count + labels, outgoing edge count + labels.
5. Search: / opens search bar, type to filter nodes by label. n/N cycles through matches. Esc clears search.
6. Deselection: Esc deselects current node (returns to normal view).

## State Tracking
- selected_node: Option<IrNodeId> in MermaidShowcaseState
- search_query: Option<String>
- search_matches: Vec<IrNodeId>
- Build adjacency lookup from IR edges on each diagram change

## Files to Modify
- crates/ftui-demo-showcase/src/screens/mermaid_showcase.rs (navigation state + keybindings)
- crates/ftui-extras/src/mermaid_render.rs (highlight rendering for selected node/edges)

## Tests
- Unit: Tab cycles through nodes in correct order
- Unit: arrow-key navigation follows correct edges
- Unit: search finds matching nodes
- Snapshot: diagram with selected node + highlighted edges

title: Harden VS16 emoji width handling — edge case tests and documentation
description:
## Context

A recent audit incorrectly reported that VS16/FE0F emoji width stripping was never implemented. Investigation reveals this is FALSE — the fix IS implemented and working:

- strip_vs16() at crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs:138-147 strips U+FE0F before width calculation
- grapheme_width() at lines 224-234 applies stripping when trust_vs16_width() is false
- trust_vs16_width() at lines 105-119 defaults to false (terminal-realistic mode)
- Comprehensive tests exist in crates/ftui-text/tests/unicode_width_corpus.rs (lines 236-279, 583-612)
- FTUI_EMOJI_VS16_WIDTH=unicode opt-in for terminals that correctly render VS16 as width 2

## Task: Hardening and Documentation

Since VS16 handling works correctly, this bead focuses on:
1. Documentation to prevent future audit false negatives
2. Edge case tests for unusual emoji sequences
3. Cache behavior verification

### 1. Document VS16 Behavior in Crate Docs
Add a "## Emoji Width Handling" section to ftui-core module docs explaining:
- Default behavior (strip VS16, text-default emoji at width 1)
- FTUI_EMOJI_VS16_WIDTH=unicode opt-in
- Which emoji are affected (text-default + VS16)
- Why the default is width=1 (most terminals render this way)

### 2. Edge Case Tests (12 new tests)

**Keycap and flag sequences (3 tests):**
1. Keycap: "#\u{FE0F}\u{20E3}" — should be width 2 (fully qualified keycap)
2. Flag sequence: "\u{1F1FA}\u{1F1F8}" (US flag) — should be width 2
3. Tag sequence: "\u{1F3F4}\u{E0067}\u{E0062}\u{E0065}\u{E006E}\u{E0067}\u{E007F}" (England flag) — width 2

**ZWJ sequences (3 tests):**
4. Family ZWJ: "\u{1F468}\u{200D}\u{1F469}\u{200D}\u{1F467}" — width 2
5. Skin tone + ZWJ: "\u{1F469}\u{1F3FD}\u{200D}\u{2764}\u{FE0F}\u{200D}\u{1F468}\u{1F3FB}" — width 2
6. Professional ZWJ: "\u{1F469}\u{200D}\u{1F52C}" (woman scientist) — width 2

**Skin tone with VS16 (2 tests):**
7. Victory hand + skin tone + VS16: "\u{270C}\u{1F3FD}\u{FE0F}" — width 2
8. Writing hand + skin tone: "\u{270D}\u{1F3FB}" — width 2

**Degenerate inputs (4 tests):**
9. Lone U+FE0F (bare VS16) — width 0 or 1 (must not panic)
10. Multiple consecutive VS16: "\u{2764}\u{FE0F}\u{FE0F}" — width 1 (extra VS16 stripped)
11. VS15 (text presentation): "\u{2764}\u{FE0E}" — width 1
12. Mixed VS15 and VS16: "\u{2764}\u{FE0E}\u{FE0F}" — must not panic, width 1

### 3. Cache Behavior Documentation
WidthCache in crates/ftui-text/src/width_cache.rs caches computed widths. Verify and document:
- OnceLock reads FTUI_EMOJI_VS16_WIDTH once at first access
- Cache keys are the grapheme string itself (policy is global)
- Document: "VS16 policy is read once at startup via OnceLock. Changing the env var mid-process has no effect."

## Key Files
- crates/ftui-core/src/lib.rs — lines 105-147, 211-236
- crates/ftui-text/tests/unicode_width_corpus.rs — existing tests + new edge cases
- crates/ftui-text/src/width_cache.rs — cache implementation

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 12 new edge case tests pass
- Rustdoc section added to ftui-core
- Cache behavior documented in code comments
- Zero regressions in existing 600+ line unicode width test corpus
- No panics on any degenerate input

title: Create CI/CD pipeline configuration
description:
INFRASTRUCTURE - CI/CD PIPELINE

## Background
Continuous integration ensures code quality, test coverage, and performance budgets are maintained. Must run on every PR and push to main.

## Technical Requirements

### GitHub Actions Workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml)

#### Jobs Overview
| Job | Trigger | Purpose | Blocking |
|-----|---------|---------|----------|
| check | PR, push | Format, clippy, tests | Yes |
| coverage | PR, push | Coverage thresholds | Yes |
| benchmarks | push to main | Performance budgets | Warn |
| e2e | PR, push | End-to-end tests | Yes |
| docs | PR, push | Doc build verification | Yes |

#### Check Job
- cargo fmt --check
- cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
- cargo test --all-features
- cargo test --no-default-features

#### Coverage Job
- Use cargo-llvm-cov for coverage
- Thresholds:
  - Overall: ≥ 70%
  - ftui-core: ≥ 80%
  - ftui-render: ≥ 75%
- Upload to codecov.io

#### Benchmarks Job
- Run on push to main only
- Performance budgets from plan:
  - Cell comparison: < 1ns
  - Present (80×24, 5% changed): p50 < 1.0ms
  - Diff scan: < 100µs
  - Layout solve (20 items): < 100µs
- Fail on 2x regression

#### E2E Job
- Run scripts/e2e_test.sh

title: task(graveyard-§7.2): Cache-Oblivious data structures for layout
description:
Apply cache-oblivious data structure principles to the layout engine widget tree traversal, ensuring optimal cache utilization regardless of cache hierarchy parameters (L1/L2/L3 sizes).

## Graveyard Entry

Section 7.2 -- Cache-Oblivious Data Structures
Priority: 3

## Background and Math Foundations

Cache-oblivious algorithms (Frigo et al. 1999) achieve optimal cache performance without knowing cache parameters. The key technique is the van Emde Boas layout for trees:
- Instead of storing a tree in BFS or DFS order in memory
- Store it in a recursive layout: top half of tree, then recursively each subtree
- This ensures that for ANY cache line size B, O(log_B(n)) cache misses per root-to-leaf path
- Compared to O(log(n)) cache misses for naive pointer-based trees

For FrankenTUI widget tree:
- Layout traversal visits every widget (DFS pre-order)
- With pointer-based tree: each node is a separate allocation, causing cache misses
- With van Emde Boas layout: related nodes are adjacent in memory, minimizing cache misses
- Expected improvement: 2-5x for large widget trees (>1000 nodes) where tree spills L2 cache

Implementation approach:
- Flatten widget tree into contiguous Vec using van Emde Boas layout
- Maintain index mapping: widget_id to position in flattened array
- Rebuild layout on tree structure change (amortized over many frames)
- Layout traversal becomes a sequential memory scan (cache-friendly)

## Structured Logging

All tests and benchmarks must emit structured JSONL evidence:
- op: veb_build, node_count, build_time_ns, memory_bytes
- op: veb_traverse, node_count, cache_misses_l1, cache_misses_l2, traverse_time_ns
- op: veb_rebuild, structural_changes, rebuild_time_ns, amortized_cost_ns
- op: veb_vs_pointer, node_count, veb_time_ns, pointer_time_ns, speedup_ratio

## Acceptance Criteria

1. van Emde Boas layout implementation for widget trees
2. Index mapping for O(1) widget lookup by ID
3. Rebuild cost amortized (only on structural changes)
4. Benchmark: cache miss comparison via perf stat (pointer vs flat vs vEB)
5. Benchmark: layout traversal time at 100, 1K, 10K widgets
6. Property test: layout results identical regardless of memory layout
7. All tests emit structured JSONL logs for evidence-ledger integration
8. CI artifacts: cache-miss comparison report, traversal-time trend data
close_reason: done

title: Keybinding Hints: Utility-Based Ranking (Bayes + VOI)
description:
## Goal
Prioritize which shortcuts to show so users see the most valuable hints first without clutter.

## Core Idea (Alien Artifact)
Treat each hint as an action with uncertain utility U and cost C (screen space + attention). Maintain a Bayesian posterior over utility from observed usage and context, then rank by expected value of information (VOI):
- Posterior mean: E[U_i | data]
- Expected net value: V_i = E[U_i] - lambda * C_i
- Optional VOI: prioritize hints whose exposure is expected to reduce uncertainty the most for new users.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Ranking is stable under small usage changes (no flicker).
- Deterministic under fixed seed and usage log.
- Supports a "debug" view showing evidence ledger and scores.

## Implementation Notes
- Use Beta-Bernoulli or Normal-Normal depending on usage signal.
- Context features: focused widget, recent command history, mode (insert/normal), and user profile.
- Provide fallback: static ordering if usage data absent.

## Tests (REQUIRED)
- unit_prior_updates: posterior updates with usage events.
- unit_ranking_stability: small deltas do not reorder beyond hysteresis.
- property_context_switch: ranking changes only when context changes.
- e2e_usage_replay: deterministic ranking across runs; log evidence ledger.

## E2E (REQUIRED)
- PTY script: simulate usage events and verify top-N hints and scores.
- Log: posterior parameters, E[U], C, VOI, final rank.

## Alien Artifact Upgrades
- Model the core decision(s) with explicit state, priors/assumptions, and invariants; write down failure modes as first-class artifacts.
- Explainability: add an evidence ledger for any non-trivial decision (why this branch, why this fallback). Prefer Bayes factors / log-likelihood contributions over ad-hoc scoring.
- Guarantees: where prediction/thresholding exists, prefer distribution-free calibration (conformal prediction) or anytime-valid testing (e-process) so we can stop early without invalid inference.
- Graceful degradation: define capability tiers + deterministic fallbacks; never fail closed without a traceable reason.


## Extreme Optimization
- Baseline first: capture p50/p95/p99 for relevant command(s) with `hyperfine` (store raw output).
- Profile next: CPU flamegraph + allocation profile; identify top-5 hotspots.
- Opportunity matrix: implement only Score ≥ 2.0 (Impact×Confidence/Effort).
- Isomorphism proof per change: ordering, tie-breaking, RNG seeds, and golden checksums must match.
- Regression gates: add microbench + budgets; failures must print actionable deltas and include log artifacts.


## Testing Plan
- Unit tests: happy path + edge cases + regression fixtures.
- Property tests: invariants (idempotence, monotonicity, determinism) where applicable.
- Fuzz tests: parsers/state machines and any input-facing logic.
- Determinism: fixed seeds/time-freeze; snapshot fixtures must be stable.
close_reason: done

title: Implement Flex layout with constraint solving
description:
PHASE 5 - FLEX LAYOUT

## Background
Flex layout provides 1D constraint-based sizing for rows/columns. Core layout primitive that most complex layouts build upon. Based on CSS Flexbox concepts adapted for terminal grid.

## Technical Requirements
- Flex struct with direction (Row/Column)
- Constraint types:
  - Fixed(u16): exact size
  - Percent(f32): percentage of parent
  - Min(u16): minimum size, grow to fill
  - Max(u16): maximum size, shrink to fit
  - Ratio(u16, u16): proportional sharing
- Constraint solving algorithm:
  1. Allocate Fixed constraints first
  2. Calculate Percent based on remaining space
  3. Distribute remainder to Min/Ratio proportionally
  4. Clamp Max constraints
- Gap/spacing between items
- Cross-axis alignment: Start, Center, End, Stretch

## Design Rationale
Flex is simpler than full 2D grid but handles 90% of TUI layouts. Constraint types mirror Ratatui's proven model. Solving algorithm is deterministic for predictable layouts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Flex struct with direction and items
- [ ] Full constraint type enum
- [ ] Deterministic constraint solver
- [ ] Gap/margin support
- [ ] Cross-axis alignment
- [ ] Nested Flex support
- [ ] Property tests for constraint invariants
- [ ] Edge case handling (overflow, zero space)

## Performance Budget
- Layout solve for 20 items: < 100µs
- No allocations for typical layouts (stack buffer)

## Location: ftui-layout crate

title: Migrate simple buffer-only widgets to Frame (Category A)
description:
## Scope

Migrate all Category A widgets - those that only write to buffer and don't need
any special Frame features.

## Migration Pattern

For each widget:

1. Change signature:
   ```rust
   // FROM:
   fn render(&self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer) {
   
   // TO:
   fn render(&self, area: Rect, frame: &mut Frame) {
   ```

2. Replace all `buf` references with `frame.buffer`:
   ```rust
   // FROM:
   buf.get_mut(x, y)
   
   // TO:
   frame.buffer.get_mut(x, y)
   ```

3. Or use a local binding for cleaner code:
   ```rust
   fn render(&self, area: Rect, frame: &mut Frame) {
       let buf = &mut frame.buffer;
       // ... rest of code unchanged
   }
   ```

## Widgets Expected in This Category

Based on functionality (to be confirmed by audit):
- Block (borders, title)
- Rule (horizontal/vertical lines)
- Scrollbar (decorative)
- Spinner (animation frames)
- Paragraph (text display)
- Progress (progress bars)

## Important

- DO NOT change any widget behavior
- DO NOT add new Frame features unless explicitly needed
- This is a MECHANICAL migration only
- If a widget turns out to need Frame features, move it to appropriate category

## Verification

After migration:
- `cargo check -p ftui-widgets` must pass
- All existing tests must pass

title: task(doctor-perf): build deterministic soak, shadow comparison, and replay-validation suites for doctor workflows
description:
Background:
Doctor changes need stronger validation than a few happy-path tests because they are invoked when people are already debugging stressful situations. A dedicated suite should prove that optimized workflows remain deterministic enough, comparable enough, and replay-friendly enough to trust.

Goal:
Create the doctor validation suite that stress-tests optimized diagnostic workflows and their artifacts.
design:
Work packages:
- Define soak scenarios, failure-path scenarios, side-by-side comparison scenarios, and adversarial challenge cases for the most important doctor workflows.
- Require focused unit/integration tests for workflow branching, artifact decisions, and replay helper generation before long-running suites execute.
- Require detailed manifests, summaries, and replay pointers from each scenario.
- Ensure the suite can expose regressions in artifact quality, determinism, comparison clarity, logging quality, fallback clarity, or challenge-fixture fragility, not just total runtime.
- Capture both average and tail metrics for operator-facing turnaround time.
- Make the suite reusable for future doctor changes beyond the first optimization wave.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Doctor optimization work gains a durable, workflow-aware validation net spanning unit, integration, scripted failure-path E2E, soak, shadow, and replay checks.
2. The bead keeps artifact quality and replayability on equal footing with raw speed.
3. Future self can read the bead and understand exactly why the suite exists, what logs it must emit, and what it must prove.
4. The suite explicitly includes challenge and negative-control cases so doctor wins must survive noisier and less-curated operational conditions.
notes: This bead is the quality backstop for the doctor lane. It exists because optimization work during diagnostics is dangerous if it is not aggressively validated.
close_reason: Implemented doctor shadow comparison suite, CI artifact map wiring, and verification docs

title: task(perf-rollout): implement tail-risk and regime-shift monitors for optimization regressions
description:
Background:
Optimization work that improves averages while harming p95/p99 or causing unstable behavior under certain regimes is a classic failure mode. The project therefore needs explicit monitors for tail risk and drift so regressions become visible before they spread.

Goal:
Define the monitoring and verdict logic that treats tail regressions and regime shifts as first-class rollout concerns.
design:
Work packages:
- Identify the tail metrics and regime-shift signals that matter most for render, runtime, and doctor lanes.
- Define how these signals should be computed, stored, and compared across revisions.
- Explain what constitutes a warning versus a hard gate failure.
- Specify conservative fallback behavior when monitors indicate the system has moved outside the previously trusted envelope.
- Ensure the monitor outputs remain understandable to humans rather than becoming purely mathematical black boxes.
- Include challenge-fixture and negative-control monitor views so the system can detect regressions that only appear outside the main curated suites.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Tail and drift concerns are no longer implicit or buried inside average-focused reports.
2. The bead gives future implementers enough context to build monitors that are both rigorous and operationally useful.
3. Rollout decisions can consume these monitors directly instead of relying on intuition about whether a change feels stable.
4. The monitor work is incomplete without detailed machine-readable monitor outputs, threshold-explanation logs, and scripted validation paths that prove alerting, warning, and hard-gate behavior.
notes: Planning correction: the monitor bead needs to be explicitly scriptable and diagnosable, not just mathematically well-posed, so users and operators can understand why a gate tripped.
close_reason: Completed (commit 052bc8de): ftui-harness/src/tail_regime_monitor.rs — integer-only byte-identical-replay monitors: nearest-rank p95/p99/max tail gates with separate warn/hard permille margins, baseline-envelope regime-shift gate, one-sided integer CUSUM sequential-drift gate; explicit warn-vs-hard semantics with gate_action() -> proceed/proceed_with_review/block_rollout for direct rollout consumption; conservative insufficient-baseline fallback (never silent pass) + noise floor; per-finding threshold-explanation sentences; challenge_fixtures()+run_self_test() covering clean negative control, hard tail regression, mean-masked tail (median improves/p99 blows out), uniform regime shift, mid-run drift, insufficient baseline. Scripted validation: tail_regime_monitor_e2e.rs (7 tests) + perf_tail_regime_monitor_e2e.sh (report JSON, monitor_reports.jsonl, selftest, replay, manifest). 14 unit + 7 E2E green, harness suite 1901 green, clippy clean, E2E status=0
